Then the chapter's headline section: the **2024-era Transformer block recipe** vs the 2017 original — (i) efficient attention: [[LocalAttention|local/sparse attention]] (used by [[GPT3|GPT-3]], which **interweaves full and sparse blocks**), [[SlidingWindowAttention|sliding-window attention]] (Longformer), **[[multiqueryattention|multi-query attention (MQA)]]** (K/V shared across all heads), **[[GroupedQueryAttention|grouped-query attention (GQA)]]** (K/V shared within head groups — used by Llama 2/3); (ii) **[[FlashAttention|FlashAttention]]** + **[[FlashAttention2|FlashAttention-2]]** as IO-aware GPU kernels; (iii) **[[PreNorm|pre-normalization]]** over post-norm, **[[RMSNorm]]** over LayerNorm, **[[SwiGLU]]** over ReLU; (iv) **[[RoPE|rotary positional embeddings]]** applied at the attention step (mixed into Q/K just before relevance scoring) rather than at input; (v) **[[SequencePacking|sequence packing]]** as the training-time efficiency that motivates relative-aware positional encodings (packed Document 50 starts at position 50 — absolute embeddings mislead). The **[[FeedForwardNetwork|feedforward layer (MLP)]]** is framed as the **memorization-and-interpolation engine** (*"The Shawshank ___"* → `Redemption`; the chapter's main FFN-stores-facts claim); the **attention layer** *"incorporates relevant information from other input tokens and positions"* (*"The dog chased the squirrel because it ___"* example). Also names **[[DecodingStrategy|decoding strategy]]** as the umbrella term — [[GreedyDecoding|greedy decoding]] (always pick highest probability; temperature=0) vs [[Sampling|sampling]] (random pick proportional to probability) — and the **raw-LM vs chat-LM** distinction (instruction-tuning + RLHF turns next-token predictors into chatbots). **Mints 16 concept pages**: [[KVCache|*]] (substantially extended), [[GroupedQueryAttention]], [[RoPE]], [[RMSNorm]], [[SwiGLU]], [[SiLU]], [[LMHead]], [[DecodingStrategy]], [[LocalAttention]], [[SlidingWindowAttention]], [[SequencePacking]], [[QueryProjection]], [[KeyProjection]], [[ValueProjection]], [[AttentionHead]], [[TokenStream]], [[ModelDimension]]. **Mints 1 entity page**: [[NoamShazeer]] (author of MQA + SwiGLU papers). Updates [[transformer]] / [[selfattention]] / [[multiheadattention]] / [[multiqueryattention]] / [[scaleddotproductattention]] / [[flashattention]] / [[FlashAttention2]] / [[positionalencoding]] / [[LayerNormalization]] / [[PreNorm]] / [[FeedForwardNetwork]] / [[GreedyDecoding]] / [[ContextLength]] / [[AutoregressiveLanguageModel]] / [[KVCache]] (concept pages) + [[Phi3Mini]] / [[Llama]] / [[HandsOnLLM]] / [[JayAlammar]] / [[MaartenGrootendorst]] / [[HuggingFace]] / [[OReilly]] / [[GPT3]] (entity pages) in place. **Position in the wiki**: complements rather than replaces the existing Transformer coverage. Where [[1706.03762-attention-is-all-you-need|the original *Attention Is All You Need* page]] is the **formal architectural paper**, and [[ai-engineering-ch02-foundation-models|Huyen's AI Engineering Ch 2]] is the **practitioner inference-time framing**, *Hands-On LLMs* Ch 3 is the **intuition-first walkthrough with a runnable model dissection**. **First wiki coverage of the 2024-era Transformer block recipe as a coherent bundle** (pre-norm + RMSNorm + SwiGLU + GQA + RoPE). **First wiki concrete on-consumer-GPU KV-cache speedup measurement** (4.5 s vs 21.8 s on Colab T4 with Phi-3-mini). **First wiki coverage of sequence packing** as the training-time motivation for relative-aware positional encodings. No direct contradictions; minor consistency notes flagged on the source page (RoPE timing of injection, GQA/MQA framing, FlashAttention scope, KV cache framing — all consistent with existing wiki content; the *"feedforward stores facts"* claim aligns with the mechanistic-interpretability literature but is not directly cited).
- [Hands-On LLMs Ch 2: Tokens and Embeddings](sources/hands-on-llm-ch02-tokens-and-embeddings.md) — **[[JayAlammar|Jay Alammar]] & [[MaartenGrootendorst|Maarten Grootendorst]] ([[OReilly|O'Reilly Media]], 2024, ISBN 978-1-098-15096-9).** The wiki's **canonical deep-dive on tokenizers and embeddings** — the two layers that bookend every modern LLM call. Three movements: (1) **comparative tour of seven trained tokenizers** ([[bert|BERT]] uncased + cased / [[GPT2|GPT-2]] / [[FLANT5|Flan-T5]] / [[GPT4|GPT-4]] / [[StarCoder2]] / [[Galactica]] / [[Phi3Mini|Phi-3]]/[[Llama]] 2) on a single contrived test string designed to expose how each handles capitalization, multilingual chars, emoji, Python code, whitespace, digits, and [[SpecialToken|special tokens]]; (2) the **[[TokenEmbedding|token-embedding]] / [[ContextualEmbedding|contextualized-word-embedding]] distinction**, demonstrated by running [[deberta|DeBERTa v3]] (`microsoft/deberta-v3-xsmall`) on `"Hello world"` → `[1, 4, 384]` tensor; (3) **[[Word2Vec|word2vec]] as conceptual ancestor** of all modern embeddings — the chapter walks [[SkipGram|skip-gram]] + [[NegativeSampling|negative-sampling]] end-to-end and re-applies the same algorithm to **music playlists** to build the [[Word2VecRecommender|song-recommendation worked example]] (Billie Jean → Kiss / Wanna Be Startin' Somethin' / Holiday; Fade To Black → Van Halen / Dio / Guns N' Roses / Judas Priest). Plus a third detour: **[[TextEmbedding|text embeddings]]** ([[SentenceTransformers|sentence-transformers]] with `all-mpnet-base-v2` → 768-dim) as the foundation for [[rag|RAG]] / [[SemanticSearch|semantic search]] in Part II. **Three design factors** for tokenizer behavior Ch 2 codifies: (a) tokenization **algorithm** ([[BPE]] / [[WordPiece]] / [[SentencePiece]] / [[CharacterTokenization|character]] / [[ByteLevelTokenization|byte]]); (b) **parameters** ([[VocabularySize|vocabulary size]] — 30K → 100K trend; [[SpecialToken|special tokens]]; capitalization); (c) **training dataset domain** (text vs code vs multilingual vs scientific). **Code-tokenizer findings**: [[GPT4|GPT-4]] / [[StarCoder2]] / [[Galactica]] use whitespace-run-as-single-token; [[StarCoder2]] / [[Galactica]] use per-digit tokens (`600` → `6 0 0`); [[Galactica]] adds `[START_REF]` / `[END_REF]` / `<work>` scientific tokens; chat models add `<\|user\|>` / `<\|assistant\|>` / `<\|system\|>` role tokens; [[GPT4|GPT-4]] / [[StarCoder2]] add [[FillInTheMiddle|fill-in-the-middle]] tokens (`<\|fim_prefix\|>` / `<\|fim_middle\|>` / `<\|fim_suffix\|>`) for code completion. **Static vs contextualized embeddings** — *"Instead of representing each token or word with a static vector, language models create contextualized word embeddings that represent a word with a different token based on its context."* Contextualized embeddings power [[NamedEntityRecognition|NER]], extractive summarization, **and AI image generation systems** ([[DALLE|DALL·E]], [[Midjourney]], [[StableDiffusion|Stable Diffusion]]). **Word2vec-beyond-NLP**: the chapter's headline non-text application is treating each song as a "word" and each playlist as a "sentence," then training `gensim.models.Word2Vec(vector_size=32, window=20, negative=50)` on the [[ShuoChen|Shuo Chen]] [[CornellUniversity|Cornell]] radio-playlist dataset — recovering same-genre / artist-adjacent neighbors without any genre or artist supervision. **Mints 11 concept pages** ([[SpecialToken]], [[FillInTheMiddle]], [[TokenEmbedding]], [[StaticEmbedding]], [[TextEmbedding]], [[SentenceEmbedding]], [[Word2VecRecommender]], [[ByteLevelTokenization]], [[WordTokenization]], [[CharacterTokenization]], [[SepToken]], [[PadToken]], [[UnkToken]], [[MaskToken]], [[VocabularySize]]) + **11 entity pages** ([[StarCoder2]], [[FLANT5]], [[deberta]], [[SentenceTransformers]], [[AllMPNetBaseV2]], [[Gensim]], [[NilsReimers]], [[IrynaGurevych]], [[ShuoChen]], [[CornellUniversity]], [[FrankHerbert]], [[MichaelJackson]], [[Metallica]], [[DALLE]]) — and **upgrades the existing [[Galactica]] concept page** from stub to substantive treatment. Updates [[Tokenization]] / [[BPE]] / [[wordpiece]] / [[sentencepiece]] / [[SubwordEmbedding]] / [[Tokenizer]] / [[Embedding]] / [[WordEmbedding]] / [[ContextualEmbedding]] / [[Word2Vec]] / [[SkipGram]] / [[CBOW]] / [[NegativeSampling]] / [[NoiseContrastiveEstimation]] / [[ClassificationToken]] / [[ClsToken]] / [[GloVe]] / [[FastText]] / [[bert]] / [[GPT2]] / [[GPT4]] (concept pages) + [[Phi3Mini]] / [[Llama]] / [[HuggingFace]] / [[OReilly]] / [[microsoft]] / [[meta]] / [[StableDiffusion]] / [[Midjourney]] / [[HandsOnLLM]] / [[JayAlammar]] / [[MaartenGrootendorst]] (entity pages) in place. **Position in the wiki**: complements rather than contradicts existing wiki content. Where [[d2l-nlp-pretraining|D2L NLP Pretraining]] is the **formal-math** treatment of word2vec / BPE / WordPiece / subword embedding, and [[ai-engineering-ch01-intro|Huyen Ch 1]] is the **practitioner-framing** of why tokenize-at-all, *Hands-On LLMs* Ch 2 is the **comparative empirical tour** — what each modern tokenizer actually does to a fixed test string. No direct contradictions; minor consistency notes flagged on [[Tokenization]] (vocab sizes consistent across sources) and [[NoiseContrastiveEstimation]] (Ch 2 framing of NCE → negative-sampling is consistent with [[d2l-nlp-pretraining|D2L]]'s formal treatment).
- [Hands-On LLMs Ch 1: An Introduction to Large Language Models](sources/hands-on-llm-ch01-introduction-to-llms.md) — **[[JayAlammar|Jay Alammar]] & [[MaartenGrootendorst|Maarten Grootendorst]] ([[OReilly|O'Reilly Media]], 2024, ISBN 978-1-098-15096-9).** Opening chapter of the wiki's **second O'Reilly 2024 LLM book** (after [[ai-engineering-chip-huyen|Chip Huyen's *AI Engineering*]]) and the **third LLM-engineering / pedagogy book overall** (after *AI Engineering* and the [[LLMEngineersHandbook|*LLM Engineer's Handbook*]]). Frames **[[LanguageAI|Language AI]]** (≈ [[NLP|natural language processing]], but broader — admits retrieval systems and other LLM-adjacent tech) as the umbrella for what the book covers; traces the compressed history from [[BagOfWords|bag-of-words]] → [[Word2Vec|word2vec]] (Mikolov et al. 2013) → [[encoderdecoder|RNN encoder-decoder]] + [[Attention|attention]] (Bahdanau-Cho-Bengio 2014) → [[transformer|Transformer]] ([[1706.03762-attention-is-all-you-need|Vaswani et al. 2017]]) → [[bert|BERT]] (encoder-only, 2018) vs [[GPT|GPT-1]] (decoder-only, 2018) → [[GPT2|GPT-2]] 1.5B → [[GPT3|GPT-3]] 175B → [[ChatGPT]] (Nov 2022, 1M users in 5 days). Adopts a **deliberately permissive LLM definition** — *"'Large' is arbitrary"* — that includes sub-1B encoder-only [[RepresentationModel|representation models]] alongside the canonical decoder-only [[GenerativeModel|generative models]]; this is the book's central two-bucket organizing axis. Codifies the **[[pretraining|pretraining]] → [[FineTuning|fine-tuning]] two-step training paradigm** ([[FoundationModel|base / foundation model]] → [[InstructModel|instruct / chat model]]). Surveys applications, names the responsible-LLM-use frame (bias, transparency, harmful content, IP, regulation — citing the **[[EuropeanAIAct|European AI Act]]**), and closes with a runnable *Generating Your First Text* example using **[[Phi3Mini|Phi-3-mini]]** (`microsoft/Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct`, 3.8B params, MIT-licensed) via [[HuggingFace|Hugging Face]] `transformers` on a [[GoogleColab|Google Colab]] T4 (16 GB VRAM). The book's pedagogical commitment — *"this book is for the GPU-poor"* — anchors the entire stance. **Backend stack**: [[HuggingFace|Hugging Face Transformers]] + [[llamacpp|llama.cpp]] + [[LangChain]] (with [[TextGenerationWebui]], [[KoboldCpp]], [[LMStudio]] as GUI alternatives). **Mints 9 concept pages** ([[LanguageAI]], [[BagOfWords]], [[RepresentationModel]], [[GenerativeModel]], [[CompletionModel]], [[InstructModel]], [[ContextLength]], [[ContextWindow]], [[OpenSourceLLM]], [[ProprietaryLLM]], [[VRAM]]) + **10 entity pages** ([[JayAlammar]], [[MaartenGrootendorst]], [[HandsOnLLM]], [[Cohere]], [[JacobDevlin]], [[AshishVaswani]], [[DzmitryBahdanau]], [[YoshuaBengio]], [[JohnMcCarthy]], [[Phi3Mini]], [[LMStudio]], [[KoboldCpp]], [[TextGenerationWebui]], [[EuropeanAIAct]]). Updates [[Word2Vec]] / [[bert]] / [[transformer]] / [[encoderdecoder]] / [[selfattention]] / [[Attention]] / [[maskedlanguagemodel]] / [[Tokenization]] / [[WordEmbedding]] / [[Embedding]] / [[LanguageModel]] / [[LargeLanguageModel]] / [[FoundationModel]] / [[pretraining]] / [[FineTuning]] / [[Mamba]] / [[RWKV]] / [[RNN]] / [[Hallucination]] / [[CommonCrawl]] / [[OReilly]] / [[HuggingFace]] / [[openai]] / [[anthropic]] / [[meta]] / [[microsoft]] / [[google]] / [[Mistral]] / [[Llama]] / [[ChatGPT]] / [[GPT]] / [[AlecRadford]] / [[TomasMikolov]] / [[LangChain]] / [[llamacpp]] / [[GoogleColab]] in place. **Soft definitional tension** with [[ai-engineering-ch01-intro|Chip Huyen's *AI Engineering* Ch 1]]: Alammar & Grootendorst's "LLM" admits sub-1B encoder-only models that Huyen's framing implicitly excludes — flagged on [[LargeLanguageModel]] as definitional difference, not contradiction. **First wiki source from the Alammar / Grootendorst pedagogical line** (Alammar's *Illustrated Transformer* / *Illustrated BERT* / *Illustrated GPT-2* blog series and Grootendorst's BERTopic / KeyBERT open-source NLP work).
