[[dis-0-introduction|Ch 0]]'s *active-reading-by-typing-the-code* pedagogy at the assembly surface. **Structural sibling of [[dis-1-8-exercises|Ch 1.8]] / [[dis-2-11-exercises|Ch 2.11]] / [[dis-4-10-exercises|Ch 4.10]] / [[dis-5-11-exercises|Ch 5.11]]** — exercise-set-closes-chapter pattern. **76th ingested DIS chapter — fully completes Ch 7 *64-bit x86 Assembly*.** No new concept pages — pure problem-set close.
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 7.6 Recursion (x86-64)](sources/dis-7-6-x86-64-recursion.md) — **Sixth leaf** of Ch 7 *x86-64 Assembly* of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]*. Applies the [[dis-7-5-x86-64-functions|Ch 7.5]] function-call apparatus ([[CallInstruction|`callq`]] / [[RetInstruction|`retq`]] / [[LeaveInstruction|`leaveq`]] + [[CallingConvention|System V calling convention]] + [[FramePointer|`%rbp`]]-anchored [[StackFrame|stack frames]]) to the **self-invoking** case via the [[Recursion|recursive]] `sumr(n)` worked example (sum from `n` down to 1). Headline rule: *"each recursive call generates a new stack frame"* — recursion adds **no new instructions** at the [[X86_64|x86-64]] [[AssemblyLanguage|assembly]] level, just a **dynamic-call-chain pattern** on top of Ch 7.5's mechanism. Recursion depth $d$ ⇒ $d + 1$ live `sumr` frames stacked along the [[CallStack|call stack]] at the deepest point — the **structural memory cost** of recursive algorithms. Base case (`n <= 0` → return 0) vs recursive case (`n + sumr(n-1)`) realized as a standard [[AsmIfThenElse|Ch 7.4.2]] if-pattern — [[CmpInstruction|`cmp`]] of `n` against `0`, [[X86JumpInstructions|`jg`]] on the negated condition (the *"jumps when condition is not true"* rule). The recursive [[CallInstruction|`callq sumr`]] is **structurally identical** to any other `callq` — the [[CallingConvention|calling convention]] (`%edi` = 1st param, `%eax` = return) applies on every invocation; the [[FramePointer|`%rbp`]]-anchored frame discipline is re-established on every entry. Return-value flow: the recursive `callq` deposits `sumr(n-1)` into `%eax`, then `add -0x4(%rbp), %eax` folds the local `n` into the running accumulator before `leaveq; retq` unwinds the frame. **Scope notes**: [[TailRecursion|tail-call optimization]] and stack-overflow / depth-limits are **not** covered — the `sumr` example is **not** tail-recursive (the `add` after the recursive call keeps it out of tail position) and the chapter does not address what happens when the [[CallStack|call stack]] runs out of room. **71st ingested DIS chapter — sixth leaf of Ch 7.** Mints **1 new concept page** ([[Recursion]] — promoted from forward-reference; the [[ComputerScience|CS]] concept now operationalized at the [[X86_64|x86-64]] [[AssemblyLanguage|assembly]] level) + **promotes 1 forward reference** ([[CallStack]] — first referenced by [[dis-7-2-x86-64-common|Ch 7.2]]'s `adder2` trace and used heavily by [[dis-7-5-x86-64-functions|Ch 7.5]] / [[StackPointer]] / [[X86StackInstructions]] / [[CallInstruction]]).
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 7.5 Functions in Assembly (x86-64)](sources/dis-7-5-x86-64-functions.md) — **Fifth leaf** of Ch 7 *x86-64 Assembly* of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]*. Closes the per-ISA tour by adding the **function-call instruction family** ([[CallInstruction|`callq`]] / [[RetInstruction|`retq`]] / [[LeaveInstruction|`leaveq`]]) on top of the [[dis-7-1-x86-64-basics|register/operand]] / [[dis-7-2-x86-64-common|data-movement/stack]] / [[dis-7-3-x86-64-arithmetic|arithmetic]] / [[dis-7-4-x86-64-conditional-loops|control-flow]] surface assembled by 7.1–7.4. Operationalizes the **System V AMD64 [[CallingConvention|calling convention]]** at the [[X86_64|x86-64]] [[AssemblyLanguage|assembly]] level: the **six argument registers** (`%rdi` / `%rsi` / `%rdx` / `%rcx` / `%r8` / `%r9` for params 1–6, stack for 7+); `%rax` as the return-value register; the [[StackPointer|`%rsp` invariant]] (*"always points to the top of the stack"*) and the [[FramePointer|`%rbp` invariant]] (*"points to the base of the current stack frame"*); and the [[CallerSavedRegister|caller-saved]] vs [[CalleeSavedRegister|callee-saved]] partition (`%rax`/`%rcx`/`%rdx`/`%rsi`/`%rdi`/`%r8`–`%r11` caller-owned vs `%rbx`/`%rbp`/`%r12`–`%r15` callee-owned). Canonical prologue (`push %rbp; mov %rsp, %rbp; sub $N, %rsp`) / epilogue ([[LeaveInstruction|`leaveq`]] = *"equivalent to `mov %rbp, %rsp` then `pop %rbp`"* + [[RetInstruction|`retq`]]) pattern formalized. **70th ingested DIS chapter — fifth leaf of Ch 7.** Mints **6 new concept pages** ([[CallInstruction]], [[RetInstruction]], [[LeaveInstruction]], [[CallingConvention]], [[CallerSavedRegister]], [[CalleeSavedRegister]]) plus **promotes 2 forward references** ([[StackPointer]], [[FramePointer]] — first flagged in [[dis-7-2-x86-64-common|Ch 7.2]]).
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 7.8 Matrices in Assembly (x86-64)](sources/dis-7-8-x86-64-matrices.md) — **Eighth leaf** of Ch 7 *x86-64 Assembly* of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]* — the **matrices extension** of [[dis-7-7-x86-64-arrays|Ch 7.7]]'s 1-D array-compilation pattern to the 2-D case. Walks two [[CLanguage|C]] [[MultidimensionalArray|2-D-array]] layouts at the [[X86_64|x86-64]] [[AssemblyLanguage|assembly]] surface: **contiguous** (statically declared `int M1[4][3]` or single-`malloc` `int *M3 = malloc(ROWS*COLS*sizeof(int))` — *"all the rows contiguously in memory"* in [[RowMajorOrder|row-major order]]) where element `M[i][j]` collapses to a single linear `i*cols + j` offset using the [[AsmArrayAccess|Ch 7.7 scaled-index pattern]] with [[LeaInstruction|`lea 0x0(,%rax,4),%rdx`]] materializing the `(i*cols+j)*4` offset (*"multiply (i*cols+j) by 4, put in %rdx"*); and **[[ArrayOfArrays|noncontiguous array-of-arrays]]** (`int **matrix` — *"each row is allocated contiguously in memory, but separate rows are not necessarily contiguous with one another"*) where access requires **two scaled-multiplies + two memory loads** (*"multiply i by 8, place in %rdx"* for the row pointer at scale 8, then *"multiply j by 4, place in %rdx"* inside the row at scale 4). Headline rule: the **layout choice is observable at the assembly surface** — contiguous = one memory load per element; noncontiguous = two-stage pointer chase + worse cache behavior. **No new instructions** — reuses [[X86MovInstruction|`mov`]], [[LeaInstruction|`lea`]], [[X86MulInstruction|`imul`]], and [[ScaledIndexAddressing|scaled-index addressing]]; the novelty is the **compilation pattern** that realizes the [[dis-2-5-arrays|Ch 2.5]] source-level layout distinction at the [[X86_64|x86-64]] level. **73rd ingested DIS chapter — eighth leaf of Ch 7.** Mints **0 new concept pages** — the existing [[MultidimensionalArray]] / [[RowMajorOrder]] / [[ArrayOfArrays]] / [[AsmArrayAccess]] machinery covers the new content.
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 7.4.3 Loops in Assembly (x86-64)](sources/dis-7-4-3-x86-64-loops.md) — **Third and final leaf** of [[dis-7-4-x86-64-conditional-loops|Ch 7.4]] of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]*. Operationalizes the [[dis-7-4-1-x86-64-preliminaries|Ch 7.4.1]] mechanism families ([[X86FlagsRegister|FLAGS]] + [[CmpInstruction|`cmp`]] + [[X86JumpInstructions|conditional jumps]]) into the **canonical compilation pattern** for [[CLanguage|C]]'s [[WhileLoop|`while`]] / [[ForLoop|`for`]] / [[DoWhileLoop|`do`–`while`]] constructs at the [[X86_64|x86-64]] [[AssemblyLanguage|assembly]] surface, via a single worked example — `sumUp(int n)`. Headline rules: (1) the **canonical `while`/`for` pattern** is **jump-to-test** — an unconditional `jmp` skips the body, lands at the condition check, and a conditional jump on the **un-negated** loop condition branches **back** to the body — the **inverse** of [[AsmIfThenElse|Ch 7.4.2]]'s if-pattern (forward jump on the **negated** condition); (2) `for` and `while` produce **identical assembly** — *"every `for` loop can be represented by a `while` loop"* — `for (init; cond; step) { body; }` decomposes mechanically to `init; while (cond) { body; step; }`; (3) `do`–`while` **drops the leading `jmp`** because the body always executes once unconditionally — *"test conditions typically execute before the body (except do-while)"* — making the do-while pattern strictly simpler at the assembly surface. **69th ingested DIS chapter — third and final leaf of [[dis-7-4-x86-64-conditional-loops|Ch 7.4]], closing the [[ControlFlow|control-flow]] section of Ch 7.** Mints **1 new concept page** ([[AsmLoopPattern]] — the canonical jump-to-test loop compilation pattern covering all three of `while` / `for` / `do`–`while`).
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 7.4.2 If Statements in Assembly (x86-64)](sources/dis-7-4-2-x86-64-if-statements.md) — **Second leaf** of [[dis-7-4-x86-64-conditional-loops|Ch 7.4]] of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]*. Operationalizes the [[dis-7-4-1-x86-64-preliminaries|Ch 7.4.1]] mechanism families ([[X86FlagsRegister|FLAGS]] + [[CmpInstruction|`cmp`]] + [[X86JumpInstructions|conditional jumps]]) into the **canonical compilation pattern** for [[CLanguage|C]]'s [[IfStatement|`if`]] / [[ElseStatement|`else`]] construct via a single worked example — `getSmallest(int x, int y)` — traced through both **unoptimized (branch-based)** and **`-O1`-optimized (branch-free, [[X86ConditionalMove|`cmov`]]-based)** [[X86_64|x86-64]] assembly. Two headline rules: (1) the branch-based form jumps on the **negated** source condition (*"a standard if statement [is] where a jump occurs when conditions are **not** true"*) — the [[X86JumpInstructions|`jle`]] in the `getSmallest` trace fires precisely when `x ≤ y`, falling through to the then-branch when the source `x > y` holds; (2) the `-O1` substitution to [[X86ConditionalMove|`cmov`]] (*"`cmov` executes both conditional branches in hardware, selecting the result afterward"*) **eliminates** the [[ControlHazard|control hazard]] / [[BranchPrediction|branch-prediction]] dependency from [[dis-5-8-pipelining-advanced|Ch 5.8]] entirely — at the cost of requiring both arms to be safely pre-evaluable (*"the compiler takes the safe road and uses jumps"* when [[NullPointerSafety|null-pointer dereference]] or side effects make pre-evaluation unsafe). **68th ingested DIS chapter — second leaf of [[dis-7-4-x86-64-conditional-loops|Ch 7.4]].** Mints **3 new concept pages** ([[X86ConditionalMove]], [[AsmIfThenElse]], [[BranchInstruction]] — last one promoted from forward-reference).
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 7.4.1 Preliminaries (x86-64 Conditional Control)](sources/dis-7-4-1-x86-64-preliminaries.md) — **First leaf** of [[dis-7-4-x86-64-conditional-loops|Ch 7.4]] of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]*. Introduces the three mechanisms every conditional construct at the [[X86_64|x86-64]] [[AssemblyLanguage|assembly]] level rests on: the **[[X86FlagsRegister|FLAGS condition-code register]]** (the single-bit ALU side-channel — ZF / SF / OF / CF), the **comparison instructions [[CmpInstruction|`cmp`]] and [[TestInstruction|`test`]]** (set flags *without* writing a destination — flag-only siblings of [[X86ArithmeticInstructions|`sub`]] and [[X86BitwiseInstructions|`and`]] respectively), and the **[[X86JumpInstructions|jump-instruction family]]** (`jmp` unconditional + signed `je`/`jne`/`jg`/`jge`/`jl`/`jle` and unsigned `ja`/`jae`/`jb`/`jbe` conditional jumps). Headline rules: (1) the **same** [[CmpInstruction|`cmp`]] sets **all four flags** — the signed/unsigned split lives entirely in the **consumer** mnemonic (`g`/`l` consume SF + OF; `a`/`b` consume CF), realizing the bit-pattern-interpretation-invariance from [[dis-4-3-signed|Ch 4.3]] / [[dis-4-5-overflow|Ch 4.5]] at the instruction surface; (2) the **`test %rax, %rax`** idiom is the canonical register-zero test (`x AND x = 0` iff `x = 0`); (3) jump instructions are the **indirect channel** through which [[InstructionPointer|`%rip`]] changes — restating [[dis-7-1-x86-64-basics|Ch 7.1]]'s *"`%rip` is read-only — cannot be written directly"* rule. **67th ingested DIS chapter — first leaf of [[dis-7-4-x86-64-conditional-loops|Ch 7.4]].** Mints **5 new concept pages** ([[X86FlagsRegister]], [[ConditionCode]], [[CmpInstruction]], [[TestInstruction]], [[X86JumpInstructions]]).
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 7.10 Buffer Overflows (x86-64)](sources/dis-7-10-x86-64-buffer-overflow.md) — **Tenth leaf** of Ch 7 *x86-64 Assembly* of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]* — the **security payoff** of the whole Ch 7 stack-discipline tour. Fuses [[dis-7-5-x86-64-functions|Ch 7.5]]'s [[CallStack|call-stack]] mechanics ([[CallInstruction|`callq`]] / [[RetInstruction|`retq`]] / [[StackFrame|stack frames]] / [[FramePointer|`%rbp`]]) with the [[CArray|C-array]] / [[CString|string]] vulnerabilities flagged in [[dis-1-5-arrays-strings|Ch 1.5]] / [[dis-2-6-strings|Ch 2.6]] into the canonical [[StackSmashing|stack-smashing]] exploit: an unbounded `scanf("%s", buf)` writes past a 12-byte buffer, overwrites the saved return address at `8(%rbp)`, and on [[RetInstruction|`retq`]] redirects [[InstructionPointer|`%rip`]] into attacker-chosen code. Walks the `secret` worked example with a precise 48-byte payload (**40 bytes of padding + 8-byte little-endian address `0x4006da`**). Three defense layers: programmer-level ([[BoundsChecking|length-specifying functions]] — `fgets` / `scanf("%12s")` / [[Strncpy|`strncpy`]] / `strncat` / `snprintf`), compiler / OS-level ([[StackCanary|stack canaries]], [[AddressSpaceLayoutRandomization|ASLR]], [[ExecutableSpaceProtection|NX / DEP]]), and **why each is bypassable** ([[ReturnOrientedProgramming|ROP]] defeats NX; canaries can be overwritten with the original value; ASLR can be brute-forced or sidestepped by NOP sleds). Closes with the **Morris Worm (1988)** ([[Daemon|`fingerd`]] overrun) and **AOL Chat Wars** case studies. Headline quote: *"The C language does not perform automatic array bounds checking"*. **75th ingested DIS chapter — tenth leaf of Ch 7.** Mints **7 new concept pages** ([[StackSmashing]], [[ReturnAddressOverwrite]], [[StackCanary]], [[AddressSpaceLayoutRandomization]], [[ExecutableSpaceProtection]], [[ReturnOrientedProgramming]], [[Daemon]]).
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 7.9 Structs in Assembly (x86-64)](sources/dis-7-9-x86-64-structs.md) — **Ninth leaf** of Ch 7 *x86-64 Assembly* of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]*. Shows how the [[CLanguage|C]] [[CStruct|struct]] aggregate compiles to [[X86_64|x86-64]] [[AssemblyLanguage|assembly]] — fields stored **contiguously in declaration order**, accessed via fixed compile-time `disp(%base)` offsets ([[X86MovInstruction|`mov %edx, 0x44(%rax)`]] writes `grad_yr` 68 bytes past struct base). Codifies the [[X86_64|x86-64]] [[AlignmentRule|alignment rule]] — *"x64's alignment policy requires that two-byte data types (i.e., `short`) reside at a two-byte-aligned address, four-byte data types (i.e., `int`, `float`, and `unsigned`) reside at four-byte-aligned addresses, and larger data types (`long`, `double`, and pointer data) reside at eight-byte-aligned addresses"* — and the [[CCompiler|compiler]]-inserted [[StructPadding|padding]] mechanism — *"the compiler adds empty bytes as padding between fields to ensure that each field satisfies its alignment requirements"* — that makes [[StructLayout|struct layout]] declaration-order-dependent. **74th ingested DIS chapter — ninth leaf of Ch 7.** Mints 4 new concept pages ([[StructLayout]], [[StructPadding]], [[AlignmentRule]], [[MemoryAlignment]]).
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 7.4 Conditional Control and Loops (x86-64)](sources/dis-7-4-x86-64-conditional-loops.md) — **Fourth leaf** of Ch 7 *x86-64 Assembly* of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]* and the **hub page** opening the three-subsection treatment of [[ControlFlow|control flow]] at the [[X86_64|x86-64]] [[AssemblyLanguage|assembly]] level. Follows [[dis-7-3-x86-64-arithmetic|Ch 7.3]]'s extended-arithmetic / bit-shift / bitwise / [[LeaInstruction|`lea`]] surface and pivots from **straight-line code** to **branch-driven non-sequential execution** — how the compiler translates [[CLanguage|C]]'s [[IfStatement|`if` / `else`]] and [[WhileLoop|`while`]] / [[ForLoop|`for`]] / [[DoWhileLoop|`do`–`while`]] constructs into instructions that **modify the [[InstructionPointer|`%rip`]] instruction pointer** based on evaluated conditions (*"modify the instruction pointer to alter program flow based on evaluated conditions"*). Three subsections (7.4.1 Preliminaries / 7.4.2 If Statements / 7.4.3 Loops) deliver the leaf mechanisms; this hub is intentionally short. **66th ingested DIS chapter — fourth leaf of Ch 7.** Hub-only — no new concept pages; subsection ingests will mint the condition-code / conditional-jump / branch-pattern pages.
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 7.3 Additional Arithmetic Instructions (x86-64)](sources/dis-7-3-x86-64-arithmetic.md) — **Third leaf** of Ch 7 *x86-64 Assembly* of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]*, following [[dis-7-2-x86-64-common|Ch 7.2]]'s data-movement / stack / `add`-`sub` primitives. **Expands the [[X86_64|x86-64]] arithmetic surface** with three new instruction families — **extended integer arithmetic** ([[X86NegInstruction|`neg`]] / `inc` / `dec`, [[X86MulInstruction|`imul`]], [[X86DivInstruction|`idiv`]]), **[[X86ShiftInstructions|bit-shift instructions]]** (`shl` / `sal` / `shr` / `sar`), and **[[X86BitwiseInstructions|bitwise logic instructions]]** (`and` / `or` / `xor` / `not`) — plus the **[[LeaInstruction|`lea` (load effective address)]] instruction**, the [[dis-7-2-x86-64-common|Ch 7.2]] forward-reference now delivered. Two headline pedagogical points: the `idiv` / multi-bit-shift hidden-operand conventions (*"prior to the execution of the `idiv` instruction, it is assumed that register `%rax` contains the dividend"*; *"the shift value `v` must either be a constant or stored in register `%cl`"*), and `lea` as an **address-arithmetic instruction that performs no memory access** (*"the `lea` instruction performs the same (sometimes complicated) operand arithmetic without the memory lookup"*) — exploited by compilers as a multi-operation arithmetic shortcut. The headline `not`-vs-`neg` clarification (*"the `not` instruction flips the bits but does not add 1"*) pins the `~x = -x - 1` identity to the assembly-instruction surface. The headline [[CompilerOptimization|strength-reduction]] quote — *"to compute `77 * 4`, most compilers will translate this operation to `77 << 2` to avoid the use of an `imul` instruction"* — surfaces the *shift-as-multiply* compiler pattern. **65th ingested DIS chapter — third leaf of Ch 7.** Mints 6 new concept pages ([[X86MulInstruction]], [[X86DivInstruction]], [[X86NegInstruction]], [[X86ShiftInstructions]], [[X86BitwiseInstructions]], [[LeaInstruction]] — last one promoted from forward-reference).
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 7.2 Common Instructions (x86-64)](sources/dis-7-2-x86-64-common.md) — **Second leaf** of Ch 7 *x86-64 Assembly* of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]*, following [[dis-7-1-x86-64-basics|Ch 7.1]]'s register / operand / addressing-mode framing. Introduces the **five most common [[X86_64|x86-64]] instructions** every assembly reader meets on sight: the data-movement primitive [[X86MovInstruction|`mov S, D`]] (*"copies a source value into a destination"*), the [[X86ArithmeticInstructions|arithmetic pair `add` / `sub`]] (`D ← D + S` and `D ← D − S` — the source-first AT&T order makes `sub` counterintuitive), and the [[X86StackInstructions|stack-management pair `push` / `pop`]] (specialized [[X86MovInstruction|`mov`]] + `sub`/`add` against [[StackPointer|`%rsp`]] — stack-grows-down, 8-byte step). Closes with a **step-by-step trace of [[dis-7-1-x86-64-basics|Ch 7.1]]'s `adder2` function** showing how the five instructions compose into a complete prologue / body / epilogue with [[CallStack|call-stack]] state tracked at each step — every `push` paired with a `pop`, the stack restored to entry state before `retq`. **Scope note**: the [[LeaInstruction|`lea`]] instruction is **not** covered here despite being commonly grouped with these primitives — it appears in a later Ch 7 section. **64th ingested DIS chapter — second leaf of Ch 7.** Mints 3 new concept pages ([[X86MovInstruction]], [[X86ArithmeticInstructions]], [[X86StackInstructions]]).
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 7.1 Diving into Assembly: Basics (x86-64)](sources/dis-7-1-x86-64-basics.md) — **First ISA-specific section** of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]* Part III, opening Ch 7 *x86-64 Assembly*. Walks `adder2` from C to [[X86_64|x86-64]] [[AssemblyLanguage|assembly]] in [[AtAndTSyntax|AT&T syntax]] and supplies the wiki's canonical references for: the **16 [[GeneralPurposeRegister|GPRs]]** (`%rax`–`%rdx`, `%rdi`, `%rsi`, `%r8`–`%r15`) plus the three special-purpose `%rsp` / `%rbp` / `%rip`; the **subregister naming scheme** (`%rax` → `%eax` → `%ax` → `%al`/`%ah`; `%r8` → `%r8d` → `%r8w` → `%r8b`); the **System V calling convention** — *"the first six parameters in registers `%rdi`, `%rsi`, `%rdx`, `%rcx`, `%r8` and `%r9`"* with `%rax` as the return value; the **instruction-structure rule** opcode + source-then-destination operands; the **three [[Operand|operand types]]** (constant / register / memory) and the two structural constraints (no constant destinations, ≤ one memory operand per instruction); the **six [[X86AddressingMode|memory addressing modes]]** of `disp(base, index, scale)` with `scale ∈ {1,2,4,8}`; and the **[[OperandSize|size-suffix]] table** (`b`/`w`/`l`/`s`/`q`/`d` → 1/2/4/4/8/8 bytes). **63rd ingested DIS chapter — first ISA-specific section after Ch 6 hub.** Promotes [[X86_64]] from forward-ref stub to first-class [[ISA]] page; mints 6 new concept pages ([[X86_64]], [[GeneralPurposeRegister]], [[AtAndTSyntax]], [[IntelSyntax]], [[OperandSize]], [[Operand]], [[X86AddressingMode]]).
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 6 Under the C: Diving into Assembly](sources/dis-6-asm-intro.md) — **Opens Part III *Assembly Programming*** of [[DiveIntoSystems]]. Single-page hub framing the three [[ISA]]-specific chapters that follow — Ch 7 [[X86_64|x86-64]], Ch 8 [[IA32]], Ch 9 [[ARM|ARMv8-A]]. Re-introduces [[AssemblyLanguage|assembly]] as *"the closest a programmer gets to coding at the machine level"* — the human-readable form of [[MachineCode|machine code]] — and motivates three chapters of ISA-specific detail via **four use cases**: (1) demystify what high-level code actually does at runtime, (2) embedded / resource-constrained programming, (3) security / vulnerability analysis, (4) performance-critical system code. Names the **four-category partition** every [[InstructionSet|ISA]] implements — arithmetic/logic, control flow, data movement, stack operations — as the structural unifier across the three dialects that follow. **62nd ingested DIS chapter — opens Part III after Ch 5 *Computer Architecture* closed at chapter 61.** Hub-only — no new concept pages, reuses [[AssemblyLanguage]] / [[MachineCode]] / [[InstructionSet]] / [[ISA]] / [[X86_64]] / [[IA32]] / [[ARM]].
- [DSPy Tutorial — Audio (Spoken QA + Emotion-Guided TTS)](sources/dspy-audio-tutorial.md) — Official [[DSPy]] tutorial at `https://dspy.ai/tutorials/audio/` — **the wiki's first receipt of an audio modality in DSPy** and the first source to exercise the [[DSPyAudio|`dspy.Audio`]] primitive end-to-end across both **input-side** (audio → text) and **output-side** (text → audio) tasks. Two complete `dspy.Module` programs: (1) **spoken question-answering** over [[SpokenSQuAD]] (`AudioLLMs/spoken_squad_test` on [[HuggingFace]]) using `dspy.ChainOfThought(SpokenQASignature)` against [[GPT4oMiniAudio|`gpt-4o-mini-audio-preview-2024-12-17`]] with `passage_audio: dspy.Audio = dspy.InputField()` — first wiki receipt of `dspy.Audio.from_array(array, sampling_rate)` and an OpenAI audio-input model in DSPy; **headline lift ~10% absolute** from [[BootstrapFewShotWithRandomSearch]] (`max_bootstrapped_demos=2, max_labeled_demos=2, num_candidate_programs=5`) and [[MIPROv2|`MIPROv2(auto="light", prompt_model=gpt-4o-mini)`]]. (2) **Emotion-guided text-to-speech** over [[CREMAD]] (six emotions: neutral / happy / sad / anger / fear / disgust) that wraps the [[GPT4oMiniTTS|`gpt-4o-mini-tts`]] HTTP API (`voice="coral"`, instruction-controllable) **outside the DSPy LM abstraction** inside a manual `dspy.Module.forward()` returning `dspy.Prediction(audio=dspy.Audio(...))`; [[MIPROv2]] optimizes the TTS `instructions=` string against a [[Wav2Vec2|Wav2Vec 2.0]] (`torchaudio.pipelines.WAV2VEC2_BASE`) mean-pooled embedding [[CosineSimilarity|cosine-similarity]] metric (with the threshold-binarize-when-trace `score > 0.8` optimizer convention); **headline lift ~0.57 → ~0.67** cosine similarity. **Three previously-undocumented constraints on the DSPy audio surface**: (1) **MIPROv2's `data_aware_proposer=False` is required** for any Signature with non-textual InputFields — the dataset-summarizer proposer cannot read audio bytes (first wiki receipt of the kwarg); (2) **audio tokens are expensive** — `max_bootstrapped_demos` / `max_labeled_demos` should stay at 0–2 and `auto="light"` is the recommended optimizer budget; (3) **audio-out is not first-class in DSPy** — the TTS endpoint must be hand-wrapped because [[DSPyLM|`dspy.LM`]] does not multiplex non-chat audio-output HTTP endpoints. **First DSPy tutorial in the corpus to ship a metric with a documented epistemic caveat about the metric itself** — *"audio reference comparisons is generally a non-trivial task due to subjective variations of evaluating speech, especially with emotional expression … Human feedback or perceptual metrics would be more suitable."* (Wav2Vec2 is a phonetic-content encoder, not an emotion encoder.) **First wiki documentation of OpenAI TTS's 11-voice catalog** (tutorial fixes `"coral"` and does not optimize the voice axis). **Mints 7 concept pages** ([[DSPyAudio]], [[SpokenSQuAD]], [[CREMAD]], [[GPT4oMiniAudio]], [[GPT4oMiniTTS]], [[Wav2Vec2]], [[EmotionGuidedTTS]]); updates [[MIPROv2]] (`data_aware_proposer=False` section), [[BootstrapFewShotWithRandomSearch]] (audio receipt with conservative-budget callout), [[SQuAD]] (Spoken-SQuAD cross-reference) in place. **Scope-limit gaps**: no printed accuracy cells (qualitative "~10%" only); no fine-tuning / GEPA / agent receipt on audio; no [[Whisper]] cascaded-ASR baseline comparison; no voice-axis ablation; no alternative emotion-encoder metric (e.g. emotion2vec); no cost / wall-time disclosure; `torch==2.0.1+cu118` pin is CUDA-specific without macOS / CPU-only flag.
- [DSPy Tutorial — Tracking DSPy Optimizers with MLflow](sources/dspy-optimizer-tracking-tutorial.md) — Official [[DSPy]] tutorial at `https://dspy.ai/tutorials/optimizer_tracking/` that **canonicalizes [[MLflow]] autologging for the [[DSPyOptimization|Optimization stage]]** — the first wiki-corpus source whose central subject is *tracking the optimization process itself* (every prior MLflow-mentioning DSPy ingest — [[dspy-custom-module]], [[dspy-tutorial-rag-as-agent]], [[dspy-entity-extraction-tutorial]] — treated `mlflow.dspy.autolog()` as a one-line side-channel). **Three structural contributions to the wiki's DSPy/MLflow corpus**: (1) the **three optimization-aware autolog kwargs** — `mlflow.dspy.autolog(log_compiles=True, log_evals=True, log_traces_from_compile=True)` — independent toggles for the three artifact families (workflow config + intermediate program versions + metric-progression curve / per-step evaluation values / per-LM-call trace tree); (2) the **parent/child run hierarchy** MLflow imposes on a [[MIPROv2|`dspy.MIPROv2`]] `compile()` call — parent run carries the optimizer config + final optimized program + metric-progression curve + training data; each child run is one intermediate `(instruction, demo-set)` candidate the [[BayesianOptimization|Bayesian surrogate]] sampled, with that candidate's instructions + demos + per-mini-batch evaluation values + full LM-call traces; (3) the **second documented load path** for optimized DSPy programs — `mlflow.artifacts.download_artifacts("mlflow-artifacts:/path/to/best_model.json")` then `program.load(model_path)`, adding parent-run-anchored provenance to the plain-JSON `program.save/load` round-trip used by [[dspy-optimizers|the Optimizers page]] and prior tutorials. **Worked example**: `dspy.ChainOfThought("question -> answer")` on [[GSM8K]] via `from dspy.datasets.gsm8k import GSM8K, gsm8k_metric` (the in-framework dataset loader + built-in metric — first wiki receipt of either), optimized by `dspy.MIPROv2(metric=gsm8k_metric, auto="light")` over `gpt-4o` — first wiki MIPROv2 receipt on GSM8K and first MIPROv2 receipt with `gpt-4o` (rather than `gpt-4o-mini` or a Llama student) as the task LM. **No headline accuracy reported** — scope is the tracking surface, not the optimization gain. **Setup recipe**: `pip install mlflow>=2.21.1` (older than the `>=3.0.0` floor [[dspy-custom-module]] called for — confirms the DSPy autolog surface predates MLflow 3.0 and is supported on both 2.x and 3.x lines), `mlflow server --backend-store-uri sqlite:///mydb.sqlite` (the tutorial asserts *"It is highly recommended to use SQL store when using MLflow tracing"* — file-based / in-memory stores lose the trace tree), `mlflow.set_tracking_uri("http://localhost:5000")` + `mlflow.set_experiment("DSPy-Optimization")`. **Memory caveat**: `log_traces_from_compile=True` storage cost grows linearly in (trials × demos × dataset size) — tutorial recommends `log_traces_from_compile=False` for large datasets. **Twelfth wiki-corpus DSPy tutorial** and the **first whose entire scope is the [[ExperimentTracking|experiment-tracking]] / observability surface** rather than a programming-stage receipt or an optimization-gain receipt; fills the **MLOps-surface rung** of the wiki's DSPy tutorial corpus between programming-stage tutorials ([[dspy-ai-text-game-tutorial]] / [[dspy-email-extraction-tutorial]] / [[dspy-llms-txt-generation-tutorial]] / [[dspy-sample-code-generation-tutorial]] / [[dspy-conversation-history]] / [[dspy-customer-service-agent]] / [[dspy-mem0-react-tutorial]] / [[dspy-yahoo-finance-react-tutorial]] / [[dspy-async-tutorial]]) and optimization-gain tutorials ([[dspy-rag-tutorial]] / [[dspy-tutorial-rag-as-agent]] / [[dspy-tutorial-math]] / [[dspy-entity-extraction-tutorial]] / [[dspy-custom-module]]). **Third [[Databricks]] touchpoint on the DSPy line** after [[MateiZaharia]]'s authorship of [[2406.11695-mipro|MIPRO]] / [[2507.19457-gepa|GEPA]] and the MLflow Gateway role in [[ai-engineering-ch10-architecture-feedback|AI Engineering Ch 10]]. **One contradiction flagged with prior corpus**: MLflow version floor — `>=2.21.1` here vs. `>=3.0.0` in [[dspy-custom-module]]; resolution: both work; the 3.0.0 floor was the more conservative recommendation. No new concept pages minted (updates [[MLflow]] / [[MIPROv2]] / [[DSPyOptimization]] / [[DSPyOptimizers]] / [[ExperimentTracking]] / [[GSM8K]] in place). **Scope-limit gaps**: no headline accuracy; no multi-run aggregation discussion; no MLflow Model Registry reconciliation with [[dspy-entity-extraction-tutorial]]'s `mlflow.dspy.log_model(...)`; no [[GEPA]]-specific tracking receipt; no cost tracking integration; no `dspy.Evaluate` standalone example; memory-budget threshold is qualitative.
- [DSPy Tutorial — Multi-Hop Search (MIPROv2 over HoVer with Llama-3.1-8B)](sources/dspy-multihop-search-tutorial.md) — Official [[DSPy]] tutorial at `https://dspy.ai/tutorials/multihop_search/` that demonstrates **prompt-space joint optimization** of a fixed-depth multi-hop retrieval program ([[Hop]]) on the [[HoVer]] three-hop subset, using [[MIPROv2|`dspy.MIPROv2`]] with [[Llama|Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct]] as the student and [[GPT4o|GPT-4o]] as **both the instruction proposer and the bootstrap-demo teacher**. **Third wiki receipt of [[HoVer]] under a DSPy optimizer** — completes the prompt-vs-weight comparison: [[dspy-tutorial-rag-as-agent|MIPROv2 over `dspy.ReAct`]] (Llama-3.2-3B, top5_recall 8 → 41.67, 5.21×), **this tutorial: MIPROv2 over `Hop` (Llama-3.1-8B, top5_recall 31.3 → 59.1, 1.89×)**, [[dspy-rl-multihop-tutorial|ArborGRPO over ResearchHop]] (Qwen-1.5B, per-page recall 61.8 → 66.2, 1.07×). **Headline number**: ~$5 of GPT-4o calls lift Llama-3.1-8B from 31.3% → 59.1% top5_recall — the **largest single-run MIPROv2 lift in the wiki for a multi-hop retrieval task with a >7B student**. **First wiki receipts within this tutorial**: [[Hop]] as the **4-hop generate-query / append-notes program shape** with typed `list[str]` outputs and output-level `list(set(titles))` dedup (structural parent of [[ResearchHop]]); inline-string typed-output Signatures inside a `dspy.ChainOfThought` call (`'... -> new_notes: list[str], titles: list[str]'`); the **dual-mode `top5_recall` metric with `recall >= 1.0` perfect-recall bootstrap gate** (stricter than [[dspy-tutorial-rag-as-agent|RAG-as-agent's]] `>= 0.5`); explicit `prompt_model=gpt4o, teacher_settings=dict(lm=gpt4o)` two-role GPT-4o binding; `minibatch_size=40, minibatch_full_eval_steps=4` MIPROv2 Bayesian-search schedule kwargs; balanced 4/4 demo budget (`max_bootstrapped_demos=4, max_labeled_demos=4`); `vincentkoc/hover-parquet` as parquet-format HoVer variant (vs prior `hover-nlp/hover`); 200/300/remainder split with `hover[650:]` test-set 150-buffer; the `$5 of GPT-4o` budget framing for MIPROv2 on multi-hop retrieval. **Second DSPy tutorial to reuse the `bm25s` + 2017 Wikipedia abstracts stack** (after [[dspy-rl-multihop-tutorial]]) — strong evidence `bm25s` is the default DSPy lightweight retrieval substrate. **Thirteenth wiki-corpus DSPy tutorial**; **second MIPROv2-on-HoVer receipt**. **Pins the 8B open-weights student-size point** between the [[dspy-tutorial-rag-as-agent|3B Llama-3.2]] and [[2406.11695-mipro|paper-era 8B Llama-3]] rungs. Mints 1 concept page ([[Hop]] — the 4-hop / 10-docs program shape, structural parent of [[ResearchHop]]); updates [[HoVer]] (third-tutorial comparison table + new section), [[MIPROv2]] (new tutorial receipt), [[ResearchHop]] (lineage note: 2-hop simplification of `Hop`), [[BM25]] (second DSPy `bm25s` receipt), [[MultiHopRAG]] (new tutorial connection) in place. **Clean operational evidence for the [[2507.19457-gepa|GEPA paper's]] central thesis** on HoVer (prompt-space wins on cost/quality: $5 / 1.89× MIPROv2 vs 18 GPU-h / 1.07× ArborGRPO on the same benchmark family).
- [DSPy Tutorial — Online RL for Multi-Hop Research (GRPO over HoVer)](sources/dspy-rl-multihop-tutorial.md) — Official [[DSPy]] tutorial at `https://dspy.ai/tutorials/rl_multihop/` — labeled **"extremely EXPERIMENTAL ... pure proof of concept"** — that runs [[grpo|GRPO]] (via [[ArborGRPO|`dspy.ArborGRPO`]]) against a 2-hop [[chainofthought|`dspy.ChainOfThought`]] retrieval program ([[ResearchHop]]) over [[HoVer]] three-hop claims with a [[BM25|BM25]] retriever over the 2017 Wikipedia abstracts corpus. **Second wiki receipt of [[ArborGRPO]] / [[Arbor]] / [[DAPO]]** after [[dspy-tutorial-rl-papillon]] — moves the RL surface from a 2-module privacy-delegation chain ([[PAPILLON]] / [[PUPA]] with [[LLMJudge|LLM-judge composite reward]]) to a **2-hop retrieval program with a deterministic title-recall reward**. **First wiki receipts within this tutorial**: [[ResearchHop]] (2-hop generate-query / append-notes program shape) as a new concept; **`program.set_lm(...)`** as the per-program LM-binding API distinct from global `dspy.configure(lm=...)`; `ArborProvider()` + `"openai/arbor:Qwen/..."` model prefix as the explicit [[DSPyLM|`dspy.LM(...)`]] binding form for Arbor-backed RL training; [[HoVer]] as a *weight-space RL* optimization target (prior HoVer DSPy receipt was [[dspy-tutorial-rag-as-agent|MIPROv2 over a `dspy.ReAct` agent]]); [[bm25s|`bm25s.BM25(k1=0.9, b=0.4)`]] + [[PyStemmer|`Stemmer`]] as the in-process Python BM25 retriever (prior wiki BM25 receipts used `rank_bm25.BM25Okapi` ([[hands-on-llm-ch08-semantic-search-and-rag]]) or hosted [[ColBERTv2]] ([[dspy-tutorial-rag-as-agent]] / [[dspy-custom-module]])); the `wiki.abstracts.2017.tar.gz` Hugging Face artifact (500MB compressed, 5M Wikipedia abstracts) downloaded via `dspy.utils.download(...)`; `Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct` named explicitly as the student model (wiki's smallest open-weights DSPy student, below the prior 3B floor); explicit GPU-partition kwargs `num_training_gpus=3, num_inference_gpus=1` (on-policy RL pattern — inference GPU holds rollout-generation copy of policy while training GPUs compute gradients); `checkpoint="single-best"` + `num_steps_for_val=50, use_train_as_val=False` early-stopping discipline; broader train_kwargs surface `scale_rewards=False, max_grad_norm=1.0, weight_decay=0.001, lr_scheduler_type="constant_with_warmup", report_to="wandb"`. **Twelfth wiki-corpus DSPy tutorial** and **second tutorial with a weight-space optimizer** — the wiki now has two parallel [[ArborGRPO]] receipts on two distinct task families ([[LLMJudge|LLM-judge reward]] axis via PAPILLON, deterministic-metric axis via [[ResearchHop]]). **Headline number**: ~18 h on 4 GPUs lifts devset recall from **61.8% → 66.2%** (+4.4 pts, ~7% relative). The tutorial itself frames this honestly as worse on cost/quality than [[MIPROv2]] / [[SIMBA]] — **first DSPy tutorial whose own conclusion documents that the demonstrated technique is dominated by prior tutorials on the same benchmark family** ([[dspy-tutorial-rag-as-agent|HoVer via MIPROv2]]: 8% → 41.67% top5_recall via prompt optimization on a different program shape). **Operational form of the [[2507.19457-gepa|GEPA paper's]] central contrast** — same 24,000-rollout total budget (1000 steps × 6 examples × 4 rollouts) the GEPA paper gave its GRPO baseline that GEPA beat by 6% average and up to 20% on HoVer. **LoRA recipe identical to the PAPILLON tutorial** (`r=8, alpha=16, dropout=0.05`, seven target modules q/k/v/o/up/down/gate `_proj`) — strong evidence this is the default DAPO+LoRA configuration ArborGRPO ships with. Mints 1 concept page ([[ResearchHop]]) + 2 entity pages ([[bm25s]], [[PyStemmer]]); updates [[ArborGRPO]] (cross-tutorial config diff table + second receipt), [[Arbor]] (explicit API surface section), [[DAPO]] (second receipt), [[HoVer]] (rl_multihop section + first weight-space receipt callout), [[grpo|GRPO]] (table of both DSPy GRPO tutorials), [[qwen|Qwen]] (Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct receipt), [[BM25]] (`bm25s` section + first DSPy BM25 receipt), [[MultiHopRAG]] in place. No contradictions — explicitly aligns with [[2507.19457-gepa|GEPA paper's]] ordering (prompt-space beats GRPO on cost/quality for sample-constrained compound-AI-system tasks).
- [PAPILLON Tutorial — Columbia-NLP-Lab Colab (MIPROv2 + Llama-3.1-8B + SGLang)](sources/papillon-colab-tutorial.md) — **Canonical author-of-record [[PAPILLON]] tutorial** from the Columbia-NLP-Lab repo (`github.com/Columbia-NLP-Lab/PAPILLON/blob/main/papillon_tutorial.ipynb`) — the upstream parent both DSPy.ai variants ([[dspy-tutorial-rl-papillon]] / [[dspy-tutorial-gepa-papillon]]) descend from. **The wiki's first MIPROv2-on-PAPILLON tutorial-grade receipt** — fills the gap between [[2507.19457-gepa|GEPA paper Table 4]]'s paper-scale MIPROv2-on-PUPA cell (81.55 Qwen3 8B / 85.37 GPT-4.1 Mini) and the existing prompt-space ([[GEPA]]) / weight-space ([[ArborGRPO]]) tutorial receipts. Stack: `dspy-ai==2.5.41` + `Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct` (served via [[SGLang]] on a single GPU, port 7501, `flashinfer` cu121/torch2.4) + `gpt-4o-mini` (collapsed three-role: untrusted external + [[MIPROv2]] prompt-proposer + [[LLMJudge]] LM). Optimizer: `dspy.MIPROv2(metric=compute_overall_score, auto="medium", num_threads=16, prompt_model=openai_lm, task_model=local_lm)` with **`minibatch_size=35, max_bootstrapped_demos=5, max_labeled_demos=0`** (first wiki receipts of all three kwargs in MIPROv2). Splits: 150/150/remainder from `pupa_new["train"]` — smallest training budget of the three PAPILLON tutorials. **Headline result: not printed** — the notebook commits seven `evaluate(...)` calls without their output cells; *runnable-receipt-of-API-surface* contribution, not headline-number. **First wiki receipts within this tutorial**: (1) MIPROv2 on a compound AI program with an external untrusted LM call (Receipts 1/1b/2/2b/3 are single-module or single-module-with-tools); (2) `minibatch_size=35` MIPROv2 kwarg; (3) `max_bootstrapped_demos=5, max_labeled_demos=0` MIPROv2 preset (most-bootstrapped / zero-labeled in the wiki, driven by PUPA's lack of CoT labels); (4) `use_legacy_loading=True` — DSPy 2.4 → 2.5 save-format backwards-compat shim on `Module.load(...)` for `papillon/optimized_prompts/llama_31_8b_instruct_prompt.json`; (5) `dspy.configure(experimental=True)` as gate on per-module `set_lm(...)`; (6) triple-segment LM identifier `openai/sglang/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct` (author-chosen middle-segment labeling beyond LiteLLM's two-segment convention); (7) pinned `dspy-ai==2.5.41` (pre-3.0 era contemporaneous with the paper); (8) original PAPILLON Signature names `CreateOnePrompt(userQuery → createdPrompt)` / `InfoAggregator(userQuery, modelExampleResponses → finalOutput)` (camelCase) before DSPy.ai's snake_case rename to `CraftRedactedRequest` / `RespondToQuery`; (9) `self.prompt_creater` typo (sic — fingerprint for code-origin tracking; DSPy.ai fixed to `craft_redacted_request`); (10) the `gptResponse` field on the failure-mode `Prediction` baking the GPT-4o-mini choice into the type system (DSPy.ai generalized to `llm_response`); (11) `JudgeLeakage` celebrity-name exclusion clause — domain heuristic absent from gepa_papillon judge; (12) interactive `while True: input(...)` REPL as DSPy compound-AI-system inference demo; (13) first-publication of `compute_overall_score = (quality + (1 − leakage)) / 2` — canonical PAPILLON reward formula both later DSPy.ai tutorials inherit; (14) pre-optimized prompt artifact shipped as reproducibility deliverable; (15) [[SGLang]] serving a DSPy compound AI program in a tutorial-grade receipt ([[SGLang]] was previously documented only abstractly via [[dspy-language-models]]); (16) [[Llama|Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct]] as a DSPy PAPILLON student (paper-spec stack); (17) Trust No Bot (arXiv:2407.11438) as upstream of PUPA's `pupa_tnb` config. **Cross-receipt vs DSPy.ai variants**: this Colab uses MIPROv2 + Llama-3.1-8B + SGLang + GPT-4o-mini; [[dspy-tutorial-rl-papillon|rl_papillon]] uses ArborGRPO + Qwen2.5-1.5B; [[dspy-tutorial-gepa-papillon|gepa_papillon]] uses GEPA + GPT-4.1-Nano. Cross-tutorial Signature-fingerprinting now documented via the field-name dictionary on [[papillon-colab-tutorial]]. **Contradictions flagged**: naming drift across the three tutorials (same I/O contract); paper-vs-tutorial `PUPA-TNB` vs `PUPA-New` self-disclosed gap; no printed headline number; GPT-4o-mini three-role collapse entangling optimization signal with untrusted-external surface; `gptResponse` field name baking GPT into the type system. **Scope-limit gaps**: no comparison to GEPA / ArborGRPO on the same Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct setup; no `max_bootstrapped_demos` sweep; no save/load receipt for the optimized PAPILLON (only paper-era `loaded_papillon.load(...)`); no `auto` preset sweep; no cost / latency / VRAM disclosure; `PORT_NUMBER = 7501` magic constant; `flashinfer` cu121/torch2.4 wheel-index brittleness; no streaming / async / observability composition. Updates [[PAPILLON]] / [[PUPA]] / [[MIPROv2]] / [[SGLang]] sources frontmatter in place; no new pages minted.
- [DSPy Tutorial — Online RL over a Multi-Module DSPy Program (PAPILLON + ArborGRPO)](sources/dspy-tutorial-rl-papillon.md) — Official [[DSPy]] tutorial at `https://dspy.ai/tutorials/rl_papillon/` — **the wiki's first receipt of [[grpo|GRPO]]-style online [[reinforcementlearning|reinforcement learning]] applied to a *multi-module* [[CompoundAISystem|compound AI system]]** via DSPy's `dspy.GRPO` / [[ArborGRPO]] compiler. Trains a tiny 1.5B-parameter local LM inside the two-module [[PAPILLON]] privacy-preserving delegation program (`dspy.ChainOfThought(CraftRedactedRequest)` → external untrusted LLM → `dspy.Predict(RespondToQuery)`) on the [[PUPA]] benchmark, optimizing a composite `(quality + (1 − leakage)) / 2` reward via an [[LLMJudge]] of dual `JudgeQuality` + `JudgeLeakage` modules. Devset composite lifts **54.6 → 60.0** in ~3 h on 4× [[NVIDIA|H100]] using [[lora|LoRA]] (rank-8, α=16, all attention + MLP projections), [[DAPO|`loss_type="dapo"`]], `beta=0.0` (no [[KLPenalty|KL]]), bf16, `lr=1e-6`, 500 train steps × 4 examples × 8 samples = 16,000 rollouts. Authors explicit: *"new and extremely EXPERIMENTAL"*, *"typically worse on cost/quality basis than"* conventional prompt optimization, *"a solid start for online RL over arbitrary LM programs for tiny LMs."* **Bookends the wiki's GRPO coverage**: contrast with [[hf-llm-course-ch12-reasoning-models|HF LLM Course Ch 12]]'s single-module `GRPOTrainer` on [[GSM8K]] (verifiable reward) and [[2507.19457-gepa|GEPA paper]]'s argument that on PUPA itself GEPA reaches **91.85** vs GRPO's **86.66** with up to 35× fewer rollouts — i.e. the *same* program / benchmark / RL-vs-prompt pairing the GEPA paper used to argue *against* GRPO for compound systems. **Mints 4 concept pages** ([[PAPILLON]], [[ArborGRPO]], [[DAPO]], [[LLMJudge]]) + **1 entity page** ([[Arbor]]); updates [[PUPA]] / [[grpo]] / [[DSPyOptimizers]] in place.
- [DSPy Tutorial — Email Information Extraction](sources/dspy-email-extraction-tutorial.md) — Official [[DSPy]] tutorial that builds an **email triage pipeline** composing **four [[DSPySignatures|Signatures]] under [[chainofthought|`dspy.ChainOfThought`]]** inside a single [[DSPyModules|`dspy.Module`]] subclass (`EmailProcessor`) — `ClassifyEmail` → `ExtractEntities` → `SummarizeEmail` → `GenerateActionItems` — wired in a sequential diamond-shaped `forward(...)` with **typed inter-Signature handoffs**: `classifier.email_type: EmailType` and `classifier.urgency: UrgencyLevel` flow into both `entity_extractor` and `action_generator`; `entity_extractor.key_entities: list[ExtractedEntity]` flows into both `summarizer` and `action_generator`. Final output is a 12-kwarg [[DSPyPrediction|`dspy.Prediction`]] fan-in aggregator — the largest in the wiki's DSPy tutorial corpus. **Eleventh wiki-corpus DSPy tutorial**; **largest multi-Signature single-Module pipeline in the corpus** — four Signatures with strict sequential pipeline data-flow. **First wiki-corpus DSPy tutorial to use an Python `Enum` type as both OutputField *and* InputField across Signature boundaries** — `EmailType` (8-value `str, Enum`) and `UrgencyLevel` (4-value `str, Enum`) cross every sub-Signature boundary, confirming the [[dspy-signatures|Signatures page's]] five-tier type system composes symmetrically across Signatures. **First wiki-corpus DSPy receipt to use `Optional[T]` in an OutputField** (`financial_amount: Optional[float]`, `deadline: Optional[str]`) — declaring nullable outputs the LM is expected to set to `None` when not applicable. **First wiki-corpus DSPy receipt embedding LM-self-reported confidence scores in a structured output** — `class ExtractedEntity(BaseModel): entity_type: str; value: str; confidence: float` — a [[ModelCalibration|calibration]]-adjacent surface that DSPy's metric / evaluation machinery does not yet tool. Programming-stage-only receipt — single LM (`openai/gpt-4o-mini`), no [[DSPyOptimizers|Optimizer]], no [[DSPyMetrics|metric]], no eval set, no quantitative accuracy claim. Sibling to [[dspy-ai-text-game-tutorial]] (3 Signatures inside `GameAI`) and [[dspy-sample-code-generation-tutorial]] (2 Signatures inside `DocumentationLearningAgent`) on the **multi-Signature single-Module Programming-stage rung**. Demo emails cover order-confirmation / support-request / meeting-invitation triplet — exercising the urgency-classification surface across `LOW` / `CRITICAL` / `MEDIUM`. Two minor internal tutorial-side inconsistencies flagged: `financial_amount: Optional[float]` has `desc` example *"e.g., `'$99.99'`"* (string example for a float field — Adapter absorbs the parsing); `os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"]` is set *after* `dspy.configure(lm=lm)` (works because [[LiteLLM]] reads env var at LM-invocation time, but reversed from canonical pattern in [[dspy-language-models|page 3]]). Soft-tension flagged: user-declared `reasoning: str` OutputField on `ClassifyEmail` **overlaps** [[chainofthought|`dspy.ChainOfThought`]]'s implicit `reasoning` field — first wiki-corpus DSPy receipt where the user-declared field name collides with a Module-injected field name. No new concept pages minted (all referenced DSPy primitives pre-exist); updates [[DSPy]] / [[chainofthought]] / [[DSPySignatures]] / [[DSPyModules]] / [[DSPyAdapters]] / [[Pydantic]] / [[EntityExtraction]] / [[Classification]] in place. No contradictions with the prior corpus.
- [DSPy Tutorial — llms.txt Generation from GitHub Repositories](sources/dspy-llms-txt-generation-tutorial.md) — Official [[DSPy]] tutorial that builds a **repo-to-[[LLMsTxt|`llms.txt`]] generator** — a [[DSPyModules|`dspy.Module`]] subclass (`RepositoryAnalyzer`) composing **three custom class-form [[DSPySignatures|Signatures]] plus one inline Signature** under [[chainofthought|`dspy.ChainOfThought`]] across a four-stage `forward()`: `AnalyzeRepository` (URL + README + tree → purpose + key concepts + architecture) → `AnalyzeCodeStructure` (tree + package configs → directories + entry points + dev info) → `dspy.ChainOfThought("repo_info -> usage_examples")` (inline string-form synthesis stage) → `GenerateLLMsTxt` (7-input synthesis → final markdown). **Inverts the documentation-to-code direction of [[dspy-sample-code-generation-tutorial]]**: there docs were the input and code was the output; here a repo is the input and structured LLM-targeted documentation is the output. Worked example is `stanfordnlp/dspy` itself — DSPy generating `llms.txt` *about* DSPy. **First wiki-corpus DSPy tutorial mixing class-form and inline string-form Signatures inside the same `dspy.Module`** (containers in I/O force class form on three of four; the third sub-Module's `str -> str` shape permits inline). **First wiki receipt of the [[LLMsTxt|`llms.txt`]] proposal as a concrete generation target**, treated as "a proposed standard for providing structured, LLM-friendly documentation about a project" — the tutorial does not cite the originating proposal. **First DSPy tutorial using the GitHub REST API as the canonical pre-LLM data source** — three plain Python helpers (`get_github_file_tree`, `get_github_file_content`, `gather_repository_info`) over the recursive tree request + base64-decoded contents endpoint produce the `(file_tree, readme_content, package_files)` tuple consumed by the Module; mirrors the [[dspy-sample-code-generation-tutorial|HTML-to-markdown-via-html2text]] pre-call pattern with GitHub-structured repos in place of arbitrary URLs. **Widest input fan-in in any DSPy tutorial Signature on record — 7 fields on `GenerateLLMsTxt`** (two `list[str]`, five `str`), operating as a structured-aggregation synthesis Signature. Generated `llms.txt` includes project overview, key concepts, architecture organization, important files and directories, and **five canonical usage-example categories**: classifier building, [[rag|RAG]] pipelines, prompt optimization, agent loops, compositional code — themselves a small ontology that maps onto the existing DSPy tutorial corpus clusters. LM is `gpt-4o-mini` via `dspy.LM(model="gpt-4o-mini")` + `dspy.configure(lm=lm)`. **Programming-stage-only receipt** — exits at rung 1 of [[DSPyProgrammingModel|the three-stage workflow]]; no [[DSPyOptimizers|Optimizer]], no [[DSPyMetrics|metric]], no eval set, no measurement of generated `llms.txt` quality. Sibling to [[dspy-ai-text-game-tutorial]] (3 Signatures), [[dspy-sample-code-generation-tutorial]] (2 Signatures), and [[dspy-email-extraction-tutorial]] (4 Signatures) on the **multi-Signature single-Module Programming-stage rung** — this tutorial extends the count to *4 sub-Modules with mixed Signature forms*. Mints two new concept pages — [[LLMsTxt]] and [[GitHubAPI]]. **Scope-limit gaps**: `llms.txt` proposal not source-attributed; no measured quality of generated output; no [[DSPyOptimizers|Optimizer]] applied; no GitHub API rate-limit / auth / truncation discussion; no prompt-injection hardening for arbitrary repo READMEs ingested into LM context; the `generate_examples` stage manually f-string-concatenates `purpose + concepts` into one input field, losing typed I/O for that stage; no caching layer for the deterministic analysis stages. No contradictions with the prior corpus.
- [DSPy Tutorial — Sample Code Generation from Documentation](sources/dspy-sample-code-generation-tutorial.md) — Official [[DSPy]] tutorial that builds a **documentation-powered code generation system** — a [[DSPyModules|`dspy.Module`]] subclass (`DocumentationLearningAgent`) composing **two custom [[DSPySignatures|Signatures]] under [[chainofthought|`dspy.ChainOfThought`]]** (`LibraryAnalyzer` for documentation analysis, `CodeGenerator` for code synthesis) and fronted by an external HTTP-fetching layer (`requests` + `BeautifulSoup` + `html2text`) that turns any documentation URL into clean markdown before any LM call. The worked examples are [[FastAPI]] and Streamlit; the canonical output is a JWT-authentication FastAPI snippet with explanation + best-practices list. **First wiki-corpus DSPy tutorial whose central task is *code generation from documentation*** — a meta-programming application distinct from RAG, agents, NER, math, conversation, and interactive fiction; **first DSPy tutorial naming `requests` + `beautifulsoup4` + `html2text` as the canonical web-scraping pre-LLM transformation triple**. Programming-stage-only receipt — sibling to [[dspy-ai-text-game-tutorial]]; no [[DSPyOptimizers|Optimizer]], no [[DSPyMetrics|metric]], no eval set, no LM named. **The two-Signature decomposition is the structural payoff** — `LibraryAnalyzer` is use-case-independent (cacheable per library) and `CodeGenerator` sees structured analysis rather than raw HTML, echoing [[dspy-custom-module|the custom-module tutorial's]] 3-stage `generate_query → retrieve → generate_answer` RAG template as the canonical DSPy idiom for non-trivial multi-stage pipelines. **Demonstrates the *rapid technology adoption* use case** the tutorial names explicitly. Dependency footprint: 4 packages — second-smallest in the wiki's DSPy tutorial corpus after [[dspy-ai-text-game-tutorial|the text-game tutorial's]] 3. Promotes [[FastAPI]] from a 1-line stub to its second corpus appearance (as the *subject* of LM-driven analysis rather than the implementation of an ML serving layer); seeds forward references for [[Streamlit]], [[BeautifulSoup]], [[html2text]]. **Scope-limit gaps**: no full code transcript on the rendered page (Signature class bodies inferred from prose), no LM specified, no quality measurement, no [[DSPyOptimizers|Optimizer]] proposed, no caching layer for the reusable analysis stage, no prompt-injection / supply-chain discussion for arbitrary-URL ingestion. No new concept pages minted — every DSPy primitive used pre-exists. No contradictions with the prior corpus.
- [DSPy Tutorial — Math Reasoning](sources/dspy-tutorial-math.md) — **Sixth wiki-corpus [[DSPy]] tutorial** and the **first benchmarked on a math-reasoning dataset**. Single-line program `dspy.ChainOfThought("question -> answer")` over the [[MATH-benchmark|MATH]] algebra subset (350+350), [[GPT|GPT-4o-mini]] student + [[GPT|GPT-4o]] teacher, [[MIPROv2|`dspy.MIPROv2(auto="medium")`]] with `max_bootstrapped_demos=4, max_labeled_demos=4`. **Lift: 74.0% → 88.57%** (+14.6 pts absolute, ~20% relative). **Fifth wiki receipt for MIPROv2 `auto="medium"`** — now spans RAG (StackExchange 53→61, RAG-QA Arena Tech 55.5→61.1), ReAct agents (HoVer 8→41.67), NER (CoNLL-2003 86→93), and symbolic math (MATH-algebra 74→88.57). **First wiki receipt where [[chainofthought|CoT]] is the entire program** — no retrieval, no tools, no history. Introduces `dspy.datasets.MATH(subset='algebra')` as an in-framework dataset loader.
- [DSPy Tutorial — Classification Fine-tuning (Banking77 via Local Llama-3.2-1B)](sources/dspy-tutorial-classification-finetuning.md) — Official [[DSPy]] tutorial at `https://dspy.ai/tutorials/classification_finetuning/` (`docs/docs/tutorials/classification_finetuning/index.ipynb`). **The wiki's first end-to-end runnable receipt of [[BootstrapFinetune|`dspy.BootstrapFinetune`]]** — the only weight-tuning optimizer in [[DSPyOptimizers|the catalog]] — and the **first DSPy tutorial whose output is a fine-tuned local open-weights model** rather than a prompt-optimized program. Distills a `dspy.ChainOfThought(f"text -> label: Literal{{CLASSES}}")` classifier from a [[GPT|GPT-4o-mini]] teacher into a locally-served [[Llama|Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct]] student on the **77-way [[Banking77]] intent classification task** (PolyAI dataset). **Two-stage receipt** — stage A bootstraps from **500 unlabeled** examples (no metric filter) → **51.5%** dev accuracy; stage B bootstraps from **500 labeled** examples with a `lambda x, y, trace=None: x.label == y.label` metric filter → **86.7%** dev accuracy. **Headline cross-model result**: the fine-tuned 1B student (86.7%) outperforms the GPT-4o-mini teacher (55%) by **+31.7 absolute / +57.6% relative** on the same 100-item devset — **a ~50× smaller open-weights model beats its API teacher** through metric-filtered bootstrap distillation, an *inverted* knowledge-distillation pattern. **First wiki receipts within this tutorial**: end-to-end `dspy.BootstrapFinetune(...)` invocation with `metric=` filter; `dspy.settings.experimental = True` as a hard precondition for weight-space optimization; `dspy.clients.lm_local.LocalProvider()` + `openai/local:<hf-model-id>` model-prefix idiom for [[SGLang]]-backed local serving; explicit `.launch()` / `.kill()` lifecycle on the fine-tuned LM between Stage A and Stage B; `DSPY_FINETUNEDIR` environment variable as a first-class DSPy knob (with `DSPY_CACHEDIR` fallback) alongside `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`; the full `train_kwargs` surface for local-LM fine-tuning (`device`, `use_peft`, `num_train_epochs`, `per_device_train_batch_size`, `gradient_accumulation_steps`, `learning_rate`, `max_seq_length`, `packing`, `bf16`, `output_dir`) passed through to the [[HuggingFaceTRL|TRL SFTTrainer]]; the `transformers==4.48.3` version pin justified inline by linking to <https://github.com/huggingface/trl/issues/2338>; the second wiki receipt of `program.deepcopy()` + `program.set_lm(lm)` (used twice — student + teacher in the same program). **Second wiki Banking77 BFT receipt** — completes the matrix begun by the [[dspy-optimizers|page 13]] narrative receipt: that one was **API self-distillation** (GPT-4o-mini → fine-tuned GPT-4o-mini, with the `hint`-as-input training-time trick, 2000 examples, 66 → 87%); this one is **cross-model open-weights distillation** (GPT-4o-mini teacher → fine-tuned local Llama-3.2-1B student, no hint trick, 500 examples, 51.5 / 55 → 86.7%). **Both converge on ~87% post-BFT within 0.3 points** despite radically different inference and fine-tuning substrates — concrete evidence that BFT's metric-filter mechanism dominates the substrate choice on closed-set classification. **Third local-weight-tuning DSPy tutorial** after [[dspy-tutorial-rl-papillon]] and [[dspy-rl-multihop-tutorial]] — fills the **supervised** weight-tuning branch (SFT-via-TRL+PEFT) alongside the **RL** weight-tuning branch (GRPO-via-Arbor) the prior two established. **SGLang is the common inference substrate** — direct via `LocalProvider` here; indirect via [[Arbor]] in the GRPO tutorials. **Twenty-ninth wiki-corpus DSPy tutorial.** Mints 2 entity pages ([[Banking77]], [[PolyAI]]); updates [[BootstrapFinetune]] (second runnable receipt + cross-architecture reconciliation table), [[DSPyOptimizers]] (third optimizer-family-end-to-end receipt), [[DSPyLM]] (`LocalProvider` + `openai/local:` prefix surface), [[SGLang]] (first DSPy-fine-tuning receipt), [[HuggingFaceTRL]] / [[HuggingFacePEFT]] / [[Llama]] (Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct student receipt) / [[meta]] / [[KnowledgeDistillation]] (student-beats-teacher inverted-distillation receipt) / [[chainofthought]] / [[MLflow]] (first MLflow save/load of a weight-tuned DSPy program) / [[Ollama]] (named as future fine-tuned-model inference substrate) / [[Classification]] / [[FineTuning]] / [[SupervisedFinetuning]] sources frontmatter in place. **Scope-limit gaps**: no cost / wall-time / VRAM disclosure; no `train_kwargs` sweep; no `use_peft=True` / LoRA ablation (headline 86.7% is full-parameter SFT); no MIPROv2-vs-BFT head-to-head on the same task; no `BetterTogether` composition; no multi-seed variance; no alternative student / teacher pairing; no SFT-dataset-composition analysis; no checkpoint resumption (Stage B re-trains from `student_lm` from scratch); no plain `program.save/load` receipt for the fine-tuned program (only MLflow path shown); no Ollama deployment (explicitly flagged as future work).
- [DSPy Tutorial — GEPA for Facility Support Analyzer (Structured Information Extraction)](sources/dspy-tutorial-gepa-facility-support-analyzer.md) — Official [[DSPy]] tutorial at `https://dspy.ai/tutorials/gepa_facilitysupportanalyzer/`. **Second wiki-corpus end-to-end runnable receipt of [[GEPA|`dspy.GEPA`]]** after [[dspy-tutorial-gepa-aime]] — extends the GEPA envelope from single-Signature math reasoning to **three-Signature enterprise classification**. Three sibling [[chainofthought|`dspy.ChainOfThought`]] predictors (`urgency_module` 3-way, `sentiment_module` 3-way, `categories_module` 10-way multi-label `List[Literal[...]]`) inside one custom `dspy.Module` (`FacilitySupportAnalyzerMM`) over the Meta-released [[FacilitySupportAnalyzer]] dataset (200 ProCare facility-support emails, 66/66/68 split shuffled with `random.Random(0)`). **Asymmetric two-model pair** — [[GPT|GPT-4.1 nano]] student (`openai/gpt-4.1-nano`, `temperature=1`) reflected on by [[GPT|GPT-5]] (`temperature=1.0`, `max_tokens=32000`); **first wiki receipt of the `gpt-4.1-nano` student tier** (cheapest GPT-4.1 model). `dspy.GEPA(metric=metric_with_feedback, auto="light", num_threads=32, track_stats=True, use_merge=False, reflection_lm=...)`. **Headline lift: 75.4% → 87.0%** on the 68-item test set (`EvaluationResult(score=87.01, ...)`) — clean **+11.6-point absolute** improvement at `auto="light"`. **Three new disclosures to the wiki's GEPA documentation**: (1) **`use_merge` is an explicit `dspy.GEPA(...)` kwarg** — first wiki receipt of the [[SystemAwareMerge|GEPA+Merge]] toggle as a kwarg name; default-equivalent disabled here; (2) **GEPA mutates one predictor per iteration on multi-module programs** — log rotates through `urgency_module.predict` (iter 1, 4, 7, ...), `sentiment_module.predict` (iter 2, 5, 8, ...), `categories_module.predict` (iter 3, 6, 9, ...), instead of rewriting all sibling predictors in one mutation step; (3) **`pred_name`-routed [[FeedbackFunction|`metric_with_feedback`]]** — the canonical multi-module $\mu_f$ pattern: a single function branches on `pred_name in {'urgency_module.predict', 'sentiment_module.predict', 'categories_module.predict'}` to return predictor-specific failure analyses ([[FeedbackFunction|first wiki receipt of this pattern]]). **Evolved instructions shape**: three orthogonal decision frameworks (one per predictor) rather than one mega-prompt — urgency frame (safety/risk + operational impact + time sensitivity + tone-vs-intent); sentiment frame (explicit emotional language vs polite formality + tone dominance); categories frame (strict evidence + scheduling-vs-complaint disambiguation + specialized-vs-routine cleaning + multi-label). **First wiki receipt of GEPA producing parallel sibling instructions** rather than one consolidated playbook ([[dspy-tutorial-gepa-aime|the AIME tutorial]]'s ~120-line single playbook is the contrast). **Pareto-front receipt**: 9 specialist programs retained alongside aggregate-best program 17 in the printed Graphviz DAG (`find_dominator_programs(...)`); programs 19 (0.74) and 21 (0.77) sit **below the un-optimized baseline** (0.72) on aggregate yet remain on the per-instance front — **concrete receipt that [[ParetoBasedCandidateSelection|specialist retention]] keeps programs with strictly worse aggregate than baseline**. Best validation candidate is program 17 at iter 35 (valset 0.8626 = 86.3%); 22 candidates total (0–21); 86% plateau reached at iter 6 (program 4) and held for 29 iterations before program 17 cleared by 0.0015 points. **First wiki documentation of the `detailed_results` surface** (`candidates`, `parents`, `val_aggregate_scores`, `val_subscores`, `per_val_instance_best_candidates`, `discovery_eval_counts`, `best_outputs_valset`, `best_idx`, `best_candidate`) and the `dag_to_dot(...)` Graphviz-DOT trajectory visualization recipe. **First wiki receipt of `display_table=True`** on `dspy.Evaluate(...)` printing a per-example results table after `evaluate(...)` returns. Closing line: *"GEPA was able to optimize GPT-4.1 nano's performance from 75% score to 87% in the auto='light' setting."* Mints 1 concept page ([[FacilitySupportAnalyzer]]); updates [[GEPA]] (third runnable receipt + three-tutorial envelope table), [[FeedbackFunction]] (multi-predictor routing section + `pred_name` switch worked example), [[ReflectivePromptMutation]] (multi-module rotation section + parallel sibling artifacts), [[ParetoBasedCandidateSelection]] (specialist-retention receipt + 9-program front DAG), [[Classification]] / [[chainofthought]] / [[DSPyOptimizers]] / [[DSPyEvaluate]] / [[DSPyMetrics]] / [[DSPyPredict]] / [[meta]] in place. **Scope-limit gaps**: no cost disclosure (same break as [[dspy-tutorial-gepa-aime]]); no `auto="medium"`/`"heavy"` comparison despite the explicit recommendation in the inline callout; no reflection-LM ablation; no save/load receipt; no MIPROv2-vs-GEPA comparison on the same task; no streaming/async/observability composition; no baseline-prompt printout (only the docstrings); `use_merge=True` ablation not run.
- [DSPy Tutorial — GEPA for AIME (Math)](sources/dspy-tutorial-gepa-aime.md) — Official [[DSPy]] tutorial at `https://dspy.ai/tutorials/gepa_aime/` (`docs/docs/tutorials/gepa_aime/index.ipynb`). **The wiki's first runnable end-to-end receipt of [[GEPA|`dspy.GEPA`]]** — the reflection-driven instruction optimizer from [[2507.19457-gepa]]. Optimizes a single-line `dspy.ChainOfThought("problem -> answer")` (one-sentence baseline instruction) on [[AIME2025|AIME-2025]] math problems with a **two-model asymmetric pair** — [[GPT|GPT-4.1 Mini]] student (`temperature=1, max_tokens=32000`) reflected on by [[GPT|GPT-5]] (`temperature=1.0, max_tokens=32000`) — using `auto="light"`, `num_threads=32`, `track_stats=True`, `reflection_minibatch_size=3`. **Headline lift: 46.7% → 56.7%** on the 150-item test set (AIME-2025 oversampled 5× for statistical stability) — a clean **+10-point absolute** improvement at the smallest budget setting. **First wiki quantification of `auto="light"`**: GEPA's logger prints *"approx 560 metric calls of the program. This amounts to 6.22 full evals on the train+val set"* — i.e. ≈6 full-evaluation budget on a 45/45 train/val split (consistent with the [[GEPA|GEPA-exempt 50/50 split]] from [[DSPyOptimization|page 12]]). Runs 22 iterations (0–21); iter 5 produces the **best validation candidate** (24/45 = 53.3%) that remains on the linear pareto front for the rest of the run. **Concrete instance of [[ParetoBasedCandidateSelection|per-instance Pareto vs aggregate divergence]]**: iter 12's candidate maxed the valset pareto-front to 0.80 while aggregate score stayed 0.42 — receipt that GEPA keeps specialist programs that solve problems no other program does. The **evolved [[ReflectivePromptMutation|reflection artifact]]** is the wiki's first concrete view of what GEPA produces: a ~120-line structured "playbook" with I/O contract, six numbered domain-specific strategy modules (base conversion, palindromes across bases, symmetric sums, intersecting subset families, AP avoidance, order statistics), and a quality-check checklist — synthesized by GPT-5 reading per-example failures + the full step-by-step contest solutions returned via the [[FeedbackFunction|`metric_with_feedback` channel]]. **Canonical instance of the feedback-function $\mu_f$ supervision**: when the training example has a `solution` field, `metric_with_feedback` returns `dspy.Prediction(score=int, feedback=<full multi-page contest solution + "Think about what takeaways you can learn">)` — the non-metric textual channel the [[2507.19457-gepa|GEPA paper]] formalizes. **Cross-receipt convergence with the paper**: paper Table 1 reports GPT-4.1 Mini × AIME-2025 baseline 45.33 → GEPA 59.33; this tutorial reports 46.7 → 56.7 at the smaller `light` budget — qualitative replication of the headline ±3-point delta consistent with the budget cut. **First wiki receipt of**: `dspy.GEPA(...)` invocation with all kwargs (`metric`, `auto`, `num_threads`, `track_stats`, `reflection_minibatch_size`, `reflection_lm`); the `optimized_program.predict.signature.instructions` inspection path; [[GPT|GPT-5]] as a reflection LM in DSPy; `metric_with_feedback` shape returning solution text as supervision; the `auto="light"` budget quantification. Sibling to [[dspy-tutorial-math]] — same program shape (`dspy.ChainOfThought` + math benchmark), different optimizer ([[MIPROv2]] vs [[GEPA]]) and harder benchmark (MATH-algebra vs AIME). Updates [[GEPA]] / [[AIME2025]] / [[ReflectivePromptMutation]] / [[FeedbackFunction]] / [[ParetoBasedCandidateSelection]] sources frontmatter in place; no new concept pages minted (all referenced GEPA primitives pre-existed from [[2507.19457-gepa]]). Scope gaps: no cost disclosure (breaking the prior tutorial convention), no `auto="medium"` / `"heavy"` comparison, no reflection-LM ablation, no save/load receipt, no per-iteration mutation-diff visualization.
- [DSPy Tutorial — GEPA for Privacy-Conscious Delegation (PAPILLON)](sources/dspy-tutorial-gepa-papillon.md) — Official [[DSPy]] tutorial at `https://dspy.ai/tutorials/gepa_papillon/`. **Second wiki-corpus runnable receipt of [[GEPA|`dspy.GEPA`]]** after [[dspy-tutorial-gepa-aime]], and **first GEPA receipt on a non-math task / compound (multi-Signature) program / LLM-judge composite reward**. Optimizes the two-module [[PAPILLON]] system on the [[PUPA]] benchmark with a **three-tier asymmetric model stack** — `openai/gpt-4.1-nano` (local student) + `openai/gpt-4.1-mini` (untrusted external) + `openai/gpt-4.1` (reflection LM) — at the smallest budget setting (`max_full_evals=1`). **Headline lift: 76.5% → 86.1%** composite (`(quality + (1 − leakage)) / 2`) on the 214-item test set (163.71 → 184.26 metric points; **+9.6 absolute / +12.5% relative**). **Companion to [[dspy-tutorial-rl-papillon]]** — same program + benchmark family, weight-space [[ArborGRPO]] receipt — the wiki now has its **first side-by-side prompt-space vs weight-space pairing** on the same compound AI program (not directly head-to-head: rl_papillon uses `pupa_new` only with 225/225/450, gepa_papillon uses `pupa_tnb`+`pupa_new` with 225/225/214). **First wiki receipts within this tutorial**: `max_full_evals` integer budget knob (distinct from the `auto={"light","medium","heavy"}` enum [[dspy-tutorial-gepa-aime|gepa_aime]] used); `track_best_outputs=True` GEPA kwarg; three-tier asymmetric model stack with a separate *untrusted external* role; GEPA on a multi-Signature compound program; GEPA with an LLM-judge composite reward; **per-axis decomposition feedback text** as a [[FeedbackFunction|$\mu_f$]] shape — `compute_overall_score_with_feedback` exposes the two reward axes (quality, leakage) separately in the feedback string, giving the reflection LM explicit credit-assignment signal between known axes (distinct from [[dspy-tutorial-gepa-aime|gepa_aime]]'s dense-narrative contest-solution $\mu_f$ — paper source-category 1 vs source-category 4); `gpt-4.1-nano` as a DSPy student (wiki's smallest GPT-4.1-family DSPy student); `gpt-4.1` (full, non-mini, non-nano) as a reflection LM in DSPy; PAPILLON GEPA training receipt at tutorial-grade scale (the [[2507.19457-gepa|paper]] reports paper-scale GEPA on PUPA at Qwen3 8B / GPT-4.1 Mini cells only); the `pupa_tnb` PUPA split (prior PUPA receipts named only `pupa_new`). **Cross-receipt convergence with [[2507.19457-gepa|the paper]]**: paper Table 4 reports GPT-4.1 Mini × PUPA as 74.18 → 94.47 (plain GEPA) / 96.46 (GEPA+Merge); this tutorial reports 76.5 → 86.1 at GPT-4.1 Nano × `max_full_evals=1` — smaller absolute optimized number consistent with the smaller student capacity + budget cut. **Confirms the [[LLMJudge]] pattern is optimizer-agnostic** — same Module slots into both [[ArborGRPO]] RL reward and GEPA scoring metric without API changes. Updates [[GEPA]] / [[PAPILLON]] / [[PUPA]] / [[LLMJudge]] / [[FeedbackFunction]] sources frontmatter in place; no new concept pages minted (all referenced primitives pre-existed from [[2507.19457-gepa]] / [[dspy-tutorial-rl-papillon]] / [[dspy-tutorial-gepa-aime]]). Contradictions flagged: PUPA split discrepancy with rl_papillon (non-overlapping test sets — composite numbers not on the same metric base); `RespondToQuery` Signature docstring drift across tutorials (same I/O contract); continuing cost-disclosure gap.
