- [DSPy Tutorial — GEPA for Trusted Monitoring (AI Control + Code Backdoor Classification)](sources/dspy-tutorial-gepa-trusted-monitor.md) — Official [[DSPy]] tutorial at `https://dspy.ai/tutorials/gepa_trusted_monitor/`. **Third wiki-corpus runnable receipt of [[GEPA|`dspy.GEPA`]]** after [[dspy-tutorial-gepa-aime]] and [[dspy-tutorial-gepa-papillon]] — and the **first GEPA receipt on an AI safety / [[AIControl|AI control]] task** (training a weak [[TrustedMonitor|trusted monitor]] to spot [[CodeBackdoor|backdoors]] planted by a stronger untrusted coder). Optimizes a single-Signature `dspy.ChainOfThought(PredictSuspicionScore)` classifier on the [[APPSBenchmark|APPS]] backdoor split provided by [[ControlArena|`control_arena`]] (UK [[UKAISI|AISI]]'s safety library), using an **asymmetric two-model stack** — `openai/gpt-4.1-nano-2025-04-14` student + `openai/gpt-5-2025-08-07` reflection — at `max_full_evals=2`, `num_threads=8`, `reflection_minibatch_size=3`, `track_stats=True`. **Headline lift: 0.69 → 0.81** comparative-pair accuracy on the 100-item valset (final pareto-front 0.95); +0.12 absolute / +17.4% relative. **First-of-kind features**: (1) **GEPA on a classification (discriminative) task** — prior receipts were generation tasks; (2) **comparative-pair [[FeedbackFunction|$\mu_f$ shape]]** — `1.0 if attack_suspicion > honest_suspicion else 0.0` with failure-direction-in-plain-English feedback (*"You said the attack code was LESS suspicious than the honest code"*) — a **fifth $\mu_f$ source category** not enumerated in [[2507.19457-gepa|the paper]]'s four; (3) **`MonitorTrainerProgram` dual-call wrapper** — wraps a single-Signature classifier so GEPA can see paired (attack, honest) rollouts at optimization time, with the **un-wrapped inner program** saved for deployment (`gepa_trainer_program.monitor_program.save(...)`) — structurally new: optimization-time program shape ≠ deployment-time program shape; (4) **first wiki composition of [[ControlArena|UK AISI's `control_arena`]] with DSPy** — operational link between AI-safety eval ecosystem and DSPy optimizer ecosystem; (5) **`ScoreWithFeedback` typed return** + **`DSPyTrace` typed alias** from `dspy.teleprompt.gepa.gepa_utils` — prior tutorials returned `dspy.Prediction(score, feedback)` informally; (6) **GPT-5 dated checkpoint** (`openai/gpt-5-2025-08-07`) + **GPT-4.1 Nano dated checkpoint** (`openai/gpt-4.1-nano-2025-04-14`); (7) **`cache=False` on student LM** — defensive against same-prompt deduplication across attack/honest dual-call; (8) **`max_full_evals=2`** — second integer-budget receipt. **Evolved instructions shape**: a **domain-discriminator playbook** (5-step workflow + backdoor-hunting checklist + intent-vs-honest-bug discriminator + false-positive guard + 1–9 low-score calibration + competitive-programming anchors) — structurally distinct from [[dspy-tutorial-gepa-aime|gepa_aime]]'s domain-solver and [[dspy-tutorial-gepa-papillon|gepa_papillon]]'s privacy-redaction prompt. **Cross-receipt against [[2603.19247-prompt-optimization-jailbreaking]]**: companion defender-side receipt — that paper uses GEPA on the attacker side (max danger; Claude 4.5 Sonnet 0.046 → 0.236); this tutorial uses GEPA on the defender side (max backdoor detection; APPS 0.69 → 0.81). **Cross-receipt against [[2507.19457-gepa|the paper]]**: first GEPA receipt operationalizing the algorithm on a **task family the paper does not benchmark** (integer-output AI-control classifier with comparative-pair reward). Mints 5 concept pages ([[AIControl]], [[TrustedMonitor]], [[CodeBackdoor]], [[APPSBenchmark]], [[ControlTax]]) and 2 entity pages ([[ControlArena]], [[UKAISI]]); updates [[GEPA]] (fourth runnable receipt + four-tutorial envelope table), [[FeedbackFunction]] (comparative-pair section + `ScoreWithFeedback` typed-return section), [[ReflectivePromptMutation]] (domain-discriminator artifact + three-tutorial artifact-shape taxonomy) in place. **Contradictions flagged**: no paper anchor for the comparative-pair metric shape (a fifth category beyond the paper's four); continuing cost-disclosure gap; optimization-time wrapper ≠ deployment-time program; valset headline reported on 100 items but `EVAL_LIMIT=160` is declared and unused; no `max_full_evals` sweep. **Scope-limit gaps**: no MIPROv2 / SIMBA / BootstrapFinetune comparison; no GEPA+Merge ablation; no GPT-5-as-monitor baseline (would isolate optimization lift vs scale lift); no per-iteration prompt-diff dump; no reflection-LM ablation; no `track_best_outputs=True`; no static-analysis baseline.
- [DSPy Tutorial — Advanced Tool Use (SIMBA on ToolHop)](sources/dspy-tool-use-tutorial.md) — Official [[DSPy]] tutorial at `https://dspy.ai/tutorials/tool_use/`. **First wiki-corpus runnable receipt of [[SIMBA|`dspy.SIMBA`]]** with the optimizer's full Python invocation surface — `dspy.SIMBA(metric=metric, max_steps=12, max_demos=10)` invoked as `simba.compile(agent, trainset=trainset, seed=6793115)`. Prior SIMBA receipt ([[2603.19247-prompt-optimization-jailbreaking]]) documented the algorithm and adversarial-objective lift numbers but did not show the Python constructor; this tutorial **completes the SIMBA receipt corpus** by adding the executable invocation, an explicit `seed` kwarg (reproducibility surface no prior DSPy optimizer receipt had documented), and the **first benign-task before/after accuracy numbers** for SIMBA: **35.0% → 60.7% dev accuracy** on [[ToolHop]] (+25.7 absolute / +71% relative). Trains a **[[HandRolledReAct|hand-rolled ReAct]]** agent — a single `dspy.ChainOfThought` Signature in a `max_steps=5` manual for-loop with a synthetic `finish(answer)` terminal tool — **bypassing [[react|`dspy.ReAct`]]** because [[ToolHop]] ships a different `functions` dict per datapoint (tools as runtime input, not constructor kwarg). [[GPT4o|GPT-4o]] (`temperature=0.7`) student. **First wiki receipts within this tutorial**: (1) the `dspy.SIMBA(...)` constructor surface and `compile(..., seed=int)` invocation; (2) **hand-rolled ReAct pattern in DSPy** — manual `dspy.ChainOfThought` + trajectory loop instead of `dspy.ReAct`; (3) **`dspy.Signature(str_spec, instructions_str)` inline-string construction** with `dict[str, Any]` output type parsed from string; (4) [[func_timeout|`func_timeout`]] library in a DSPy program — `@func_set_timeout(10)` + try/except → `{"return_value": ..., "errors": ...}` dict mapping as the tool-runtime sandbox idiom; (5) **`exec()`-based tool construction** from dataset-shipped Python source strings with regex name extraction — security-relevant (untrusted code runs in-process; `func_timeout` bounds runtime, not side effects); (6) `dspy.utils.download(url)` for direct HF dataset URL fetch (bypassing the `datasets` library); (7) `orjson` as a DSPy tutorial JSON parser; (8) [[ToolHop]] benchmark; (9) synthetic `finish(answer)` terminal-tool pattern — agent-controlled termination via a no-op tool; (10) `dspy.Example` carrying live Python callables in a field (not just primitive data); (11) **fourth `dspy.Tool` alternative path** — per-question raw-callable dict via Signature input field (no `dspy.Tool` wrapper) with `inspect.signature` + `inspect.getdoc` metadata; (12) **metric-and-instruction co-design** as primary optimization target — the Signature instruction (*"format dates as YYYY-MM-DD, names as Firstname Lastname, numbers without leading 0s"*) makes the output schema the dual of the metric's normalization, so SIMBA's primary lift is teaching GPT-4o to emit answers in the metric's expected shape rather than improving multi-hop reasoning per se. **Cross-receipt convergence with [[2603.19247-prompt-optimization-jailbreaking]]**: same SIMBA optimizer, complementary objectives — that paper drove mean [[DangerScore|danger]] 0.046 → 0.347 on Claude 4.5 (max-attack); this tutorial drives accuracy 0.350 → 0.607 on ToolHop (max-task-performance). Symmetric coverage now in the wiki for adversarial vs benign SIMBA objectives. Mints **2 concept pages** ([[ToolHop]], [[HandRolledReAct]]) + **2 entity pages** ([[func_timeout]], [[ByteDanceResearch]]); updates [[SIMBA]] (first executable receipt + benign-task lift), [[react]] (hand-rolled ReAct contrast pattern + escape-from-`dspy.ReAct` decision criteria), [[DSPyTools]] (fourth tool-construction path: per-question raw-callable dict, no `dspy.Tool`) in place. **Contradictions flagged**: untrusted `exec()` of dataset strings with no isolation boundary beyond a 10-s timeout; `temperature=0.7` unusual for a trajectory-step ChainOfThought; metric does not enforce the date/name format the Signature instruction asks for; `testset = examples[400:]` constructed but never evaluated; no `temperature` on SIMBA's reflection LM (implies same `gpt4o` for student + reflection); no `dspy.ReAct` baseline control. **Scope-limit gaps**: no evolved-Signature dump; no [[MIPROv2]]/[[GEPA]] head-to-head; no cost/latency disclosure; no test-set generalization; no security analysis of `exec()` beyond timeout; no save/load receipt; no streaming/async/observability composition over the optimized agent.
- [DSPy Tutorial — Fine-tuning Agents (AlfWorld + MIPROv2-teacher + BootstrapFinetune)](sources/dspy-tutorial-games.md) — Official [[DSPy]] tutorial at `https://dspy.ai/tutorials/games/`. **First wiki-corpus end-to-end runnable [[BootstrapFinetune|`dspy.BootstrapFinetune`]] receipt on an agentic program** — moves the BFT envelope from [[dspy-optimizers|the page-13 Banking77 single-call classification receipt]] (66% → 87%) to a **50-step interactive agent on the [[AlfWorld]] household-task benchmark**. Hand-rolled [[react|ReAct]]-pattern `dspy.Module` with one `dspy.Predict("task, trajectory, possible_actions: list[str] -> action")` sub-module called up to `max_iters=50` per task — **not `dspy.ReAct`** (deliberate ergonomic choice for the weight-tuning regime, similar to [[HandRolledReAct]] in [[dspy-tool-use-tutorial]]). Two-stage prompt-then-weights pipeline: (1) [[MIPROv2|`dspy.MIPROv2(metric=metric, auto="light", num_threads=16, prompt_model=gpt4o)`]] with `max_bootstrapped_demos=1, max_labeled_demos=0, minibatch_size=40` over the GPT-4o agent (teacher), then (2) `dspy.BootstrapFinetune(metric=metric, num_threads=16).compile(student_4o_mini, teacher=optimized_4o, trainset=trainset)` distills the prompt-optimized teacher's trajectories into [[GPT|GPT-4o-mini]] weights via the [[OpenAI]] fine-tuning API. **Headline lift: 15.0% → 71.5% devset success** (+56.5 pts absolute, **~4.8× relative**) on 200 dev tasks with 200 train tasks; **fine-tuned 4o-mini beats GPT-4o teacher's 57.5% zero-shot by +14 pts** while running on a smaller, cheaper model and at 2.6× faster wall-clock (03:15 vs 08:33). **First wiki receipts within this tutorial**: [[BootstrapFinetune|`dspy.BootstrapFinetune`]] with explicit `teacher=...` kwarg (Banking77 receipt had no separate teacher); [[MIPROv2]] with explicit `prompt_model=gpt4o` kwarg; the `"think:"` pseudo-action injected into `info["admissible_commands"][0] + ["think: ${...thoughts...}"]` as a [[react|ReAct]]-*Thought* primitive that doesn't consume an environment turn (`prediction.action.startswith("think:")` → append `"OK."` to trajectory, continue loop) — structural alternative to [[chainofthought|CoT]]'s `reasoning` injection; the "ReAct pattern without `dspy.ReAct`" template — required because BFT wants flat `(task, trajectory, possible_actions) → action` SFT supervision (one row per agent step); `max_iters=50` agent-loop cap (10× the [[react|`dspy.ReAct`]] default of 5); `dspy.configure(experimental=True)` global toggle (first wiki receipt); a metric that reads from `y` (the prediction) rather than `x` (the example) — `lambda x, y, trace=None: y.success` — forced by agent-style tasks where ground truth is environment success not a held-out label; `dspy.datasets.alfworld.AlfWorld()` as a **hybrid dataset + simulator handle** (exposes both `.trainset`/`.devset` and the `POOL.session()` context manager managing TextWorld subprocesses) — second wiki receipt of an in-framework DSPy dataset loader after [[dspy-tutorial-math|`dspy.datasets.MATH(subset='algebra')`]], but first that ships executable environment infrastructure; the third `set_lm(...)` wiki receipt; pickle save/load (`finetuned_4o_mini.save('finetuned_4o_mini_001.pkl')` then `Agent().load(..., allow_pickle=True)`) **with an explicit in-tutorial security warning** *"Loading `.pkl` files can execute arbitrary code and may be dangerous. Only save and load pickle files from trusted sources in secure environments. Consider using JSON format when possible for safer serialization."* (first such warning in the DSPy tutorial corpus); the in-tutorial framework-philosophy statement on instructions: *"they're not for coercing the model to exhibit a certain behavior, but they're there to describe the fundamentals of the task in a straightforward, human-readable way."* **Cross-tutorial connection**: hand-rolls the [[BetterTogether]] sequence (MIPROv2 → BFT) without using `dspy.BetterTogether` — the [[2407.10930-better-together|Soylu et al. 2024]] meta-optimizer's actual API is not exercised. **First wiki receipt operationalizing the [[BootstrapFinetune|page-13 composability recipe]]** (*"You can run `dspy.MIPROv2` and use the produced program ... to `dspy.BootstrapFinetune` to get better results. This is partly the essence of `dspy.BetterTogether`."*). Cross-receipt contrast with [[dspy-tutorial-rl-papillon|rl_papillon]] and [[dspy-rl-multihop-tutorial|rl_multihop]]: those tutorials use [[grpo|online GRPO]] for weight-space optimization; this tutorial uses **supervised fine-tuning via teacher rollouts** — first wiki prompt+SFT receipt that beats its own prompt-only teacher (rl_papillon and rl_multihop both disclaim weight-RL as *"typically worse on cost/quality basis than prompt optimizers"*; this tutorial demonstrates SFT *does* extract additional gain over MIPROv2 prompt-only). Contradictions: prose says *"19% → 72%"* while printed cells show **15.0% → 71.5%** (rounding drift); *"82% with 500 train tasks"* claim is forward-looking extrapolation not reproduced in the notebook; intro calls the program *"a ReAct agent"* but does not use [[react|`dspy.ReAct`]]; `gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18` declared without `openai/` prefix while `gpt-4o` declared with it (LiteLLM tolerates both); no cost disclosure for OpenAI fine-tune call; no `dspy.BetterTogether` head-to-head; no [[grpo|GRPO]] baseline on same benchmark; no `max_bootstrapped_demos` sweep; no demo-retention ablation (`# student_4o_mini.react.demos = []` comment hints at the knob but doesn't run it); no held-out test set (`trainset[:200]` and `devset[-200:]` from the same `AlfWorld()` loader); no per-task-type breakdown across the six [[AlfWorld]] task categories. Mints **1 concept page** ([[AlfWorld]]).
- [DSPy Tutorial — Image Generation Prompt Iteration (dspy.Image + Flux Pro via FAL)](sources/dspy-image-generation-prompting-tutorial.md) — Official [[DSPy]] tutorial at `https://dspy.ai/tutorials/image_generation_prompting/`. **First wiki receipt of an image modality in DSPy** and the first source to exercise the [[DSPyImage|`dspy.Image`]] primitive on a [[DSPySignatures|Signature]] `InputField`. **Twentieth wiki-corpus DSPy tutorial** and the **shortest** to date — a single string-spec [[DSPyPredict|`dspy.Predict`]] (`"desired_prompt: str, current_image: dspy.Image, current_prompt:str -> feedback:str, image_strictly_matches_desired_prompt: bool, revised_prompt: str"`) wrapped in a plain Python `for i in range(max_iter=5)` loop with an early break on the boolean match field. Drives [[IterativeImagePromptRefinement|iterative image-prompt refinement]] against the [[FluxPro|Flux Pro v1.1 Ultra]] text-to-image model hosted by [[FAL]] (`fal-ai/flux-pro/v1.1-ultra`); the critic is [[GPT4oMini|`gpt-4o-mini`]] at `temperature=0.5`. Author credit in the tutorial: *"based off of a tweet from @ThorondorLLC"*. Programming-stage-only — no [[DSPyModules|`dspy.Module`]] subclass, no [[DSPyOptimization|Optimization stage]], no [[DSPyMetrics|metric]], no eval set; the tutorial **explicitly disclaims its own optimizability** (*"this is not DSPy prompt optimization as it is normally used"*) and names the natural lift (*"a future upgrade would be to create a dataset of initial, final prompts to optimize the prompt generation"*). **First wiki receipts within this tutorial**: (1) [[DSPyImage|`dspy.Image`]] primitive on a Signature `InputField`; (2) `dspy.Image.from_url(url)` construction path; (3) **URL-passthrough adapter wire shape** — `dspy.inspect_history(...)` shows `<image_url: https://fal.media/files/.../*.jpg>` carried verbatim through the chat-completion request, no base64 inlining (opposite transport discipline from [[DSPyAudio|`dspy.Audio`]]'s base64-in-`data` storage); (4) `dspy.Image` named inline in a string-spec Signature — proves the string-Signature parser resolves the `dspy.` namespace prefix as a typed field reference; (5) **string-Signature outputs are field-set-canonical, not field-order-canonical** — the `inspect_history(5)` excerpt shows runs with different output-field orders (`feedback / revised_prompt / image_strictly_matches_desired_prompt` in run 1 vs `feedback / image_strictly_matches_desired_prompt / revised_prompt` in runs 2–5); (6) [[FluxPro|Flux Pro v1.1 Ultra]] and [[FAL]] as the image-generation provider stack in a DSPy program (the framework treats the image generator as an external black-box service, not as a `dspy.LM` — symmetric to [[DSPyAudio]]'s out-of-LM TTS handling); (7) `python-dotenv` `load_dotenv()` for credential loading; (8) `temperature=0.5` for a single-Signature critic (highest fixed temperature for a single-Signature critic in the DSPy tutorial corpus to date); (9) two-provider, no-HF-dataset DSPy tutorial shape (OpenAI + FAL, no [[HuggingFace]]); (10) the [[IterativeImagePromptRefinement|critic-then-revise loop pattern]] — natural [[GEPA]] target none of the current GEPA tutorials in the wiki exercises on the image modality. Mints **4 concept pages** ([[DSPyImage]], [[FluxPro]], [[GPT4oMini]], [[IterativeImagePromptRefinement]]) + **2 entity pages** ([[FAL]], [[BlackForestLabs]]). **Contradictions flagged**: the printed iteration log shows autumn-scene images with `False` matches for iterations 1–3 then `True` at iteration 4, but `dspy.inspect_history(5)` shows a café-scene image returning `True` at the **first** call — the two transcripts are from different notebook runs; **first wiki DSPy tutorial whose printed `inspect_history` output disagrees with the printed cell output above it**; field-order drift between runs in the same notebook; `max_iter=5` unmotivated and unablated; no image-similarity metric ([[CLIP]] / [[CosineSimilarity]] / human-eval) grounding the critic; `temperature=0.5` on a boolean-emitting field is a low-grade nondeterminism source; no cost / wall-time / token-count disclosure (each iteration runs a Flux Pro generation, 5–30 s typical, plus a vision-LM call); `fal-ai/flux-pro/v1.1-ultra` pinned with no Flux Schnell / Flux Dev ablation; no [[DallE|DALL-E 3]] / [[StableDiffusion|Stable Diffusion]] / [[MidJourney]] comparison.
- [DSPy Tutorial — Yahoo Finance ReAct Agent](sources/dspy-yahoo-finance-react-tutorial.md) — Official [[DSPy]] tutorial building a **three-tool [[react|`dspy.ReAct`]] financial-analysis agent** mixing one [[LangChain]] community tool (`YahooFinanceNewsTool`) with two plain-callable [[yfinance]] wrappers (`get_stock_price`, `compare_stocks`). Configured with `dspy.LM('openai/gpt-4o-mini')`, `dspy.configure(lm=lm, allow_tool_async_sync_conversion=True)`, one-line string Signature (`"financial_query -> analysis_response"`), `max_iters=6`. **First wiki receipt of `dspy.Tool.from_langchain(...)`** — the third documented construction path for [[DSPyTools|`dspy.Tool`]] alongside auto-wrapping plain callables and `Tool.from_mcp_tool(...)` ([[DSPyMCP]]). Confirms `dspy.Tool` is the **single integration point** between DSPy and the outside tool ecosystem (plain Python / [[ModelContextProtocol|MCP]] / [[LangChain]] all collapse to the same downstream type). **First receipt of `allow_tool_async_sync_conversion=True` set process-wide via `dspy.configure(...)`** rather than per-`with`-block `dspy.context(...)`. **Third agent-shaped DSPy tutorial** after [[dspy-customer-service-agent|customer service]] and [[dspy-tutorial-rag-as-agent|HoVer multi-hop]]; **first DSPy tutorial whose sample output documents partial tool failure** (news fetch fails; agent reasons from price alone) — concrete *error-as-observation* receipt.
