- [DSPy Tutorial — ProgramOfThought (LocalSandbox + ChainOfThought failure case + MultiHopSearchWithPoT)](sources/dspy-tutorial-program-of-thought.md) — Official [[DSPy]] tutorial at `https://dspy.ai/tutorials/program_of_thought/`. **The canonical end-to-end receipt of [[DSPyProgramOfThought|`dspy.ProgramOfThought`]]** in the wiki corpus. Three escalating receipts: (1) [[LocalSandbox|`dspy.LocalSandbox`]] as a standalone code-execution primitive — `sandbox = dspy.LocalSandbox(); sandbox.execute("value = 2*5 + 4\nvalue") == 14`; (2) a side-by-side [[chainofthought|`dspy.ChainOfThought`]] **failure** vs. `dspy.ProgramOfThought` **success** on `"Compute 12! / sum of prime numbers between 1 and 30."` — same `BasicGenerateAnswer(question -> answer)` Signature, same LM, swap of one constructor name: CoT returns `'3,710,009'` (wrong — final division fails despite correct `12!=479,001,600` and prime-sum `129`), PoT returns `'3713190.697674419'` (correct); (3) a custom `MultiHopSearchWithPoT` `dspy.Module` composing `dspy.ChainOfThought(GenerateSearchQuery)` with `dspy.ProgramOfThought(GenerateAnswer, max_iters=3)` over [[ColBERTv2]]-retrieved Wikipedia context, answering *"square of (atomic number of the metal in the gift from France to the US in the late 19th century) + (sum of digits in the first 10 primes)"* → `'2025'` (= 43² where 43 = 29 + 14). [[Llama3|Meta `Llama-3-70b-Instruct`]] LM via `dspy.LM("openai/meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-70b-Instruct", api_base="API_BASE", api_key="None")` — first wiki receipt of Llama-3-70b-Instruct in a DSPy tutorial and of the OpenAI-prefix + LiteLLM-mediated open-weight pattern with placeholder credentials. **First wiki receipts within this tutorial**: (1) [[LocalSandbox|`dspy.LocalSandbox`]] as a user-instantiable public primitive (prior pages described it only as a hidden internal mechanism inside `dspy.ProgramOfThought`); (2) `dspy.ProgramOfThought(GenerateAnswer, max_iters=3)` — the iteration-cap kwarg, undisclosed on prior pages (default value still undisclosed); (3) **printed CoT-arithmetic-failure-then-PoT-success comparison on the same prompt** — concrete operational demo of the [[DSPyProgrammingModel|swap-without-modifying-the-signature]] portability claim and of the *built-in sound critic* claim on [[DSPyProgramOfThought]]; (4) **multi-hop RAG pipeline whose final answer module is `dspy.ProgramOfThought` instead of `dspy.ChainOfThought`** — first wiki receipt of this composition (`MultiHopSearchWithPoT`); (5) `from dspy.dsp.utils import deduplicate` — first wiki receipt of the legacy `dspy.dsp.*` namespace shim (carried over from the framework's earlier name *Demonstrate-Search-Predict*). Programming-stage-only — no metric, no eval set, no [[DSPyOptimizers|Optimizer]] (sibling to [[dspy-ai-text-game-tutorial]], [[dspy-sample-code-generation-tutorial]], [[dspy-custom-module]]). **Contradictions / gaps flagged**: (1) `LocalSandbox`'s actual safety boundary undisclosed — the tutorial calls it an *"adapted Python sandbox"* but does not describe file-system / network / process isolation; gap vs. [[dspy-mcp-tutorial]]'s explicit child-process MCP isolation and [[dspy-tool-use-tutorial]]'s [[func_timeout|`@func_set_timeout(10)`]] + try/except (latter had no isolation beyond timeout); (2) the `wiki17_abstracts` ColBERTv2 endpoint at `http://20.102.90.50:2017` is a publicly-hosted shared server with no SLA — operational risk for reproducers; (3) no cost / latency / token-budget disclosure (continuing tutorial-corpus gap); (4) no `max_iters` ablation; (5) the tutorial labels two sections `## 3)` — upstream copy-paste typo, not a wiki contradiction. Mints **1 concept page** ([[LocalSandbox]]); updates [[DSPyProgramOfThought]] (canonical CoT-vs-PoT receipt + `max_iters` kwarg + `LocalSandbox` linkage + tutorial in sources frontmatter) and [[chainofthought]] (canonical printed CoT-failure receipt + tutorial in sources frontmatter) in place.
- [DSPy Tutorial — Async Programming](sources/dspy-async-tutorial.md) — Short single-page [[DSPy]] tutorial at `https://dspy.ai/tutorials/async/` that **canonicalizes the async-programming surface across the whole DSPy stack** — not just the [[DSPyTools|Tools]] axis. Three load-bearing additions to the corpus: (1) **`acall()` is universal on every built-in [[DSPyModules|Module]]** — `dspy.Predict.acall(...)`, `dspy.ChainOfThought.acall(...)`, `dspy.ReAct.acall(...)`, by extension every [[DSPyPredict|`dspy.Predict`]]-derived module — first wiki receipt that `acall` is module-wide, not Tools-specific; (2) **`aforward()` is the async counterpart to `forward()` on custom `dspy.Module` subclasses** — first wiki receipt of `aforward`, a further lift from the [[PyTorch]] *override-the-entry-method* idiom (`forward → aforward` with the async-suffix convention); (3) **explicit framework-authored sync-vs-async decision rubric** — four-and-four (sync for prototyping / research / small-to-medium apps / debuggability; async for high-QPS services / async-only tools / concurrent requests / production scalability) with a candid trade-offs paragraph (*"complex error handling, potential subtle bugs, intricate code structures, and runtime environment differences between interactive notebooks (Jupyter, Colab) and standard Python environments"*). Re-confirms `tool.acall(...)` ([[dspy-tools|first documented]]) and `allow_tool_async_sync_conversion=True` in both per-block `dspy.context(...)` ([[dspy-tools]]) and process-wide `dspy.configure(...)` ([[dspy-yahoo-finance-react-tutorial|first received here]]) forms, side-by-side. Canonical custom-module example chains two [[chainofthought|`dspy.ChainOfThought`]] predictions with `await self.predict1.acall(...)` then `await self.predict2.acall(...)` — explicit *"sequentially but asynchronously"* in-code comment is the framework's expectation-management moment: **async DSPy ≠ concurrent DSPy** by default; `asyncio.gather(...)` is the user's responsibility. Programming-stage-only — no metric, no optimizer, no dataset; deliberately the framework's *production-readiness shape* rather than an evaluation rung. Mints 1 concept page ([[DSPyAsync]] — the framework-wide async pattern, orthogonal to [[DSPyProgrammingModel|the four-concerns decomposition]]); updates [[DSPyTools]] / [[DSPyModules]] / [[DSPyPredict]] sources frontmatter in place. No contradictions — extends every prior DSPy ingest along an orthogonal async axis.
- [DSPy Tutorial — Streaming](sources/dspy-streaming-tutorial.md) — Short single-page [[DSPy]] tutorial at `https://dspy.ai/tutorials/streaming/` that **canonicalizes the framework's streaming surface** — a sidecar-architecture token-streaming layer composing orthogonally over every [[DSPyModules|Module]] without changing the [[DSPyProgrammingModel|four-concerns decomposition]]. Three load-bearing additions to the corpus: (1) **`dspy.streamify(program, stream_listeners=[...])`** — the single wrapper that lifts any [[DSPyModules|`dspy.Module`]] into a streaming generator (async by default, sync via `async_streaming=False`); (2) **`dspy.streaming.StreamListener(signature_field_name=...)`** — the per-field listener that yields `StreamResponse(predict_name, signature_field_name, chunk)` envelopes, with `allow_reuse=True` for loop-bodied modules ([[react|`dspy.ReAct`]]) and explicit `(predict, predict_name)` disambiguation for **duplicate field names across sub-modules**; (3) **`dspy.streaming.StatusMessageProvider`** — a six-hook subclass-and-override surface (`lm_start/end`, `module_start/end`, `tool_start/end`) emitting `StatusMessage(message=...)` objects through the **same generator** as the token chunks, so a UI consumer reads a single typed stream of `StreamResponse | Prediction | StatusMessage`. **Sidecar architecture disclosure** — *"streaming is implemented in a sidecar fashion: we enable streaming on the LM so that LM outputs a stream of tokens. We send these tokens to a side channel, which is being continuously read by the user-defined listeners"* — and the [[DSPyAdapters|Adapter]] is in the streaming loop because *"Listeners' internal mechanism changes according to the adapter behind the scene"* (field-boundary detection depends on adapter wire format — [[DSPyAdapters|`ChatAdapter`]] delimiter vs [[DSPyAdapters|`JSONAdapter`]] JSON shape). Three operational subtleties: streaming is **disabled by cache hit** (only the final [[DSPyPrediction|`Prediction`]] arrives when the [[DSPyLM|LM]] call is cached — the multi-field example uses `dspy.LM(..., cache=False)` deliberately); `StreamResponse` chunks are **buffered until the next field appears** (last chunk is usually multi-token because finalization is detected by field-boundary, not by special token); and the streamed field must be of **type `str`** — non-string [[DSPySignatures|Signature]] outputs ([[Pydantic]] / `list[str]` / [[DSPyHistory|`dspy.History`]] / `dspy.Image` / nested types) are not streamable, narrowing the [[DSPySignatures|five-tier type system]] to one tier for the streaming axis. **First wiki receipt of**: `dspy.streamify`, `StreamListener`, `StreamResponse`, `StatusMessageProvider`, `StatusMessage`, `async_streaming` kwarg, [[react|`dspy.ReAct`]]'s implicit `next_thought` per-iteration field name, `named_predictors()` as the **public stream-identity surface** (previously documented only for [[DSPyOptimizers|Optimizer]] consumption on [[DSPyModules|the Modules page]]), and the disclosure that the [[DSPyAdapters|Adapter]] is in the streaming loop (the [[DSPyAdapters|Adapters page]] documented formatting/parsing only, not stream segmentation). Sibling-axis tutorial to [[dspy-async-tutorial]] — both canonicalize production-shaped surfaces over the same async-native [[LiteLLM]] substrate, but with different wrapping idioms (wrapper function vs `acall` method). Programming-stage-only — no metric, no optimizer, no dataset. Mints 1 concept page ([[DSPyStreaming]] — the framework-wide streaming pattern, orthogonal to [[DSPyProgrammingModel|the four-concerns decomposition]]); updates [[DSPyAsync]] / [[DSPyAdapters]] / [[DSPyModules]] / [[DSPyLM]] sources frontmatter in place. No contradictions — extends every prior DSPy ingest along an orthogonal streaming axis.
- [DSPy Tutorial — Deployment](sources/dspy-deployment-tutorial.md) — Short single-page [[DSPy]] tutorial at `https://dspy.ai/tutorials/deployment/` that **canonicalizes the framework's production-serving surface** — two recommended packaging paths ([[FastAPI]] for lightweight REST, [[MLflow]] for versioned enterprise deployments). Three load-bearing additions to the corpus: (1) **`dspy.asyncify(program)`** — first wiki receipt of the sync-program-to-async-callable wrapper, a **fifth async surface** alongside the four [[DSPyAsync|already documented]] (`acall`, `aforward`, `tool.acall`, `allow_tool_async_sync_conversion`); distinct from `acall` (event-loop dispatch on a natively-async program) because asyncify runs the **sync** inner program on a **thread pool** (`dspy.configure(async_max_workers=N)`, default 8) — the right tool for *existing sync code fronted by an async web service*; (2) **`mlflow.dspy.log_model(program, ..., task="llm/v1/chat")` + `mlflow models serve` + `mlflow models build-docker`** — first wiki receipt of [[MLflow]] as **serving** layer (prior nine MLflow receipts cover *track / trace / store*); the `task="llm/v1/chat"` argument exposes the served model behind an **OpenAI-compatible chat interface** (`{"messages": [{"role", "content"}]}`), making OpenAI-client codebases work unchanged against a DSPy-optimized backend; (3) **`dspy.utils.streaming.streaming_response(stream)` + [[FastAPI]]'s `StreamingResponse(..., media_type="text/event-stream")`** — closes [[DSPyStreaming|the Streaming concept page's]] forward reference to *"natural transports for the streaming generator at the web layer"* with a concrete [[ServerSentEvents|SSE]] recipe. **MLflow custom-Module-wrapping constraint** (MLflow 2.22.0+): bare [[DSPyPredict|`dspy.Predict`]] / [[chainofthought|`dspy.ChainOfThought`]] **will not log directly** — must wrap in a custom [[DSPyModules|`dspy.Module`]] subclass whose `forward()` takes positional args (signature-inference requirement); re-anchors [[DSPyModules|the Modules-page]] *"put your logic in a custom module"* discipline as a **deployment-time** requirement complementing its autolog-time and [[DSPyOptimizers|optimizer]]-time uses. Sibling-axis tutorial to [[dspy-async-tutorial]] (dispatch axis) and [[dspy-streaming-tutorial]] (streaming axis) — together the three constitute DSPy's framework-level *production-shape* documentation. Programming-stage-only — no metric, no optimizer, no dataset. Mints no new concept page; updates [[DSPyAsync]] (asyncify section + sources frontmatter), [[DSPyStreaming]] (SSE web-transport receipt + sources frontmatter), [[MLflow]] (model-serving section + sources frontmatter), [[FastAPI]] / [[Uvicorn]] / [[ServerSentEvents]] entity pages in place. No contradictions — extends every prior DSPy ingest along an orthogonal *serve* axis. Scope-limit gaps: no production-monitoring code, no load-test numbers, no auth/authz, no `aforward`-routed-program serving example, no streaming-from-MLflow recipe.
- [DSPy Tutorial — Saving and Loading Programs](sources/dspy-saving-tutorial.md) — Short single-page [[DSPy]] tutorial at `https://dspy.ai/tutorials/saving/` that **canonicalizes the framework's two-mode program-persistence surface** — composing orthogonally over every prior DSPy artifact ([[DSPySignatures|Signatures]] / [[DSPyModules|Modules]] / [[DSPyAdapters|Adapters]] / [[DSPyLM|LM]] bindings / [[DSPyOptimizers|Optimizer]]-refined instructions/demos) without changing the [[DSPyProgrammingModel|four-concerns decomposition]]. Two modes selected by the `save_program` flag on `Module.save(...)`: (1) **state-only** (`save_program=False`) — persists signature + demos + configurable module attributes only; architecture must be **reconstructed in code** before `loaded.load(path)`; sub-format chosen by file extension (`.json` default — plain-text, human-readable, the every-prior-receipt path that anchors [[DSPyOptimizers|the Optimizers page's]] *"writing code instead of strings"* inspectability commitment; `.pkl` pickle fallback for non-JSON-serializable objects like [[DSPyImage|`dspy.Image`]] / `datetime`); (2) **whole-program** (`save_program=True`, **`dspy>=2.6.0`**) — persists architecture + state + dependency-version metadata together via [[Cloudpickle|`cloudpickle`]] into a **directory** (not a single file); recovered by the top-level `dspy.load(path)` with no reconstruction step. **First wiki receipt of**: `save_program` flag, `dspy.load(...)` top-level entry point, `allow_pickle=True` explicit-acknowledgement gate (the save/load analog of [[DSPyCache|`restrict_pickle=True`]]'s cache-side allowlist), `modules_to_serialize=[...]` opt-in invoking `cloudpickle.register_pickle_by_value(...)` for **by-value** custom-module serialization (class definitions travel with the artifact instead of being import-resolved at load time), and the **pre-3.0.0 backward-compatibility non-guarantee** (*"no guarantee of backward compatibility across DSPy versions"* — explicit disavowal; 3.0.0+ commits to BC within major versions). Three operational subtleties: **JSON state-only flattens demos to `dict`** (not [[DSPyExample|`dspy.Example`]] — pickle and whole-program modes preserve identity); **state-only `.json` is the only inspectable mode** (pickle / cloudpickle artifacts are opaque binaries); **whole-program pickles the bound LM reference** — load-side environment must have credentials or reconfigure the LM after load. Sibling-axis tutorial to [[dspy-async-tutorial]] / [[dspy-streaming-tutorial]] / [[dspy-cache-tutorial]] / [[dspy-observability-tutorial]] / [[dspy-deployment-tutorial]] — all canonicalize production-shape surfaces (async / streaming / caching / observability / serving / persistence) orthogonal to the four-concerns decomposition. The wiki's six-axis production-shape sibling cluster is now complete. Programming-stage-only — no metric, no optimizer, no dataset; deliberately the framework's *durable-artifact shape* documentation. Mints 1 concept page ([[DSPySaving]] — the two-mode persistence surface, decision tree, security posture, BC contract); updates [[DSPyOptimizers]] (anchors the save section to the new concept page), [[DSPyOptimization]] (workflow output's persistence story), [[DSPyModules]] / [[DSPyLM]] sources frontmatter in place. No contradictions — **completes** the [[DSPyOptimizers|Optimizers catalog page's]] JSON-only persistence story by adding the pickle and whole-program modes the catalog deferred, plus the security and BC fine print; the cache-tutorial's `restrict_pickle` allowlist and this tutorial's `allow_pickle` flag are **complementary** pickle-safety patterns over the same threat. Scope-limit gaps: no on-disk artifact size or load-latency comparison across modes; no migration recipe for the 2.x → 3.x BC boundary; no transitive-dependency guidance for `modules_to_serialize=`; no streaming-friendly persistence path (does whole-program round-trip a `dspy.streamify(...)`-wrapped program?); no JSON schema for the state-only format.
- [DSPy Tutorial — Caching](sources/dspy-cache-tutorial.md) — Short single-page [[DSPy]] tutorial at `https://dspy.ai/tutorials/cache/` that **canonicalizes the framework's three-layer caching architecture** — composing orthogonally over every [[DSPyModules|Module]] without changing the [[DSPyProgrammingModel|four-concerns decomposition]]. Three load-bearing additions to the corpus: (1) **three independent cache layers** — in-memory ([[LRUCache]] via `cachetools.LRUCache`), on-disk (`diskcache.FanoutCache`), and **provider-side [[PromptCaching]]** (server-managed by [[anthropic|Anthropic]] / [[openai|OpenAI]]) — first two enabled by default, third opt-in via `cache_control_injection_points=[{"location": "message", "role": "system"}]` on [[DSPyLM|`dspy.LM(...)`]]; (2) **`dspy.configure_cache`** as the single configuration surface — `enable_disk_cache` / `enable_memory_cache` / `disk_size_limit_bytes` / `memory_max_entries` plus the security pair `restrict_pickle` / `safe_types`; (3) **`dspy.clients.Cache` subclassing** as the custom-key-logic escape hatch — override `cache_key()` / `get()` / `put()`, then assign `dspy.cache = CustomCache(...)`, with the canonical example using `sha256(orjson.dumps(messages, ...))` to ignore model selection so semantically-equivalent prompts share cache hits across [[DSPyLM|LM]] versions. Three operational disclosures: **default `cache_key` hashes all litellm request args except credentials** — the model name is part of the key, so switching models under `dspy.context(...)` misses by default (contrasts with [[dspy-streaming-tutorial|the streaming tutorial's]] reverse interaction — *streaming is disabled by cache hit*); **cached responses return `None` for `result.get_lm_usage()` under [[DSPyLM|`track_usage=True`]]** because no provider call occurred (the usage-tracking ↔ caching interaction is now documented end-to-end across the corpus); and **`restrict_pickle=True` enables an allowlist-based deserializer** defending against arbitrary code execution from tampered on-disk caches — default allowlist covers LiteLLM/OpenAI response types and NumPy reconstruction helpers, plus user `safe_types`; **unapproved types are treated as cache misses with a log entry, not raised exceptions** (graceful-degradation discipline, not fail-loud). **First wiki receipt of**: `dspy.configure_cache`, `dspy.clients.Cache`, `cache_control_injection_points`, `restrict_pickle` / `safe_types`, `disk_size_limit_bytes` / `memory_max_entries`, `disk_cache_dir`, `dspy.clients.DISK_CACHE_DIR`, and the `(memory, disk, provider)` three-layer taxonomy. Sibling-axis tutorial to [[dspy-async-tutorial]] and [[dspy-streaming-tutorial]] — all three canonicalize production-shape surfaces (async / streaming / caching) orthogonal to the four-concerns decomposition. Programming-stage-only — no metric, no optimizer, no dataset. Mints 1 concept page ([[DSPyCache]] — the framework-wide caching pattern); updates [[DSPyLM]] / [[DSPyModules]] / [[DSPyPredict]] sources frontmatter in place. No contradictions — extends every prior DSPy ingest along an orthogonal caching axis.
- [DSPy Tutorial — Output Refinement (BestOfN and Refine)](sources/dspy-output-refinement-tutorial.md) — Short single-page [[DSPy]] tutorial at `https://dspy.ai/tutorials/output_refinement/best-of-n-and-refine/` that **canonicalizes the framework's inference-time output-refinement surface** — two sibling modules ([[DSPyBestOfN|`dspy.BestOfN`]] and [[DSPyRefine|`dspy.Refine`]]) wrapping any [[DSPyModules|Module]] in a **reward-driven retry loop** with shared four-kwarg API (`module`, `N`, `reward_fn(args, pred) -> float`, `threshold`, plus optional `fail_count`). **Migration receipt** — *"As of DSPy 2.6, these modules replace `dspy.Suggest` and `dspy.Assert`"* — the first wiki-corpus statement that the [[DSPyAssert]] / [[DSPySuggest]] API from [[2312.13382-dspy-assertions]] is deprecated; the boolean-constraint surface becomes a scalar-reward surface (`reward_fn` + `threshold`), `Assert`'s halt-on-fail maps to `BestOfN(..., fail_count=1)`, and the retry-with-feedback mechanism from [[AssertionDrivenBacktracking|backtracking]] survives in `Refine` but with framework-synthesized feedback in place of user-authored `msg`. Three worked examples — one-word-answer constraint (deterministic reward, `N=3`, shared verbatim across both modules), `FactualityJudge`-driven refinement (LM-as-judge composed with `Refine`), and length-controlled summarization (`BestOfN(N=50, threshold=0.9)` with tapering soft-margin reward `1.0 - distance/125` around a 75-word target). **Distinguishing properties**: `BestOfN` is pure selection across independent rollouts (cache-bypass via distinct rollout IDs); `Refine` is selection plus an extra per-failed-rollout feedback-generation LM call that shifts the sampling distribution toward higher-reward regions across iterations. **First wiki receipt of**: `dspy.BestOfN`, `dspy.Refine`, the two-arg `reward_fn(args, pred)` signature, the `fail_count` error-tolerance parameter, the rollout-ID cache-bypass mechanism for *intentional* cache misses (the inverse of the [[dspy-cache-tutorial|caching tutorial's]] hit-path), and LM-judge composition as a reward function. Mints 2 concept pages ([[DSPyBestOfN]] / [[DSPyRefine]]); updates [[DSPyAssert]] / [[DSPySuggest]] in place with deprecation notes; updates [[bestofn]] with a cross-link from the generic test-time-scaling pattern to its DSPy-module instantiation. **One contradiction with the prior corpus** — [[DSPyAssert]] / [[DSPySuggest]] were documented as the active API; reconciled by marking both deprecated as of DSPy 2.6 while preserving them as the historical source for the underlying [[AssertionDrivenBacktracking]] / [[AssertionDrivenExampleBootstrapping]] / [[CounterexampleBootstrapping]] compile-time machinery formalized by [[2312.13382-dspy-assertions]]. Programming-stage-only — no metric, no optimizer, no dataset, no quantitative benchmark numbers (zero before/after lift). Sibling-axis tutorial to [[dspy-async-tutorial]] / [[dspy-streaming-tutorial]] / [[dspy-cache-tutorial]] / [[dspy-observability-tutorial]] — all canonicalize framework-level production-shape surfaces orthogonal to the [[DSPyProgrammingModel|four-concerns decomposition]]. **Scope-limit gaps**: no rollout-ID mechanism explanation; no `Refine` feedback-prompt form shown; no `dspy.streamify` / [[DSPyOptimizers|Optimizer]] composition receipts; no cost / latency disclosure for `N=50`; ambiguous selection rule (first-clear-threshold vs full-N-then-argmax); no compile-time optimization equivalent of [[AssertionDrivenExampleBootstrapping|the assertion-paper's example bootstrapping]]; no `Refine` formal pseudocode; no fail-mode taxonomy (low-reward vs exception).
- [DSPy Tutorial — Debugging & Observability](sources/dspy-observability-tutorial.md) — Short single-page [[DSPy]] tutorial at `https://dspy.ai/tutorials/observability/` that **canonicalizes the three-tier observability stack** of the framework: (tier 1) `dspy.inspect_history(n=N)` — zero-dep print of last *N* LM calls; (tier 2) [[MLflow]] tracing via `mlflow.autolog()` against a `mlflow server` backend — full trace tree with prompts, responses, timing, parent/child structure; (tier 3) custom instrumentation via `dspy.utils.callback.BaseCallback` subclass + `dspy.configure(callbacks=[...])`. **First wiki receipt of `BaseCallback`** and its six start/end handler pairs (`on_module_*`, `on_lm_*`, `on_adapter_format_*`, `on_adapter_parse_*`, `on_tool_*`, `on_evaluate_*`). **First wiki receipt of the unscoped `mlflow.autolog()` form** for DSPy autotracing (vs the kwarg-bearing `mlflow.dspy.autolog(...)` form in [[dspy-custom-module]] / [[dspy-tutorial-rag-as-agent]] / [[dspy-optimizer-tracking-tutorial]]) and the **lowest MLflow floor** in the corpus (`mlflow>=2.18.0`, vs 2.21.1 and 3.0.0 elsewhere). **Establishes the canonical retrieval-staleness diagnosis pattern**: a [[react|`dspy.ReAct`]] agent over the [[ColBERTv2]] Wikipedia endpoint returns a fluent-but-stale answer about Shohei Ohtani's team; the bug is invisible at the LM-output layer (chain-of-thought looks well-grounded) and only becomes visible by hovering the retriever span in the MLflow trace UI; fix is to substitute a [[Tavily]] web-search [[DSPyTools|`dspy.Tool`]] — no other program changes. Sibling-axis tutorial to [[dspy-async-tutorial]] / [[dspy-streaming-tutorial]] / [[dspy-cache-tutorial]] — all four canonicalize production-shape surfaces (async / streaming / caching / observability) orthogonal to the four-concerns decomposition. Programming-stage-only — no dataset, no optimizer, no metric. Mints 3 concept pages ([[DSPyObservability]], [[DSPyCallback]], [[InspectHistory]]) and 1 entity page ([[Tavily]]); updates [[MLflow]] and [[ColBERTv2]] in place. No contradictions — slots underneath the existing MLflow-integration ladder, with the staleness lesson reinforcing that the [[ColBERTv2]] Wikipedia endpoint is a frozen snapshot (correct for benchmarks, wrong for time-sensitive queries).
- [DSPy Tutorial — Building AI Agents (Customer Service Agent)](sources/dspy-customer-service-agent.md) — Canonical end-to-end production-shaped receipt for [[react|`dspy.ReAct`]] in [[DSPy]]: a seven-tool airline customer-service agent over a five-class [[Pydantic]] domain (`Date`, `UserProfile`, `Flight`, `Itinerary`, `Ticket`), driven by a two-field [[DSPySignatures|Signature]] (`user_request: str` → `process_result: str`). The tool list splits into the three production-agent categories — **lookup** (`fetch_flight_info` / `fetch_itinerary` / `get_user_info` / `pick_flight`), **mutation** (`book_flight` / `cancel_itinerary`), and **escalation** (`file_ticket`) — establishing the discipline that every customer-service ReAct agent needs an escalation surface as the [[LLMModuloFramework|LLM-Modulo]] safety valve. Three structural properties: (i) **tools are plain Python functions with docstrings + type hints** — no `dspy.Tool(...)` wrapping required when passed into `dspy.ReAct(..., tools=[...])`; (ii) **the user-facing Signature is independent of the tool list** — two fields scope the interface, seven tools scope the action surface; (iii) **[[Pydantic]] models compose at any depth** — tools take/return nested `Itinerary` ⊃ `Flight` + `UserProfile`, `Flight` ⊃ `Date`. Returned [[DSPyPrediction|`Prediction`]] carries **three fields**: `trajectory` (full think-act-observe log), `reasoning` (final-decision explanation, the same field [[ChainOfThought|`dspy.ChainOfThought`]] adds), and the user-declared `process_result` — only the last was declared on the Signature. `dspy.inspect_history()` is the canonical debugging surface (cross-tutorial confirmation that it's a standard cross-Module hook, not a Module-specific feature). **Second wiki-corpus DSPy tutorial** (after [[dspy-conversation-history]]); fills rung 4 of the DSPy application stack (single-agent multi-tool task) between the [[dspy-conversation-history|multi-turn-conversation]] rung and the [[2408.15232-co-storm|multi-agent collaborative-discourse]] rung. **First wiki-corpus page to show a deployment-shaped LM agent** — every prior DSPy ingest scoped either toy benchmarks ([[hotpotqa|HotPotQA]] / [[GSM8K]] / [[Iris]] / [[Banking77]]) or research domains; the customer-service-agent shape (NL request → tool selection → structured action → user-facing response with confirmation) is the production application shape the corpus had been missing. **Scope-limit gap**: tutorial does **not** add [[DSPyAssertions|LM Assertions]] inside mutation tools — a production deployment needs `dspy.Assert(...)` checks inside `book_flight` etc. to prevent silently invalid bookings. Mints [[CustomerServiceAgent]] concept page; updates [[react]] / [[DSPy]] in place.
- [DSPy Tutorial — Memory-Enabled ReAct Agents with Mem0](sources/dspy-mem0-react-tutorial.md) — **Ninth wiki-corpus [[DSPy]] tutorial** and the **first whole-system worked example of a memory-enabled agent over an external persistent store**. Wires [[Mem0]] (`mem0ai`) — a long-term-memory layer with an internal extraction LM over a vector index — into a [[react|`dspy.ReAct`]] agent by exposing Mem0's CRUD methods (`store_memory` / `search_memories` / `get_all_memories`) as bound-method tools alongside three preference-helper wrappers (`set_reminder` / `get_preferences` / `update_preferences`) and a `get_current_time` utility. Two-field Signature (`user_input: str → response: str`); the persistence policy is one sentence in the Signature docstring — *"Whenever you answer a user's input, remember to store the information in memory so that you can use it later"* — without which the agent would only read from memory, never write. Configuration is the canonical Mem0 two-block shape: `llm` (extraction LM — `gpt-4o-mini` @ T=0.1) + `embedder` (`text-embedding-3-small`). `max_iters=6`. Tools take `user_id` from the API surface — **multi-tenant from the first line of code**, though the tutorial demo uses a single `"default_user"`. Demonstrates seven-turn personalization (food preferences → exercise preferences → reminder → hiking → summary) over an Alice persona. **First wiki receipt of [[Mem0]]** (new entity page minted); slots above [[dspy-customer-service-agent]] on the DSPy application stack as rung 5 — *single-agent multi-tool + external persistent memory*. Like [[dspy-conversation-history]] and [[dspy-ai-text-game-tutorial]], deliberately exits at the *Programming* rung — no [[DSPyOptimizers|Optimizer]], no [[DSPyMetrics|metric]], no eval set. Tool-class-as-namespace pattern (bound methods of a `MemoryTools` class become DSPy tools — mild extension of the customer-service-agent's plain-function discipline). Counter-positions against in-process memory patterns ([[ConversationBufferMemory]] / [[ConversationSummaryMemory]] / [[DSPyHistory|`dspy.History`]]) — Mem0's distinguishing properties are (i) the internal extraction LM (decides what to store rather than storing everything) and (ii) first-class multi-tenancy. Scope gaps: no persistent storage backend (in-memory default), no expiration / TTL / compaction, no conflict resolution (`update_memory` exists but is not in `tools=[...]`), no cost tracking for the hidden Mem0-internal extraction LM, no comparison against [[DSPyHistory|`dspy.History`]]. Updates [[LongTermMemory]] (new "Concrete implementations" table + Mem0 receipt callout + `sources:` frontmatter) / [[react]] / [[DSPy]] in place.
- [DSPy Tutorial — Entity Extraction](sources/dspy-entity-extraction-tutorial.md) — Canonical [[DSPy]] receipt for **decoder-LM entity extraction on [[CoNLL2003|CoNLL-2003]]** — the wiki's first DSPy page anchored to a classical-NLP token-classification application slice. Single-Signature single-Module program: `tokens: list[str] -> extracted_people: list[str]` wrapped in [[ChainOfThought|`dspy.ChainOfThought`]] over `openai/gpt-4o-mini`; **86.0% exact-list-match zero-shot → 93.0% after [[MIPROv2|`dspy.MIPROv2(auto="medium", max_bootstrapped_demos=4)`]]** on a 200-example test slice — a **+7-point absolute lift** for **$0.26 USD** total LiteLLM-reported cost. Reframes [[NamedEntityRecognition|NER]] as **subset selection** (return the tokens that are persons) rather than per-token [[BIOTagging|BIO]] classification — bypassing the BIO surface entirely. The task narrows CoNLL-2003 to **persons only** (`ner_tag ∈ {1, 2}` — `B-PER` + `I-PER`); other entity types are out of scope. **Metric is strict ordered-list equality** (`prediction.extracted_people == example.expected_extracted_people`) — the simple-metric regime from [[dspy-metrics|page 11]], harsher than the span-level [[seqeval]] F1 the encoder-NER world uses. Inspecting the optimized prompt (`dspy.inspect_history(n=1)`) reveals MIPROv2 injected **both a rewritten task instruction** *(a synthesized "regulatory compliance and public-health communication" domain framing — a known [[MIPROv2|proposer hallucination]] that nonetheless optimizes the metric)* **and four bootstrapped few-shot demos** — the joint instruction-and-demo axis the [[2406.11695-mipro|MIPRO paper]] formalized. Cost tracking via `sum(x['cost'] for x in lm.history if x['cost'])`; save/load via plain-text JSON (`optimized_extractor.save("optimized_extractor.json")`). Opt-in [[MLflow|MLflow]] integration via `mlflow.dspy.autolog()` + `mlflow.dspy.log_model(...)` for production-shaped experiment tracking. **Third wiki-corpus DSPy tutorial** after [[dspy-conversation-history|multi-turn chatbot]] and [[dspy-customer-service-agent|seven-tool ReAct agent]]; fills the **classical-NLP token-classification rung** in the DSPy application stack and provides the **decoder-LM counterpart** to [[hands-on-llm-ch11-fine-tuning-representation-models|*Hands-On LLMs* Ch 11]]'s encoder-fine-tuning NER receipt on the same [[CoNLL2003|CoNLL-2003]] dataset — making CoNLL-2003 the first wiki dataset where both encoder-fine-tuning and decoder-LLM prompt-optimization receipts coexist (note: the two numbers are **not directly comparable** — different metrics). The +7-point lift fits the [[2604.14585-prompt-optimization-coin-flip|*can but doesn't* pattern]] — the LM zero-shot defaults to extracting any capitalized token regardless of person/non-person semantics; MIPROv2 installs the **"persons only, not locations or organizations"** discrimination. Mints 1 concept page ([[EntityExtraction]] — the umbrella for *return-the-subset* extraction as distinct from per-token [[NamedEntityRecognition|NER]]); updates [[NamedEntityRecognition]] / [[CoNLL2003]] / [[MIPROv2]] / [[chainofthought]] / [[DSPy]] / [[MLflow]] in place.
- [DSPy Tutorial — Building RAG as Agent](sources/dspy-tutorial-rag-as-agent.md) — Canonical end-to-end receipt for **[[react|`dspy.ReAct`]] multi-hop retrieval agent over [[HoVer]] (three-hop subset), optimized by [[MIPROv2]] with [[OpenAI|GPT-4o]] as teacher and [[Llama|Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct]] as student**. **First wiki receipt with explicit teacher/student model decoupling** (`teacher_settings=dict(lm=gpt4o), prompt_model=gpt4o`) — GPT-4o invoked *"a very small number of times"* during compilation; deployment runs entirely on 3B Llama. Two complementary tools: `search_wikipedia` (top-5 docs + titles for positions 5–30) + `lookup_wikipedia` (full page text). Custom dual-mode `top5_recall` metric (`recall >= 1.0` boolean during optimization; decimal during evaluation) — first wiki receipt of [[DSPyMetrics|the trace-aware pattern]] for **list-membership recall**. **Headline result: 8% → 41.67% top5_recall (5× improvement)** on the same student model, same tools, same metric — pure prompt optimization, no weight tuning. First wiki receipt to surface MIPROv2 kwargs `max_errors=999` (brittle student needs error budget) and `max_iters=20` on `dspy.ReAct` (three-hop claims need long loops). MIPROv2 config: `auto="medium"`, `max_bootstrapped_demos=3, max_labeled_demos=0` (no human-labeled demos). Third wiki-corpus DSPy tutorial after [[dspy-conversation-history]] (no tools, no opt) and [[dspy-customer-service-agent]] (typed-domain tools, no opt) — this tutorial fills the *open-domain retrieval + end-to-end optimization* slot. The 5× lift exceeds the [[2406.11695-mipro|MIPRO paper's]] HoVer lift (30.2 → 44.7, 1.5×) because the paper used the larger [[Llama3_8BInstruct|Llama-3-8B]] student; 3B has more headroom. [[MLflow]] integration via `mlflow.dspy.autolog()` traces the ReAct trajectory. Save/load via plain-text JSON. Updates [[react]] / [[MIPROv2]] / [[HoVer]] / [[MLflow]] in place.
- [DSPy Tutorial — Building a Creative Text-Based AI Game](sources/dspy-ai-text-game-tutorial.md) — Official [[DSPy]] tutorial that builds an interactive text-based adventure game by composing **three [[DSPySignatures|Signatures]] under [[chainofthought|`dspy.ChainOfThought`]] modules** inside a single [[DSPyModules|`dspy.Module`]] subclass (`GameAI`). **The wiki's first DSPy tutorial that exits at the *Programming* rung** of [[DSPyProgrammingModel|the three-stage workflow]] — no [[DSPyOptimizers|Optimizer]], no [[DSPyMetrics|metric]], no eval set, no [[MIPROv2]] sweep. Three typed Signatures with rich container output types — `StoryGenerator → scene_description: str, available_actions: list[str], npcs_present: list[str], items_available: list[str]`; `DialogueGenerator → npc_response: str, mood_change: str, quest_offered: bool, information_revealed: str`; `ActionResolver → success: bool, outcome_description: str, stat_changes: dict[str, int], items_gained: list[str], experience_gained: int` — receipt that **class-form Signatures are mandatory once outputs include `list[str]` / `dict[str, int]` containers**. `GameAI(dspy.Module)` wraps each Signature in [[chainofthought|`dspy.ChainOfThought`]] (the *start simple* default, never justified — just followed); exposes `generate_scene()` / `handle_dialogue()` / `resolve_action()`. **Single LM** (`dspy.LM(model='openai/gpt-4o-mini')`) for all three Signatures — no `dspy.context(...)`, no teacher/student split, no per-Signature temperature. Deterministic Python (`Player`/`GameContext`/`GameEngine` dataclasses, save/load, inventory, leveling) owns *state*; LM owns *creative generation* and proposes *bounded structured mutations* (`stat_changes`, `items_gained`, `experience_gained`) Python applies — the **"LM handles creative generation while game logic remains deterministic and controllable"** thesis. **Seventh wiki-corpus DSPy tutorial** after [[dspy-conversation-history|multi-turn chatbot]], [[dspy-customer-service-agent|seven-tool ReAct agent]], [[dspy-custom-module|custom-module RAG]], [[dspy-rag-tutorial|RAG]], [[dspy-tutorial-rag-as-agent|RAG-as-agent]], [[dspy-entity-extraction-tutorial|entity extraction]], and [[dspy-tutorial-math|MATH algebra]] — fills the **creative-systems / interactive-fiction application** rung that the corpus had not yet covered, and the **smallest dependency footprint** of any DSPy tutorial in the wiki (`pip install dspy rich typer` — three packages). Updates [[DSPySignatures]] / [[chainofthought]] / [[DSPyModules]] sources frontmatter in place; no new concept pages minted (all referenced DSPy primitives pre-existed); the tutorial's *omissions* (no Optimizer, no metric, no multi-turn LM history, no tool calls) are deliberate scope-narrowing rather than gaps.
- [DSPy Tutorial — Managing Conversation History](sources/dspy-conversation-history.md) — Canonical tutorial source for [[DSPy]] at the **multi-turn chatbot** application layer. The load-bearing disclosure: *"DSPy does not provide such functionality out of the box, meaning users are required to manage the conversation history on their own"* — [[DSPyModules|`dspy.Module`]] has no built-in inter-turn state capture. Defines [[DSPyHistory|`dspy.History`]] as the [[DSPySignatures|Signature]] field type (DSPy-special tier-five, alongside [[DSPyImage|`dspy.Image`]]) with a `messages: list[dict[str, Any]]` attribute; specifies the **two essential procedures** (declare a `history: dspy.History = dspy.InputField()` field; thread + append the instance through the conversation loop); ships the canonical five-line interactive-chatbot receipt with `gpt-4o-mini`. Discloses the structural property that **history-bearing [[DSPyExample|`dspy.Example`]] demos render as a single turn with the messages serialized as JSON** rather than expanded — *"DSPy renders the history as a single message in the few-shot examples to maintain compatibility with the OpenAI standard format"* — keeping prompt envelopes bounded under [[BootstrapFewShot|few-shot]] / [[BootstrapFewShotWithRandomSearch|BFRS]] / [[MIPROv2|MIPRO]] demo budgets and preserving the OpenAI `messages=[...]` shape the [[LiteLLM]] layer expects. First wiki-corpus DSPy page anchored to a *tutorial* rather than a *Learn* reference or paper. Fills the missing **single-agent multi-turn** rung in the DSPy application stack between [[DSPyPredict|single-call]] and [[CoSTORM|multi-agent collaborative-discourse]]. Mints 2 concept pages — [[DSPyHistory]] (the `dspy.History` primitive) and [[ConversationHistory]] (the general LM-application concept). Inherits the [[2604.27707-agentic-memory-is-a-memo|*"agentic memory is lookup, not memory"*]] limitations (Ω(k²) generalization gap + persistent prompt-injection vulnerability) since the flat-list `messages` is re-fed verbatim into the prompt each turn.
- [DSPy Learn — Optimizers](sources/dspy-optimizers.md) — **Page 13 of 13** of the [[DSPy]] *Learn* documentation and the **closing page of the corpus**. Where [[dspy-optimization-overview|the Optimization Overview]] (page 12) shipped the **workflow-level** contract (three inputs — *program + metric + training set*; one output — *optimized program*; 30/300 sizing; inverted 20/80 train/val split; four iteration axes), **this page ships the catalog** — the concrete `dspy.<OptimizerName>` registry enumerates: `LabeledFewShot` / [[BootstrapFewShot|`BootstrapFewShot`]] / [[BootstrapFewShotWithRandomSearch|`BootstrapFewShotWithRandomSearch`]] / `KNNFewShot` / `COPRO` / [[MIPROv2|`MIPROv2`]] / `SIMBA` / [[GEPA|`GEPA`]] / [[BootstrapFinetune|`BootstrapFinetune`]] / `Ensemble` / `BetterTogether`, grouped into five families (Automatic Few-Shot Learning / Automatic Instruction Optimization / Automatic Finetuning / Program Transformations / Meta-Optimizers). Names the historical rename — *"Formerly called teleprompters. We are making an official name update."* Reveals the **composability** claim: optimizers can be chained (`dspy.MIPROv2` then `dspy.BootstrapFinetune`, then top-k extraction into `dspy.Ensemble`) — the **structural essence** of `dspy.BetterTogether`. Three orthogonal what's-being-tuned axes: **demonstrations** (few-shot examples) / **instructions** (natural-language task descriptions) / **LM weights** (fine-tuning); only [[MIPROv2]] tunes more than one axis; only [[BootstrapFinetune]] tunes weights. Five-rule getting-started rubric: **10 examples → [[BootstrapFewShot]]**, **50+ → [[BootstrapFewShotWithRandomSearch]]**, **0-shot prompts → [[MIPROv2]] (0-shot mode)**, **40+ trials + 200+ examples → [[MIPROv2]] (full)**, **post-success efficiency → [[BootstrapFinetune]]**. Documents the **three-stage MIPROv2 algorithm** as the structural template for non-trivial optimizers: bootstrapping → grounded proposal → discrete search via [[BayesianOptimization|Bayesian Optimization]]. Records explicit operating-cost ballpark: *"A typical simple optimization run costs on the order of $2 USD and takes around ten minutes"*; *"a few cents up to tens of dollars"*. Three worked end-to-end receipts: **ReAct + MIPROv2(auto="light") on HotPotQA (24% → 51%)**, **RAG + MIPROv2(auto="medium") with [[llmasjudge|`SemanticF1`]] metric on StackExchange (53% → 61%)**, **Banking77 classification + BootstrapFinetune on `gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18` (66% → 87%, only weight-tuning receipt; 2000 examples; `Literal[tuple(CLASSES)]`-typed [[DSPySignatures|Signature]]; the only `set_lm(...)` exercise in the corpus)**. **Save/load inspectability**: `optimized_program.save(path)` produces plain-text JSON — consistent with DSPy's *"writing code instead of strings"* discipline. **Closes the DSPy *Learn* corpus at 13/13**; **resolves every long-standing forward reference** prior twelve pages carried — [[DSPyOptimizers]], [[BootstrapFewShot]], [[BootstrapFewShotWithRandomSearch]], [[MIPROv2]], [[BootstrapFinetune]], [[GEPA]] (the only optimizer named on page 12 as carve-out from the 20/80 split). Mints 6 concept pages — [[DSPyOptimizers]] (canonical catalog page, sibling to [[DSPyOptimization]] — workflow vs catalog, mirroring [[DSPyEvaluation]] / [[DSPyMetrics]]), [[BootstrapFewShot]], [[BootstrapFewShotWithRandomSearch]], [[MIPROv2]], [[GEPA]], [[BootstrapFinetune]]; folds minor variants (`KNNFewShot` / `COPRO` / `SIMBA` / `Ensemble` / `BetterTogether` / `LabeledFewShot`) into the catalog table on [[DSPyOptimizers]].
- [DSPy Learn — Optimization Overview](sources/dspy-optimization-overview.md) — **Page 12 of 13** of the [[DSPy]] *Learn* documentation and the **opening page of the Optimization stage** in the [[dspy-learn-index|three-stage Programming → Evaluation → Optimization]] model. Where the Programming stage (pages 2–8) defined *how to express* a DSPy program and the Evaluation stage (pages 9–11) defined *how to measure* one, **this page defines *how to improve* one**. The canonical one-sentence definition: *"Once you have a system and a way to evaluate it, you can use DSPy optimizers to tune the prompts or weights in your program."* The page commits the framework to four load-bearing positions: (1) **the optimizer's three inputs are a program, a metric, and a training set** — DSPy's structural answer to *"what does it mean to optimize an LLM pipeline?"*; the output is an **optimized program** (same `dspy.Module` subclass, refined instructions / demonstrations / weights); (2) **training-set size scales from 30 to 300+** — *"You can often get substantial value out of 30 examples, but aim for at least 300 examples"* — an explicit expansion from [[DSPyEvaluation|the Evaluation stage's]] 20–200-example dev set, mirroring the *"start simple, then grow"* discipline at the training-set layer; (3) **the conventional ML train/val split is inverted to 20/80 for most prompt optimizers** — *"For most prompt optimizers, we recommend allocating 20% of your data for training and 80% for validation, contrary to typical deep learning conventions. This is because prompt optimizers tend to overfit on small training sets"* — with the **named exception of [[GEPA]]**, *"the only specific optimizer mentioned on this page"*, which *"follows standard ML practice — maximizing the training set size while keeping the validation set sufficiently sized to represent the downstream task distribution"*; (4) **iterative development spans four axes, not just optimizer-choice** — *"Iterative development is key. DSPy gives you the pieces to do that incrementally"* — across **data, program structure, metric, and optimizer**; three of the six diagnostic questions point **back into the Programming and Evaluation stages**, making the Optimization stage **open under revision from the prior two** (not a black-box terminus). Mints 1 concept page ([[DSPyOptimization]]) — the canonical anchor for the optimization **workflow** (the *fourth artifact* of [[DSPyProgrammingModel|the Programming Model]] — completes the four-artifact picture Signatures / Modules / Adapters / Optimizers at the workflow level alongside [[DSPyEvaluation|Evaluation]] as the connective stage between Programming and Optimization). Deliberately defers the **catalog** of specific optimizers ([[BootstrapFewShot]], [[BootstrapFewShotWithRandomSearch]], [[MIPROv2]], [[BootstrapFinetune]], [[GEPA]], and others) to page 13 ([[DSPyOptimizers|Optimizers]]) — the split mirrors the [[DSPyEvaluation]] / [[DSPyMetrics]] precedent of one page anchoring the workflow and the sibling page anchoring the per-algorithm machinery. The wiki's coverage of the [[DSPy]] *Learn* corpus is now 12/13; the single remaining sibling ingest ([[DSPyOptimizers|Optimizers]], page 13) will fill in the optimizer registry and resolve the [[DSPyOptimizers]] / [[BootstrapFewShot]] / [[BootstrapFewShotWithRandomSearch]] / [[MIPROv2]] / [[BootstrapFinetune]] / [[GEPA]] forward references this page carries.
- [DSPy Learn — Metrics](sources/dspy-metrics.md) — **Page 11 of 13** of the [[DSPy]] *Learn* documentation; **third page of the [[DSPyEvaluation|Evaluation stage]]** (after [[dspy-evaluation-overview|the Evaluation Overview]] page 9 and [[dspy-data|Data Handling]] page 10). Expands **Step 2** of the four-step iterative-evaluation loop — *"define a DSPy metric"* — into the concrete **`(example, pred, trace=None) -> score`** function-signature contract every DSPy artifact composes against. Canonical claim: *"A DSPy metric is just a function in Python that takes `example` (e.g., from your training or dev set) and the output `pred` from your DSPy program, and outputs a `float` (or `int` or `bool`) score."* The page sharpens [[dspy-evaluation-overview|the Evaluation Overview's]] *"a function that takes examples from your data and takes the output of your system, and returns a score"* into a **typed Python function signature** with three structurally important properties: (a) **type-symmetric on the data side** — because [[DSPyPrediction|`dspy.Prediction`]] is a subclass of [[DSPyExample|`dspy.Example`]] ([[dspy-data|page 10]]), the metric author writes `example.answer == pred.answer` with no class-aware branching; (b) **regime-asymmetric on the calling side** — the optional third argument `trace` switches behavior between **evaluation/optimization** (`trace is None`, returns continuous `float`/`int`) and **bootstrapping** (`trace is not None`, returns strict `bool` for demo selection); (c) **scalar return** — `float` / `int` / `bool` are the only valid return types. Two regimes the Overview only named: **simple metrics** (one-line scalar comparisons — `example.answer.lower() == pred.answer.lower()`; built-ins `dspy.evaluate.metrics.answer_exact_match` and `dspy.evaluate.metrics.answer_passage_match`) for short-form tasks, and **AI-feedback metrics** (a `class Assess(dspy.Signature)` rubric template plus N `dspy.Predict(Assess)` invocations summed and thresholded) for long-form tasks — DSPy's structural operationalization of the [[llmasjudge|LLM-as-judge]] pattern. The tweet metric receipt is the canonical hybrid pattern: **multi-property AI judgment** (two `Predict(Assess)` calls) + **deterministic hard gate** (`len(tweet) <= 280`) + **regime-dependent return type** (`score >= 2` for bootstrap, `score / 2.0` for evaluation) — the wiki's first explicit demonstration that a DSPy metric is **not all-or-nothing AI-feedback**; it mixes LLM-as-judge with deterministic gates. Documents the **trace-aware bootstrap recipe** `validate_hops` — the only intermediate-step validator in the *Learn* corpus so far, inspecting `[outputs.query for *_, outputs in trace if 'query' in outputs]` to filter degenerate multi-hop trajectories at bootstrap-time. Operationalizes the **recursive-metric-optimization** claim ([[DSPyEvaluation|Step 4]] of the four-step loop) — the AI-feedback metric is itself a DSPy program (calls `dspy.Predict(Assess)`) and therefore is **optimizable by a [[DSPyOptimizers|DSPy Optimizer]]** the same way the system program is. Closes with **`dspy.Evaluate`** — the parallel dev-set-evaluation harness — documented via the four-kwarg construction signature (`devset` / `num_threads` / `display_progress` / `display_table`) and the **reusable two-phase pattern** (construct once with the dev set; call multiple times with `(program, metric)` pairs). Mints 2 concept pages — [[DSPyMetrics]] (the canonical `(example, pred, trace) -> score` contract; **resolves the long-standing forward reference** carried by [[DSPyEvaluation]] / [[dspy-evaluation-overview]] / [[dspy-data]] / [[DSPyExample]] / [[DSPyPrediction]] / every prior DSPy ingest) and [[DSPyEvaluate]] (the dev-set-evaluation utility — a thread-parallel wrapper around the raw `for x in devset: pred = program(**x.inputs()); score = metric(x, pred)` loop with progress + tabular display). Two sibling ingests remain to close the *Learn* corpus at 13/13: page 12 (Optimization Overview), page 13 ([[DSPyOptimizers|Optimizers]]).
- [DSPy Learn — Data Handling](sources/dspy-data.md) — **Page 10 of 13** of the [[DSPy]] *Learn* documentation; **second page of the [[DSPyEvaluation|Evaluation stage]]** (after [[dspy-evaluation-overview|the Evaluation Overview]]). Expands **Step 1** of the four-step iterative-evaluation loop — *"collect an initial development set"* — into the concrete **data container** every other DSPy artifact reads from. Canonical claim: DSPy's data primitive is a typed Python dict-with-utilities — [[DSPyExample|`dspy.Example`]] — that (a) accepts arbitrary field names and value types (*"Examples can have any field keys and any value types, though usually values are strings"*), (b) carries an **input/label separation** as attached `input_keys` metadata rather than a structural partition (the `with_inputs("field1", ...)` method tags inputs; `inputs()` / `labels()` return non-mutating partition views), and (c) is the **parent class** that [[DSPyPrediction|`dspy.Prediction`]] subclasses (*"Your DSPy modules will return values of the type `Prediction`, which is a special sub-class of `Example`"*) — making the [[DSPyMetrics|metric]]'s `(example, prediction) -> score` contract type-symmetric. The page commits the framework to three load-bearing positions: (1) *"DSPy is a machine learning framework, so working in it involves training sets, development sets, and test sets"* — locates DSPy inside the supervised-ML tradition rather than presenting it as a separate paradigm; (2) **datasets are plain Python lists** of `dspy.Example` (*"trainset = [dspy.Example(report=..., summary=...), ...]"*) — DSPy does **not** introduce a `Dataset` class, a `train_test_split(...)` helper, or HuggingFace / CSV / JSON loaders; train/dev/test splits are Python slicing; (3) **inputs-only sufficiency** — *"You can use DSPy effectively without any intermediate or final labels, but you will need at least a few example inputs"* — the data-side mirror of [[dspy-evaluation-overview|the Evaluation Overview's]] *intermediate-step labels are almost never needed* commitment. The compact API surface — `dspy.Example(**fields)` construction, dot-notation access, `with_inputs(...)` tagging, `inputs()` / `labels()` partition accessors — is deliberately small; the framework reuses Python's `list` and `dict` semantics for everything that does not need framework-level machinery. Mints 2 concept pages — [[DSPyExample]] (the data primitive) and [[DSPyData]] (the dataset / split convention) — and **resolves both long-standing forward references** carried by [[DSPyEvaluation]] / [[dspy-evaluation-overview]] since the Evaluation stage opened on page 9.
- [DSPy Learn — Evaluation Overview](sources/dspy-evaluation-overview.md) — **Page 9 of 13** of the [[DSPy]] *Learn* documentation and the **opening page of the Evaluation stage** in the [[dspy-learn-index|three-stage Programming → Evaluation → Optimization]] model. Operationalizes the Evaluation stage as a **four-step iterative loop**: (1) collect an initial development set of 20–200 examples — *"Even 20 input examples of your task can be useful, though 200 goes a long way"* — from adjacent public datasets ([[HuggingFace]] / StackExchange) → permissive-license re-use → manual labeling → deployed-demo collection; (2) define a DSPy metric as a callable `(example, prediction) -> score` — scalar `accuracy` for simple tasks, a **smaller DSPy program** for long-form tasks (DSPy's structural operationalization of the [[llmasjudge|LLM-as-judge]] pattern); (3) run development evaluations to produce a **baseline score** + a **qualitative diagnostic** that may force a return to the Programming stage rather than proceed forward; (4) (recursive) optimize the metric itself when it is a DSPy program — *"That's usually easy because the output of the metric is usually a simple value (e.g., a score out of 5), so the metric's metric is easy to define and optimize by collecting a few examples"*. Three load-bearing commitments distinguish DSPy Evaluation from generic ML evaluation: **small dev sets are sufficient** (20-example floor; 200-example ceiling for diminishing returns); **intermediate-step labels are almost never needed** — *"You almost never need labels for the intermediate steps in your program in DSPy"* — DSPy's structural answer to the intermediate-supervision problem in chain-of-thought training; **the metric is itself iterative** — *"Invest in defining metrics and improving them incrementally over time"* — the [[DSPyProgrammingModel|"start simple, then grow"]] discipline from page 2 restated at the metric layer. Mints 1 concept page ([[DSPyEvaluation]]) as the canonical anchor for DSPy's evaluation philosophy. Motivates the next two pages — **Data Handling** (page 10, forward reference [[DSPyData]]) which will expand Step 1 into [[DSPyExample|`dspy.Example`]] mechanics, and **[[DSPyMetrics|Metrics]]** (page 11, forward reference) which will expand Step 2 into the full `(example, prediction) -> score` contract — without overstepping into either; the deliberate scope limit lets sibling ingests fill in the data-handling and metric machinery.
- [DSPy Learn — MCP](sources/dspy-mcp.md) — **Page 8 of 13** of the [[DSPy]] *Learn* documentation. Defines DSPy's integration with the **[[ModelContextProtocol|Model Context Protocol (MCP)]]** — [[anthropic|Anthropic]]'s open protocol that standardizes how applications expose tools, resources, and context to language models. **DSPy does not manage MCP server connections directly**; the user opens a `ClientSession` via the `mcp` Python SDK and uses **[[DSPyMCP|`dspy.Tool.from_mcp_tool(session, tool)`]]** to convert each MCP-side tool descriptor into a [[DSPyTools|`dspy.Tool`]] instance. Converted tools then compose through every existing DSPy pathway — [[react|`dspy.ReAct`]] as the canonical entry point — without any further MCP-aware code. Two transports: **stdio** (`stdio_client` + `StdioServerParameters` for local processes) and **streamable HTTP** (`streamablehttp_client` for remote servers). Both share the same `ClientSession` API once open — the conversion code is byte-identical across transports. **MCP execution is asynchronous end-to-end**: [[react|`dspy.ReAct`]] must be invoked via `.acall(...)` and the agent invocation must live inside the `async with` session block (the session closes when the block exits; further tool calls would fail). Installation: `pip install -U "dspy[mcp]"`. Mints 2 concept pages — [[ModelContextProtocol]] (the framework-agnostic protocol; **resolves the long-standing forward reference** carried by [[DSPy]] / [[DSPyTools]] / [[dspy-learn-index]] / [[dspy-tools]]) and [[DSPyMCP]] (the DSPy-specific binding, lighter-weight; the split mirrors the [[LiteLLM]] / [[DSPyLM]] precedent of protocol/library upstream + framework-binding downstream). Updates [[anthropic|Anthropic]] entity page in-place with MCP-authorship attribution — a new wiki role for Anthropic alongside its frontier-model and managed-API-provider roles. **First external tool-source protocol the corpus records** — confirms the [[DSPyTools|`dspy.Tool`]] abstraction is open under tool origin (local function vs MCP server) and vindicates the [[dspy-tools|page-7]] async-tool surface (`tool.acall(...)`, `dspy.context(allow_tool_async_sync_conversion=True)`) as load-bearing infrastructure rather than corner-case feature.
- [DSPy Tutorial — Use MCP Tools in DSPy (Airline Agent)](sources/dspy-mcp-tutorial.md) — Official [[DSPy]] tutorial at `https://dspy.ai/tutorials/mcp/`. **Canonical applied receipt** for the [[DSPyMCP|DSPy ⇄ MCP binding]] — supplies the whole-program worked example the [[dspy-mcp|Learn — MCP page]]'s API-surface snippets pointed at. Stands up a **seven-tool airline-domain [[FastMCP]] server** in ~150 lines (`mcp = FastMCP("Airline Agent")` + `@mcp.tool()` decorators on `fetch_flight_info` / `fetch_itinerary` / `pick_flight` / `book_itinerary` / `cancel_itinerary` / `get_user_info` / `file_ticket`), drives it from a `dspy.ReAct(DSPyAirlineCustomerService, tools=dspy_tools)` agent whose Signature is two fields (`user_request: str` → `process_result: str`), and runs the whole thing via `asyncio.run(...)` with a `stdio_client` + `ClientSession` `async with` nest. **MCP variant of [[dspy-customer-service-agent]]** — same five-class [[Pydantic]] domain (`Date` / `UserProfile` / `Flight` / `Itinerary` / `Ticket`), same airline booking domain, same canonical request (`"please help me book a flight from SFO to JFK on 09/01/2025, my name is Adam"`), but tools now sit behind MCP packaging instead of being passed as plain Python callables; the diff isolates the **MCP packaging layer** as the only variable and confirms [[DSPyMCP|the binding's]] *"MCP-converted tools are indistinguishable from local-function tools after conversion"* claim. **First whole-program MCP server in the wiki corpus** — prior MCP ingests ([[dspy-mcp]]) were client-side API snippets. **First wiki-corpus appearance of [[FastMCP]]** (entity minted) — the decorator-style `mcp.server.fastmcp.FastMCP` helper that lets a Python file declare an MCP server with `mcp = FastMCP("Name")` + `@mcp.tool()` per function + `mcp.run()`. **First wiki-corpus DSPy receipt of serialization-boundary defensive coding** — the `pick_flight` body uses `x.get('duration') if isinstance(x, dict) else x.duration` to accommodate the JSON-wire downgrade from [[Pydantic]] `BaseModel` to plain `dict`. Names two small but portable subpatterns: **(1) deterministic-utility tools** — `pick_flight` pushes ordering / comparison / tie-breaking out of the LM and into deterministic Python the LM merely invokes; **(2) LM-friendly type design** — *"Somehow LLM is bad at specifying `datetime.datetime`"* justifies a custom integer-field `Date(BaseModel)` over Python's built-in `datetime`. Carries the **first explicit hosted-notebook-incompatibility callout** in the DSPy tutorial corpus (*"This tutorial cannot be run in hosted IPython notebooks like Google Colab or Databricks notebooks"*) — stdio child-process spawn is unsupported in those sandboxes. Updates 3 concept pages in-place ([[DSPyMCP]], [[ModelContextProtocol]], [[CustomerServiceAgent]] each gain this tutorial as a second source) plus the [[Pydantic]] entity (now records this corpus's first JSON-wire serialization-boundary receipt).
- [DSPy Learn — Tools](sources/dspy-tools.md) — Page 7 of 13 of the [[DSPy]] *Learn* documentation. Defines the **Tools** sub-system — the primitive DSPy uses to let an [[DSPyLM|LM]] invoke external Python functions. Presents **two equal-status approaches**: **(1)** the **fully-managed** [[react|`dspy.ReAct`]] [[DSPyModules|Module]] (framework-owned think-act-observe loop; the returned [[DSPyPrediction|`Prediction`]] carries a `trajectory` field tracking every reasoning step and tool call) and **(2)** **manual handling** via [[DSPyPredict|`dspy.Predict`]] over a [[DSPySignatures|Signature]] whose input is `tools: list[dspy.Tool]` and whose output is `dspy.ToolCalls` (user owns the loop). Documents the [[DSPyTools|`dspy.Tool`]] wrapper surface — `.name` (from `__name__`), `.desc` (from docstring), `.args` (from type hints + defaults), `str(tool)` (the canonical text the LM sees) — plus the `dspy.ToolCalls` model-output type and the three `ToolCall.execute()` lookup modes (automatic-by-name / `functions={}` dict / `functions=[]` `Tool` list — **requires DSPy 3.0.4b2+**). **Native function calling** is configured at the [[DSPyAdapters|Adapter]] layer via `use_native_function_calling=` (defaults: [[DSPyAdapters|`ChatAdapter`]]=`False`, [[DSPyAdapters|`JSONAdapter`]]=`True`; automatic fallback to text-based parsing for models that don't support it — the **second model-capability scoping** in the [[dspy-learn-index|Learn corpus]] after [[DSPyAdapters|`JSONAdapter`]]'s `response_format` requirement). **Async tools** are first-class via `tool.acall(...)` plus the `dspy.context(allow_tool_async_sync_conversion=True)` sync-from-async opt-in. Three tool-function design rules: clear, detailed docstrings; explicit type hints; prefer basic types or [[Pydantic|Pydantic]] models. Names *void-return tools* as the most informative reason to choose manual handling (managed [[react|`dspy.ReAct`]]'s loop feeds observations back into reasoning, so side-effect-only tools — logging, telemetry, fire-and-forget actions — don't fit). Mints 1 concept page ([[DSPyTools]]) — **resolves the long-standing forward reference** carried by [[DSPy]] / [[DSPyProgrammingModel]] / [[DSPySignatures]] / [[DSPyLM]] / [[DSPyModules]] / [[DSPyAdapters]] / [[react|ReAct]] / [[dspy-learn-index]] / [[dspy-programming-overview]] / [[dspy-language-models]] / [[dspy-signatures]] / [[dspy-modules]] / [[dspy-adapters]] since the corpus opened on 2026-05-17. Extends [[react|ReAct]] in-place with a *managed-vs-manual* duality section rather than minting a parallel `DSPyReAct` page.
- [DSPy Learn — Adapters](sources/dspy-adapters.md) — Page 6 of 13 of the [[DSPy]] *Learn* documentation. **Defines** the **third** of the four orthogonal artifacts [[DSPyProgrammingModel|the Programming Model]] factors out of a conventional prompt — the **Adapter**: *"the bridge between `dspy.Predict` and the actual Language Model (LM)"*. Three responsibilities: (1) convert a [[DSPySignatures|Signature]] into a system message; (2) format input data (multi-turn messages, demo injection, conversation history, function calls, and DSPy-special types — [[DSPyTools|`Tool`]] / `dspy.Image` / `dspy.History`) into the LM's request shape; (3) parse the LM's textual response into a typed [[DSPyPrediction|`dspy.Prediction`]]. Two configuration channels — `dspy.configure(adapter=...)` (global) and `with dspy.context(adapter=...)` (block-local) — mirror the [[DSPyLM|LM]] bind modes. Two introspection hooks: `adapter.format(signature, demos, inputs)` returns the full multi-turn message list; `adapter.format_system_message(signature)` returns only the system message. Documents two built-in adapters in detail: **`dspy.ChatAdapter`** (the default; uses `[[ ## field_name ## ]]` delimiters; inlines JSON schemas for non-primitive types; *"universal compatibility: works with all language models"*; includes **automatic fallback to `JSONAdapter` on failure**; trade-off — *"more boilerplate output tokens compared to other adapters"*) and **`dspy.JSONAdapter`** (uses the LM's native `response_format` parameter — *"effective for models that support structured output"*; minimal boilerplate → lower latency; **model-capability-gated** — *"requires models supporting the `response_format` parameter; incompatible with smaller open-source models lacking this capability"* — the **first explicit model-capability boundary** in the [[dspy-learn-index|Learn corpus]]). Two further built-ins named only — **`dspy.XMLAdapter`** (XML-formatted I/O) and **`dspy.TwoStepAdapter`** (two-step extract-then-format workflow). Custom adapters supported via `Adapter`-subclass + `format()`/`parse()` override. Worked example: the same `NewsQA` [[DSPySignatures|Signature]] with a `list[pydantic.BaseModel]` output runs under both adapters with a **one-kwarg edit** — the page's most explicit *"swap the adapter without touching the signature"* demonstration, the third concrete *"swap N, leave M unchanged"* receipt in the wiki after [[DSPyLM|`dspy.LM`]]'s LM-swap and [[DSPyModules|`dspy.Module`]]'s strategy-swap. Mints 1 concept page ([[DSPyAdapters]]) — **resolves the long-standing forward reference** carried by [[DSPy]] / [[DSPyProgrammingModel]] / [[DSPySignatures]] / [[DSPyLM]] / [[DSPyModules]] / [[dspy-learn-index]] / [[dspy-programming-overview]] / [[dspy-language-models]] / [[dspy-signatures]] / [[dspy-modules]] since the corpus opened on 2026-05-17.
- [DSPy Learn — Modules](sources/dspy-modules.md) — Page 5 of 13 of the [[DSPy]] *Learn* documentation. **Defines** the second of the four orthogonal artifacts [[DSPyProgrammingModel|the Programming Model]] factors out of a conventional prompt — the **Module**: *"a building block for programs that use LMs"*, where *"each built-in module abstracts a prompting technique"* and the same module is *"generalized to handle any signature."* Establishes [[DSPyPredict|`dspy.Predict`]] as the **minimal primitive every other Module is built on top of** (*"Internally, all other DSPy modules are built using `dspy.Predict`"*) and enumerates the seven built-ins: [[DSPyPredict|`dspy.Predict`]] (identity — *"does not modify the signature"*; stores instructions + demonstrations + LM-weight updates), [[ChainOfThought|`dspy.ChainOfThought`]] (*"teaches the LM to think step-by-step"* — adds a `reasoning` field to the user's signature under the hood; *"in many cases, simply swapping `dspy.ChainOfThought` in place of `dspy.Predict` improves quality"*), [[DSPyProgramOfThought|`dspy.ProgramOfThought`]] (*"teaches the LM to output code, whose execution results will dictate the response"*), [[react|`dspy.ReAct`]] (tool-using agent; `tools=[...]` kwarg of plain Python callables), [[DSPyMultiChainComparison|`dspy.MultiChainComparison`]] (N CoT samples + LM comparison Predict), [[DSPyRecursiveLanguageModel|`dspy.RLM`]] (**Recursive Language Model** — sandboxed Python REPL + recursive sub-LLM calls *"when context is too large to fit in the prompt effectively"*), and function-style [[DSPyMajority|`dspy.majority`]] (vote over a set of [[DSPyPrediction|`Prediction`]]s; **zero LM cost**). Composes via `class MyProgram(dspy.Module)` with PyTorch-shaped `__init__` (sub-modules as `self.*` attributes for `named_predictors()` / `named_parameters()` walks that [[DSPyOptimizers|Optimizers]] consume) and `forward(...)`; *"DSPy is just Python code that uses modules in any control flow you like, with a little magic internally at compile time to trace your LM calls."* Documents the LM-usage telemetry surface (DSPy 2.6.16+): `dspy.configure(track_usage=True)` plus `prediction.get_lm_usage()` returning `{provider/model: {prompt/completion/total tokens + details}}` aggregated across every LM call inside `forward()`, with cached responses correctly returning `{}` per [[LiteLLM]]'s cache discipline. Five worked examples (math / RAG / classification with `Literal[...]` / information extraction / ReAct agent) plus the canonical multi-hop search `class Hop(dspy.Module)`. Mints 7 concept pages: [[DSPyModules]] (resolves the long-standing forward reference carried by [[DSPy]] / [[DSPyProgrammingModel]] / [[DSPySignatures]] / [[DSPyLM]] / [[dspy-learn-index]] / [[dspy-programming-overview]] / [[dspy-language-models]] / [[dspy-signatures]]), [[DSPyPredict]], [[DSPyProgramOfThought]], [[DSPyMultiChainComparison]], [[DSPyRecursiveLanguageModel]], [[DSPyMajority]], [[DSPyPrediction]]. Extends [[ChainOfThought]] and [[react|ReAct]] **in place** with *DSPy implementation* sections rather than minting `DSPyChainOfThought` / `DSPyReAct` duplicates.
- [DSPy Learn — Signatures](sources/dspy-signatures.md) — Page 4 of 13 of the [[DSPy]] *Learn* documentation. **Defines** the first of the four orthogonal artifacts [[DSPyProgrammingModel|the Programming Model]] factors out of a conventional prompt — the **Signature**, *"a declarative specification of input/output behavior of a DSPy module"*. Documents both surface forms: **inline** strings like `"sentence -> sentiment: bool"`, `"context: list[str], question: str -> answer: str"` (RAG QA), `"question, choices: list[str] -> reasoning: str, selection: int"` (multi-output) — with an `instructions=` kwarg for top-level guidance; and **class-based** signatures (`class Emotion(dspy.Signature)`) which add three things the inline form cannot — task-description **docstring**, **`dspy.InputField(desc=...)`** input hints, and **`dspy.OutputField(desc=...)`** output constraints. Enumerates the five-tier type system: basic Python (`str` / `int` / `bool`), `typing` composites (`list[str]` / `dict[str, int]` / `Optional[float]` / `Union[str, int]`), arbitrary pydantic models, dot-notation nested types (`MyContainer.Query`), and DSPy-special types `dspy.Image` (multi-modal input via `dspy.Image.from_url(...)`) + `dspy.History` (conversational context). Names `typing.Literal[...]` as the DSPy-idiomatic closed-set classification primitive and demonstrates input-type-checking as warn-not-fail (`dspy.configure(warn_on_type_mismatch=False)` to disable). Most consequential implementation note: *"Many DSPy modules expand signatures under the hood. For example, `dspy.ChainOfThought` adds a `reasoning` field."* — the mechanism that lets a user's `'document -> summary'` Signature acquire a `response.reasoning` slot without the user declaring it. Closes with the framework's value claim: *"their primary value emerges when composing multiple signatures into larger DSPy modules and compiling these into optimized prompts and finetunings."* Mints 1 concept page ([[DSPySignatures]]) — resolves the long-standing forward reference carried by [[DSPy]] / [[DSPyProgrammingModel]] / [[DSPyLM]] / [[dspy-learn-index]] / [[dspy-programming-overview]] / [[dspy-language-models]] since the corpus opened on 2026-05-17.
- [DSPy Learn — Language Models](sources/dspy-language-models.md) — Page 3 of 13 of the [[DSPy]] *Learn* documentation. Operationalizes [[dspy-programming-overview|the Programming Overview's]] *"swap the LM without changing the rest of your logic"* portability claim into a **two-line code change** via the [[DSPyLM|`dspy.LM`]] universal client — `provider/model-name` string + `dspy.configure(lm=...)` (global, thread-safe) or `with dspy.context(lm=...):` (block-local, thread-safe). Names **[[LiteLLM]]** as the upstream provider-abstraction layer DSPy routes through (*"DSPy supports dozens of LLM providers via LiteLLM"*) and demonstrates one API spanning three deployment regimes: **managed** ([[openai|OpenAI]] / [[anthropic|Anthropic]] / [[gemini|Gemini]] / Vertex AI / [[Databricks]] / [[Anyscale]] / [[TogetherAI|Together AI]] / [[microsoft|Azure]]), **self-hosted GPU** ([[SGLang]] via OpenAI-compatible endpoint), and **local laptop** ([[Ollama]]). Adds four framework-level capabilities on top of LiteLLM: default-on **caching** (`cache=False` to disable), **`rollout_id`** deterministic cache-busting (OpenAI / Databricks), per-call **`lm.history`** telemetry (`prompt / messages / kwargs / response / outputs / usage / cost / timestamp / uuid / model / response_model / model_type`), and **`model_type="responses"`** opt-in for [[openai|OpenAI]]'s Responses API. Mints 1 concept ([[DSPyLM]]) and 4 entities ([[LiteLLM]], [[Ollama]], [[SGLang]], [[TogetherAI]]).
- [DSPy Learn — Programming Overview](sources/dspy-programming-overview.md) — Page 2 of 13 of the [[DSPy]] *Learn* documentation; opens the **Programming** stage of the [[dspy-learn-index|three-stage model]] and operationalizes it as **define your task → define your initial pipeline → craft a handful of examples**. Anchors DSPy's framework-level thesis — *"DSPy is a bet on writing code instead of strings"* — and names the **four concerns** a conventional prompt entangles into one non-portable string: **signature** (typed I/O), **adapter** (formatting / parsing), **module logic** (strategy, e.g. "thinking step by step"), and **manual optimization** (trial-and-error). DSPy *separates* these concerns and *automates* the lower-level ones, yielding three concrete portability claims: swap the LM/adapter without touching pipeline code; swap one module for another (`dspy.ChainOfThought` ↔ `dspy.ProgramOfThought`) without modifying [[DSPySignatures|signatures]]; run prompt-optimization *or* weight fine-tuning against the same program. Recommends starting simple — *"perhaps with just a single `dspy.ChainOfThought` module"* — and adding complexity incrementally. Mints one concept page ([[DSPyProgrammingModel]]) covering the separation-of-concerns philosophy.
- [DSPy Learn — Index](sources/dspy-learn-index.md) — Top-level index page of the [[DSPy]] *Learn* documentation. Frames DSPy as a small learnable API for building AI systems through a strict **three-stage development model**: **Programming** ("defining your task, its constraints, exploring a few examples, and using that to inform your initial pipeline design") → **Evaluation** ("collect an initial development set, define your DSPy metric, and use these to iterate on your system more systematically") → **Optimization** ("use DSPy optimizers to tune the prompts or weights in your program"). The stage order is load-bearing: *"it's unproductive to launch optimization runs using a poorly designed program or a bad metric."* Indexes 12 sub-pages — Programming Overview / Language Models / [[DSPySignatures|Signatures]] / [[DSPyModules|Modules]] / [[DSPyAdapters|Adapters]] / [[DSPyTools|Tools]] / [[ModelContextProtocol|MCP]] / Evaluation Overview / Data Handling / [[DSPyMetrics|Metrics]] / Optimization Overview / [[DSPyOptimizers|Optimizers]] — that will be filled in by sibling ingests. **Page 1 of 13** of the DSPy Learn corpus; opens the wiki's first dedicated LLM-programming-framework source cluster.
