- [Attention Is All You Need](sources/1706.03762-attention-is-all-you-need.md) — Vaswani et al. (Google Brain + Google Research + University of Toronto) propose the **Transformer**, a sequence…
- [BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding](sources/1810.04805-bert.md) — Devlin, Chang, Lee & Toutanova (Google AI Language) introduce **BERT** — Bidirectional Encoder Representations from…
- [Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer](sources/1910.10683-t5.md) — Raffel, Shazeer, Roberts et al. (Google) introduce **T5** — the Text-to-Text Transfer Transformer — along with the **C4** corpus and a unified text-to-text framework. Definitive 2020-era controlled ablation of every axis of NLP transfer learning; T5-11B reaches SOTA on 18 of 24 benchmarks (GLUE 90.3, SuperGLUE 88.9 — within 0.9 of human).
- [Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models](sources/2001.08361-scaling-laws.md) — Kaplan, McCandlish et al. (OpenAI + Johns Hopkins) establish empirical **power-law scaling** of Transformer LM cross-entropy loss in $N$ (params), $D$ (tokens), $C$ (compute) across 7+ orders of magnitude; architecture shape is second-order. Derives the **compute-efficient training** regime — very large models, modest data, stop short of convergence — that anchored the GPT-3 era and successor scale-up.
- [Position: LLMs Can't Plan, But Can Help Planning in LLM-Modulo Frameworks](sources/2402.01817-llm-modulo.md) — Kambhampati et al. ([[ArizonaStateUniversity]]) argue autoregressive LLMs cannot plan or self-verify autonomously (PlanBench: ~12% on Blocksworld, ~0% on Mystery BW) but can be enormously useful in an **LLM-Modulo Framework** — a Generate-Test-Critique loop where the LLM proposes candidates and external sound critics (e.g. VAL) supply correctness. 82% on Blocksworld via 15 backprompt rounds; 6× over CoT/ReAct on TravelPlanner.
- [FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness](sources/2205.14135-flashattention.md) — Dao, Fu, Ermon, Rudra & Ré (Stanford + Buffalo SUNY) introduce **FlashAttention** — IO-aware, exact, fused-kernel attention. 7.6× speedup on GPT-2, first Transformer to beat chance on Path-X (16K); now the default attention implementation for modern Transformers.
- [Gemini: A Family of Highly Capable Multimodal Models](sources/2312.11805-gemini.md) — Gemini Team, [[GoogleDeepMind]] introduce **Gemini 1.0** (Ultra / Pro / Nano) — natively-multimodal Transformer-decoder foundation models. First to exceed human-expert MMLU (90.04%); SOTA on 30/32 reported benchmarks; defines the frontier-multimodal-deployment template (three-size family, native multimodality, RLHF flywheel, dangerous-capabilities evaluation) adopted across the field.
- [DSPy Assertions: Computational Constraints for Self-Refining Language Model Pipelines](sources/2312.13382-dspy-assertions.md) — Singhvi, Shetty, Tan, Potts, Sen, Zaharia & Khattab ([[UCBerkeley]] + [[stanforduniversity|Stanford]], arXiv:2312.13382v2, Dec 2023 / Feb 2024) introduce **[[LMAssertions|LM Assertions]]** — first-class `Assert` / `Suggest` programming constructs that express arbitrary computational constraints on [[DSPy]] module outputs and enforce them via retry-with-feedback. Defines big-step operational semantics for retry-counted states $\sigma_r$, and ships three assertion-driven optimizations on top of [[BootstrapFewShotWithRandomSearch|`BootstrapFewShotWithRandomSearch`]]: **[[AssertionDrivenBacktracking|backtracking]]** (inference-time, failing module re-invoked with prior output + error message injected), **[[AssertionDrivenExampleBootstrapping|example bootstrapping]]** (teacher uses backtracking during demo collection — bootstrapped few-shots satisfy every assertion at every intermediate module), and **[[CounterexampleBootstrapping|counterexample bootstrapping]]** (failure-then-fix traces become negative few-shot demonstrations). Evaluated on four [[hotpotqa|HotPotQA]]-derived tasks ([[MultiHopQA]] / [[LongFormQA]] / [[QuizGen]] / [[TweetGen]]) over `gpt-3.5-turbo` + [[ColBERTv2]] retrieval — combining compile-time + inference-time strategies (`C+Infer w/ Assert`) lifts **[[QuizGen]] valid-JSON output from 37.6% → 100%**, **QuizGen composite Validity 30.5% → 87.2%**, **[[TweetGen]] No-"#" 21.3% → 96.2%**, and **[[MultiHopQA]] Suggestions Passed 66.3% → 95.7%**. Identifies the **conflicting-suggestions failure mode** (sequential `Suggest` statements can override each other during self-refinement — Engaging drops when stacked with No-#/Concise/Faithful in [[TweetGen]]) and shows assertion-driven pipelines are **less sensitive to instruction quality** under deliberately minimal prompts. Released as `dspy.Assert` / `dspy.Suggest` in [[DSPy]]; **predates** [[2406.11695-mipro|MIPRO]] / [[2407.10930-better-together|BetterTogether]] / [[2507.19457-gepa|GEPA]] in the DSPy-adjacent research arc and supplies the *runtime self-refinement primitive* the later optimization papers tacitly rely on. **Mints 10 concept pages** ([[LMAssertions]], [[DSPyAssert]], [[DSPySuggest]], [[AssertionDrivenBacktracking]], [[AssertionDrivenExampleBootstrapping]], [[CounterexampleBootstrapping]], [[MultiHopQA]], [[LongFormQA]], [[QuizGen]], [[TweetGen]]) + **3 entity pages** ([[ArnavSinghvi]], [[ManishShetty]], [[ShangyinTan]]). Resolves the long-standing [[DSPyAssertions]] forward reference carried since the DSPy Learn corpus closed.
- [Optimizing Instructions and Demonstrations for Multi-Stage Language Model Programs](sources/2406.11695-mipro.md) — [[KristaOpsahlOng|Opsahl-Ong]], [[MichaelJRyan|Ryan]], [[JoshPurtell|Purtell]], [[DavidBroman|Broman]], [[ChristopherPotts|Potts]], [[MateiZaharia|Zaharia]] & [[OmarKhattab|Khattab]] ([[stanforduniversity|Stanford]] + [[BasisAI|Basis]] + [[KTH]] + [[UCBerkeley]], EMNLP 2024, arXiv:2406.11695v2) — **the canonical paper for [[MIPROv2|MIPRO]]** (**M**ulti-prompt **I**nstruction **PR**oposal **O**ptimizer). Formalizes [[PromptOptimization|prompt optimization]] for multi-stage [[LMProgram|LM programs]] $\Phi$ as $\Phi^* = \arg\max_{\mathbf{V}\mapsto S}\frac{1}{|\mathcal{D}|}\sum\mu(\Phi_{\mathbf{V}\mapsto S}(x), x')$; identifies two challenges — the **proposal challenge** (intractable string space) and the **[[CreditAssignment|credit-assignment challenge]]** (no per-module labels). Algorithm 1 templates a generic `Initialize → Propose → Update → ExtractOptimizedSets` LM-program optimizer. Three proposal strategies ([[BootstrapDemonstrations|bootstrap demos]] / **grounding** with dataset+program+demo context / **learning to propose** with [[BayesianOptimization|Bayesian]] meta-model over proposer hyperparameters) × three credit-assignment strategies (greedy / **[[TreeStructuredParzenEstimator|TPE]] surrogate** via [[Optuna]] / history-based [[OPRO]]) instantiates the optimizer family — [[BootstrapRandomSearch|Bootstrap Random Search]] (Khattab et al. 2024 baseline, demos-only), Bayesian Bootstrap, [[ModuleLevelOPRO|Module-Level OPRO]] (instructions-only, extension of [[OPRO|Yang et al. 2023]]), **MIPRO** (joint), 0-Shot MIPRO, 0-Shot MIPRO++, Program-Level OPRO, CA-OPRO. **MIPRO wins 5/7 tasks** by up to **13% absolute** on the new [[DSPyOptimizerBenchmark|DSPy Optimizer Benchmark]] ([[hotpotqa|HotPotQA]] / [[HotPotQAConditional]] / [[Iris]] / [[IrisTypo]] / [[HeartDisease]] / [[ScoNe]] / [[HoVer]]) with [[Llama3_8BInstruct|Llama-3-8B]] as task LM, GPT-3.5 as proposer (GPT-4o teacher for hard tasks), 20–50 trials per run × 5 runs, Wilcoxon signed-rank significance. **Five lessons** — (L1) bootstrapped demos are essential, (L2) joint optimization wins overall, (L3) **instruction optimization wins on conditional-rule tasks** (HotPotQA-Conditional / Iris-Typo / Heart-Disease — even **corrects the misspelled "versicolour" seed prompt** in Iris-Typo), (L4) grounding helps overall but **best proposal strategy varies by task** (motivates MIPRO++), (L5) optimizer rankings vary with budget. **Mints 1 source page + 12 concept pages** ([[LMProgram]], [[OPRO]], [[ModuleLevelOPRO]], [[BootstrapRandomSearch]], [[BootstrapDemonstrations]], [[TreeStructuredParzenEstimator]], [[Optuna]], [[DSPyOptimizerBenchmark]], [[HotPotQAConditional]], [[IrisTypo]], [[HeartDisease]], [[ScoNe]]) + 6 entity pages ([[KristaOpsahlOng]], [[MichaelJRyan]], [[JoshPurtell]], [[DavidBroman]], [[BasisAI|Basis]], [[KTH]]). **Promotes [[MIPROv2]] from DSPy-docs-only to paper-anchored.** Updates [[hotpotqa]], [[HoVer]], [[Iris]], [[BayesianOptimization]], [[OmarKhattab]], [[ChristopherPotts]], [[MateiZaharia]], [[stanforduniversity]], [[UCBerkeley]] in place.
- [Fine-Tuning and Prompt Optimization: Two Great Steps that Work Better Together](sources/2407.10930-better-together.md) — [[DilaraSoylu|Soylu]], [[ChristopherPotts|Potts]] & [[OmarKhattab|Khattab]] ([[stanforduniversity|Stanford]], arXiv 2024) introduce **[[BetterTogether]]** — the first published bi-axial optimizer for [[CompoundAISystem|compound AI systems]] that **alternates prompt optimization (Π) and weight fine-tuning (Θ)**. Algorithm 1's three-step schedule `Π → Θ → Π` instantiates with [[BootstrapFewShotWithRandomSearch|BFRS]] for prompt steps and [[BootstrapFinetune|BFT]] for the weight step. Three tasks ([[hotpotqa|HotPotQA]] / [[GSM8K]] / [[Iris]]) × three LMs ([[Mistral7BInstructV02|Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2]] / [[Llama2_7BChat|Llama-2-7B-chat]] / [[Llama3_8BInstruct|Llama-3-8B-Instruct]]) = 9 cells; **BetterTogether wins in 7/9**. Gains over the better single-axis baseline: **5–78% HotPotQA, 2.5–10% GSM8K, 3.5–88% Iris**. Released as `dspy.BetterTogether` in [[DSPy]]; introduces the $\Phi_{\langle\Theta,\Pi\rangle}$ formalism that [[2507.19457-gepa|GEPA (ICLR 2026)]] subsequently adopts. **Mints 1 new concept page ([[BetterTogether]])** + 1 new benchmark concept ([[Iris]]) + 3 new LM entity stubs ([[Mistral7BInstructV02]], [[Llama2_7BChat]], [[Llama3_8BInstruct]]) + 1 new entity ([[DilaraSoylu]]). **Resolves the dangling `[[soylu2024fine]]` link in [[CompoundAISystem]]**.
- [GEPA: Reflective Prompt Evolution Can Outperform Reinforcement Learning](sources/2507.19457-gepa.md) — Agrawal, Tan, Soylu, Ziems et al. ([[UCBerkeley]] + [[stanforduniversity|Stanford]] + [[BespokeLabsAI]] + [[NotreDame]] + [[Databricks]] + [[MITAcademic|MIT]]; senior authors [[MateiZaharia]] / [[OmarKhattab]] / [[DanKlein]] / [[IonStoica]] / [[AlexandrosDimakis]] / [[ChristopherPotts]]) introduce **GEPA (Genetic-Pareto)** — a [[ReflectivePromptMutation|reflective prompt mutation]] + [[ParetoBasedCandidateSelection|Pareto-based candidate selection]] + optional [[SystemAwareMerge|System Aware Merge]] crossover optimizer for [[CompoundAISystem|compound AI systems]] that **outperforms [[grpo|GRPO]] RL by up to 20% with up to 35× fewer rollouts** and beats [[MIPROv2]] by >10% (+12% on AIME-2025). Six benchmarks ([[hotpotqa|HotpotQA]], [[IFBench]], [[HoVer]], [[PUPA]], [[AIME2025|AIME-2025]], [[LiveBenchMath]]) × two models (Qwen3 8B, GPT-4.1 Mini). Adds [[FeedbackFunction|feedback function]] $\mu_f$ that extends scalar reward with [[EvaluationTrace|evaluation-trace text]]. Demonstrates [[InferenceTimeSearch|inference-time search]] (30.52% mean vector utilization on AMD XDNA2 [[NPUEval]]; >20% $fast_1$ on [[KernelBench]] CUDA) and [[AdversarialPromptSearch|adversarial prompt search]] (drops GPT-5 Mini AIME-2025 pass@1 from 76% → 10%). **ICLR 2026 Oral.** Mints **10 new concept pages** ([[ReflectivePromptMutation]], [[ParetoBasedCandidateSelection]], [[SystemAwareMerge]], [[FeedbackFunction]], [[EvaluationTrace]], [[CompoundAISystem]], [[GeneticPareto]], [[InferenceTimeSearch]], [[AdversarialPromptSearch]], [[XDNA2]]) + **6 benchmark concept pages** ([[IFBench]], [[HoVer]], [[PUPA]], [[AIME2025]], [[LiveBenchMath]], [[NPUEval]], [[KernelBench]]) and **promotes [[GEPA]] from DSPy-docs-only to paper-anchored**; mints **12 entity pages** ([[UCBerkeley]], [[BespokeLabsAI]], [[NotreDame]], [[MITAcademic]], [[LakshyaAgrawal]], [[OmarKhattab]], [[MateiZaharia]], [[DanKlein]], [[IonStoica]], [[ChristopherPotts]], [[AlexandrosDimakis]], [[KoushikSen]], [[MengJiang]]).
- [DSPy Guardrails: Building Safe LLM Applications via Self-Refining Language Model Pipelines](sources/dspy-guardrails.md) — [[BoxiYu|Yu]] & [[PinjiaHe|He]] ([[CUHKShenzhen|CUHK-Shenzhen]], 2024) propose **[[DSPyGuardrails]]**: build LLM safety guardrails as automatically-optimized [[DSPy]] programs rather than hand-written rules. Two-step recipe: define an [[LMProgram|LLM Program]] with a `guardrails` [[DSPySignatures|signature]] field over [[ChainOfThought|`dspy.ChainOfThought`]], then optimize with [[BootstrapFewShot]] on a jailbreak dataset. On [[CodeAttack]] vs gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct, **[[AttackSuccessRate|ASR]] drops 75% → 5%** (vs 30% without the optimizer — the optimizer is load-bearing). Critiques [[LlamaGuard]] / [[NeMoGuardrails]] / [[GuardrailsAI]] as **manual-configuration baselines** that can't keep up with evolving [[Jailbreak|jailbreaks]]. Single-attack, single-model, 20-prompt eval — narrow but early evidence that auto-optimized prompt programs are competitive with hand-engineered safety rules. **Earliest DSPy-as-safety-tool paper** in this wiki; predates [[2406.11695-mipro|MIPRO]] / [[2407.10930-better-together|BetterTogether]] / [[2507.19457-gepa|GEPA]] as stronger successor optimizers for the same application slot.
- [MedVAL: Toward Expert-Level Medical Text Validation with Language Models](sources/2507.03152-medval.md) — [[AsadAali|Aali]], Bikia, Varma, Chiou, Ostmeier, Singhvi, ... [[AkshayChaudhari|Chaudhari]] ([[stanforduniversity|Stanford University]] + [[StanfordMIMI]], arXiv:2507.03152v5, 6 Feb 2026). Introduces **[[MedVAL]]** — self-supervised distillation method for training LM validators of clinical text without physician labels or reference outputs. Three stages: (1) synthetic data generation with controlled perturbations $\delta \in \{0, 0.33, 0.67, 1.0\}$ mapped to a physician-defined 4-class **[[RiskLevelTaxonomy|risk taxonomy]]**, (2) filter via the **[[GeneratorValidatorConsistency|$\mathcal{M}_\mathrm{MedVAL}$ consistency metric]]**, (3) **[[BootstrapFinetune|`dspy.BootstrapFinetune`]] + [[QLoRA]]** PEFT (the paper contributes QLoRA support back into [[DSPy]] via a GitHub PR). Releases **[[MedVALBench]]** (6 tasks × 840 physician-annotated outputs, 12-physician panel including 7 internal-medicine MDs + 5 radiologists + 3 bilingual residents), **[[MedVAL4B|MedVAL-4B]]** (Qwen3-4B base, F1 = 0.527 — best open-source), and the 4-class risk taxonomy. Headline: average baseline F1 **36.7% → 51.0%** ($p < 0.001$) across 10 LMs; safe/unsafe binary F1 **66.2% → 82.8%**; GPT-4o MedVAL F1 = **0.587** (best overall) is **statistically non-inferior to a single human expert** on multi-annotated subsets (paired bootstrap B=10,000, $p < 0.001$). **[[MedVAL4B|MedVAL-Qwen3-4B]] (4B, open) beats baselines of MedGemma-27B / Llama-3.3-70B / GPT-4o Mini / Gemini 2.0 Flash** — task-aware distillation beats domain pre-adaptation at 7× smaller scale. Generalizes +84% F1 on **unseen** tasks (impression2simplified, bhc2spanish, dialogue2note) and +5.3% accuracy on external **[[MEDEC]]** benchmark from [[MedHELM]]. **MedVAL-Pearson-correlation with physicians = 0.825** (GPT-4o) / **0.833** (Qwen3-4B); [[AlignScore]] = 0.678; [[BERTScore]] = 0.141; [[ROUGE]]-L = 0.259 — *"reference-based similarity is not a faithful proxy for reference-free clinical risk grading."* **First wiki paper to extend [[DSPy]]'s local PEFT pipeline with QLoRA**, first to apply `dspy.BootstrapFinetune` to clinical safety, first to show **LLM-as-a-judge non-inferiority to a physician** on medical text. Mints **29 new concept pages** ([[MedVAL]], [[MedVALBench]], [[MedVAL4B]], [[RiskLevelTaxonomy]], [[MedicalTextValidation]], [[GeneratorValidatorConsistency]], [[QLoRA]], [[MedGemma]], [[LLMAsAJudge]], [[MEDEC]], [[MedHELM]], [[FActScore]], [[GREEN]], [[MedHAL]], [[VeriFact]], [[DocLens]], [[ReXTrust]], [[ReXErr]], [[FineRadScore]], [[NonInferiorityTest]], [[McNemarTest]], [[KrippendorffAlpha]], [[CohensKappa]], [[MedicationQA]], [[MeQSum]], [[Openi]], [[MIMICIV]], [[MIMICIVBHC]], [[ACIBench]]) + **13 new entity pages** ([[AsadAali]], [[AkshayChaudhari]], [[EmilyAlsentzer]], [[DaveVanVeen]], [[ChristianBluethgen]], [[SanmiKoyejo]], [[CurtisLangloo]], [[JasonHom]], [[RoxanaDaneshjou]], [[StanfordMIMI]], [[ARPAH]], [[MIDRC]], [[VanVeen2024]]). Updates [[DSPy]] / [[stanforduniversity]] / [[BootstrapFinetune]] / [[lora]] / [[qwen]] / [[AlignScore]] / [[BERTScore]] / [[ROUGE]] / [[Hallucination]] / [[F1Score]] / [[knowledgedistillation]] / [[MIMIC]] in place.
- [Neural at ArchEHR-QA 2025: Agentic Prompt Optimization for Evidence-Grounded Clinical QA](sources/2025-bionlp-archehr-qa-neural.md) — [[SaiPrasannaTejaReddy|Reddy]], Majeedi, Gajjala, Xu, Rai & Potlapalli ([[universityofchicago|University of Chicago]] — the **[[Ours_Neural|Neural]]** team), BioNLP 2025 Shared Tasks pp. 104–109, 1 Aug 2025. **Runner-up (2nd place, overall 51.5)** at the [[ArchEHRQA2025|ArchEHR-QA 2025]] shared task on [[EvidenceGroundedQA|evidence-grounded clinical QA]] over [[MIMIC]]-derived EHR notes. Decomposes the task into a two-stage [[LMProgram|LM program]] — (1) sentence-level **essentiality classification** with [[selfconsistency|self-consistency]] $R=5$ majority vote, (2) **answer synthesis** ≤75 words with explicit citations — and **optimizes each stage's prompt end-to-end with [[MIPROv2|`dspy.MIPROv2`]]** ([[2406.11695-mipro|Opsahl-Ong et al. 2024]]) on the 20-case dev split. Backbone [[GPT4_1|GPT-4.1]] at 10k context; temp 0.3 during optimization, temp 0.7 during $R=5$ stochastic sampling. Stage 2's composite reward = $\mathbb{1}[\le 75\text{ words}] + \mathbb{1}[\text{format}] + \tfrac{1}{6}\sum_m m$ over $m \in \{[[bleu|BLEU]], [[ROUGE]], [[SARI]], [[BERTScore]], [[AlignScore]], [[MEDCON]]\}$. **Beats few-shot baseline by 10 points, zero-shot by 20** — empirical case for prompt optimization as a cost-effective alternative to fine-tuning when supervised clinical data is scarce. **First peer-reviewed shared-task placement to use MIPROv2 in clinical NLP**. Mints **10 new concept pages** ([[ArchEHRQA2025]], [[MIMIC]], [[emrQA]], [[BERTScore]], [[AlignScore]], [[MEDCON]], [[ROUGE]], [[SARI]], [[EvidenceGroundedQA]], [[GPT4_1]]) + **11 new entity pages** ([[SaiPrasannaTejaReddy]], [[Ours_Neural]], [[SarveshSoni]], [[DinaDemnerFushman]], [[BioNLP2025]], [[DMISLab]], [[LAILab]], [[LAMAR_BioNLP]], [[AnusriPampari]], [[TianyiZhang]], [[WenwaiYim]]). Updates [[universityofchicago]] / [[MIPROv2]] / [[selfconsistency]] / [[bleu]] / [[PromptOptimization]] in place.

- [Prompt Optimization Is a Coin Flip: Diagnosing When It Helps in Compound AI Systems](sources/2604.14585-prompt-optimization-coin-flip.md) — [[XingZhang|Zhang]], [[GuanghuiWang|Wang]], [[YanweiCui|Cui]], [[WeiQiu|Qiu]], [[ZiyuanLi|Li]], [[BingZhu|Zhu]] & [[PeiyangHe|He]] ([[AWSGenerativeAIInnovationCenter|AWS Generative AI Innovation Center]] + [[HSBC]] Technology Center China, arXiv:2604.14585v1, 17 Apr 2026). **First controlled empirical audit of prompt optimization in [[CompoundAISystem|compound AI systems]].** Tests the two implicit assumptions of [[TextGrad]] / [[DSPy]]/[[MIPROv2]] / [[GPTSwarm]] / [[Helix]]: **(A)** individual agent prompts are worth optimizing, **(B)** agent prompts interact, requiring joint optimization. **Both fail in most conditions.** Across **72 optimization runs on [[ClaudeHaiku45|Claude Haiku 4.5]] (6 methods × 4 tasks × 3 repeats), 49% score below zero-shot** (binomial $p = 0.91$ — coin flip); on [[AmazonNovaLite|Amazon Nova Lite]], 14/24 method×task means below zero-shot. **$A \times B$ interaction term non-significant in all six model×task conditions** of Study 1 ($p > 0.52$, all $F < 1.0$, 0.18–2.15% of total variance). The one task where optimization works ([[HelpSteer2]], +6.8 pts EvoPrompt) has **[[CanButDoesntPattern|exploitable output structure]]** — JSON rubric the model *can* produce but does not default to; the other three free-form tasks ([[FeedbackBench]], [[WildBench]], [[XSum]]) show **negative average gains** across all 6 methods. [[ModelSpecificityShelfLife|Model specificity dominates]] — which agent matters, which task benefits, and which method works all reverse with the executor model. Constructive contribution: a **two-stage [[CompoundAIDiagnostic|practitioner decision framework]]** — Stage 1 [[ANOVAVarianceDecomposition|ANOVA coupling test]] (~$80, 1 day) rules out [[JointOptimization|joint optimization]] if $F < 1$; Stage 2 [[HeadroomTest|headroom test]] (~$5, 10 min) rules out per-agent optimization if best-of-N gain $< 2$ pts. Diagnostic costs ~1% of a [[TextGrad]] run and would have ruled it out in 3 of 4 tasks studied. Introduces **[[PROSEOptimizer|PROSE]]** — the authors' own risk-aware evolutionary optimizer with Sharpe-ratio + DRO fitness; shows no measurable advantage over simpler methods (a deliberate negative result). Methodological contribution: **[[ANOVAVarianceDecomposition|ANOVA decomposition]] as a falsifiable evaluation protocol for compositional behavior in multi-agent systems**. Mints **15 concept pages** ([[AgentCoupling]], [[ANOVAVarianceDecomposition]], [[HeadroomTest]], [[CanButDoesntPattern]], [[CoinFlipOptimization]], [[JointOptimization]], [[IndependentOptimization]], [[CompoundAIDiagnostic]], [[ModelSpecificityShelfLife]], [[PROSEOptimizer]], [[TextGrad]], [[GPTSwarm]], [[Helix]], [[PromptBreeder]], [[ProTeGi]]) + **4 benchmark concept pages** ([[XSum]], [[MBPP]], [[HelpSteer2]], [[WildBench]], [[FeedbackBench]]) + **13 entity pages** ([[XingZhang]], [[GuanghuiWang]], [[YanweiCui]], [[WeiQiu]], [[ZiyuanLi]], [[BingZhu]], [[PeiyangHe]], [[AWSGenerativeAIInnovationCenter]], [[HSBC]], [[ClaudeHaiku45]], [[AmazonNovaLite]], [[ClaudeSonnet46]], [[Nie2026Iterative]]). Updates [[CompoundAISystem]] / [[PromptOptimization]] / [[MIPROv2]] / [[GEPA]] / [[BetterTogether]] / [[hotpotqa]] / [[Amazon]] / [[anthropic]] in place.

([[googledeepmind|Google DeepMind]]) introduce the **[[AICoMathematician|AI co-mathematician]]** — a stateful agentic workbench in which a top-level [[ProjectCoordinatorAgent|Project Coordinator]] delegates per-goal [[WorkstreamCoordinator|Workstream Coordinators]] over a shared file system and a living LaTeX [[WorkingPaper|working paper]]. Seven design principles ([[ProgressiveDisclosure]], track-manage-communicate uncertainty, preserve failed explorations, native artifacts). Harness over [[gemini|Gemini 3.1 Pro]] + [[GeminiDeepThink|Deep Think]] — no model training. **48% on [[FrontierMath]] Tier 4** (new high; base = 19%); 87% on internal 100-question research-math benchmark. ([[universityofmaryland|UMD]] + [[universityofvirginia|UVA]] + [[washingtonuniversityinstlouis|WUSTL]] + [[universityofnorthcarolina|UNC]] + [[google|Google]] + [[meta|Meta]]) reframe [[testtimescaling|TTS]] strategy design as **automatic controller discovery** over a [[WidthDepthSearch|width–depth]] control space. Explorer [[claudecode|Claude Code]] iteratively edits a Python controller against an [[OfflineReplayEnvironment|offline replay environment]]; [[BetaParameterization|single-scalar $\beta$]] + [[ExecutionTraceFeedback|execution traces]] keep search tractable. - [The Bystander Effect in Multi-Agent Reasoning: Quantifying Cognitive Loafing in Collaborative Interactions](sources/2605.10698-bystander-effect-mas.md) — Shehata & Li ([[universityofwaterloo|U Waterloo]]) audit 22,500 trajectories × 3 SOTA models × 3 benchmarks × 25 swarm permutations. Static simulated peer consensus (no live MAS dialogue) collapses [[gpt54|GPT-5.4]] SWE-bench accuracy 1.00→0.23 at $n=2$ auditors. Formalize [[AgenticSovereignty]] with an exponential [[SovereigntyDecayLaw]], closed-form [[InteractionDepthLimit]] $D_L$, and the [[SovereigntyGap]] $G_\mathcal{S}=\mathcal{V}_{int}-\mathcal{A}_{ext}$ distinguishing [[AlignmentHallucination]] ($G\gg 0$, derives-then-lies) from [[IntegrativeReasoningBypass]] ($G\ll 0$, never-derives). [[LeadAnchorEffect]] proves social load is non-commutative; [[claudeopus47|Claude Sonnet 4.6]] is the lone "Fortified Mind".

([[MindLab]] + NTU + Fudan + SJTU + CUHK + HKUST-GZ) augment a frozen Transformer with a compact 8×8 **online state of associative memory** updated by gated delta-rule learning; readout generates low-rank attention corrections without text reinjection or weight updates. 1.31× MemoryAgentBench, 1.20× LoCoMo over Qwen3-4B baseline; 0.12% parameter overhead. Proposes a fourth memory paradigm beyond TMM/OMM/PMM — productive tension with [[2604.27707-agentic-memory-is-a-memo]]'s Ω(k²) retrieval bound.
- [Position: Agentic AI System Is a Foreseeable Pathway to AGI](sources/2605.12966-agentic-ai-to-agi.md) — Liao, S. Li, Wen, J. Wang & W. Zhang ([[ShanghaiJiaoTongUniversity]] + [[ShanghaiInnovationInstitute]] + [[universitycollegelondon|UCL]], ICML 2026) prove a learning-theoretic case for **[[AgenticAI|Agentic AI]]** as a *foreseeable* pathway to AGI: under a [[StructuredRealWorldDistribution]] (union of low-dim manifolds), a routing-based agentic system achieves error $\mathcal{O}(K\!\cdot\!N^{-1/d_{\max}})$ vs the monolith's $\mathcal{O}(N^{-1/D})$ — *exponentially* better since $d_{\max}\!\ll\! D$ — and avoids the [[AverageTrap]] (irreducible quadratic penalty from conflicting per-task gradients). General agentic systems formalized as DAGs $\Psi\!=\!(\mathcal{G},\mathcal{F},\Lambda)$ with [[CompositionalCapacity]] $C(\mathcal{G})$ and [[TopologicalEdgeWeight]] decomposition as principled design tools; [[MixtureOfExperts|MoE]] reinterpreted as the single-layer routing instance.

- [Dive into Deep Learning — Preface](sources/d2l-preface.md) — [[AstonZhang|Zhang]], [[ZacharyLipton|Lipton]], [[MuLi|Li]] & [[AlexanderSmola|Smola]] introduce *Dive into Deep Learning* (D2L) — free, open, multi-framework ([[MXNet]] / [[PyTorch]] / [[TensorFlow]] / [[JAX]]) [[DeepLearning|deep-learning]] textbook built as executable [[Jupyter]] notebooks. - [Dive into Deep Learning — Introduction](sources/d2l-introduction.md) — [[AstonZhang|Zhang]], [[ZacharyLipton|Lipton]], [[MuLi|Li]] & [[AlexanderSmola|Smola]]'s broad-survey opener: defines [[MachineLearning]] as "the study of algorithms that can learn from experience"; **four-components** framing (data / model / objective / optimizer); landscape of paradigms ([[SupervisedLearning|supervised]] — [[Regression]], [[Classification]], tagging, [[RecommenderSystems|recommender]], sequence; [[UnsupervisedLearning|unsupervised]]; [[SelfSupervisedLearning|self-supervised]]; [[reinforcementlearning|RL]] with [[MarkovDecisionProcess|MDP]] / contextual-bandit / [[MultiArmedBandits|MAB]] cases); historical roots (Bernoulli / Gauss / Fisher / Shannon / Turing / Hebb / Rosenblatt → 1995–2005 NN winter → data + compute + algorithms revival); [[DeepLearning]] defined as multi-level [[RepresentationLearning]] with [[EndToEndTraining|end-to-end training]] that replaces [[FeatureEngineering|feature engineering]]; [[ImageNet]] 28%→2.25%, [[MNIST]] "considered huge", DeepBlue / AlphaGo / Libratus, [[generativeadversarialnetwork|GANs]] → [[DiffusionModel|diffusion]] (DALL-E 2 / Imagen).
- [Dive into Deep Learning — Linear Regression](sources/d2l-linear-regression.md) — [[AstonZhang|Zhang]], [[ZacharyLipton|Lipton]], [[MuLi|Li]] & [[AlexanderSmola|Smola]]'s seven-section first modeling chapter: [[LinearRegression]] as a single-layer neural network ($\hat y = \mathbf{w}^\top\mathbf{x} + b$), [[MeanSquaredError|squared loss]] motivated both functionally and as [[MaximumLikelihoodEstimation|Gaussian MLE]], closed-form solution $\mathbf{w}^* = (\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X})^{-1}\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{y}$ vs [[MinibatchSGD|minibatch SGD]] as the universal DL optimizer (batch size 32–256, $\eta$ "user-defined"), the D2L OO scaffold ([[Module]] / [[DataModule]] / [[Trainer]], inspired by [[PyTorchLightning]]), `SyntheticRegressionData` with known ground truth $(\mathbf{w}=[2,-3.4]^\top, b=4.2)$, from-scratch + concise [[PyTorch]]/[[MXNet]]/[[TensorFlow]]/[[JAX]] implementations, [[Generalization]] theory (training vs. population risk, IID, [[Underfitting]]/[[Overfitting]], [[ModelSelection]], $K$-fold [[CrossValidation]]), and [[WeightDecay]] / $\ell_2$ regularization with the $(1-\eta\lambda)$ shrinkage update.
- [Dive into Deep Learning — Multilayer Perceptrons](sources/d2l-multilayer-perceptrons.md) — [[AstonZhang|Zhang]], [[ZacharyLipton|Lipton]], [[MuLi|Li]] & [[AlexanderSmola|Smola]]'s seven-section first-truly-deep chapter: [[HiddenLayer|hidden layers]] + [[ActivationFunction|nonlinear activation]] make [[MultilayerPerceptron|MLPs]] strictly more expressive than affine models; [[ReLU]] / [[Sigmoid]] / [[Tanh]] surveyed (ReLU dominates hidden layers); [[UniversalApproximationTheorem|universal approximation]] ([[GeorgeCybenko|Cybenko 1989]]); [[ForwardPropagation|forward]] / [[Backpropagation|backward]] propagation worked through on the [[ComputationalGraph]] with $\ell_2$-regularized loss; [[VanishingGradient]] / [[ExplodingGradient]] from $L$-layer Jacobian products + permutation-symmetry breaking; [[XavierInitialization|Xavier]] / [[HeInitialization|He]] init derivations; modern generalization story — over-parametrization, [[InterpolationRegime|interpolation regime]], [[DoubleDescent|double descent]] ([[PreetumNakkiran|Nakkiran]] et al. 2021), [[NeuralTangentKernel|NTK]] ([[ArthurJacot|Jacot]] et al. 2018), [[EarlyStopping|early stopping]] as the surviving classical regularizer; [[Dropout]] ([[NitishSrivastava|Srivastava]], [[GeoffreyHinton|Hinton]], [[AlexKrizhevsky|Krizhevsky]] et al. 2014) as unbiased multiplicative-noise injection that breaks [[Coadaptation|co-adaptation]]; capstone [[Kaggle]] House Prices (Ames, Iowa 2006–2010; [[Cock-2011|De Cock 2011]]) regression case study. D2L's transition from linear models to genuine deep networks.
- [Dive into Deep Learning — Builders' Guide](sources/d2l-builders-guide.md) — [[AstonZhang|Zhang]], [[ZacharyLipton|Lipton]], [[MuLi|Li]] & [[AlexanderSmola|Smola]]'s seven-section "power-user" chapter: the universal **[[NeuralNetworkModule|module / block]]** abstraction ([[PyTorch]] `nn.Module`, [[MXNet]] `nn.Block`, Keras `tf.keras.Model`, Flax `linen.Module`); `Sequential` as a thin daisy-chain subclass; **[[ParameterAccess|parameter access]]** (`state_dict()`, `named_parameters()`) and **[[ParameterSharing|tied / shared parameters]]**; built-in + custom **[[ParameterInitialization|initialization]]** with `net.apply(init_fn)`; **[[LazyInitialization|lazy init]]** (`nn.LazyLinear`) deferring shape inference to the first forward pass; **[[CustomLayer|custom layers]]** with/without learnable [[Parameter|Parameters]]; **[[FileIO|file I/O]]** + [[Checkpoint|checkpointing]] via [[StateDict|`state_dict`]] (architecture *not* serialized — code rebuilds it); and **[[GPU]] usage** — `torch.device('cuda:i')`, model `.to(device)`, same-device-operand rule, and the cardinal "transfers are slow" cost model.
- [Dive into Deep Learning — Computational Performance](sources/d2l-computational-performance.md) — [[AstonZhang|Zhang]], [[ZacharyLipton|Lipton]], [[MuLi|Li]] & [[AlexanderSmola|Smola]]'s seven-section systems-and-scaling chapter — bridges single-GPU to multi-GPU and multi-machine training. [[ImperativeProgramming|Imperative]] vs [[SymbolicProgramming|symbolic]] programming + hybrid bridges ([[TorchScript|`torch.jit.script`]], `tf.function`/[[XLA]], MXNet `hybridize()`); [[AsyncComputation|asynchronous frontend/backend dispatch]] over the [[ComputationalGraph|dep-graph]] (PyTorch GPU ops async by default) + implicit-blocker pitfalls; [[AutoParallelism|automatic parallelism]] across devices + computation–communication overlap; the [[hardware]] + [[MemoryHierarchy|latency table]] (registers / L1 / L2 / L3 / DRAM / [[HBM]] / SSD / network) — *"few large transfers, not many small ones"*; CPU [[Vectorization|SIMD]] (NEON / AVX2 / AVX-512) and GPU [[TensorCore|tensor cores]]; interconnects ([[PCIe]] 4.0 ×16 = 32 GB/s; [[NVLink]] = 100+ GB/s; [[Ethernet]] = 1–10 GB/s); the three ways to parallelize ([[ModelParallelism|network partition]] / [[TensorParallelism|layerwise split]] / [[DataParallelism|data parallelism]]) with the recommendation that **data parallelism is the default**; from-scratch [[AllReduce]] on a custom LeNet + concise `nn.DataParallel` on ResNet-18; [[ParameterServer|parameter server]] (Li, Andersen, Park et al. 2014) with $\mathcal{O}(m/n)$ scaling math, [[KeyValueStore|push/pull]] semantics, and [[RingAllReduce|ring synchronization]]'s $O(1)$-in-$n$ bandwidth-optimal aggregation (6 ms across 8× V100 over [[NVLink]]); [[NCCL]] / [[Horovod]] as production all-reduce backends. The textbook foundation under [[DistributedTraining]] / [[DataParallelism]] / [[AllReduce]] / [[ParameterServer]].
- [Dive into Deep Learning — Computer Vision](sources/d2l-computer-vision.md) — [[AstonZhang|Zhang]], [[ZacharyLipton|Lipton]], [[MuLi|Li]] & [[AlexanderSmola|Smola]]'s 14-section *Computer Vision* chapter — D2L's first Part 3 application chapter, leveraging [[CNN]] / [[ResNet]] / [[VGG]] backbones from [[d2l-convolutional-neural-networks]] / [[d2l-convolutional-modern]] for the four canonical CV tasks beyond classification. [[DataAugmentation|Image augmentation]] (flip / crop / color-jitter as cheap regularization, "indispensable for [[AlexNet]]") + [[FineTuning]] (four-step pretrain → copy → replace-head → train, smaller LR on backbone vs $10\times$ on new head) → [[BoundingBox|bounding boxes]] (corner ↔ center-width-height) → [[AnchorBox|anchor boxes]] (centered on each pixel at scales $s$ and aspect ratios $r$, the $n+m-1$ trick) + [[IntersectionOverUnion|IoU = Jaccard]] + [[NonMaxSuppression|NMS]] + greedy anchor↔ground-truth assignment with $((x_b-x_a)/w_a)/\sigma_x$ offset parameterization → [[MultiscaleObjectDetection|multiscale detection]] via feature-map pyramids → [[SSD|Single-Shot Multibox Detection]] ([[WeiLiu|Liu]] et al. 2016) as the single-stage detector + the [[RCNN]] ([[RossGirshick|Girshick]] et al. 2014, selective-search-driven) → [[FastRCNN]] (one forward pass + [[ROIPooling]]) → [[FasterRCNN]] ([[ShaoqingRen|Ren]]/[[KaimingHe|He]]/Girshick 2015, [[RegionProposalNetwork|RPN]] replaces selective search) → [[MaskRCNN]] ([[KaimingHe|He]] et al. 2017, [[ROIAlign]] + per-RoI FCN mask head) two-stage lineage → [[SemanticSegmentation]] vs [[InstanceSegmentation]] vs image segmentation distinction on [[PascalVOC2012]] (21 classes, fixed RGB colormap labels) → [[TransposedConvolution|transposed conv]] (= fractionally-strided conv) as the upsampling primitive that broadcasts via the kernel ($s$, padding $s/2$, kernel $2s$ → $s\times$ upsampling) with [[BilinearInterpolation|bilinear-interpolation]] init → [[FCN|Fully Convolutional Network]] ([[JonathanLong|Long]], [[EvanShelhamer|Shelhamer]] & [[TrevorDarrell|Darrell]] 2015): ResNet-18 backbone + $1\times1$ conv to $K=21$ classes + transposed-conv stride-32 upsample → per-pixel softmax → [[StyleTransfer|Gatys neural style transfer]] ([[LeonGatys|Gatys]], [[AlexanderEcker|Ecker]] & [[MatthiasBethge|Bethge]] 2016) iteratively optimizes the *synthesized image itself* on a frozen [[VGG|VGG-19]] with content loss + [[GramMatrix|Gram-matrix]] style loss + total-variation loss → and two Kaggle capstones ([[CIFAR10]] image classification and Dog Breed Identification on an [[ImageNet]] subset). The unifying theme: **layerwise / multiscale feature reuse on pretrained ImageNet CNN backbones** across every CV task — the paradigm that NLP would later mirror with [[BERT]] / [[GPT]] pretraining.
- [Dive into Deep Learning — Convolutional Neural Networks](sources/d2l-convolutional-neural-networks.md) — [[AstonZhang|Zhang]], [[ZacharyLipton|Lipton]], [[MuLi|Li]] & [[AlexanderSmola|Smola]]'s six-section [[CNN]] chapter: derives the [[ConvolutionalLayer|convolutional layer]] from two priors on image data ([[TranslationInvariance|translation invariance]] + [[Locality|locality]]) imposed on a generic [[MultilayerPerceptron|MLP]] — collapsing a $10^{12}$-parameter fully-connected layer over a $1000\times1000$ image into $4\Delta^2$ shared weights; walks the operational stack — [[CrossCorrelation|cross-correlation]] (what frameworks actually compute and call "convolution"), [[Padding|padding]] / [[Stride|stride]] output-shape arithmetic ($(n_h-k_h+p_h+s_h)/s_h \times \ldots$), multi-channel kernels of shape $c_o\times c_i\times k_h\times k_w$ including the [[OneByOneConvolution|$1\times1$ conv]] (per-pixel FC over channels), [[MaxPooling|max-]] / [[AveragePooling|average-pooling]] (parameter-free, per-channel), and [[ReceptiveField|receptive fields]] (Hubel & Wiesel lineage) — and culminates in a from-scratch implementation of [[LeNet|LeNet-5]] ([[YannLeCun|LeCun]] et al. 1989/1998; conv→sigmoid→AvgPool→conv→sigmoid→AvgPool→FC→FC→FC), the first CNN to match SVMs on a real task ([[MNIST]] OCR; <1% per-digit error; deployed in ATMs and "some ATMs still run the code [[LeonBottou|Bottou]] wrote in the 1990s").
- [Dive into Deep Learning — Modern Convolutional Neural Networks](sources/d2l-convolutional-modern.md) — [[AstonZhang|Zhang]], [[ZacharyLipton|Lipton]], [[MuLi|Li]] & [[AlexanderSmola|Smola]]'s eight-section post-[[LeNet]] CNN tour ([[AlexNet]] 2012 → [[VGG]] 2014 → [[NetworkInNetwork|NiN]] 2013 → [[GoogLeNet]] / [[Inception]] 2014 → [[BatchNormalization|BatchNorm]] 2015 → [[ResNet]] + [[ResNeXt]] 2015/2017 → [[DenseNet]] 2017 → design-spaces / [[RegNet]] 2020). [[AlexNet]] ([[AlexKrizhevsky|Krizhevsky]], [[IlyaSutskever|Sutskever]], [[GeoffreyHinton|Hinton]]) breaks the hand-engineered-features paradigm on [[ImageNet]] with [[ReLU]] + [[Dropout]] + image augmentation on two GTX 580 GPUs; [[VGG]] ([[KarenSimonyan|Simonyan]] & [[AndrewZisserman|Zisserman]], Oxford) introduces blocks of small $3\times3$ convs + max-pool — "deep and narrow beats shallow"; [[NetworkInNetwork|NiN]] introduces the $1\times1$ conv as per-channel FC and [[GlobalAveragePooling|global average pooling]] to kill the FC head; [[GoogLeNet]] ([[ChristianSzegedy|Szegedy]] et al.) [[Inception|multi-branch concatenation]] + stem/body/head template; [[BatchNormalization]] ([[SergeyIoffe|Ioffe]] & [[ChristianSzegedy|Szegedy]]) reparametrizes activations with learnable $\gamma,\beta$ — internal-covariate-shift motivation now disputed; [[ResNet]] ([[KaimingHe|He]] et al.) makes the identity easy to learn via $f(\mathbf{x})=\mathbf{x}+g(\mathbf{x})$ residual blocks, solving the degradation problem and enabling 152-layer networks; [[ResNeXt]] adds grouped convolutions for $g\times$ FLOP reduction; [[DenseNet]] ([[GaoHuang|Huang]] et al.) replaces addition with channel concatenation for aggressive feature reuse; [[RegNet]] ([[IliaRadosavovic|Radosavovic]] et al.) optimizes *distributions* of networks via empirical CDFs — discovering principles ("share bottleneck ratio, share group width, increase channels and depth across stages, linear width-vs-block-index") instead of single architectures. Closes with the [[VisionTransformer|ViT]] transition: "scalability trumps inductive biases."
- [Dive into Deep Learning — Linear Classification](sources/d2l-linear-classification.md) — [[AstonZhang|Zhang]], [[ZacharyLipton|Lipton]], [[MuLi|Li]] & [[AlexanderSmola|Smola]]'s seven-section second modeling chapter: [[Softmax|softmax regression]] = one-hot labels + affine layer + softmax + [[CrossEntropyLoss|cross-entropy]] derived as categorical NLL; prediction-minus-target gradient as an [[ExponentialFamily|exponential-family]] property; the [[LogSumExp|LogSumExp trick]] for numerical stability (frameworks fuse softmax + log + cross-entropy on logits); [[FashionMNIST|Fashion-MNIST]] as the running benchmark replacing [[MNIST]]; `Classifier` base class with `accuracy` / `validation_step`; statistical-learning-theory cluster — [[HoeffdingsInequality|Hoeffding]]-bound test-set sizing (~10–15k samples for ±0.01 at 95% confidence), [[UniformConvergence|uniform convergence]] via [[VCDimension|VC dimension]], [[TestSetReuse|adaptive overfitting]]; the canonical [[DistributionShift|distribution-shift]] taxonomy — [[CovariateShift]] / [[LabelShift]] / [[ConceptShift]] with importance-weighted [[EmpiricalRiskMinimization|ERM]] correction (logistic-regression domain classifier estimates $p(\mathbf x)/q(\mathbf x)$; confusion-matrix inversion estimates $p(y)/q(y)$); learning-paradigm taxonomy (batch / online / bandits / control / RL).
- [Dive into Deep Learning — Notation](sources/d2l-notation.md) — Reference symbol table for [[d2l-preface|D2L]] across five domains: numerical objects ($x$ scalar / $\mathbf{x}$ vector / $\mathbf{X}$ matrix / $\mathsf{X}$ [[Tensor|tensor]]), set theory ($\mathcal{X}$ set, $\mathbb{Z}$/$\mathbb{R}$ number systems), functions and operators (transpose, $\odot$, $\|\cdot\|_p$ [[Norm|norm]], $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ [[InnerProduct|inner product]]), calculus ($\partial$ [[PartialDerivative|partial derivative]], $\nabla_{\mathbf{x}}$ [[Gradient|gradient]]), and probability / information theory ($X\sim P$, $P(X\mid Y)$, $\mathbb{E}[X]$, $\textrm{Var}/\textrm{Cov}/\rho$, $H(X)$ entropy, $D_{\textrm{KL}}$). "Rule of thumb": indefinite-article entries are placeholders; definite-article entries are reserved literals.
- [Dive into Deep Learning — Preliminaries](sources/d2l-preliminaries.md) — [[AstonZhang|Zhang]], [[ZacharyLipton|Lipton]], [[MuLi|Li]] & [[AlexanderSmola|Smola]]'s seven-section "survival skills" chapter — [[NDArray|n-dim tensors]] (constructors, indexing, [[Broadcasting]], in-place ops, NumPy interop), [[pandas]] preprocessing (CSV → impute → one-hot → tensor), [[LinearAlgebra]] (scalars → vectors → matrices → tensors → Hadamard → reductions → [[DotProduct]] → matmul → [[Norm|norms]] $\ell_1$/$\ell_2$/$\ell_p$/Frobenius), [[Calculus]] (derivatives → [[PartialDerivative|partials]] → [[Gradient|gradients]] → [[ChainRule|chain rule]]), [[Autograd|automatic differentiation]] ([[ComputationalGraph]] forward-build / backward-walk; Wengert 1964 → Speelpenning 1980 → Griewank 1989; framework cheat-sheet for [[PyTorch]] / [[TensorFlow]] / [[JAX]] / [[MXNet]]; detach / control flow), [[probability]] + statistics ([[ProbabilitySpace]] / Kolmogorov axioms / [[RandomVariable|RVs]] / [[JointProbability|joint]] / [[ConditionalProbability|conditional]] / [[StatisticalIndependence|independence]] / [[BayesTheorem]] HIV-test example), and API lookup (`dir`/`help`). Uses column-vector gradient convention (opposite of [[mml-book|MML]]).
- [Dive into Deep Learning — Recommender Systems](sources/d2l-recommender-systems.md) — [[ShuaiZhang|Zhang]] ([[Amazon]]), [[AstonZhang|Zhang]] ([[Amazon]]) & [[YiTay|Tay]] ([[google|Google]])'s ten-section *Recommender Systems* chapter — D2L's only chapter on **personalized retrieval / ranking** as a learning problem distinct from classification and regression. Builds the [[RecommenderSystems|recommender]] stack from first principles on [[MovieLens]] 100K: [[CollaborativeFiltering|CF]] taxonomy ([[MemoryBasedCF|memory-based]] / [[ModelBasedCF|model-based]] / hybrid; [[ImplicitFeedback]] vs [[ExplicitFeedback]] per [[YifanHu|Hu]]/[[YehudaKoren|Koren]]/Volinsky 2008) → rating-prediction with [[MatrixFactorization]] ([[YehudaKoren|Koren]], Bell & Volinsky 2009; Funk 2006, [[NetflixPrize]]) and [[AutoRec]] ([[SuvashSedhain|Sedhain]] et al. 2015) → personalized ranking with [[BPR]] ([[SteffenRendle|Rendle]] et al. 2009) and [[HingeLossRanking|Hinge]] loss → [[NeuMF]] ([[XiangnanHe|He]] et al. 2017) fusing [[GMF]] + MLP subnetworks → [[CaserModel|Caser]] sequence-aware CNN ([[JiaxiTang|Tang]] & [[KeWang|Wang]] 2018) capturing union-level + point-level temporal patterns → **feature-rich CTR** pivot to [[FactorizationMachines]] ([[SteffenRendle|Rendle]] 2010) with $\mathcal{O}(kd)$ pairwise-interaction reformulation, and [[DeepFM]] ([[HuifengGuo|Guo]], [[RuimingTang|Tang]], Ye, He 2017) parallelizing FM with a deep MLP for high-order interactions. The textbook foundation under every modern personalization / advertising / e-commerce ranking system.
- [Dive into Deep Learning — Recurrent Neural Networks](sources/d2l-recurrent-neural-networks.md) — [[AstonZhang|Zhang]], [[ZacharyLipton|Lipton]], [[MuLi|Li]] & [[AlexanderSmola|Smola]]'s seven-section RNN chapter — D2L's pivot from fixed-length data to *sequence* modeling: [[AutoregressiveModel|autoregressive]] sequence math + $k$-step extrapolation error compounding; text preprocessing pipeline (load → tokenize → vocabulary → numeric corpus) on H. G. Wells' *The Time Machine*; [[ZipfsLaw|Zipfian]] unigram/bigram/trigram empirics; [[LanguageModel|language models]] = $\prod_t P(x_t\mid x_{<t})$ via chain rule; [[NGram|$n$-gram]] baselines + [[LaplaceSmoothing]] (and why they fail); [[Perplexity]] = $\exp(\text{avg-CE})$ as the NLP-standard LM metric; the [[RNN]] recurrence $\mathbf{H}_t = \phi(\mathbf{X}_t \mathbf{W}_\textrm{xh} + \mathbf{H}_{t-1}\mathbf{W}_\textrm{hh} + \mathbf{b}_\textrm{h})$ as MLP-plus-one-term with weight-tied parameters across time, [[HiddenState|hidden state]] as memory vs hidden layer, concatenation-matmul equivalence; from-scratch [[CharacterLevelLanguageModel|character-level RNN LM]] with [[OneHotEncoding|one-hot]] inputs, softmax + cross-entropy, [[TeacherForcing|teacher forcing]] (targets = inputs shifted by 1), and **[[GradientClipping|gradient clipping]]** $\mathbf{g}\leftarrow\min(1,\theta/\|\mathbf{g}\|)\mathbf{g}$ as a ubiquitous-but-honest hack; high-level-API parity via `nn.RNN` / `SimpleRNN`; closed-form [[BPTT]] (Werbos 1990) on the unrolled graph, $\partial L/\partial\mathbf{h}_t = \sum_i (\mathbf{W}_\textrm{hh}^\top)^{T-i}\mathbf{W}_\textrm{qh}^\top \partial L/\partial \mathbf{o}_{T+t-i}$ — eigenvalue powers manifest as [[VanishingGradient|vanishing]] / [[ExplodingGradient|exploding]] gradients; full / regular / randomized [[TruncatedBPTT]] strategies (Jaeger 2002; Tallec & Ollivier 2017 — randomized does no better than regular). Forward references to gated [[LSTM]] / [[GRU]] (next chapter) and [[transformer|Transformers]] ("RNNs have ceded considerable market share").
- [Dive into Deep Learning — Natural Language Processing: Applications](sources/d2l-nlp-applications.md) — [[AstonZhang|Zhang]], [[ZacharyLipton|Lipton]], [[MuLi|Li]] & [[AlexanderSmola|Smola]]'s seven-section *NLP Applications* chapter — the downstream companion to [[d2l-nlp-pretraining]]. Applies [[GloVe]] / [[BERT]] to two representative tasks ([[SentimentAnalysis|sentiment]] on [[IMDb]], [[NaturalLanguageInference|NLI]] on [[SNLI]]) across **four architectural choices** for the same task — [[BidirectionalRNN]] + GloVe (§sentiment-rnn), [[TextCNN]] ([[YoonKim|Kim]] 2014, §sentiment-cnn), [[DecomposableAttention]] ([[AnkurParikh|Parikh]], Täckström, Das & Uszkoreit 2016, §nli-attention with the linear-complexity *decomposition trick* $e_{ij}=f(\mathbf{a}_i)^\top f(\mathbf{b}_j)$ that prefigures [[SelfAttention]]), and fine-tuned [[BERT]] (§nli-bert). Closes with the [[FineTuningBert]] template: **minimal architecture changes** for sequence-level (single-text classification, text-pair classification, text-pair regression) and token-level (POS tagging, [[QuestionAnswering|QA]] on [[SQuAD]]) applications — all sharing the [[ClsToken|`[CLS]`]] aggregate or per-token hidden states. The applied-NLP analogue of [[d2l-computer-vision]]'s *pretrained backbone + fine-tune* template. Articulates the engineering trade-off: BERT requires minimal architecture changes but maximum compute; hand-crafted models are feasible when compute is constrained.
- [Dive into Deep Learning — Natural Language Processing: Pretraining](sources/d2l-nlp-pretraining.md) — [[AstonZhang|Zhang]], [[ZacharyLipton|Lipton]], [[MuLi|Li]] & [[AlexanderSmola|Smola]]'s ten-section *NLP Pretraining* chapter — D2L's pivot from architectures to **upstream text-representation pretraining**: [[Word2Vec|word2vec]] ([[SkipGram|skip-gram]] + [[CBOW]]) trained efficiently with [[NegativeSampling]] (NCE-style binary classification against $K$ noise words, $\mathcal{O}(K)$ per step) or [[HierarchicalSoftmax]] (binary-tree factorization, $\mathcal{O}(\log_2|\mathcal{V}|)$); [[GloVe]] ([[JeffreyPennington|Pennington]], [[RichardSocher|Socher]] & [[ChrisManning|Manning]] 2014) as squared-loss factorization of the global co-occurrence matrix $\sum_{ij}h(x_{ij})(\mathbf{u}_j^\top\mathbf{v}_i+b_i+c_j-\log x_{ij})^2$ justified by the ratio of co-occurrence probabilities (solid:ice/steam ≈ 8.9 example); [[FastText]] ([[PiotrBojanowski|Bojanowski]], [[EdouardGrave|Grave]], [[ArmandJoulin|Joulin]] et al. 2017) as character-$n$-gram [[SubwordEmbedding|subword embedding]] $\mathbf{v}_w=\sum_{g\in\mathcal{G}_w}\mathbf{z}_g$ — OOV-robust; [[BPE|Byte Pair Encoding]] ([[RicoSennrich|Sennrich]] et al. 2015) as the fixed-vocab variable-length subword tokenizer underpinning [[GPT2|GPT-2]] / [[RoBERTa]]; the [[AnalogyTask|word-analogy task]] $d=\arg\max_w\cos(\textrm{vec}(w),\textrm{vec}(c)+\textrm{vec}(b)-\textrm{vec}(a))$ recovering man:woman::son:daughter / beijing:china::tokyo:japan / bad:worst::big:biggest / do:did::go:went directly from 50-d GloVe vectors. Closes by pivoting from context-independent ("bank" = "bank") to [[ContextualEmbedding|context-sensitive]] representations — [[TagLM]] → CoVe → [[ELMo]] → [[GPT]] → [[BERT]] — and re-builds the BERT pretraining pipeline ([[MaskedLanguageModel|MLM]] 15%-mask with 80/10/10 [MASK]/random/unchanged split + [[NextSentencePrediction|NSP]] binary classification on the `[CLS]` token + [[WordPiece]] 30K vocab + learnable positional embeddings) end-to-end on [[BookCorpus]] (800M words) + [[EnglishWikipedia]] (2.5B words) — a 3.3B-word self-supervised corpus with no labeling cost. The textbook foundation under **every modern LLM input layer** and the canonical companion to [[1810.04805-bert]].
- [Dive into Deep Learning — Reinforcement Learning](sources/d2l-reinforcement-learning.md) — [[PratikChaudhari|Chaudhari]] (Penn / Amazon), [[RasoolFakoor|Fakoor]] & [[KavoshAsadi|Asadi]] (Amazon)'s three-section RL chapter — D2L's compact introduction to **sequential decision-making**: [[MarkovDecisionProcess|MDP]] formalism $(\mathcal{S},\mathcal{A},T,r)$ with [[TransitionFunction|transition kernel]] / [[RewardFunction|reward]] / Markov property (and the state-expansion trick when dynamics appear non-Markovian) + [[DiscountFactor|discount factor]] $\gamma$ for infinite-horizon returns (§mdp) → [[PolicyFunction|stochastic policies]], [[ValueFunction|value]] / [[ActionValueFunction|action-value]] functions, the [[BellmanEquation|Bellman]] one-step decomposition ("the remainder of an optimal trajectory is also optimal" — [[RichardBellman|Bellman]] 1950s [[DynamicProgramming|DP]] principle), and [[ValueIteration|Value Iteration]] $V_{k+1}(s)=\max_a\{r(s,a)+\gamma\sum_{s'}P(s'\mid s,a)V_k(s')\}$ converging to $V^*$ from arbitrary $V_0$ in ~10 sweeps on FrozenLake-v1 ($\gamma=0.95$) when the MDP is fully known (§value-iter) → [[QLearning|Q-Learning]] ([[ChristopherWatkins|Watkins]] & Dayan 1992) — the [[ModelFreeLearning|model-free]] alternative when $P(s'\mid s,a)$ is unknown — replaces the analytic expectation with sample averages: $Q(s_t,a_t)\!\leftarrow\!(1-\alpha)Q(s_t,a_t)+\alpha[r_t+\gamma\max_{a'}Q(s_{t+1},a')]$ ([[TemporalDifferenceLearning|TD]] update, $\alpha$ learning rate); converges in ~250 episodes — the price of model-free learning. [[OffPolicyLearning|Off-policy]] structure (behavior policy $\pi_e$ ≠ target policy $\arg\max_a\hat{Q}$), [[EpsilonGreedy|$\epsilon$-greedy]] / softmax-temperature [[ExplorationExploitation|exploration]], and Q-Learning's self-correcting property (overestimated $\hat{Q}(s,a)$ is corrected by the next visit's poor rewards) — the chapter is RL distilled to first principles, with DQN flagged as the deep-RL successor responsible for *"the resurgence of reinforcement learning."*
- [Dive into Deep Learning — Modern Recurrent Neural Networks](sources/d2l-recurrent-modern.md) — [[AstonZhang|Zhang]], [[ZacharyLipton|Lipton]], [[MuLi|Li]] & [[AlexanderSmola|Smola]]'s eight-section *Modern RNN* chapter — sequel to [[d2l-recurrent-neural-networks]], motivated entirely by the [[VanishingGradient|vanishing-gradient]] pathology. [[LSTM]] ([[SeppHochreiter|Hochreiter]] & [[JurgenSchmidhuber|Schmidhuber]] 1997) introduces the [[MemoryCell|memory cell]] with [[InputGate|input]] / [[ForgetGate|forget]] / [[OutputGate|output]] gates and a weight-1 self-recurrence; [[GRU]] ([[KyunghyunCho|Cho]] et al. 2014) streamlines this to [[ResetGate|reset]] + [[UpdateGate|update]] gates over a single hidden state. [[DeepRNN|Deep RNNs]] stack $L$ layers; [[BidirectionalRNN|bi-RNNs]] ([[MikeSchuster|Schuster]] & [[KuldipPaliwal|Paliwal]] 1997) concatenate forward + backward passes (encoder-only — "no future at inference" blocks decoder use). Pivots to [[MachineTranslation|MT]] as the canonical [[SeqToSeq|seq2seq]] task: [[EncoderDecoder|encoder-decoder]] template ([[KyunghyunCho|Cho]] et al. 2014; [[IlyaSutskever|Sutskever]] et al. 2014 — [[1409.3215-seq2seq]]) with [[TeacherForcing|teacher-forced]] decoder and masked-by-`valid_len` cross-entropy; [[BLEU]] ([[KishorePapineni|Papineni]] et al. 2002) as modified-$n$-gram-precision with brevity penalty; [[BeamSearch|beam search]] with length-penalty $\frac{1}{L^\alpha}\sum\log P$ ($\alpha\!=\!0.75$) bridges [[GreedyDecoding|greedy]] $\mathcal{O}(\|\mathcal{Y}\|T')$ and exhaustive $\mathcal{O}(\|\mathcal{Y}\|^{T'})$ at $\mathcal{O}(k\|\mathcal{Y}\|T')$. Textbook bridge from RNN-era sequence modeling to the [[transformer|Transformer]].
- [Dive into Deep Learning — Attention Mechanisms and Transformers](sources/d2l-attention-and-transformers.md) — [[AstonZhang|Zhang]], [[ZacharyLipton|Lipton]], [[MuLi|Li]] & [[AlexanderSmola|Smola]]'s nine-section attention chapter — D2L's pivot from gated-RNN [[SeqToSeq|seq2seq]] into the [[Transformer|Transformer]] regime. Builds attention from the [[QueryKeyValue|database query]] analogy up: [[NadarayaWatson|Nadaraya–Watson]] kernel regression as the half-century precursor → [[ScaledDotProductAttention|scaled dot-product]] vs [[AdditiveAttention|additive]] [[AttentionScoringFunctions|scoring]] (with [[MaskedSoftmax|masked softmax]] for padding) → [[BahdanauAttention|Bahdanau attention]] as differentiable alignment for [[MachineTranslation|MT]] → [[MultiHeadAttention]] as projection-diversified parallel pools → [[SelfAttention]] (the all-pairs $O(n^2 d)$ view with $O(1)$ sequential ops + $O(1)$ max path length) + sinusoidal [[PositionalEncoding]] (with the $2\times 2$ relative-offset projection identity) → the full [[1706.03762-attention-is-all-you-need|Vaswani et al. 2017]] [[Transformer]] block (multi-head + positionwise [[FeedForwardNetwork|FFN]] + [[ResidualConnection|residual]] + [[LayerNormalization|LayerNorm]], with causal-masked decoder self-attention preserving autoregressiveness) → the foundation-model triptych (encoder-only [[BERT]] / encoder–decoder [[T5]] / decoder-only [[GPT]] family) with [[2001.08361-scaling-laws|power-law scaling]], in-context learning, [[ChainOfThought|chain-of-thought]], [[RLHF]] / [[InstructGPT]] / [[ChatGPT]] → and the [[VisionTransformer|Vision Transformer]] ([[Dosovitskiy|Dosovitskiy]] et al. 2021): patches-as-tokens + learnable [[ClsToken|`<cls>` token]] + [[PreNorm|pre-norm]] + [[GELU]] MLP, "scalability trumps inductive biases."
- [Dive into Deep Learning — Optimization Algorithms](sources/d2l-optimization.md) — [[AstonZhang|Zhang]], [[ZacharyLipton|Lipton]], [[MuLi|Li]] & [[AlexanderSmola|Smola]]'s eleven-section theoretical chapter on gradient-based optimization: optimization vs. generalization, nonconvex DL pathologies ([[SaddlePoint|saddle points]], [[VanishingGradient|vanishing gradients]]), [[Convexity|convexity]] primer (sets, functions, [[JensensInequality|Jensen]], Hessian PSD, Lagrangian / penalty / projection), [[GradientDescent|GD]] from Taylor expansion + [[NewtonsMethod|Newton]] + [[Preconditioning|preconditioning]] + [[LineSearch|line search]], [[StochasticGradientDescent|SGD]] with $\mathcal{O}(1/\sqrt{T})$ convex convergence, [[MinibatchSGD|minibatch SGD]] trade-off, [[Momentum|momentum]] / leaky averaging with eigendecomposition analysis ([[BorisPolyak|Polyak]] 1964, [[YuriiNesterov|Nesterov]] 2018), [[Adagrad]] ([[JohnDuchi|Duchi]] et al. 2011) → [[RMSProp]] ([[GeoffreyHinton|Hinton]] 2012) → [[Adadelta]] ([[MatthewZeiler|Zeiler]] 2012) → [[Adam]] ([[DiederikKingma|Kingma]] & [[JimmyBa|Ba]] 2014, with bias correction) + [[Yogi]] divergence-fix, and [[LearningRateScheduler|LR schedules]] (factor / multifactor / polynomial / [[CosineLRSchedule|cosine annealing]] / [[Warmup|warmup]]). The wiki's canonical reference for every gradient-based optimizer beneath every NN.
- [Dive into Deep Learning — Gaussian Processes](sources/d2l-gaussian-processes.md) — [[AndrewGordonWilson|Wilson]] ([[NewYorkUniversity|NYU]] / [[amazon|Amazon]])'s guest three-section chapter on **[[GaussianProcess|Gaussian processes (GPs)]]** — the function-space approach to Bayesian regression. GP defined as *"a collection of random variables, any finite number of which have a joint Gaussian distribution"*; prior specified by mean + [[KernelFunction|kernel]]; [[RBFKernel|RBF kernel]] derived as $J\to\infty$ Riemann limit of an RBF basis; [[NeuralNetworkKernel|neural-network kernel]] from infinite-width Bayesian NN ([[RadfordNeal|Neal 1996]] — [[NeuralTangentKernel|NTK]] precursor); closed-form Gaussian posterior $m_*=K(X_*,X)[K+\sigma^2 I]^{-1}\mathbf{y}$; [[MarginalLikelihood|marginal-likelihood]] hyperparameter learning encodes [[OccamsRazor|Occam's razor]] via the log-det term; clean [[EpistemicUncertainty|epistemic]] / [[AleatoricUncertainty|aleatoric]] uncertainty decomposition; $\mathcal{O}(n^3)$ [[CholeskyDecomposition|Cholesky]] bottleneck caps exact GPs at ~10k points, addressed by [[GPyTorch]] (Wilson group's PyTorch-integrated scalable-GP library, SKI / KISS-GP).
- [Dive into Deep Learning — Generative Adversarial Networks](sources/d2l-generative-adversarial-networks.md) — [[AstonZhang|Zhang]], [[ZacharyLipton|Lipton]], [[MuLi|Li]] & [[AlexanderSmola|Smola]]'s two-section *Generative Adversarial Networks* chapter — D2L's first dedicated generative-modeling chapter. §`gan` builds the [[generativeadversarialnetwork|GAN]] from scratch on a 2-D Gaussian toy: [[Generator|generator]] $G$ maps noise $\mathbf z\sim\mathcal{N}(0,1)$ to fakes, [[Discriminator|discriminator]] $D$ classifies real-vs-fake, the two play a [[MinMaxGame|minimax game]] $\min_D \max_G\{-E_x\log D(\mathbf x) - E_z\log(1-D(G(\mathbf z)))\}$ ([[IanGoodfellow|Goodfellow]], Pouget-Abadie, Mirza et al. 2014). The non-saturating $\min_G\{-\log D(G(\mathbf z))\}$ reformulation fixes the vanishing-gradient pathology of the original $\max_G$ objective by feeding fakes through $D$ with the *real* label $y=1$. §`dcgan` scales to RGB images via [[DCGAN]] ([[AlecRadford|Radford]], Metz & Chintala 2015): all-convolutional discriminator (4 strided convs + [[BatchNormalization|BN]] + [[LeakyReLU]] $\alpha=0.2$) and mirror-image generator (4 [[TransposedConvolution|transposed convs]] + BN + [[ReLU]], $1{\times}1{\times}100 \to 4{\times}4 \to 8{\times}8 \to 16{\times}16 \to 32{\times}32 \to 64{\times}64$ with channel widths $100\!\to\!512\!\to\!256\!\to\!128\!\to\!64\!\to\!3$ and final $\tanh$ to $[-1,1]$), trained on Pokémon sprites. Practical recipe: same LR for both nets, weights init $\mathcal{N}(0, 0.02)$, **Adam $\beta_1 = 0.5$** (vs default $0.9$) to track the fast-changing adversarial gradients — the single most-cited hyperparameter tweak in the GAN literature.
- [Dive into Deep Learning — Hyperparameter Optimization](sources/d2l-hyperparameter-optimization.md) — [[AaronKlein|Klein]], [[MatthiasSeeger|Seeger]] & [[CedricArchambeau|Archambeau]] ([[Amazon]])'s five-section guest chapter on **[[HyperparameterOptimization|hyperparameter optimization (HPO)]]** — D2L's only chapter cast entirely as **[[BlackBoxOptimization|black-box optimization]]**. Builds HPO from scratch (`HPOSearcher` / `HPOScheduler` / `HPOTuner` API), implements [[RandomSearch]] from a SciPy `loguniform` config space, distributes it asynchronously via [[SyneTune]], introduces [[MultiFidelityOptimization|multi-fidelity HPO]] with [[SuccessiveHalving]] ([[Jamieson|Jamieson & Talwalkar 2016]] / [[Karnin|Karnin et al. 2013]]) and pivots to **[[ASHA|asynchronous successive halving]]** ([[LishaLi|Li]] et al. 2018) — the algorithm that promotes configurations the moment any $\eta$ observations land on a rung. Cites [[JamesBergstra|Bergstra]] & [[YoshuaBengio|Bengio]] 2012 for random-beats-grid; [[JasperSnoek|Snoek]] et al. 2012 for [[BayesianOptimization|BO]]. Positions [[NeuralArchitectureSearch|NAS]] and [[AutoML]] as natural HPO extensions.
- [Dive into Deep Learning — Appendix: Tools for Deep Learning](sources/d2l-appendix-tools.md) — [[AstonZhang|Zhang]], [[ZacharyLipton|Lipton]], [[MuLi|Li]] & [[AlexanderSmola|Smola]]'s eight-section operational appendix — D2L's tooling layer. [[Jupyter]] as the primary authoring environment (the `notedown` plugin for editing markdown-source notebooks; `ssh myserver -L 8888:localhost:8888` port-forwarding for remote kernels) → [[AmazonSageMaker]] as the fastest path to a GPU notebook (`ml.p3.2xlarge` = V100 + 8-core CPU, *"powerful enough for most of the book"*; SageMaker clones the framework-specific D2L repo at provision time) → [[AmazonEC2]] as the cheaper-but-more-work alternative (Ubuntu AMI → SSH key pair → `chmod 400 D2L_key.pem` → `apt-get install cuda` for [[CUDA]] 12.1 → `nvidia-smi` → [[Miniconda]] + `pip install d2l==1.0.3` → port-forward Jupyter) → [[GoogleColab]] as the free-tier alternative for readers without an AWS account → *Selecting Servers and GPUs* hardware guide for on-prem builds with explicit Beginner / 1-GPU / 2-GPU / 4-GPU / 8-GPU server recipes (power supply / chassis / cooling / [[PCIe]] lanes — *"runs loud and hot. You do not want it under your desk"*) and [[NVIDIA]]-dominates-because-of-CUDA framing → *Contributing* tutorial walking GitHub fork → clone → `git commit` → pull-request flow with `%%tab pytorch` / `%%tab tensorflow` framework-tag conventions → and the `d2l` Python package API ([[D2LPackage]]) alphabetically autodoc'd — [[Module]] / [[DataModule]] / [[Trainer]] / [[MultiHeadAttention]] / [[TransformerEncoder]] / [[Seq2Seq]] / [[Vocab]], helpers `try_gpu` / `bleu` / `corr2d` / `masked_softmax`. **Closes the D2L corpus at 26/26 chapters.**
- [Dive into Deep Learning — Appendix: Mathematics for Deep Learning](sources/d2l-appendix-mathematics.md) — [[BrentWerness|Werness]] & [[RachelHu|Hu]] ([[Amazon]]) and the [[d2l-preface|D2L]] authors' eleven-section *Mathematics for Deep Learning* appendix — D2L's dedicated math reference shelf, sitting outside Parts 1–3. Geometry of vectors ([[DotProduct|dot product]] $=\|\mathbf{u}\|\|\mathbf{v}\|\cos\theta$ in any dimension, [[CosineSimilarity|cosine similarity]] as brightness-invariant, [[Hyperplane|hyperplanes]] as decision planes "the role of the deep neural network is to find a non-linear embedding such that the target classes can be separated cleanly by hyperplanes") + matrices as **skew/rotate/scale** transformations + [[LinearDependence]] / [[Rank]] / [[Determinant]] / [[EinsteinSummation|Einstein notation]] + [[Eigendecomposition]] $\mathbf{A}=\mathbf{W}\boldsymbol\Sigma\mathbf{W}^{-1}$ with $\det(\mathbf{A})=\prod_i\lambda_i$ → [[SingleVariableCalculus|single-variable calculus]]: derivatives as local linearization $f(x+\epsilon)\approx f(x)+\epsilon f'(x)$, pre-1986 *finite differences* vs [[Backpropagation|backprop]] (Rumelhart-Hinton-Williams 1986), [[TaylorSeries|Taylor expansion]] → [[MultivariableCalculus|multivariable calculus]]: [[Gradient|gradient]] as direction of steepest ascent via $\boldsymbol\epsilon\cdot\nabla L=\|\nabla L\|\cos\theta$, *"the most important mathematical concept in machine learning: the direction of steepest descent points in the direction of $-\nabla L$"*, multivariate [[ChainRule]] = [[Backpropagation]] → [[IntegralCalculus|integral calculus]]: $\int_a^b f=\lim\sum_i\epsilon\cdot f(x_i)$, [[FundamentalTheoremOfCalculus|fundamental theorem of calculus]], change of variables = "chain rule for integrals" → [[RandomVariable|random variables]]: [[ProbabilityDensityFunction|PDF]] / [[CumulativeDistributionFunction|CDF]] / joint / marginal / [[Covariance]] / [[Correlation]] → [[MaximumLikelihoodEstimation|MLE]] $=$ minimum [[CrossEntropy|NLL]] under independence; Bayesian interpretation with uninformative prior → asymptotic theory ([[FisherInformation|Fisher information]] / [[CramerRaoBound|Cramér-Rao]] / consistency / asymptotic normality) → [[BernoulliDistribution|Bernoulli]] / Discrete Uniform / Continuous Uniform / Binomial / [[PoissonDistribution|Poisson]] / [[GaussianDistribution|Normal]] / [[ExponentialDistribution|Exponential]] distributions + [[CentralLimitTheorem|CLT]] *"the normal distribution is essentially the limit of any sum of a large number of equal small independent contributions"* → [[NaiveBayes]] on binarized [[MNIST]] (~84% with conditional-independence assumption + [[LaplaceSmoothing]] + log-space) → [[Statistics|statistics]] ([[MeanSquaredError|MSE]] = [[BiasVarianceDecomposition|bias² + variance]], [[HypothesisTesting|hypothesis testing]] with type-I/II errors, statistical power, *p*-values, [[ConfidenceInterval|confidence intervals]]) → [[InformationTheory|information theory]] ([[SelfInformation|self-information]] $I(X)=-\log_2 p$, [[Entropy|Shannon entropy]] $H(X)=-E[\log p]$, joint / conditional entropy, [[MutualInformation|mutual information]] $I(X,Y)=H(X)+H(Y)-H(X,Y)\geq 0$, [[KullbackLeiblerDivergence|KL divergence]] $D_{KL}(P\|Q)\geq 0$ asymmetric, **[[CrossEntropy|cross-entropy]] = $H(P)+D_{KL}(P\|Q)$** which is *why* classification with [[CrossEntropyLoss|cross-entropy loss]] = MLE under categorical likelihood). Re-derives every load-bearing identity ([[MeanSquaredError|MSE]] $=$ Gaussian-NLL [[d2l-linear-regression]] §3.1.5, [[CrossEntropyLoss|cross-entropy]] $=$ categorical-NLL [[d2l-linear-classification]] §softmax) from first principles. The math reference shelf under every later D2L chapter — *"most software developers no longer need to worry about the theory of computable functions, neither should deep learning practitioners need to worry about the theoretical foundations of maximum likelihood learning — but we are not quite there yet."*
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 5.4.2 Control Circuits](sources/dis-5-4-2-control-circuits.md) — [[SuzanneJMatthews|Matthews]] / [[TiaNewhall|Newhall]] / [[KevinCWebb|Webb]]'s **second subsection** of [[dis-5-4-circuits|Ch 5.4]] — gate-level construction of the [[ControlCircuit|control]] category. *"Control circuits are used throughout a system. On the processor, they drive the execution of program instructions on program data. They also control loading and storing values to different levels of storage (between registers, cache, and RAM)."* Three named circuits: [[Multiplexer|MUX]] (*"selects, or chooses, one of several values"* — two-way 1-bit form `Out = (NOT(S) AND B) OR (S AND A)`; $N$-way uses $\log_2 N$ select bits decoded into $N$ AND-gate selectors merged by an $N$-way OR; two-way $N$-bit MUX stacks $N$ parallel 1-bit MUXes on a shared select line), [[Demultiplexer|DMUX]] (*"the inverse of a multiplexer"* — 1 input → $N$ outputs), [[Decoder]] (*"takes an encoded input and enables one of several outputs based on the input value"* — $\log_2 N \to N$ one-hot; also the **internal selection mechanism** inside every $N$-way MUX). CPU payoff: *"the CPU may use a multiplexer circuit to select from which [[CpuRegister|CPU register]] to read an instruction operand value"* — [[ControlUnit|control unit]]'s decode phase emits the select-bit signals. **Scope note**: **no encoder** circuit ($2^N \to N$ inverse of decoder) is introduced; the word *"encoded"* appears only inside the decoder definition. No sequencer / state-machine control, no tri-state buffers. **53rd ingested chapter**; **4 new concept pages** ([[ControlCircuit]] — promoted from forward-ref to category page; [[Multiplexer]]; [[Demultiplexer]]; [[Decoder]]). [[DiveIntoSystems]] corpus now at **53 chapters**.
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 5.4.1 Arithmetic and Logic Circuits](sources/dis-5-4-1-arithmetic-logic-circuits.md) — [[SuzanneJMatthews|Matthews]] / [[TiaNewhall|Newhall]] / [[KevinCWebb|Webb]]'s **first subsection** of [[dis-5-4-circuits|Ch 5.4]] — gate-level construction of the [[ArithmeticLogicCircuit|arithmetic-and-logic]] category. Three-step methodology ([[TruthTable|truth table]] → Boolean expression → [[LogicGate|gate]] network) walked through on the [[OneBitEqualityCircuit|1-bit equality circuit]] (≡ [[XnorGate|XNOR]]) and the [[HalfAdder|1-bit adder]] (one [[XorGate|XOR]] + one [[AndGate|AND]] → `Sum`, `CarryOut`). Extends to the [[FullAdder|1-bit full adder]] (`A` + `B` + `CarryIn` → `Sum = A XOR B XOR CarryIn`; `CarryOut = majority` — 8-row truth table promoted from [[dis-4-4-1-addition|Ch 4.4.1]]) and cascades $N$ of them into a **[[RippleCarryAdder|ripple-carry adder]]** — *"this type of N-bit adder circuit, built from N 1-bit adder circuits, is called a ripple carry adder"* and *"the SUM result ripples or propagates through the circuit from the low-order to the high-order bits."* Subtraction reuses the same N full adders + a row of inverters (or [[XorGate|XOR]]-mode gates) + `CarryIn_0 = 1` — *"a subtraction circuit that computes (A − B) can be built from adder and negation circuits"* — gate-level realization of [[dis-4-4-2-subtraction|Ch 4.4.2]]'s flip-and-add-one trick, no new arithmetic hardware. **Scope note**: multiplexer / op-select MUX is **not** introduced at this level; a full multi-op [[ArithmeticLogicUnit|ALU]] diagram is deferred. **52nd ingested chapter**; **5 new concept pages** ([[ArithmeticLogicCircuit]] — promoted from forward-ref to category page; [[OneBitEqualityCircuit]]; [[HalfAdder]]; [[FullAdder]] — promoted from cross-chapter forward-ref stub to first-class page; [[RippleCarryAdder]]). [[DiveIntoSystems]] corpus now at **52 chapters**.
