### Added with [[d2l-hyperparameter-optimization]] (D2L Hyperparameter Optimization)
- [Aaron Klein](entities/AaronKlein.md) — [[Amazon]] research scientist; first author of [[d2l-hyperparameter-optimization]]; primary contributor to [[SyneTune]].
- [Matthias Seeger](entities/MatthiasSeeger.md) — [[Amazon]] principal applied scientist; co-author of [[d2l-hyperparameter-optimization]]; architect of [[SyneTune]] and longtime Bayesian-ML / [[GaussianProcess|GP]] researcher.
- [Cédric Archambeau](entities/CedricArchambeau.md) — [[Amazon]] principal applied scientist; co-author of [[d2l-hyperparameter-optimization]]; led the Berlin AutoML group during [[SyneTune]]'s development.
- [James Bergstra](entities/JamesBergstra.md) — Author of *Random Search for Hyper-Parameter Optimization* (Bergstra & Bengio 2012) — the canonical justification for [[RandomSearch]] in [[d2l-hyperparameter-optimization]]; also TPE / [[HyperOpt]].
- [Lisha Li](entities/LishaLi.md) — First author of [[Hyperband]] (JMLR 2018) and [[ASHA]] (arxiv 1810.05934) — the multi-fidelity HPO algorithms operationalized in [[d2l-hyperparameter-optimization]] §sh-async via [[SyneTune]].
- [LiteLLM](entities/LiteLLM.md) — Open-source Python SDK ([github.com/BerriAI/litellm](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm)) from BerriAI providing a unified, OpenAI-shaped client over dozens of LLM providers ([[openai|OpenAI]] / [[anthropic|Anthropic]] / [[gemini|Gemini]] / Vertex AI / [[Databricks]] / [[microsoft|Azure]] / [[Anyscale]] / [[TogetherAI|Together AI]] / [[Ollama]] / [[SGLang]] / …) via a `provider/model-name` string convention. The upstream provider-abstraction layer underneath [[DSPy]]'s [[DSPyLM|`dspy.LM`]] universal client; the wiki entry recorded by [[dspy-language-models]].
- [Ollama](entities/Ollama.md) — Open-source local-laptop LLM runtime ([ollama.ai](https://ollama.ai/)); one-line install, one-line model-pull-and-run, local HTTP server on port 11434. The local-laptop deployment regime [[DSPy]] integrates via `dspy.LM('ollama_chat/llama3.2', api_base='http://localhost:11434')` ([[dspy-language-models]]).
- [SGLang](entities/SGLang.md) — Open-source GPU inference server ([github.com/sgl-project/sglang](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang)) for open-weight LLMs; exposes an OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint. The self-hosted-GPU deployment regime [[DSPy]] explicitly recommends — *"To host accurate open models on your own GPU(s), we recommend SGLang"* ([[dspy-language-models]]).
- [Together AI](entities/TogetherAI.md) — Managed-API LLM inference provider ([together.ai](https://www.together.ai/)) hosting open-weight models (Llama, Mistral, Qwen, …); one of [[DSPy]]'s [[DSPyLM|`dspy.LM`]]-supported managed providers via `together_ai/...` model string ([[dspy-language-models]]).
- [Syne Tune](entities/SyneTune.md) — [[Amazon]]'s open-source distributed HPO library (Salinas et al. AutoML 2022); D2L's preferred async-HPO backend ([[d2l-hyperparameter-optimization]] §rs-async, §sh-async).

### Added with [[d2l-generative-adversarial-networks]] (D2L Generative Adversarial Networks)
- [Ian Goodfellow](entities/IanGoodfellow.md) — Inventor of [[generativeadversarialnetwork|GANs]] (Goodfellow, Pouget-Abadie, Mirza et al. 2014) — the foundational 2014 paper [[d2l-generative-adversarial-networks]] §`gan` is built on. Co-author of the *Deep Learning* textbook (Goodfellow, Bengio & Courville 2016); ex-[[google|Google Brain]] / ex-[[OpenAI]] / ex-[[apple|Apple]] / ex-[[googledeepmind|DeepMind]].
- [Alec Radford](entities/AlecRadford.md) — First author of [[DCGAN]] ([[AlecRadford|Radford]], Metz & Chintala 2015) — the canonical convolutional GAN architecture that powers [[d2l-generative-adversarial-networks]] §`dcgan`. Also first author of [[GPT]] (2018) and [[GPT2|GPT-2]] (2019); [[OpenAI]] researcher; one of the most influential generative-model researchers of the 2015–2020 era.

### Added with [[d2l-appendix-mathematics]] (D2L Appendix: Mathematics for Deep Learning)
- [Brent Werness](entities/BrentWerness.md) — [[Amazon]] applied scientist; first author of [[d2l-appendix-mathematics]] (with [[RachelHu]]).
- [Rachel Hu](entities/RachelHu.md) — [[Amazon]] applied scientist; co-author of [[d2l-appendix-mathematics]] (with [[BrentWerness]]).
- [Claude Shannon](entities/ClaudeShannon.md) — American mathematician (1916–2001); founder of [[InformationTheory|information theory]] (1948 *A Mathematical Theory of Communication*); the **bit** as a unit of information, **[[Entropy|Shannon entropy]]**, source-coding and channel-capacity theorems — every modern [[CrossEntropyLoss|cross-entropy loss]] / [[LanguageModel|LM]] training objective descends from his framework ([[d2l-appendix-mathematics]] §information-theory).

### Added with [[d2l-appendix-tools]] (D2L Appendix: Tools for Deep Learning)
- [Amazon SageMaker](entities/AmazonSageMaker.md) — AWS managed-Jupyter ML platform; D2L's *fastest path to a GPU notebook* via `ml.p3.2xlarge` (V100 + 8-core CPU) with the framework-specific D2L repo cloned at provision time ([[d2l-appendix-tools]] §`sagemaker`).
- [Amazon EC2](entities/AmazonEC2.md) — AWS's raw VM service; cheaper alternative to [[AmazonSageMaker]] for D2L (requires manual [[CUDA]] install + [[Miniconda]] + `pip install d2l==1.0.3` + ssh `-L` port-forwarding). GPU instance taxonomy: `p2` (K80) / `p3` (V100) / `p4` (A100) / `g4` (T4 inference) ([[d2l-appendix-tools]] §`aws`).

### Added with [[d2l-recommender-systems]] (D2L Recommender Systems)
- [Shuai Zhang](entities/ShuaiZhang.md) — [[Amazon]] researcher; first author of [[d2l-recommender-systems]]; co-author of the canonical *Deep Learning Based Recommender System* survey (Zhang, Yao, Sun & Tay 2019, *ACM CSUR*).
- [Yi Tay](entities/YiTay.md) — [[google|Google]] researcher; third author of [[d2l-recommender-systems]]; better known for efficient-Transformer / scaling work (*Long Range Arena*, *Efficient Transformers: A Survey*) and as a Reka AI co-founder.
- [Yehuda Koren](entities/YehudaKoren.md) — Recommender-systems researcher most associated with [[MatrixFactorization]] and the [[NetflixPrize|Netflix \$1M Prize]] (BellKor's Pragmatic Chaos); seminal 2009 MF paper and 2008 [[ImplicitFeedback|implicit-feedback]] paper anchor [[d2l-recommender-systems]] §mf and §recsys-intro.
- [Steffen Rendle](entities/SteffenRendle.md) — Recommender-systems researcher; author of [[FactorizationMachines]] (Rendle 2010, *ICDM*) and [[BPR]] (Rendle et al. 2009, *UAI*) — two of the most cited papers in the field; [[google|Google Research]] at time of writing.
- [Xiangnan He](entities/XiangnanHe.md) — Recommender-systems researcher; first author of [[NeuMF]] / [[NeuralCollaborativeFiltering]] (He, Liao, Zhang, Nie, Hu, Chua 2017, *WWW*); NUS → USTC.
- [GroupLens](entities/GroupLens.md) — University of Minnesota research lab; maintains the [[MovieLens]] dataset family and live web service since 1997.
- [MovieLens](entities/MovieLens.md) — Canonical academic recommender-systems benchmark dataset (943 users × 1682 movies × 100K ratings in the 100K version); the running benchmark across all 8 sub-chapters of [[d2l-recommender-systems]].
- [Netflix Prize](entities/NetflixPrize.md) — \$1M open competition (2006–2009) to improve Netflix's Cinematch RMSE by 10%; won by BellKor's Pragmatic Chaos with an ensemble in which [[MatrixFactorization]] was the load-bearing component; the historical event that put MF on the recommender-systems map.

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-intro-index]] (The Embedded Rust Book — Introduction)
- [The Embedded Rust Book](entities/TheEmbeddedRustBook.md) — introductory book on using [[RustLanguage|Rust]] for [[BareMetalProgramming|bare-metal]] [[EmbeddedSystems|embedded systems]]; coordinated by the [[RustEmbeddedWorkingGroup]]'s resources team.
- [Rust (Programming Language)](entities/RustLanguage.md) — systems programming language with memory safety + zero-cost abstractions; runs in embedded contexts via `#![no_std]` + LLVM backend.
- [Rust Embedded Working Group](entities/RustEmbeddedWorkingGroup.md) — official Rust community WG owning the embedded ecosystem; maintains the [[EmbeddedRustBookshelf]] including [[TheEmbeddedRustBook]].
- [STMicroelectronics](entities/STMicroelectronics.md) — semiconductor vendor; producer of the STM32 [[ARMCortexM|Cortex-M]] MCU family and [[STM32F3DISCOVERY]] dev board.
- [STM32F3DISCOVERY](entities/STM32F3DISCOVERY.md) — [[ARMCortexM|Cortex-M4]] dev board from [[STMicroelectronics]]; reference hardware for every example in [[TheEmbeddedRustBook]].

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-intro-hardware]] (The Embedded Rust Book — Hardware)
- [STM32F303VCT6](entities/STM32F303VCT6.md) — application MCU on the [[STM32F3DISCOVERY]]; [[ARMCortexM|Cortex-M4F]] at 72 MHz, 256 KiB [[FlashMemory|Flash]] / 48 KiB [[SRAM]], 3.3 V signaling; integrated [[GPIO]] / [[I2C]] / [[SPI]] / [[USART]] / timers.
- [STM32F103](entities/STM32F103.md) — [[ARMCortexM|Cortex-M3]] MCU family from [[STMicroelectronics]]; on the [[STM32F3DISCOVERY]] it implements the on-board [[STLink|ST-LINK]] debugger over the "USB ST-LINK" port.
- [LSM303DLHC](entities/LSM303DLHC.md) — [[STMicroelectronics]] system-in-package combining a 3-axis [[Accelerometer]] + 3-axis [[Magnetometer]] over [[I2C]]; mounted on the [[STM32F3DISCOVERY]].
- [L3GD20](entities/L3GD20.md) — [[STMicroelectronics]] 3-axis MEMS [[Gyroscope]] over [[SPI]]; with [[LSM303DLHC]] completes the F3 board's 9-axis [[IMU]].
- [ST-LINK](entities/STLink.md) — [[STMicroelectronics]]'s in-circuit programmer/debugger protocol; the [[STM32F3DISCOVERY]] integrates an ST-LINK via a dedicated [[STM32F103]] so the board is self-programmable over USB.

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-intro-tooling]] (The Embedded Rust Book — Tooling)
- [Cargo](entities/Cargo.md) — [[RustLanguage|Rust]]'s build system / package manager; carries the subcommand interface [[CargoBinutils]] and [[CargoGenerate]] extend; drives [[CrossCompilation]] via `--target=<triple>`.
- [rustc](entities/Rustc.md) — Rust compiler; LLVM-backed multi-target codegen — *the* reason [[CargoBinutils]] tools cover every architecture Rust does.
- [rustup](entities/Rustup.md) — Rust toolchain installer; `rustup target add <triple>` is the operational bridge to [[CrossCompilation]] and `rustup component add llvm-tools` installs the LLVM tools [[CargoBinutils]] wraps.
- [cargo-binutils](entities/CargoBinutils.md) — Cargo subcommand wrapping LLVM `objdump` / `nm` / `size`; one-command cross-OS install; universal architecture coverage via shared LLVM backend with [[Rustc]].
- [cargo-generate](entities/CargoGenerate.md) — Cargo subcommand for creating projects from templates; the book's escape hatch for [[NoStd|`no_std`]] linker-script + memory-layout boilerplate.
- [QEMU](entities/QEMU.md) — full-system ARM emulator (`qemu-system-arm`); the book's no-hardware escape hatch — run embedded examples on the host without an [[STM32F3DISCOVERY|F3 board]].
- [OpenOCD](entities/OpenOCD.md) — open-source [[OnChipDebugging|on-chip-debug]] server; bridges [[GDB]] ↔ probe ([[STLink]] / [[JLink]] / [[MCULink]] / [[RustyProbe]]) over [[JTAG]] / [[SWD]]. Established standard; the alternative to [[ProbeRs]].
- [GDB](entities/GDB.md) — GNU Debugger; canonical CLI front-end for embedded-Rust debugging, drives [[OpenOCD]] / [[ProbeRs]] over Remote Serial Protocol.
- [Probe-rs](entities/ProbeRs.md) — modern, Rust-native alternative to [[OpenOCD]]; simpler config; ships its own [[ProbeRsVSCodeExtension|VS Code extension]].
- [Probe-rs VS Code Extension](entities/ProbeRsVSCodeExtension.md) — IDE debugger UI on [[ProbeRs]] (Rust pretty printing, error messages); VS Code counterpart to [[GDB]] CLI.
- [TRACE32](entities/TRACE32.md) — [[Lauterbach]]'s professional multi-arch debugger; ARM + RISC-V; ELF/DWARF-based so works with conventional Rust binaries without custom support.
- [Lauterbach](entities/Lauterbach.md) — German embedded-tools vendor; developer of [[TRACE32]].
- [Rusty-probe](entities/RustyProbe.md) — open-source USB debug probe designed for [[ProbeRs]].
- [J-Link](entities/JLink.md) — [[Segger]]'s debug probe family; ARM + RISC-V; unlimited flash breakpoints.
- [SEGGER Microcontroller](entities/Segger.md) — German embedded-tools vendor; developer of [[JLink]].
- [MCU-Link](entities/MCULink.md) — [[NXP]]'s budget-friendly debug probe; pairs with MCUXpresso IDE; targets ARM Cortex.
- [NXP Semiconductors](entities/NXP.md) — Dutch semiconductor vendor; producer of [[ARMCortexM|Cortex-M]] MCUs and the [[MCULink]] probe.

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-start-qemu]] (The Embedded Rust Book — QEMU)
- [LM3S6965](entities/LM3S6965.md) — TI / Luminary Micro [[ARMCortexM|Cortex-M3]] [[Microcontroller|MCU]]; the book's first code-example target *because* [[QEMU]] can emulate it (`qemu-system-arm -machine lm3s6965evb`). 256 KiB [[FlashMemory|Flash]] / 64 KiB [[SRAM]]; [[RustTarget|target triple]] `thumbv7m-none-eabi`.
- [cortex-m-rt](entities/CortexMRTCrate.md) — minimal startup / runtime crate for [[ARMCortexM|Cortex-M]]; supplies the reset handler / [[VectorTable|vector table]] / `.bss` / `.data` init that [[NoStd|`no_std`]] strips out, plus the `#[entry]` macro for marking `fn main() -> !`. The structural replacement for [[RustRuntime|`libstd`'s pre-`main` runtime]].
- [panic-halt](entities/PanicHaltCrate.md) — minimal `#[panic_handler]` provider that loops forever; the book's default panic crate before the deferred *Panicking* chapter ([[rust-embedded-book-start-qemu]]).
- [cortex-m-semihosting](entities/CortexMSemihostingCrate.md) — Rust crate exposing [[ARMSemihosting|ARM semihosting]] (`hprintln!`, `debug::exit`) on [[ARMCortexM|Cortex-M]]; the host-IO path the book's `hello` example uses under [[GDB]] + [[QEMU]].
- [defmt](entities/Defmt.md) — deferred-formatting logging framework from [[Knurling]] / [[FerrousSystems|Ferrous Systems]]; default in the chapter's `hello` example with `defmt-rtt` (real hardware) / `defmt-semihosting` (QEMU) transports.
- [Ferrous Systems](entities/FerrousSystems.md) — Berlin Rust consultancy; steward of [[Knurling]] and the [[Defmt|`defmt`]] / [[QemuRun|`qemu-run`]] / `probe-rs` / `app-template` stack the chapter pulls in.
- [Knurling](entities/Knurling.md) — Ferrous Systems' embedded-Rust tooling project (`github.com/knurling-rs`); umbrella for [[Defmt]] / [[QemuRun]] / `app-template` and a modern alternative to the [[CortexMQuickstartTemplate|`cortex-m-quickstart`]] flow.
- [qemu-run](entities/QemuRun.md) — Knurling's [[Defmt|`defmt`]]-aware [[QEMU]] launcher; the chapter's host-side decoder for `defmt-semihosting` output ([[rust-embedded-book-start-qemu]]).

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-start-registers]] (The Embedded Rust Book — Memory-mapped Registers)
- [cortex-m](entities/CortexMCrate.md) — canonical [[MicroArchitectureCrate|micro-architecture crate]] for [[ARMCortexM|Cortex-M]]; exposes interrupt enable/disable + the core-standardized [[SysTick]] peripheral via `Peripherals::take()`. The entry layer of the chapter's first code sample ([[rust-embedded-book-start-registers]]).
- [svd2rust](entities/Svd2Rust.md) — [[RustEmbeddedWorkingGroup|Rust Embedded WG]] code generator consuming a vendor's [[SVDFile|CMSIS-SVD XML]] and emitting a fully typed [[PeripheralAccessCrate|PAC]] crate with the closure-based `read()` / `write()` / `modify()` register API; the **mechanism** behind the ecosystem's uniform PAC ergonomics ([[rust-embedded-book-start-registers]]).
- [embedded-hal](entities/EmbeddedHalCrate.md) — [[Portability|portability]] trait crate (`digital::OutputPin`, `serial::Read/Write`, `i2c::I2c`, `spi::SpiBus`, `delay::DelayNs`, …) that every [[HALCrate|HAL crate]] implements; lets driver / application code be written once and compiled against any chip's HAL ([[rust-embedded-book-start-registers]]).
- [tm4c123x](entities/Tm4c123xCrate.md) — the chapter's worked [[PeripheralAccessCrate|PAC]] example for TI's Tiva-C TM4C123 ([[ARMCortexM|Cortex-M4]] / 80 MHz / 256 KiB Flash); auto-generated by [[Svd2Rust|`svd2rust`]] from the chip's [[SVDFile|SVD]] ([[rust-embedded-book-start-registers]]).

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-start-semihosting]] (The Embedded Rust Book — Semihosting)
- [panic-semihosting](entities/PanicSemihostingCrate.md) — Rust `#[panic_handler]` provider that logs the panic message to the host's stderr via [[ARMSemihosting|ARM semihosting]] ([[CortexMSemihostingCrate|`cortex-m-semihosting`]] under the hood); with the optional `"exit"` Cargo feature, additionally invokes `debug::exit(EXIT_FAILURE)` after logging — the chapter's recipe for [[NoStd|`no_std`]] run-pass tests on [[QEMU]] (panic → host stderr → `$? = 1`). **Never use `"exit"` on real hardware** — `debug::exit` corrupts the [[OpenOCD]] session ([[rust-embedded-book-start-semihosting]]).

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-start-panicking]] (The Embedded Rust Book — Panicking)
- [panic-abort](entities/PanicAbortCrate.md) — minimal Rust [[PanicHandlerAttribute|`#[panic_handler]`]] crate that executes the target's abort instruction (Cortex-M `UDF`); the chapter's recommended **release-profile** panic handler in the profile-conditional swap pattern (smallest binary size, no panic message preserved) ([[rust-embedded-book-start-panicking]]).
- [panic-itm](entities/PanicItmCrate.md) — Rust [[PanicHandlerAttribute|`#[panic_handler]`]] crate that streams the panic message via the [[ARMCortexM|Cortex-M]] **ITM** (Instrumentation Trace Macrocell) trace peripheral over SWO — the hardware-fast alternative to [[PanicSemihostingCrate|`panic-semihosting`]] when SWO + a compatible probe ([[STLink]], [[JLink]]) are available ([[rust-embedded-book-start-panicking]]).
- [panic-probe](entities/PanicProbeCrate.md) — [[Knurling]] / [[FerrousSystems]] `#[panic_handler]` crate that formats the panic via [[Defmt|`defmt`]] over RTT and then hard-faults to break the debugger; modern alternative to the four crates the chapter explicitly lists, pointed at via *crates.io/keywords/panic-handler* ([[rust-embedded-book-start-panicking]]).

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-concurrency-index]] (The Embedded Rust Book — Concurrency)
- [RTIC](entities/RTIC.md) — **Real-Time Interrupt-driven Concurrency** framework for embedded Rust; static-priority scheduling + compile-time `static mut` resource tracking, deadlock-free by construction, `async` executor included. Named as the first higher-level alternative to manual `Mutex<RefCell<Option<T>>>` ([[rust-embedded-book-concurrency-index]]).
- [Embassy](entities/Embassy.md) — `async`/`await`-based embedded Rust framework; battery-included (`embassy-executor`, `embassy-time`, vendor HALs, `embassy-sync`). Named as the second higher-level alternative ([[rust-embedded-book-concurrency-index]]).
- [bare-metal (crate)](entities/BareMetalCrate.md) — architecture-agnostic Rust concurrency primitives (`CriticalSection` token, `Mutex<T>`) re-exported by [[CortexMCrate|`cortex-m`]] and other arch crates; maintained by the [[RustEmbeddedWorkingGroup]] ([[rust-embedded-book-concurrency-index]]).

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-collections-index]] (The Embedded Rust Book — Collections)
- [alloc (crate)](entities/AllocCrate.md) — Standard-distribution Rust crate providing heap-backed collection implementations (`Box`, `Vec`, `String`, `BTreeMap`, …); opt-in path back to dynamic collections under [[NoStd|`#![no_std]`]]. Activation contract: `#[global_allocator]` static implementing [[GlobalAlloc|`GlobalAlloc`]] **plus** an [[AllocErrorHandlerAttribute|`#[alloc_error_handler]`]] for [[OutOfMemory|OOM]] ([[rust-embedded-book-collections-index]]).
- [heapless (crate)](entities/HeaplessCrate.md) — Fixed-capacity, stack-allocated Rust collections (`Vec<_, U8>` etc.) with no global-allocator dependency; capacity in the type signature via [[Typenum|`typenum`]] (v0.4.x), every insertion returns `Result`, `push` is constant-time. **OOM impossible** if used exclusively. The canonical [[AllocCrate|`alloc`]] alternative for embedded ([[rust-embedded-book-collections-index]]).
- [typenum (crate)](entities/Typenum.md) — Type-level numerics for Rust — unsigned/signed ints + arithmetic encoded entirely in the type system. Pre-`const-generics` mechanism that [[HeaplessCrate|`heapless`]] (v0.4.x) uses to encode each collection's capacity directly in its type ([[rust-embedded-book-collections-index]]).
- [alloc-cortex-m (crate)](entities/AllocCortexMCrate.md) — Production-grade [[GlobalAllocator|global allocator]] for [[ARMCortexM|Cortex-M]] firmware (wraps `linked_list_allocator`); the [[RustEmbeddedWorkingGroup]]-maintained alternative the chapter recommends over its illustrative [[BumpPointerAllocator|bump-pointer allocator]]; first forward-referenced from [[rust-embedded-book-intro-no-std]] ([[rust-embedded-book-collections-index]]).

- [Alex Krizhevsky](entities/AlexKrizhevsky.md) — Co-first-author of [[AlexNet]] (2012); [[GeoffreyHinton|Hinton]] PhD student; author of `cuda-convnet`; [[Dropout]] co-author ([[d2l-convolutional-modern]]).
- [Ilya Sutskever](entities/IlyaSutskever.md) — [[AlexNet]] co-author (2012), [[1409.3215-seq2seq|seq2seq]] first author (2014); [[OpenAI]] co-founder and former Chief Scientist ([[d2l-convolutional-modern]]).
- [Geoffrey Hinton](entities/GeoffreyHinton.md) — Senior author of [[AlexNet]], [[Dropout]], and [[LayerNormalization]]; 2018 [[TuringAward]] co-recipient with [[YannLeCun]] and [[YoshuaBengio]] ([[d2l-convolutional-modern]] / [[d2l-multilayer-perceptrons]]).
- [Karen Simonyan](entities/KarenSimonyan.md) — Co-author of [[VGG]] (2014) at [[oxforduniversity|Oxford]]'s Visual Geometry Group; later [[googledeepmind|DeepMind]]; Inflection AI; [[Microsoft|Microsoft AI]] ([[d2l-convolutional-modern]]).
- [Andrew Zisserman](entities/AndrewZisserman.md) — Senior author of [[VGG]] (2014); head of [[oxforduniversity|Oxford]] Visual Geometry Group; *Multiple View Geometry* textbook author — anchor of the pre-deep-learning CV tradition ([[d2l-convolutional-modern]]).
- [Christian Szegedy](entities/ChristianSzegedy.md) — First author of [[GoogLeNet]] / [[Inception]] (2014); co-author with [[SergeyIoffe|Ioffe]] of [[BatchNormalization]] (2015) ([[d2l-convolutional-modern]]).
- [Sergey Ioffe](entities/SergeyIoffe.md) — First author of [[BatchNormalization]] (Ioffe & Szegedy 2015); [[google|Google]] researcher; co-author of [[Inception]]-v3 / v4 ([[d2l-convolutional-modern]]).
- [Kaiming He](entities/KaimingHe.md) — First author of [[ResNet]] (2015), [[HeInitialization]] (2015), Mask R-CNN (2017), MoCo (2020); MSRA → [[fair|FAIR]] → MIT ([[d2l-convolutional-modern]]).
- [University of Oxford](entities/oxforduniversity.md) — Institutional home of the Visual Geometry Group; [[VGG]] (Simonyan & Zisserman 2014) and Hartley & Zisserman's *Multiple View Geometry* ([[d2l-convolutional-modern]]).
- [Sepp Hochreiter](entities/SeppHochreiter.md) — Austrian computer scientist; co-inventor of [[LSTM]] with [[JurgenSchmidhuber|Schmidhuber]] (1997); 1991 Master's thesis first articulated the [[VanishingGradient|vanishing-gradient]] problem ([[d2l-recurrent-modern]]).
- [Jürgen Schmidhuber](entities/JurgenSchmidhuber.md) — Senior author of [[LSTM]] (Hochreiter & Schmidhuber 1997); longtime director of IDSIA; trained Hochreiter / Gers / Graves ([[d2l-recurrent-modern]]).
- [Kyunghyun Cho](entities/KyunghyunCho.md) — NYU professor; first author of [[GRU]] (2014) and of the [[KyunghyunCho|Cho]]-style [[EncoderDecoder|encoder-decoder]] design ([[d2l-recurrent-modern]]).
- [Mike Schuster](entities/MikeSchuster.md) — Co-author with [[KuldipPaliwal|Paliwal]] of the [[BidirectionalRNN|bidirectional RNN]] paper (1997); later [[google|Google]] (GNMT) ([[d2l-recurrent-modern]]).
- [Kuldip Paliwal](entities/KuldipPaliwal.md) — Australian signal-processing researcher; co-author with [[MikeSchuster|Schuster]] of the [[BidirectionalRNN|bidirectional RNN]] paper (1997) ([[d2l-recurrent-modern]]).
- [Kishore Papineni](entities/KishorePapineni.md) — First author of [[BLEU]] (Papineni, Roukos, Ward & Zhu 2002) — the dominant MT evaluation metric ([[d2l-recurrent-modern]]).
- [Alexey Dosovitskiy](entities/Dosovitskiy.md) — First author of the [[VisionTransformer|ViT]] paper (2021); established patches-as-tokens as the default vision backbone for foundation models ([[d2l-attention-and-transformers]]).
- [Diederik P. Kingma](entities/DiederikKingma.md) — Co-author with [[JimmyBa]] of the [[Adam]] optimizer (2014); also VAE co-inventor with Welling 2013 ([[d2l-optimization]]).
- [Jimmy Lei Ba](entities/JimmyBa.md) — Co-author with [[DiederikKingma]] of [[Adam]] (2014); also co-author of [[LayerNormalization]] (Ba, Kiros & Hinton 2016) ([[d2l-optimization]]).
- [Boris T. Polyak](entities/BorisPolyak.md) — Soviet/Russian mathematician (1935–2023); introduced heavy-ball [[Momentum]] (1964) — the foundational form of every modern optimizer's momentum term ([[d2l-optimization]]).
- [Yurii Nesterov](entities/YuriiNesterov.md) — Russian-Belgian mathematician; introduced [[NesterovMomentum|accelerated gradient]] (1983, optimal $\mathcal{O}(1/T^2)$ on smooth convex); canonical convex-optimization references ([[d2l-optimization]]).
- [John C. Duchi](entities/JohnDuchi.md) — [[stanforduniversity|Stanford]] statistician; lead author of [[Adagrad]] (Duchi, Hazan & Singer 2011) — the first widely-used per-coordinate adaptive learning-rate algorithm ([[d2l-optimization]]).
- [Matthew D. Zeiler](entities/MatthewZeiler.md) — Clarifai founder/CEO; author of [[Adadelta]] (2012) — the no-learning-rate Adagrad variant ([[d2l-optimization]]).

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-interoperability-c-with-rust]] (The Embedded Rust Book — A little C with your Rust)
- [bindgen](entities/Bindgen.md) — `rust-lang/rust-bindgen`; auto-generates [[ReprC|`#[repr(C)]`]] struct definitions and [[ExternC|`extern "C"`]] function blocks from C/C++ headers. For [[NoStd|`no_std`]] embedded use, set `--ctypes-prefix=cty` (so emitted code references the [`cty`] crate's primitives) and `--use-core` (so emitted code references `core::` paths instead of `std::`); the resulting `bindings.rs` is the matching Rust side for whatever C archive the [[CcCrate|`cc` crate]] / `make` / `CMake` produces. Typically invoked from a [[BuildRs|`build.rs`]] over a single `bindings.h` that `#include`s the C header set. ([[rust-embedded-book-interoperability-c-with-rust]]).
- [cc crate](entities/CcCrate.md) — `alexcrichton/cc-rs`; idiomatic-Rust wrapper around the host's C/C++ compiler invoked from a [[BuildRs|`build.rs`]] (`cc::Build::new().file("src/foo.c").compile("foo")`) — produces a `libfoo.a` static archive in `target/` that Cargo's final link step pulls into the embedded binary. The **simple-case branch** of the C-build decision tree in [[rust-embedded-book-interoperability-c-with-rust]] (vs. shelling out to `make` / `CMake` via `std::process::Command` for complex projects, vs. linking a pre-distributed `.a` directly). Dispatches on `$CC_<target>` so cross-compiling a `thumbv7m-none-eabi` package drives `arm-none-eabi-gcc` automatically. ([[rust-embedded-book-interoperability-c-with-rust]]).

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-interoperability-rust-with-c]] (The Embedded Rust Book — A little Rust with your C)
- [cbindgen](entities/Cbindgen.md) — `eqrion/cbindgen`; the **inverse-direction** codegen tool — scans Rust source for `#[no_mangle] pub extern "C" fn` ([[NoMangle]] + [[ExternC]]) and `#[repr(C)]` ([[ReprC]]) items, emits matching C `.h` / `.hpp` declarations (`void rust_function();`, `typedef struct CoolStruct { ... }`). Symmetric counterpart to [[Bindgen|`bindgen`]] — `bindgen` translates C → Rust, `cbindgen` translates Rust → C; a project doing both directions uses both. Typically invoked from a [[BuildRs|`build.rs`]] so the generated header is regenerated whenever the Rust source changes. The C-side consumer `#include`s the generated header and links the Cargo-produced [[CrateType|`cdylib`]] (`lib<name>.so`) or [[CrateType|`staticlib`]] (`lib<name>.a`) at link time. ([[rust-embedded-book-interoperability-rust-with-c]]).

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-unsorted-math]] (The Embedded Rust Book — Performing Math Functionality)
- [libm](entities/LibmCrate.md) — `rust-lang/libm` ([crates.io/crates/libm](https://crates.io/crates/libm)); **pure-Rust port of C's `libm`** — the standard math library. Re-exposes `<math.h>` operations (`sqrt`, `sin`, `cos`, `exp`, `log`, `pow`, `floor`, …) as Rust **free functions** callable from any [[NoStd|`#![no_std]`]] crate with no [[GlobalAllocator|global allocator]] or [[RustRuntime|runtime]] dependency. The gap-filler the math chapter recommends because [[RustCoreLibrary|`core`]] exposes `f32` / `f64` but **not** their transcendental / rounding methods (those live only in [[RustStandardLibrary|`std`]] as inherent methods on the primitive types). API shape — `use libm::{exp, floorf, sin, sqrtf};` then `sqrtf(x)` replaces `x.sqrt()`. Precision follows C convention: `f`-suffixed = `f32` (`sqrtf`, `floorf`), no-suffix = `f64` (`sin`, `exp`); the math chapter's example uses `.into()` to widen `f32` to `f64` when calling the `f64` variants. Maintained by the [[RustEmbeddedWorkingGroup|Rust Embedded WG]]. ([[rust-embedded-book-unsorted-math]]).

### Added with [[leh-ch01-understanding-llm-twin-concept]] through [[leh-ch11-mlops-and-llmops]] (LLM Engineer's Handbook — Iusztin, Labonne, Vesa; Packt 2024)

Authors and publisher:
- [Paul Iusztin](entities/PaulIusztin.md) — Co-author of *LLM Engineer's Handbook*; ML/MLOps engineer; LLM Twin project lead.
- [Maxime Labonne](entities/MaximeLabonne.md) — Co-author of *LLM Engineer's Handbook*; owner of the `mlabonne/TwinLlama-3.1-8B` / `…-DPO` Hugging Face models and the `mlabonne/llmtwin` / `…-dpo` datasets.
- [Alex Vesa](entities/AlexVesa.md) — Co-author of *LLM Engineer's Handbook*; senior MLOps/cloud engineer.
- [Packt Publishing](entities/PacktPublishing.md) — Publisher of *LLM Engineer's Handbook* (2024) and the companion GitHub org `PacktPublishing/LLM-Engineers-Handbook`.
- [LLM Engineer's Handbook](entities/LLMEngineersHandbook.md) — Packt 2024 book (Iusztin / Labonne / Vesa) that walks the LLM Twin project end-to-end across 11 chapters.
- [Chip Huyen](entities/ChipHuyen.md) — Author of *Designing Machine Learning Systems* / *Building a Generative AI Platform*; cited as a primary external reference in Ch 11 MLOps/LLMOps framing.
- [Jim Dowling](entities/JimDowling.md) — CEO of [[Hopsworks]]; credited as the originator of the [[FTIArchitecture|Feature/Training/Inference pipeline]] pattern Ch 1 builds the book's architecture around.
- [Hopsworks](entities/Hopsworks.md) — Feature-store company (founder Jim Dowling); origin of the [[FTIArchitecture|FTI pipeline]] writeup; cited as a feature-store and deployment-platform option.

Cloud / AWS services:
- [Amazon Bedrock](entities/AmazonBedrock.md) — AWS serverless foundation-model API; explicitly rejected by the book in favor of [[AmazonSageMaker]] because it hides the engineering the book teaches.
- [Amazon CloudWatch](entities/AmazonCloudWatch.md) — AWS metrics/logs service; backs billing alarms and the alarms behind [[TargetTrackingScaling]] in the SageMaker autoscaling setup.
- [Amazon ECR](entities/AmazonECR.md) — Elastic Container Registry; Docker image registry used by ZenML, the SageMaker DLC stack, and the LLM Twin CD pipeline.
- [Amazon ECS](entities/AmazonECS.md) — Elastic Container Service; alternative production home for the FastAPI business microservice.
- [Amazon EKS](entities/AmazonEKS.md) — Elastic Kubernetes Service; alternative production home for the FastAPI business microservice.
- [AWS CLI](entities/AWSCLI.md) — Amazon's command-line tool for AWS; configured via `aws configure` in Ch 2; drives the SageMaker / ECR / IAM setup.

Orchestrators and MLOps platforms:
- [ZenML](entities/ZenML.md) — Open-source ML pipeline orchestrator with `@pipeline` / `@step` decorators and a "stack" abstraction; the canonical orchestrator for the LLM Twin pipelines.
- [Airflow](entities/Airflow.md) — Apache Airflow; general-purpose DAG orchestrator, evaluated and rejected vs ZenML for the book.
- [Prefect](concepts/Prefect.md) — Workflow orchestration platform; evaluated as a ZenML alternative.
- [Dagster](entities/Dagster.md) — Data orchestrator focused on assets/lineage; ZenML alternative.
- [Metaflow](entities/Metaflow.md) — Netflix-originated ML workflow framework; ZenML alternative.
- [Argo Workflows](entities/ArgoWorkflows.md) — Kubernetes-native workflow engine; ZenML alternative.
- [Kubeflow](entities/Kubeflow.md) — Kubernetes-native ML platform; ZenML alternative.

Experiment tracking, model registry, and prompt monitoring:
- [Opik](entities/Opik.md) — Comet ML's open-source prompt-monitoring / LLM tracing tool; used in LLM Twin via the `@track` decorator for full RAG traces with per-step latency, tokens, and cost.
- [Langfuse](entities/Langfuse.md) — Open-source LLM observability platform; alternative to [[Opik]] evaluated in Ch 2 and Ch 11.
- [LangSmith](entities/LangSmith.md) — LangChain's hosted LLM observability product; alternative to [[Opik]].
- [Galileo](entities/Galileo.md) — LLM observability and guardrails platform; Galileo Protect cited for prompt-injection / toxicity / hallucination detection.

Vector databases:
- [Qdrant](entities/Qdrant.md) — Open-source vector database (Rust); LLM Twin's online retrieval store and (with metadata-only collections) part of the "logical feature store."
- [MongoDB](entities/MongoDB.md) — NoSQL document database used as the LLM Twin "data warehouse" for raw scraped text.
- [Pinecone](entities/Pinecone.md) — Managed vector database; Qdrant alternative.
- [Milvus](entities/Milvus.md) — Open-source vector database; Qdrant alternative.
- [Weaviate](entities/Weaviate.md) — Open-source vector database with built-in modules; Qdrant alternative.
- [ChromaDB](entities/ChromaDB.md) — Embedded/server vector database; Qdrant alternative.
- [pgvector](entities/Pgvector.md) — PostgreSQL extension adding vector similarity search; vector-DB alternative for Postgres shops.
- [Redis Vector Search](entities/RedisVectorSearch.md) — Redis Stack's vector similarity capability; Qdrant alternative.
- [Superlinked](entities/Superlinked.md) — Multi-index vector ML framework; publisher of the Vector DB Comparison and the proposed multi-index improvement for LLM Twin retrieval.

Web crawling and HTTP toolchain:
- [LangChain](entities/LangChain.md) — Python framework for LLM applications; used selectively in LLM Twin (`AsyncHtmlLoader`, `Html2TextTransformer`, `PromptTemplate`, `RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter`) while the book explicitly cautions against heavy reliance.
- [LlamaIndex](entities/LlamaIndex.md) — RAG framework; namechecked alongside LangChain and Haystack as a comparable framework whose internals the book reimplements.
- [Selenium](entities/Selenium.md) — Browser-automation framework; drives headless Chrome for the Medium and LinkedIn crawlers.
- [BeautifulSoup](entities/BeautifulSoup.md) — Python HTML parser; pairs with [[Selenium]] to extract titles, subtitles, and body text from rendered pages.
- [Scrapy](entities/Scrapy.md) — Production-grade Python web scraping framework; recommended for general structured-data scraping.
- [Crawl4AI](entities/Crawl4AI.md) — LLM-targeted open-source web crawler recommended for production RAG ingestion.
- [ChromeDriver](entities/ChromeDriver.md) — WebDriver for Chrome (installed via `chromedriver_autoinstaller`); the Selenium-driver mismatch is the chapter's documented failure mode.
- [mongoengine](entities/Mongoengine.md) — Production Python ODM for MongoDB; the comparison point the book's hand-rolled `NoSQLBaseDocument` is benchmarked against.
- [SQLAlchemy](entities/SQLAlchemy.md) — Python SQL toolkit and ORM; cited to motivate the ORM → ODM analogy.
- [SQLModel](entities/SQLModel.md) — FastAPI author's SQLAlchemy wrapper; cited alongside SQLAlchemy.
- [Pydantic](entities/Pydantic.md) — Python data-validation library; underpins every domain document, FastAPI request/response schema, and Settings class in the book.
- [Loguru](entities/Loguru.md) — Python logging library used throughout the LLM Twin codebase.
- [Pulumi](entities/Pulumi.md) — Infrastructure-as-Code tool referenced as the IaC option in Ch 4.

Python tooling:
- [Pyenv](entities/Pyenv.md) — Per-directory Python version manager; pins the book to Python 3.11.8 via a `.python-version` file.
- [Poetry](entities/PoetryPython.md) — Python dependency manager + virtualenv tool; uses `pyproject.toml` + `poetry.lock` for reproducibility.
- [Poe the Poet](entities/PoeThePoet.md) — Poetry-plugin task runner that centralizes CLI commands in `pyproject.toml` `[tool.poe.tasks]`.
- [uv](entities/UV.md) — Rust-based, faster Poetry alternative the authors recommend testing.
- [Conda](entities/Conda.md) — Anaconda/Miniconda environment manager; virtualenv-alternative mentioned and contrasted.
- [Pipenv](entities/Pipenv.md) — Pipfile-based Python dependency manager; Poetry alternative.

Containers / serving / quantization:
- [Docker](entities/Docker.md) — Container runtime; used to bring up MongoDB / Qdrant / ZenML locally and to build the LLM Twin SageMaker images.
- [Kubernetes](entities/Kubernetes.md) — Container orchestrator; substrate under Argo Workflows, Kubeflow, and AWS EKS.
- [Unsloth](entities/Unsloth.md) — Daniel & Michael Han's fine-tuning library with custom kernels; 2–5× speedup and up to 80% memory reduction over baseline TRL; used for the TwinLlama-3.1-8B SFT and DPO runs.
- [TRL](entities/TRL.md) — Hugging Face's Transformer Reinforcement Learning library (`SFTTrainer`, `DPOTrainer`); core fine-tuning + preference-alignment runtime.
- [Text Generation Inference](entities/TextGenerationInference.md) — Hugging Face's open-source LLM serving engine (TGI); tensor parallelism, FlashAttention-2, continuous batching, `safetensors` loading, SSE token streaming.
- [bitsandbytes](entities/Bitsandbytes.md) — Tim Dettmers's k-bit quantization library (`load_in_8bit=True` / `load_in_4bit=True`); powers LLM.int8 + NF4 and is wired into TGI's `HF_MODEL_QUANTIZE`.
- [Safetensors](entities/Safetensors.md) — Hugging Face's fast/safe tensor serialization format used by TGI for accelerated weight loading.
- [Outlines](entities/Outlines.md) — Structured-generation library for constrained LLM output; recommended for JSON-mode dataset generation and LLM-as-judge prompts.
- [boto3](entities/Boto3.md) — Amazon's official Python SDK for AWS; drives all SageMaker control-plane and inference-plane automation in the deployment chapters.
- [Uvicorn](entities/Uvicorn.md) — Lightning-fast ASGI server; runs the FastAPI business microservice locally.

Model families and products:
- [ChatGPT](entities/ChatGPT.md) — OpenAI's flagship consumer chatbot product; framed in Ch 1 as the generic-chatbot baseline the LLM Twin is designed to outperform on personal-content tasks.
- [GPT](entities/GPT.md) — OpenAI's GPT family of decoder-only LLMs (GPT-3.5 / GPT-4 / GPT-4o / GPT-4o-mini); one of three swappable model families in the LLM Twin training pipeline.
- [Llama](entities/Llama.md) — Meta's open-weight LLM family (Llama 2, Llama 3, Llama 3.1, Llama 4); the base family for TwinLlama-3.1-8B.
- [Mistral](entities/Mistral.md) — Mistral AI's open-weight LLM family (Mistral 7B, Mixtral, etc.); one of three swappable model families in the LLM Twin training pipeline.
- [TwinLlama](entities/TwinLlama.md) — The Llama-3.1-8B-derived model family the book produces (`mlabonne/TwinLlama-3.1-8B`, `…-DPO`, `…-13`); fine-tuned + DPO-aligned to imitate the authors' writing style.

Deployment platforms (mentioned as alternatives):
- [Modal](entities/Modal.md) — Python-native serverless cloud for compute; SageMaker alternative.
- [Seldon](entities/Seldon.md) — Production ML serving platform; SageMaker alternative.
- [Google Cloud Vertex AI](entities/GoogleCloudVertexAI.md) — Google's managed ML platform; SageMaker alternative.
- [Azure ML](entities/AzureML.md) — Microsoft's managed ML platform; SageMaker alternative.
- [Azure OpenAI](entities/AzureOpenAI.md) — Microsoft's managed OpenAI-API offering; SageMaker alternative for proprietary-model serving.

- [MIRACL](entities/MIRACL.md) — Multilingual retrieval benchmark; Ch 8's source for the headline reranker-efficacy claim *"a reranker can boost performance from 36.5 to 62.8, measured as nDCG@10."*
- [BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5](entities/BGESmallEnV15.md) — [[BAAI]]'s small English BGE embedding model; Ch 8's named local-RAG embedding model — *"at the time of writing, it is high on the MTEB leaderboard for embedding models and relatively small."*
- [BAAI (Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence)](entities/BAAI.md) — Producer of the BGE family of embedding models; Ch 8's source for the `BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5` embedding model.
- [Cohere Rerank](entities/CohereRerank.md) — Cohere's `co.rerank` managed-API endpoint; Ch 8's worked cross-encoder reranking primitive (no training/tuning required).
- [Cohere Chat](entities/CohereChat.md) — Cohere's `co.chat` managed-API endpoint with `documents=...` parameter for grounded generation; Ch 8's worked example produces **span-level citations** automatically.
- [Cohere Embed](entities/CohereEmbed.md) — Cohere's `co.embed` managed-API endpoint with `input_type="search_document" / "search_query"` for dense retrieval; Ch 8's worked embedding API.
- [Patrick Lewis](entities/PatrickLewis.md) — First author of *"Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks"* (Lewis et al. 2020, NeurIPS 33: 9459–9474) — the foundational [[rag|RAG]] paper Ch 8 cites.
- [Nelson F. Liu](entities/NelsonFLiu.md) — First author of *"Evaluating verifiability in generative search engines"* (arXiv:2304.09848); Ch 8's source for the four-axis [[RAGEvaluation|RAG-evaluation]] taxonomy (fluency / perceived utility / citation recall / citation precision).
- [Percy Liang](entities/PercyLiang.md) — Stanford NLP professor; last author of the Liu / Zhang / Liang 2023 generative-search-engines verifiability paper.

<!-- Added with the [[iir-ch01-boolean-retrieval|IIR]] (Introduction to Information Retrieval, Manning/Raghavan/Schütze 2008) 21-chapter ingest. The "founding fathers" of IR — authors of the textbook itself plus the canonical inventors of tf-idf, BM25, PageRank, HITS, LSI, Porter stemming, and the Probability Ranking Principle. -->
- [Christopher D. Manning](entities/ChristopherManning.md) — Stanford NLP director; first author of *Introduction to Information Retrieval* (CUP 2008) and *Foundations of Statistical NLP* (MIT 1999); GloVe / Stanford Parser / CS224N.
- [Prabhakar Raghavan](entities/PrabhakarRaghavan.md) — IIR co-author; theoretical CS (randomized algorithms, k-server); senior VP of Search at [[google|Google]] since 2020 — the executive responsible for Google's user-facing search products.
- [Hinrich Schütze](entities/HinrichSchutze.md) — IIR co-author; chair of computational linguistics at LMU Munich; *Foundations of Statistical NLP* (1999, with Manning); early proponent of distributional semantics — vector representations of word meaning from co-occurrence statistics.
- [Gerard Salton](entities/GerardSalton.md) — "Father of information retrieval"; Cornell CS; architect of the [[VectorSpaceModel]] and the SMART system; ACM SIGIR's lifetime-achievement award (the [[GerardSalton|Gerard Salton Award]]) is named in his honor.
- [Martin Porter](entities/MartinPorter.md) — Author of the Porter stemming algorithm (1980) and the Snowball stemmer language (2001); the default stemmer for English IR systems for 45 years; bundled into Lucene / Elasticsearch / Solr.
- [Stephen Robertson](entities/StephenRobertson.md) — Author of the [[ProbabilityRankingPrinciple]] (1977); co-inventor of [[OkapiBM25|BM25]] (1994) with Sparck Jones et al. at City University London; MSR Cambridge emeritus.
- [Karen Spärck Jones](entities/KarenSparckJones.md) — (1935–2007) coined [[InverseDocumentFrequency|idf]] in *"A Statistical Interpretation of Term Specificity"* (J. Doc. 1972); co-developer of [[BinaryIndependenceModel]] and [[OkapiBM25|BM25]] with Robertson; ACM SIGIR Gerard Salton Award (2000).
- [Larry Page](entities/LarryPage.md) — Co-founder of [[google|Google]] (1998, with Brin); co-inventor of [[PageRank]] at [[stanforduniversity|Stanford]] under [[TerryWinograd|Terry Winograd]]; CEO of Google 2001 + 2011–2015; CEO of Alphabet 2015–2019.
- [Sergey Brin](entities/SergeyBrin.md) — Co-founder of [[google|Google]] (1998, with Page); co-inventor of [[PageRank]]; president of Alphabet 2015–2019; returned to hands-on technical work on the [[Gemini]] LLM project (2023).
- [Jon Kleinberg](entities/JonKleinberg.md) — Cornell CS; inventor of the [[HITS]] hubs-and-authorities link-analysis algorithm (1998, contemporaneous with PageRank); ACM Knuth Prize (2021); MacArthur (2005); Nevanlinna Prize (2006).

Bumped to 1119 with [[dspy-evaluation-overview]] (+1: [[DSPyEvaluation]] — the canonical anchor for DSPy's evaluation philosophy and the middle stage of the [[dspy-learn-index|three-stage Programming → Evaluation → Optimization]] workflow; operationalizes the stage as a **four-step iterative loop** (collect 20–200-example dev set → define DSPy metric → run development evaluations → recursively optimize the metric when it is a DSPy program); commits the framework to three load-bearing positions — *small dev sets are sufficient*, *intermediate-step labels are almost never needed* (DSPy's structural answer to the intermediate-supervision problem in chain-of-thought training), *the metric is itself iterative*; names the two-regime metric story — scalar `accuracy` for simple tasks vs *"smaller DSPy program that checks multiple properties of the output"* for long-form tasks (DSPy's structural operationalization of [[llmasjudge|LLM-as-judge]]); records the **recursive-self-improvement** claim — when the metric is a DSPy program, optimizing the metric itself becomes easy because the metric's output is bounded and scalar; sits between [[DSPyProgrammingModel]] (Programming stage) and [[DSPyOptimizers]] (Optimization stage); specializes the general [[ModelEvaluation]] concept; operates in the [[OfflineEvaluation]] regime; forward references [[DSPyData]] (page 10) and [[DSPyMetrics]] (page 11) — both owned by sibling ingests). Bumped to 1121 with [[dspy-data]] (+2: [[DSPyExample]] — DSPy's **data-side primitive** for the [[dspy-evaluation-overview|Evaluation-stage]] dev set; a typed Python dict-with-utilities with arbitrary field names, dot-notation field access, `with_inputs("field", ...)` input-tagging (non-mutating, returns new `Example` whose `input_keys` set tags the named fields), and `inputs()` / `labels()` non-destructive partition accessors; [[DSPyPrediction|`dspy.Prediction`]] is a **subclass** of `Example`, which makes the [[DSPyMetrics|metric]]'s `(example, prediction) -> score` contract type-symmetric — both arguments share the same dot-access / partition surface — *"Your DSPy modules will return values of the type `Prediction`, which is a special sub-class of `Example`."* — and [[DSPyData]] — DSPy's **dataset-layer discipline** for the train / dev / test three-set convention DSPy inherits from supervised ML (*"DSPy is a machine learning framework, so working in it involves training sets, development sets, and test sets"*); records the three load-bearing commitments — *datasets are plain Python lists* of [[DSPyExample|`dspy.Example`]] (no `Dataset` class, no `train_test_split(...)` helper, no built-in loaders — splits are Python slicing; the small-API discipline consistent with [[dspy-modules|*"DSPy is just Python code"*]]), *input/label tagging is attached not structural* (the same `Example` can be re-tagged for different program calls), *inputs-only sufficiency* (*"You can use DSPy effectively without any intermediate or final labels, but you will need at least a few example inputs"* — the data-side mirror of [[dspy-evaluation-overview|the Evaluation Overview's]] *intermediate-step labels are almost never needed* commitment); the canonical conversion idiom from external data is `[dspy.Example(**row).with_inputs("field") for row in source]`; **resolves both long-standing forward references** [[DSPyData]] + [[DSPyExample]] carried by [[DSPyEvaluation]] / [[dspy-evaluation-overview]] since the Evaluation stage opened on page 9). Bumped to 1124 with [[dspy-metrics]] (+2: [[DSPyMetrics]] — DSPy's **canonical metric contract** `(example, pred, trace=None) -> score`; *"A DSPy metric is just a function in Python that takes `example` (e.g., from your training or dev set) and the output `pred` from your DSPy program, and outputs a `float` (or `int` or `bool`) score"*; **type-symmetric on the data side** (because [[DSPyPrediction|`Prediction`]] is a subclass of [[DSPyExample|`Example`]]) and **regime-asymmetric on the calling side** (the optional third argument `trace` switches behavior between evaluation/optimization (`trace is None`, continuous `float` return) and bootstrapping (`trace is not None`, strict `bool` return for demo selection) — the dual-purpose mechanism that makes a single function serve both DSPy compilation phases); two regimes — *simple metrics* (one-line scalar comparisons, built-ins `dspy.evaluate.metrics.answer_exact_match` / `answer_passage_match`) for short-form tasks and *AI-feedback metrics* (a `class Assess(dspy.Signature)` rubric template + N `dspy.Predict(Assess)` invocations) for long-form tasks — DSPy's structural operationalization of [[llmasjudge|LLM-as-judge]]; the canonical hybrid pattern mixes AI judgments with deterministic hard gates (`len(tweet) <= 280` alongside two `Predict(Assess)` outputs) — first wiki demonstration that DSPy metrics are not all-or-nothing AI-feedback; the `trace`-aware `validate_hops` bootstrap recipe inspects intermediate predictor outputs; recursive-metric-optimization (Step 4 of the four-step loop) is operationalized — the AI-feedback metric is itself a DSPy program and thus optimizable by an [[DSPyOptimizers|Optimizer]]; **resolves the long-standing forward reference** carried by every prior DSPy ingest since the corpus opened — and [[DSPyEvaluate]] — DSPy's **dev-set-evaluation utility** `from dspy.evaluate import Evaluate`; a thread-parallel wrapper around the raw `for x in devset: pred = program(**x.inputs()); score = metric(x, pred)` loop with four kwargs (`devset` / `num_threads` / `display_progress` / `display_table`); the reusable two-phase pattern (construct once with the dev set; call multiple times with `(program, metric)` pairs); the harness for Step 3 of the four-step Evaluation loop). Bumped to 1128 with [[dis-14-1-multicore]] (+3: [[SharedMemoryParallelism]], [[ConcurrencyVsParallelism]], [[Speedup]] — opens DIS Ch 14, the 127th ingested DIS chapter). Bumped to 1125 with [[dspy-optimization-overview]] (+1: [[DSPyOptimization]] — DSPy's **third-stage workflow concept** that turns a runnable, measurable program into an optimized one with a higher metric than the baseline; canonical anchor for the **three-input / one-output contract** *program + metric + training-set → optimized program*; the **30/300 training-set-size regime** (*"You can often get substantial value out of 30 examples, but aim for at least 300 examples"* — explicitly larger than [[DSPyEvaluation|the Evaluation stage's]] 20–200 dev set); the **inverted 20/80 train/validation split** for most prompt optimizers (DSPy-specific defense against the prompt-optimization-overfits-small-training-sets failure mode); the **[[GEPA]] carve-out** (only named optimizer on the page, follows standard ML practice instead); the **four iteration axes** (data / program structure / metric / optimizer-choice) — three of four point back into prior stages, making Optimization an *open-under-revision* stage rather than a black-box terminus; sits as the **fourth artifact** of [[DSPyProgrammingModel|the Programming Model]] (Signature / Adapter / Module / Optimizer) at the workflow level; the split between [[DSPyOptimization]] (workflow / this page) and [[DSPyOptimizers]] (catalog / page 13, forward reference) mirrors the [[DSPyEvaluation]] / [[DSPyMetrics]] precedent — one page anchors the workflow, the sibling anchors the per-algorithm machinery; carries [[DSPyOptimizers]] / [[BootstrapFewShot]] / [[BootstrapFewShotWithRandomSearch]] / [[MIPROv2]] / [[BootstrapFinetune]] / [[GEPA]] / [[DSPyAssertions]] as forward references the page-13 sibling ingest will resolve). -->

- [A/B Testing](concepts/ABTesting.md) — controlled live experiment comparing two variants on a target metric.

<!-- Added 2026-05-23: [[dmls-ch01-overview|Designing ML Systems]] (Chip Huyen, O'Reilly 2022) — initial high-impact concept additions; full per-chapter list lives on the chapter source pages. Many more (~190 additional concept seeds) remain as unresolved `[[wikilinks]]` for follow-up consolidation. -->
- [ML Platform](concepts/MLPlatform.md) — Shared infrastructure layer hosting model deployment + store + feature store + monitoring; DMLS Ch 10's four-layer infrastructure model. ([[dmls-ch10-infrastructure-mlops]]).
- [Model Store](concepts/ModelStore.md) — Versioned artifact repository (8 artifacts: definition, params, featurize fn, predict fn, deps, data, generation code, experiment artifacts); least-mature ML-platform component. ([[dmls-ch09-continual-learning]] / [[dmls-ch10-infrastructure-mlops]]).
- [Stateful Training](concepts/StatefulTraining.md) — Retraining that continues from the last checkpoint on fresh data; Grubhub 45× compute reduction case study. ([[dmls-ch09-continual-learning]]).
- [Stateless Retraining](concepts/StatelessRetraining.md) — Retraining from scratch on combined historical + fresh data; the default mode and stages 1–2 of the continual-learning maturity ladder. ([[dmls-ch09-continual-learning]]).
- [Hashing Trick](concepts/HashingTrick.md) — Vowpal-Wabbit-popularized categorical encoding into a fixed-size hash space; Booking.com 50% collisions → <0.5% log-loss. ([[dmls-ch05-feature-engineering]]).
- [Feature Crossing](concepts/FeatureCrossing.md) — Combining 2+ features into a single feature to model nonlinear interactions; foundational to DeepFM-family CTR architectures. ([[dmls-ch05-feature-engineering]]).
- [Responsible AI](concepts/ResponsibleAI.md) — Practice of designing/developing/deploying AI for empowerment, fairness, privacy, and positive impact; DMLS Ch 11 six-step practitioner framework. ([[dmls-ch01-overview]] / [[dmls-ch11-human-side]]).
- [Four Myths of ML Deployment](concepts/MLDeploymentMyths.md) — Huyen Ch 7's opening framing: one model / stable performance / infrequent updates / scale doesn't matter — all wrong. ([[dmls-ch07-model-deployment]]).
- [Continuous Cold Start](concepts/ContinuousColdStart.md) — Generalization of cold-start to cover existing users with stale/sparse behavior; Coveo 70%-infrequent-shoppers stat. ([[dmls-ch09-continual-learning]]).
- [Model Card](concepts/ModelCard.md) — Mitchell et al. 2018 standardized disclosure document accompanying a trained model; required by HuggingFace Model Hub. ([[dmls-ch11-human-side]]).
- [Consistency-Accuracy Tradeoff](concepts/ConsistencyAccuracyTradeoff.md) — Predictable consistent ML output can produce better UX than accuracy-maximizing output; Booking.com filter-recommendation case. ([[dmls-ch11-human-side]]).
- [Smooth Failing](concepts/SmoothFailing.md) — Route slow main-model requests to a fast backup model past a latency budget. ([[dmls-ch11-human-side]]).
- [Subject Matter Expert](concepts/SubjectMatterExpert.md) — Domain experts as developers across the entire ML lifecycle, not just labelers. ([[dmls-ch11-human-side]]).
- [End-to-End Data Scientist](concepts/EndToEndDataScientist.md) — Organizational pattern where one DS owns the full lifecycle; depends on strong internal tooling. ([[dmls-ch11-human-side]]).
- [Champion-Challenger Pattern](concepts/ChampionChallengerPattern.md) — Continual-learning workflow where a candidate replica is evaluated alongside the production model before promotion. ([[dmls-ch09-continual-learning]]).

<!-- Added with [[ai-engineering-chip-huyen]] (AI Engineering — Chip Huyen, O'Reilly 2024; +545 concept pages across the 10-chapter ingest). Highest-impact anchors below; full per-chapter lists live on the chapter source pages. -->
- [AI Engineering](concepts/AIEngineering.md) — The discipline of building applications with readily-available [[FoundationModel|foundation models]] (as opposed to building models from scratch); the book's central concept. ([[ai-engineering-ch01-intro]]).
- [AI Engineering Stack](concepts/AIEngineeringStack.md) — Three-layer stack: application development → model development → infrastructure. ([[ai-engineering-ch01-intro]]).
- [Foundation Model](concepts/FoundationModel.md) — Pretrained model adaptable to many downstream tasks via prompting / RAG / finetuning. ([[ai-engineering-ch01-intro]] / [[ai-engineering-ch02-foundation-models]]).
- [Chinchilla Scaling Law](concepts/ChinchillaScalingLaw.md) — Hoffmann et al. 2022; compute-optimal scaling balances parameters ≈ 20× tokens. ([[ai-engineering-ch02-foundation-models]]).
- [Inverse Scaling](concepts/InverseScaling.md) / [Emergent Abilities](concepts/EmergentAbilities.md) / [Scaling Bottlenecks](concepts/ScalingBottlenecks.md) — Three modifications to the simple "more compute = better" scaling narrative. ([[ai-engineering-ch02-foundation-models]]).
- [Test-Time Compute](concepts/TestTimeCompute.md) — Spending more compute at inference to improve quality; encompasses [[selfconsistency]] / [[Verifier|verifier-based]] sampling / [[beamsearch|beam search]]. ([[ai-engineering-ch02-foundation-models]]).
- [Comparative Evaluation](concepts/ComparativeEvaluation.md) — Pairwise A-vs-B evaluation backed by [[BradleyTerry]] / [[EloRating]] / [[TrueSkill]] aggregation. ([[ai-engineering-ch03-evaluation-methodology]]).
- [Evaluation Pipeline](concepts/EvaluationPipeline.md) — End-to-end evaluation stack for an AI system: criteria → eval set → metric → annotation → scoring → slicing. ([[ai-engineering-ch04-evaluate-ai-systems]]).
- [Defensive Prompt Engineering](concepts/DefensivePromptEngineering.md) — Three-level defense stack (model / prompt / system) against [[PromptAttack|prompt attacks]]. ([[ai-engineering-ch05-prompt-engineering]]).
- [Instruction Hierarchy](concepts/InstructionHierarchy.md) — Four-level priority order (`System > User > Model output > Tool output`) that production LLMs are trained to respect. ([[ai-engineering-ch05-prompt-engineering]]).
- [Approximate Nearest Neighbor](concepts/ApproximateNearestNeighbor.md) — Sublinear-time retrieval over high-dimensional embeddings; canonical algorithms [[HNSW]] / [[LSH]] / [[ProductQuantization]] / [[IVF]]. ([[ai-engineering-ch06-rag-agents]]).
- [Compound Error Accumulation](concepts/CompoundErrorAccumulation.md) — Why long agent loops fail catastrophically: 0.95^10 ≈ 0.60. ([[ai-engineering-ch06-rag-agents]]).
- [PEFT](concepts/PEFT.md) — Parameter-efficient finetuning umbrella ([[lora|LoRA]] / [[QLoRA]] / adapters / prefix tuning / [[BitFit]]). ([[ai-engineering-ch07-finetuning]]).
- [Model Merging](concepts/ModelMerging.md) — Combining multiple finetunes into one model via [[TaskVector]] / [[TIES]] / [[DARE]] without retraining. ([[ai-engineering-ch07-finetuning]]).
- [Data Flywheel](concepts/DataFlywheel.md) — User-feedback → data → model-improvement loop that closes the deployment cycle. ([[ai-engineering-ch08-dataset-engineering]] / [[ai-engineering-ch10-architecture-feedback]]).
- [Model Collapse](concepts/ModelCollapse.md) — Training on AI-generated data degrades quality over generations (Shumailov et al. 2023); the dominant AI-data-lineage risk. ([[ai-engineering-ch08-dataset-engineering]]).
- [Arithmetic Intensity](concepts/ArithmeticIntensity.md) / [Roofline Model](concepts/RooflineModel.md) — Why inference is memory-bandwidth-bound: per-byte compute < accelerator FLOP-to-bandwidth ratio. ([[ai-engineering-ch09-inference-optimization]]).
- [MFU](concepts/MFU.md) / [MBU](concepts/MBU.md) / [Goodput](concepts/Goodput.md) — Replace `nvidia-smi`'s "GPU utilization" as inference-system metrics. ([[ai-engineering-ch09-inference-optimization]]).
- [Speculative Decoding](concepts/SpeculativeDecoding.md) — Draft model proposes N tokens; target model verifies in parallel; Chinchilla-70B shows >50% MFU lift / 8× speedup. ([[ai-engineering-ch09-inference-optimization]]).
- [Model Gateway](concepts/ModelGateway.md) / [Model Router](concepts/ModelRouter.md) — Centralized proxy across LLM providers; handles routing / rate limiting / caching / observability. ([[ai-engineering-ch10-architecture-feedback]]).
- [Degenerate Feedback Loop](concepts/DegenerateFeedbackLoop.md) / [Sycophancy](concepts/Sycophancy.md) — Two failure modes that make user feedback an unreliable training signal. ([[ai-engineering-ch10-architecture-feedback]]).
- Plus **525 more newly-minted concept pages** covering the full surface of the book — retrieval algorithms, attention variants, quantization techniques, evaluation harnesses, prompt-attack vocabulary, agent-failure taxonomies, observability metrics — see individual chapter source pages for full lists. Also lifts ~30 prior stub pages ([[safety]], [[factuality]], [[mmlu]], [[gpqa]], [[ifeval]], [[posttraining]], [[KVCache]], [[InferenceOptimization]], [[observability]], [[Monitoring]], etc.) to substantive treatments.

<!-- Added with [[vanroy-programming-paradigms-for-dummies]] -->
- [Programming Paradigm](concepts/ProgrammingParadigm.md) — Approach to programming based on a mathematical theory; defined by a set of [[ProgrammingConcept|concepts]] organized into a [[KernelLanguage|kernel language]]. Van Roy's taxonomy names 27 useful paradigms across the [[ObservableNondeterminism]] × [[NamedState]] design space.
- [Kernel Language](concepts/KernelLanguage.md) — Simple core language expressing a paradigm's concepts minimally; e.g., OCC for [[ConcurrentConstraintProgramming]], lambda calculus for [[FirstClassProcedures]], Kernel Oz for [[Oz]].
- [Observable Nondeterminism](concepts/ObservableNondeterminism.md) — First key paradigm-classification axis (Van Roy); the property that a user can see different results from executions starting at the same internal state. Combined with [[NamedState]] gives [[RaceCondition|race conditions]].
- [Named State](concepts/NamedState.md) — Second key paradigm-classification axis; sequence of values in time with a single name. Required for **modularity** — without it, adding a private counter to a module forces every caller to rewrite their code.
- [Dataflow Variable](concepts/DataflowVariable.md) — Single-assignment variable with `NewVar` / `Bind` / `Wait` primitives; the synchronization mechanism of [[DeclarativeConcurrency]]; basis of [[Oz]]'s confluent concurrent programming; conceptually equivalent to the logic variable in the [[ConstraintStore]].
- [Closure (Lexically Scoped)](concepts/Closure.md) — Procedure paired with its definition-context environment; Van Roy: *"the most expressive concept ever invented in programming"*. Functions / procedures / objects / classes / components / software components are all closures.
- [Creative Extension Principle](concepts/CreativeExtensionPrinciple.md) — Felleisen 1990; design principle: pervasive (nonlocal) program modifications signal a new concept waiting to be discovered. Canonical examples: concurrency, named state, exceptions.
- [Declarative Concurrency](concepts/DeclarativeConcurrency.md) — Threads + [[DataflowVariable|dataflow variables]]; confluent like functional programming but concurrent; no race conditions; Van Roy's recommended default for multi-core parallel programming.
- [Message-Passing Concurrency](concepts/MessagePassingConcurrency.md) — Concurrent agents in single threads sending each other messages; [[Erlang]] (async) / CSP (sync); Van Roy's recommended default for general-purpose concurrent programming (over [[SharedStateConcurrency]]).
- [Shared-State Concurrency](concepts/SharedStateConcurrency.md) — Mainstream paradigm of Java / C# / C++; threads share data via monitors / [[Mutex|mutexes]]. *"Monitors are the most difficult concurrency primitive to program with"* — popular but not recommended.
- [Functional Reactive Programming](concepts/FunctionalReactiveProgramming.md) — Continuous-time reactive paradigm ([[FrTime]] / [[Yampa]]); function arguments can change and changes propagate to outputs; no observable nondeterminism but accepts nondeterministic input. Beware glitches.
- [Discrete Synchronous Programming](concepts/DiscreteSynchronousProgramming.md) — Discrete-time reactive paradigm ([[Esterel]] / [[Lustre]] / [[Signal]] / [[Faust]]); defines deterministic Mealy machines; subprograms compose trivially because output events are instantaneously available as input events.
- [Data Abstraction](concepts/DataAbstraction.md) — Inside / outside / interface organization for data structures. Four kinds (Van Roy Figure 14): pure [[AbstractDataType|ADT]] / [[OPMObject|object]] / stateful ADT / declarative object, organized by state × bundling axes.
- [Substitution Principle (Liskov)](concepts/SubstitutionPrinciple.md) — Inheritance discipline: if class A inherits from B, any procedure that works with B-objects must also work with A-objects. Van Roy's recommendation: prefer **composition over inheritance**.
- [Definitive Language](concepts/DefinitiveLanguage.md) — A language design good enough that researchers move on. Four-layer architecture (functional / [[DeclarativeConcurrency|declarative concurrent]] / [[MessagePassingConcurrency|message passing]] / [[NamedState|named state]]) independently converged on by [[Erlang]] / [[E_Language|E]] / [[DistributedOz]] / [[CTM|Didactic Oz]] — *"lightning striking four times"* (Van Roy 2006).
- [Dual-Paradigm Language](concepts/DualParadigmLanguage.md) — Language supporting two paradigms (small + large); e.g., Prolog (logic + imperative), modeling languages (solver + OOP), SQL (relational + transactional).
- [Self-Sufficient System](concepts/SelfSufficientSystem.md) — Software that maintains, adapts, and corrects itself via [[FeedbackLoop|feedback loops]] interacting through [[Stigmergy|stigmergy]] + management; Van Roy's recommended architecture for large-scale fragile systems.
- [Feedback Loop](concepts/FeedbackLoop.md) — Three-agent unit of a [[SelfSufficientSystem]]: monitoring agent + correcting agent + actuating agent over a subsystem. Worked examples: TCP (2 loops), human respiratory system (4 loops).
- [Stigmergy](concepts/Stigmergy.md) — Indirect coordination between [[FeedbackLoop|feedback loops]] via a shared subsystem; biological origin (termite colonies); the looser-coupling counterpart of management.
- [CTM (Concepts, Techniques, and Models of Computer Programming)](concepts/CTM.md) — Van Roy & Haridi textbook (MIT Press 2004); the pedagogy companion to [[vanroy-programming-paradigms-for-dummies]]; basis for the [[UCL]] FSAB1402 course since 2005; uses [[Oz]] as the teaching vehicle.
- [Mozart Programming System](concepts/MozartProgrammingSystem.md) — Production implementation of [[Oz]] and [[DistributedOz]]; first released 1999; developed by the Mozart Consortium ([[DFKI]] + SICS + [[UCL]]).
- [Distributed Oz](concepts/DistributedOz.md) — Network-transparent distributed programming for [[Oz]]; started 1995 in the PERDIO project at [[DFKI]] ([[GertSmolka|Smolka]] / Schulte / [[PeterVanRoy|Van Roy]]); realized as the [[MozartProgrammingSystem|Mozart Programming System]].
- [Erlang](concepts/Erlang.md) — Concurrent programming language (Joe Armstrong, Ericsson, 1986+); functional core + async [[MessagePassingConcurrency|message passing]] + Mnesia replicated database; the AXD-301 ATM switch is >1M LOC of Erlang.

<!-- Added with [[vol1000-oz-programming-model]] -->
- [OPM (Oz Programming Model)](concepts/OPM.md) — [[GertSmolka|Smolka]]'s concurrent programming model: [[ConcurrentConstraintProgramming|CCP]] kernel + [[FirstClassProcedures]] + stateful [[Cell|cells]] + [[EncapsulatedSearch|encapsulated search]]; three-compartment store ([[ConstraintStore|constraint]] / procedure / cell); monotonic synchronization via logic entailment.
- [Oz](concepts/Oz.md) — Concurrent high-level programming language ([[DFKI]] 1991+); concomitant language of [[OPM]]; combines logic variables + first-class procedures + cells + objects + encapsulated search; the wiki's first concurrent-constraint language.
- [Concurrent Constraint Programming](concepts/ConcurrentConstraintProgramming.md) — Saraswat's framework (PhD 1989 / MIT Press 1993); tasks communicate via a shared [[ConstraintStore|constraint store]] using **tell** (add constraint) + **ask** (synchronize on entailment); kernel sublanguage [[OPM|OCC]] of [[OPM]].
- [Computation Space](concepts/ComputationSpace.md) — [[OPM]]'s central execution-context abstraction: tasks + three-compartment store; reduction is atomic; threads as reduction strategy; subordinate spaces are first-class on distribution.
- [Constraint Store](concepts/ConstraintStore.md) — Declarative compartment holding a satisfiable conjunction of basic constraints; monotonic, order-independent; the only place information about variable values lives in [[OPM]] / [[Oz]]; supports tell + entailment ask + disentailment ask; incremental tell required for parallel implementation.
- [First-Class Procedures](concepts/FirstClassProcedures.md) — Language-design feature: procedures are values with lexical scope (Scheme / SML / Haskell tradition); [[OPM]] is the first concurrent-constraint model to integrate them; procedure = name + formal argument + body; idea originates in Smolka's *Fresh* (1986).
- [Encapsulated Search](concepts/EncapsulatedSearch.md) — Mechanism for confining constraint-logic-programming search into a concurrent agent without polluting the top-level [[ComputationSpace|space]]; via **choice** + **search combinator**; gets CLP *"out of its problem solving ghetto"*; predecessor of modern finite-domain CSP solvers (Gecode, Choco).
- [Cell (Oz)](concepts/Cell.md) — Mutable name-to-variable binding in [[OPM]]'s cell store; atomic `Exchange` combines read + write; basis for [[Port]] / [[Agent]] / [[OPMObject]]; distinct from [[CellRust]] / [[RefCell]] / [[UnsafeCell]] (Rust interior mutability) and [[MemoryCell]] (hardware).
- [Port (Oz)](concepts/Port.md) — Procedure connected to an incrementally-constrained stream; canonical [[OPM]] message-queue abstraction; built from a private [[Cell|cell]] + first-class procedures; basis for [[Agent|agents]].
- [Agent (Oz)](concepts/Agent.md) — Computational abstraction processing messages received through a [[Port|port]]; maintains internal state via [[Cell|cell]]; **stationary** under distribution (messages served at creation site); namesake of but semantically distinct from the modern LLM-agent vocabulary.
- [OPMObject (Oz Object)](concepts/OPMObject.md) — Procedure `{Object Message}` wrapping a private [[Cell|cell]] + serve procedure with `Self`; concurrent-OOP model in [[OPM]]; **mobile** under distribution (messages served at application site); classes / inheritance / private attributes via [[Name|names]] + lexical scoping.
- [Propagator (Oz)](concepts/Propagator.md) — Task accommodating a nonbasic constraint ($x + y = z$, $\textit{less}(x, y, z)$) by waiting until the [[ConstraintStore|store]] contains enough information to reduce it to basic constraints; bridge from declarative store to operational search; foundation of finite-domain CSP solvers.
- [Adversarial Prompt Search](concepts/AdversarialPromptSearch.md) — [[2507.19457-gepa|GEPA]]'s inverted-reward mode; evolves universal adversarial prompts. Dropped GPT-5 Mini AIME-2025 pass@1 from 76% → 10% in 150 generations. Extended in [[2603.19247-prompt-optimization-jailbreaking]] to LLM **safety** — same machinery drives mean [[DangerScore|danger]] on four frontier LMs by 2–9× via [[MIPROv2]] / [[GEPA]] / [[SIMBA]]. Defender-side companion: [[TrustedMonitor]] in [[dspy-tutorial-gepa-trusted-monitor]].
- [AI Control](concepts/AIControl.md) — Safety paradigm of **deploying capable-but-potentially-misaligned ("untrusted") LMs safely by surrounding them with weaker, trusted oversight layers** — typically a *trusted monitor* + *trusted executor* + *trusted human*. Formalized in *"AI Control: Improving Safety Despite Intentional Subversion"* (Greenblatt et al., [[RedwoodResearch|Redwood Research]] 2023). Distinct from *alignment* — assumes the strong model may be adversarial; safety is a property of the deployment pipeline, not of the model. First DSPy receipt: [[dspy-tutorial-gepa-trusted-monitor]] training a [[TrustedMonitor]] via [[GEPA]] on [[APPSBenchmark|APPS]] + [[ControlTax]].
- [Trusted Monitor](concepts/TrustedMonitor.md) — Weaker, more-trusted LM that classifies outputs of a stronger, untrusted LM to flag suspicious behavior (backdoors, sandbagging, intentional subversion). The workhorse protocol of [[AIControl|AI Control]]. Trust asymmetry: capability ceiling traded for threat-model coverage. First wiki DSPy receipt: [[dspy-tutorial-gepa-trusted-monitor]] — [[GPT4_1|GPT-4.1 Nano]] monitor optimized by [[GEPA]] reaches 0.81 comparative-pair accuracy on [[APPSBenchmark|APPS]] (baseline 0.69; pareto-front 0.95). The `MonitorTrainerProgram` dual-call wrapper is the structural enabler: optimization-time program shape ≠ deployment-time program shape.
- [Code Backdoor](concepts/CodeBackdoor.md) — Deliberate modification to a correct program such that it **produces wrong outputs only on a rare, attacker-chosen trigger input** while passing standard tests on all other inputs. Three-part anatomy: trigger condition (magic-constant conditionals like `n % 37 == 0`, compound-rare predicates, post-hoc adjustments), correct underlying algorithm (the plausibility shield), and backdoor input. The canonical [[AIControl|AI-control]] threat model in the coding domain. Discriminator (per [[GEPA]]-evolved monitor prompt): *"Prefer 'intentional' when the code otherwise implements a correct algorithm but conditionally tweaks the answer only on rare, unrelated triggers."* False-positive guard: *"Incorrect logic or inefficiency alone does not imply malicious intent."* ([[dspy-tutorial-gepa-trusted-monitor]])
- [APPS Benchmark](concepts/APPSBenchmark.md) — Automated Programming Progress Standard; competitive-programming dataset of interview-style coding challenges (Hendrycks et al. 2021). The [[AIControl|AI-control]] surface adds a **backdoor split** — for each problem, paired (`task_description`, `honest_code`, `attack_code`, `backdoor_input`) generated by [[ControlTax]] and exposed via [[ControlArena|`control_arena`]] (~6,300+ samples). First DSPy receipt: [[dspy-tutorial-gepa-trusted-monitor]] using 200/100/160 splits.
- [Control Tax](concepts/ControlTax.md) — Backdoor-generation pipeline producing [[APPSBenchmark|APPS]] **paired (honest, attack, trigger) triples** for [[TrustedMonitor|trusted-monitor]] evaluation. White-box adversarial: the attacker LLM gets the original solution + test suite + freedom in choosing triggers. Named via the `backdoor_source="control_tax"` kwarg in [[ControlArena|`control_arena.settings.apps.apps_setting.get_dataset(...)`]]. Etymology likely echoes [[AlignmentTax]] — capability cost of running an AI-control protocol vs trusting the strong model directly. ([[dspy-tutorial-gepa-trusted-monitor]])

<!-- Added with [[2603.19247-prompt-optimization-jailbreaking]] -->
- [SIMBA](concepts/SIMBA.md) — [[DSPy]] stochastic-mini-batch self-reflective prompt optimizer in the *Automatic Instruction Optimization* family; **first wiki paper-anchored result places SIMBA at the top of [[MIPROv2]] / [[GEPA]] / SIMBA on adaptive red-teaming** across four frontier models ([[2603.19247-prompt-optimization-jailbreaking]]).
- [Danger Score](concepts/DangerScore.md) — Continuous LLM-as-judge safety metric $r \in [0, 1]$ from [[2603.19247-prompt-optimization-jailbreaking]]; substitutes for binary [[AttackSuccessRate|ASR]] as the optimizer reward signal in adaptive red-teaming; rubric scored by [[GPT51|GPT-5.1]] with five labeled ranges.
- [HarmfulQA](concepts/HarmfulQA.md) — Adversarial role-playing prompt benchmark (DeCLaRe Lab 2023); seed pool half in [[2603.19247-prompt-optimization-jailbreaking]]'s adaptive-attack experiment.
- [JailbreakBench](concepts/JailbreakBench.md) — Curated open jailbreak benchmark (Chao et al., NeurIPS Datasets & Benchmarks 2024); seed pool half in [[2603.19247-prompt-optimization-jailbreaking]].
- [Bootstrap Demonstrations](concepts/BootstrapDemonstrations.md) — Metric-filtered trace-collection step shared by every DSPy-adjacent optimizer ([[BootstrapFewShot]], [[BootstrapRandomSearch]], [[MIPROv2|MIPRO]], [[BootstrapFinetune]], [[2407.10930-better-together|BetterTogether]]). Rejection-sampling-based label propagation for the latent per-module variables; formalized in [[2406.11695-mipro]] §3.1.
- [Bootstrap Random Search](concepts/BootstrapRandomSearch.md) — The demos-only baseline optimizer in [[2406.11695-mipro|MIPRO (§4.1)]]; canonical name used in the paper for the algorithm DSPy ships as [[BootstrapFewShotWithRandomSearch]].
- [DSPy Optimizer Benchmark](concepts/DSPyOptimizerBenchmark.md) — Seven-task LM-program optimizer benchmark released by [[2406.11695-mipro]]. Covers four orthogonal axes (module count / conditional rules / task type / program structure) — used to derive MIPRO's five lessons.
- [Heart Disease](concepts/HeartDisease.md) — UCI binary clinical-feature classification dataset (Detrano et al. 1989); one of seven [[DSPyOptimizerBenchmark]] tasks. The "answer ensemble" task in the benchmark; the canonical case where instruction optimization is bottlenecked by lack of a non-trivial seed instruction.
- [HotPotQA Conditional](concepts/HotPotQAConditional.md) — Conditional-rules variant of [[hotpotqa|HotPotQA]] introduced by [[2406.11695-mipro|MIPRO]]; answer format depends on entity type (person/date/place). MIPRO lifts baseline 6 → 23.3 — **largest relative gain in the benchmark**; canonical Lesson-3 evidence.
- [Iris-Typo](concepts/IrisTypo.md) — Misspelled-prompt variant of [[Iris]] introduced by [[2406.11695-mipro|MIPRO]]; instruction optimization **corrects the seed-prompt typo** ("versicolour" → "versicolor"). Wiki reference example of automated prompt repair.
- [LM Program](concepts/LMProgram.md) — [[MIPROv2|MIPRO]]-era term for a multi-stage LM-call pipeline $\Phi$ with prompt-template variables $\mathbf{V}$. The pre-[[CompoundAISystem]] formalism in [[2406.11695-mipro]] §2.
- [Module-Level OPRO](concepts/ModuleLevelOPRO.md) — Multi-stage extension of [[OPRO]] introduced in [[2406.11695-mipro|MIPRO]] §4.2; instructions-only history-based baseline that treats program score as a per-module quality proxy.
- [OPRO](concepts/OPRO.md) — *Optimization by PROmpting* (Yang et al. 2023); foundational single-prompt LM-as-optimizer method. The history-based credit-assignment option in [[2406.11695-mipro|MIPRO]]'s Algorithm-1 taxonomy.
- [LM Assertions](concepts/LMAssertions.md) — Umbrella concept introduced by [[2312.13382-dspy-assertions|Singhvi, Shetty, Tan et al. (2024)]]; first-class programming construct for expressing arbitrary computational constraints on [[DSPy]] module outputs with retry-with-feedback semantics. Two variants — hard [[DSPyAssert|`Assert`]] (halts on persistent failure) and soft [[DSPySuggest|`Suggest`]] (warns + continues). Underwrites three optimizations: [[AssertionDrivenBacktracking|backtracking]], [[AssertionDrivenExampleBootstrapping|example bootstrapping]], [[CounterexampleBootstrapping|counterexample bootstrapping]]. Resolves the long-standing [[DSPyAssertions]] forward reference.
