- [dspy.Assert](concepts/DSPyAssert.md) — The **hard** variant of [[LMAssertions|LM Assertions]] from [[2312.13382-dspy-assertions]]. After $R$ failed retries with feedback-injected re-prompts, raises `AssertionError` and halts the pipeline. Sibling of [[DSPySuggest|`dspy.Suggest`]]. **Deprecated in [[DSPy]] 2.6** → [[DSPyBestOfN|`dspy.BestOfN`]] / [[DSPyRefine|`dspy.Refine`]] per [[dspy-output-refinement-tutorial]].
- [dspy.Suggest](concepts/DSPySuggest.md) — The **soft** variant of [[LMAssertions|LM Assertions]] from [[2312.13382-dspy-assertions]]. After $R$ failed retries, logs `SuggestionError` and continues to the next module. Paper diagnoses the **conflicting-suggestions** failure mode when multiple `Suggest`s sit sequentially on the same output ([[TweetGen]] case study). Sibling of [[DSPyAssert|`dspy.Assert`]]. **Deprecated in [[DSPy]] 2.6** → [[DSPyBestOfN|`dspy.BestOfN`]] / [[DSPyRefine|`dspy.Refine`]] per [[dspy-output-refinement-tutorial]].
- [dspy.BestOfN](concepts/DSPyBestOfN.md) — DSPy 2.6 output-refinement module that wraps any [[DSPyModules|Module]] in a **reward-driven retry loop**: runs the wrapped module up to **N times with distinct rollout IDs**, returns the first prediction whose `reward_fn(args, pred) -> float` clears `threshold` or the best-scoring rollout overall. `fail_count` controls error-tolerance. The DSPy-module instantiation of generic [[bestofn|Best-of-N]] with programmable scoring and threshold-based early-exit. Sibling of [[DSPyRefine|`dspy.Refine`]]. Replaces [[DSPyAssert]] (mapped as `fail_count=1`).
- [dspy.Refine](concepts/DSPyRefine.md) — DSPy 2.6 output-refinement module — same API as [[DSPyBestOfN|`dspy.BestOfN`]] plus an **automatic feedback loop**: between rollouts, the framework synthesizes detailed performance feedback from the prior `reward_fn` score and injects it as a hint for the next rollout. Inherits the retry-with-feedback semantics from [[AssertionDrivenBacktracking|assertion-driven backtracking]] but with framework-synthesized feedback in place of user-authored `msg` strings. Canonical use: LM-judge-driven self-correction (the tutorial's `FactualityJudge` example). Replaces [[DSPySuggest]].
- [Assertion-Driven Backtracking](concepts/AssertionDrivenBacktracking.md) — Inference-time control-flow mechanism behind [[LMAssertions]]: on constraint failure, the failing DSPy module is re-invoked with its prior erring output + the user error message injected as `Past Query` / `Instruction` prompt fields. Implemented via the `Retry` meta-module that tracks failed predictions. [[2312.13382-dspy-assertions]].
- [Assertion-Driven Example Bootstrapping](concepts/AssertionDrivenExampleBootstrapping.md) — Compile-time optimization wrapping [[AssertionDrivenBacktracking|backtracking]] around the **teacher** in [[BootstrapFewShotWithRandomSearch]]: bootstrapped few-shot demos are guaranteed to satisfy every assertion at every intermediate module, not only the final-answer metric. Lifts [[TweetGen]] Engaging from 2.0% to 73.0%. [[2312.13382-dspy-assertions]].
- [Counterexample Bootstrapping](concepts/CounterexampleBootstrapping.md) — Compile-time optimization that captures `(failing output, error, corrected output)` triples produced during [[AssertionDrivenBacktracking|backtracking]] and uses them as negative few-shot demonstrations. Teaches the student model to avoid the failure mode on first try — *"the program still has the ability to generate more responses that adhere to programmer-defined assertions"* without runtime backtracking overhead. [[2312.13382-dspy-assertions]].
- [MultiHopQA](concepts/MultiHopQA.md) — [[hotpotqa|HotPotQA]]-derived 2-hop CoT + retrieval + answer task from [[2312.13382-dspy-assertions]]. Two soft suggestions (query length < 100 / query distinct from prior hops) improve retrieval recall **6.5–7.9%** and answer correctness **3.4–14.4%**.
- [LongFormQA](concepts/LongFormQA.md) — [[hotpotqa|HotPotQA]]-derived 2-hop + cited-paragraph task from [[2312.13382-dspy-assertions]]. Two suggestions: citation density (Python check) + per-line faithfulness (LM-judged via a sub-DSPy program — first wiki demonstration that [[DSPySuggest|`Suggest`]]'s `constraint` argument accepts arbitrary expressions including LM calls). Citation Faithfulness **77.3% → 92.7%** with `C+Infer w/ Assert`.
- [QuizGen](concepts/QuizGen.md) — [[hotpotqa|HotPotQA]]-derived JSON-quiz-generation task from [[2312.13382-dspy-assertions]]. Paper's headline result: valid-JSON output **37.6% → 100%**; composite Validity **30.5% → 87.2%**. The cleanest demonstration of assertion-driven backtracking enforcing a hard structural constraint.
- [TweetGen](concepts/TweetGen.md) — [[hotpotqa|HotPotQA]]-derived tweet-generation task from [[2312.13382-dspy-assertions]]. Five suggestions (no hashtags / ≤280 chars / correct answer / engaging / faithful) — three deterministic checks + two LM-judged. Showcases the **conflicting-suggestions** failure mode: stacking all five in sequential self-refinement can hurt the *Engaging* metric. No-"#" **21.3% → 96.2%**; Engaging **29.3% → 85.0%**.
- [Optuna](concepts/Optuna.md) — Open-source HPO framework (Akiba et al. 2019). The [[TreeStructuredParzenEstimator|TPE]] backbone that powers [[MIPROv2|MIPRO]]'s discrete search.
- [ScoNe](concepts/ScoNe.md) — Scoped-negation NLI benchmark (She, Potts, Bowman & Geiger, ACL 2023); one of seven [[DSPyOptimizerBenchmark]] tasks. Canonical example of grounding hurting — motivates 0-Shot MIPRO++.
- [Tree-Structured Parzen Estimator](concepts/TreeStructuredParzenEstimator.md) — TPE; Bergstra et al. 2011's Bayesian surrogate. Handles categorical / hierarchical search spaces; used by [[MIPROv2|MIPRO]] via [[Optuna]] for joint multi-module credit assignment.
- [AIME 2025](concepts/AIME2025.md) — Competition math benchmark (Balunović et al., MathArena 2025). Core benchmark of [[2507.19457-gepa|GEPA]] and adversarial-search target.
- [Compound AI System](concepts/CompoundAISystem.md) — The formalism $\Phi = (M, C, \mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y})$ for modular language-model systems; learnable parameters partition into $\Pi_\Phi$ (prompts) + $\Theta_\Phi$ (weights). [[GEPA]] optimizes the first; [[grpo|GRPO]] optimizes the second.
- [Evaluation Trace](concepts/EvaluationTrace.md) — The natural-language text the *environment* produces while computing a reward (compiler errors, judge rationales, profiler output). Distinct from execution trace; surfaced by [[FeedbackFunction|$\mu_f$]]. ([[2507.19457-gepa]])
- [Feedback Function](concepts/FeedbackFunction.md) — [[2507.19457-gepa|GEPA]]'s $\mu_f$ extending scalar reward $\mu$ to return `(score, feedback_text)`. The load-bearing non-metric supervision channel.
- [Genetic-Pareto](concepts/GeneticPareto.md) — Etymology of GEPA's name: genetic-algorithm evolution + per-instance Pareto-frontier selection.
- [HoVer](concepts/HoVer.md) — Hop-wise verification benchmark (Jiang et al. 2020); multi-hop claim verification. Core benchmark of [[2507.19457-gepa|GEPA]].
- [AlfWorld](concepts/AlfWorld.md) — Text-only re-implementation of the ALFRED household-task suite ([Shridhar et al. 2021](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.03768)) inside a [[TextWorld]] interactive-fiction environment; canonical default benchmark for long-horizon [[react|ReAct]]-style agents ([[react|Yao et al. 2022]]). Six task types (pick & place, examine in light, clean / heat / cool & place, pick two & place); 50-step canonical iteration cap; binary `won` reward. `dspy.datasets.alfworld.AlfWorld()` ships a hybrid dataset + simulator handle. Wiki's only receipt: [[dspy-tutorial-games]] — GPT-4o-mini **15.0% → 71.5%** via [[MIPROv2|`MIPROv2(auto="light")`]] + [[BootstrapFinetune]].
- [IFBench](concepts/IFBench.md) — Instruction-following benchmark (Pyatkin et al. 2025). Core benchmark of [[2507.19457-gepa|GEPA]].
- [Iris](concepts/Iris.md) — Classic Fisher 1936 flower-classification benchmark (UCI). Extrapolation task in [[2407.10930-better-together|BetterTogether]] — largest *relative* gains (3.5–88%); on llama-2-7b vanilla scores 0.0% so only Π-first strategies work (Π → Θ → Π reaches 65.3%).
- [Inference-Time Search](concepts/InferenceTimeSearch.md) — Treat target tasks as $D_{train}$ to "overfit" them; the artifact is a set of solutions, not a generalizable prompt. [[2507.19457-gepa|GEPA]]'s mode for NPUEval / KernelBench code generation.
- [KernelBench](concepts/KernelBench.md) — CUDA kernel generation benchmark on NVIDIA V100 (Ouyang et al. 2025); $fast_p$ speed metric. Inference-time-search benchmark in [[2507.19457-gepa|GEPA]].
- [LiveBench-Math](concepts/LiveBenchMath.md) — Contamination-free math benchmark (White et al. 2025). Core benchmark of [[2507.19457-gepa|GEPA]].
- [NPUEval](concepts/NPUEval.md) — AMD XDNA2 NPU kernel-generation benchmark (Kalade & Schelle 2025); vector-utilization metric. Inference-time-search benchmark in [[2507.19457-gepa|GEPA]].
- [Pareto-based Candidate Selection](concepts/ParetoBasedCandidateSelection.md) — [[2507.19457-gepa|GEPA]]'s exploration mechanism; per-instance Pareto frontier + frequency-weighted sampling. Ablation: roughly half of GEPA's gain.
- [Facility Support Analyzer](concepts/FacilitySupportAnalyzer.md) — Meta-released enterprise classification dataset (200 ProCare facility-support emails) with three gold labels per email (urgency 3-way, sentiment 3-way, categories 10-way multi-label). Canonical test bed for multi-module [[GEPA]] with [[FeedbackFunction|`pred_name`-routed feedback]] in [[dspy-tutorial-gepa-facility-support-analyzer]] (75.4% → 87.0% with GPT-4.1 nano student + GPT-5 reflector at `auto="light"`).
- [PUPA](concepts/PUPA.md) — Privacy-Utility Pareto benchmark (Li et al. 2025a); privacy-aware LLM delegation. Core benchmark of [[2507.19457-gepa|GEPA]]; training surface of [[PAPILLON]] via [[ArborGRPO]] in [[dspy-tutorial-rl-papillon]].
- [PAPILLON](concepts/PAPILLON.md) — Privacy-preserving LLM delegation program (Li et al. 2025a); two-module DSPy program — `CraftRedactedRequest` ([[chainofthought|ChainOfThought]]) → external untrusted LLM → `RespondToQuery` ([[DSPyPredict|Predict]]). Evaluated on [[PUPA]]. The wiki's canonical worked-example of multi-module GRPO training.
- [ArborGRPO](concepts/ArborGRPO.md) — Experimental [[DSPyOptimizers|DSPy optimizer]] (`dspy.GRPO`) that extends [[grpo|GRPO]] / [[DAPO]] to multi-module [[CompoundAISystem|compound AI programs]] over the [[Arbor|`arbor-ai`]] framework. One scalar reward propagates to all modules sharing a [[lora|LoRA]]-tuned local LM. Authors disclaim it as *"typically worse on cost/quality basis than"* prompt optimization.
- [DAPO](concepts/DAPO.md) — *Decoupled clip and dynamic sampling Policy Optimization*; [[grpo|GRPO]] variant used as the default `loss_type="dapo"` in [[ArborGRPO]] / [[dspy-tutorial-rl-papillon]] / [[dspy-rl-multihop-tutorial]].
- [ResearchHop](concepts/ResearchHop.md) — Fixed-depth 2-hop [[DSPyModules|`dspy.Module`]] introduced by [[dspy-rl-multihop-tutorial]] — two [[chainofthought|`dspy.ChainOfThought`]] sub-modules (`generate_query`, `append_notes`) in a hop-loop `forward(...)` over a [[BM25|BM25]] retriever; the canonical [[ArborGRPO]] / [[grpo|GRPO]] student program for multi-hop retrieval on [[HoVer]]. First-hop bootstraps from the claim; last-hop early-exits before `append_notes`. Deterministic title-recall reward.
- [Hop](concepts/Hop.md) — Fixed-depth **4-hop / 10-docs-per-hop** [[DSPyModules|`dspy.Module`]] from [[dspy-multihop-search-tutorial]] — the **structural parent of [[ResearchHop]]**. Two [[chainofthought|`dspy.ChainOfThought`]] sub-modules (`generate_query`, `append_notes`) with **typed `list[str]` output Signatures** and **output-level `list(set(titles))` dedup**. Every hop calls both sub-modules (no first-hop bootstrap, no last-hop early-exit) — **8 LM calls per claim**. Canonical [[MIPROv2]] prompt-optimization student program for multi-hop retrieval on [[HoVer]] (31.3 → 59.1 top5_recall via ~$5 of [[GPT4o|GPT-4o]] on a [[Llama|Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct]] student).
- [Hand-Rolled ReAct](concepts/HandRolledReAct.md) — Manual `dspy.ChainOfThought` + trajectory-loop alternative to [[react|`dspy.ReAct`]]; the minimum-viable agent harness in DSPy. One Signature (`question, trajectory, functions -> next_selected_fn, args: dict[str, Any]`), one `max_steps` for-loop, one synthetic `finish(answer)` terminal tool. Appropriate when tool sets vary per example, when termination needs custom logic, when tool metadata schema needs author control, or when untrusted tool code requires sandbox-aware invocation. Canonical receipt: [[dspy-tool-use-tutorial]] on [[ToolHop]] with [[SIMBA]] (35.0% → 60.7%). Composes with any DSPy optimizer because the agent is still a regular `dspy.Module`.
- [ToolHop](concepts/ToolHop.md) — Multi-hop tool-use benchmark released by [[ByteDanceResearch]] (`bytedance-research/ToolHop` on [[HuggingFace]]). Each datapoint ships a **per-question Python tool source-code bundle** (an `exec()`-able list of function definitions, each ending in a `# Example usage` suffix that must be stripped) + a question + a gold short-form answer requiring **multi-hop tool composition**. Hops are tool calls, not text retrievals — distinguishing ToolHop from [[hotpotqa|HotPotQA]] / [[HoVer]] / [[MultiHopQA]] / [[MultiHopRAG]]. First wiki DSPy receipt: [[dspy-tool-use-tutorial]] using 100/300/595 train/dev/test splits with a [[HandRolledReAct|hand-rolled ReAct]] agent + [[SIMBA]] (35.0% → 60.7% dev). Security-relevant: the `exec()`-based tool construction pattern runs untrusted code in-process; [[func_timeout|`func_timeout`]] bounds runtime but not side effects.
- [LLMJudge](concepts/LLMJudge.md) — DSPy module pattern composing multiple [[chainofthought|`dspy.ChainOfThought`]] judges into a scalar metric / RL reward. Canonical wiki receipt: [[PAPILLON]]'s dual-axis quality + privacy-leakage judge in [[dspy-tutorial-rl-papillon]]. Position-bias control via paired A/B swap.
- [dspy.Image](concepts/DSPyImage.md) — [[DSPy]]'s first-class **image primitive** — type used inside [[DSPySignatures|Signatures]] to declare image-bearing `InputField`s. Two construction paths: `dspy.Image.from_url(url)` for hosted HTTPS URLs (the path exercised by [[dspy-image-generation-prompting-tutorial]]) and `dspy.Image.from_file(...)` / base64 paths inherited from the broader primitive family. **URL-passthrough transport** through the [[DSPyAdapters|Adapter]] — `<image_url: https://...>` wire shape carried verbatim into the chat-completion request, **opposite discipline** from [[DSPyAudio|`dspy.Audio`]]'s base64-in-`data` storage. Image-in supported end-to-end via vision-capable LMs ([[GPT4oMini|`gpt-4o-mini`]] in the first receipt); image-out is **not** first-class — wrap an external image-generator HTTP endpoint (e.g. [[FAL]] / [[FluxPro|Flux Pro]]) outside the DSPy `LM` abstraction and wrap returned URLs via `dspy.Image.from_url(...)` for *input* on the next iteration. Recognized **inline in string-spec Signatures** (`"... current_image: dspy.Image ..."`). First wiki receipt: [[dspy-image-generation-prompting-tutorial]]. Sibling to [[DSPyAudio]] in the multimodal-primitive taxonomy.
- [Iterative Image Prompt Refinement](concepts/IterativeImagePromptRefinement.md) — Critic-then-revise loop for text-to-image generation: a vision-capable LM scores a generated image against the user's *desired* prompt, returns natural-language feedback plus a revised prompt, and a host Python loop re-generates with the revision until the critic returns a match (or a max-iteration budget is hit). Mechanized in [[dspy-image-generation-prompting-tutorial]] as a single [[DSPyPredict|`dspy.Predict`]] (`desired_prompt × current_image × current_prompt → feedback × match: bool × revised_prompt`) driven by a plain Python `for` with early break. **Not** wrapped as a [[DSPyModules|`dspy.Module`]] in the first receipt — therefore **not optimizable as-is**; the natural lift target is [[GEPA]] (reflective-prompt-evolution Optimizer) which automates exactly this loop. The most natural candidate in the DSPy tutorial corpus for a [[GEPA]] receipt on a multimodal task.
- [dspy.Audio](concepts/DSPyAudio.md) — [[DSPy]]'s first-class audio primitive — type used inside [[DSPySignatures|Signatures]] to declare audio-bearing `InputField` / `OutputField`s. Two construction paths: `dspy.Audio.from_array(array, sampling_rate)` for [[HuggingFace]] dataset decoding, and `dspy.Audio(data=<base64-encoded WAV bytes>)` for HTTP round-trips. Audio-in supported end-to-end via audio-capable LMs ([[GPT4oMiniAudio]]); audio-out is not first-class — wrap the TTS endpoint inside `dspy.Module.forward()` and return `dspy.Prediction(audio=dspy.Audio(...))`. Optimizer constraint: [[MIPROv2]]'s [[DataAwareProposer|`data_aware_proposer`]] must be `False` when any InputField is a non-textual primitive. First wiki receipt: [[dspy-audio-tutorial]].
- [Spoken-SQuAD](concepts/SpokenSQuAD.md) — Audio-input variant of [[SQuAD]] where the passage is delivered as a speech recording rather than text. HuggingFace hosting at `AudioLLMs/spoken_squad_test` with three fields (`context` as `{"array": ndarray, "sampling_rate": int}`, `instruction`, `answer`). End-to-end **speech understanding + reading comprehension** in a single model, distinguishing audio-native LLMs from cascaded ASR-then-LLM pipelines. First wiki receipt: [[dspy-audio-tutorial]] with [[GPT4oMiniAudio|`gpt-4o-mini-audio-preview-2024-12-17`]] + [[chainofthought]] + [[ExactMatch|`answer_exact_match`]].
- [CREMA-D](concepts/CREMAD.md) — **Crowd-sourced Emotional Multimodal Actors Dataset** — audio clips of actors speaking the same line with one of six target emotions (`neutral`, `happy`, `sad`, `anger`, `fear`, `disgust`). Fixed-line × variable-emotion design **holds content constant** across the emotion axis. First wiki receipt: [[dspy-audio-tutorial]] uses it **inverted** — not as a classification benchmark but as `(raw_line, emotion_label, reference_audio)` triplets for [[EmotionGuidedTTS|emotion-guided TTS]] training with a [[Wav2Vec2]] cosine-similarity metric.
- [gpt-4o-mini](concepts/GPT4oMini.md) — [[openai|OpenAI]]'s small, vision-capable multimodal LLM — cost-efficient sibling of `gpt-4o`. Snapshot tag `gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18` used by [[dspy-tutorial-games]]; rolling alias used as the vision critic in [[dspy-image-generation-prompting-tutorial]] (`temperature=0.5`, [[DSPyImage|`dspy.Image`]] `InputField`). Also used as the prompt-proposer LM in several MIPROv2 tutorials, and as the student in the [[BootstrapFinetune]] / GPT-4o-teacher pipeline of [[dspy-tutorial-games]] (fine-tuned 4o-mini beats GPT-4o zero-shot 71.5% vs 57.5% on [[AlfWorld]] at ~2.6× wall-clock speed). Member of [[GPT|GPT family]]; modality-suffixed siblings are [[GPT4oMiniAudio]] and [[GPT4oMiniTTS]].
- [gpt-4o-mini-audio](concepts/GPT4oMiniAudio.md) — [[openai|OpenAI]]'s audio-input variant of GPT-4o-mini — chat-completion model that accepts audio in the `messages` array (text + audio in, text out only). Wiki's first receipt pins `gpt-4o-mini-audio-preview-2024-12-17`. Compatible out of the box with [[DSPyAudio|`dspy.Audio`]] InputFields via [[DSPyLM]] / [[LiteLLM]]. Audio tokens dominate cost — drives the conservative optimizer-budget discipline in [[dspy-audio-tutorial]].
- [gpt-4o-mini-tts](concepts/GPT4oMiniTTS.md) — [[openai|OpenAI]]'s instruction-controllable text-to-speech model — distinguishing feature vs prior OpenAI TTS endpoints is an explicit `instructions=` parameter for natural-language tone / pitch / emotion / speaker-characteristic control. **11 named voices**; tutorial uses `"coral"`. Lives outside DSPy's [[DSPyLM|`dspy.LM`]] abstraction (non-chat endpoint) — must be hand-wrapped inside `dspy.Module.forward()`. First wiki receipt: [[dspy-audio-tutorial]] where [[MIPROv2]] optimizes the `instructions=` string against [[CREMAD]] reference recordings (~0.57 → ~0.67 [[Wav2Vec2]] cosine similarity).
- [Wav2Vec 2.0](concepts/Wav2Vec2.md) — [[meta|Meta]] FAIR's self-supervised speech representation model (Baevski et al. NeurIPS 2020); [[ContrastiveLearning|contrastive]] objective over masked quantized latents on unlabeled speech. **Wiki's first receipt: [[dspy-audio-tutorial]] uses it as a frozen audio encoder for a similarity metric, not for ASR** — `torchaudio.pipelines.WAV2VEC2_BASE.get_model().eval()` + mean-pooled embedding + [[CosineSimilarity|cosine similarity]] vs reference recording. Tutorial honest about the choice: Wav2Vec2 is a phonetic-content encoder, not an emotion encoder; a paralinguistic-emotion encoder would likely give stronger metric signal.
- [Emotion-Guided TTS](concepts/EmotionGuidedTTS.md) — [[DSPy]] pattern for treating a TTS endpoint's `instructions=` parameter as a **prompt to be optimized by a prompt-optimizer**, even though the endpoint is not a chat-completion LM. Minted in [[dspy-audio-tutorial]] §3. Three load-bearing structural choices: (1) the TTS call sits *outside* the DSPy LM abstraction in a manual `forward()`; (2) the optimized artifact is the *instruction string*, consumed by a non-chat HTTP endpoint; (3) the module returns audio inside a [[DSPyPrediction|`dspy.Prediction`]] with an `audio=` field of type [[DSPyAudio|`dspy.Audio`]]. Headline: [[MIPROv2|`MIPROv2(auto="light")`]] on [[CREMAD]] lifts [[Wav2Vec2]] cosine ~0.57 → ~0.67. Generalizes to any non-chat generative endpoint parameterized by a natural-language string (image-gen prompts, agent action instructions, etc.).
- [Reflective Prompt Mutation](concepts/ReflectivePromptMutation.md) — [[2507.19457-gepa|GEPA]]'s mutation operator: an LLM reads `(prompt, trace, score, feedback_text)` and proposes a revised prompt for one module.
- [System Aware Merge](concepts/SystemAwareMerge.md) — [[2507.19457-gepa|GEPA]]'s optional module-level crossover operator (the **GEPA+Merge** variant).
- [XDNA2](concepts/XDNA2.md) — AMD's second-generation NPU architecture; target of [[NPUEval]].
- [ADC (Analog-to-Digital Converter)](concepts/ADC.md) — MCU peripheral that samples a continuously-variable input voltage to an integer. [[ATmega328P]] has a 10-bit successive-approximation ADC, 6 channels, ~15 kSPS, with `ADCSRA` / `ADMUX` / `ADCH:ADCL` registers ([[embedded-controllers-fiore]] ch. 25–26).
- [ALU (Arithmetic Logic Unit)](concepts/ALU.md) — CPU sub-unit performing arithmetic and bitwise ops on register operands; on the [[AVR]], outputs feed the [[StatusRegister]] flag bits ([[embedded-controllers-fiore]] ch. 16).
- [ATmega 328P](concepts/ATmega328P.md) — 8-bit [[AVR]] microcontroller from [[Atmel]] on the [[ArduinoUno|Arduino Uno]]: 32 k Flash / 2 k SRAM / 1 k EEPROM, [[HarvardArchitecture|Harvard]] [[RISC]], 26 interrupt vectors, three [[GPIO]] ports (B/C/D), six 10-bit [[ADC]] channels, three [[TimerCounter|timer/counters]], six [[PulseWidthModulation|PWM]] outputs ([[embedded-controllers-fiore]]).
- [AVR](concepts/AVR.md) — [[Atmel]]'s family of 8-bit [[RISC]] [[HarvardArchitecture|Harvard]] microcontrollers; substrate of nearly every classic [[Arduino]] board. Distinguished by 32 GPRs and most-instructions-in-one-cycle ([[embedded-controllers-fiore]] ch. 16).
- [Arduino (platform)](concepts/Arduino.md) — Open-source MCU dev platform built around [[ATmega328P|AVR]] / [[ARMCortexM|Cortex-M]] boards plus an IDE and the Wiring library (`setup`/`loop`/`pinMode`/`digitalWrite`/`analogRead`/`analogWrite`/`delay`/`map`). The pedagogical default in [[embedded-controllers-fiore]] chs. 15–29.
- [Arduino Uno](concepts/ArduinoUno.md) — Reference [[Arduino]] board built around the [[ATmega328P]]: 16 MHz, three GPIO ports, six 10-bit [[ADC]] channels, three [[TimerCounter|timers]], six [[PulseWidthModulation|PWM]] pins, 40 mA per pin / 200 mA chip-wide.
- [Abduction](concepts/Abduction.md) — Inference to the best explanation; the philosophical framing of [[ModelSelection]] across model classes ([[mml-book]] §8.2 marginal).
- [Abstraction](concepts/Abstraction.md) — Simplified, stable interface hiding implementation details. The [[OperatingSystem|OS]]'s core product per [[dis-0-introduction]]; the lens through which [[DiveIntoSystems]] frames *"writing efficient code"* — abstractions are necessary for productivity, performance comes from knowing which physical details they hide.
- [Activation Function](concepts/ActivationFunction.md) — nonlinearity that lets neural networks learn non-linear mappings.
- [AddressSanitizer (ASan)](concepts/AddressSanitizer.md) — Compile-time-instrumented memory-error detector (`-fsanitize=address`); modern alternative to [[Valgrind]] / [[Memcheck]] with ~2× slowdown (vs Memcheck's ~10–50×), full [[StackSection|stack]] + [[DataSection|globals]] coverage via red zones, but requires recompilation and **does not** catch [[UninitializedReadError|uninitialized reads]] (MemorySanitizer's job). Not covered by [[dis-3-3-valgrind|DIS Ch 3.3]] but the canonical CI tool every C codebase in 2026 runs alongside Memcheck.
- [Adam](concepts/Adam.md) — adaptive-moment optimizer, default for most deep-learning training.
- [Adapter Layers](concepts/adapterlayers.md) — Parameter-efficient fine-tuning via small bottleneck blocks inserted into Transformer FFN sub-layers; ablated against full fine-tuning in T5.
- [Adversarial Ensemble](concepts/adversarialensemble.md) — 
- [Agentic AI](concepts/AgenticAI.md) — DAG-composed system of specialized learnable agents (Liao et al. Def. 4.1); exponentially superior sample/parameter efficiency vs monolithic learners under the [[StructuredRealWorldDistribution]]; generalizes [[MixtureOfExperts]] in scope, topology and routing.
- [Agentic Algorithm Discovery](concepts/AgenticAlgorithmDiscovery.md) — LLM-driven program search (FunSearch → EoH → AlphaEvolve → Meta-Harness → AutoTTS). Explorer LLM proposes/refines code-defined algorithms; sandbox returns scalar scores + execution traces; iterate. Execution-trace feedback beats scalar feedback; constrained search spaces (e.g. [[BetaParameterization]]) improve generalization.
- [Agentic Harness](concepts/agenticharness.md) — 
- [Agentic Reinforcement Learning](concepts/agenticreinforcementlearning.md) — 
- [Agentic Sovereignty](concepts/AgenticSovereignty.md) — Probability $\mathcal{S}\in[0,1]$ that a propagator LLM keeps its internal derivation independent of swarm consensus. Governed by the [[SovereigntyDecayLaw]]; 0.5-crossing defines $D_L$. From [[2605.10698-bystander-effect-mas]].
- [Alignment Hallucination](concepts/AlignmentHallucination.md) — Failure mode where the model derives correctly internally then sycophantically externalizes a falsehood; operationalized as [[SovereigntyGap]] $G_\mathcal{S}\gg 0$. Existence proof of CoT/output divergence under social pressure.
- [AlphaZero](concepts/alphazero.md) — 
- [Anyscale Jobs](concepts/AnyscaleJobs.md) — managed batch Ray job primitive on Anyscale.
- [Anyscale Services](concepts/AnyscaleServices.md) — managed online Ray Serve deployments with autoscaling and canaries.
- [Anyscale Workspaces](concepts/AnyscaleWorkspaces.md) — interactive Ray dev environment mirroring production.
- [Argparse](concepts/Argparse.md) — Python standard-library CLI builder.
- [Arrange-Act-Assert](concepts/ArrangeActAssert.md) — three-step pattern for structuring unit tests.
- [Apriori Algorithm](concepts/AprioriAlgorithm.md) — Breadth-first frequent-itemset search with monotone support-based pruning; inner loops embarrassingly parallel ([[parproc-ch14-statistics-data-mining]] §14.1.3–14.1.4).
- [ASHA](concepts/ASHA.md) — async successive-halving scheduler for hyperparameter search.
- [Additive Attention](concepts/AdditiveAttention.md) — [[BahdanauAttention|Bahdanau]]-style attention scoring function $\mathbf{w}_v^\top\tanh(\mathbf{W}_q\mathbf{q}+\mathbf{W}_k\mathbf{k})$; one-hidden-layer MLP on the query–key concatenation; used when $\mathbf{q}$ and $\mathbf{k}$ have different dimensions ([[d2l-attention-and-transformers]]).
- [Attention](concepts/Attention.md) — mechanism for dynamically weighting input parts when producing each output.
- [Attention Is All You Need (Concept)](concepts/AttentionIsAllYouNeed.md) — 2017 paper introducing the transformer architecture.
- [Attention Mask](concepts/AttentionMask.md) — mask zeroing disallowed token interactions (padding, causal).
- [Attention Pooling](concepts/AttentionPooling.md) — The softmax-weighted sum $\sum_i\alpha(\mathbf{q},\mathbf{k}_i)\mathbf{v}_i$ that is the aggregation step of every attention mechanism; differentiable generalization of a database lookup ([[d2l-attention-and-transformers]]).
- [Attention Scoring Functions](concepts/AttentionScoringFunctions.md) — The pre-softmax compatibility $a(\mathbf{q},\mathbf{k})$ — dot-product $\mathbf{q}^\top\mathbf{k}/\sqrt{d}$ (modern default) vs additive $\mathbf{w}_v^\top\tanh(\mathbf{W}_q\mathbf{q}+\mathbf{W}_k\mathbf{k})$ (Bahdanau) ([[d2l-attention-and-transformers]]).
- [Bahdanau Attention](concepts/BahdanauAttention.md) — Bahdanau, Cho & Bengio 2014 differentiable alignment for [[MachineTranslation|MT]]: per-step context $\mathbf{c}_{t'}=\sum_t\alpha(\mathbf{s}_{t'-1},\mathbf{h}_t)\mathbf{h}_t$; structural fix for the fixed-vector bottleneck of [[1409.3215-seq2seq]] and direct ancestor of [[SelfAttention]] ([[d2l-attention-and-transformers]]).
- [Autoencoder](concepts/Autoencoder.md) — network that reconstructs its input through a bottleneck.
- [Autograd](concepts/Autograd.md) — automatic-differentiation engines powering backpropagation.
- [Autoregressive Model](concepts/AutoregressiveModel.md) — Sequence model that regresses a signal on its own past, $P(x_t\mid x_{<t})$; underlies $n$-gram, RNN, and Transformer LMs ([[d2l-recurrent-neural-networks]]).
- [Autoresearch](concepts/autoresearch.md) — 
- [Autoscaling](concepts/Autoscaling.md) — automatic adjustment of compute capacity to load.
- [Average Pooling](concepts/AveragePooling.md) — [[Pooling]] operator returning the mean of each window; LeNet-era default, now mostly superseded by [[MaxPooling]] except as global average pooling at network end ([[d2l-convolutional-neural-networks]]).
- [AutoTTS](concepts/AutoTTS.md) — Environment-driven framework ([[2605.08083-autotts]]) that **automates [[testtimescaling|test-time scaling]] strategy design** by treating it as controller synthesis over a [[WidthDepthSearch|width–depth]] control space. Three pillars: [[OfflineReplayEnvironment]], [[BetaParameterization]], [[ExecutionTraceFeedback]]. Discovers the [[ConfidenceMomentumController|CMC]] in 5 rounds / $39.9 / 160 min.
- [Average Trap](concepts/AverageTrap.md) — Irreducible quadratic penalty $\epsilon = \sum_k \tfrac{\alpha_k}{2}\|\theta^*_{\text{mono}}-\theta^*_k\|^2_{H_k}$ a monolithic learner pays from conflicting per-task gradients (Liao et al. Prop. 3.3); the "Generalist's Penalty."
- [AWS IAM](concepts/AWSIAM.md) — AWS identity and access management policy system.
- [BPTT](concepts/BPTT.md) — Backpropagation Through Time (Werbos 1990); unroll the RNN and apply chain rule with weight-tied gradients summed across time; exposes vanishing/exploding gradients via $(\mathbf{W}_\textrm{hh}^\top)^k$ powers ([[d2l-recurrent-neural-networks]]).
- [Bitwise Operations](concepts/BitwiseOperations.md) — `& | ^ ~ << >>` — the operator family that makes register-poking possible; pervasive in embedded C, rare in desktop code. Idioms: `x |= (1<<n)` set, `x &= ~(1<<n)` clear, `x ^= (1<<n)` toggle ([[embedded-controllers-fiore]] ch. 4).
- [Backpropagation](concepts/Backpropagation.md) — chain-rule algorithm for computing neural-network gradients.
- [Bandwidth](concepts/Bandwidth.md) — Bits per unit time a [[CommunicationBottleneck|communication]] channel can carry; orthogonal-and-independent companion to [[Latency]]; raised via bus width (shared-memory) / parallel network paths (clusters) / link speed ([[parproc-ch02-recurring-performance-issues]] §2.5).
- [Bank Conflict](concepts/BankConflict.md) — Hardware serialization penalty when multiple processors (or [[GPU]] warp lanes) simultaneously access the *same* memory bank; the [[parproc-ch03-shared-memory-parallelism|Ch3]] §3.2.2 worked example (16 threads × 1 M elements × 4 low-order banks all hit bank 0) and its stride-1 fix; stride/bank theorem `gcd(s,b)=1`; mitigations include padding and [[MemoryInterleaving|interleaving discipline]] choice.
- [Barrier (synchronization)](concepts/Barrier.md) — "A point in the code that all threads must reach before continuing"; Pthreads `pthread_barrier_wait`, OpenMP `#pragma omp barrier`, Rdsm `barr()` ([[parproc-ch01-intro-parallel-processing]]); correct two-counter implementation and parallel [[TreeBarrier|tree]] / [[ButterflyBarrier|butterfly]] schemes delivered in [[parproc-ch03-shared-memory-parallelism|Ch3]] §3.12.
- [Butterfly Barrier](concepts/ButterflyBarrier.md) — Parallel [[Barrier]] in which each node bit-flip-handshakes with $\log_2 n$ partners over $\log_2 n$ phases (`i ⊕ 2^k`); *"a butterfly exchange amounts to a number of simultaneously tree operations"* ([[parproc-ch03-shared-memory-parallelism]] §3.12.4.2.2).
- [Batch Inference](concepts/BatchInference.md) — offline bulk-prediction workload optimized for throughput.
- [Batch Normalization](concepts/BatchNormalization.md) — per-batch activation normalization that stabilizes deep training.
- [Bayesian Linear Regression](concepts/BayesianLinearRegression.md) — Full-Bayesian counterpart of MLE [[LinearRegression]]; closed-form Gaussian posterior under Gaussian prior + Gaussian likelihood ([[mml-book]] §9.3). Calibrated predictive uncertainty + marginal-likelihood model selection.
- [Bayesian Optimization](concepts/BayesianOptimization.md) — surrogate-model-based hyperparameter search.
- [Beam Search](concepts/beamsearch.md) — 
- [Behavioral Testing](concepts/BehavioralTesting.md) — capability-grouped input/output tests for ML models.
- [Bell-La Padula](concepts/belllapadula.md) — 
- [BERT](concepts/bert.md) — 
- [Binary Representation](concepts/BinaryRepresentation.md) — Encoding of integers, floats, characters, and instructions as bit patterns inside [[ComputerHardware|hardware]]; previewed in [[dis-0-introduction]] as a prerequisite for explaining C arithmetic, overflow, signed/unsigned semantics, and floating-point precision.
- [Best-of-N](concepts/bestofn.md) — Generate $N$ candidates, pick one. Width-only degenerate case of the [[WidthDepthSearch|width–depth control space]]; [[selfconsistency|Self-Consistency]] = BoN + majority vote.
- [Beta Parameterization](concepts/BetaParameterization.md) — Search-tractability discipline from [[2605.08083-autotts|AutoTTS]]: every candidate TTS controller exposes only a single scalar $\beta\in[0,1]$ mapped monotonically to all internal hyperparameters. Ablation: removing it cuts held-out accuracy 53.1→49.0 (search overfits to extreme pruning thresholds).
- [Biconditional Correctness](concepts/biconditionalcorrectness.md) — 
- [Black](concepts/Black.md) — opinionated Python code formatter.
- [Black-Box Shift Detection](concepts/BlackBoxShiftDetection.md) — detecting drift from model outputs alone.
- [BLEU](concepts/bleu.md) — 
- [Blocksworld](concepts/Blocksworld.md) — Canonical classical-planning domain; PlanBench shows LLMs solve 11–59% zero-shot and 0–4% on the obfuscated *Mystery BW* variant — the smoking-gun retrieval-not-planning result.
- [Breakpoint](concepts/Breakpoint.md) — Debugger marker that pauses the debuggee at a chosen source line / function / address — [[GDB]]'s primary control primitive. Four set-forms (`break 42` / `break file.c:42` / `break func` / `break *0x4011a0`); program reaches it via [[GdbRun|`run`]], state is inspected with [[GdbPrint|`print`]] / [[GdbBacktrace|`bt`]], execution resumes with [[StepDebug|`next` / `step` / `cont`]]. Software implementation overwrites the target byte with an `int3` trap; hardware breakpoints use limited CPU debug registers. Conditional form (`break 42 if x > 100`) skips irrelevant iterations ([[dis-3-1-gdb]]).
- [Bystander Effect (in Multi-Agent Reasoning)](concepts/BystanderEffect.md) — Architectural failure mode where simulated peer consensus (static prompt content, no live dialogue) triggers a propagator LLM to discard its own correct derivation. [[gpt54|GPT-5.4]] SWE-bench collapses 1.00→0.23 at $n=2$.
- [Cauchy-Schwarz Inequality](concepts/CauchySchwarzInequality.md) — $|\langle\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}\rangle|\leq\|\mathbf{x}\|\|\mathbf{y}\|$ ([[mml-book]] §3.3); the inequality that lets inner products define angles and induces the triangle inequality for the induced norm.
- [C4](concepts/c4.md) — 745 GB heuristically-filtered Common Crawl corpus released with T5; the canonical large diverse web-text pre-training data set.
- [Calculus](concepts/Calculus.md) — Minimum-viable calculus for deep learning: derivatives → partials → gradients → Jacobian/Hessian → chain rule → Taylor expansion. Engine behind every parameter update. [[d2l-preliminaries]] §Calculus.
- [Canary Deployment](concepts/CanaryDeployment.md) — gradual traffic shift to a new model version.
- [Cargo Features](concepts/CargoFeatures.md) — [[Cargo]]'s named-boolean opt-in/opt-out compilation toggles — Rust's `#[cfg(feature="X")]`-gated replacement for embedded-C `#ifdef`; declared per crate in `Cargo.toml`, **additive across the dependency tree** (any enabling consumer turns the feature on for everyone, so a feature must never break the API of crates that don't ask for it) ([[rust-embedded-book-c-tips-index]]).
- [Capability Gate](concepts/capabilitygate.md) — 
- [Capability vs Alignment](concepts/CapabilityVsAlignment.md) — distinction between what a model can do and what it does.
- [Chain-of-Thought](concepts/chainofthought.md) — 
- [Character-Level Language Model](concepts/CharacterLevelLanguageModel.md) — LM that operates over character tokens (~30 vocab on *The Time Machine*); D2L's pedagogical RNN-LM example ([[d2l-recurrent-neural-networks]]).
- [CheckList](concepts/CheckList.md) — behavioral NLP testing methodology.
- [Checkpoint](concepts/Checkpoint.md) — serialized snapshot of model and optimizer state.
- [Chi-Squared Test](concepts/ChiSquaredTest.md) — categorical goodness-of-fit / independence test.
- [Cholesky Decomposition](concepts/CholeskyDecomposition.md) — $\mathbf{A}=\mathbf{L}\mathbf{L}^\top$ for symmetric positive-definite $\mathbf{A}$ ([[mml-book]] §4.3); the "square root of a matrix." Underlies multivariate-Gaussian sampling and fast SPD linear solves.
- [CI/CD](concepts/CICD.md) — automated integration and deployment pipelines.
- [CISC](concepts/CISC.md) — Complex Instruction Set Computing; multi-cycle instructions, fewer registers; opposite of [[RISC]]. Modern x86 is internally RISC wrapped in a CISC ISA ([[embedded-controllers-fiore]] ch. 16).
- [Cross-Compiler](concepts/CrossCompiler.md) — compiler that runs on one architecture (host) and emits machine code for another (target). The canonical embedded toolchain shape — you cannot natively develop on a 2 k-SRAM MCU. `avr-gcc` for AVR, `arm-none-eabi-gcc` for Cortex-M ([[embedded-controllers-fiore]] ch. 15).
- [Class (OOP)](concepts/Class.md) — blueprint bundling data and behavior in object-oriented code.
- [Class Imbalance](concepts/ClassImbalance.md) — classification setting with dramatically uneven label frequencies.
- [CLI](concepts/CLI.md) — text-based interface for invoking programs with commands and flags.
- [Cluster (parallel computing)](concepts/Cluster.md) — Networked commodity machines used as a parallel processing system; [[Beowulf]] is the canonical recipe ([[parproc-ch01-intro-parallel-processing]]).
- [CNN](concepts/CNN.md) — Convolutional neural network — *the* vision-architecture family, derived from imposing [[TranslationInvariance]] + [[Locality]] on an MLP. Stacks [[ConvolutionalLayer|conv layers]] + nonlinearities + [[Pooling]]; ancestor [[LeNet]] (1989) through [[AlexNet]] / [[ResNet]] / [[VisionTransformer|ViT]] ([[d2l-convolutional-neural-networks]]).
- [Code Organization](concepts/CodeOrganization.md) — structuring projects into modules and layers.
- [Code Style](concepts/CodeStyle.md) — conventions for formatting and structuring source code.
- [Cilk](concepts/Cilk.md) — Parallel C-extension language whose defining contribution is a [[WorkStealing|work-stealing]] runtime (`cilk_spawn` / `cilk_sync`); the named exemplar in [[parproc-ch02-recurring-performance-issues]] §2.4.4 ("the elegant Cilk language").
- [Co-adaptation](concepts/Coadaptation.md) — Phenomenon where hidden units rely on specific upstream activation patterns; [[Dropout]]'s target ([[d2l-multilayer-perceptrons]]).
- [Co-STORM (Collaborative STORM)](concepts/CoSTORM.md) — Collaborative-discourse information-seeking system from [[2408.15232-co-storm]]; $N$ [[PerspectiveGuidedExpert|perspective-guided experts]] + a [[ModeratorAgent|moderator]] over a dynamic [[CoSTORMMindMap|mind map]]; outperforms [[RAGChatbot|RAG Chatbot]] and [[STORM]]+QA on the [[WildSeek]] dataset; 70%/78% human-preferred over [[GoogleSearch|Search]] / RAG.
- [Co-STORM Mind Map](concepts/CoSTORMMindMap.md) — Dynamic hierarchical concept tree $\mathcal{M}=(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{E})$ maintained by [[CoSTORM|Co-STORM]] with `insert` + `reorganize` ops; tracks discourse, reduces user cognitive load, serves as outline for the final cited report; users judged 80 snapshots as accurately tracking the discourse 71% of the time.
- [Collaborative Discourse](concepts/CollaborativeDiscourse.md) — Educational-psychology grounding ([[Nussbaum2008]] / [[Osborne2010]] / [[Roschelle1995]]) for multi-party discussion with **different points of view** as a vehicle for human learning; operationalized in [[CoSTORM|Co-STORM]] via perspective-guided experts + moderator + mind map + mixed-initiative turn-management.
- [ColBERTv2](concepts/ColBERTv2.md) — **Late-interaction dense-retrieval model** (Khattab, Santhanam et al. 2022); successor to ColBERT (Khattab & Zaharia 2020) with denoised supervision + residual compression. Encodes query and document into **per-token contextualized BERT vectors** and aggregates relevance via **MaxSim** — sits between bi-encoders (one vector per passage; loses fine-grained matching) and cross-encoders (joint attention; slow). [[DSPy]]'s **default Wikipedia retriever**: `dspy.ColBERTv2(url=...)(query, k=...)`; the canonical public endpoint is `http://20.102.90.50:2017/wiki17_abstracts` (5.9M Wikipedia 2017 abstracts — same corpus as [[hotpotqa|HotPotQA]]). **Not a `dspy.Module` subclass** — a thin retrieval-client wrapper; the discipline is to wrap the call in a plain Python function inside [[DSPyModules|`dspy.Module`]] subclasses' `forward` methods (so retrieval is **invisible to [[DSPyOptimizers|optimizers]]** — endpoint, ranker, and `k` are fixed inputs). Used across the wiki by [[dspy-custom-module]] (canonical receipt), [[dspy-modules]] (multi-hop `Hop`), [[react]] (`search_wikipedia` tool), [[MIPROv2]] / [[2407.10930-better-together|BetterTogether]] / [[2507.19457-gepa|GEPA]] (HotPotQA receipts), and [[2312.13382-dspy-assertions|DSPy Assertions]] (shared retrieval substrate). Promoted from long-standing forward reference on ingest of [[dspy-custom-module]].
- [Cognitive Loafing](concepts/CognitiveLoafing.md) — LLM analogue of *social loafing* (Ringelmann 1913): integrative effort $E_{int}$ falls below task entropy $\mathcal{H}_\tau$ under swarm pressure. The $\mathcal{B}=1$ failure state in [[2605.10698-bystander-effect-mas]].
- [Cache Coherency](concepts/CacheCoherency.md) — Hardware protocol layer ensuring multi-cache consistency for shared memory lines; snoopy invalidate vs update on a bus (analogous to write-back vs write-through in uniprocessor caches), directory-based protocols off-bus, [[MESI]] as the Pentium exemplar ([[parproc-ch03-shared-memory-parallelism]] §3.5). Distinct from [[MemoryConsistency]] — coherency answers *"do caches agree?"*, consistency answers *"when does a new value become visible?"*.
- [Cache Memory](concepts/CacheMemory.md) — Small, fast on-chip section of the CPU storing copies of recently accessed RAM; organized in blocks; accesses are either cache hits (fast) or cache misses (full block fetched from RAM, possibly evicting another block). Hit rates typically exceed 90% due to [[LocalityOfReference]]. ([[parproc-appA-systems-issues]] §A.2.1)
- [Cache Level (L1 / L2 / L3)](concepts/CacheLevel.md) — The three-tier stratification of [[CacheMemory|cache]] inside a modern processor — *"L1 (very small and fast, near the [[ALU]]), L2 (larger and slower), and L3 (shared among multicore CPUs)"* ([[dis-11-1-memory-hierarchy]]). L1/L2 per-core; **L3 shared across all cores of a [[MulticoreProcessor|multicore CPU]]** — the natural cross-core data-exchange tier and the [[CacheCoherency|coherence]] / [[FalseSharing|false-sharing]] contention point.
- [Kernel](concepts/Kernel.md) — Privileged core of the [[OperatingSystem|OS]] — runs in [[KernelMode|kernel mode]], discovers hardware, launches [[Process|processes]], and handles [[Interrupt|interrupts]] + [[SystemCall|system-call]] traps. Mapped into the top of every process's address space for cheap [[ContextSwitch|context switching]] ([[dis-13-1-booting-running]]).
- [Kernel Mode](concepts/KernelMode.md) — Privileged [[CPU]] execution mode that runs the [[Kernel|OS kernel]]; unrestricted instructions + full memory + direct hardware access. Entered via trap ([[SystemCall]]) or hardware [[Interrupt]] ([[dis-13-1-booting-running]]).
- [User Mode](concepts/UserMode.md) — Unprivileged [[CPU]] execution mode for application code; restricted instruction set, OS-authorized memory regions only, no direct hardware access. Escapes to [[KernelMode|kernel mode]] only via [[SystemCall|trap]] or [[Interrupt|interrupt]] ([[dis-13-1-booting-running]]).
- [System Call](concepts/SystemCall.md) — Controlled [[UserMode|user]] → [[KernelMode|kernel]] gateway: user program loads syscall number into a designated [[CpuRegister|register]] and issues a **trap instruction**; CPU switches privilege and dispatches to the OS handler. *"the location varies according to the ISA"* ([[dis-13-1-booting-running]]).
- [Process State](concepts/ProcessState.md) — The four-state [[Process|process]] life cycle from [[dis-13-2-processes|DIS Ch 13.2]]: **Ready** (could run) / **Running** (on CPU) / **Blocked** (waiting on event) / **Exited** ([[Zombie|zombie]] pending [[Wait|`wait`]] reap). [[Scheduler|Scheduler]] only picks from Ready.
- [Process Control Block (PCB)](concepts/ProcessControlBlock.md) — Per-[[Process|process]] kernel data structure ([[dis-13-2-processes|DIS 13.2]]): [[ProcessID|PID]] + address-space info + saved [[CpuRegister|register]] snapshot + open-file list + current [[ProcessState|state]]; the destination of [[ContextSwitch|context-switch]] register saves.
- [`exec` (POSIX)](concepts/Exec.md) — POSIX [[SystemCall|syscall]] family (`execvp` / `execve` / ...) that **overlays the calling [[Process|process]]'s image** with a new program; preserves [[ProcessID|PID]], reinitializes everything else. Paired with [[Fork|`fork`]] as the canonical Unix process-spawn pattern. *Never returns on success* — only on failure ([[dis-13-2-processes|DIS 13.2]]).
- [`wait` / `waitpid` (POSIX)](concepts/Wait.md) — POSIX [[SystemCall|syscall]] that **reaps a terminated child** ([[Zombie|zombie]]) — collects [[ExitStatus|exit status]] and frees the [[ProcessControlBlock|PCB]]; blocks the parent in [[ProcessState|Blocked]] state until [[Signal|`SIGCHLD`]] arrives. Foreground vs background shell commands differ only in whether `wait` is called synchronously or in a signal handler ([[dis-13-2-processes|DIS 13.2]]).
- [Scheduler](concepts/Scheduler.md) — [[Kernel|OS kernel]] component that picks **which [[ProcessState|Ready]] [[Process|process]] runs next and for how long** — the **policy** half of the OS's process-execution stack, paired with [[ContextSwitch|context switch]] as the **mechanism** ([[dis-13-2-processes|DIS 13.2]]).
- [Process Scheduling](concepts/ProcessScheduling.md) — The **policy** of choosing the next [[ProcessState|Ready]] [[Process|process]] and its [[Timesharing|quantum]]; separable from the [[ContextSwitch|context-switch]] mechanism. [[dis-13-2-processes|DIS 13.2]] defers specific policies (round-robin, priority, CFS) to a dedicated OS textbook.
- [Multiprogramming](concepts/Multiprogramming.md) — OS-design discipline of **keeping multiple [[Process|processes]] resident** so the [[Scheduler|scheduler]] can switch to a [[ProcessState|Ready]] process whenever the current one blocks on I/O. Distinct from [[Timesharing]] (quantum-driven) but complementary ([[dis-13-2-processes|DIS 13.2]]).
- [Zombie Process](concepts/Zombie.md) — A [[Process|process]] that has called [[Exit|`exit`]] but whose [[ProcessControlBlock|PCB]] persists because the parent has not yet [[Wait|`wait`ed]]. Holds the [[ExitStatus|exit status]] until reaped; adopted by [[Init|`init`]] if the parent dies first ([[dis-13-2-processes|DIS 13.2]]).
- [`init` Process (PID 1)](concepts/Init.md) — The first user-level [[Process|process]] created at [[Bootloader|boot]] — **root of the [[Process|process]] hierarchy** and adopter of orphans. Modern Linux PID 1 is typically systemd ([[dis-13-2-processes|DIS 13.2]]).
- [Wall Time](concepts/WallTime.md) — Total elapsed real-world duration of a [[Process|process]] — counts Running + [[ProcessState|Blocked]] + Ready. **Affected by concurrent processes** on a [[Multiprogramming|multiprogrammed]] system. The "what the user sees" clock ([[dis-13-2-processes|DIS 13.2]]).
- [CPU Time](concepts/CPUTime.md) — Duration a [[Process|process]] **actually held a CPU** — counts only [[ProcessState|Running]]. **Unaffected by other processes** — the honest number for optimization work; can exceed wall time on multicore parallel programs ([[dis-13-2-processes|DIS 13.2]]).
- [Bootloader](concepts/Bootloader.md) — Small OS-bringup *boot block* that [[Firmware|firmware]] ([[BIOS]] / [[UEFI]]) loads from disk into RAM at power-up and jumps to, handing CPU control from firmware to the [[Kernel|kernel]] ([[dis-13-1-booting-running]]).
- [Cachegrind](concepts/Cachegrind.md) — [[Valgrind]] suite's [[CacheMemory|cache]]-simulation tool — `valgrind --tool=cachegrind --cache-sim=yes ./prog` simulates L1 + LL hit/miss counts and `cg_annotate` decodes per-source-line attribution. Headline benchmark: row-major vs column-major matrix-sum → **62,688 vs 1,062,996 D1 misses** (~17× delta) producing **4.61× runtime gap** at zero algorithmic-complexity change ([[dis-11-5-cachegrind]]). Deterministic simulator (not HW sampler); ~20–100× slowdown.
- [Cache Line](concepts/CacheLine.md) — Unit of storage inside a [[CacheMemory|CPU cache]] — a fixed-size chunk (typically **16–64 bytes**) of consecutive bytes copied between [[RAM]] and cache atomically. Bundles a **data block** with **metadata** (valid bit, tag, optional dirty bit). The granularity at which hardware exploits [[SpatialLocality|spatial locality]] ([[dis-11-4-caching]]).
- [Cache Hit](concepts/CacheHit.md) — Request satisfied from [[CacheMemory|cache]] without stalling for [[RAM|main memory]]; ~1 ns vs ~100 ns miss penalty — the central performance lever of the [[MemoryHierarchy|memory hierarchy]]. Hit rates >90 % routine on programs with good [[LocalityOfReference|locality]] ([[dis-11-4-caching]]).
- [Cache Miss](concepts/CacheMiss.md) — Requested address not in [[CacheMemory|cache]]; CPU stalls for [[RAM|main memory]] then installs the fetched block. **3C taxonomy**: **compulsory** (first access, unavoidable) / **capacity** ([[WorkingSet|working set]] > cache) / **conflict** (placement-restriction-induced — the class [[SetAssociativeCache|set-associative]] caches attack) ([[dis-11-4-caching]]).
- [Cache Replacement Policy](concepts/CacheReplacementPolicy.md) — Rule selecting which [[CacheLine|line]] to evict on a [[CacheMiss|miss]] into a full set. [[LeastRecentlyUsed|LRU]] is canonical (leverages [[TemporalLocality|temporal locality]]); FIFO / Random are simpler alternatives. Irrelevant for [[DirectMappedCache|direct-mapped]] (no choice) ([[dis-11-4-caching]]).
- [Least Recently Used (LRU)](concepts/LeastRecentlyUsed.md) — Canonical [[CacheReplacementPolicy|cache replacement policy]]; evicts the line whose last access is furthest in the past. Justified by [[TemporalLocality|temporal locality]] — *"recently used data is likely to be used again"* ([[dis-11-4-caching]]). Pseudo-LRU (binary-tree, NRU) approximations dominate high-associativity hardware.
- [Direct-Mapped Cache](concepts/DirectMappedCache.md) — Simplest [[CacheMemory|cache]] placement architecture — each memory address maps to **exactly one** [[CacheLine|cache line]] via the index bits. Cheapest lookup hardware; highest **conflict-miss rate**. Survives in embedded / microcontroller caches and some branch-prediction structures ([[dis-11-4-caching]]).
- [Set Associative Cache](concepts/SetAssociativeCache.md) — Modern dominant [[CacheMemory|cache]] placement — each address maps to a set of **N lines** (typically 2–8); all N tags compared in parallel; [[LeastRecentlyUsed|LRU]] selects eviction. *"Offers a good compromise between complexity and conflicts"* ([[dis-11-4-caching]]). Used by L1 / L2 / L3 in all modern CPUs.
- [Fully Associative Cache](concepts/FullyAssociativeCache.md) — Maximum-flexibility [[CacheMemory|cache]] placement — any address can occupy any [[CacheLine|line]]; lookup compares every tag in parallel. Zero conflict misses but lookup cost scales with cache size → *"generally unfit for a general-purpose CPU cache"* ([[dis-11-4-caching]]). Persists in [[TLB|TLBs]] / victim caches / micro-op caches.
- [Write-Back Cache](concepts/WriteBackCache.md) — Modern dominant **write policy** — writes update [[CacheMemory|cache]] only, mark the line **dirty**, propagate to [[RAM|main memory]] only on eviction. *"Amortizing the cost of a memory access across many writes significantly improves performance"* ([[dis-11-4-caching]]); complicates [[CacheCoherency|coherence]].
- [Write-Through Cache](concepts/WriteThroughCache.md) — Simpler **write policy** — every write updates [[CacheMemory|cache]] AND [[RAM|main memory]] simultaneously. No dirty bit; natural [[CacheCoherency|coherence]]; bandwidth-hungry. Dominated by [[WriteBackCache|write-back]] for CPU caches; persists in some GPU / embedded caches ([[dis-11-4-caching]]).
- [Hard Disk Drive (HDD)](concepts/HardDisk.md) — Mechanical magnetic-platter-based [[NonVolatileMemory|non-volatile]] secondary storage; **5–10 ms latency** (seek + rotational + transfer), 0.5–10 TB capacity, lowest cost-per-byte; rotating platters at 5,000–15,000 RPM divided into tracks + sectors ([[dis-11-2-storage-devices]]); ~10⁵× slower than [[DRAM]] because mechanical motion gates access; biases code toward sequential / block-oriented patterns ([[LocalityOfReference]] matters even at the disk tier).
- [Solid-State Drive (SSD)](concepts/SolidStateDrive.md) — [[FlashMemory|Flash-memory]]-based [[NonVolatileMemory|non-volatile]] secondary storage with **no moving parts**; 0.1–1 ms latency, 0.5–2 TB capacity, moderate cost-per-byte; ~10–100× faster than [[HardDisk|HDDs]] (eliminates seek + rotational latency), still ~10³–10⁴× slower than [[DRAM]] ([[dis-11-2-storage-devices]]). **Naming disambiguation**: not to be confused with [[SSD|SSD (Single-Shot MultiBox Detector)]] — the object-detection model — which lives at `concepts/SSD.md`.
- [Non-Volatile Memory](concepts/NonVolatileMemory.md) — The volatility-axis category for storage technologies that **retain contents when power is removed**; the non-volatile floor of the [[MemoryHierarchy|memory hierarchy]] holds the program binary, [[OperatingSystem|OS kernel]], and user data across reboots; members in the wiki — [[FlashMemory]] / [[SolidStateDrive]] / [[HardDisk]] (magnetic tape / optical / network-remote named only); persistence ≠ reliability — each technology has a distinct wear / failure model (HDD mechanical, [[FlashMemory|flash]] finite-write-endurance, tape/optical decade-scale decay) ([[dis-11-2-storage-devices]]).
- [Coherent Caches](concepts/CoherentCaches.md) — Cache-coherence protocol layer in [[SMP]]/multicore systems ensuring all processors see a consistent view of shared memory ([[parproc-ch01-intro-parallel-processing]]); full treatment delivered in [[parproc-ch03-shared-memory-parallelism]] §3.5.
- [Context Switch](concepts/ContextSwitch.md) — OS operation triggered at each quantum boundary in [[Timesharing]]: saves all register values (PC, EFLAGS, etc.) of the outgoing process and restores those of the incoming process. ([[parproc-appA-systems-issues]] §A.1.1)
- [Crossbar Interconnect](concepts/Crossbar.md) — Non-blocking $n \times n$ switch grid wiring $n$ processors to $n$ memory modules; $n^2$ pathways guarantee $n$ simultaneous distinct-destination packets but cost $O(n^2)$. Sun Microsystems Enterprise 10000 used a 16×16 crossbar ([[parproc-ch03-shared-memory-parallelism]] §3.3.3.1).
- [COGS](concepts/cogs.md) — 
- [Compare-Exchange](concepts/CompareExchange.md) — Two-node pool-and-split primitive: nodes combine data, lower-ID keeps lower half, higher-ID keeps upper half; foundational operation in [[BitonicMergesort]], [[Hyperquicksort]], and [[OddEvenTransposition]] ([[parproc-ch12-parallel-sorting]] §12.2.4).
- [Communication Bottleneck](concepts/CommunicationBottleneck.md) — *"Whether you are on a shared-memory, message-passing or other platform, communication is always a potential bottleneck"* — the [[parproc-ch02-recurring-performance-issues]] §2.1 opener; covers bus / [[CoherentCaches|cache-coherency]] traffic in shared-memory, network packets in clusters, and CPU↔GPU + on-device contention in [[GPU|GPUs]]; trades off against [[LoadBalancing]].
- [Complementary Learning Systems](concepts/complementarylearningsystems.md) — 
- [Composite Social Load](concepts/CompositeSocialLoad.md) — $\mathcal{L}(\vec{a},p)=\sum_i w_i\,\alpha(a_i)\,\kappa(p,a_i)$: positional weight × base authority × kinship multiplier. Drives the [[SovereigntyDecayLaw]]; non-commutative via the [[LeadAnchorEffect]].
- [Compositional Capacity](concepts/CompositionalCapacity.md) — Topology Factor $C(\mathcal{G})=\sum_u \omega_u$ — sum of per-agent [[TopologicalWeight]]s — that governs the *error magnitude* of an Agentic AI DAG (Liao et al. Thm 4.3).
- [Compiler Optimization](concepts/CompilerOptimization.md) — Family of compiler program-transformation passes ([[GCC|`gcc`]] `-O0` / `-O1` / `-O2` / `-O3` / `-Os` / `-Oz` / `-Og` / `-Ofast`) that trade source-to-binary correspondence for speed / size — preserving observable behavior per the [[AsIfRule|as-if rule]]. The orthogonal axis to [[GccDashG|`-g`]] [[DebugSymbol|debug-info]]: at `-O2`+ the compiler reorders / inlines / eliminates / vectorizes instructions, breaking [[GDB|GDB]]'s line-to-instruction mapping and producing `<optimized out>` for register-resident variables. [[dis-3-1-gdb|Ch 3.1]]'s rule: **debug at `-O0 -g`** (*"compiler-optimized code is often very difficult to debug because sequences of optimized machine code often do not clearly map back to C source code"*) ([[dis-3-1-gdb]]).
- [Compute-Efficient Training](concepts/computeefficienttraining.md) — The fixed-compute training regime derived from scaling laws: very large models, modest data, stop short of convergence.
- [Computational Graph](concepts/ComputationalGraph.md) — DAG of tensor values + differentiable primitives that [[Autograd]] walks backward via the chain rule. Dynamic (PyTorch, MXNet) vs static (TF `tf.function`, JAX `jit`); supports Python control flow; activations cached for backward. [[d2l-preliminaries]] §Autograd.
- [Computer Hardware](concepts/ComputerHardware.md) — Physical components of a [[ComputerSystem|computer system]]: [[CPU]], [[RAM]], I/O ports, secondary storage; modern norm is [[MulticoreProcessor|multicore]] silicon often packaged as a [[SystemOnAChip|SoC]] ([[dis-0-introduction]]).
- [Computer System](concepts/ComputerSystem.md) — Per [[DiveIntoSystems]] Ch 0: [[ComputerHardware|hardware]] **plus** an [[OperatingSystem|OS]] delivering a general-purpose, reprogrammable environment. Restrictive definition that **excludes** calculators and bare [[Microcontroller|microcontrollers]] — the wiki's first formal definition of "computer system."
- [CPU Register](concepts/CpuRegister.md) — small, fixed-size storage **inside the [[CPU]]** holding operands / addresses / status flags for the executing instruction; fastest tier of the [[MemoryHierarchy|memory hierarchy]]. Inspected from [[GDB]] via `info registers` (whole file), [[GdbPrint|`print $rax`]] (one register, `$`-prefix disambiguates from C identifiers), [[GdbDisplay|`display $rax`]] (auto-print), [[GdbSet|`set $rax = 0`]] (write). x86-64 general-purpose set `%rax`/`%rbx`/`%rcx`/`%rdx`/`%rsi`/`%rdi`/`%rbp`/`%rsp` + special-purpose [[InstructionPointer|`%rip`]] / `%eflags`; [[IA32]] uses `%eax` / `%eip` ([[dis-3-5-gdb-assembly|DIS Ch 3.5]]).
- [Core File (Core Dump)](concepts/CoreFile.md) — OS-written disk snapshot of a process's memory + CPU registers at abnormal termination (typically [[SegmentationFault|`SIGSEGV`]] / `SIGBUS` / `SIGABRT`). Enables **post-mortem [[Debugger|debugging]]** — `gdb ./buggy core` overlays the executable's [[DebugSymbol|symbols]] onto the dump, exposing [[GdbBacktrace|`bt`]] / [[GdbPrint|`print`]] / `info registers` on the frozen state. Execution cannot resume. Default `RLIMIT_CORE=0` on most modern distributions; enable with `ulimit -c unlimited`. Captures heap / stack / .data / .bss / register set / [[CommandLineArguments|argv]]; not text segment (read-only, recovered from binary), not kernel-side I/O buffers ([[dis-3-1-gdb]]).
- [Concept Drift](concepts/ConceptDrift.md) — shift in the P(y|x) relationship over time.
- [Concept Shift](concepts/ConceptShift.md) — Subtype of [[DistributionShift|distribution shift]] where the **labeling function** $P(y\mid\mathbf x)$ itself drifts (soft-drink names by US region, DSM mental-illness criteria). Hardest shift type to correct principally; usual remedy is continual fine-tuning on fresh labels ([[d2l-linear-classification]]).
- [Covariate Shift](concepts/CovariateShift.md) — Subtype of [[DistributionShift|distribution shift]] where $P(\mathbf x)$ changes but $P(y\mid\mathbf x)$ does not (photos → cartoons of cats/dogs); correctable by importance-weighted [[EmpiricalRiskMinimization|ERM]] with $\beta_i = \exp(h(\mathbf x_i))$ estimated by a binary logistic-regression domain classifier ([[d2l-linear-classification]]).
- [Confidence Momentum Controller (CMC)](concepts/ConfidenceMomentumController.md) — TTS controller discovered by [[AutoTTS]] ([[2605.08083-autotts]]). Four non-obvious mechanisms: EMA-momentum stopping (gate fires only when both `ema_conf ≥ thresh` AND non-negative delta), coupled width–depth control via shared EMA-delta, alignment-aware depth allocation (aligned branches get burst probes), conservative branch abandonment (≥2 active branches always preserved).
- [Confident Learning](concepts/ConfidentLearning.md) — framework for finding likely-mislabeled examples.
- [Conditional Breakpoint](concepts/ConditionalBreakpoint.md) — [[Breakpoint]] that halts only when an attached expression evaluates true (`break loc if expr` or `condition N (expr)`); the headline workflow for **loop-iteration-of-interest** and **state-triggered halts** ([[dis-3-2-gdb-commands|DIS Ch 3.2]]: *"pause at a breakpoint inside a loop only after some number of iterations or pause the program at a breakpoint only when the value of a variable has an interesting value"*). Trap fires every hit, then GDB evaluates the condition and silently resumes if false — so cost is one trap per loop iteration even when false. Composes with [[GdbInfo|`info breakpoints`]] and the `commands N … end` script block for log-and-continue debugging without recompilation.
- [Conditional Probability](concepts/ConditionalProbability.md) — $P(B\mid A) = P(A,B)/P(A)$ — restrict to subset where $A=a$, renormalize. Product rule, conditional independence, explaining-away reversals. [[d2l-preliminaries]] §Multiple Random Variables.
- [Concurrency vs Parallelism](concepts/ConcurrencyVsParallelism.md) — Foundational distinction [[dis-14-1-multicore|DIS Ch 14.1.1]] codifies: **concurrency** is the *appearance* of simultaneous execution via [[ContextSwitch|context-switch]] interleaving on a single core; **parallel execution** is *"the simultaneous execution of instructions from processes running on multiple cores"*. Every parallel execution is concurrent; not the converse. Implies the [[CPUTime|CPU-time]] vs [[WallClockTime|wall-clock-time]] split — adding cores shrinks wall-clock but not any one process's CPU time. Single-thread runtimes (Python GIL, JS event loop) give concurrency without parallelism; [[Pthreads]] / Go goroutines give both.
- [Conjugate Prior](concepts/ConjugatePrior.md) — Prior that keeps the posterior in the same family ([[mml-book]] §6.6); exists for every [[ExponentialFamily]] likelihood. Gaussian-Gaussian conjugacy is what makes [[BayesianLinearRegression]] tractable.
- [Contextual Embedding](concepts/ContextualEmbedding.md) — token vector that depends on surrounding context.
- [Context Vector](concepts/ContextVector.md) — encoder summary or attention-weighted sum consumed by a decoder.
- [Continual Learning](concepts/continuallearning.md) — 
- [Convex Optimization](concepts/ConvexOptimization.md) — Optimization problems where local minima are global ([[mml-book]] §7.3). Underlies linear regression, ridge, Lasso, [[SupportVectorMachine|SVM]]; strong duality enables dual formulations.
- [Channels (CNN)](concepts/Channels.md) — Third axis of an image tensor (RGB, hyperspectral) and of CNN feature maps; multi-channel kernels have shape $c_o\times c_i\times k_h\times k_w$; deeper layers trade spatial resolution for channel depth ([[d2l-convolutional-neural-networks]]).
- [Convolution](concepts/Convolution.md) — sliding-window operation core to CNN feature extraction; the unique linear translation-equivariant local operator on a 2D grid. Frameworks actually compute [[CrossCorrelation|cross-correlation]] under this name.
- [Convolutional Layer](concepts/ConvolutionalLayer.md) — parameterized layer wrapping a [[CrossCorrelation|cross-correlation]] operator with a learnable kernel ($c_o\times c_i\times k_h\times k_w$) and bias; the workhorse of every [[CNN]] ([[d2l-convolutional-neural-networks]]).
- [Cross-Correlation](concepts/CrossCorrelation.md) — the operator deep-learning frameworks compute and (mis)call "convolution"; differs from true [[Convolution|convolution]] only by a kernel flip — invisible to learned models.
- [Computer Vision](concepts/ComputerVision.md) — Application domain transformed by [[DeepLearning]]; [[CNN|CNNs]] are its backbone per [[d2l-preface]]. *Stub.*
- [Coordination Layer](concepts/coordinationlayer.md) — 
- [Classification](concepts/Classification.md) — Supervised task with discrete labels — *which one?* problems. Binary / multiclass / hierarchical / multi-label variants; softmax + [[CrossEntropyLoss|cross-entropy]] the default training recipe. [[d2l-introduction]] anchor.
- [Cross-Entropy Loss](concepts/CrossEntropyLoss.md) — standard loss for classification and language modeling.
- [CPU](concepts/CPU.md) — Central processing unit; fetches/decodes/executes machine instructions. Named in [[dis-0-introduction]] as one of the four core [[ComputerHardware|hardware]] components; in modern form essentially always a [[MulticoreProcessor|multicore processor]] often packaged inside a [[SystemOnAChip|SoC]].
- [CSV Format](concepts/CSVFormat.md) — plain-text comma-separated tabular data format.
- [CUDA](concepts/CUDA.md) — NVIDIA's GPU parallel-computing platform.
- [CUDA Thread Indexing (`threadIdx` / `blockIdx` / `blockDim`)](concepts/CudaThreadIndex.md) — The built-in per-thread/per-block index variables every [[CUDA]] kernel uses to compute its data slice; the canonical 1-D pattern `int i = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;` is what makes [[SIMT|SIMT]] productive ([[dis-15-1-gpu]]).
- [Data Covariance Matrix](concepts/DataCovarianceMatrix.md) — $\mathbf{S}=\frac{1}{N}\sum\mathbf{x}_n\mathbf{x}_n^\top$ ([[mml-book]] §10.1); SPSD object whose eigenvectors are the principal components, eigenvalues the explained variances. The central object of [[PrincipalComponentAnalysis|PCA]].
- [Dijkstra Shortest-Path Algorithm](concepts/DijkstraAlgorithm.md) — Classical single-source shortest-paths algorithm with nonnegative weights; used as the **recurring worked example** throughout [[parproc-ch04-introduction-to-openmp]] (§4.2 base parallel version, §4.3 `for`+`schedule` refactor, §4.10 quad-core timing scan + fine-tuning that swaps `critical` for `mymins[]` + post-barrier `single`).
- [Curse of Dimensionality](concepts/CurseOfDimensionality.md) — Bellman 1957; the $\geq C\!\cdot\! N^{-1/(2+D)}$ minimax lower bound (Stone 1982) for Lipschitz function approximation; the central obstacle that the [[StructuredRealWorldDistribution]] prior breaks.
- [Data Direction Register (DDR)](concepts/DataDirectionRegister.md) — MCU register selecting per-pin direction (1=output, 0=input). Part of the AVR GPIO triple alongside [[PortRegister|PORTx]] and [[PinRegister|PINx]]; on [[ATmega328P]] one DDR per port (DDRB/DDRC/DDRD) ([[embedded-controllers-fiore]] ch. 18–21).
- [Data Display Debugger (DDD)](concepts/DataDisplayDebugger.md) — GNU graphical front-end that wraps [[GDB]] (and `dbx` / `wdb` / `jdb`) with a click-to-set-breakpoint source view, graphical data-structure visualization (its differentiator — pointer fields drawn as arrows between boxes), and clickable [[GdbBacktrace|stack-frame]] panel. Sends standard GDB commands under the hood; the *"point-and-click"* alternative to terminal-only GDB use ([[dis-3-1-gdb]]).
- [Debug Symbols](concepts/DebugSymbol.md) — DWARF metadata a compiler embeds in an executable so a [[Debugger|source-level debugger]] can map machine addresses ↔ source lines, variable names ↔ stack/register locations, and types ↔ byte layouts. Encodes line-number tables, symbol tables per [[VariableScope|scope]], type tree, function descriptors + unwind info, optionally macros. Produced by [[GccDashG|`gcc -g`]]; consumed by [[GDB]] / [[Objdump]] / [[Valgrind]]. Required for [[GdbPrint|`print var`]] to resolve `var`'s type and location; without DWARF, GDB falls back to address-level inspection. Conventionally stripped from release binaries (`strip`) and archived separately ([[dis-3-1-gdb]]).
- [Debugger](concepts/Debugger.md) — Program-control-of-another-program tool category — *"a program that controls the execution of another program… it allows programmers to see what their programs are doing as they run"* ([[dis-3-1-gdb]]). The defining capabilities: pause execution at [[Breakpoint|breakpoints]], [[StepDebug|single-step]] through source lines, [[GdbPrint|inspect]] variable / register / memory state, switch between [[StackFrame|stack frames]], and analyze [[CoreFile|post-mortem]] dumps. Two bug taxonomies it addresses: **logic bugs** (run-to-completion, wrong output) and **crashes** (typically [[SegmentationFault|segfaults]] in C). Sub-categories: source-level (DWARF-driven, e.g. [[GDB]]) / machine-level / GUI wrapper ([[DataDisplayDebugger|DDD]]) / remote (GDB+[[OpenOCD]] for [[OnChipDebugging|embedded]]). Sits on the OS's [[Ptrace|`ptrace`]] mechanism (named-and-deferred).
- [Custom Layer](concepts/CustomLayer.md) — Subclassing the framework's [[NeuralNetworkModule|module class]] to implement a new operation; parameter-free layers override only `forward`, parameter-carrying layers wrap tensors in `nn.Parameter` ([[d2l-builders-guide]]).
- [d2l Package](concepts/D2LPackage.md) — Lightweight Python utility shipped with [[d2l-preface|*Dive into Deep Learning*]]; `#@save` blocks persist into it as importable helpers.
- [Database](concepts/Database.md) — structured persistent store for transactional or analytical access.
- [Data Drift](concepts/DataDrift.md) — shift in the input distribution P(x) over time.
- [Data Engineering](concepts/DataEngineering.md) — building reliable data ingest, transform, and serving systems.
- [Data Lake](concepts/DataLake.md) — raw-storage architecture without schema-on-write.
- [Data Leakage](concepts/DataLeakage.md) — train-time contamination by information unavailable at inference.
- [Data Lineage](concepts/DataLineage.md) — tracking the provenance of datasets and artifacts.
- [DataLoader](concepts/DataLoader.md) — PyTorch wrapper providing batching, shuffling, and parallel IO.
- [Data Observability](concepts/DataObservability.md) — monitoring data freshness, schema, and distribution.
- [Data Pipeline](concepts/DataPipeline.md) — orchestrated sequence of data transformations.
- [Data Quality](concepts/DataQuality.md) — fitness of data for its intended use.
- [Dataset](concepts/Dataset.md) — collection of training/evaluation examples wrapped by framework abstractions.
- [DataModule](concepts/DataModule.md) — Base class for datasets in the [[d2l-linear-regression|D2L]] OO scaffold; provides `train_dataloader()` / `val_dataloader()`. Inspired by [[PyTorchLightning|Lightning]]'s `LightningDataModule`.
- [Data Splitting](concepts/DataSplitting.md) — partitioning datasets into train, validation, and holdout.
- [Data Warehouse](concepts/DataWarehouse.md) — schema-on-write analytical store optimized for SQL.
- [Decision Making Under Uncertainty](concepts/DecisionMakingUnderUncertainty.md) — Bayesian-decision-theory framing of choosing actions under unknown outcomes (Murphy Ch 5). Justifies the [[ProbabilisticPerspective]] via Dutch-book / Cox / Savage axioms; the operational backbone of reward hacking, IRL, and the [[BystanderEffect]] under social load.
- [Deep Learning](concepts/DeepLearning.md) — Subfield of ML using multi-layer [[NeuralNetwork|neural networks]] trained end-to-end with gradient-based optimization. Subject of [[d2l-preface|*Dive into Deep Learning*]]. *Stub — to be expanded with later D2L chapters.*
- [Decorator (Python)](concepts/Decorator.md) — higher-order function that wraps callables to add behavior.
- [Design Matrix](concepts/DesignMatrix.md) — Matrix $\mathbf{X}\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times D}$ collecting training inputs as rows ([[mml-book]] §9.2); $\boldsymbol\theta_{\text{ML}}=(\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X})^{-1}\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{y}$.
- [Determinant](concepts/Determinant.md) — Signed volume of the column parallelepiped ([[mml-book]] §4.1); tests invertibility; multiplicative under matrix products; basis-invariant.
- [Determinism](concepts/Determinism.md) — identical outputs from identical inputs for reproducibility.
- [Developer Experience](concepts/DeveloperExperience.md) — friction shaping how developers build.
- [Distributed Computing](concepts/DistributedComputing.md) — coordinating work across many machines.
- [Distributed Training](concepts/DistributedTraining.md) — training a model across multiple GPUs/nodes.
- [Distribution Shift](concepts/DistributionShift.md) — Training and test distributions differ. The single largest cause of ML deployment failures; the [[d2l-linear-classification]] anchor for the [[CovariateShift|covariate]] / [[LabelShift|label]] / [[ConceptShift|concept]]-shift taxonomy and importance-weighted [[EmpiricalRiskMinimization|ERM]] correction. Operational detection via [[AlibiDetect]] / [[EvidentlyAI]] / [[TorchDrift]] / [[WhyLogs]].
- [Docstrings](concepts/Docstrings.md) — in-source documentation strings on modules, classes, functions.
- [Documentation](concepts/Documentation.md) — written artifacts explaining how a system works.
- [Double Descent](concepts/DoubleDescent.md) — Non-monotonic test-error curve in over-parametrized regimes (test error ↓ then ↑ at interpolation threshold then ↓ again). Frames why classical complexity bounds fail for deep nets ([[d2l-multilayer-perceptrons]]).
- [Dot Product](concepts/DotProduct.md) — sum of element-wise vector products; core of attention and matmul.
- [DSPy Adapters](concepts/DSPyAdapters.md) — DSPy's **formatting / parsing layer** introduced in [[dspy-adapters]] (page 6 of 13). *"The bridge between `dspy.Predict` and the actual Language Model (LM)."* Three responsibilities: convert a [[DSPySignatures|Signature]] into a system message, format input data (multi-turn messages, demos, conversation history, function calls, and DSPy-special types — [[DSPyTools|`Tool`]] / `dspy.Image` / `dspy.History`) into the LM's request shape, and parse the LM's response into a typed [[DSPyPrediction|`dspy.Prediction`]]. Bound via `dspy.configure(adapter=...)` (global) or `with dspy.context(adapter=...):` (block-local), both thread-safe. Default is `dspy.ChatAdapter` — delimiter-based (`[[ ## field_name ## ]]`), universal compatibility, JSON schemas inlined for non-primitive types, automatic fallback to `JSONAdapter` on parse failure. Alternative `dspy.JSONAdapter` uses the LM's native `response_format` parameter — faster but model-capability-gated (the **first explicit model-capability boundary** in the DSPy *Learn* corpus). Two further built-ins named only on the page: `dspy.XMLAdapter` (XML I/O) and `dspy.TwoStepAdapter` (two-step extract-then-format). Custom adapters supported via `Adapter`-subclass + `format()`/`parse()` override. Two introspection hooks: `adapter.format(signature, demos, inputs)` returns the full multi-turn message list; `adapter.format_system_message(signature)` returns only the system message. The **single funnel** through which every DSPy-typed value crosses into the LM's wire format. The **third** of [[DSPyProgrammingModel|the Programming Model's]] four orthogonal artifacts; resolves the long-standing forward reference carried by every prior DSPy ingest.
- [DSPy Async](concepts/DSPyAsync.md) — DSPy's **framework-wide async-programming surface** introduced in [[dspy-async-tutorial]]. `acall()` is universal on every built-in [[DSPyModules|Module]] ([[DSPyPredict|`dspy.Predict`]] / [[chainofthought|`dspy.ChainOfThought`]] / [[react|`dspy.ReAct`]] / [[DSPyProgramOfThought|`dspy.ProgramOfThought`]] / [[DSPyMultiChainComparison|`dspy.MultiChainComparison`]] / [[DSPyRecursiveLanguageModel|`dspy.RLM`]]); `aforward()` is the async counterpart to `forward()` on custom `dspy.Module` subclasses — a further lift from the [[PyTorch]] *override-the-entry-method* idiom (`forward → aforward` with the async-suffix convention). `tool.acall(...)` for [[DSPyTools|`dspy.Tool`]] async invocation; `allow_tool_async_sync_conversion=True` configurable per-block via `dspy.context(...)` or process-wide via `dspy.configure(...)` for sync code that needs to invoke async tools. **Async DSPy ≠ concurrent DSPy by default** — chained `await predict.acall(...)` calls run **sequentially**; users must reach for `asyncio.gather(...)` to get parallel sub-predictions. Framework-authored sync-vs-async rubric: sync for prototyping / research / small-to-medium apps / debuggability; async for high-QPS services / async-only tools / concurrent requests / production scalability. Async is **orthogonal** to [[DSPyProgrammingModel|the four-concerns decomposition]] — Signatures, Adapters, and Optimizers are unchanged under async dispatch. **Distinct from [[AsyncComputation]]** (GPU-backend dispatch) and [[AsynchronousInference]] (deployment topology) — three orthogonal "async" layers that compose.
- [DSPy Callback (`BaseCallback`)](concepts/DSPyCallback.md) — DSPy's **user-programmable instrumentation interface** — tier 3 of [[DSPyObservability]]. Subclass `dspy.utils.callback.BaseCallback`, override any of six start/end handler pairs (`on_module_*`, `on_lm_*`, `on_adapter_format_*`, `on_adapter_parse_*`, `on_tool_*`, `on_evaluate_*`), and register process-wide via `dspy.configure(callbacks=[...])`. Handler signatures: `*_start(call_id, instance, inputs)` / `*_end(call_id, outputs, exception)` — `call_id` pairs start with end for nested calls; `exception=None` on success.
