Trade-off vs `mlflow.autolog()`: more boilerplate, but arbitrary user logic per event (e.g. filter [[react|ReAct]]'s reasoning steps by checking `instance.signature.__name__ == "Thought"`); two tiers are stackable, not mutually exclusive. First wiki receipt — [[dspy-observability-tutorial]].
- [DSPy Cache](concepts/DSPyCache.md) — DSPy's **framework-wide three-layer caching surface** introduced in [[dspy-cache-tutorial]]. In-memory ([[LRUCache]] via `cachetools.LRUCache`) + on-disk (`diskcache.FanoutCache`) are **enabled by default**; provider-side [[PromptCaching]] is opt-in via `cache_control_injection_points` on [[DSPyLM|`dspy.LM(...)`]]. Single configuration surface `dspy.configure_cache(enable_disk_cache=, enable_memory_cache=, disk_size_limit_bytes=, memory_max_entries=, restrict_pickle=, safe_types=)`. Default `cache_key` hashes **all** litellm request args except credentials — model name is part of the key, so switching models misses by default; override `cache_key`/`get`/`put` on a `dspy.clients.Cache` subclass for custom logic (e.g., hash only `messages` so semantically-equivalent prompts share hits across model versions). Cached calls return `None` for `result.get_lm_usage()` under [[DSPyLM|`track_usage=True`]] because no provider call occurred — and streaming is **disabled by cache hit** per [[DSPyStreaming]]. `restrict_pickle=True` enables an allowlist-based deserializer (LiteLLM/OpenAI response types + NumPy reconstruction helpers + user `safe_types`) defending against arbitrary code execution from tampered on-disk caches; unapproved types degrade to a cache miss with a log entry, not a raised exception. Caching is **orthogonal** to [[DSPyProgrammingModel|the four-concerns decomposition]] — applies uniformly to [[DSPyPredict]] / [[DSPyModules]] / [[DSPyAsync|async]] modules — and pairs with [[DSPyEvaluation]] / [[DSPyOptimization]] where long optimizer runs benefit massively from the disk layer.
- [DSPy Data Handling](concepts/DSPyData.md) — DSPy's **dataset-layer discipline** introduced in [[dspy-data]] (page 10 of 13); the data-collection-and-splitting layer that operationalizes Step 1 of [[DSPyEvaluation|the four-step iterative-evaluation loop]] (*"collect an initial development set"*). Frames DSPy as a machine learning framework that uses the conventional train / dev / test three-set convention (*"DSPy is a machine learning framework, so working in it involves training sets, development sets, and test sets"*); records the three load-bearing commitments — **datasets are plain Python lists** of [[DSPyExample|`dspy.Example`]] (no `Dataset` class, no `train_test_split(...)` helper, no built-in HuggingFace / CSV / JSON loaders — splits are Python slicing; the small-API discipline consistent with [[dspy-modules|*"DSPy is just Python code"*]]); **input/label tagging is attached metadata** ([[DSPyExample|`with_inputs(...)`]]), not a structural `(X, y)` partition (the same `Example` can be re-tagged for different program calls); **inputs-only sufficiency** — *"You can use DSPy effectively without any intermediate or final labels, but you will need at least a few example inputs"* — the data-side mirror of [[dspy-evaluation-overview|the Evaluation Overview's]] *intermediate-step labels are almost never needed* commitment. Three per-example value types — *inputs, intermediate labels, final label* — whose required shape depends on the [[DSPyMetrics|metric]] (reference-free needs inputs only; reference-based needs inputs + final labels). The canonical idiom for converting external data is `[dspy.Example(**row).with_inputs("field") for row in source]`; [[HuggingFace]] is the primary public-dataset source named in the *"adjacent public datasets"* sourcing option. The dataset-collection layer; pairs with [[DSPyExample]] (the per-datapoint primitive).
- [DSPy Evaluation](concepts/DSPyEvaluation.md) — DSPy's **middle stage** in the [[dspy-learn-index|three-stage Programming → Evaluation → Optimization]] workflow, canonical source [[dspy-evaluation-overview]] (page 9 of 13). The measurement discipline that turns a runnable DSPy program (Programming-stage output) into a **measurable, comparable, optimizable artifact** (Optimization-stage input). Three reusable deliverables: a **development set** (20–200 worked examples), a **metric** (a callable `(example, prediction) -> score` — scalar for simple tasks, a [[DSPyModules|`dspy.Module`]] for long-form tasks), and a **baseline score** (the metric on the dev set under the current unoptimized program). Operationalized as a **four-step iterative loop**: collect dev set → define metric → run development evaluations → (recursively) optimize the metric when it is itself a DSPy program. Three load-bearing framework commitments: *small dev sets are sufficient* (*"Even 20 input examples of your task can be useful, though 200 goes a long way"* — Evaluation is **diagnostic**, not training), *intermediate-step labels are almost never needed* (the metric scores final outputs only — DSPy's structural answer to the intermediate-supervision problem in chain-of-thought training), *the metric is itself iterative* (the [[DSPyProgrammingModel|"start simple, then grow"]] discipline restated at the metric layer; the metric has versions over the project's lifetime). The **recursive-self-improvement** claim — when the metric is a DSPy program, optimizing the metric itself becomes easy because the metric's output is bounded and scalar — is structurally novel relative to other LLM-evaluation frameworks the wiki has recorded. Sits between [[DSPyProgrammingModel]] (Programming stage) and [[DSPyOptimizers]] (Optimization stage); the metric is the **interface contract** between them. Specializes the general [[ModelEvaluation]] concept; operates in the [[OfflineEvaluation]] regime ([[OnlineEvaluation]] is out of scope). Forward references to [[DSPyData]] (page 10, will expand Step 1) and [[DSPyMetrics]] (page 11, will expand Step 2) — both owned by sibling ingests.
- [DSPy Evaluate](concepts/DSPyEvaluate.md) — DSPy's **dev-set-evaluation utility** `dspy.Evaluate` (`from dspy.evaluate import Evaluate`) introduced in [[dspy-metrics]] (page 11 of 13); a reusable thread-parallel harness that runs a [[DSPyMetrics|metric]] over a [[DSPyData|dataset]] under a [[DSPyModules|program]]. Constructor binds the dev set + ergonomic kwargs (`devset=YOUR_DEVSET`, `num_threads=...`, `display_progress=...`, `display_table=N`) once; the call invokes with `(program, metric)` pairs — *"the evaluator can be re-used in your code"* — so the same instance compares multiple candidate programs against the same dev set with the same metric. Equivalent under the hood to the raw `for x in devset: pred = program(**x.inputs()); score = metric(x, pred)` loop, with thread-pool parallelism + TQDM-style progress bar + `display_table=N` tabular sample of inputs/outputs/scores. **Always calls metrics with `trace=None`** — the `trace is not None` regime is reserved for the [[DSPyOptimizers|Optimizer's]] bootstrap phase. The Step-3 harness in [[DSPyEvaluation|the four-step Evaluation loop]]: produces the **baseline score** (numeric) + the **qualitative diagnostic** (tabular display) the loop's Step 3 commits to.
- [DSPy Example](concepts/DSPyExample.md) — DSPy's **data-side primitive** introduced in [[dspy-data]] (page 10 of 13); the typed Python dict-with-utilities that holds a single datapoint in a training / development / test set. *"The core data type for data in DSPy is `Example`."* Four-method API: construction (`dspy.Example(field1=v1, field2=v2, ...)` with arbitrary field names and value types — no enforced schema, the [[DSPySignatures|Signature]] supplies the schema), dot-notation access (`ex.field_name` — the same convention [[DSPyPrediction|`dspy.Prediction`]] uses), `with_inputs("field", ...)` input-tagging (returns a **new** `Example` whose attached `input_keys` set tags the named fields; non-mutating; warn-not-fail — *"be careful about marking your labels as inputs, unless you mean it"*), and `inputs()` / `labels()` non-destructive partition accessors (return new `Example`s containing only input or only non-input fields). The structurally important inheritance: **[[DSPyPrediction|`dspy.Prediction`]] is a subclass of `Example`** — *"Your DSPy modules will return values of the type `Prediction`, which is a special sub-class of `Example`"* — which makes the [[DSPyMetrics|metric]]'s `(example, prediction) -> score` contract **type-symmetric** (both arguments share the same dot-access / `inputs()` / `labels()` surface; a metric written for one works on the other). Datasets are plain `list[dspy.Example]`; train/dev/test splits are Python slicing. The data-side primitive paired with [[DSPyPredict|`dspy.Predict`]] (the strategy-side minimal primitive). Pairs with [[DSPyData]] (the dataset-layer discipline). **Resolves the long-standing forward reference** carried by [[DSPyEvaluation]] / [[dspy-evaluation-overview]] since the Evaluation stage opened on page 9.
- [DSPy LM](concepts/DSPyLM.md) — DSPy's universal **LM-client abstraction** introduced in [[dspy-language-models]]. A single class — `dspy.LM(provider/model-name, api_key=..., **kwargs)` — wraps every supported provider behind one initializer signature; routes provider plumbing through [[LiteLLM]] under the hood; bound to the rest of the program via thread-safe `dspy.configure(lm=...)` (global) or `with dspy.context(lm=...):` (block-local). Spans three deployment regimes with the same API: managed ([[openai|OpenAI]] / [[anthropic|Anthropic]] / [[gemini|Gemini]] / [[Databricks]] / [[Anyscale]] / [[TogetherAI|Together AI]] / [[microsoft|Azure]]), self-hosted GPU ([[SGLang]]), local laptop ([[Ollama]]). Adds default-on caching, `rollout_id` deterministic cache-busting, per-call `lm.history` telemetry, and a `model_type="responses"` opt-in for the OpenAI Responses API. The concrete operationalization of [[DSPyProgrammingModel|the Programming Model's]] *"swap the LM without changing the rest of your logic"* portability claim.
- [DSPy Majority](concepts/DSPyMajority.md) — DSPy's **function-style vote aggregator** introduced in [[dspy-modules]]. *"Can do basic voting to return the most popular response from a set of predictions."* Zero LM cost; pure Python over a collection of [[DSPyPrediction|`Prediction`]] objects; **the only built-in that does not take a [[DSPySignatures|Signature]]**. Decision rule is syntactic equality of the output field(s); the comparison-not-vote counterpart is [[DSPyMultiChainComparison|`dspy.MultiChainComparison`]] which costs one extra LM call but can adjudicate semantically-equivalent-but-syntactically-different outputs.
- [DSPy Metrics](concepts/DSPyMetrics.md) — DSPy's **canonical metric contract** introduced in [[dspy-metrics]] (page 11 of 13). *"A DSPy metric is just a function in Python that takes `example` (e.g., from your training or dev set) and the output `pred` from your DSPy program, and outputs a `float` (or `int` or `bool`) score."* The function signature is `(example, pred, trace=None) -> float | int | bool`. **Type-symmetric on the data side**: because [[DSPyPrediction|`Prediction`]] is a subclass of [[DSPyExample|`Example`]] ([[dspy-data|page 10]]), the metric author writes `example.answer == pred.answer` with no class-aware branching. **Regime-asymmetric on the calling side**: the optional third argument `trace` is the **dual-purpose mechanism** — `trace is None` returns a continuous `float`/`int` for [[DSPyEvaluate|`dspy.Evaluate`]] / [[DSPyOptimizers|Optimizer]] evaluation passes; `trace is not None` returns a strict `bool` for bootstrap demo selection (only top-scoring trajectories become few-shot demonstrations). **Two regimes**: *simple metrics* (one-line scalar comparisons like `example.answer.lower() == pred.answer.lower()`, plus built-ins `dspy.evaluate.metrics.answer_exact_match` and `dspy.evaluate.metrics.answer_passage_match`) for short-form tasks; *AI-feedback metrics* (a `class Assess(dspy.Signature)` rubric template plus N `dspy.Predict(Assess)` invocations summed and thresholded) for long-form tasks — **DSPy's structural operationalization of the [[llmasjudge|LLM-as-judge]] pattern** (the judge is a typed Signature, not a hand-written prompt; the judge composes with the rest of DSPy the same way every other [[DSPyModules|Module]] does; the judge is optimizable by [[DSPyOptimizers|Optimizers]]). The canonical hybrid pattern combines **multi-property AI judgment** with **deterministic hard gates** (`len(tweet) <= 280` mixed with two `Predict(Assess)` outputs) — the wiki's first explicit demonstration that a DSPy metric is **not all-or-nothing AI-feedback**; the deterministic gate is a [[LLMModuloFramework|*sound* critic]], the LM-judged dimensions are *soft* critics. The `trace`-aware `validate_hops` bootstrap recipe inspects intermediate predictor outputs (`[outputs.query for *_, outputs in trace if 'query' in outputs]`) — the only intermediate-step validator in the *Learn* corpus so far, bootstrap-only because *"DSPy will not try to track the steps of your program"* during plain evaluation. **Recursive-metric-optimization** (Step 4 of [[DSPyEvaluation|the Evaluation loop]]) is operationalized — the AI-feedback metric is itself a DSPy program (calls `dspy.Predict(Assess)`) and therefore optimizable by an [[DSPyOptimizers|Optimizer]] the same way the system program is; the *"metric of the metric"* is easier to define because the metric's output is bounded and scalar. The metric is the **interface contract between the Evaluation and Optimization stages** — the only signal an Optimizer climbs. **Resolves the long-standing forward reference [[DSPyMetrics]]** carried by [[DSPyEvaluation]] / [[dspy-evaluation-overview]] / [[dspy-data]] / [[DSPyExample]] / [[DSPyPrediction]] / [[DSPyModules]] / [[DSPyProgrammingModel]] / every prior DSPy ingest since the corpus opened on 2026-05-17.
- [DSPy Modules](concepts/DSPyModules.md) — DSPy's **swappable-strategy abstraction** introduced in [[dspy-modules]] (page 5 of 13). *"A DSPy module is a building block for programs that use LMs"*, generalized over any [[DSPySignatures|Signature]], with learnable parameters (instructions + demonstrations + LM-weight references) and PyTorch-shaped `__init__` + `forward(...)` composition (*"inspired directly by NN modules in PyTorch"*). Seven built-ins: [[DSPyPredict|`dspy.Predict`]] (minimal primitive — *"all other DSPy modules are built using `dspy.Predict`"*), [[ChainOfThought|`dspy.ChainOfThought`]] (adds `reasoning`), [[DSPyProgramOfThought|`dspy.ProgramOfThought`]] (output-code-then-execute), [[react|`dspy.ReAct`]] (tool-using agent via `tools=[...]`), [[DSPyMultiChainComparison|`dspy.MultiChainComparison`]] (N-CoT + LM comparison), [[DSPyRecursiveLanguageModel|`dspy.RLM`]] (recursive sub-LLM calls in a sandboxed REPL for over-context cases), and function-style [[DSPyMajority|`dspy.majority`]]. Composes via `class MyProgram(dspy.Module)` with sub-modules as `self.*` attributes (enumerated by `named_predictors()` / `named_parameters()` for [[DSPyOptimizers|Optimizer]] consumption); composition is *plain Python control flow*. Returns [[DSPyPrediction|`dspy.Prediction(...)`]] carrying output fields as attributes plus `get_lm_usage()` cost-accounting telemetry (DSPy 2.6.16+). The **second** of [[DSPyProgrammingModel|the Programming Model's]] four orthogonal artifacts; resolves the long-standing forward reference carried by every prior DSPy ingest.
- [DSPy MCP Integration](concepts/DSPyMCP.md) — DSPy's **framework-specific binding** to the [[ModelContextProtocol|Model Context Protocol]], introduced in [[dspy-mcp]] (page 8 of 13). Rests on a single class-method — `dspy.Tool.from_mcp_tool(session, tool)` — that converts an MCP-side tool descriptor (from `await session.list_tools()`) into a [[DSPyTools|`dspy.Tool`]] instance whose execution callback routes asynchronously back through the open `mcp.ClientSession`. The conversion preserves the MCP tool's name, description, and parameter schema; the resulting `dspy.Tool` is **indistinguishable** from a locally-built one — it composes through [[react|`dspy.ReAct`]], through manual [[DSPyPredict|`dspy.Predict`]] with `tools: list[dspy.Tool]` input, and through direct `tool.acall(...)` invocation. DSPy does **not** manage MCP connections — the user opens the session via the `mcp` Python SDK (stdio via `stdio_client` + `StdioServerParameters`, or streamable HTTP via `streamablehttp_client`); DSPy's contribution is the conversion layer. Three operational constraints: (1) use `.acall(...)`, not the sync form (MCP execution is async end-to-end); (2) the agent invocation must live *inside* the `async with` session block (closing the session invalidates further tool calls); (3) the toolset is fixed for the lifetime of the session unless `list_tools()` is re-issued. Installation: `pip install -U "dspy[mcp]"`. The split between [[DSPyMCP]] (this page) and [[ModelContextProtocol]] (the protocol itself) mirrors the [[LiteLLM]] / [[DSPyLM]] precedent — protocol/library upstream + framework-binding downstream.
- [DSPy MultiChainComparison](concepts/DSPyMultiChainComparison.md) — DSPy built-in [[DSPyModules|Module]] from [[dspy-modules]]. *"Can compare multiple outputs from `ChainOfThought` to produce a final prediction."* Runs N `dspy.ChainOfThought` samples over the same Signature (typically at higher `temperature` for variance) plus a final [[DSPyPredict|`dspy.Predict`]] that compares the N candidates. The LM-comparison counterpart to [[DSPyMajority|`dspy.majority`]]'s syntactic vote; strictly more expressive but pays one extra LM call. DSPy-side equivalent of the *self-consistency-with-LM-aggregator* pattern.
- [DSPy Observability](concepts/DSPyObservability.md) — DSPy's **three-tier observability stack** for debugging program execution, consolidated by [[dspy-observability-tutorial]]. Tier 1: [[InspectHistory|`dspy.inspect_history(n=N)`]] — zero-dep print of last *N* LM calls (LM-only, no metadata, no call-tree). Tier 2: [[MLflow]] autolog (`mlflow.autolog()` or `mlflow.dspy.autolog(...)`) — full trace tree across [[DSPyModules|Modules]] / [[DSPyLM|LMs]] / retrievers / [[DSPyTools|tools]], with timing and parent/child structure; the autolog hook walks `self.*` sub-module attributes set in `__init__`, so plain-function pipelines outside a `dspy.Module` are invisible (one of two operational reasons the framework recommends "putting your logic with a custom module"). Tier 3: [[DSPyCallback|`BaseCallback`]] — user-programmable instrumentation via six start/end handler pairs + `dspy.configure(callbacks=[...])`. The three tiers are **additive, not mutually exclusive**. Establishes the canonical retrieval-staleness diagnosis pattern: outputs that look fluent at the LM layer can be stale-retriever bugs invisible without trace-UI inspection of the retriever span (Shohei Ohtani / [[ColBERTv2]] / [[Tavily]] worked example).
- [DSPy Inspect History](concepts/InspectHistory.md) — DSPy's **tier-1 observability** utility — `dspy.inspect_history(n=N)`. Zero-dep print of the last *N* LM calls to stdout; prompt as-rendered and response. Three documented limitations motivate the upgrade to tier 2 ([[MLflow]] autolog): LM-only (no [[DSPyTools|tool]] / retriever / [[DSPyAdapters|adapter]] coverage), no metadata (latency / module names / parent-child structure), ambiguous ordering under nested predictions. Survives despite the limitations because it is zero-friction (no install, no server, no code change) and faithful to the wire (shows exactly the prompt as sent). Distinct from [[DSPyLM|`dspy.LM.history`]] (per-client wire log) and [[DSPyHistory|`dspy.History`]] (Signature field type for conversation history) despite the shared word.
- [DSPy Optimization](concepts/DSPyOptimization.md) — DSPy's **third-stage workflow concept** introduced in [[dspy-optimization-overview]] (page 12 of 13); the canonical anchor for the **optimization workflow** in the [[dspy-learn-index|three-stage Programming → Evaluation → Optimization]] model. *"Once you have a system and a way to evaluate it, you can use DSPy optimizers to tune the prompts or weights in your program."* The **three-input, one-output contract**: a [[DSPyModules|`dspy.Module`]] program + a `(example, pred, trace=None) -> score` [[DSPyMetrics|metric]] + a `list[dspy.Example]` training set → an **optimized program** (same `dspy.Module` subclass, refined instructions / demonstrations / weight references). The **training-set size regime**: *"You can often get substantial value out of 30 examples, but aim for at least 300 examples"* — explicitly larger than [[DSPyEvaluation|the Evaluation stage's]] 20–200-example dev-set regime; the 30–300 progression mirrors the *"start simple, then grow"* discipline at the training-set layer. The **inverted 20/80 train/validation split** for most prompt optimizers — *"For most prompt optimizers, we recommend allocating 20% of your data for training and 80% for validation, contrary to typical deep learning conventions. This is because prompt optimizers tend to overfit on small training sets"* — a DSPy-specific defense against a DSPy-specific failure mode, not a universal rule. The **[[GEPA]] carve-out** — the only specific optimizer named on [[dspy-optimization-overview|the Overview page]], and only to disclose that GEPA *"follows standard ML practice — maximizing the training set size while keeping the validation set sufficiently sized to represent the downstream task distribution"*. The **four iteration axes** — data / program structure / metric / optimizer-choice — three of which point **back into the Programming and Evaluation stages**, making Optimization an *open-under-revision* stage rather than a black-box terminus; *"Iterative development is key. DSPy gives you the pieces to do that incrementally."* The **fourth artifact** of [[DSPyProgrammingModel|the Programming Model]] (Signature / Adapter / Module / Optimizer) at the workflow level — completes the four-artifact picture alongside [[DSPyEvaluation|Evaluation]] as the connective stage between Programming and Optimization. The split between [[DSPyOptimization]] (workflow / this page) and [[DSPyOptimizers]] (catalog / page 13, forward reference) mirrors the [[DSPyEvaluation]] / [[DSPyMetrics]] precedent — one page anchors the workflow, the sibling anchors the per-algorithm machinery (`BootstrapFewShot`, `BootstrapFewShotWithRandomSearch`, `MIPROv2`, `BootstrapFinetune`, [[GEPA]], etc.).
- [DSPy History](concepts/DSPyHistory.md) — [[DSPy]]'s [[DSPySignatures|Signature]] field type for conversation history, minted by [[dspy-conversation-history]]. A DSPy-special type (tier five in the [[DSPySignatures|Signatures]] type system, alongside [[DSPyImage|`dspy.Image`]]) with a single attribute `messages: list[dict[str, Any]]` — each entry a dict of input + output field values for one prior turn. Declared on a Signature as `history: dspy.History = dspy.InputField()`; instantiated at runtime as `dspy.History(messages=[])`; appended via `history.messages.append({"question": question, **outputs})` per turn. Three structural properties: **developer-owned lifecycle** (DSPy does **not** automate history management — `dspy.Module` has no built-in inter-turn state capture), **first-class field type** (composes through every [[DSPy]] mechanism — [[DSPyPredict|`dspy.Predict`]], [[ChainOfThought|`dspy.ChainOfThought`]], [[react|`dspy.ReAct`]], [[DSPyExample|`dspy.Example`]], [[DSPyEvaluate|`dspy.Evaluate`]], [[DSPyOptimizers|Optimizers]]), and **single-turn JSON rendering under [[BootstrapFewShot|few-shot]] demos** (the entire `messages` list serializes as JSON inside one demo turn, not expanded into multiple `role=user`/`role=assistant` pairs — *"to maintain compatibility with the OpenAI standard format"*). The most literal instance of *lookup* memory in [[DSPy]] — inherits the [[2604.27707-agentic-memory-is-a-memo|Ω(k²) generalization gap + prompt-injection]] limitations of flat append-only conversation memory.
- [Customer Service Agent](concepts/CustomerServiceAgent.md) — The general application pattern for single-LM-agent multi-tool deployments with a typed domain model, minted by [[dspy-customer-service-agent]]. Five structural elements: (i) **typed domain model** (Pydantic / structured types for users, transactions, tickets, nested at any depth); (ii) **tool list** split into three categories — *lookup* (read-only, safe to retry), *mutation* (state-changing, requires [[DSPyAssert|hard-constraint]] gating), *escalation* (handoff to human as the [[LLMModuloFramework|LLM-Modulo]] safety valve); (iii) **two-field [[DSPySignatures|Signature]]** (`user_request: str` → `process_result: str`) with docstring as the agent's system instruction and `OutputField(desc=...)` scoping what the response must contain; (iv) **[[react|`dspy.ReAct`]] (or analogous) Module** driving the think-act-observe loop; (v) **trajectory log** for introspection via `dspy.inspect_history()`. The smallest agent shape with mutation — sits between read-only information agents ([[CoSTORM]]) and trajectory-shaped multi-step decision systems; **production deployments at this rung dominate enterprise LM applications** (support bots, booking assistants, e-commerce help, IT helpdesks). The reference instantiation is the [[dspy-customer-service-agent|airline customer-service agent]]: 7 tools / 5 Pydantic types / 1 two-field Signature / `dspy.ReAct` Module. Documents the **hard-constraint gap**: a production deployment must wrap every mutation tool with [[DSPyAssert|`dspy.Assert`]] preconditions (date in future, origin ≠ destination, user has email for confirmation) to prevent the agent from silently creating invalid records — the agent-pattern realization of the [[2402.01817-llm-modulo|LLM-Modulo]] sound-critic principle. Multi-turn variants compose with the [[ConversationHistory|conversation-history pattern]] (`history: dspy.History` added to the Signature).
- [Conversation History](concepts/ConversationHistory.md) — The general LM-application concept the [[DSPyHistory|DSPy primitive]] operationalizes, minted alongside it by [[dspy-conversation-history]]. The **inter-turn state** of a multi-turn LM application — the sequence of prior `(input, output)` pairs the model conditions on for coherence across turns. Structurally, the application owns the lifecycle (capture / persist / re-inject) because the LM is stateless and the framework cannot supply application-policy decisions (when to construct, append, truncate, persist, discard). Documents DSPy's **single-turn JSON rendering** for [[BootstrapFewShot|few-shot]] demos as a **conscious structural trade-off** (compact envelopes + OpenAI-standard-format compatibility wins over conversational role-cue preservation). Places conversation history at rung 3 of the LM-application complexity ladder: stateless single call → module-local single call → **multi-turn conversation** ([[DSPyHistory]]) → tool-using agent ([[react|ReAct]]) → multi-agent collaborative discourse ([[CoSTORM]]) → long-horizon compound system ([[2407.10930-better-together|BetterTogether]] / [[2507.19457-gepa|GEPA]]). Records the [[2604.27707-agentic-memory-is-a-memo|*"agentic memory is lookup, not memory"*]] tension and the resulting limitations of flat-list history (no compression, no selective recall, no isolation against prompt injection).
- [DSPy Optimizers](concepts/DSPyOptimizers.md) — DSPy's **catalog-level concept** for the third-stage [[DSPyOptimization|Optimization]] family — the canonical anchor minted by [[dspy-optimizers]] (page 13 of 13 of the *Learn* corpus); the **catalog-level sibling** of [[DSPyOptimization]] (workflow vs catalog, mirroring [[DSPyEvaluation]] / [[DSPyMetrics]]). Each optimizer is a callable surfaced under the `dspy.<OptimizerName>` namespace ([[BootstrapFewShot|`dspy.BootstrapFewShot`]], [[MIPROv2|`dspy.MIPROv2`]], [[GEPA|`dspy.GEPA`]], [[BootstrapFinetune|`dspy.BootstrapFinetune`]], etc.) implementing the same `Optimizer(metric=..., **config).compile(program, trainset=...) -> optimized_program` interface, but with different search strategies and data-budget contracts. The framework's prior name for the family is **"teleprompters"** — *"Formerly called teleprompters. We are making an official name update."* Three orthogonal **what-it-tunes** axes (demonstrations / instructions / LM weights). Five families: **Automatic Few-Shot Learning** (`LabeledFewShot`, [[BootstrapFewShot]], [[BootstrapFewShotWithRandomSearch]], `KNNFewShot`), **Automatic Instruction Optimization** (`COPRO`, [[MIPROv2]], `SIMBA`, [[GEPA]]), **Automatic Finetuning** ([[BootstrapFinetune]]), **Program Transformations** (`Ensemble`), **Meta-Optimizers** (`BetterTogether`). [[MIPROv2]]'s three-stage decomposition (bootstrapping → grounded proposal → discrete search via [[BayesianOptimization|Bayesian Optimization]]) is the **structural template** for non-trivial DSPy optimizers — every algorithm in the catalog occupies a position in the (collect, propose, search) three-step space. **Composability**: optimizers are first-class composable units — *"You can run `dspy.MIPROv2` and use the produced program as an input to `dspy.MIPROv2` again or, say, to `dspy.BootstrapFinetune` ... This is partly the essence of `dspy.BetterTogether`"* — sequential composition (`BetterTogether`'s prompt → weight → prompt schedule) and ensemble composition (top-k extraction → `dspy.Ensemble` for inference-time voting). DSPy can scale **both** *pre-inference-time compute* (the optimizer's budget) and *inference-time compute* (the ensemble's vote) from a single optimizer run — structurally novel relative to `sklearn.GridSearchCV`-style ML hyperparameter optimization. **Save/load** produces plain-text JSON (`optimized_program.save(path)`) — the optimizer's output is inspectable, not opaque, consistent with the *"writing code instead of strings"* discipline. **Resolves the long-standing forward reference [[DSPyOptimizers]]** carried by every prior DSPy ingest since the corpus opened on 2026-05-17.
- [DSPy Predict](concepts/DSPyPredict.md) — DSPy's **minimal primitive [[DSPyModules|Module]]** from [[dspy-modules]]. *"Basic predictor. Does not modify the signature."* The substrate every other built-in Module is built on top of — *"Internally, all other DSPy modules are built using `dspy.Predict`"*. Stores instructions + demonstrations + LM-weight updates (the learnable-parameter store [[DSPyOptimizers|Optimizers]] tune). Two-step usage: declare with a [[DSPySignatures|Signature]] (+ config kwargs), then call with input arguments by name. Generation parameters can be set at declare time as defaults or per-call via the `config={...}` kwarg.
- [DSPy Prediction](concepts/DSPyPrediction.md) — DSPy's **typed return object** from [[dspy-modules]]. Every [[DSPyModules|Module]] call returns a `dspy.Prediction(...)` exposing the calling Module's expanded-Signature output fields as attributes (e.g. `response.reasoning` + `response.answer` for [[ChainOfThought|`dspy.ChainOfThought`]]'s injected `reasoning` field). From DSPy 2.6.16, carries the `get_lm_usage()` cost-accounting telemetry method returning `{provider/model: {prompt/completion/total tokens + details}}` aggregated across **every** LM call inside `forward()`, with cached responses returning `{}` per [[LiteLLM]]'s cache discipline. The contract user-defined `class MyProgram(dspy.Module)` subclasses must honor on return — `return dspy.Prediction(notes=notes, titles=titles)` — to compose with the rest of the framework.
- [DSPy ProgramOfThought](concepts/DSPyProgramOfThought.md) — DSPy built-in [[DSPyModules|Module]] from [[dspy-modules]]. *"Teaches the LM to output code, whose execution results will dictate the response."* The code-execution counterpart to [[ChainOfThought|`dspy.ChainOfThought`]]; routes the LM's reasoning step through *executable Python* rather than prose. Built-in **sound critic** in the [[LLMModuloFramework|LLM-Modulo]] sense — code execution is deterministic adjudication. [[dspy-programming-overview|The Programming Overview]] names `dspy.ChainOfThought` ↔ `dspy.ProgramOfThought` as a canonical swap-without-touching-signature portability example.
- [DSPy Programming Model](concepts/DSPyProgrammingModel.md) — The *writing-code-instead-of-strings* design philosophy of [[DSPy]] introduced by [[dspy-programming-overview]]. Factors a "conventional prompt" into **four orthogonal concerns** — [[DSPySignatures|signature]] (typed I/O), [[DSPyAdapters|adapter]] (formatting / parsing), [[DSPyModules|module]] logic (strategy: CoT / [[react|ReAct]] / tool use), and [[DSPyOptimizers|optimization]] (search over instructions / demos / weights) — and gives each one a named, swappable API artifact. Yields three portability claims: swap LM/adapter without touching the rest, swap modules without touching signatures, run prompt-tuning *or* weight-tuning against the same program. Pairs with the "start simple, then grow" discipline (recommended starting point: a single `dspy.ChainOfThought` module).
- [DSPy Recursive Language Model](concepts/DSPyRecursiveLanguageModel.md) — DSPy built-in [[DSPyModules|Module]] from [[dspy-modules]]. *"`dspy.RLM`: A Recursive Language Model that explores large contexts through a sandboxed Python REPL with recursive sub-LLM calls. Use when context is too large to fit in the prompt effectively."* DSPy's framework-level answer to **context-overflow** — recursion is a first-class strategy, not a model-side problem; the sandboxed Python REPL is the execution boundary that contains the LM's exploration. Distinct from RAG ([[ChainOfThought|`dspy.ChainOfThought`]] over `'context, question -> response'` with retrieval) and from summarize-then-answer.
- [DSPy Saving](concepts/DSPySaving.md) — DSPy's **framework-wide two-mode program-persistence surface** introduced in [[dspy-saving-tutorial]]. Two modes selected by the `save_program` flag on `Module.save(...)`: **state-only** (`save_program=False`; signature + demos + configurable attributes only; architecture **reconstructed in code** before `loaded.load(path)`; `.json` default for inspectability — the path every prior `optimized_program.save(...)` wiki receipt exercises — or `.pkl` fallback for non-JSON-native types like [[DSPyImage|`dspy.Image`]] / `datetime`, gated by `allow_pickle=True` on load) and **whole-program** (`save_program=True`, **`dspy>=2.6.0`**; architecture + state + dependency-version metadata serialized via [[Cloudpickle|`cloudpickle`]] into a **directory**, recovered by the top-level `dspy.load(path)` with no reconstruction step). `modules_to_serialize=[...]` opt-in invokes `cloudpickle.register_pickle_by_value(...)` for **by-value** custom-module serialization — class definitions travel with the artifact instead of being import-resolved at load time, the canonical pattern for shipping a custom-Module program to a deployment target that does not have the saving-side code installed. Three operational subtleties: **JSON state-only flattens demos to `dict`** (not [[DSPyExample|`dspy.Example`]] — pickle and whole-program modes preserve identity); **state-only `.json` is the only inspectable mode** (the *"cat it to read the prompt"* discipline from [[DSPyOptimizers]] only applies here); **whole-program pickles the bound LM reference** — the load-side environment must have credentials or reconfigure the LM after load. **Backward-compatibility posture**: pre-3.0.0 carries an explicit *"no guarantee of backward compatibility across DSPy versions"* — pin DSPy versions in production; re-run [[DSPyOptimizers|Optimizers]] on version upgrades; the whole-program directory's recorded dependency version is the load-side BC-check anchor for the future-3.0.0+ guarantee. Pickle-safety pattern is **complementary** to [[DSPyCache|`restrict_pickle=True`]] — Saving opts for an **explicit user flag** (`allow_pickle=True`), Cache opts for an **allowlist-based deserializer**; both target the same arbitrary-code-execution risk and both endorse JSON as the safer default. Sibling-axis concept to [[DSPyCache]] / [[DSPyAsync]] / [[DSPyStreaming]] / [[DSPyObservability]] — all production-shape surfaces orthogonal to the [[DSPyProgrammingModel|four-concerns decomposition]]; pairs with [[MLflow]] as the *plain-file* counterpart to the [[dspy-optimizer-tracking-tutorial|MLflow-wrapped]] provenance-bearing persistence path (`mlflow.dspy.log_model(...)` wraps these primitives) and underpins the [[dspy-deployment-tutorial|Deployment tutorial's]] `mlflow models serve` path.
- [DSPy Tools](concepts/DSPyTools.md) — DSPy's **typed wrapper around a Python function the [[DSPyLM|LM]] can invoke** — `dspy.Tool` — and the matching `dspy.ToolCalls` model-output type, introduced in [[dspy-tools]] (page 7 of 13). `dspy.Tool` exposes `.name` (from `__name__`), `.desc` (from docstring), `.args` (from type hints + defaults), and `str(tool)` (the canonical text the LM sees). `dspy.ToolCalls` carries the LM's requested invocations back into Python; each `call.execute(...)` resolves the requested tool against the calling scope, an explicit `functions={"name": fn}` dict, or an explicit `functions=[dspy.Tool(fn)]` list (**DSPy 3.0.4b2+**). Two equal-status approaches: fully-managed via [[react|`dspy.ReAct`]] (framework-owned think-act-observe loop; returned [[DSPyPrediction|`Prediction`]] carries a `trajectory` field) and manual via [[DSPyPredict|`dspy.Predict`]] over a Signature with `tools: list[dspy.Tool]` input + `dspy.ToolCalls` output. Native function calling is per-[[DSPyAdapters|Adapter]] via `use_native_function_calling=` (defaults: [[DSPyAdapters|`ChatAdapter`]]=`False`, [[DSPyAdapters|`JSONAdapter`]]=`True`; automatic fallback to text-parsing for models that don't support it — the **second model-capability scoping** in the Learn corpus). Async tools first-class via `tool.acall(...)` + `dspy.context(allow_tool_async_sync_conversion=True)` sync-from-async opt-in. The fifth DSPy-special type (after `dspy.Image` / `dspy.History` / `dspy.Prediction` / Signature-input types). Resolves the long-standing forward reference carried by every prior DSPy ingest.
- [DSPy Streaming](concepts/DSPyStreaming.md) — DSPy's **framework-wide token-and-status streaming surface** introduced in [[dspy-streaming-tutorial]]. `dspy.streamify(program, stream_listeners=[...])` wraps any [[DSPyModules|`dspy.Module`]] into a generator (async by default, sync via `async_streaming=False`); `dspy.streaming.StreamListener(signature_field_name=..., allow_reuse=False, predict=None, predict_name=None)` pulls a single `str`-typed [[DSPySignatures|Signature]] output from the LM token side-channel, yielding `StreamResponse(predict_name, signature_field_name, chunk)` envelopes; `dspy.streaming.StatusMessageProvider` is a six-hook subclass-and-override surface (`lm_start/end`, `module_start/end`, `tool_start/end`) emitting `StatusMessage(message=...)` lifecycle events on the **same generator**. **Sidecar architecture** — the LM is the producer, the side channel is buffered, the user-declared listeners are consumers; the program's structure is unchanged. **The [[DSPyAdapters|Adapter]] is in the streaming loop** — field-boundary detection depends on adapter wire format ([[DSPyAdapters|`ChatAdapter`]] delimiter vs [[DSPyAdapters|`JSONAdapter`]] JSON shape). Three structural constraints: streamed field must be `str`-typed (the [[DSPySignatures|five-tier type system]] collapses to one tier for streaming — container / [[Pydantic]] / nested / DSPy-special types ([[DSPyHistory|`dspy.History`]], `dspy.Image`) are not streamable); chunks are buffered until field finalization (last chunk usually multi-token); cache hits bypass token streaming (only the final [[DSPyPrediction|`Prediction`]] arrives). `predict_name` comes from `named_predictors()` — promoted from [[DSPyOptimizers|Optimizer]]-internal enumeration to the **public stream-identity surface**; dotted paths for nested sub-Modules (`'predict.predict'` for [[DSPyPredict|`dspy.Predict`]] inside [[chainofthought|`dspy.ChainOfThought`]] inside outer module). Consumer routes a three-type union: `StreamResponse | StatusMessage | Prediction`. `allow_reuse=True` unlocks per-iteration streaming inside [[react|`dspy.ReAct`]]'s loop (canonical target: the implicit `next_thought` field). Sibling-axis concept to [[DSPyAsync]] — both are production-shaped surfaces over the same async-native [[LiteLLM]] substrate; both orthogonal to the [[DSPyProgrammingModel|four-concerns decomposition]]; both default to async transport.
- [DSPy Signatures](concepts/DSPySignatures.md) — DSPy's **declarative input/output specification** introduced in [[dspy-signatures]] (page 4 of 13). *"A signature is a declarative specification of input/output behavior of a DSPy module."* Two equivalent surface forms: **inline** (`"question -> answer"`, `"context: list[str], question: str -> answer: str"`) optionally paired with an `instructions=` kwarg, and **class-based** (`class Emotion(dspy.Signature)`) which adds task-description docstrings, `dspy.InputField(desc=...)` input hints, and `dspy.OutputField(desc=...)` output constraints. Five-tier type system: basic Python (`str` / `int` / `bool`), `typing` composites (`list[str]` / `dict[str, int]` / `Optional[float]` / `Union[str, int]`), pydantic models, dot-notation nested types, and DSPy-special types (`dspy.Image` for multi-modal, `dspy.History` for conversational context). `typing.Literal[...]` is the idiomatic closed-set-classification primitive. Input-type-checking is warn-not-fail (disable via `dspy.configure(warn_on_type_mismatch=False)`). Modules can **expand signatures under the hood** — `dspy.ChainOfThought` injects a `reasoning` field the user never declared. The **stable interface** that survives [[DSPyModules|Module]] / [[DSPyAdapters|Adapter]] / [[DSPyLM|LM]] swaps; the first of the four orthogonal artifacts [[DSPyProgrammingModel|the Programming Model]] names.
- [Dropout](concepts/Dropout.md) — regularizer that randomly zeros activations during training.
- [Discrete Fourier Transform](concepts/DiscreteFourierTransform.md) — Discrete analog of the [[FourierSeries]] for n sampled values: cₖ = (1/n) Σⱼ xⱼ q^{jk}, q = e^{−2πi/n}; equivalent to the matrix product C = (1/n)AX over a Vandermonde matrix; invertible (X = A(1/q)C); parallel computation via FFT recursion (O(n log n)) or matrix-multiply approach from Ch11; 2-D DFT separates into row-wise then column-wise 1-D DFTs ([[parproc-ch13-audio-image-processing]] §13.2).
- [Dynamic Task Assignment](concepts/DynamicTaskAssignment.md) — Processors determine their tasks as the computation proceeds (shared task farm, atomic-counter `schedule(dynamic)`, [[WorkStealing]]); flexible but pays continuous [[CommunicationBottleneck|communication]] cost; [[parproc-ch02-recurring-performance-issues]] §2.4 argues [[StaticTaskAssignment|static]] typically wins.
- [DVC](concepts/DVC.md) — git-style versioning for large data and model artifacts.
- [Diffusion Model](concepts/DiffusionModel.md) — Deep generative model that reverses a forward noise-adding process; replaced [[generativeadversarialnetwork|GANs]] in DALL-E 2 / Imagen.
- [Flux Pro (v1.1 Ultra)](concepts/FluxPro.md) — Commercial-tier text-to-image diffusion model from [[BlackForestLabs|Black Forest Labs]] (the team behind [[StableDiffusion|Stable Diffusion]] before founding the new lab). Flux family ships three quality/cost tiers — Schnell (fastest, open weights), Dev (open weights, non-commercial), Pro (closed, API-only). First wiki receipt: [[dspy-image-generation-prompting-tutorial]] uses the `fal-ai/flux-pro/v1.1-ultra` endpoint hosted by [[FAL]]; returned URLs are wrapped via [[DSPyImage|`dspy.Image.from_url(...)`]] for the next critic iteration.
- [Early Stopping](concepts/EarlyStopping.md) — halting training when validation loss plateaus.
- [Edge Detection](concepts/EdgeDetection.md) — Identifying object-boundary pixels by suppressing low-frequency DFT coefficients (high-pass filter) and inverting; dual of [[ImageSmoothing]]; parallelization identical to the parallel 2-D DFT pipeline ([[parproc-ch13-audio-image-processing]] §13.5.3). Also applies to 1-D audio for speech segmentation.
- [Eigendecomposition](concepts/Eigendecomposition.md) — $\mathbf{A}=\mathbf{P}\mathbf{D}\mathbf{P}^{-1}$ for diagonalizable square $\mathbf{A}$ ([[mml-book]] §4.4); symmetric $\mathbf{A}$ ⇒ $\mathbf{P}$ orthogonal (spectral theorem). The engine of [[PrincipalComponentAnalysis|PCA]].
- [Eigenvalue](concepts/Eigenvalue.md) — Scalar $\lambda$ satisfying $Av = \lambda v$; dominant eigenvalue found by the [[PowerMethod|power method]]; large-scale parallel eigenvalue extraction via CULA SVD ([[parproc-ch11-parallel-matrix-operations]] §11.6).
- [Eigenvector](concepts/Eigenvector.md) — Nonzero vector $v$ satisfying $Av = \lambda v$; dominant eigenvector is the target of the [[PowerMethod|power method]]; used in PageRank and PCA ([[parproc-ch11-parallel-matrix-operations]] §11.6).
- [Enumeration Sort](concepts/EnumerationSort.md) — O(n²) sort that determines each element's rank by counting smaller elements; trivially parallelizable outer loop (one thread per element); inner loop also parallelizable via reduction ([[parproc-ch12-parallel-sorting]] §12.7).
- [ELT](concepts/ELT.md) — extract/load/transform pattern with in-warehouse transformations.
- [Empirical Risk Minimization](concepts/EmpiricalRiskMinimization.md) — Murphy §1.2.1.4: $\hat\theta=\arg\min_\theta \frac{1}{N}\sum_n \ell(y_n,f(x_n;\theta))$. Recovers misclassification (zero-one), MSE (quadratic), [[MaximumLikelihoodEstimation|MLE]] (NLL). [[2605.12966-agentic-ai-to-agi]]'s [[AverageTrap]] is an ERM-pathology argument under heterogeneous task manifolds.
- [End-to-End Training](concepts/EndToEndTraining.md) — Jointly optimize every layer of a pipeline against the final loss; replaces handcrafted [[FeatureEngineering|feature engineering]] (Canny / [[SIFT]]); the deep-learning principle that unified [[ComputerVision]] / [[SpeechRecognition]] / [[NLP]] under one toolkit.
- [EM Algorithm](concepts/EMAlgorithm.md) — Expectation-Maximization: iterative MLE under latent variables ([[mml-book]] Ch 11). Workaround for the no-closed-form [[GaussianMixtureModel|GMM]] MLE; alternates between [[Responsibility|responsibilities]] (E) and parameter updates (M).
- [Embarrassingly Parallel](concepts/EmbarrassinglyParallel.md) — Old meaning: trivially decomposable. New (modern) meaning: **low [[CommunicationBottleneck|communication]] needs** — [[parproc-ch02-recurring-performance-issues]] §2.3.1 flags the terminology drift. A problem can be "embarrassingly easy to write" yet **not** embarrassingly parallel under the new meaning (the Ch1 prime-finder qualifies as the former but fails the latter).
- [False Sharing](concepts/FalseSharing.md) — [[CacheCoherency|Cache-coherency]] pathology
- [Fibonacci Numbers](concepts/FibonacciNumbers.md) — Sequence $f_n = f_{n-1} + f_{n-2}$; computable in $O(\log n)$ matrix multiplications via the 2×2 recurrence matrix $A = \bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}1&1\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$ and repeated squaring ([[parproc-ch11-parallel-matrix-operations]] §11.4.2).
- [Fox's Algorithm](concepts/FoxAlgorithm.md) — MPI distributed-memory [[MatrixMultiplication|matrix multiplication]]: cyclic broadcast of A blocks within row-bands + downward shift of B blocks over $m = n/\sqrt{p}$ steps; Cannon's algorithm differs by rotating in both dimensions ([[parproc-ch11-parallel-matrix-operations]] §11.3.1).: two unrelated variables share a cache line, so a write to one invalidates the other at remote caches; the *"ping-pong"* effect cycles coherency transactions; fix is padding ([[parproc-ch03-shared-memory-parallelism]] §3.5.3). Magnified 8× at the 4 KB page granularity used by [[SoftwareDSM]].
- [Fetch-and-Add](concepts/FetchAndAdd.md) — Atomic read-modify-write returning the *pre*-increment value in one round trip via memory-side hardware adders ([[parproc-ch03-shared-memory-parallelism]] §3.4.3). Optionally **packet-combined** in multistage networks (§3.7): two `F&A(X,1)` packets meeting at a switch coalesce into one `F&A(X,2)`. Sibling of [[TestAndSet]].
- [Encoder-Decoder](concepts/encoderdecoder.md) — 
- [EEPROM](concepts/EEPROM.md) — Electrically Erasable PROM; byte-programmable non-volatile MCU storage for user settings. [[ATmega328P]] has 1 k of EEPROM with ~100 k write-cycle endurance and ~3.3 ms/byte write latency ([[embedded-controllers-fiore]] ch. 16).
- [ETL](concepts/ETL.md) — extract/transform/load classic data pipeline pattern.
- [Execution Trace Feedback](concepts/ExecutionTraceFeedback.md) — History-design principle for [[AgenticAlgorithmDiscovery|agentic algorithm discovery]]: feed the explorer LLM per-step decision traces, not just scalar acc/cost. From [[2604.25850-agentic-harness-engineering|Meta-Harness]] + [[2605.08083-autotts|AutoTTS]]. Ablation: removing traces produces *worse* accuracy with *more* tokens.
- [Experiential Learning](concepts/experientiallearning.md) — 
- [Experiment Tracking](concepts/ExperimentTracking.md) — systematic logging of training runs and artifacts.
- [Exponential Family](concepts/ExponentialFamily.md) — Parametric family with $p(\mathbf{x}\mid\boldsymbol\theta)=h(\mathbf{x})\exp(\langle\boldsymbol\eta,\mathbf{T}\rangle - A)$ ([[mml-book]] §6.6). Gaussian, Bernoulli, Multinomial, Poisson all members; every member has a [[ConjugatePrior]].
- [Exploding Gradient](concepts/ExplodingGradient.md) — runaway gradient magnitudes destabilizing training.
- [F1 Score](concepts/F1Score.md) — harmonic mean of precision and recall.
- [SemanticF1](concepts/SemanticF1.md) — `dspy.evaluate.SemanticF1`: reference-based [[llmasjudge|LLM-as-judge]] [[DSPyMetrics|DSPy metric]] that decomposes both gold and predicted answers into atomic claims and computes F1 over claim coverage. The metric is **itself a DSPy program** (a small composition over a typed [[DSPySignatures|`class Assess(dspy.Signature)`]] rubric), so it is **recursively optimizable**. Canonical wiki receipts converge on ~**61% as the post-optimization ceiling** for a single-hop CoT-based [[rag|RAG]] on gpt-4o-mini with [[MIPROv2|MIPROv2]] `auto="medium"` — [[dspy-rag-tutorial]] (42 → 55.5 → 61.1 on [[RAGQAArenaTech]]) and [[dspy-optimizers]] Receipt 2 (53 → 61 on StackExchange). Sibling to surface metrics ([[bleu|BLEU]] / [[ROUGE]]), embedding metrics ([[BERTScore]]), and NLI-claim metrics ([[AlignScore]]) — the **LLM-judged claim-coverage** entry in the reference-based metric family. Reference-free clinical sibling is [[MedVAL]].
- [RAG-QA Arena Tech](concepts/RAGQAArenaTech.md) — The *"Tech"* split of the **RAG-QA Arena** benchmark (Han et al., 2024); ~1,000 long-form QA pairs over technical topics (programming, sysadmin, web dev, networking) drawn from StackExchange-style sources. Paired with a **28,000-document downsampled technical corpus** (each doc truncated to 6K characters; [[openai|OpenAI]] `text-embedding-3-small` embeddings; top-`k=5` retrieval). Used in [[dspy-rag-tutorial]] with the 200/300/500 train/dev/test split — establishes **42% / 55.5% / 61.1% [[SemanticF1]]** as the canonical no-RAG / un-optimized-RAG / [[MIPROv2|MIPROv2]]-optimized performance envelope. The wiki's canonical small-scale long-form-QA benchmark for DSPy RAG receipts.
- [Fano's Inequality](concepts/fanosinequality.md) — 
- [fastText](concepts/FastText.md) — subword-aware static word embedding model.
- [Fast Fourier Transform](concepts/FastFourierTransform.md) — Cooley-Tukey O(n log n) divide-and-conquer DFT algorithm; splits n-point DFT into two n/2-point DFTs recursively; parallel strategies: FFT recursion (analogous to Quicksort/Hyperquicksort from Ch12) or matrix-multiply approach (preferred in shared memory — avoids thread starvation); inverse FFT uses same structure; 2-D FFT exploits separability ([[parproc-ch13-audio-image-processing]] §13.3).
- [FFTW](concepts/FFTW.md) — "Fastest Fourier Transform in the West"; free CPU-parallel [[FastFourierTransform|FFT]] library at fftw.org; provides [[OpenMP]] and [[MPI]] callable versions; counterpart to [[CUFFT]] for CPU-bound workloads ([[parproc-ch13-audio-image-processing]] §13.4.3).
- [Feasibility](concepts/Feasibility.md) — whether an ML solution is technically and economically viable.
- [Feature Engineering](concepts/FeatureEngineering.md) — crafting model inputs from raw data.
- [Feature Map](concepts/FeatureMap.md) — Function $\boldsymbol\phi:\mathbb{R}^D\to\mathbb{R}^K$ ([[mml-book]] §9.2) lifting inputs into a higher-dim space where linear methods capture non-linear relations. Polynomial regression and kernel SVM rely on it.
- [Feature Quality](concepts/FeatureQuality.md) — fitness of engineered features for modeling.
- [Feature Scaling](concepts/FeatureScaling.md) — normalizing features to comparable ranges.
- [Feature Store](concepts/FeatureStore.md) — centralized system serving features to training and inference.
- [Few-Shot Learning](concepts/FewShotLearning.md) — adapting a model from a handful of labeled examples.
- [File I/O (Tensors & Models)](concepts/FileIO.md) — Framework save/load for raw tensors, dicts of tensors, and entire model [[StateDict|state dicts]]; substrate of [[Checkpoint|checkpointing]] ([[d2l-builders-guide]]).
- [Feed-Forward Network (positionwise FFN)](concepts/FeedForwardNetwork.md) — Two-layer MLP applied identically at every sequence position inside each [[Transformer]] block; non-attention nonlinearity, ~⅔ of block parameters; $d_{\textrm{ff}}=2048$ vs $d_{\textrm{model}}=512$ in the vanilla Transformer ([[d2l-attention-and-transformers]]).
- [Filter (Convolutional)](concepts/Filter.md) — Learnable kernel tensor of shape $c_o\times c_i\times k_h\times k_w$ that a [[ConvolutionalLayer|conv layer]] slides across an input; gradient descent can recover hand-designed edge / blur / derivative filters from input-output pairs ([[d2l-convolutional-neural-networks]]).
- [Fine-Tuning](concepts/FineTuning.md) — continuing pretraining on a task-specific dataset.
- [Flake8](concepts/Flake8.md) — Python linter combining pyflakes, pycodestyle, McCabe.
- [FlashAttention](concepts/flashattention.md) — IO-aware exact attention via tiling + recomputation; the default attention kernel for modern Transformers.
- [Forward Propagation](concepts/ForwardPropagation.md) — Input→output pass that computes and caches intermediate variables along the [[ComputationalGraph]]; partner of [[Backpropagation]] ([[d2l-multilayer-perceptrons]]).
- [Fudan University](concepts/fudanuniversity.md) — Co-author affiliation on [[2605.12357-delta-mem]]. (Filed under concepts/ for historical reasons; semantically an entity.)
- [`fork()` (POSIX Process Creation)](concepts/Fork.md) — [[OperatingSystem|POSIX]] [[SystemCall|system call]] that **creates a new [[Process|process]] by duplicating the calling one**. Signature `pid_t fork(void)` returns **twice** — once in the parent (returning the child's [[ProcessID|PID]]), once in the child (returning `0`). Child inherits parent's open FDs / signal table / environment / [[ProcessMemory|memory image]] (copy-on-write). Substrate for `fork()` + `exec*()` process spawn, multi-process servers, and the kernel-level primitive behind [[GdbFollowFork|`set follow-fork-mode`]] ([[dis-3-4-gdb-advanced|DIS Ch 3.4]]).
- [GDB Backtrace (`bt` / `where` / `frame N`)](concepts/GdbBacktrace.md) — [[GDB]] command family that inspects the active call stack at a halt point — the runtime view of [[dis-1-4-functions|Ch 1.4]]'s [[StackFrame|stack-of-frames]] model. `bt` / `where` print all frames innermost-first (`#0 func(args) at file:line`); `frame N` switches the inspection context so [[GdbPrint|`print var`]] resolves `var` in frame `N`'s [[VariableScope|scope]] and reads its [[LocalVariable|locals]] / [[FunctionParameter|parameters]]. The canonical crash-debugging primitive — invoked immediately after a [[SegmentationFault|segfault]] to localize the offending call chain; works identically on [[CoreFile|core files]] for post-mortem analysis ([[dis-3-1-gdb]]).
- [GDB `attach` (Debug a Running Process)](concepts/GdbAttach.md) — [[GDB]] feature that **connects the debugger to an already-running [[Process|process]]** via `gdb <prog> <pid>` or `attach <pid>` — the workflow opposite to [[GdbRun|`run`]]. On attach, the target [[Process|process]] **pauses** (kernel-side [[Ptrace|`ptrace`]]) — inspect with [[GdbBacktrace|`bt`]] / [[GdbPrint|`print`]], set [[Breakpoint|breakpoints]], then [[StepDebug|`cont`]] / `detach`. Canonical use cases: already-running daemons / servers, post-warmup heisenbugs, multi-process debugging (paired with [[GdbFollowFork]]). Self-pause idiom `kill(getpid(), SIGSTOP)` opens a guaranteed attach window from inside the program ([[dis-3-4-gdb-advanced|DIS Ch 3.4]]).
- [GDB Breakpoint Management](concepts/GdbBreakpointManagement.md) — six-command family for manipulating numbered [[Breakpoint|breakpoints]] without re-setting them: `enable N` / `disable N` (toggle silence), `delete N` / `delete` (remove one / all), `clear N` (remove by source line rather than ID), `ignore N M` (skip the next `M` hits), `condition N (expr)` (attach a [[ConditionalBreakpoint|conditional]]). Plus [[GdbInfo|`info breakpoints`]] for the full table. `clear` / `delete` distinction: `delete` by **ID**, `clear` by **source location** ([[dis-3-2-gdb-commands|DIS Ch 3.2]]).
- [GDB `disassemble` (`disass`)](concepts/GdbDisassemble.md) — [[GDB]] command that prints [[AssemblyLanguage|assembly]] for a function or address range — the entry point to **assembly-level debugging**. Forms: `disass main` (whole function via [[DebugSymbol|symbol table]]), `disass 0x1234 0x1248` (address range), bare `disass` (current function). Output marks the current [[InstructionPointer|PC]] with `=>`. Companion `x/i $pc` ([[GdbExamineMemory|`x`]] in instruction format) shows the single next instruction. The escape hatch when [[CompilerOptimization|`-O2`]] / stripped binaries / [[CLibrary|libc]] internals defeat source-level [[StepDebug|`step`]] ([[dis-3-5-gdb-assembly|DIS Ch 3.5]]).
- [GDB `display`](concepts/GdbDisplay.md) — [[GDB]] command that **registers an expression to auto-print at every pause** — every [[Breakpoint|breakpoint]] hit, every [[StepDebug|`step` / `next`]]. The *passive-poll* sibling to one-shot [[GdbPrint|`print`]] and to write-triggered [[Watchpoint|`watch`]]. `display/f expr` supports the same format specifiers as [[GdbPrint|`print`]]; `undisplay N` removes; `disable display N` / `enable display N` toggle. [[GdbInfo|`info display`]] lists active entries ([[dis-3-2-gdb-commands|DIS Ch 3.2]]).
- [GDB `follow-fork-mode` (Fork-Aware Debugging)](concepts/GdbFollowFork.md) — [[GDB]] setting that controls which side of a [[Fork|`fork()`]] system call the debugger follows — the primitive that makes [[GDB]] usable for **multi-process programs**. Default: **parent** (*"by default, GDB follows the parent after a call to `fork()`"*). `set follow-fork-mode child` switches to the new child; `show follow-fork-mode` displays current setting. The unfollowed side runs free; attach a second [[GDB]] session via [[GdbAttach|`gdb <prog> <pid>`]] to debug both. User-side tip of [[Ptrace|`ptrace`]]'s `PTRACE_O_TRACEFORK` option ([[dis-3-4-gdb-advanced|DIS Ch 3.4]]).
- [GDB `x` (Examine Memory)](concepts/GdbExamineMemory.md) — [[GDB]] **raw-memory inspection** primitive: `x/nfu address` reads `n` units (`b`/`h`/`w`/`g` sizes) starting at `address` and renders them in format `f` (`d`/`u`/`x`/`o`/`t`/`c`/`s`/`i`/`f`/`a`). The escape hatch when [[GdbPrint|`print`]]'s type-awareness is wrong, absent, or in the way — used for stripped binaries / [[CoreFile|core dumps]] / [[VoidPointer|`void *`]] regions / [[LinkedList|pointer-chain]] walks / `x/i $pc` live disassembly / `x/wx $rsp` stack-top inspection ([[dis-3-2-gdb-commands|DIS Ch 3.2]]).
- [GDB `info threads` (Thread Enumeration)](concepts/GdbInfoThreads.md) — [[GDB]] sub-command that **enumerates all active threads in the debuggee** — the entry point to thread-aware debugging. Per-row columns: GDB thread number (used in [[GdbThreadSwitch|`thread <N>`]]), [[Pthreads|`pthread_t`]] library ID, kernel-side LWP ID, current source position; `*` marks the current thread. Most platforms maintain 1:1 correspondence between the three IDs. Paired with [[GdbThreadSwitch|`thread <N>`]] (drill into one thread) and [[GdbThreadApply|`thread apply all bt`]] (snapshot every thread) for the canonical multi-thread debugging workflow ([[dis-3-6-gdb-pthreads|DIS Ch 3.6]]).
- [GDB `thread apply all` (Broadcast Command)](concepts/GdbThreadApply.md) — [[GDB]] command that **runs a [[GDB]] command in the context of every thread**, printing each thread's result. The broadcast counterpart to [[GdbThreadSwitch|`thread <N>`]]'s point-switch. Canonical use: `thread apply all bt` — every thread's [[GdbBacktrace|backtrace]] in one go, the corpus's first **deadlock-and-livelock diagnostic primitive** (every thread blocked in `pthread_mutex_lock` reveals the cycle at a glance). Also broadcast forms like `thread apply <N> <M> <cmd>` for a specific thread list ([[dis-3-6-gdb-pthreads|DIS Ch 3.6]]).
- [GDB `thread <N>` (Thread Context Switch)](concepts/GdbThreadSwitch.md) — [[GDB]] command that **switches the inspection context to a specific thread** (identified by GDB thread number from [[GdbInfoThreads|`info threads`]]). After the switch, [[GdbBacktrace|`bt`]] / [[GdbPrint|`print`]] / [[GdbInfo|`info locals`]] / [[CpuRegister|`info registers`]] all resolve against the named thread's [[StackFrame|frame]] / [[VariableScope|scope]] / register snapshot — the multi-thread analog of [[GdbBacktrace|`frame N`]]'s frame switch. Necessary because each thread owns a **separate [[ExecutionStack|execution stack]]** with its own [[LocalVariable|locals]]; without `thread <N>`, [[GdbPrint|`print`]] silently inspects only the breakpoint-triggering thread ([[dis-3-6-gdb-pthreads|DIS Ch 3.6]]).
- [GDB `info` (Reflection Sub-commands)](concepts/GdbInfo.md) — [[GDB]] command hub for reflecting over debuggee + debugger state. Canonical sub-commands: `info locals` ([[LocalVariable|locals]] in current frame), `info args` ([[FunctionParameter|parameters]]), `info break` / `info breakpoints` (full table with hit count + condition), `info registers` (CPU register file `%rax`/`%rip`/…), `info frame` (saved IP + frame pointer + caller), `info display`, `info threads`, `info sharedlibrary`, `info functions`, `info variables`. The reflection layer over GDB's own bookkeeping; pairs with [[GdbBacktrace|`frame N; info locals`]] for caller-frame inspection ([[dis-3-2-gdb-commands|DIS Ch 3.2]]).
- [GDB `list` (`l`)](concepts/GdbList.md) — [[GDB]] command that shows source code around the current execution point or a user-named line / function / file. Default 10 lines (configurable via `set listsize N`). Forms: `list` (current point) / `list N` / `list N,M` / `list main` / `list file.c:42` / `list file.c:func`; bare `list` after a previous `list` **continues** to the next 10 lines. After [[GdbBacktrace|`frame N`]] switches frames, `list` shows source around frame `N`'s line — scope-aware like [[GdbPrint|`print`]] ([[dis-3-1-gdb|Ch 3.1]] / [[dis-3-2-gdb-commands|Ch 3.2]]).
- [GDB `print` (`p`)](concepts/GdbPrint.md) — [[GDB]] command that **evaluates an expression in the debuggee's current frame scope and prints the result** — the workhorse inspection primitive. Format specifiers `/x` (hex), `/t` (binary), `/c` (ASCII), `/d` / `/u` / `/o` / `/f` (numeric formats); `print *(int *)0x8ff4bc10` does typed dereference of a raw address; `print arr[0]@10` shows an artificial 10-element array; `print func(args)` actually **invokes the function** in the debuggee (side effects persist). Resolves variable names in the current [[StackFrame|frame]]'s scope — so [[GdbBacktrace|`frame N; print var`]] reads frame `N`'s view ([[dis-3-1-gdb|Ch 3.1]] / [[dis-3-2-gdb-commands|Ch 3.2]]).
- [GDB `stepi` / `nexti` (Single-Instruction Stepping)](concepts/GdbStepi.md) — [[AssemblyLanguage|assembly]]-level duals of [[StepDebug|`step` / `next`]]: each advances **one machine instruction** instead of one source line. `stepi` / `si` steps **into** `call` instructions (*"the `si` command steps into function calls, meaning that GDB will pause the program at the first instruction of the called function"*); `nexti` / `ni` treats `call` as **atomic** — same call-handling distinction as [[StepDebug|`step` vs `next`]], one abstraction level lower. Canonical pairing: [[GdbDisassemble|`disass`]] for the map, `stepi` to walk it, [[GdbDisplay|`display/i $pc`]] + [[CpuRegister|`info registers`]] to observe state between each step ([[dis-3-5-gdb-assembly|DIS Ch 3.5]]).
- [GDB `run` (`r`)](concepts/GdbRun.md) — [[GDB]] command that **starts the debuggee from the beginning**, optionally with shell-style arguments (`run 2 40 100` → `argc=4`, `argv = {"./a.out", "2", "40", "100"}`) and redirections (`run < in.txt > out.txt`). Re-arms all active [[Breakpoint|breakpoints]] as trap instructions in the loaded `.text`, executes from `_start` → `__libc_start_main` → [[MainFunction|`main`]], halts at the first breakpoint hit / signal / exit. Re-run with bare `run` reuses the last argument list; `show args` displays them, `set args …` updates them; `start` runs to a temporary breakpoint at `main` ([[dis-3-1-gdb|Ch 3.1]] / [[dis-3-2-gdb-commands|Ch 3.2]]).
- [GDB `set` (Live Variable Mutation)](concepts/GdbSet.md) — [[GDB]] command that **rewrites a variable in the running debuggee without recompiling** — the mutation primitive opposite to [[GdbPrint|`print`]]'s read. `set var x = 123 * y` writes through any [[LValue|lvalue]]: locals / parameters / globals / struct fields / array elements / `*(int *)addr` / registers (`set $rax = 0`). Overloaded with debugger-config namespace (`set pagination off`) — disambiguate via the `var` keyword. Session-only; can violate compiler-assumed invariants under [[CompilerOptimization|`-O2`]] (register-cached writes invisible) ([[dis-3-2-gdb-commands|DIS Ch 3.2]]).
- [GDB Signal Control (`signal` / `handle` / `info signal`)](concepts/GdbSignalControl.md) — [[GDB]] command family for **sending, intercepting, and inspecting [[Signal|POSIX signals]]** in the debuggee. Three sub-features: (1) `signal <SIG>` sends a [[Signal|signal]] (e.g., `signal SIGCONT` to resume a self-paused process, `signal SIGUSR1` to trigger a user handler); (2) `handle <SIG> stop` makes [[GDB]] **halt** when the debuggee receives `<SIG>` — the signal-equivalent of a [[Breakpoint|breakpoint]] (e.g., `handle SIGBUS stop` for the alignment-fault scenario); (3) `info signal` / `info SIGALRM` reflects over per-signal handling rules. Modifiers per signal: `stop` / `nostop`, `print` / `noprint`, `pass` / `nopass`. Brings signal-driven code under deterministic debugging — without `handle`, signal handlers run **asynchronously** outside [[GDB]]'s single-step model ([[dis-3-4-gdb-advanced|DIS Ch 3.4]]).
- [GDB `whatis` (Type Query)](concepts/GdbWhatis.md) — [[GDB]] command that **reports the static type of an expression without evaluating it**. `whatis (x + 3.4)` → `type = double` (confirms [[CTypePromotion|usual arithmetic conversion]]); `whatis p` returns `int *`; `whatis func` returns the function signature. **Does not chase typedefs** — for deep [[Typedef|`typedef`]] / struct expansion use the sibling `ptype` command which prints full struct member layouts with offsets ([[dis-3-2-gdb-commands|DIS Ch 3.2]]).
- [`gcc -g` (Debug-Info Flag)](concepts/GccDashG.md) — The [[GCC|`gcc`]] flag that embeds [[DebugSymbol|DWARF debug symbols]] in the produced executable; the **load-bearing precondition** for [[GDB|source-level debugging]]. Levels: `-g0` (off) / `-g1` (functions + externals only) / `-g` = `-g2` (default — full symbols) / `-g3` (adds macros for `info macro`) / `-ggdb` (GDB-preferred format). Conventional debug build flags: **`-O0 -g`** — disabling [[CompilerOptimization|optimization]] keeps the line-to-instruction mapping monotonic. Symbols typically 2–3× the binary size; stripped from release binaries via `strip` and optionally archived separately (`objcopy --only-keep-debug`) ([[dis-3-1-gdb]]).
- [GAIA](concepts/gaia.md) — Mialon et al. 2024 General-AI-Assistant benchmark; in [[2605.10698-bystander-effect-mas]] used as the high-entropy semantic background, not for its labels.
- [Gated Delta-Rule Learning](concepts/gateddeltarule.md) — Online update rule for δ-mem's OSAM matrix; SGD on online regression loss with per-dimension retention gate.
- [Gaussian Elimination](concepts/GaussianElimination.md) — Direct solver for $Ax=b$ via row reduction to (reduced) row echelon form; CUDA implementation limited to ~30×30 matrices under 4K shared memory and single block constraint ([[parproc-ch11-parallel-matrix-operations]] §11.5.1–11.5.2).
- [Gaussian Distribution](concepts/GaussianDistribution.md) — The Gaussian/normal density ([[mml-book]] §6.5); closed under marginalization, conditioning, and linear transforms; the noise model behind least-squares regression and the prior behind [[BayesianLinearRegression]].
- [GELU](concepts/GELU.md) — Gaussian Error Linear Unit ($x\cdot\Phi(x)$); smoother ReLU used in [[VisionTransformer|ViT]], [[BERT]], GPT-2/3 ([[d2l-attention-and-transformers]]).
- [GEPA](concepts/GEPA.md) — DSPy's **reflection-based instruction optimizer** from [[dspy-optimizers]] (page 13 of 13). `dspy.GEPA` — the only [[DSPyOptimizers|optimizer in the catalog]] that **uses an LM to reflect on the program's trajectory** and propose prompts addressing the gaps. *"Uses LM's to reflect on the DSPy program's trajectory, to identify what worked, what didn't and propose prompts addressing the gaps. Additionally, GEPA can leverage domain-specific textual feedback to rapidly improve the DSPy program."* Two distinguishing ingredients: **LM reflection on trajectories** (structurally distinct from [[MIPROv2]]'s generative *grounded proposal* — GEPA explicitly **reflects** on outcomes and diagnoses failures) and **domain-specific textual feedback** (the only optimizer in the catalog that names a textual-feedback input distinct from the scalar metric — useful for domains where *why* an output is wrong is easier to articulate than a numeric score). **The only optimizer named on [[dspy-optimization-overview|page 12]]** of the *Learn* corpus — and named precisely because it is the **named carve-out** from the framework-level **inverted 20/80 train/val split** recommendation. *"However, the GEPA optimizer follows standard ML practice — maximizing the training set size while keeping the validation set sufficiently sized to represent the downstream task distribution."* The mechanism that justifies the exemption — left implicit on page 12 and only partially developed on page 13 — is that reflection-driven instruction proposals are **more robust to small training sets** than search-driven mechanisms. This is the **single most non-obvious per-optimizer disclosure** in the *Learn* corpus — reading the per-optimizer documentation is **load-bearing** before applying the 20/80 split mechanically. **Resolves the long-standing forward reference [[GEPA]]** carried by [[DSPyOptimization]] / [[dspy-optimization-overview]] since page 12 named GEPA as the framework's only carved-out optimizer.
- [Gaussian Mixture Model](concepts/GaussianMixtureModel.md) — Convex mix of $K$ Gaussians ([[mml-book]] Ch 11); MLE has no closed form ⇒ fit by [[EMAlgorithm]]. $k$-means is the hard-assignment limit.
- [Generalization](concepts/Generalization.md) — performance on unseen data from the same distribution.
- [Generalization Gap](concepts/GeneralizationGap.md) — $\mathcal{L}(\theta;p^*)-\mathcal{L}(\theta;\mathcal{D}_{\text{train}})$ — the operational definition of overfitting (Murphy §1.2.3). Classical U-shape vs modern double-descent in overparameterized DNNs; what [[ScalingLaws]] empirically shrinks.
- [Generative Adversarial Network (GAN)](concepts/generativeadversarialnetwork.md) — [[IanGoodfellow|Goodfellow]] et al. 2014; [[MinMaxGame|minimax]] [[Generator]]-vs-[[Discriminator]] framework with non-saturating $\min_G\{-\log D(G(\mathbf{z}))\}$ generator loss; [[DCGAN]] ([[AlecRadford|Radford]] et al. 2015) is the canonical all-convolutional scale-up ([[d2l-introduction]] / [[d2l-generative-adversarial-networks]]).
- [Generative Agents](concepts/generativeagents.md) — 
- [Git](concepts/Git.md) — dominant distributed version-control system.
- [Graph Connectedness](concepts/GraphConnectedness.md) — Testing whether every vertex can reach every other; reduces to computing adjacency matrix powers $A^r$ up to $A^{n-1}$ via [[MatrixMultiplication|parallel matrix multiplication]] ([[parproc-ch11-parallel-matrix-operations]] §11.4.1).
- [Git Hooks](concepts/GitHooks.md) — scripts run at git lifecycle events.
- [Git LFS](concepts/GitLFS.md) — large-file storage extension for git.
- [GloVe](concepts/GloVe.md) — co-occurrence-factored static word embeddings.
- [GPU](concepts/GPU.md) — Massively-parallel compute device dominated by [[NVIDIA]] hardware via [[CUDA]]; same-device-operand rule + "transfers are slow" cost model from [[d2l-builders-guide]].
- [GPU Memory Hierarchy](concepts/gpumemoryhierarchy.md) — SRAM vs HBM vs DRAM tiers; the asymmetry that makes IO-awareness pay off on modern accelerators.
- [Gradient](concepts/Gradient.md) — vector of partial derivatives of a loss w.r.t. parameters.
- [Gradient Clipping](concepts/GradientClipping.md) — Project gradient onto $\|\mathbf{g}\|\leq\theta$ ball, $\mathbf{g}\leftarrow\min(1,\theta/\|\mathbf{g}\|)\mathbf{g}$; ubiquitous-but-honest hack for [[ExplodingGradient|exploding gradients]] in RNN training ([[d2l-recurrent-neural-networks]]).
- [Gradient Descent](concepts/GradientDescent.md) — iterative parameter update in the negative gradient direction.
- [Gradual Unfreezing](concepts/gradualunfreezing.md) — Top-down layer-by-layer fine-tuning schedule (Howard & Ruder, 2018); evaluated against full fine-tuning in T5.
- [GRPO](concepts/grpo.md) — 
- [GRU](concepts/GRU.md) — simplified gated recurrent cell, lighter than LSTM.
- [Hallucination](concepts/Hallucination.md) — confident but factually wrong LLM output.
- [Hash-Chained Audit](concepts/hashchainedaudit.md) — 
- [He Initialization](concepts/HeInitialization.md) — Kaiming-He variance $\sigma^2 = 2/n_\text{in}$; the [[ReLU]]-aware [[WeightInitialization|initialization]] (factor-of-2 correction because ReLU zeroes half its inputs) ([[d2l-multilayer-perceptrons]]).
- [Hidden Layer](concepts/HiddenLayer.md) — Intermediate fully-connected layer whose output is a learned representation; together with [[ActivationFunction|nonlinearity]] makes [[MultilayerPerceptron|MLPs]] strictly more expressive than affine maps ([[d2l-multilayer-perceptrons]]).
- [Hidden State](concepts/HiddenState.md) — Persistent memory variable $\mathbf{H}_t$ of an [[RNN]]; an *input* to the current step computed from $\mathbf{X}_t$ + $\mathbf{H}_{t-1}$. Distinct from a hidden *layer* ([[d2l-recurrent-neural-networks]]).
- [Hoeffding's Inequality](concepts/HoeffdingsInequality.md) — Finite-sample concentration bound $P(\bar X - \mu \geq t) \leq \exp(-2nt^2/(b-a)^2)$ for bounded RVs. In ML: gives the ~10–15k test-set size needed for ±0.01 error estimation at 95% confidence ([[d2l-linear-classification]]).
- [Holdout Dataset](concepts/HoldoutDataset.md) — reserved data used once for final evaluation.
- [Hollowed Mind](concepts/HollowedMind.md) — Klein & Klein 2025: terminal cognitive-dependency state with frictionless external answers. In [[2605.10698-bystander-effect-mas]] the $\mathcal{S}\to 0$ terminus; reached once $n\geq D_L$.
- [Horovod](concepts/Horovod.md) — MPI-style ring-allreduce distributed training library.
- [HotpotQA](concepts/hotpotqa.md) — Multi-hop QA benchmark (Yang et al. 2018); used by δ-mem in the no-context recovery ablation.
- [Human-in-the-Loop](concepts/humanintheloop.md) — 
- [Hyperquicksort](concepts/Hyperquicksort.md) — Distributed [[Quicksort]] for hypercube / power-of-2 message-passing systems; d rounds of median broadcast + partner compare-exchange; result is globally sorted chunks across PEs ([[parproc-ch12-parallel-sorting]] §12.1.3).
- [Hyperparameter Tuning](concepts/HyperparameterTuning.md) — searching the non-learned-parameter space for best validation performance.
- [IFEval](concepts/ifeval.md) — Instruction-following evaluation (Zhou et al. 2023); δ-mem's general-capability preservation check.
- [Histogram](concepts/Histogram.md) — Discrete frequency table counting data points per bin; crude [[ProbabilityDensityFunction]] estimator; CUDA image histogram via Podlozhnyuk histogram64/256 subhistogram-merge algorithm ([[parproc-ch14-statistics-data-mining]] §14.2.2).
- [Image Smoothing](concepts/ImageSmoothing.md) — Suppressing noise in digital images via spatial-domain neighbor averaging or frequency-domain low-pass filtering (zero high-frequency DFT coefficients, invert); dual of [[EdgeDetection]]; parallelized via the parallel 2-D DFT pipeline; intensity clamping to [0, 255] required post-operation ([[parproc-ch13-audio-image-processing]] §13.5.1–13.5.2).
- [Importance Weighting](concepts/ImportanceWeighting.md) — sample reweighting for covariate-shift correction.
- [Itemset Analysis](concepts/ItemsetAnalysis.md) — Data-mining task finding frequent item co-occurrences in transaction databases; association rules defined by support (P(I∧J)) and confidence (P(J|I)) ([[parproc-ch14-statistics-data-mining]] §14.1).
- [Inner Product](concepts/InnerProduct.md) — Bilinear, symmetric, positive-definite mapping ([[mml-book]] §3.2); gives geometry (length, angle, distance) on top of a vector space. SPD matrices encode all inner products.
- [Injec Agent](concepts/injecagent.md) — 
- [Integration Testing](concepts/IntegrationTesting.md) — exercising multiple components together to catch contract bugs.
- [Integrative Reasoning Bypass](concepts/IntegrativeReasoningBypass.md) — Binary failure state $\mathcal{B}=1$ in [[2605.10698-bystander-effect-mas]]: $E_{int}\ll\mathcal{H}_\tau$; the formal $G_\mathcal{S}\ll 0$ regime of the [[SovereigntyGap]]. Contrast with [[AlignmentHallucination]].
- [Instruction Pointer (`%rip` / `%eip`)](concepts/InstructionPointer.md) — special-purpose [[CpuRegister|CPU register]] holding the **address of the next instruction to execute** — x86-64 `%rip`, [[IA32|IA-32]] `%eip`, generic name **program counter** (`pc` on ARM / RISC-V). The assembly-level *"you are here"* state, marked with `=>` in [[GdbDisassemble|`disass`]] output. [[GDB]] aliases `$pc` to whichever register plays the IP role on the current [[ISA]], so `x/i $pc` and `display/i $pc` are portable. Advances by the instruction's byte width on each [[GdbStepi|`stepi`]]; updated implicitly by every instruction and explicitly by `jmp` / `call` / `ret` / `je` etc. Writable via [[GdbSet|`set $rip = 0x...`]] but a surgical tool ([[dis-3-5-gdb-assembly|DIS Ch 3.5]]).
- [Interaction Depth Limit](concepts/InteractionDepthLimit.md) — Minimum $n$ at which [[AgenticSovereignty]] falls below 0.5 — i.e. the [[BystanderEffect]] triggers. Empirical $D_L\approx 2$ for [[gpt54|GPT-5.4]]; $\to\infty$ for [[claudeopus47|Claude Sonnet 4.6]].
- [Interpolation Regime](concepts/InterpolationRegime.md) — Training regime where the model perfectly fits the training set; classical theory's blowup point but modern deep nets' working regime ([[d2l-multilayer-perceptrons]]).
- [Interpretability](concepts/Interpretability.md) — degree to which a model's decisions can be understood.
- [Inverse-Wisdom Law](concepts/InverseWisdomLaw.md) — Shehata & Li 2026b (arxiv 2604.27274): architecturally-diverse "fragmented" swarms exert *more* pressure than unified-front swarms; corollary — diversity is a defense against the [[BystanderEffect]].
