- [-pthread compile flag](concepts/GccPthreadFlag.md) — [[GCC]] flag for compiling + linking [[Pthreads]] programs: `gcc -o program program.c -pthread`. Distinct from bare `-lpthread` — also predefines threading macros (`_REENTRANT`) and may adjust code-generation for thread-safety ([[dis-14-2-posix|DIS Ch 14.2]]).
- [Synchronization](concepts/Synchronization.md) — Umbrella term for the family of primitives — [[Mutex|mutexes]], [[Semaphore|semaphores]], [[Barrier|barriers]], [[ConditionVariable|condition variables]], [[ReadersWriterLock|readers-writer locks]] — that coordinate access to shared mutable state. *"Enforcing a particular execution order among threads to ensure program correctness, even though it may increase runtime"* ([[dis-14-3-synchronization|DIS Ch 14.3]]).
- [Race Condition](concepts/RaceCondition.md) — *"Any situation where simultaneous execution of operations yields incorrect outcomes"* — strictly broader sibling of [[DataRace|data race]] ([[dis-14-3-synchronization|DIS Ch 14.3]]). Includes check-then-act bugs that don't involve concurrent writes. Heisenbug property: timing-dependent, hard to reproduce.
- [Semaphore](concepts/Semaphore.md) — Count-based synchronization primitive *"managing concurrent access to a resource pool by tracking availability count rather than ownership"* ([[dis-14-3-2-semaphores|DIS Ch 14.3.2]]). Counting vs binary; POSIX `sem_init` / `sem_wait` / `sem_post` / `sem_destroy`. Any thread can post (vs mutex's ownership rule) — the structural property that makes semaphores the natural [[ProducerConsumer|producer/consumer]] primitive.
- [Condition Variable](concepts/ConditionVariable.md) — Blocking-wait-until-predicate synchronization primitive *"eliminating wasteful CPU polling"* ([[dis-14-3-3-other-syncs|DIS Ch 14.3.3]]). Always paired with a [[Mutex]]; Pthreads `pthread_cond_wait` / `signal` / `broadcast`. Canonical predicate-loop idiom (`while`, not `if`) defends against spurious wakeups and condition-change races.
- [Readers-Writer Lock](concepts/ReadersWriterLock.md) — Synchronization primitive specializing the [[Mutex]] for read-heavy workloads: many concurrent readers OR one exclusive writer ([[dis-14-3-3-other-syncs|DIS Ch 14.3.3]]). Pthreads `pthread_rwlock_rdlock` / `wrlock` / `unlock`. Writer-starvation risk; bookkeeping overhead.
- [pthread_mutex_init](concepts/PthreadMutexInit.md) — [[Pthreads]] mutex initialization: `pthread_mutex_init(&mutex, NULL)`. Called in `main` before thread creation ([[dis-14-3-1-mutex|DIS Ch 14.3.1]]).
- [pthread_mutex_lock](concepts/PthreadMutexLock.md) — [[Pthreads]] mutex acquire: `pthread_mutex_lock(&mutex)`. Blocks if held by another thread ([[dis-14-3-1-mutex|DIS Ch 14.3.1]]).
- [pthread_mutex_unlock](concepts/PthreadMutexUnlock.md) — [[Pthreads]] mutex release: `pthread_mutex_unlock(&mutex)`. Same thread that locked must unlock — the ownership rule distinguishing mutex from [[Semaphore|semaphore]] ([[dis-14-3-1-mutex|DIS Ch 14.3.1]]).
- [pthread_mutex_destroy](concepts/PthreadMutexDestroy.md) — [[Pthreads]] mutex teardown: `pthread_mutex_destroy(&mutex)`. Called after `pthread_join`-ing all workers ([[dis-14-3-1-mutex|DIS Ch 14.3.1]]).
- [sem_init](concepts/SemInit.md) — POSIX semaphore initialization: `sem_init(&sem, pshared, value)`. `pshared = 0` for thread sharing within process ([[dis-14-3-2-semaphores|DIS Ch 14.3.2]]).
- [sem_wait](concepts/SemWait.md) — POSIX semaphore acquire (decrement-and-block): *"If the value exceeds 0, execution continues immediately. If 0, the thread blocks"* ([[dis-14-3-2-semaphores|DIS Ch 14.3.2]]).
- [sem_post](concepts/SemPost.md) — POSIX semaphore release (increment-and-wake). Any thread can post — the asymmetry distinguishing semaphores from mutexes ([[dis-14-3-2-semaphores|DIS Ch 14.3.2]]).
- [sem_destroy](concepts/SemDestroy.md) — POSIX semaphore teardown ([[dis-14-3-2-semaphores|DIS Ch 14.3.2]]).
- [pthread_barrier_init](concepts/PthreadBarrierInit.md) — [[Pthreads]] barrier initialization: `pthread_barrier_init(&barr, attr, N)` where `N` is the thread count required to release ([[dis-14-3-3-other-syncs|DIS Ch 14.3.3]]).
- [pthread_barrier_wait](concepts/PthreadBarrierWait.md) — [[Pthreads]] barrier rendezvous: first `N-1` callers block, the `N`-th releases all ([[dis-14-3-3-other-syncs|DIS Ch 14.3.3]]).
- [pthread_barrier_destroy](concepts/PthreadBarrierDestroy.md) — [[Pthreads]] barrier teardown ([[dis-14-3-3-other-syncs|DIS Ch 14.3.3]]).
- [pthread_cond_init](concepts/PthreadCondInit.md) — [[Pthreads]] condition variable initialization ([[dis-14-3-3-other-syncs|DIS Ch 14.3.3]]).
- [pthread_cond_wait](concepts/PthreadCondWait.md) — [[Pthreads]] condition-variable atomic-release-and-block: `pthread_cond_wait(&cond, &mutex)` atomically releases `mutex` while blocking on `cond`, re-acquires before returning ([[dis-14-3-3-other-syncs|DIS Ch 14.3.3]]). Use inside `while (!predicate)` loop to defend against spurious wakeups.
- [pthread_cond_signal](concepts/PthreadCondSignal.md) — [[Pthreads]] condition variable signal — wake one scheduler-chosen waiter ([[dis-14-3-3-other-syncs|DIS Ch 14.3.3]]).
- [pthread_cond_broadcast](concepts/PthreadCondBroadcast.md) — [[Pthreads]] condition variable broadcast — wake all waiters ([[dis-14-3-3-other-syncs|DIS Ch 14.3.3]]).
- [pthread_cond_destroy](concepts/PthreadCondDestroy.md) — [[Pthreads]] condition variable teardown ([[dis-14-3-3-other-syncs|DIS Ch 14.3.3]]).
- [Parallel Speedup](concepts/ParallelSpeedup.md) — Formal [[ParallelComputing|parallel-computing]] performance metric: $\text{Speedup}(c) = T_1/T_c$ ([[dis-14-4-1-performance-basics|DIS Ch 14.4.1]]). Formalizes the informal 1/c rule from [[dis-14-1-multicore|Ch 14.1.2]]'s [[Speedup]]; bounded above by [[AmdahlsLaw|Amdahl]] in the [[StrongScaling|strong-scaling]] regime, linear in $c$ under [[GustafsonsLaw|Gustafson]] in the [[WeakScaling|weak-scaling]] regime. Superlinear speedup (>$c$) possible via per-thread working sets fitting in cache.
- [Parallel Efficiency](concepts/ParallelEfficiency.md) — Per-core utilization metric: $\text{Efficiency}(c) = \text{Speedup}(c)/c$ ([[dis-14-4-1-performance-basics|DIS Ch 14.4.1]]). Range $[0,1]$; **1.0 = linear-speedup ideal**, declines as cores grow per [[AmdahlsLaw|Amdahl]]. Makes per-core cost visible — 8× speedup on 16 cores = 0.5 efficiency = half the hardware is idle.
- [Amdahl's Law](concepts/AmdahlsLaw.md) — Theoretical speedup ceiling for the serial fraction $S$ of a program ([[dis-14-4-1-performance-basics|DIS Ch 14.4.1]]): $\text{Speedup}(c) = 1/(S + P/c)$, asymptote $1/S$ as $c \to \infty$. **90% parallelizable code caps at 10×**, regardless of cores. Assumes **fixed problem size** — the assumption [[GustafsonsLaw|Gustafson-Barsis]] inverts. Bounds [[StrongScaling|strong scaling]].
- [Gustafson-Barsis Law](concepts/GustafsonsLaw.md) — Problem-scaling alternative to [[AmdahlsLaw|Amdahl's Law]] ([[dis-14-4-2-performance-advanced|DIS Ch 14.4.2]]): assumes problem size grows with cores, so the parallel fraction grows too — *"the amount of work that can be done in parallel varies linearly with the number of processors."* Linear in $c$, justifies HPC machines. Bounds [[WeakScaling|weak scaling]]. Core count and parallel fraction are *"virtually never"* independent in practice.
- [Strong Scaling](concepts/StrongScaling.md) — Scalability regime: **fixed problem, grow cores** ([[dis-14-4-2-performance-advanced|DIS Ch 14.4.2]]). Linear strong scaling means $\text{Speedup}(c) = c$; bounded by [[AmdahlsLaw|Amdahl]]. Curves flatten as cores grow — diminishing returns from the serial fraction. Right metric for latency-critical jobs and hardware evaluation.
- [Weak Scaling](concepts/WeakScaling.md) — Scalability regime: **grow problem and cores together**, each core sees fixed work ([[dis-14-4-2-performance-advanced|DIS Ch 14.4.2]]). Linear weak scaling means **runtime stays constant** as $c$ and problem size grow; bounded by [[GustafsonsLaw|Gustafson-Barsis]]. The regime that justifies HPC / cluster machines (more cores → bigger problems, not faster small problems).
- [Test Coverage](concepts/Coverage.md) — fraction of code exercised by a test suite.
- [Test Set Reuse (Adaptive Overfitting)](concepts/TestSetReuse.md) — Repeated test-set evaluation invalidates its unbiased-estimator property: (i) multiple-hypothesis testing blows up per-classifier false-discovery rates; (ii) information leaks to the modeler, breaking the IID-of-classifier-choice premise of Hoeffding's analysis (Dwork et al. 2015). [[d2l-linear-classification]] anchor.
- [Testing](concepts/Testing.md) — discipline of validating code, data, and models.
- [Text-to-Text Framework](concepts/texttotextframework.md) — Unified NLP interface casting every task as string→string with a task-prefix prompt; introduced for T5.
- [Text Classification](concepts/TextClassification.md) — assigning categorical labels to text.
- [Tokenization](concepts/Tokenization.md) — splitting text into model-input units.
- [Trace](concepts/Trace.md) — Sum of diagonal entries of a square matrix ([[mml-book]] §4.1); cyclic-invariant, basis-invariant, equals sum of eigenvalues. Frobenius norm and many regression derivations rewrite via trace.
- [Tokenizer](concepts/Tokenizer.md) — component implementing tokenization.
- [Timer / Counter](concepts/TimerCounter.md) — MCU peripheral that increments on every clock tick to generate delays, count events, produce [[PulseWidthModulation|PWM]], drive periodic interrupts. [[ATmega328P]] has three (TC0/TC1 8-bit, TC2 16-bit; the Arduino runtime uses TC0/TC1 for `delay()`/`millis()`) ([[embedded-controllers-fiore]] ch. 28).
- [Topological Edge Weight](concepts/TopologicalEdgeWeight.md) — Liao et al. Lemma 4.4: $\mathcal{W}(e^*) = $ Upstream History · Local Valve · Downstream Future — the gradient flux through a specific edge; design rule: contractive at long-chain endpoints, ultra-tight before critical decisions.
- [Topological Weight](concepts/TopologicalWeight.md) — Liao et al. Lemma 4.2: $\omega_u = \|d\mathcal{L}/dx_u\|$ — per-agent gradient sensitivity aggregated along all paths to sinks; building block of [[CompositionalCapacity]].
- [Timesharing](concepts/Timesharing.md) — OS mechanism giving each process a short CPU turn (quantum/timeslice, typically 50–60 ms) enforced via hardware timer interrupts; rapid turn-taking creates the illusion of simultaneous execution. Foundation for understanding process scheduling costs in parallel programs. ([[parproc-appA-systems-issues]] §A.1)
- [Train/Val/Test Split](concepts/TrainValTestSplit.md) — partitioning data for fit, tune, and test.
- [Trainer](concepts/Trainer.md) — abstraction encapsulating training loops.
- [Training-Serving Skew](concepts/TrainingServingSkew.md) — mismatch between training and production data/transforms.
- [Transfer Learning](concepts/TransferLearning.md) — reusing pretrained knowledge for new tasks.
- [Translation Invariance](concepts/TranslationInvariance.md) — Function unchanged by input shifts; the prior that, imposed on an MLP, forces the [[Convolution|convolution]] operator ([[d2l-convolutional-neural-networks]] §why-conv). Conv layers are translation *equivariant*; [[MaxPooling]] adds local *invariance*.
- [Translation Lookaside Buffer](concepts/TranslationLookasideBuffer.md) — Hardware cache for page-table entries in a [[VirtualMemory]] system; eliminates the double memory-access overhead of virtual-to-physical address translation. Flushed or invalidated on [[ContextSwitch]], adding TLB warm-up cost to context switching. ([[parproc-appA-systems-issues]] §A.2.3)
- [Transformer](concepts/transformer.md) — 
- [Teacher Forcing](concepts/TeacherForcing.md) — Autoregressive-LM training scheme: feed the ground-truth previous token at every step (targets = inputs shifted by 1); enables parallel within-sequence training but introduces exposure bias at inference ([[d2l-recurrent-neural-networks]]).
- [Tree Barrier](concepts/TreeBarrier.md) — Parallelized [[Barrier]] structured as $\log_2 n$ levels of nested sub-barriers; reduces serial fan-in from $O(n)$ to $O(\log n)$ ([[parproc-ch03-shared-memory-parallelism]] §3.12.4.2.1). Sibling of [[ButterflyBarrier]].
- [Tree of Thoughts (ToT)](concepts/TreeOfThoughts.md) — Yao et al. NeurIPS 2023 prompting framework; recast in [[2402.01817-llm-modulo]] as "prompt diversification" — any soundness comes from external problem-specific verifiers, not the tree.
- [Truncated BPTT](concepts/TruncatedBPTT.md) — Practical BPTT variants — full / regular / randomized truncation — terminating the gradient recursion after a finite window. Regular truncation (Jaeger 2002) is what frameworks implement; randomized (Tallec & Ollivier 2017) is unbiased but empirically no better ([[d2l-recurrent-neural-networks]]).
- [Trust Root](concepts/trustroot.md) — 
- [Turn Management (Co-STORM)](concepts/TurnManagement.md) — The protocol in [[CoSTORM|Co-STORM]] that decides who speaks next: user injection preempts; otherwise round-robin among experts; after $L=2$ consecutive non-question turns the system invokes the [[ModeratorAgent|moderator]] to redirect. Implements [[MixedInitiativeDiscourse|mixed-initiative]] dialogue.
- [Type Hints](concepts/TypeHints.md) — Python static type annotations.
- [Typer](concepts/Typer.md) — Python CLI library built on type hints.
- [Underfitting](concepts/Underfitting.md) — Model too simple → high training error + small [[GeneralizationGap|gap]]; the diagnostic mirror image of [[Overfitting]] ([[d2l-linear-regression]] §3.6).
- [Unknown Unknowns](concepts/UnknownUnknowns.md) — Information the user is *unaware they should be seeking* ([[Kirzner1997|Kirzner 1997]] *discovery* vs *successful search*); the central design target of [[CoSTORM|Co-STORM]] — surfaced via multi-perspective experts + the [[ModeratorAgent|moderator]]'s **uncited-source reranking**.
- [Utterance Intent (Co-STORM)](concepts/UtteranceIntent.md) — Four-way intent taxonomy in [[CoSTORM|Co-STORM]] (Original Question / Information Request / Potential Answer / Further Details) from [[QuEtAl2019|Qu et al. 2019]]; partitions into *question-asking* (no search) vs *question-answering* (retrieve + cite); drives the [[TurnManagement|turn-management]] override.
- [Uniform Convergence](concepts/UniformConvergence.md) — Statistical-learning-theory property: with high probability, the empirical error of *every* classifier $f\in\mathcal F$ simultaneously converges to its true error. Justifies [[EmpiricalRiskMinimization|ERM]] generalization when paired with a complexity measure ([[VCDimension|VC dimension]], Rademacher) ([[d2l-linear-classification]]).
- [Universal Approximation Theorem](concepts/UniversalApproximationTheorem.md) — Single-hidden-layer MLP with arbitrary width can approximate any continuous function ([[GeorgeCybenko|Cybenko 1989]]); existence ≠ learnability; depth still wins in practice ([[d2l-multilayer-perceptrons]]).
- [Unit Testing](concepts/UnitTesting.md) — testing the smallest functional units in isolation.
- [Uninitialized Read (Memory Error)](concepts/UninitializedReadError.md) — The [[CLanguage|C]] bug class where the program reads from memory that has been **allocated but never written**. *"Accessing values from memory that haven't been initialized, such as `x = ptr[3]` when that array index hasn't been assigned"* per [[dis-3-3-valgrind|DIS Ch 3.3]]. Returns whatever bit pattern was left over — silent when it happens to be benign, catastrophic when it isn't. Detected by [[Memcheck]] via per-bit V-bit shadow tracking propagated through arithmetic, errored only on **use** (branch / syscall / output). The classic *flaky / disappears-under-the-debugger* bug. ([[dis-3-3-valgrind]]).
- [University of Maryland (UMD)](concepts/universityofmaryland.md) — Primary author affiliation on [[2605.08083-autotts]] ([[AutoTTS]]); [[HengHuang]]'s group runs the Parallel-Probe / AutoTTS TTS-discovery line via [[TongZheng]]. (Filed under concepts/ for historical reasons; semantically an entity.)
- [Valgrind](concepts/Valgrind.md) — **Dynamic binary-instrumentation framework** for [[CLanguage|C]] / C++ whose flagship tool [[Memcheck]] detects heap memory errors — *"Valgrind's Memcheck debugging tool highlights heap memory errors in programs"* ([[dis-3-3-valgrind|DIS Ch 3.3]]). Workflow: `gcc -g` + `valgrind -v ./a.out` (+ `--leak-check=yes` for per-leak detail). Heap-only — *"does not detect stack memory access errors at the same granularity as it does with heap memory, and it does not detect memory access errors with global data memory"*. ~10–50× slowdown, no recompilation needed. The **second** of [[dis-2-10-summary|Ch 2.10]]'s two debugging tools (after [[GDB]]); promoted from forward-ref stub. ([[dis-3-3-valgrind]]).
- [Vanishing Gradient](concepts/VanishingGradient.md) — gradients shrinking to zero in deep nets.
- [Verification Levels](concepts/verificationlevels.md) — 
- [Versioning](concepts/Versioning.md) — tracking changes to code, data, and models.
- [Virtual Environment](concepts/VirtualEnvironment.md) — isolated Python interpreter and dependencies.
- [Virtual Memory](concepts/VirtualMemory.md) — OS/hardware mechanism mapping each program's virtual addresses to physical RAM via a page table; goals are overcoming physical memory limits, relieving the compiler of real-address management, and enforcing security. Non-resident pages generate page faults (OS + disk access) — catastrophically more expensive than cache misses. The [[TranslationLookasideBuffer]] avoids double memory access per translation. ([[parproc-appA-systems-issues]] §A.2.2)
- [Voyager](concepts/voyager.md) — 
- [Weight Decay](concepts/WeightDecay.md) — $\ell_2$ [[Regularization]]: penalize $\tfrac{\lambda}{2}\|\mathbf{w}\|^2$; the [[MinibatchSGD|SGD]] update becomes $\mathbf{w}\leftarrow(1-\eta\lambda)\mathbf{w}-\eta\hat{\mathbf{g}}$, literally *decaying* weights each step. Framework-integrated into the optimizer ([[d2l-linear-regression]] §3.7).
- [Watchpoint](concepts/Watchpoint.md) — [[Debugger|debugger]] primitive that **pauses on memory write** (`watch expr`) rather than PC reach — the *data-trigger* counterpart to [[Breakpoint|breakpoints]]. Hardware-assisted on most architectures (x86: DR0–DR3 debug registers; ARM: watchpoint control units) — 4 hardware slots typical, software fallback is single-step-and-check at ~100× slowdown. Variants: `watch` (write), `rwatch` (read), `awatch` (read or write). Canonical use: **find the line that corrupts a variable** — GDB reports `Old value` / `New value` at the exact write site. Shares the [[GdbBreakpointManagement|`enable` / `disable` / `delete`]] lifecycle with breakpoints ([[dis-3-1-gdb|Ch 3.1]] / [[dis-3-2-gdb-commands|Ch 3.2]]).
- [Weight Initialization](concepts/WeightInitialization.md) — choosing starting values for network parameters.
- [Width–Depth Search](concepts/WidthDepthSearch.md) — 2D control space spanning [[testtimescaling|TTS]]: width = parallel branches, depth = per-branch generation budget. [[2605.08083-autotts|AutoTTS]] shows every TTS algorithm (SC@64, ASC, ESC, ST-BoN, Parallel-Probe) is a hand-designed path through this space; controllers can be discovered automatically over it.
- [WildSeek (dataset)](concepts/WildSeek.md) — 100 (topic, goal) pairs across 24 domains, collected from the publicly-deployed [[STORM]] web app, rule-filtered + [[gpt-4o|GPT-4o]]-classified for motivation quality. Introduced in [[2408.15232-co-storm]]. **First dataset in this wiki to capture user *goals***, not just queries.
- [Xavier Initialization](concepts/XavierInitialization.md) — Glorot variance $\sigma^2 = 2/(n_\text{in}+n_\text{out})$; the [[WeightInitialization|initialization]] for symmetric activations ([[Tanh]] / [[Sigmoid]]); ReLU variant is [[HeInitialization|He]] ([[d2l-multilayer-perceptrons]]).
- [Word2Vec](concepts/Word2Vec.md) — shallow neural model for word embeddings.
- [WordPiece](concepts/wordpiece.md) — 
- [Workload Function](concepts/WorkloadFunction.md) — user-defined callable for distributed runtimes.
- [Work Stealing](concepts/WorkStealing.md) — A peer-to-peer [[DynamicTaskAssignment|dynamic-task-assignment]] strategy where idle threads raid the work queues of busy peers; the [[Cilk|Cilk language]]'s approach. [[NormMatloff]] cautions in [[parproc-ch02-recurring-performance-issues]] §2.4.4 that *"accessing the other work queue is going to be expensive in terms of time and memory contention overhead."*
- [Writing Granularity (TSW / SSW / MSW)](concepts/writinggranularity.md) — Three δ-mem state-update strategies: per-token, per-message-segment, multiple parallel sub-states.
- [Zero-Shot Learning](concepts/ZeroShotLearning.md) — task performance without labeled examples.
- [Zipf's Law](concepts/ZipfsLaw.md) — Empirical power-law observation that word-rank-$i$ frequency $n_i \propto i^{-\alpha}$; bigrams and trigrams also follow Zipf's law with smaller exponents. The structural reason count-based $n$-gram LMs break down ([[d2l-recurrent-neural-networks]]).
- [δ-mem](concepts/deltamem.md) — Online-state memory mechanism augmenting a frozen Transformer; from [[2605.12357-delta-mem]].

### From *Python for Data Analysis 3E* (May 2026 ingest)
- [Broadcasting](concepts/Broadcasting.md) — NumPy's shape-alignment rule for element-wise ops on differently-shaped arrays; trailing-dimension matching; broadcast axes are read-only views, not copies.
- [Bitonic Mergesort](concepts/BitonicMergesort.md) — Parallel sorting network based on bitonic sequences; pairwise [[CompareExchange]] operations split a bitonic sequence into two bitonic halves; O(log² n) parallel steps ([[parproc-ch12-parallel-sorting]] §12.2.5).
- [Bubble Sort](concepts/BubbleSort.md) — O(n²) serial comparison sort; inner-loop [[CompareExchange]] structure parallelizes directly in shared memory; basis for [[OddEvenTransposition]] ([[parproc-ch12-parallel-sorting]] §12.3.1).
- [Bucket Sort](concepts/BucketSort.md) — Range-partition sorting algorithm; substrate for the parallel [[SamplingBucketSort]] variant ([[parproc-ch01-intro-parallel-processing]]).
- [Categorical Data](concepts/CategoricalData.md) — pandas extension dtype storing integer codes + categories array; memory-efficient for low-cardinality strings; faster groupby. Analogous to R's `factor`.
- [DataFrame](concepts/DataFrame.md) — 2-D column-oriented labeled table; the central [[pandas]] data structure. Modeled after R's `data.frame`; each column is a [[Series]] sharing a common row [[pandasIndex|Index]].
- [Extension Data Types](concepts/ExtensionDataTypes.md) — pandas extension arrays beyond NumPy: nullable `Int64`/`boolean`/`string` (with `pd.NA`), `category`, tz-aware `datetime64[ns, tz]`. Solves the "missing data forces float64" pain.
- [Global Interpreter Lock (GIL)](concepts/GlobalInterpreterLock.md) — CPython mechanism preventing concurrent execution of Python bytecode; limits CPU-bound multithreading. Escape via multi-process, C-extensions that release the GIL, or [[Numba]] `nogil`.
- [HDF5](concepts/HDF5.md) — Hierarchical Data Format v5; self-describing binary container for typed N-D arrays + groups. `h5py` / PyTables / `pd.HDFStore`. Strong for scientific arrays; [[Parquet]] is the table sibling.
- [Hierarchical Indexing (MultiIndex)](concepts/HierarchicalIndexing.md) — pandas index with multiple levels per axis; lets a 2-D DataFrame represent higher-dimensional data. Backbone of `stack`/`unstack` reshape and `groupby` on index levels.
- [IPython](concepts/IPython.md) — Enhanced interactive Python shell (Fernando Pérez, 2001); tab completion, introspection (`?`/`??`), magic commands (`%run`/`%timeit`/`%debug`/`%pdb`), shell integration. The Python kernel powering [[Jupyter]].
- [Jupyter](concepts/Jupyter.md) — Web-based notebook platform spun out of IPython (2014); language-agnostic kernel architecture (40+ kernels); `.ipynb` JSON file format. Python kernel = IPython.
- [matplotlib](concepts/matplotlib.md) — Foundational Python plotting library (John Hunter, 2002); MATLAB-style API; publication-quality static figures; substrate of [[seaborn]] and pandas's `.plot` accessor.
- [ndarray](concepts/NDArray.md) — NumPy's N-dimensional homogeneous array; data pointer + dtype + shape + strides. Strides enable zero-copy views (slicing, transpose, reverse).
- [Numba](concepts/Numba.md) — LLVM-based JIT compiler for Python; `@numba.njit` / `@numba.vectorize` / `@guvectorize`; reaches C-level speed on numeric Python; can release the [[GlobalInterpreterLock|GIL]].
- [NumPy](concepts/NumPy.md) — Foundational numerical-computing package for Python; ndarray + ufuncs + broadcasting + linear algebra + PRNG + C API. Forged in 2005 by Travis Oliphant from Numeric + Numarray.
- [pandas](concepts/pandas.md) — Dominant Python library for structured / tabular / time-series data analysis. [[Series]] + [[DataFrame]] + [[pandasIndex|Index]] + groupby + reshape + IO + time series. Created by [[WesMcKinney]] in 2008 at [[AQRCapitalManagement]].
- [pandas Index](concepts/pandasIndex.md) — Immutable labeled axis attached to [[Series]] / [[DataFrame]]; enables label-based selection and arithmetic data alignment. Variants: RangeIndex, DatetimeIndex, PeriodIndex, CategoricalIndex, MultiIndex.
- [Apache Parquet](concepts/Parquet.md) — Columnar binary file format with embedded schema and per-column compression; de facto interchange format between data tools. pandas: `pd.read_parquet` / `df.to_parquet` (`pyarrow` backend).
- [Patsy](concepts/Patsy.md) — R-style formula library (`y ~ x0 + x1 + C(category)`) for building design matrices; bundled with [[statsmodels]].
- [Python (language)](concepts/PythonLanguage.md) — General-purpose dynamically-typed interpreted language; significant indentation; everything-is-an-object; "glue" interop with C/C++/FORTRAN; dominant data-analysis language via the NumPy / pandas / sklearn / matplotlib / IPython stack.
- [Resampling](concepts/Resampling.md) — Time-indexed analog of [[SplitApplyCombine|groupby]] in pandas: bin a time series into fixed-frequency intervals and aggregate. `ts.resample("M").mean()`; OHLC; `pd.Grouper(freq=)`.
- [scikit-learn](concepts/scikitlearn.md) — Dominant Python ML library; uniform estimator API (`.fit`/`.predict`/`.score`). Classification / regression / clustering / dim. reduction / preprocessing / model selection. Pipelines + ColumnTransformer + GridSearchCV.
- [SciPy](concepts/SciPy.md) — Scientific-computing sub-package collection on top of [[NumPy]]: integrate / linalg / optimize / signal / sparse / special / stats. Pair with NumPy for MATLAB-equivalent coverage.
- [seaborn](concepts/seaborn.md) — High-level statistical visualization library on top of [[matplotlib]]; tidy-DataFrame-aware (`data=`, `x=`, `y=`, `hue=`); relplot / catplot / histplot / regplot / pairplot.
- [Series](concepts/Series.md) — pandas 1-D labeled array (values + Index); the column type of [[DataFrame]]; vectorized arithmetic with index-based alignment.
- [Split-Apply-Combine](concepts/SplitApplyCombine.md) — [[HadleyWickham]]'s organizing pattern (2011 *JSS*): split data by keys, apply a function per group, combine results. pandas implementation: `groupby(...).agg`/`.transform`/`.filter`/`.apply`.
- [statsmodels](concepts/statsmodels.md) — Python library for classical statistical modeling (OLS / GLS / GLM / Logit, AR/ARIMA, state-space, nonparametric, tests). Emphasizes *inference* (SE, p-values, CIs) where [[scikitlearn]] emphasizes prediction.
- [Universal Functions (ufuncs)](concepts/UniversalFunctions.md) — Element-wise NumPy functions that operate on ndarrays in a single C loop (unary + binary, all broadcasting-aware); ufunc methods include `.reduce`, `.accumulate`, `.outer`, `.reduceat`.

### Added with [[2605.06651v2-ai-co-mathematician]] (AI co-mathematician)
- [AI co-mathematician](concepts/AICoMathematician.md) — [[googledeepmind|Google DeepMind]] interactive agentic workbench for math research; harness over [[gemini|Gemini 3.1 Pro]] + [[GeminiDeepThink|Deep Think]]; 48% on [[FrontierMath]] Tier 4; seven design principles.
- [Project Coordinator Agent](concepts/ProjectCoordinatorAgent.md) — Top-level agent in [[AICoMathematician]] hierarchy that converses with the user, formalizes intent, delegates [[WorkstreamCoordinator|Workstream Coordinators]].
- [Workstream Coordinator](concepts/WorkstreamCoordinator.md) — Per-goal coordinator that runs linear action sequences, spawns specialized sub-agents, produces a fully-reviewed LaTeX [[WorkingPaper|working paper]].
- [Working Paper](concepts/WorkingPaper.md) — The native LaTeX artifact in AI co-mathematician — exposition + margin annotations + internal links + reviewer-passed.
- [Progressive Disclosure](concepts/ProgressiveDisclosure.md) — UX design principle: interface mirrors agent hierarchy; high-level intent by default, drill-down on demand.
- [Reviewer-Pleasing Bias](concepts/ReviewerPleasingBias.md) — Failure mode (False Consensus): strict reviewer satisfiability can converge on flawed but undetectable arguments — empirical instance of the [[BystanderEffect]] inside a reviewer bank.
- [Death Spiral](concepts/DeathSpiral.md) — Non-Termination failure mode of iterative reviewer loops; degrades into increasingly hallucinated reasoning. Dual of [[ReviewerPleasingBias]].
- [Jagged Frontier](concepts/JaggedFrontier.md) — Dell'Acqua et al. framing for the uneven capability surface of frontier AI; motivates broader evaluation.
- [Gemini Deep Think](concepts/GeminiDeepThink.md) — Deep-reasoning variant of [[gemini|Gemini]]; prover sub-agent in AI co-mathematician.
- [FrontierMath](concepts/FrontierMath.md) — [[EpochAI]] research-math benchmark; Tier 4 = 50 problems crafted as short-term research projects. AI co-mathematician = 23/48 (48%, new high).
- [IMO Proof Bench](concepts/IMOProofBench.md) — IMO-style proof benchmark; one of the static problem-solving benchmarks the AI co-mathematician paper argues the field over-relies on.
- [PutnamBench](concepts/PutnamBench.md) — Putnam competition benchmark; same critique.
- [MATH benchmark](concepts/MATH-benchmark.md) — Hendrycks et al. 2021 competition-math benchmark.
- [GSM8K](concepts/GSM8K.md) — Cobbe et al. 2021 grade-school math word-problem benchmark.
- [DeepSearchQA](concepts/DeepSearchQA.md) — General fact-finding benchmark; auxiliary capability emphasized in the AI co-mathematician evaluation argument.
- [Hard2Verify](concepts/Hard2Verify.md) — Mistake-finding benchmark in competition-math proofs.
- [Kourovka Notebook](concepts/KourovkaNotebook.md) — Group-theory open-problem collection; Problem 21.10 (just-finite presentations) resolved by Lackenby with AI co-mathematician.
- [Stirling Coefficients](concepts/StirlingCoefficients.md) — Symmetric-power-representation case study (Bérczi); log-concavity conjectures.
- [Hamiltonian Diffeomorphism](concepts/HamiltonianDiffeomorphism.md) — Rezchikov perturbation-lemma case study.
- [Moving Sofa Problem](concepts/MovingSofaProblem.md) — Computational-geometry open problem (Moser 1966); the walkthrough example in AI co-mathematician §3.
- [Minerva](concepts/Minerva.md) — Lewkowycz et al. 2022; founding modern AI-for-math line.
- [Galactica](concepts/Galactica.md) — Meta science LM 2022.
- [Llemma](concepts/Llemma.md) — Open math LM 2024.
- [Mathstral](concepts/Mathstral.md) — Mistral AI math 7B.
- [Qwen2.5-Math](concepts/Qwen25Math.md) — Alibaba math LM 2024.
- [DeepSeekMath](concepts/DeepSeekMath.md) — Open math LM 2024.
- [The AI Scientist](concepts/AIScientist.md) — Sakana AI automated discovery system 2024.
- [The AI Scientist v2](concepts/AIScientistV2.md) — Workshop-level automated discovery 2025.
- [Skywork Open Reasoner](concepts/SkyworkOpenReasoner.md) — Open reasoner 2025.

### From [[islr-seventh-printing|ISLR]] (Ch.2–10)
- [Backward Stepwise Selection](concepts/BackwardStepwiseSelection.md) — Greedy top-down subset selection; drops least-useful predictor each step.
- [Bagging](concepts/Bagging.md) — Bootstrap-aggregating high-variance learners ([[DecisionTrees]]); Breiman 1996.
- [Basis Functions](concepts/BasisFunctions.md) — Fixed non-linear transforms turning a linear model into a flexible regressor.
- [Best Subset Selection](concepts/BestSubsetSelection.md) — Exact $2^p$ search for the best-fitting subset; infeasible past $p\approx 40$.
- [Bias-Variance Trade-Off](concepts/BiasVarianceTradeoff.md) — Decomposition of expected test error; lens for every chapter in ISLR.
- [Boosting](concepts/Boosting.md) — Sequential small-tree ensemble fitting residuals; ancestor of XGBoost/LightGBM.
- [Bootstrap](concepts/Bootstrap.md) — Efron's resampling with replacement; standard errors for any estimator; foundation of [[Bagging]].
- [BootstrapFewShot](concepts/BootstrapFewShot.md) — DSPy's **canonical few-shot demonstration-tuning optimizer** from [[dspy-optimizers]] (page 13 of 13). `dspy.BootstrapFewShot` — the recommended starting point for any [[DSPyOptimizers|optimization run]] with around **10 training examples**. Tunes **only demonstrations** (the few-shot examples in each [[DSPyPredict|`dspy.Predict`]]'s prompt), leaving instructions and weights untouched. Three-step mechanism: (1) sample up to `max_labeled_demos` ground-truth examples from `trainset`; (2) run a `teacher` module (defaults to your program) to bootstrap additional traces; filter via the [[DSPyMetrics|metric]] in `trace is not None` mode (strict-bool return); keep only metric-passing traces; (3) install metric-passing demos as each Predict's `demos` attribute. Optional `teacher=...` kwarg enables **stronger-teacher / weaker-student** setups for harder tasks. The structural primitive — *metric-validated trace collection* — is shared with [[BootstrapFewShotWithRandomSearch]], `KNNFewShot`, [[MIPROv2]] (bootstrapping stage), and [[BootstrapFinetune]].
- [BootstrapFewShotWithRandomSearch](concepts/BootstrapFewShotWithRandomSearch.md) — DSPy's **random-search-augmented version of [[BootstrapFewShot]]** from [[dspy-optimizers]]. `dspy.BootstrapFewShotWithRandomSearch` — recommended for runs with **50+ training examples**. Wraps [[BootstrapFewShot]] with random search over multiple bootstrap seeds; selects the best candidate program. Candidate set evaluated: uncompiled original + `LabeledFewShot`-optimized + [[BootstrapFewShot]] with unshuffled examples + `num_candidate_programs` randomized [[BootstrapFewShot]] candidates. The randomization defends against [[BootstrapFewShot]]'s single-seed brittleness — different demo orderings can produce meaningfully different program behaviors. Used as the **canonical worked-example** for the general optimizer API in the page's *How do I use an optimizer?* section (note: variable name `teleprompter` is a legacy holdover from the pre-rename era — *"Formerly called teleprompters"*).
- [BetterTogether](concepts/BetterTogether.md) — DSPy's **meta-optimizer** from [[2407.10930-better-together|Soylu, Potts & Khattab (2024)]]. `dspy.BetterTogether` — alternates [[BootstrapFewShotWithRandomSearch|BFRS]] prompt optimization with [[BootstrapFinetune|BFT]] weight fine-tuning in a three-step schedule **Π → Θ → Π**. Wins in **7 of 9** (task, LM) cells across HotPotQA / GSM8K / Iris × Mistral-7B / Llama-2-7B / Llama-3-8B; gains 5–78% / 2.5–10% / 3.5–88% over the better single-axis baseline. Establishes the canonical two-direction motivation: prompt-opt *before* fine-tune yields a higher-quality SFT dataset; prompt-opt *after* fine-tune adjusts prompts to the shifted prior. The **only Meta-Optimizer family entry** in the catalog.
- [BootstrapFinetune](concepts/BootstrapFinetune.md) — DSPy's **only weight-tuning optimizer** from [[dspy-optimizers]]. `dspy.BootstrapFinetune` — the bridge between DSPy's prompt-tuning regime (every other optimizer) and the underlying LM's [[FineTuning|fine-tuning]] regime. *"Distills a prompt-based DSPy program into weight updates. The output is a DSPy program that has the same steps, but where each step is conducted by a finetuned model instead of a prompted LM."* Two-step mechanism: bootstrap traces with metric filter (same as [[BootstrapFewShot]]) → fine-tune the LM on the filtered traces as a supervised-fine-tuning dataset. The **only optimizer in the catalog that targets the LM's weights** rather than its prompts; realizes the *"or weights"* half of [[DSPyOptimization|the three-input contract's]] *"tune the prompts or weights"* commitment. **Post-success efficiency move**: recommended workflow is *first prompt-optimize with a large LM (7B+), then BootstrapFinetune to distill into a smaller LM*. Worked Banking77 receipt: 2000 examples; [[ChainOfThought|`dspy.ChainOfThought`]]; `Literal[tuple(CLASSES)]`-typed [[DSPySignatures|Signature]]; simple lambda metric; `classify.set_lm(lm)` per-Module LM binding (**the only `set_lm(...)` exercise in the entire *Learn* corpus**); **66% → 87% improvement on GPT-4o-mini** — the largest of the three worked receipts on page 13. Implicitly outside the [[DSPyOptimization|workflow page's]] inverted 20/80 train/val split (the *prompt optimizers tend to overfit* rationale doesn't apply to weight-tuning).
- [Classification and Regression Trees (CART)](concepts/ClassificationAndRegressionTrees.md) — Breiman et al. 1984; recursive binary partitioning with cost-complexity pruning.
- [Classification Tree](concepts/ClassificationTree.md) — Majority-class tree fit with [[GiniIndex]] / cross-entropy splits.
- [Cross-Validation](concepts/CrossValidation.md) — Resampling test-error estimator; standard tuning-parameter selector.
- [Decision Trees](concepts/DecisionTrees.md) — Recursive binary partitions; interpretable but high-variance; basis for tree ensembles.
- [Dendrogram](concepts/Dendrogram.md) — Tree visualization of [[HierarchicalClustering]] merges.
- [The Elements of Statistical Learning (ESL)](concepts/ElementsOfStatisticalLearning.md) — Hastie/Tibshirani/Friedman 2001/2009; the technical reference ISLR re-presents accessibly.
- [Forward Stepwise Selection](concepts/ForwardStepwiseSelection.md) — Greedy bottom-up subset selection; adds best predictor each step.
- [Generalized Additive Models (GAMs)](concepts/GeneralizedAdditiveModels.md) — $y = \beta_0 + \sum_j f_j(x_j) + \epsilon$ with smooth per-feature $f_j$; Hastie & Tibshirani 1986.
- [Generalized Linear Models (GLMs)](concepts/GeneralizedLinearModels.md) — Nelder & Wedderburn 1972; unifies linear + logistic + Poisson regression via link functions.
- [Gini Index](concepts/GiniIndex.md) — Node-impurity split criterion for [[ClassificationTree|classification trees]].
- [Hierarchical Clustering](concepts/HierarchicalClustering.md) — Agglomerative nested clustering visualized as a [[Dendrogram]]; no pre-specified $K$.
- [k-Fold Cross-Validation](concepts/KFoldCrossValidation.md) — $k\in\{5,10\}$; the standard bias-variance compromise.
- [K-Means Clustering](concepts/KMeansClustering.md) — Lloyd's algorithm; partitions into pre-specified $K$ clusters minimizing within-cluster SS.
- [K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN)](concepts/KNearestNeighbors.md) — Non-parametric average-of-neighbors predictor; suffers in high $p$.
- [Lasso](concepts/Lasso.md) — $\ell_1$-penalized regression; performs variable selection; Tibshirani 1996.
- [Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation (LOOCV)](concepts/LeaveOneOutCrossValidation.md) — $n$-fold CV; low bias, high variance; closed-form shortcut for OLS.
- [Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA)](concepts/LinearDiscriminantAnalysis.md) — Bayes-rule classifier under shared-covariance Gaussian classes; Fisher 1936.
- [Local Regression](concepts/LocalRegression.md) — LOESS — locally weighted polynomial fits at each target point.
- [Maximal Margin Classifier](concepts/MaximalMarginClassifier.md) — Hard-margin separating hyperplane; ancestor of the [[SupportVectorMachine|SVM]].
- [Partial Least Squares (PLS)](concepts/PartialLeastSquares.md) — Supervised dimension-reduction regression; covariance-maximizing components.
- [Polynomial Regression](concepts/PolynomialRegression.md) — Linear model in $\{x, x^2, \dots, x^d\}$; global curvature with one knob.
- [Principal Components Regression (PCR)](concepts/PrincipalComponentsRegression.md) — Regress $Y$ on top-$M$ [[PCA]] components; unsupervised dimension reduction.
- [Quadratic Discriminant Analysis (QDA)](concepts/QuadraticDiscriminantAnalysis.md) — [[LinearDiscriminantAnalysis|LDA]] with per-class covariances; quadratic decision boundary.
- [ROC Curve](concepts/ROCCurve.md) — TPR-vs-FPR plot summarizing a classifier's threshold trade-off.
- [Random Forests](concepts/RandomForests.md) — [[Bagging]] + random per-split predictor sampling that decorrelates trees; Breiman 2001.
- [Regression Splines](concepts/RegressionSplines.md) — Piecewise polynomials joined at knots; basis-expansion fit by OLS.
- [Regression Tree](concepts/RegressionTree.md) — [[DecisionTrees|Decision tree]] predicting region means; RSS-based splits.
- [Ridge Regression](concepts/RidgeRegression.md) — $\ell_2$-penalized regression; shrinks but keeps all coefficients.
- [Smoothing Splines](concepts/SmoothingSplines.md) — Penalized-RSS spline with $\int g''(t)^2\,dt$ smoothness penalty.
- [Statistical Learning](concepts/StatisticalLearning.md) — The field's umbrella term; toolbox for modeling and understanding data.
- [Step Debugging (`next` / `step` / `cont`)](concepts/StepDebug.md) — [[GDB]]'s three execution-advance primitives after a [[Breakpoint|breakpoint]] halt. `next` advances one source line treating function calls as opaque (one step); `step` advances one source line entering called functions (requires [[DebugSymbol|symbols]] to descend meaningfully); `cont` resumes until the next breakpoint, crash, or termination. Plus `stepi` / `nexti` (instruction-level), `finish` (run to current function's return), `until` (run out of current source line). Headline rule from [[dis-3-1-gdb|Ch 3.1]]: *"to inspect the function's behavior, use `step` instead of `next`."* Distinct from [[PointerIncrement|pointer step]] (`ptr++`) and [[StepFunctions|step functions]] (analysis) — three unrelated uses of *step* in the wiki ([[dis-3-1-gdb]]).
- [Step Functions](concepts/StepFunctions.md) — Bin-indicator basis for piecewise-constant fits.
- [Supervised Learning](concepts/SupervisedLearning.md) — Predict $Y$ from $X$ given labeled training pairs.
- [Support Vector Classifier](concepts/SupportVectorClassifier.md) — Soft-margin generalization of the [[MaximalMarginClassifier]].
- [Tree-Based Methods](concepts/TreeBasedMethods.md) — Umbrella for single trees + [[Bagging]] / [[RandomForests]] / [[Boosting]] ensembles.
- [Unsupervised Learning](concepts/UnsupervisedLearning.md) — Structure discovery in $X$ without labels; PCA, K-means, hierarchical clustering.
- [Validation Set Approach](concepts/ValidationSetApproach.md) — Single train/test split; the simplest (and noisiest) form of [[CrossValidation]].
- [Vector Space](concepts/VectorSpace.md) — Set with addition + scalar multiplication satisfying the eight axioms ([[mml-book]] §2.4); the algebraic structure underlying ML (every "input is a vector" is a vector-space commitment).
- [AlexNet](concepts/AlexNet.md) — 8-layer CNN ([[AlexKrizhevsky|Krizhevsky]], [[IlyaSutskever|Sutskever]], [[GeoffreyHinton|Hinton]] 2012) that won [[ImageNet]] ILSVRC 2012 and ignited the modern deep-learning era; [[ReLU]] + [[Dropout]] + image augmentation on dual GTX 580s ([[d2l-convolutional-modern]]).
- [Vision Transformer (ViT)](concepts/VisionTransformer.md) — Dosovitskiy et al. 2021 application of the [[Transformer]] encoder to image classification: patches-as-tokens + learnable [[ClsToken|`<cls>` token]] + [[PreNorm|pre-norm]] + [[GELU]] MLP; "scalability trumps inductive biases" — outperforms ResNets at 300M+ training images ([[d2l-attention-and-transformers]]).
- [`<cls>` Token](concepts/ClsToken.md) — Learnable token prepended to a Transformer input whose final representation serves as a global / sequence-level summary; classification head in [[BERT]] + [[VisionTransformer|ViT]] ([[d2l-attention-and-transformers]]).
- [VGG](concepts/VGG.md) — CNN family ([[KarenSimonyan|Simonyan]] & [[AndrewZisserman|Zisserman]] 2014, [[oxforduniversity|Oxford]]) built from blocks of small $3\times3$ convolutions; "deep and narrow beats shallow"; first to propose a *family* of architectures parameterized by depth ([[d2l-convolutional-modern]]).
- [Network in Network (NiN)](concepts/NetworkInNetwork.md) — Lin/Chen/Yan 2013 CNN introducing **$1\times1$ convolutions** (per-pixel FC over channels) and **[[GlobalAveragePooling|global average pooling]]** (kills the parameter-hungry FC head) — both primitives universally adopted afterwards ([[d2l-convolutional-modern]]).
- [GoogLeNet](concepts/GoogLeNet.md) — 22-layer CNN ([[ChristianSzegedy|Szegedy]] et al. 2015) winning ILSVRC 2014 with stacked [[Inception]] blocks; established the universal **stem / body / head** template; first CNN cheaper *and* more accurate than predecessors ([[d2l-convolutional-modern]]).
- [Inception block](concepts/Inception.md) — Multi-branch CNN module ($1\times1$ / $1\times1\to3\times3$ / $1\times1\to5\times5$ / pool→$1\times1$, concatenated). Uses $1\times1$ convs as channel-reduction bottlenecks; eliminates the "pick the right kernel size" debate ([[d2l-convolutional-modern]]).
- [ResNet](concepts/ResNet.md) — 152-layer-capable residual CNN ([[KaimingHe|He]] et al. 2015); $f(\mathbf{x})=\mathbf{x}+g(\mathbf{x})$ makes the identity easy to learn; solved the degradation problem; ILSVRC 2015 winner; residual idea ubiquitous in [[transformer|Transformers]] / RNNs / GNNs ([[d2l-convolutional-modern]]).
- [ResNeXt](concepts/ResNeXt.md) — Grouped-convolution generalization of [[ResNet]] ([[Xie|Xie]], [[RossGirshick|Girshick]], [[PiotrDollar|Dollár]] et al. 2017, [[fair|FAIR]]); same transformation in all branches; building block of [[RegNet]] ([[d2l-convolutional-modern]]).
- [DenseNet](concepts/DenseNet.md) — CNN ([[GaoHuang|Huang]] et al. 2017) where each layer's output is concatenated (not added) to all previous layers' outputs; strong feature reuse, smaller parameter count, heavier GPU memory ([[d2l-convolutional-modern]]).
- [RegNet](concepts/RegNet.md) — CNN family ([[IliaRadosavovic|Radosavovic]] et al. 2020) output of a **design-space** optimization over distributions of networks; AnyNet → AnyNet_E via empirical-CDF-based constraint tightening; transferable design principles instead of a single architecture ([[d2l-convolutional-modern]]).
- [Residual connection](concepts/ResidualConnection.md) — Shortcut path $\mathbf{x}+g(\mathbf{x})$ that lets a block trivially represent the identity; solves degradation; ubiquitous in [[ResNet]] / [[Transformer]] / GNNs / RNNs since 2015 ([[d2l-convolutional-modern]]).
- [Residual block](concepts/ResidualBlock.md) — Two $3\times3$ convs + [[BatchNormalization|BN]] + [[ReLU]] wrapped in a [[ResidualConnection|residual connection]]; the canonical [[ResNet]] building block. Bottleneck and pre-activation variants ([[d2l-convolutional-modern]]).
- [Global average pooling](concepts/GlobalAveragePooling.md) — Average each channel over its entire spatial extent; zero parameters; the default modern CNN classification-head replacement for the FC layer stack ([[NetworkInNetwork|NiN]] → universal) ([[d2l-convolutional-modern]]).
- [Grouped convolution](concepts/GroupedConvolution.md) — Conv with $g$ disjoint channel groups; reduces parameters and FLOPs by factor $g$ at the cost of cross-group information flow; foundational to [[ResNeXt]] / MobileNet / EfficientNet; historical origin in [[AlexNet]]'s dual-GPU split ([[d2l-convolutional-modern]]).
- [Bottleneck (CNN block)](concepts/Bottleneck.md) — $1\times1$ (reduce) → $k\times k$ → $1\times1$ (restore) compute-frugality pattern; central to deeper [[ResNet]] variants and [[ResNeXt]]; counter-found by [[RegNet]] design-space study to be skip-worthy on average ([[d2l-convolutional-modern]]).
- [Layer normalization](concepts/LayerNormalization.md) — Per-observation normalization ([[Ba|Ba]], [[JamieKiros|Kiros]], [[GeoffreyHinton|Hinton]] 2016); independent of batch size; identical at train and test; default in [[transformer|Transformers]] where [[BatchNormalization|BN]] is awkward ([[d2l-convolutional-modern]]).
- [Neural architecture search (NAS)](concepts/NeuralArchitectureSearch.md) — Automated architecture-design via RL / evolution / gradient methods (Zoph & Le 2016 → EfficientNet 2019); produces single networks at enormous compute cost; design-spaces ([[RegNet]]) are the cheaper, insight-yielding alternative ([[d2l-convolutional-modern]]).
- [Stem (CNN)](concepts/Stem.md) — Initial CNN section that ingests the image and produces a coarsened, channel-rich feature map for the body; popularized as a named section by [[GoogLeNet]]; universal in modern CNNs ([[d2l-convolutional-modern]]).
- [Network head (CNN)](concepts/NetworkHead.md) — Final CNN section that converts the body's feature map into a task-specific output (classification / detection / segmentation); modern default = [[GlobalAveragePooling]] + FC ([[d2l-convolutional-modern]]).
- [Memory cell](concepts/MemoryCell.md) — The composite unit of an [[LSTM|LSTM]] cell: an internal state $\mathbf{C}_t$ with a self-connected weight-1 recurrent edge, gated by [[InputGate|input]] / [[ForgetGate|forget]] / [[OutputGate|output]] multiplicative gates ([[d2l-recurrent-modern]]).
- [Input gate](concepts/InputGate.md) — Sigmoid LSTM gate $\mathbf{I}_t = \sigma(\cdot)$ controlling how much of the candidate cell update enters the [[MemoryCell|memory cell]] ([[d2l-recurrent-modern]]).
- [Forget gate](concepts/ForgetGate.md) — Sigmoid LSTM gate $\mathbf{F}_t = \sigma(\cdot)$ controlling how much of the prior cell state persists; added to LSTM by Gers, Schmidhuber & Cummins 2000 ([[d2l-recurrent-modern]]).
- [Output gate](concepts/OutputGate.md) — Sigmoid LSTM gate $\mathbf{O}_t = \sigma(\cdot)$ controlling how much of $\tanh(\mathbf{C}_t)$ is exposed as the hidden state $\mathbf{H}_t$ ([[d2l-recurrent-modern]]).
- [Open Educational Resource (OER)](concepts/OER.md) — Teaching materials released under permissive (typically Creative Commons) licenses for free redistribution + derivation; the publishing model behind [[JamesFiore]]'s [[embedded-controllers-fiore|*Embedded Controllers Using C and Arduino*]] (CC BY-NC-SA).
- [Reset gate](concepts/ResetGate.md) — Sigmoid [[GRU]] gate $\mathbf{R}_t = \sigma(\cdot)$ controlling how much of the previous hidden state contributes to the candidate; "short-term dependencies" ([[d2l-recurrent-modern]]).
- [Update gate](concepts/UpdateGate.md) — Sigmoid [[GRU]] gate $\mathbf{Z}_t = \sigma(\cdot)$ parameterizing the convex combination of old and candidate hidden states; "long-term dependencies"; jointly subsumes LSTM's [[InputGate|input]] + [[ForgetGate|forget]] gates ([[d2l-recurrent-modern]]).
- [Deep RNN](concepts/DeepRNN.md) — Multi-layer recurrent network: $L$ stacked RNN layers with per-layer recurrences; output uses only the topmost layer's hidden state. Common range $L \in [1,8]$, $h \in [64, 2056]$ ([[d2l-recurrent-modern]]).
- [Bidirectional RNN](concepts/BidirectionalRNN.md) — RNN that concatenates a forward and a backward pass over the same input ([[MikeSchuster|Schuster]] & [[KuldipPaliwal|Paliwal]] 1997); encoder-side use only — "no future at inference" blocks autoregressive decoding ([[d2l-recurrent-modern]]).
- [Greedy decoding](concepts/GreedyDecoding.md) — Auto-regressive decoding that picks $\operatorname{argmax}$ at each step; cost $\mathcal{O}(\|\mathcal{Y}\|T')$; locally optimal, globally suboptimal; equivalent to [[BeamSearch|beam search]] with $k=1$ ([[d2l-recurrent-modern]]).
- [Causal mask](concepts/CausalMask.md) — The Transformer-era autoregressive constraint: attention at position $t$ is forbidden from attending to positions $> t$; the structural successor to [[BidirectionalRNN|bi-RNN]]'s encoder-only restriction ([[d2l-recurrent-modern]]).
- [Adagrad](concepts/Adagrad.md) — Per-coordinate adaptive-learning-rate method ([[JohnDuchi|Duchi]], Hazan & Singer 2011); $\mathbf{s}_t = \mathbf{s}_{t-1}+\mathbf{g}_t^2$ accumulator as cheap diagonal-Hessian proxy; effective for sparse features but rate decay too aggressive for nonconvex DL ([[d2l-optimization]]).
- [RMSProp](concepts/RMSProp.md) — Tieleman & [[GeoffreyHinton|Hinton]] 2012; replaces [[Adagrad]]'s unbounded accumulator with leaky average $\mathbf{s}_t = \gamma\mathbf{s}_{t-1}+(1-\gamma)\mathbf{g}_t^2$, decoupling rate schedule from coordinate adaptivity ([[d2l-optimization]]).
- [Adadelta](concepts/Adadelta.md) — [[MatthewZeiler|Zeiler]] 2012; [[Adagrad]] variant with no global learning rate — uses leaky average of past parameter changes $\Delta\mathbf{x}_{t-1}$ as the unit-matching numerator ([[d2l-optimization]]).
- [Convexity](concepts/Convexity.md) — The property that makes local minima global minima; chord-above-function on convex sets; tests via Hessian PSD ([[Hessian]] $\succeq 0$) or [[JensensInequality|Jensen's inequality]] ([[d2l-optimization]]).
- [Saddle Point](concepts/SaddlePoint.md) — Zero-gradient point that is neither a local min nor max (Hessian eigenvalues mixed sign); exponentially more common than local minima in high dimensions and the dominant stalling pathology for DL optimization ([[d2l-optimization]]).
- [Newton's Method](concepts/NewtonsMethod.md) — Second-order optimization: $\mathbf{x}\leftarrow\mathbf{x}-\mathbf{H}^{-1}\nabla f$; one-step convergence on quadratics, $\mathcal{O}(d^3)$ inversion infeasible for DL, fatal on nonconvex Hessians with negative eigenvalues ([[d2l-optimization]]).
- [Preconditioning](concepts/Preconditioning.md) — Rescaling the optimization problem to lower the [[ConditionNumber|condition number]]; diagonal preconditioning $\textrm{diag}(\mathbf{H})^{-1}\nabla f$ is the cheap DL-friendly proxy that motivates [[Adagrad]] / [[RMSProp]] / [[Adam]] ([[d2l-optimization]]).
- [Nesterov Accelerated Gradient](concepts/NesterovMomentum.md) — [[YuriiNesterov|Nesterov]] 1983 refinement of [[BorisPolyak|Polyak]] momentum: evaluate gradient at lookahead position $\mathbf{x}_{t-1}-\eta\beta\mathbf{v}_{t-1}$ for optimal $\mathcal{O}(1/T^2)$ rate on smooth convex objectives ([[d2l-optimization]]).
- [Cosine Learning Rate Schedule](concepts/CosineLRSchedule.md) — Loshchilov & Hutter 2016 half-cosine decay $\eta_T + \tfrac{\eta_0-\eta_T}{2}(1+\cos(\pi t/T))$ — slow at start and end, fast in middle; now ubiquitous in LLM pretraining ([[d2l-optimization]]).
- [Learning Rate Warmup](concepts/Warmup.md) — Linear ramp of $\eta$ from $0$ to $\eta_0$ over the first $W$ steps before applying any decay; prevents early-training divergence in deep networks (Gotmare, Keskar, Xiong et al. 2018); standard in [[transformer|Transformer]] pretraining ([[d2l-optimization]]).
- [Yogi](concepts/Yogi.md) — Zaheer, Reddi et al. 2018 (NeurIPS); [[Adam]] divergence-fix that replaces $(1-\beta_2)(\mathbf{g}_t^2 - \mathbf{s}_{t-1})$ with $(1-\beta_2)\mathbf{g}_t^2\odot\textrm{sgn}(\mathbf{g}_t^2 - \mathbf{s}_{t-1})$ — magnitude-of-update no longer depends on deviation magnitude ([[d2l-optimization]]).

### Added with [[d2l-computational-performance]] (D2L Computational Performance)

- [Imperative Programming](concepts/ImperativeProgramming.md) — Statement-by-statement interpretation (Python, PyTorch eager, TF2 eager) — easy to write/debug, but Python-interpreter overhead stalls multi-GPU systems ([[d2l-computational-performance]] §`hybridize`).
- [Symbolic Programming](concepts/SymbolicProgramming.md) — Define → compile → execute (Theano, original TF, MXNet `Symbol`) — whole-program optimization, no Python in the inner loop, Python-independent serialized graphs for deployment ([[d2l-computational-performance]] §`hybridize`).
- [TorchScript](concepts/TorchScript.md) — [[PyTorch]]'s symbolic-compilation bridge: `torch.jit.script(net)` converts an imperative `nn.Module` into a serializable C++-backend graph; cousin of `tf.function` / MXNet `hybridize()` / [[XLA]] ([[d2l-computational-performance]] §`hybridize`).
- [Asynchronous Computation](concepts/AsyncComputation.md) — Frontend/backend decoupling via a task queue + [[ComputationalGraph|dep-graph]] tracker. PyTorch GPU ops async by default; `print` / `.item()` / `.numpy()` are *implicit blockers* that ruin perf ([[d2l-computational-performance]] §`async-computation`).
- [Automatic Parallelism](concepts/AutoParallelism.md) — Runtime schedules independent ops across devices without explicit parallel code; companion is computation–communication overlap (`non_blocking=True` PCIe DMA during backprop) ([[d2l-computational-performance]] §`auto-parallelism`).
- [Data Parallelism](concepts/DataParallelism.md) — Each GPU holds a full model replica, shards the batch, computes local gradients, [[AllReduce|all-reduces]], updates locally. **Recommended default** for multi-GPU training; scales minibatch + LR by $k$ ([[d2l-computational-performance]] §`multiple-gpus`).
- [Model Parallelism](concepts/ModelParallelism.md) — Shard the *model* across GPUs ([[PipelineParallelism|by layer]] or [[TensorParallelism|within layer]]). Required when the model doesn't fit on one GPU (frontier LLMs); avoided otherwise due to tight cross-GPU sync ([[d2l-computational-performance]] §`multiple-gpus`).
- [AllReduce](concepts/AllReduce.md) — The collective primitive of data-parallel training: sum vectors across $k$ devices, broadcast result back. Strategy interacts with bus topology — D2L's 4-GPU example: 15 ms (split-aggregation) vs 60 ms (gather-on-GPU0) vs 80 ms (CPU) ([[d2l-computational-performance]] §`multiple-gpus`).
- [Ring AllReduce](concepts/RingAllReduce.md) — Bandwidth-optimal [[AllReduce]]: time *does not grow with $n$*. 160 MB across 8× V100 over NVLink takes ~6 ms via two passes (reduce-scatter + all-gather) along a ring. Popularized by Baidu 2017 + [[Horovod]] 2018; the algorithm [[NCCL]] implements ([[d2l-computational-performance]] §`parameterserver`).
- [Parameter Server](concepts/ParameterServer.md) — Centralized-aggregation distributed-training architecture (Smola & Narayanamurthy 2010; Li, Andersen, Park et al. 2014). Workers `push` gradients, servers aggregate, workers `pull` parameters. Sharding across $n$ servers gives $\mathcal{O}(m/n)$ scaling; matching $m=n$ → constant. Now less common than [[AllReduce]] for dense LLM training ([[d2l-computational-performance]] §`parameterserver`).
- [NCCL](concepts/NCCL.md) — NVIDIA Collective Communications Library — topology-aware [[AllReduce]] / [[RingAllReduce]] / all-gather / broadcast over [[NVLink]] / [[PCIe]] / InfiniBand; the default backend for PyTorch DDP, TF MultiWorkerMirroredStrategy, MXNet KVStore, [[Horovod]] ([[d2l-computational-performance]] §`hardware`).
- [NVLink](concepts/NVLink.md) — NVIDIA's proprietary high-bandwidth GPU↔GPU interconnect: 18 GB/s per link × 6 links on V100 (~100 GB/s aggregate), 12 links on H100 (~900 GB/s). ~3–10× faster than [[PCIe]]; enables ring-allreduce to scale to many GPUs ([[d2l-computational-performance]] §`hardware`).
- [PCIe](concepts/PCIe.md) — Standard CPU↔peripheral bus: PCIe 4.0 ×16 = 32 GB/s, ~5 µs latency. Lane budgets (EPYC: 128, Xeon: 48, desktop: 16–20) limit how many GPUs a CPU can drive at full bandwidth ([[d2l-computational-performance]] §`hardware`).
- [HBM](concepts/HBM.md) — High Bandwidth Memory — 3D-stacked DRAM on a silicon interposer beside the GPU die; V100 (900 GB/s) / A100 (1.6–2.0 TB/s) / H100 (3 TB/s) / B200 (8 TB/s). Server-only; consumer GPUs use GDDR6/6X ([[d2l-computational-performance]] §`hardware`).
- [Tensor Core](concepts/TensorCore.md) — NVIDIA's specialized matrix-multiply-accumulate unit (Volta 2017+) — performs $4{\times}4$–$16{\times}16$ FMA per clock at FP16/BF16/TF32/FP8/FP4; what drives the FLOP/s gap between training-grade and consumer GPUs ([[d2l-computational-performance]] §`hardware`).
- [Vectorization (SIMD)](concepts/Vectorization.md) — Same instruction on multiple data elements per cycle. ARM NEON (128-bit), x86 AVX2 (256-bit), AVX-512 (512-bit), fused multiply-add. The CPU-side scaffolding that makes DL workloads tolerable on CPU; GPUs are SIMD at extreme scale ([[d2l-computational-performance]] §`hardware`).
- [Memory Hierarchy](concepts/MemoryHierarchy.md) — Register → L1/L2/L3 → DRAM → SSD → network pyramid; with D2L's consolidated latency table (1.5 ns L1 / 5 ns L2 / 16 ns L3 / 46 ns DRAM / 200 ns GPU HBM / 30 µs NVLink 1 MB / 80 µs PCIe 1 MB / 500 µs cross-DC RTT / 150 ms CA↔NL). The universal cost model under [[gpumemoryhierarchy]] and [[FlashAttention]] ([[d2l-computational-performance]] §`hardware`).

### Added with [[d2l-computer-vision]] (D2L Computer Vision)

- [Data Augmentation](concepts/DataAugmentation.md) — Random label-preserving image transforms (flip / crop / color-jitter) — cheapest regularizer in DL; "indispensable for [[AlexNet]]" per [[d2l-computer-vision]] §`image-augmentation`. Training-only; test-time predictions stay deterministic.
- [Bounding Box](concepts/BoundingBox.md) — Axis-aligned rectangle localizing an object; two equivalent representations $(x_1, y_1, x_2, y_2)$ and $(c_x, c_y, w, h)$ with D2L's `box_corner_to_center` / `box_center_to_corner` converters ([[d2l-computer-vision]] §`bounding-box`).
- [Anchor Box](concepts/AnchorBox.md) — Pre-defined candidate bbox parameterized by scale $s$ + aspect ratio $r$ (width $ws\sqrt{r}$, height $hs/\sqrt{r}$); D2L's $n+m-1$ trick avoids the $whnm$ explosion. Greedy IoU-matched assignment with $\sigma_{xy}=0.1$, $\sigma_{wh}=0.2$ offset parameterization ([[d2l-computer-vision]] §`anchor`).
- [Intersection over Union (IoU)](concepts/IntersectionOverUnion.md) — Jaccard index $|A\cap B|/|A\cup B|$ on bounding-box pixel sets; the universal similarity / matching / evaluation metric for [[ObjectDetection|detection]] ([[d2l-computer-vision]] §`anchor`).
- [Non-Maximum Suppression (NMS)](concepts/NonMaxSuppression.md) — Greedy deduplication of predicted boxes: sort by confidence, iteratively keep top + drop boxes with IoU > $\epsilon$ ([[d2l-computer-vision]] §`anchor`). Soft-NMS / DETR-bipartite-matching are post-D2L alternatives.
- [Multiscale Object Detection](concepts/MultiscaleObjectDetection.md) — Place [[AnchorBox|anchors]] on feature maps at multiple CNN depths; smaller maps (larger receptive fields) detect larger objects. Avoids the >2M-anchors-per-image blowup of per-pixel anchor generation ([[d2l-computer-vision]] §`multiscale-object-detection`).
- [Object Detection](concepts/ObjectDetection.md) — CV task: per-object `(class, bbox)` pairs. Two families: single-stage ([[SSD]] / YOLO) and two-stage ([[RCNN]] → [[FastRCNN]] → [[FasterRCNN]] → [[MaskRCNN]]); modern third family: end-to-end set prediction (DETR) ([[d2l-computer-vision]]).
- [SSD (Single-Shot Multibox Detection)](concepts/SSD.md) — Single-stage anchor-based detector ([[WeiLiu|Liu]] et al. 2016): truncated [[VGG]]/[[ResNet]] backbone + multiscale feature blocks + per-pixel $a(q+1)$-channel class head + $4a$-channel bbox head; "simple, fast, and widely used" ([[d2l-computer-vision]] §`ssd`).
- [R-CNN (Regions with CNN features)](concepts/RCNN.md) — Pioneering CNN detector ([[RossGirshick|Girshick]] et al. 2014): [[SelectiveSearch|selective search]] → 2000 proposals → per-region CNN forward pass → per-class SVMs. Massive [[ImageNet|ImageNet]]-pretraining accuracy jump but ~10 s/image ([[d2l-computer-vision]] §`rcnn`).
- [Fast R-CNN](concepts/FastRCNN.md) — Girshick 2015: one whole-image CNN forward pass + [[ROIPooling|RoI pooling]] per proposal + per-RoI FC head with softmax + bbox regression. End-to-end trainable; ~10× speedup over R-CNN ([[d2l-computer-vision]] §`rcnn`).
- [Faster R-CNN](concepts/FasterRCNN.md) — [[ShaoqingRen|Ren]], [[KaimingHe|He]], Girshick 2015: replace [[SelectiveSearch]] with a jointly-trained [[RegionProposalNetwork|Region Proposal Network]] ($3\times3$ conv + per-anchor binary class + bbox regression + [[NonMaxSuppression|NMS]]); ~5 FPS on a single GPU ([[d2l-computer-vision]] §`rcnn`).
- [Mask R-CNN](concepts/MaskRCNN.md) — [[KaimingHe|He]], Gkioxari, Dollár & Girshick 2017: [[FasterRCNN]] + [[ROIAlign|RoI align]] (bilinear interp preserves alignment) + per-RoI [[FCN]] mask head — instance segmentation ([[d2l-computer-vision]] §`rcnn`).
- [RoI Pooling](concepts/ROIPooling.md) — Pooling layer extracting fixed-shape $h_2 \times w_2$ features from variable-shape regions. Output shape is a layer parameter, not derived from window/stride. Introduced in [[FastRCNN]] ([[d2l-computer-vision]] §`rcnn`).
- [RoI Align](concepts/ROIAlign.md) — [[ROIPooling]] without rounding artifacts: [[BilinearInterpolation|bilinear interpolation]] at continuous RoI coordinates. ~10% mask-AP boost vs RoI pooling in [[MaskRCNN]] ([[d2l-computer-vision]] §`rcnn`).
- [Region Proposal Network (RPN)](concepts/RegionProposalNetwork.md) — Small fully-conv network in [[FasterRCNN]] that learns to propose regions: per-pixel anchors + binary class + bbox offset → NMS → top-K proposals. Trained jointly with the detection head ([[d2l-computer-vision]] §`rcnn`).
- [Selective Search](concepts/SelectiveSearch.md) — Classical bottom-up hierarchical superpixel-merging region-proposal algorithm (Uijlings et al. 2013); used by [[RCNN]] / [[FastRCNN]]; replaced by [[RegionProposalNetwork|RPN]] in [[FasterRCNN]]. ~2 s/image (CPU) was the dominant bottleneck ([[d2l-computer-vision]] §`rcnn`).
- [Semantic Segmentation](concepts/SemanticSegmentation.md) — CV task: per-pixel class label; *does not* distinguish object instances. Canonical model [[FCN]] on [[PascalVOC2012]] (21 classes); pixel-level borders "obviously more fine-grained" than detection ([[d2l-computer-vision]] §`semantic-segmentation-and-dataset`).
- [Instance Segmentation](concepts/InstanceSegmentation.md) — Pixel-level recognition of individual object instances; strict generalization of [[SemanticSegmentation]]. Canonical model: [[MaskRCNN]] ([[d2l-computer-vision]] §`semantic-segmentation-and-dataset`).
- [Transposed Convolution](concepts/TransposedConvolution.md) — Upsampling conv (= fractionally-strided conv): broadcasts each input element via the kernel; padding applied to output not input; stride is on intermediate results. For stride $s$, padding $s/2$, kernel $2s$ → exactly $s\times$ upsampling. Powers [[FCN]], U-Net, GAN decoders, diffusion U-Nets ([[d2l-computer-vision]] §`transposed-conv`).
- [FCN (Fully Convolutional Network)](concepts/FCN.md) — [[JonathanLong|Long]], [[EvanShelhamer|Shelhamer]] & [[TrevorDarrell|Darrell]] 2015: ResNet-18 backbone (drop GAP+FC) + $1\times1$ conv (channels → $K$ classes) + [[TransposedConvolution|transposed-conv]] stride-32 upsampler init with [[BilinearInterpolation|bilinear kernel]] → per-pixel softmax cross-entropy ([[d2l-computer-vision]] §`fcn`).
- [Style Transfer (Neural Style)](concepts/StyleTransfer.md) — [[LeonGatys|Gatys]], [[AlexanderEcker|Ecker]] & [[MatthiasBethge|Bethge]] 2016: optimize a *synthesized image*'s pixels (not network weights) on a frozen [[VGG|VGG-19]] to match content image features at a deep layer + match style image's [[GramMatrix|Gram matrices]] at multiple layers + minimize total-variation noise ([[d2l-computer-vision]] §`neural-style`).
- [Gram Matrix](concepts/GramMatrix.md) — $G = \phi_\text{flat}\phi_\text{flat}^\top$ for a feature map $\phi$: inter-channel co-activation statistics, spatially invariant — perfect for "style" in [[StyleTransfer]]. Also central to kernel methods ([[d2l-computer-vision]] §`neural-style`).
- [Bilinear Interpolation](concepts/BilinearInterpolation.md) — Weighted average of 4 nearest grid cells; standard upsampling primitive. Two roles in [[d2l-computer-vision]]: [[FCN]] transposed-conv initialization + [[ROIAlign]] continuous feature sampling.
- [Pascal VOC 2012](concepts/PascalVOC2012.md) — Classical CV benchmark — 21 classes (20 + bg) with fixed RGB-colormap segmentation labels shape-matched to input images; the canonical dataset for [[SemanticSegmentation]] in [[d2l-computer-vision]] §`semantic-segmentation-and-dataset`.
- [CIFAR-10](concepts/CIFAR10.md) — 60k 32×32 RGB images, 10 classes (Krizhevsky & Hinton ~2009); D2L's running benchmark for [[DataAugmentation]] and a Kaggle-competition walk-through in §`kaggle-cifar10`.

### Added with [[d2l-nlp-pretraining]] (D2L NLP Pretraining)

- [Word Embedding](concepts/WordEmbedding.md) — Mapping each word in a vocabulary to a fixed-length dense real vector encoding meaning + relationships. The umbrella concept the entire [[d2l-nlp-pretraining]] chapter operationalizes; replaces sparse one-hot (cosine sim ≡ 0) with [[Word2Vec]] / [[GloVe]] / [[FastText]] static vectors and [[ContextualEmbedding|contextual embeddings]] from [[ELMo]] / [[GPT]] / [[BERT]].
- [Skip-Gram](concepts/SkipGram.md) — One of two [[Word2Vec|word2vec]] models ([[TomasMikolov|Mikolov]] et al. 2013): predict context words from a center word via softmax over dot products $\exp(\mathbf{u}_o^\top\mathbf{v}_c)/\sum_i\exp(\mathbf{u}_i^\top\mathbf{v}_c)$. Trained with [[NegativeSampling]] or [[HierarchicalSoftmax]]. The model [[GloVe]] reinterprets and [[FastText]] augments ([[d2l-nlp-pretraining]] §word2vec).
- [Continuous Bag of Words (CBOW)](concepts/CBOW.md) — Mirror of [[SkipGram]]: predict the center word from the average of its context-word vectors. Trains faster (1 prediction per window vs $2m$), uses context vectors as the final representation, but skip-gram tends to win on rare words and analogies ([[d2l-nlp-pretraining]] §word2vec).
- [Negative Sampling](concepts/NegativeSampling.md) — Approximate-training trick replacing the [[Word2Vec|word2vec]] softmax with a per-pair binary classifier: positive (center, context) pair vs $K$ noise words sampled from $P(w)$ (typically unigram$^{3/4}$). Per-step cost drops from $\mathcal{O}(|\mathcal{V}|)$ to $\mathcal{O}(K)$. Default trainer for [[SkipGram]] / [[CBOW]] / [[FastText]] ([[d2l-nlp-pretraining]] §approx-training).
- [Noise Contrastive Estimation (NCE)](concepts/NoiseContrastiveEstimation.md) — General estimation principle (Gutmann & Hyvärinen 2010) for unnormalized probabilistic models: distinguish data samples from noise samples via binary classification; the partition function becomes a learnable free parameter. [[NegativeSampling]] is NCE with the noise-probability term dropped — fast but no longer a consistent density estimator ([[d2l-nlp-pretraining]] §approx-training).
- [Hierarchical Softmax](concepts/HierarchicalSoftmax.md) — Approximate-training trick for [[Word2Vec|word2vec]] (Morin & Bengio 2005) that replaces the flat $|\mathcal{V}|$-way softmax with a Huffman-style binary tree; each conditional probability factorizes as a product of $\mathcal{O}(\log_2|\mathcal{V}|)$ sigmoids along the root-to-leaf path. Counterpart to [[NegativeSampling]] ([[d2l-nlp-pretraining]] §approx-training).
- [Subword Embedding](concepts/SubwordEmbedding.md) — Word-representation approach decomposing each word into smaller pieces (character $n$-grams, [[BPE]] merges, [[WordPiece]] pieces) and summing/looking-up their embeddings. Motivations: OOV robustness, morphological sharing, fixed-size variable-length vocabularies. Anchored by [[FastText]]; underpins essentially every modern LLM input layer ([[d2l-nlp-pretraining]] §subword-embedding).
- [Byte Pair Encoding (BPE)](concepts/BPE.md) — Statistical subword tokenizer ([[RicoSennrich|Sennrich]], Haddow & Birch 2015) that learns a fixed-size vocabulary by greedy frequency-based merging of consecutive symbols. Underpins [[GPT2|GPT-2]] / [[GPT3|GPT-3]] / [[RoBERTa]] tokenization; [[WordPiece]] is the unigram-likelihood variant used by [[BERT]] ([[d2l-nlp-pretraining]] §subword-embedding §Byte-Pair-Encoding).
- [Analogy Task](concepts/AnalogyTask.md) — Intrinsic evaluation for [[WordEmbedding|word embeddings]]: predict $d$ in $a:b::c:d$ via $\arg\max_w\cos(\textrm{vec}(w),\textrm{vec}(c)+\textrm{vec}(b)-\textrm{vec}(a))$. Recovers semantic (man:woman::son:daughter; beijing:china::tokyo:japan) and syntactic (bad:worst::big:biggest; do:did::go:went) structure directly from 50-d GloVe ([[d2l-nlp-pretraining]] §similarity-analogy).
- [Classification Token ([CLS])](concepts/ClassificationToken.md) — Special token prepended to every [[BERT]] input; its final hidden state serves as the aggregate sequence vector for sequence-level classification heads ([[NextSentencePrediction]], sentiment, NLI, paraphrase). The `[SEP]` token marks segment boundaries; learned segment embeddings $\mathbf{e}_A$ / $\mathbf{e}_B$ identify which sentence each position belongs to ([[d2l-nlp-pretraining]] §bert).

### Added with [[d2l-nlp-applications]] (D2L NLP Applications)

- [TextCNN](concepts/TextCNN.md) — 1-D CNN sentence classifier ([[YoonKim|Kim]] 2014): multiple kernel widths (3 / 4 / 5) over [[GloVe]] embeddings → [[MaxOverTimePooling|max-over-time pooling]] → concat → dropout → FC. The canonical CNN-for-NLP baseline ([[d2l-nlp-applications]] §`sentiment-analysis-cnn`).
- [Sentiment Analysis](concepts/SentimentAnalysis.md) — Text-classification task assigning affective polarity (pos / neg) to a sequence; the canonical instance of *single-text classification* ([[d2l-nlp-applications]] §`sentiment-analysis-*`). Three architectural choices: [[BidirectionalRNN]] + [[GloVe]], [[TextCNN]] + GloVe, fine-tuned [[BERT]].
- [Natural Language Inference](concepts/NaturalLanguageInference.md) — Text-pair task (also: *recognizing textual entailment*) labeling (premise, hypothesis) pairs as **entailment / contradiction / neutral** ([[d2l-nlp-applications]] §`natural-language-inference-*`).
- [SNLI](concepts/SNLI.md) — Stanford Natural Language Inference corpus (Bowman, Angeli, Potts & Manning, EMNLP 2015) — 500k+ labeled English sentence pairs, balanced across the three NLI labels. The canonical NLI benchmark ([[d2l-nlp-applications]]).
- [Decomposable Attention](concepts/DecomposableAttention.md) — Parikh, Täckström, Das & Uszkoreit 2016 attention-only NLI model: **attend → compare → aggregate** over GloVe embeddings + MLPs; the **decomposition trick** $e_{ij} = f(\mathbf{a}_i)^\top f(\mathbf{b}_j)$ gives linear $\mathcal{O}(m+n)$ complexity. A direct forerunner of [[SelfAttention]] ([[d2l-nlp-applications]] §`natural-language-inference-attention`).
- [Fine-Tuning BERT](concepts/FineTuningBert.md) — The applied-NLP fine-tuning template: minimal architecture change (extra FC head), full-encoder fine-tuning, four downstream categories (single-text classification / text-pair classification / text-pair regression / token-level tagging / span prediction) all using the [[ClsToken|`[CLS]`]] hidden state or per-token vectors ([[d2l-nlp-applications]] §`finetuning-bert`).
- [IMDb](concepts/IMDb.md) — Stanford large movie review dataset (Maas et al. 2011); 25k train + 25k test reviews, balanced positive / negative. D2L's canonical [[SentimentAnalysis|sentiment-analysis]] benchmark ([[d2l-nlp-applications]] §`sentiment-analysis-and-dataset`).
- [Semantic Textual Similarity](concepts/SemanticTextualSimilarity.md) — Text-pair *regression* task (Cer et al. 2017); STS-B scores sentence pairs on a 0–5 ordinal scale. Fine-tune BERT with `[CLS]` → linear regressor + MSE ([[d2l-nlp-applications]] §`finetuning-bert`).
- [Question Answering](concepts/QuestionAnswering.md) — Token-level NLP task; extractive QA predicts answer span $\arg\max_{i\le j}(s_i+e_j)$ from passage. The canonical token-level [[FineTuningBert|BERT fine-tuning]] application ([[d2l-nlp-applications]] §`finetuning-bert`).
- [SQuAD](concepts/SQuAD.md) — Stanford Question Answering Dataset v1.1 (Rajpurkar, Zhang, Lopyrev & Liang 2016) — canonical extractive QA benchmark with answer-span supervision ([[d2l-nlp-applications]] §`finetuning-bert`).
- [CoLA](concepts/CoLA.md) — Corpus of Linguistic Acceptability (Warstadt, Singh & Bowman 2019); single-text classification of grammaticality used in GLUE ([[d2l-nlp-applications]] §`finetuning-bert`).
- [Max-Over-Time Pooling](concepts/MaxOverTimePooling.md) — 1-D global max-pooling along the temporal axis (Collobert et al. 2011); the variable-length-to-fixed-vector reducer in [[TextCNN|textCNN]] ([[d2l-nlp-applications]] §`sentiment-analysis-cnn`).

### Added with [[d2l-reinforcement-learning]] (D2L Reinforcement Learning)

- [Value Iteration](concepts/ValueIteration.md) — The canonical **model-based** RL algorithm: iterate the [[BellmanEquation|Bellman optimality recurrence]] $V_{k+1}(s)=\max_a\{r(s,a)+\gamma\sum_{s'}P(s'\mid s,a)V_k(s')\}$ to convergence (~10 sweeps on FrozenLake-v1, $\gamma=0.95$). Requires fully known [[TransitionFunction|transitions]] and rewards ([[d2l-reinforcement-learning]] §value-iter).
- [Q-Learning](concepts/QLearning.md) — [[ChristopherWatkins|Watkins]] & Dayan 1992 **[[ModelFreeLearning|model-free]] [[OffPolicyLearning|off-policy]] [[TemporalDifferenceLearning|TD]]** algorithm: replaces the $\sum_{s'}P(s'\mid s,a)$ expectation with a sample. Update $Q(s_t,a_t)\!\leftarrow\!(1-\alpha)Q(s_t,a_t)+\alpha[r_t+\gamma\max_{a'}Q(s_{t+1},a')]$. Self-correcting and convergent even from random $\pi_e$; DQN's foundation ([[d2l-reinforcement-learning]] §qlearning).
- [Bellman Equation](concepts/BellmanEquation.md) — Recursive identity $V^\pi(s)=\sum_a\pi(a\mid s)[r(s,a)+\gamma\sum_{s'}P(s'\mid s,a)V^\pi(s')]$ decomposing value into immediate reward + discounted future value. Optimality form $V^*(s)=\max_a\{r(s,a)+\gamma\sum_{s'}P(s'\mid s,a)V^*(s')\}$. The foundation of all RL algorithms ([[d2l-reinforcement-learning]] §value-iter).
- [Dynamic Programming](concepts/DynamicProgramming.md) — [[RichardBellman|Bellman]]'s 1950s framework — *"the remainder of an optimal trajectory is also optimal"* — the algorithmic basis of [[ValueIteration]] and planning under known MDPs ([[d2l-reinforcement-learning]] §value-iter).
- [Policy (RL)](concepts/PolicyFunction.md) — A mapping from states to actions. Stochastic $\pi(a\mid s)$ or deterministic $\pi(s)$. Behavior policy $\pi_e$ vs target policy $\arg\max_a\hat{Q}$ distinguishes [[OffPolicyLearning|off-policy]] from on-policy ([[d2l-reinforcement-learning]]).
- [Value Function](concepts/ValueFunction.md) — $V^\pi(s)=\mathbb{E}_{a_t\sim\pi}[\sum_t\gamma^t r(s_t,a_t)]$ — expected discounted return from state $s$ under $\pi$. Satisfies the [[BellmanEquation|Bellman equation]] ([[d2l-reinforcement-learning]]).
- [Action-Value Function (Q)](concepts/ActionValueFunction.md) — $Q^\pi(s,a)$ generalizes $V^\pi$ by fixing the first action. The central quantity for model-free RL because $\arg\max_a Q^*(s,a)$ recovers the optimal policy without needing $P$ ([[d2l-reinforcement-learning]]).
- [Discount Factor](concepts/DiscountFactor.md) — $\gamma\in[0,1)$ in the return $\sum_t\gamma^t r_t$. Keeps infinite-horizon sums finite; encodes near-term-reward preference. D2L uses $\gamma=0.95$ ([[d2l-reinforcement-learning]] §mdp).
- [Transition Function](concepts/TransitionFunction.md) — $T(s,a,s')=P(s'\mid s,a)$ — the MDP's stochastic dynamics, $\sum_{s'}T(s,a,s')=1$. Required by [[ValueIteration]], replaced by sampling in [[QLearning]] ([[d2l-reinforcement-learning]] §mdp).
- [Reward Function](concepts/RewardFunction.md) — $r:\mathcal{S}\times\mathcal{A}\to\mathbb{R}$. Designed by the user — *"the reward is designed by the user with the goal in mind"* ([[d2l-reinforcement-learning]] §mdp).
- [Epsilon-Greedy](concepts/EpsilonGreedy.md) — The canonical exploration policy: $\arg\max_{a'}\hat{Q}(s,a')$ w.p. $1-\epsilon$, uniform over $\mathcal{A}$ otherwise. Softmax-temperature variant is a continuous-valued alternative ([[d2l-reinforcement-learning]] §qlearning).
- [Exploration vs Exploitation](concepts/ExplorationExploitation.md) — The fundamental RL trade-off. Q-Learning's structural coupling between all $(s,a)$ values means insufficient exploration corrupts $\hat{Q}$ everywhere ([[d2l-reinforcement-learning]] §qlearning).
