- [Temporal-Difference Learning](concepts/TemporalDifferenceLearning.md) — Bootstrap-based model-free RL family. TD error $r_t+\gamma V(s_{t+1})-V(s_t)$ (or Q-form for [[QLearning]]). Splits into on-policy (SARSA) and off-policy ([[QLearning]]) variants ([[d2l-reinforcement-learning]] §qlearning).
- [Off-Policy Learning](concepts/OffPolicyLearning.md) — Behavior policy $\pi_e$ ≠ target policy $\pi^*$. Enables exploration decoupling, replay-buffer data reuse, and learning from demonstrations. [[QLearning]] is the canonical case ([[d2l-reinforcement-learning]] §qlearning).
- [Model-Free Learning](concepts/ModelFreeLearning.md) — RL without explicit knowledge of $P(s'\mid s,a)$. [[QLearning]] / DQN / REINFORCE / policy gradient. The default when $\mathcal{S}$ is too large to enumerate ([[d2l-reinforcement-learning]] §qlearning).

### Added with [[d2l-gaussian-processes]] (D2L Gaussian Processes)

- [Gaussian Process](concepts/GaussianProcess.md) — *"A collection of random variables, any finite number of which have a joint Gaussian distribution"*; distribution over functions specified by mean $m(x)$ + [[KernelFunction|kernel]] $k(x,x')$. Closed-form Gaussian posterior under additive Gaussian noise; weight-space and function-space views interchangeable ([[d2l-gaussian-processes]]).
- [Kernel / Covariance Function](concepts/KernelFunction.md) — Symmetric PSD function $k(x,x')=\textrm{Cov}(f(x),f(x'))$ specifying the [[GaussianProcess|GP]] prior. Encodes smoothness / periodicity / [[Stationarity|stationarity]] / length-scale; closure under sum, product, and pointwise transformation enables a *kernel grammar* ([[d2l-gaussian-processes]]).
- [RBF / Squared-Exponential Kernel](concepts/RBFKernel.md) — $k(x,x')=a^2\exp(-\tfrac{1}{2\ell^2}\|x-x'\|^2)$; the most popular kernel; stationary; derivable as $J\to\infty$ Riemann limit of $J$ Gaussian basis functions; a GP with RBF is a [[UniversalApproximator|universal approximator]] ([[d2l-gaussian-processes]] gp-priors).
- [Matérn Kernel](concepts/MaternKernel.md) — Smoothness-parameterized family $\nu>0$ generalizing [[RBFKernel|RBF]] ($\nu\to\infty$) and [[OUKernel|OU]] ($\nu=1/2$). Default alternative to RBF in spatial statistics; one-line swap in [[GPyTorch]] ([[d2l-gaussian-processes]]).
- [Neural Network Kernel](concepts/NeuralNetworkKernel.md) — [[RadfordNeal|Neal 1996]] kernel: a one-hidden-layer Bayesian NN at infinite width is a GP with closed-form arcsine kernel; non-stationary; historical precursor to [[NeuralTangentKernel|NTK]] ([[d2l-gaussian-processes]] gp-priors §NN kernel).
- [Marginal Likelihood](concepts/MarginalLikelihood.md) — $\log p(\mathbf{y}\mid\theta,X)=-\tfrac{1}{2}\mathbf{y}^\top[K_\theta+\sigma^2 I]^{-1}\mathbf{y}-\tfrac{1}{2}\log|K_\theta+\sigma^2 I|+c$; data-fit + complexity-penalty decomposition encodes [[OccamsRazor|Occam's razor]] automatically. The standard objective for learning kernel hyperparameters; does *not* factorize over data ⇒ full-batch optimizers only ([[d2l-gaussian-processes]] gp-inference).
- [Epistemic Uncertainty](concepts/EpistemicUncertainty.md) — Reducible uncertainty about the model itself; in [[GaussianProcess|GP]] regression, captured by $\textrm{diag}(S_*)$. Grows away from training data, shrinks with more data ([[d2l-gaussian-processes]]).
- [Aleatoric Uncertainty](concepts/AleatoricUncertainty.md) — Irreducible observation noise $\sigma^2$; persists independent of data quantity. *"Without being precise about what the uncertainty represents, it is essentially meaningless"* ([[d2l-gaussian-processes]] gp-inference).

### Added with [[d2l-hyperparameter-optimization]] (D2L Hyperparameter Optimization)

- [Hyperparameter Optimization (HPO)](concepts/HyperparameterOptimization.md) — Casting non-learned settings (learning rate, depth, regularization, [[Dropout]] rate) as a [[BlackBoxOptimization|black-box optimization]] problem $\mathbf{x}_\star\in\arg\min_{\mathbf{x}\in\mathcal{X}} f(\mathbf{x})$ over a structured config space with priors. The umbrella concept covering [[RandomSearch]], [[BayesianOptimization]], [[SuccessiveHalving]], [[Hyperband]], [[ASHA]]; full algorithmic treatment is [[d2l-hyperparameter-optimization]]'s.
- [Random Search](concepts/RandomSearch.md) — Independent prior sampling from the config space; universal HPO baseline. [[JamesBergstra|Bergstra]] & [[YoshuaBengio|Bengio]] 2012 prove it beats grid search on effective-low-dim problems. Trivially parallelizable → linear async speed-up ([[d2l-hyperparameter-optimization]] §hyperopt-intro / §rs-async).
- [Grid Search](concepts/GridSearch.md) — Cartesian product over equi-spaced per-hyperparameter grids. The strict HPO baseline; dominated by [[RandomSearch]] in deep-learning settings.
- [Successive Halving](concepts/SuccessiveHalving.md) — [[Jamieson]] & Talwalkar 2016 / [[Karnin]] et al. 2013 multi-fidelity scheduler: train $N=\eta^K$ configs at $r_\text{min}$, keep top $1/\eta$ at each rung, only one reaches $r_\text{max}$. The foundation of [[Hyperband]] / [[ASHA]] ([[d2l-hyperparameter-optimization]] §sh-intro).
- [Hyperband](concepts/Hyperband.md) — [[LishaLi|Li]] et al. 2018 — wraps [[SuccessiveHalving]] in an outer bracket loop hedging over $(n, r)$ to eliminate the user-tuning burden ([[d2l-hyperparameter-optimization]]).
- [Multi-Fidelity Optimization](concepts/MultiFidelityOptimization.md) — Extending HPO to $f(\mathbf{x}, r)$ with $r$ a resource budget (epochs, training-subset size, CV folds). Reduces *total compute*, not just wall-clock — distinct from parallelism ([[d2l-hyperparameter-optimization]] §sec_mf_hpo).
- [Black-Box Optimization](concepts/BlackBoxOptimization.md) — Minimizing a function accessible only through (noisy) queries: no gradients, no Hessians, no structural form. The framing under which HPO operates ([[d2l-hyperparameter-optimization]] §hyperopt-intro).

### Added with [[d2l-generative-adversarial-networks]] (D2L Generative Adversarial Networks)

- [Generator](concepts/Generator.md) — The "fake-sample synthesizer" half of a [[generativeadversarialnetwork|GAN]]: a differentiable function $G:\mathbf{z}\mapsto\mathbf{x}'$ that maps noise $\mathbf{z}\sim\mathcal{N}(0, 1)$ (the *latent variable*) to a sample mimicking the data distribution. Trained to fool the [[Discriminator]] via $\min_G\{-\log D(G(\mathbf{z}))\}$ — the non-saturating reformulation of Goodfellow's original $\max_G\{-\log(1-D(G(\mathbf{z})))\}$ ([[d2l-generative-adversarial-networks]] §`gan`).
- [Discriminator](concepts/Discriminator.md) — The "two-sample classifier" half of a [[generativeadversarialnetwork|GAN]]: a binary classifier $D:\mathbf{x}\mapsto[0,1]$ trained to distinguish real data ($y=1$) from generator outputs ($y=0$) via standard [[BinaryCrossEntropy|BCE]] cross-entropy. Provides the training signal for the [[Generator]] ([[d2l-generative-adversarial-networks]] §`gan`).
- [Min-Max Game](concepts/MinMaxGame.md) — Two-player zero-sum game-theoretic framing of [[generativeadversarialnetwork|GAN]] training: $\min_D \max_G\{-E_x\log D(\mathbf{x}) - E_z\log(1-D(G(\mathbf{z})))\}$. At Nash equilibrium $D\equiv 1/2$ and the generator distribution equals the data distribution. The canonical training objective from Goodfellow et al. 2014 ([[d2l-generative-adversarial-networks]] §`gan`).
- [Mode Collapse](concepts/ModeCollapse.md) — The dominant pathology of [[generativeadversarialnetwork|GAN]] training: the [[Generator]] learns to produce only a small subset of data modes, exploiting the [[Discriminator]]'s weakness rather than matching the full data distribution. Foreshadowed in the chapter's exercise *"does an equilibrium exist where the generator wins?"* ([[d2l-generative-adversarial-networks]]).
- [DCGAN](concepts/DCGAN.md) — Deep Convolutional GAN ([[AlecRadford|Radford]], Metz & Chintala 2015): all-convolutional [[generativeadversarialnetwork|GAN]] architecture with no FC layers. Discriminator = 4 strided convs + [[BatchNormalization|BN]] + [[LeakyReLU]] $\alpha=0.2$; generator = 4 [[TransposedConvolution|transposed convs]] + BN + [[ReLU]] + final $\tanh$. The first architecture to make GAN training reliably stable on natural images ([[d2l-generative-adversarial-networks]] §`dcgan`).
- [Leaky ReLU](concepts/LeakyReLU.md) — Variant activation $\textrm{leaky ReLU}(x) = x$ if $x>0$ else $\alpha x$ with $\alpha\in(0,1)$ (typically $0.2$). Non-zero gradient for negative inputs fixes the "dying ReLU" problem that cripples [[DCGAN]] discriminators trained with standard [[ReLU]]. Canonical activation in [[Discriminator|GAN discriminators]] ([[d2l-generative-adversarial-networks]] §`dcgan`).

### Added with [[d2l-recommender-systems]] (D2L Recommender Systems)

- [Collaborative Filtering](concepts/CollaborativeFiltering.md) — Central [[RecommenderSystems|recommender-systems]] abstraction: filtering information via collaboration among users / agents / data sources (Tapestry, Goldberg et al. 1992). Splits into [[MemoryBasedCF|memory-based]] (nearest-neighbor — Sarwar et al. 2001) and [[ModelBasedCF|model-based]] (latent-factor) families; model-based dominates because it handles sparsity and scales. Neural extensions ([[AutoRec]], [[NeuMF]]) make up the bulk of [[d2l-recommender-systems]].
- [Matrix Factorization](concepts/MatrixFactorization.md) — Canonical model-based CF baseline ([[YehudaKoren|Koren]], Bell & Volinsky 2009; Funk 2006). Factor $\mathbf{R}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n} \approx \mathbf{P}\mathbf{Q}^\top$ with bias terms: $\hat{R}_{ui}=\mathbf{p}_u\mathbf{q}_i^\top + b_u + b_i$; train by regularized [[MeanSquaredError|MSE]] on observed pairs. Load-bearing component of the [[NetflixPrize]] grand-prize-winning ensemble ([[d2l-recommender-systems]] §mf).
- [AutoRec](concepts/AutoRec.md) — [[CollaborativeFiltering|CF]] rating-prediction reframed as an [[Autoencoder]] ([[SuvashSedhain|Sedhain]] et al. 2015): $h(\mathbf{R}_{*i})=f(\mathbf{W}\cdot g(\mathbf{V}\mathbf{R}_{*i}+\mu)+b)$ with gradient-masking on unobserved entries. Outperforms [[MatrixFactorization|linear MF]] on MovieLens 100K — first concrete demo of "neural net > linear baseline" on explicit feedback ([[d2l-recommender-systems]] §autorec).
- [BPR (Bayesian Personalized Ranking)](concepts/BPR.md) — Pairwise log-sigmoid ranking loss for [[ImplicitFeedback|implicit-feedback]] recommenders ([[SteffenRendle|Rendle]] et al. 2009, *UAI*): $\textrm{BPR-OPT}=-\sum_{(u,i,j)}\ln\sigma(\hat{y}_{ui}-\hat{y}_{uj})+\lambda\|\Theta\|^2$ derived from MAP estimation; trained on `(user, positive, negative)` triples via [[NegativeSampling]] ([[d2l-recommender-systems]] §ranking).
- [Hinge Loss (Ranking)](concepts/HingeLossRanking.md) — Pairwise margin loss $\sum\max(m-\hat{y}_{ui}+\hat{y}_{uj}, 0)$ used as an interchangeable alternative to [[BPR]] in implicit-feedback recommenders ([[d2l-recommender-systems]] §ranking). Different from the SVM hinge loss for classification.
- [NeuMF (Neural Matrix Factorization)](concepts/NeuMF.md) — Two-branch deep recommender ([[XiangnanHe|He]] et al. 2017, *WWW*): parallel [[GMF]] (Hadamard product + dense head) + MLP (concat embeddings + stacked dense), fused by concatenation + sigmoid. Trained with [[BPR]] on implicit feedback; evaluated by [[HitRate|Hit@k]] / [[AUC]] ([[d2l-recommender-systems]] §neumf).
- [Neural Collaborative Filtering](concepts/NeuralCollaborativeFiltering.md) — Umbrella framework for replacing [[MatrixFactorization]]'s inner-product head with learnable neural-network heads ([[XiangnanHe|He]] et al. 2017). Instances: [[GMF]], [[NeuMF]], NGCF, LightGCN, attention-based extensions ([[d2l-recommender-systems]]).
- [GMF (Generalized Matrix Factorization)](concepts/GMF.md) — Neural-network generalization of MF's inner-product head: $\hat{y}_{ui}=\alpha(\mathbf{h}^\top(\mathbf{p}_u\odot\mathbf{q}_i))$. Recovers MF exactly when $\mathbf{h}=\mathbf{1}$, $\alpha=$ identity. Used as one of two parallel subnetworks in [[NeuMF]] ([[d2l-recommender-systems]] §neumf).
- [Caser](concepts/CaserModel.md) — Convolutional Sequence Embedding Recommendation ([[JiaxiTang|Tang]] & [[KeWang|Wang]] 2018, *WSDM*): treats the last $L$ items' embedding matrix $\mathbf{E}^{(u,t)}\in\mathbb{R}^{L\times k}$ as an "image" + runs **horizontal convolutions** (union-level patterns: "milk + butter → flour") and **vertical convolutions** (point-level: single-item-to-target). Concatenates with a long-term user-taste embedding ([[d2l-recommender-systems]] §seqrec).
- [Sequence-Aware Recommendation](concepts/SequenceAwareRecommendation.md) — Recommender sub-family in which input is ordered, timestamped user-action history ([[Quadrana]], [[Cremonesi]] & [[DietmarJannach|Jannach]] 2018). Canonical models: [[CaserModel|Caser]] (CNN), GRU4Rec (RNN), SASRec / BERT4Rec (Transformer). Distinct from but closely related to session-based recommendation ([[d2l-recommender-systems]] §seqrec).
- [Factorization Machines](concepts/FactorizationMachines.md) — General-purpose supervised model unifying linear regression, [[MatrixFactorization]], and polynomial-kernel SVMs ([[SteffenRendle|Rendle]] 2010, *ICDM*): $\hat{y}=w_0+\sum w_i x_i + \sum_{i<j}\langle\mathbf{v}_i,\mathbf{v}_j\rangle x_i x_j$ with the $\mathcal{O}(kd)$ reformulation of the pairwise term making FM tractable on sparse high-cardinality CTR inputs ([[d2l-recommender-systems]] §fm).
- [DeepFM](concepts/DeepFM.md) — Parallel fusion of [[FactorizationMachines|FM]] + deep MLP sharing a single embedding table ([[HuifengGuo|Guo]], [[RuimingTang|Tang]], Ye & He 2017, *IJCAI*): $\hat{y}=\sigma(\hat{y}^{(FM)}+\hat{y}^{(DNN)})$. Eliminates the manual feature-crossing required by [[WideAndDeep|Wide & Deep]]; outperforms FM on CTR ([[d2l-recommender-systems]] §deepfm).
- [Click-Through Rate (CTR) Prediction](concepts/CTRPrediction.md) — Binary-classification task — predict click probability given high-cardinality sparse categorical features (ad id / site id / device / time / user profile, etc.). Underwrites every monetized digital surface: search ads, display ads, social-feed ads. Canonical benchmarks: [[CriteoDataset|Criteo]], [[AvazuDataset|Avazu]] ([[d2l-recommender-systems]] §ctr).
- [Implicit Feedback](concepts/ImplicitFeedback.md) — User preference inferred from observable behavior (clicks, purchases, watches, dwell time) rather than proactively stated ratings ([[YifanHu|Hu]], [[YehudaKoren|Koren]] & Volinsky 2008). Abundant but noisy; positive-only by default; forces [[NegativeSampling]] + pairwise/listwise losses; evaluated by ranking metrics not RMSE ([[d2l-recommender-systems]]).
- [Explicit Feedback](concepts/ExplicitFeedback.md) — User preference proactively stated (star ratings, thumbs up/down, written reviews). High-quality but scarce, censored / biased toward extremes. Supports the rating-prediction / [[RMSE]] regime ([[MatrixFactorization]], [[AutoRec]]) ([[d2l-recommender-systems]] / [[d2l-introduction]]).
- [Interaction Matrix](concepts/InteractionMatrix.md) — Central data structure of [[CollaborativeFiltering|CF]] recommenders: $\mathbf{R}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$, row = user, column = item, value = interaction. **93.695% sparse** on MovieLens 100K; production recommenders routinely 99.99%+ sparse — the defining empirical challenge ([[d2l-recommender-systems]]).
- [Hit Rate (Hit@k)](concepts/HitRate.md) — Top-$k$ retrieval metric for implicit-feedback recommenders: $\textrm{Hit}@\ell = \frac{1}{m}\sum_u \mathbf{1}(\textrm{rank}_{u,g_u}\le\ell)$ where $g_u$ is the held-out ground-truth item for user $u$. Paired with [[AUC]] in [[NeuMF]] and [[CaserModel|Caser]] evaluation ([[d2l-recommender-systems]]).

### Added with [[d2l-appendix-mathematics]] (D2L Appendix: Mathematics for Deep Learning)

- [Information Diversity (metric)](concepts/InformationDiversity.md) — Average pairwise dissimilarity over retrieved info embeddings: $1 - \frac{\sum_{i\neq j}\cos(\mathbf{i},\mathbf{j})}{|\mathcal{I}|(|\mathcal{I}|-1)}$ — process-quality proxy in [[CoSTORM|Co-STORM]]'s evaluation. Captures retrieval breadth; **does not** capture whether the report cites the diverse set.
- [Information Seeking](concepts/InformationSeeking.md) — User-facing task of finding + sense-making information across multiple sources ([[Pirolli2009]]). [[CoSTORM|Co-STORM]]'s [[2408.15232-co-storm|Table 1]] partitions the prior art (IR / single-turn QA / conversational QA / report generation) along three axes: multiple sources, ongoing interaction, curated report — only Co-STORM covers all three.
- [Information Theory](concepts/InformationTheory.md) — [[ClaudeShannon|Shannon]] 1948 framework for information storage / transmission / manipulation. Core quantities: [[SelfInformation|self-information]], [[Entropy|entropy]], joint / conditional entropy, [[MutualInformation|mutual information]], [[KullbackLeiblerDivergence|KL divergence]], [[CrossEntropy|cross-entropy]] — the language under every classification loss, every LM training objective, and every [[ContrastiveLearning|contrastive]] representation-learning method ([[d2l-appendix-mathematics]] §information-theory).
- [Entropy](concepts/Entropy.md) — Expected [[SelfInformation|self-information]] $H(X)=-\mathbb{E}[\log p(X)]$ — the average number of bits to encode one realization. Maximum on uniform; *"information is gained by observing rare events"* ([[d2l-appendix-mathematics]] §information-theory).
- [Self-Information](concepts/SelfInformation.md) — Surprisal of a single event $I(X)=-\log_2 p(X)$ in bits; uniquely characterized by non-negativity + additivity for independent events ([[d2l-appendix-mathematics]] §information-theory).
- [KL Divergence](concepts/KullbackLeiblerDivergence.md) — Asymmetric directional distance $D_{KL}(P\|Q)=\mathbb{E}_P[\log p/q]\geq 0$ (Gibbs); zero iff $P=Q$. The link $H(P,Q)=H(P)+D_{KL}(P\|Q)$ is *why* [[CrossEntropyLoss|cross-entropy]] = [[MaximumLikelihoodEstimation|MLE]]; foundation of [[VariationalInference|VI]] / [[VariationalAutoencoder|VAEs]], [[RLHF]] / [[GRPO]] / [[PPO]] KL penalties, and [[Diffusion]] training objectives ([[d2l-appendix-mathematics]] §information-theory).
- [Mutual Information](concepts/MutualInformation.md) — Symmetric information $I(X;Y)=H(X)+H(Y)-H(X,Y)\geq 0$ between two RVs; zero iff independent. Foundation of [[InfoNCE]] / [[ContrastiveLearning|contrastive]] objectives (SimCLR / CLIP / MoCo) and the [[InformationBottleneck]] ([[d2l-appendix-mathematics]] §information-theory).
- [Cross-Entropy](concepts/CrossEntropy.md) — $H(P,Q)=-\mathbb{E}_P[\log q(x)] = H(P)+D_{KL}(P\|Q)$ — the information-theoretic *concept* underneath every classification / LM training [[CrossEntropyLoss|loss]] ([[d2l-appendix-mathematics]] §information-theory).
- [Naive Bayes](concepts/NaiveBayes.md) — Probabilistic classifier applying [[BayesTheorem|Bayes' rule]] with the **naive conditional-independence** assumption $P(\mathbf{x}\mid y)=\prod_i P(x_i\mid y)$ — collapses $\mathcal{O}(2^d)$ joint estimation to $\mathcal{O}(d)$. ~84% on binarized [[MNIST]] in D2L's demo despite the assumption being wrong; canonical case of "wrong but useful" ([[d2l-appendix-mathematics]] §naive-bayes).
- [Bernoulli Distribution](concepts/BernoulliDistribution.md) — Single coin flip $X\sim\text{Bernoulli}(p)$ with $\mu=p,\sigma^2=p(1-p)$; the per-feature likelihood for binary [[NaiveBayes|naive Bayes]] and the parameter form behind [[LogisticRegression|logistic regression]] / [[GAN|GAN]] discriminators ([[d2l-appendix-mathematics]] §distributions).
- [Central Limit Theorem](concepts/CentralLimitTheorem.md) — Sums of i.i.d. RVs (finite mean / variance) converge to a Gaussian. *"The normal distribution is essentially the limit of any sum of a large number of equal small independent contributions"* — the empirical justification for Gaussian noise everywhere in ML, for [[XavierInitialization|Xavier]]/[[HeInitialization|He]] init, and for [[ConfidenceInterval|confidence-interval]] construction ([[d2l-appendix-mathematics]] §distributions).
- [Probability Density Function](concepts/ProbabilityDensityFunction.md) — Continuous-RV density $p(x)$ with $P(X\in[x,x+\epsilon])\approx\epsilon\cdot p(x)$; non-negative + integrates to 1. Foundation of [[MaximumLikelihoodEstimation|MLE]] / density estimation / [[NormalizingFlow|normalizing flows]] / [[Diffusion]] / [[VariationalAutoencoder|VAE]] objectives ([[d2l-appendix-mathematics]] §random-variables).
- [Hypothesis Testing](concepts/HypothesisTesting.md) — Frequentist framework for $H_0$ vs $H_A$ decisions via test statistic / rejection region / significance level $\alpha$ / power $1-\beta$ / *p*-value. Foundation of [[ABTesting]] and every $z$-/$t$-/$\chi^2$-/F-test ([[d2l-appendix-mathematics]] §statistics).
- [Confidence Interval](concepts/ConfidenceInterval.md) — Random interval $[L,U]$ with $P(L\leq\theta\leq U)=1-\alpha$ — the frequentist *coverage* reading, **not** "θ has 95% probability of being here." Dual of [[HypothesisTesting|hypothesis testing]]; the $\bar X\pm 1.96\sigma/\sqrt n$ rule of [[ABTesting]] reporting ([[d2l-appendix-mathematics]] §statistics).
- [Bias-Variance Decomposition](concepts/BiasVarianceDecomposition.md) — $\text{MSE}=\text{bias}^2+\text{variance}$ for any estimator; in supervised learning extends to the classical U-shaped train/test-error curve in capacity (with the modern [[DoubleDescent|double-descent]] qualification under overparametrization). Foundation of [[CrossValidation]] / [[Bagging]] / [[Boosting]] design ([[d2l-appendix-mathematics]] §statistics).
- [Fisher Information](concepts/FisherInformation.md) — Variance of the score $\mathcal{I}(\theta)=\mathbb{E}[(\partial_\theta\log p)^2]=-\mathbb{E}[\partial_\theta^2\log p]$. Sets the [[CramerRaoBound|Cramér-Rao lower bound]] on unbiased-estimator variance; the [[MaximumLikelihoodEstimation|MLE]] achieves it asymptotically. Foundation of [[NaturalGradient]] / [[KFAC]] / [[LaplaceApproximation|Laplace approximation]] / [[ElasticWeightConsolidation|EWC]] ([[d2l-appendix-mathematics]] §maximum-likelihood).
- [Cosine Similarity](concepts/CosineSimilarity.md) — Magnitude-invariant similarity $\cos\theta=\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{w}/(\|\mathbf{v}\|\|\mathbf{w}\|)\in[-1,1]$; the default similarity metric for embeddings / contrastive learning / vector databases / attention. *"The angle between $\mathbf{v}$ and $0.1\mathbf{v}$ is zero"* ([[d2l-appendix-mathematics]] §geometry-linear-algebraic-ops).
- [Hyperplane](concepts/Hyperplane.md) — $(d-1)$-dimensional generalization of a line/plane: $\{\mathbf{v}:\mathbf{w}\cdot\mathbf{v}=c\}$ divides $\mathbb{R}^d$ into two half-spaces. *"The role of the deep neural network is to find a non-linear embedding such that the target classes can be separated cleanly by hyperplanes"* — D2L's hand-built FashionMNIST decision plane $\mathbf{w}=\bar{\mathbf{x}}_1-\bar{\mathbf{x}}_0$ ([[d2l-appendix-mathematics]] §geometry-linear-algebraic-ops).
- [Einstein Summation](concepts/EinsteinSummation.md) — Compact notation $y_{il}=X_{ijkl}A_{jk}$ where repeated indices are implicitly summed; recovers dot product / matmul / trace / outer product / batched-matmul as one-liners. Foundation of `np.einsum` / `torch.einsum` / `tf.einsum` / `jax.einsum`; the readable form of multi-head [[Attention]] and tensor-parallel matmuls ([[d2l-appendix-mathematics]] §geometry-linear-algebraic-ops).

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-intro-index]] (The Embedded Rust Book — Introduction)

- [Embedded Systems](concepts/EmbeddedSystems.md) — Computing systems designed to run as a dedicated component inside a larger device; constrained memory / compute / power; often interface with the physical world via sensors / actuators. The domain [[TheEmbeddedRustBook]] targets ([[rust-embedded-book-intro-index]]).
- [Microcontroller](concepts/Microcontroller.md) — Single-chip MCU combining CPU core + on-chip memory (Flash + SRAM) + fixed peripherals (GPIO / timers / ADCs / I2C / SPI / UART). The compute substrate the book focuses on; [[STM32F3DISCOVERY]] is the worked example ([[rust-embedded-book-intro-index]]).
- [Bare-Metal Programming](concepts/BareMetalProgramming.md) — Execution model where firmware runs directly on hardware with no OS underneath; the model literally named in the book's title ([[rust-embedded-book-intro-index]]). Implies `#![no_std]` in Rust + manual interrupt handlers + linker scripts.
- [ARM Cortex-M](concepts/ARMCortexM.md) — 32-bit RISC processor core family from Arm Ltd. designed for [[Microcontroller|microcontroller]] use; the standardized ISA used in every example in [[TheEmbeddedRustBook]] ([[rust-embedded-book-intro-index]]).
- [Cross Compilation](concepts/CrossCompilation.md) — Building a binary on a host architecture for execution on a different target architecture; standard in embedded development because target MCUs cannot host a compiler. Rust handles this via `rustup target add` + Cargo `--target=<triple>` + LLVM backend ([[rust-embedded-book-intro-index]]).
- [Memory-Mapped I/O](concepts/MemoryMappedIO.md) — Hardware-interface convention where peripheral registers are exposed at fixed CPU addresses; the dominant peripheral-access model on [[ARMCortexM|Cortex-M]]. In Rust, typed PAC / HAL crates wrap MMIO with `volatile` + type-state enforcement at compile time ([[rust-embedded-book-intro-index]]).
- [Interrupt](concepts/Interrupt.md) — Asynchronous control-flow event in which the CPU suspends current execution, saves context, jumps to an ISR, then resumes after return. On [[ARMCortexM|Cortex-M]], dispatched by the NVIC; Rust HAL crates expose `#[interrupt]`-attributed handlers ([[rust-embedded-book-intro-index]]).
- [Interrupt Service Routine (ISR)](concepts/InterruptServiceRoutine.md) — Short function the CPU executes in response to an interrupt; installed via `ISR(VECTOR_vect)` macro on AVR. 26 vectors on [[ATmega328P]]; ISRs must be short, must mark shared variables `volatile`, and on AVR must explicitly save SREG. C-language counterpart of Rust's `#[interrupt]` ([[embedded-controllers-fiore]] ch. 29).
- [I2C](concepts/I2C.md) — Inter-Integrated Circuit: two-wire (SDA + SCL) multi-drop synchronous serial bus for connecting MCUs to sensors / EEPROMs / low-bandwidth peripherals. Listed as prerequisite knowledge in [[TheEmbeddedRustBook]] ([[rust-embedded-book-intro-index]]).
- [SPI](concepts/SPI.md) — Serial Peripheral Interface: four-wire (MOSI / MISO / SCK / CS) full-duplex synchronous serial bus; higher bandwidth than [[I2C]] at the cost of more pins. Listed as prerequisite knowledge in [[TheEmbeddedRustBook]] ([[rust-embedded-book-intro-index]]).
- [Rust 2018 Edition](concepts/Rust2018Edition.md) — Reference snapshot of [[RustLanguage|Rust]] language idioms (late 2018); introduced the module-path / `use` reform, NLL, `?` in `main`. The edition targeted by [[TheEmbeddedRustBook]] ([[rust-embedded-book-intro-index]]).

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-intro-hardware]] (The Embedded Rust Book — Hardware)

- [GPIO](concepts/GPIO.md) — General-purpose digital input/output pins, the most basic MCU peripheral; [[MemoryMappedIO|MMIO]]-accessed register banks. Exposed on the [[STM32F3DISCOVERY]] via two header rows; the canonical "blinky" first peripheral and the textbook example of Rust HAL type-state design ([[rust-embedded-book-intro-hardware]]).
- [USART](concepts/USART.md) — Universal Synchronous/Asynchronous Receiver-Transmitter; serial peripheral (UART = async-only subset). The [[STM32F303VCT6]] integrates USART blocks; listed alongside [[I2C]] and [[SPI]] as a prerequisite "common interface" in the prior chapter ([[rust-embedded-book-intro-hardware]]).
- [Accelerometer](concepts/Accelerometer.md) — Sensor measuring proper acceleration (3-axis MEMS). On the [[STM32F3DISCOVERY]], integrated with a magnetometer on the [[LSM303DLHC]] chip over [[I2C]] ([[rust-embedded-book-intro-hardware]]).
- [Magnetometer](concepts/Magnetometer.md) — Sensor measuring the local magnetic-field vector (3-axis MEMS); doubles as a digital compass with tilt compensation via an accelerometer. On the [[LSM303DLHC]] chip on the [[STM32F3DISCOVERY]] ([[rust-embedded-book-intro-hardware]]).
- [Gyroscope](concepts/Gyroscope.md) — Sensor measuring angular velocity (3-axis MEMS); fused with accel + mag for full 3-D orientation. On the [[L3GD20]] chip on the [[STM32F3DISCOVERY]] over [[SPI]] ([[rust-embedded-book-intro-hardware]]).
- [IMU](concepts/IMU.md) — Inertial Measurement Unit — multi-axis accel + gyro (+ mag) sensor bundle; the [[STM32F3DISCOVERY]] ships a 9-axis IMU via [[LSM303DLHC]] + [[L3GD20]] ([[rust-embedded-book-intro-hardware]]).
- [Flash Memory](concepts/FlashMemory.md) — Non-volatile electrically-erasable on-chip memory holding the firmware image on every MCU; 256 KiB on the [[STM32F303VCT6]] ([[rust-embedded-book-intro-hardware]]). Hard ceiling on every code example in [[TheEmbeddedRustBook]].
- [SRAM](concepts/SRAM.md) — Volatile fast on-chip memory for runtime stack / `.data` / `.bss` / DMA buffers; 48 KiB on the [[STM32F303VCT6]] ([[rust-embedded-book-intro-hardware]]). Hard limit on the firmware's runtime working set.

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-intro-no-std]] (The Embedded Rust Book — `no_std`)

- [`no_std`](concepts/NoStd.md) — Crate-level [[RustLanguage|Rust]] attribute (`#![no_std]`) that links [[RustCoreLibrary|`libcore`]] instead of [[RustStandardLibrary|`libstd`]]; the one-line switch that puts a crate into bare-metal mode and the gate every code example in [[TheEmbeddedRustBook]] passes through ([[rust-embedded-book-intro-no-std]]).
- [Rust Core Library (`libcore`)](concepts/RustCoreLibrary.md) — Platform-agnostic subset of the Rust standard library — language primitives + atomic / SIMD intrinsics — with **no OS / runtime / allocator assumptions**. What [[NoStd|`#![no_std]`]] crates link against ([[rust-embedded-book-intro-no-std]]).
- [Rust Standard Library (`libstd`)](concepts/RustStandardLibrary.md) — The full default Rust standard library — OS abstractions (FS / net / threads / heap) plus a [[RustRuntime|pre-`main` runtime]]. Structurally unusable on [[BareMetalProgramming|bare metal]] ([[rust-embedded-book-intro-no-std]]).
- [Heap Allocation (Dynamic Memory)](concepts/HeapAllocation.md) — Runtime allocator-backed memory (`Box` / `Vec` / `String`); off by default under [[NoStd|`#![no_std]`]] because dynamic memory is *"not always desirable in an embedded environment"*; opt back in via the `alloc` crate + global allocator (e.g. `alloc-cortex-m`) ([[rust-embedded-book-intro-no-std]]).
- [Rust Runtime (Pre-`main` Initialization)](concepts/RustRuntime.md) — The init layer [[RustStandardLibrary|`libstd`]] ships — stack-overflow protection, `argv` processing, main-thread spawn — that runs *before* `main()`. Absent in [[NoStd|`no_std`]]; must be replaced by a runtime crate like `cortex-m-rt` on bare metal ([[rust-embedded-book-intro-no-std]]).
- [Hosted Environment](concepts/HostedEnvironment.md) — One of the two embedded execution regimes from [[rust-embedded-book-intro-no-std]]: OS underneath (POSIX-class) providing FS / net / threads / mem; [[RustStandardLibrary|`libstd`]] fully usable. Linux-class SoCs (e.g. Raspberry Pi). Mutually exclusive with [[BareMetalProgramming|bare metal]].
- [Bootloader](concepts/Bootloader.md) — *Stage-0* program that runs first on reset, before any application code; minimal hardware init + hand-off to the application image. One of the floor-level use cases [[NoStd|`no_std`]] + [[RustCoreLibrary|`libcore`]] enable in [[RustLanguage|Rust]]; structurally unreachable from [[RustStandardLibrary|`libstd`]] ([[rust-embedded-book-intro-no-std]]).

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-intro-tooling]] (The Embedded Rust Book — Tooling)

- [On-Chip Debugging](concepts/OnChipDebugging.md) — Live host-driven inspection / control of a running [[Microcontroller|MCU]] via a hardware probe over [[JTAG]] / [[SWD]]; in the embedded-Rust stack, three layers: probe-server ([[OpenOCD]] / [[ProbeRs]]) ↔ debugger ([[GDB]] / [[ProbeRsVSCodeExtension]] / [[TRACE32]]) ↔ probe ([[STLink]] / [[JLink]] / [[MCULink]] / [[RustyProbe]]) ([[rust-embedded-book-intro-tooling]]).
- [JTAG](concepts/JTAG.md) — IEEE 1149.1 4-/5-wire debug-and-test wireline; one of two hardware transports ([[SWD]] is the other) in the embedded-Rust [[OnChipDebugging|on-chip-debug]] stack ([[rust-embedded-book-intro-tooling]]).
- [SWD (Serial Wire Debug)](concepts/SWD.md) — ARM's two-wire alternative to [[JTAG]] for [[ARMCortexM|Cortex-M]]; same capabilities, two pins instead of four; dominant probe-to-target transport for the embedded-Rust ecosystem ([[rust-embedded-book-intro-tooling]]).
- [Rust Target (Target Triple)](concepts/RustTarget.md) — `arch-vendor-os-abi` quadruple ([[Cargo]] `--target=<triple>`) naming the cross-compile target — e.g. `thumbv7em-none-eabihf` for the [[STM32F303VCT6]]'s [[ARMCortexM|Cortex-M4F]]; installed via `rustup target add` ([[Rustup]]); the operational unit of [[CrossCompilation]] ([[rust-embedded-book-intro-tooling]]).

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-intro-install-linux]] (The Embedded Rust Book — Installation (Linux))

- [Udev Rules](concepts/UdevRules.md) — Linux `udev` subsystem rules (in `/etc/udev/rules.d/`) matching kernel `uevent`s to set device-node names / symlinks / permissions / ACLs; the canonical way to grant non-root user access to a USB debug probe via `ATTRS{idVendor}` / `ATTRS{idProduct}` + `TAG+="uaccess"` ([[rust-embedded-book-intro-install-linux]]).

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-start-qemu]] (The Embedded Rust Book — QEMU)

- [cortex-m-quickstart Template](concepts/CortexMQuickstartTemplate.md) — [[RustEmbeddedWorkingGroup]] project template for new [[ARMCortexM|Cortex-M]] Rust apps; pre-wires [[CortexMRTCrate|`cortex-m-rt`]] + [[PanicHaltCrate|`panic-halt`]] + `Cargo.toml` + `memory.x` + `.cargo/config.toml` with the four [[RustTarget|target triples]] enumerated; instantiable via [[CargoGenerate|`cargo-generate`]] (against the [[Knurling]] `app-template`), `git clone`, or zip download ([[rust-embedded-book-start-qemu]]).
- [ARM Semihosting](concepts/ARMSemihosting.md) — convention by which [[ARMCortexM|ARM]] firmware requests host syscalls (stdout / stderr / `exit` / file IO) via a magic trap (`BKPT 0xAB` on Cortex-M) intercepted by the debugger or emulator; the no-debug-session host-IO path under [[QEMU]] (`-semihosting-config enable=on`); wrapped in Rust by [[CortexMSemihostingCrate|`cortex-m-semihosting`]]; one of two [[Defmt|`defmt`]] transports ([[rust-embedded-book-start-qemu]]).
- [Vector Table](concepts/VectorTable.md) — fixed-address table of function pointers ([[ARMCortexM|Cortex-M]] reset / NMI / HardFault / IRQs); lives at `0x0` (base of [[FlashMemory|Flash]]) as the `.vector_table` ELF section emitted by [[CortexMRTCrate|`cortex-m-rt`]]; observed 1 KiB / 256 entries in the chapter's `cargo size` output ([[rust-embedded-book-start-qemu]]).
- [Linker Script](concepts/LinkerScript.md) — text file consumed by `ld` / `lld` declaring target memory regions + section placement; **mandatory** in [[BareMetalProgramming|bare-metal]] (no loader); the `memory.x` convention from [[CortexMRTCrate|`cortex-m-rt`]] requires only the `MEMORY` block (FLASH + RAM) from the user; supports optional `_stack_start` / `_stext` / custom-RAM overrides ([[rust-embedded-book-start-qemu]]).

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-start-hardware]] (The Embedded Rust Book — Hardware (Getting Started))

- [OpenOCD Configuration (`openocd.cfg`)](concepts/OpenOCDConfig.md) — small Tcl-syntax file consumed by [[OpenOCD]] at startup that pairs an **interface cfg** (which hardware probe is attached — e.g. `interface/stlink.cfg` for newer F3 boards, `interface/stlink-v2.cfg` for older revisions) with a **target cfg** (which MCU family — `target/stm32f3x.cfg` for the [[STM32F303VCT6]] on the [[STM32F3DISCOVERY]]). The [[CortexMQuickstartTemplate|`cortex-m-quickstart`]] template ships a working one at project root ([[rust-embedded-book-start-hardware]]).
- [GDB `load` (Flashing via the Debugger)](concepts/GDBLoad.md) — the [[GDB]] command that writes the loaded ELF into the target's [[FlashMemory|Flash]] through the connected debug server ([[OpenOCD]] / [[ProbeRs]]); in the embedded-Rust model documented by *[[TheEmbeddedRustBook]]*, `load` *is* the flashing step — no separate `st-flash` invocation. Walks every ELF section with a non-zero LMA (typically `.vector_table`, `.text`, `.rodata`) and writes each at its declared LMA over GDB's Remote Serial Protocol. Bad `memory.x` config → silent post-`continue` hang ([[rust-embedded-book-start-hardware]]).

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-start-registers]] (The Embedded Rust Book — Memory-mapped Registers)

- [Micro-architecture Crate](concepts/MicroArchitectureCrate.md) — **Layer 1** of the embedded-Rust four-layer crate stack: a crate wrapping routines + peripherals common to every MCU using a given processor core (not a specific chip part-number). Canonical example: [[CortexMCrate|`cortex-m`]] for [[ARMCortexM|Cortex-M]] ([[rust-embedded-book-start-registers]]).
- [Peripheral Access Crate (PAC)](concepts/PeripheralAccessCrate.md) — **Layer 2** of the stack: a thin, auto-generated wrapper over the [[MemoryMappedIO|MMIO]] register map of a specific MCU part number. Generated by [[Svd2Rust|`svd2rust`]] from the vendor's [[SVDFile|SVD]]. Exposes the closure-based `reg.read()` / `reg.write(|w| …)` / `reg.modify(|r, w| …)` API ([[rust-embedded-book-start-registers]]).
- [HAL Crate](concepts/HALCrate.md) — **Layer 3** of the stack: ergonomic, portable peripheral API sitting on top of a [[PeripheralAccessCrate|PAC]]; implements the [[EmbeddedHalCrate|`embedded-hal`]] traits. Uses `constrain()` / `split()` to consume the raw PAC peripheral; uses [[TypeStateProgramming|type-state]] to make hardware misconfiguration a compile error ([[rust-embedded-book-start-registers]]).
- [Board Crate](concepts/BoardCrate.md) — **Layer 4** of the stack: pre-configures peripherals + GPIO pins for a specific dev board (e.g. `stm32f3-discovery` for the [[STM32F3DISCOVERY]]). The book's recommended starting point for new embedded-Rust developers; but the book itself stays board-crate-agnostic ([[rust-embedded-book-start-registers]]).
- [SVD File (CMSIS-SVD)](concepts/SVDFile.md) — [[ARM]] CMSIS-SVD XML format describing a chip's full register map (every peripheral / register / sub-field / reset value / valid enumeration). The canonical input to [[Svd2Rust|`svd2rust`]] — the machine-readable form of the chip's Technical Reference Manual register section ([[rust-embedded-book-start-registers]]).
- [Type-State Programming](concepts/TypeStateProgramming.md) — Design pattern encoding a value's runtime state-machine directly in the compile-time type system; illegal state transitions become compile errors. The chapter's worked example: GPIO pin modes as distinct types (`into_af_push_pull::<AF1>()`) and `Serial::new` borrowing a `Clock` struct that can only be produced after PLL configuration. "All with no run-time cost" ([[rust-embedded-book-start-registers]]).
- [SysTick](concepts/SysTick.md) — 24-bit countdown timer **standardized into the [[ARMCortexM|Cortex-M]] core itself** (present and identical on every Cortex-M MCU); exposed by the [[CortexMCrate|`cortex-m`]] [[MicroArchitectureCrate|micro-arch crate]] (not by any chip PAC). The OS-tick / scheduler / coarse-delay primitive ([[rust-embedded-book-start-registers]]).

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-start-panicking]] (The Embedded Rust Book — Panicking)

- [`#[panic_handler]` Attribute](concepts/PanicHandlerAttribute.md) — Rust language attribute marking the **single** `fn(&PanicInfo) -> !` that defines a [[NoStd|`no_std`]] program's panicking behavior; must appear exactly once in the entire dependency graph; conventionally supplied by linking one of the canonical panic-handler crates (`use panic_X as _;`) with profile-conditional `cfg(debug_assertions)` to swap dev vs release behavior ([[rust-embedded-book-start-panicking]]).
- [PanicInfo (`core::panic::PanicInfo`)](concepts/PanicInfo.md) — the struct passed by reference to every `#[panic_handler]`, carrying the panic's **location** (file / line / column) and **payload** (formatted message). Lives in `core::panic` so it works under `no_std`; the four book-listed handlers ([[PanicAbortCrate|`panic-abort`]] / [[PanicHaltCrate|`panic-halt`]] / [[PanicItmCrate|`panic-itm`]] / [[PanicSemihostingCrate|`panic-semihosting`]]) either ignore it (silent halt/abort) or format it onto a host channel ([[rust-embedded-book-start-panicking]]).

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-start-exceptions]] (The Embedded Rust Book — Exceptions)

- [Exascale Computing](concepts/ExascaleComputing.md) — 10^18 (one quintillion) [[FLOPS]] threshold; the contemporary [[HighPerformanceComputing|HPC]] frontier. Frontier (ORNL, 2022) / Aurora (ANL) / El Capitan (LLNL) — heterogeneous [[Cluster|clusters]] of [[MulticoreProcessor|multicore]] CPUs + [[GPU|GPUs]] over high-bandwidth fabrics; coordinated via [[MPI]] / [[NCCL]]. Energy is the binding constraint (~$1M/MW/yr); fault tolerance is mandatory at 10^4+ nodes ([[dis-15-3-exascale]]).
- [`#[exception]` Attribute](concepts/ExceptionAttribute.md) — [[CortexMRTCrate|`cortex-m-rt`]] attribute macro marking a Rust `fn` as the handler for a specific named [[ARMCortexM|Cortex-M]] exception ([[SysTick]], [[HardFault]], `NMI`, …) or the catch-all [[DefaultHandler]]. Enforces two safety-relevant properties: handlers are **software-uncallable** (compile error to call directly) and `static mut` inside the body is therefore **safe** (rewritten to `&mut` — hardware-only invocation on a single core precludes reentrancy). Sibling to [[PanicHandlerAttribute|`#[panic_handler]`]] ([[rust-embedded-book-start-exceptions]]).
- [DefaultHandler](concepts/DefaultHandler.md) — [[CortexMRTCrate|`cortex-m-rt`]]'s catch-all exception handler — `#[no_mangle]` infinite loop occupying every unfilled [[VectorTable|vector-table]] slot (debugger-breakpoint-friendly). Overridable via `#[exception] fn DefaultHandler(irqn: i16)`; `irqn` < 0 ⇒ Cortex-M architectural exception, `irqn` ≥ 0 ⇒ device-specific [[Interrupt|IRQ]] number ([[rust-embedded-book-start-exceptions]]).
- [HardFault Exception](concepts/HardFault.md) — [[ARMCortexM|Cortex-M]] architectural exception fired when the program enters an invalid state (escalated fault). Unique among [[ExceptionAttribute|`#[exception]`]] handlers: **mandatory** signature `fn(&ExceptionFrame) -> !` (must diverge — returning from a hard fault is UB). `cortex-m-rt`'s `HardFaultTrampoline` materializes the [[ExceptionFrame]] from the hardware-pushed register snapshot. QEMU caveat: `-machine lm3s6965evb` does not check memory loads, so example only faults on real hardware ([[rust-embedded-book-start-exceptions]]).
- [ExceptionFrame](concepts/ExceptionFrame.md) — register-snapshot struct (`r0, r1, r2, r3, r12, lr, pc, xpsr`) in [[CortexMRTCrate|`cortex-m-rt`]] mirroring the eight 32-bit words [[ARMCortexM|Cortex-M]] hardware pushes onto the stack at exception entry. Argument of every [[HardFault]] handler; `pc` is the diagnostic primitive — cross-reference against `cargo objdump -d` to identify the faulting instruction ([[rust-embedded-book-start-exceptions]]).

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-start-interrupts]] (The Embedded Rust Book — Interrupts)

- [NVIC (Nested Vectored Interrupt Controller)](concepts/NVIC.md) — the [[ARMCortexM|Cortex-M]] core's architecturally-standardized memory-mapped interrupt controller. Dispatches both architectural exceptions and device-specific [[Interrupt|interrupts]] through the same [[VectorTable|vector table]], honors per-source programmable [[InterruptPriority|priority]], and supports preemption ("Nested") + direct per-source handler pointers ("Vectored"). Three advanced-use properties [[TheEmbeddedRustBook]] flags: programmable priorities, nesting/preemption, and the clear-reason requirement (handler must clear the peripheral flag or the NVIC re-pends endlessly) ([[rust-embedded-book-start-interrupts]]).
- [`#[interrupt]` Attribute](concepts/InterruptAttribute.md) — declarative surface for device-specific interrupt handlers; sibling to [[ExceptionAttribute|`#[exception]`]]. **Not** used directly from `cortex-m-rt-macros` — must come via the device-crate re-export (e.g. `use lm3s6965::interrupt;`, typically generated by [[Svd2Rust|`svd2rust`]] from the chip's [[SVDFile|SVD]]) so the compiler verifies the named interrupt exists on the target chip. Same software-uncallable + `static mut`-is-safe guarantees as `#[exception]` ([[rust-embedded-book-start-interrupts]]).
- [Interrupt Priority](concepts/InterruptPriority.md) — the per-source programmable priority the [[NVIC]] honors when dispatching pending interrupts; determines both **dispatch order** (highest-priority pending source wins) and **preemption** (higher-priority sources interrupt running lower-priority handlers, pushing a second [[ExceptionFrame]]). Must be configured *before* enabling the handler in the NVIC ([[rust-embedded-book-start-interrupts]]).

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-peripherals-index]] (The Embedded Rust Book — Peripherals)

- [Peripheral](concepts/Peripheral.md) — silicon block on a [[Microcontroller|microcontroller]] dedicated to outside-world interaction (sensors / motor controllers / displays / keyboards / serial buses / timers / DMA) — distinct from the CPU core, on-chip RAM, and on-chip Flash. Lets firmware offload work to dedicated hardware (analogue of GPU offload on a desktop). Operated via the [[MemoryMappedIO|MMIO]] convention — a **hardware API, not a software API** (contrasted with Vulkan / Metal / OpenGL); the interface is **language-agnostic** ("Assembly, C, or Rust"). On [[ARMCortexM|Cortex-M]] MCUs (no MMU, linear physical address space), peripheral register blocks are slotted between the [[FlashMemory|Flash ROM]] region near `0x0000_0000` and the [[SRAM]] region near `0x2000_0000` ([[rust-embedded-book-peripherals-index]]).

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-peripherals-a-first-attempt]] (The Embedded Rust Book — A first attempt in Rust)

- [Volatile Memory Access](concepts/VolatileMemoryAccess.md) — a memory access the compiler is forbidden to elide, reorder, fuse, or split. Required for [[MemoryMappedIO|MMIO]] since every read/write has an observable side effect on the [[Peripheral|peripheral]]. **C vs Rust contrast**: C qualifies the *variable* (`volatile uint32_t *`); Rust qualifies the **access** via `core::ptr::read_volatile` / `write_volatile`. Naive struct-pointer access doesn't work because the optimizer drops "dead" repeated stores; the [[VolatileRegisterCrate|`volatile_register`]] crate provides `RW<T>` / `RO<T>` typed wrappers that perform volatile access internally ([[rust-embedded-book-peripherals-a-first-attempt]]).
- [Raw Pointer](concepts/RawPointer.md) — Rust's unchecked pointer type (`*const T` / `*mut T`). Unlike `&T` / `&mut T`, raw pointers escape borrow-checker rules, can be null/dangling/unaligned, require `unsafe` to dereference, and can be cast directly from integers (`0xE000_E010 as *mut SysTick`). The standard entry point for typing a [[MemoryMappedIO|memory-mapped]] register block in Rust; also the access primitive that `read_volatile` / `write_volatile` operate on (volatile access lives below the reference layer because it violates `&T`'s no-side-effect contract) ([[rust-embedded-book-peripherals-a-first-attempt]]).
- [`#[repr(C)]`](concepts/ReprC.md) — Rust struct-layout attribute pinning fields to C-compiler layout (source order, natural alignment, no compiler-driven reordering). Mandatory on every register-block struct because the hardware datasheet defines fixed offsets; without it, the Rust compiler is free to silently shuffle fields and `register.cvr` would read from the wrong physical register. Companions: `#[repr(transparent)]` for newtype wrappers (e.g. [[VolatileRegisterCrate|`volatile_register`]]'s `RW<T>`), `#[repr(packed)]` for unaligned protocol parsers ([[rust-embedded-book-peripherals-a-first-attempt]]).

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-peripherals-borrowck]] (The Embedded Rust Book — The Borrow Checker)

- [Borrow Checker](concepts/BorrowChecker.md) — Rust's compile-time aliasing-discipline checker: at any point in a program, a value has either any number of shared references (`&T`) or exactly one mutable reference (`&mut T`), never both. The three rules for safe [[Peripheral|peripheral]] access map directly onto it: rule (2) "any number of read-only holders" = `&T`; rule (3) "exclusive holder for read-write" = `&mut T`. Rule (1) ([[VolatileMemoryAccess|volatile]] access) is orthogonal — concerns *how* a single access compiles, not aliasing. Precondition: **exactly one Rust value per physical peripheral** — the gap that [[rust-embedded-book-peripherals-a-first-attempt]]'s `SystemTimer::new()` left open, motivating the next sub-section's singleton pattern ([[rust-embedded-book-peripherals-borrowck]]).

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-peripherals-singletons]] (The Embedded Rust Book — Singletons)

- [Singleton](concepts/Singleton.md) — design pattern that restricts a type to at most one live instance for the lifetime of the program. In embedded Rust, the **bridge** between the [[BorrowChecker|borrow checker]]'s aliasing discipline and the physical uniqueness of hardware: manufactures the "exactly one Rust value per physical [[Peripheral|peripheral]]" precondition at runtime via a one-shot gate (`static mut PERIPHERALS = Some(...)` + a `take_*` method that `replace`s with `None`; second call panics). The **one-time `unsafe` bargain** — pay one `Option` + `replace` at startup, get whole-program [[BorrowChecker]] safety. Three tiers: hand-rolled, [[CortexMCrate|`cortex-m`]]'s `singleton!()` macro, and [[CortexMRTIC|`cortex-m-rtic`]]'s `#[rtic::app]` ([[rust-embedded-book-peripherals-singletons]]).
- [`Peripherals::take()`](concepts/PeripheralsTake.md) — the canonical embedded-Rust API for obtaining the [[Singleton|singleton]] handle to a peripheral set; standardized across [[CortexMCrate|`cortex-m`]] (for Cortex-M architectural peripherals: [[SysTick]] / [[NVIC]] / SCB / DWT / MPU) and across every chip [[PeripheralAccessCrate|PAC]] generated by [[Svd2Rust|`svd2rust`]] (for device peripherals: [[GPIO]] / [[USART]] / [[SPI]] / [[I2C]] / timers). Returns `Option<Peripherals>` — `Some(p)` first call, `None` thereafter; the productionized form of the hand-rolled singleton gate. [[CortexMRTIC|`cortex-m-rtic`]] further wraps this to eliminate the `.unwrap()` ([[rust-embedded-book-peripherals-singletons]]).

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-static-guarantees-index]] (The Embedded Rust Book — Static Guarantees)

- [Static Guarantee](concepts/StaticGuarantee.md) — a property of a program **checked at compile time** so that a class of errors becomes a type error instead of a runtime fault, and the corresponding runtime check can be **omitted entirely**. The chapter-opener's framing concept and the unifying umbrella over four embedded-Rust design families already present in the wiki: (1) data-race freedom via `Send` / `Sync` marker traits ([[RustLanguage]]); (2) initialization ordering ([[TypeStateProgramming]] — serial port can only be built after pins are configured); (3) configuration-dependent operations ([[TypeStateProgramming]] — `set_low` on a floating-input pin is a compile error); (4) access control ([[BorrowChecker]] + [[Singleton]] — exactly one Rust value per physical [[Peripheral|peripheral]]). The trade: **zero runtime cost** + earlier failure + self-documenting APIs, in exchange for API-design effort and more elaborate type signatures ([[rust-embedded-book-static-guarantees-index]]).

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-static-guarantees-typestate-programming]] (The Embedded Rust Book — Typestate Programming)

- [Builder Pattern](concepts/BuilderPattern.md) — Rust design idiom in which a complex object is constructed step-by-step through an intermediate builder value, then converted to the target type via a terminal consuming-`self` method (`into_foo(self) -> Foo`). Identified by [[rust-embedded-book-static-guarantees-typestate-programming]] as a **special case of [[TypeStateProgramming|typestate programming]]** — *"if you have used the Builder Pattern in Rust, you have already started using Typestate Programming!"* Three typestate properties make the pattern enforceable rather than advisory: (1) no direct construction path for the target type, (2) consuming-`self` on every configuration step (so the builder is rebuilt, not mutated), (3) one-shot terminal transition. Extends to N-state builder chains where each intermediate state is its own type. ([[rust-embedded-book-static-guarantees-typestate-programming]]).
- [Type-State Programming](concepts/TypeStateProgramming.md) — **updated in-place** (existing page since [[rust-embedded-book-start-registers]] introduced the pattern operationally on GPIO pin modes + clock configuration). Added: the [Wikipedia: typestate analysis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Typestate_analysis) definition (*"the encoding of information about the current state of an object into the type of that object"*); the canonical [[BuilderPattern|builder-pattern]] worked example (`FooBuilder` → `Foo` via consuming `into_foo(self)`); the **two language features** that make the pattern enforceable (strong typing + move semantics by default); the four-family table positioning typestate as the mechanism behind two of [[StaticGuarantee]]'s four embedded-Rust families (initialization ordering + configuration-dependent operations). ([[rust-embedded-book-static-guarantees-typestate-programming]]).

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-static-guarantees-state-machines]] (The Embedded Rust Book — Peripherals as State Machines)

- [Finite State Machine](concepts/FiniteStateMachine.md) — Computational model with a finite set of *states*, a finite set of *transitions*, and rules for which transitions are allowed from which states. Crucially, the **valid-state set is a strict subset of the representable-state set**: most bit-patterns of an FSM's storage do not correspond to a valid state. [[rust-embedded-book-static-guarantees-state-machines]] applies the FSM to embedded peripherals — *"the peripherals of a microcontroller can be thought of as set of state machines"* — and works out a hierarchical FSM for a [[GPIO]] pin (seven leaf states under three intermediate states; transitions are explicit walks through the tree, no diagonal jumps; the backing register's `input_mode = 11` is **explicitly invalid**). Positions [[TypeStateProgramming]] as the **Rust mechanism** for encoding an FSM into the type system so that illegal transitions become compile errors — the FSM is the *what*, typestate is the *how*. ([[rust-embedded-book-static-guarantees-state-machines]]).

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-static-guarantees-design-contracts]] (The Embedded Rust Book — Design Contracts)

- [Design by Contract](concepts/DesignByContract.md) — Bertrand-Meyer-originated software design approach making preconditions / postconditions / invariants **explicit obligations** of caller and callee. [[rust-embedded-book-static-guarantees-design-contracts]] frames contracts on embedded peripherals as a sharp choice between **runtime enforcement** (every method checks state on entry and returns `Result<(), ()>` on violation — *"wastes time and resources"*, pollutes return types) and **compile-time enforcement** (the type system makes the violating call un-typeable — *"if they try to perform an illegal state transition, the code will not compile!"*). Worked side-by-side on the same [[GPIO]] register block: Design A (runtime) vs Design B ([[TypeStateProgramming|typestate]] over `GpioConfig<ENABLED, DIRECTION, MODE>`). Positions [[TypeStateProgramming]] as the **mechanism** for compile-time DbC in Rust and unifies the four [[StaticGuarantee|static-guarantee]] families (data-race freedom, init-ordering, config-dependent ops, access control) as DbC contracts mechanized at compile time. ([[rust-embedded-book-static-guarantees-design-contracts]]).

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-static-guarantees-zero-cost-abstractions]] (The Embedded Rust Book — Zero Cost Abstractions)

- [Zero Cost Abstraction](concepts/ZeroCostAbstraction.md) — Program abstraction whose **runtime cost (CPU cycles, RAM, code space) is zero** relative to the equivalent hand-written low-level code — *"the ability to move certain behaviors to compile time execution or analysis."* The named concept of the closing sub-section of the [[StaticGuarantee|*Static Guarantees*]] chapter. Mechanically substantiated on the file-25 `GpioConfig<ENABLED, DIRECTION, MODE>` typestate API with five lines of `core::mem::size_of` evidence — every state marker plus the fully parameterized configured-pin handle are **zero bytes**. Transition methods *"boil down to a single assembly instruction — storing a constant register value to a register location"* and *"render to the same machine code as a direct register access."* Compositional: *"as long as all components used are zero sized types, the whole structure will not exist at runtime."* Macro escape hatch for combinatorial state taxonomies. Settles the *"zero runtime cost"* row of the [[StaticGuarantee]] trade-off table and mechanizes the *"All with no run-time cost!"* claim already on [[TypeStateProgramming]] / [[BuilderPattern]] / [[DesignByContract]]. ([[rust-embedded-book-static-guarantees-zero-cost-abstractions]]).
- [Zero Sized Type](concepts/ZeroSizedType.md) — Rust type with **`size_of::<T>() == 0`** — typically a unit struct (`struct Enabled;`). *"Contain no actual data … act 'real' at compile time — you can copy them, move them, take references to them, etc., however the optimizer will completely strip them away."* The **mechanism** under [[ZeroCostAbstraction]]: state-marker structs encode information at the type level while taking zero bytes at runtime. **Compositional** — ZST-of-ZST is a ZST, so multi-axis typestate handles like `GpioConfig<ENABLED, DIRECTION, MODE>` carry three independent state parameters with no runtime cost. The reason the [[TypeStateProgramming|typestate]] *"All with no run-time cost!"* invariant holds: monomorphization specializes the type, the optimizer strips the ZST fields. Used pervasively in the embedded-Rust corpus as typestate state markers, [[BuilderPattern|builder]]-terminal markers, [[Svd2Rust|svd2rust]]-generated PAC register-block proxies, and [[Singleton]] tokens. ([[rust-embedded-book-static-guarantees-zero-cost-abstractions]]).

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-portability-index]] (The Embedded Rust Book — Portability)

- [Portability (Embedded)](concepts/Portability.md) — The property of writing peripheral-driver and application code **once** and having it compile + run against many chips / vendors / boards. Framed by [[TheEmbeddedRustBook|*The Embedded Rust Book*]]'s *Portability* chapter as the **"very important topic"** of embedded development. The chapter's central architectural payoff is the **M·N → M+N collapse**: with M [[HALCrate|HAL implementations]] and N [[DriverCrate|driver crates]], the ecosystem would otherwise converge on M·N total bindings; routing both sides through the [[EmbeddedHalCrate|`embedded-hal`]] trait crate collapses this to M+N. Embedded portability is **trait-based** (compile-time contract) rather than syscall-based, because firmware has no OS substrate. Three layers of porting effort: HAL implementations (chip-specific, full reimplementation per chip), drivers (chip-agnostic, **zero port-cost**), applications (*"the part which requires the most adaptation efforts"* — pin reassignment + peripheral-conflict resolution + bus-config). ([[rust-embedded-book-portability-index]]).
- [Driver Crate](concepts/DriverCrate.md) — A crate that implements custom functionality for an internal or external hardware component (sensor / display / actuator), connected to a peripheral implementing [[EmbeddedHalCrate|`embedded-hal`]] traits. Initialized with a **trait-bounded generic** over the peripheral type — the driver itself depends on the *trait*, not on any specific HAL crate, so it is **chip-agnostic**. The N-side of the [[Portability|M·N → M+N collapse]]. Three component categories named by [[rust-embedded-book-portability-index]]: sensors (temperature, magnetometer, accelerometer, light), displays (LED arrays, LCD displays), actuators (motors, transmitters). Concrete corpus examples: [[LSM303DLHC]] (I2C accel/mag), [[L3GD20]] (SPI gyro). ([[rust-embedded-book-portability-index]]).
- [Hardware Abstraction Layer (HAL)](concepts/HardwareAbstractionLayer.md) — Umbrella concept for a software layer that **equalizes platform-specific hardware differences** so programs above it can be written device-independent. Per the Wikipedia definition quoted by [[rust-embedded-book-portability-index]]: *"sets of routines in software that emulate some platform-specific details … by providing standard operating system (OS) calls to hardware."* Traditional HALs are realized as **OS syscall surfaces**, which fails on embedded targets (*"firmware images compiled as a whole … no operating systems"*) — the embedded-Rust answer is a **trait-based** HAL ([[EmbeddedHalCrate|`embedded-hal`]]) with four implementation flavors: low-level register access, OS-syscall-style (Linux sysfs), mock-for-testing, and adapter-as-HAL (e.g. I2C multiplexer or GPIO expander). ([[rust-embedded-book-portability-index]]).

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-concurrency-index]] (The Embedded Rust Book — Concurrency)

- [Send (Rust trait)](concepts/Send.md) — Marker trait indicating a type *"can safely be moved to another thread"*. In embedded, interrupts count as a separate thread; values shared `main` ↔ ISR via [[Mutex]] must be `Send` (so `Mutex<T>: Sync` holds for `T: Send`). ([[rust-embedded-book-concurrency-index]]).
- [Sync (Rust trait)](concepts/Sync.md) — Marker trait indicating a type *"can be safely shared between multiple threads"*. **`static` requires `Sync`** — the load-bearing rule that forces interior-mutability containers (`Cell` / `RefCell` / `UnsafeCell` — all non-`Sync`) to be wrapped in a `cortex_m::interrupt::Mutex` (which **is** `Sync`) before living in a `static`. `unsafe impl Sync` is the manual escape hatch (single-core only). ([[rust-embedded-book-concurrency-index]]).
- [Critical Section](concepts/CriticalSection.md) — *"A context where interrupts are disabled."* The chapter's first synchronization primitive; realized on Cortex-M as `cortex_m::interrupt::free(|cs| …)`. Central trick: the `&CriticalSection` token **statically proves** the caller is inside a critical section with **zero runtime cost**; one token serves many resources. Single-core only — does not give exclusivity on SMP. ([[rust-embedded-book-concurrency-index]]).
- [Atomic](concepts/Atomic.md) — Hardware-supported indivisible RMW operation; the **multi-core-safe** alternative to critical sections. Cortex-M split: `thumbv6` (M0 / M0+) has only atomic load/store, `thumbv7` (M3 and above) has full **Compare-and-Swap (CAS)** — the basis of retry-loop `fetch_add`. `Ordering::Relaxed` is sufficient on single-core. ([[rust-embedded-book-concurrency-index]]).
- [Mutex](concepts/Mutex.md) — Mutual-exclusion synchronization primitive. Embedded-Rust convention (`cortex_m::interrupt::Mutex`): **the lock is a critical section**, so no separate lock-state, no [[Deadlock|deadlock]] possible, and `Mutex<T>: Sync` for any `T: Send`. Canonical peripheral-sharing pattern: **`Mutex<RefCell<Option<T>>>`** — `Mutex` for `Sync`, `RefCell` for reference-granting interior mutability, `Option` for deferred runtime move-in after `Peripherals::take()`. ([[rust-embedded-book-concurrency-index]]).
- [Cell (Rust)](concepts/CellRust.md) — Middle layer of safe [[InteriorMutability|interior mutability]]: copy-in / copy-out only (no references, `T: Copy`). Not `Sync`; wrapped in `Mutex<Cell<u32>>` for the canonical shared-counter pattern. Zero runtime cost — no aliasing rules to check. ([[rust-embedded-book-concurrency-index]]).
- [RefCell](concepts/RefCell.md) — Top safe layer of [[InteriorMutability|interior mutability]] — gives out **references** (`Ref<'_, T>` / `RefMut<'_, T>`) with **runtime borrow-counting** (panics on violation). Required for non-`Copy` shared state like peripheral structs. Cargo of the canonical **`Mutex<RefCell<Option<T>>>`** embedded peripheral-sharing pattern. ([[rust-embedded-book-concurrency-index]]).
- [UnsafeCell](concepts/UnsafeCell.md) — Bottom layer of [[InteriorMutability|interior mutability]] — `unsafe` core primitive; *"allows you to obtain multiple mutable references to its value, but only with unsafe code."* Auto-derives **not `Sync`**; that's the rule that forces every safe-`static` interior-mutability construction in embedded Rust to wrap an `UnsafeCell` in something the programmer proves `Sync`. ([[rust-embedded-book-concurrency-index]]).
- [Interior Mutability](concepts/InteriorMutability.md) — Rust pattern of mutating a value through a shared `&T` reference, realized as a three-layer stack ([[UnsafeCell]] → [[CellRust|`Cell`]] → [[RefCell]]) trading compile-time guarantees for runtime checks at increasing safety levels. Central to embedded Rust because shared state is statically allocated and must therefore live behind a `&T` from both `main` and the [[Interrupt|interrupt]] handler. ([[rust-embedded-book-concurrency-index]]).
- [Data Race](concepts/DataRace.md) — The canonical embedded concurrency failure mode — unsynchronized read-modify-write across the `main` ↔ [[Interrupt|interrupt]] boundary. The chapter's worked frequency-counter example: increment splits into load-add-store; interrupt fires between, reset is silently lost, *"we count twice as many transitions for that period."* Why `static mut` is always `unsafe` in Rust. ([[rust-embedded-book-concurrency-index]]).
- [Deadlock](concepts/Deadlock.md) — Liveness failure where threads wait on each other's locks. **Not** caught by Rust's `unsafe` boundary — *"possible even in safe Rust."* The reason classical blocking [[Mutex|mutexes]] are inappropriate for interrupt handlers (ISR blocks on a lock `main` holds; `main` can never resume to release it). Critical-section-gated mutexes sidestep deadlock by construction; [[RTIC]] is *provably deadlock-free* via priority-ceiling. ([[rust-embedded-book-concurrency-index]]).

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-collections-index]] (The Embedded Rust Book — Collections)

- [Global Allocator](concepts/GlobalAllocator.md) — Single program-wide source of dynamic memory; selected via the `#[global_allocator]` attribute on a `static` implementing [[GlobalAlloc|`GlobalAlloc`]]. Under [[NoStd|`#![no_std]`]] there is **no default** — the user must declare one before any [[AllocCrate|`alloc`]] collection can be constructed. Embedded canonical choice: [[AllocCortexMCrate|`alloc-cortex-m`]]. Interrupt safety on single-core requires wrapping the allocator's mutation in a [[CriticalSection|critical section]] (`cortex_m::interrupt::free`). ([[rust-embedded-book-collections-index]]).
- [GlobalAlloc trait](concepts/GlobalAlloc.md) — The `unsafe trait core::alloc::GlobalAlloc` (`alloc` + `dealloc` of `Layout`) that any [[GlobalAllocator|global allocator]] must implement. Null pointer return from `alloc` signals [[OutOfMemory|OOM]]. ([[rust-embedded-book-collections-index]]).
- [Out Of Memory (OOM)](concepts/OutOfMemory.md) — Allocator failure: no contiguous, aligned region of the requested size is available. **Implicit and non-local in [[AllocCrate|`alloc`]]** — every `Vec::push` is an OOM site, and the cause (a leak / [[MemoryFragmentation|fragmentation]] elsewhere) may be far from the observed site; *"memory leaks are possible in safe Rust."* **Impossible in pure-[[HeaplessCrate|`heapless`]] programs** — no allocator → no shared resource to exhaust. Dispatched on by `#[alloc_error_handler]`. ([[rust-embedded-book-collections-index]]).
- [#[alloc_error_handler] attribute](concepts/AllocErrorHandlerAttribute.md) — Unstable attribute (`#![feature(alloc_error_handler)]`) marking a `fn(Layout) -> !` as the program's [[OutOfMemory|OOM]] handler under [[NoStd|`#![no_std]`]]; the second half of the two-piece activation contract for [[AllocCrate|`alloc`]] (the first being `#[global_allocator]`). ([[rust-embedded-book-collections-index]]).
- [Bump-Pointer Allocator](concepts/BumpPointerAllocator.md) — Simplest possible [[GlobalAllocator|global allocator]] design: monotonically increase a `head` pointer through a fixed region; **no `free`**. The chapter's illustrative `#[global_allocator]` implementation — `UnsafeCell<usize>` `head` + `unsafe impl Sync` + `cortex_m::interrupt::free` for single-core interrupt safety + null-pointer-on-overflow OOM signal. O(1) alloc, smallest code size, never reclaims; explicitly **not** for production (*"we *strongly* suggest you use a battle tested allocator from crates.io"*). ([[rust-embedded-book-collections-index]]).
- [Fixed-Capacity Collection](concepts/FixedCapacityCollection.md) — Data structure whose maximum size is encoded in its type and that **never reallocates**; capacity-exhaustion surfaces as explicit `Result`. The [[HeaplessCrate|`heapless`]] design pattern. Three wins for embedded: [[OutOfMemory|OOM]] impossible / local, linker-detectable RAM overcommit, constant-time inserts ([[WorstCaseExecutionTime|WCET]]). Trade-off: lower load factor (can't `shrink_to_fit`) + per-instance capacity choice. ([[rust-embedded-book-collections-index]]).
- [Memory Fragmentation](concepts/MemoryFragmentation.md) — Runtime accumulation of unusable gaps in a heap allocator's address space: total free memory suffices for the request, but no contiguous + aligned region does. Inflates *apparent* memory usage, makes [[OutOfMemory|OOM]] non-local in space and time, makes `shrink_to_fit` allocator-discretionary, and makes [[WorstCaseExecutionTime|WCET]] of `alloc`-based operations unbounded. Sidestepped entirely by [[FixedCapacityCollection|fixed-capacity collections]]. ([[rust-embedded-book-collections-index]]).
- [Worst Case Execution Time (WCET)](concepts/WorstCaseExecutionTime.md) — Upper bound on execution time across all inputs/states; **the** performance metric for hard real-time. `alloc::Vec::push` WCET is unbounded (depends on allocator + runtime capacity via the realloc tail); `heapless::Vec::push` is *"constant time"* — the decisive embedded trade-off axis. ([[rust-embedded-book-collections-index]]).

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-design-patterns-hal-gpio]] (The Embedded Rust Book — HAL GPIO)

- [Erased Pin](concepts/ErasedPin.md) — [[HALCrate|HAL]]-design pattern for [[GPIO]] pin types that **moves pin (and optionally port) identity from compile time to runtime**, trading compile-time-pin-distinctness for the ability to store heterogeneous pins in a single collection (`[Pin; N]` / `Vec<Pin>` / `&dyn`). Named **`C-ERASED-PIN`** in the HAL Checklist. Two-stage erasure: `PA0::erase_pin(self) -> PA { pin: u8 }` collapses 16 ZSTs into a 1-byte handle (pin identity → runtime); `PA::erase_port(self) -> Pin { port: Port, pin: u8 }` further collapses 4 ports into a ≤2-byte handle (port identity → runtime). Composes with [[PinTypeState]]: typestate parameter rides through both erasure stages — *"both erased and non-erased pin types should provide the same API."* ([[rust-embedded-book-design-patterns-hal-gpio]]).
- [Pin Type-State](concepts/PinTypeState.md) — The application of [[TypeStateProgramming|typestate programming]] to [[GPIO]] pin configuration in [[HALCrate|HAL]] APIs. Pin state (input/output + per-direction mode such as push-pull / open-drain / floating / pull-up / pull-down) is encoded as a **type parameter** on the pin handle, so calling `set_high` on a floating-input pin is a **compile error**. Named **`C-PIN-STATE`** in the HAL Checklist. Two-axis state space — `Input<Floating|PullUp|PullDown>` / `Output<PushPull|OpenDrain>` — via `PhantomData<S>`, bounded by **sealed traits** `PinState`/`InputState`/`OutputState` (downstream crates cannot add their own states). Required-method API: `into_input` / `into_output` **consuming-`self` transitions** **plus** `with_input_state` / `with_output_state` **scoped-reconfiguration variants** (`&mut self` + `FnOnce(&mut PA1<N>) -> R`) for *"temporarily reconfigur[ing] a pin in a different state without moving it"* — an addition over the vanilla [[BuilderPattern|builder-style]] typestate. ([[rust-embedded-book-design-patterns-hal-gpio]]).

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-c-tips-index]] (The Embedded Rust Book — Tips for embedded C developers)

- [Cargo Features](concepts/CargoFeatures.md) — [[Cargo]]'s named-boolean opt-in/opt-out compilation toggles — the Rust idiomatic replacement for the embedded-C preprocessor `#ifdef`. Declared per crate under `[features]` in `Cargo.toml`; gated in source with `#[cfg(feature = "X")]` on the next item or block; **additive across the dependency tree** — *"if any crate in your dependency tree enables a feature for another crate, that feature will be enabled for all users of that crate"* — so a feature must never break the API of crates that don't enable it. Compose with `target_arch` / `target_os` cfg predicates and with `const fn` for compile-time array-size variation (the `static BUF: [u32; array_size()] = ...` pattern). The chapter cautions **most code should *not* reach for `#[cfg]`** — *"better to simply include all the code and allow the compiler to remove dead code when optimising."* Canonical embedded uses: `default-features = false` + opt-in `std` for [[NoStd|`no_std`]]-or-hosted crates; per-chip gates on family-wide [[PeripheralAccessCrate|PACs]]; behavior toggles like [[PanicSemihostingCrate|`panic-semihosting`]]'s `"exit"` feature. ([[rust-embedded-book-c-tips-index]]).
- [Rust Macro](concepts/RustMacro.md) — Rust's compile-time **metaprogramming facility** — the replacement for C function-style `#define`s. Operates on **token trees** at parse time (not on text like the C preprocessor) and expands into **syntactically complete units** (expression / statement / item / pattern). Two flavors: **macros-by-example** (`macro_rules!`, function-call syntax — the common case, pattern-matches token trees with capture variables) and **procedural macros** (`fn(TokenStream) -> TokenStream` in a `proc-macro = true` crate; three sub-forms — function-like, derive, **attribute**). Unlike C preprocessor, Rust macros are **hygienic** and macros that splice fragments of identifiers (`prefix##_handler`) or expand to **part** of an item list **do not translate**. Embedded uses everywhere: [[CortexMRTCrate|`cortex-m-rt`]]'s `#[entry]` / [[ExceptionAttribute|`#[exception]`]] / [[InterruptAttribute|`#[interrupt]`]] / [[PanicHandlerAttribute|`#[panic_handler]`]] attribute macros, [[Svd2Rust|`svd2rust`]]-generated PAC closure API (`reg.write(|w| w.field().bits(...))`), [[Defmt|`defmt`]]'s `info!` / `warn!` interpolation, [[RTIC|`#[rtic::app]`]], [[Embassy|`#[embassy_executor::main]`]]. Chapter pushes back against macros-by-default — *"in many cases a regular function is easier to understand and will be inlined to the same code as a macro"* (see [[rust-embedded-book-design-patterns-hal-predictability|`C-INLINE`]] for the cross-crate inlining discipline). ([[rust-embedded-book-c-tips-index]]).

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-interoperability-c-with-rust]] (The Embedded Rust Book — A little C with your Rust)

- [build.rs](concepts/BuildRs.md) — [[Cargo]]'s **pre-build hook** — a Rust file at the package root compiled and executed on the **compilation host**, after the package's dependencies are built and **before** the package itself. Three canonical embedded uses: (1) code generation (running [[Bindgen]] over a C header to emit `bindings.rs`); (2) shelling out to external build systems (`std::process::Command` to invoke `make` / `CMake`); (3) direct C compilation via the [[CcCrate|`cc` crate]]. **Critical host/target split:** even when the package itself targets `thumbv7m-none-eabi` / [[NoStd|`no_std`]], `build.rs` runs on the host and may use any host-runnable crate — *"you may use any Rust crates which will run on your compilation host."* Also the standard place for [[LinkerScript|linker-script]] generation in the [[CortexMQuickstartTemplate|`cortex-m-quickstart`]] family. ([[rust-embedded-book-interoperability-c-with-rust]], [[rust-embedded-book-c-tips-index]]).
- [extern "C"](concepts/ExternC.md) — Rust's **calling-convention selector** for FFI boundaries; declares C-ABI parameter passing / register usage / stack discipline (rather than Rust's unstable internal ABI). Two forms: imported declaration block (`extern "C" { pub fn cool_function(...); }` — function defined in C, called from Rust) and exported definition (`#[no_mangle] pub extern "C" fn my_callback(...)` — function defined in Rust, called from C). The **function-ABI companion** to [[ReprC|`#[repr(C)]`]]'s struct-layout discipline; both are required on every FFI boundary. Rust references (`&T` / `&mut T`) cannot cross `extern "C"` — they get rewritten to [[RawPointer|raw pointers]] (`*const T` / `*mut T`) because C has no notion of borrow-checked references. **C++ has no stable ABI** for [[Rustc|rustc]] to target, so C++ interop always goes through a thin `extern "C"` C wrapper layer. ([[rust-embedded-book-interoperability-c-with-rust]], [[rust-embedded-book-interoperability-rust-with-c]]).

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-interoperability-rust-with-c]] (The Embedded Rust Book — A little Rust with your C)

- [#[no_mangle]](concepts/NoMangle.md) — Rust function attribute that **disables symbol-name mangling** — the emitted symbol in the object file matches the source identifier exactly (`rust_function`) instead of the namespace-and-hash-encoded long form (`_ZN8my_crate13rust_function17h6c2e4a8b3d5f1e9aE`). The **linker** companion to [[ExternC|`extern "C"`]]'s **calling-convention** half — both are required on every Rust function exported to C, alongside `pub` for visibility. Specifically for the **exported** direction (Rust → C); the **imported** direction ([[rust-embedded-book-interoperability-c-with-rust|C → Rust]]) doesn't need it because the `extern "C" { fn ... }` block references symbols defined elsewhere. Related — `#[link_name = "..."]` for renaming imported symbols, `#[export_name = "..."]` for renaming exported symbols. ([[rust-embedded-book-interoperability-rust-with-c]]).
- [Crate Type (cdylib / staticlib)](concepts/CrateType.md) — [[Cargo]]'s `[lib] crate-type = ["cdylib"]` / `["staticlib"]` / `["rlib"]` declaration in `Cargo.toml` — selects the **systems-library output format** the Rust compiler emits. `cdylib` produces a **dynamic library with a C-compatible export table** (`lib<name>.so` / `<name>.dll` / `lib<name>.dylib`) — only `#[no_mangle] pub extern "C" fn` symbols are exposed; suitable for hosted-OS consumers with a dynamic loader. `staticlib` produces a **static archive** (`lib<name>.a` / `<name>.lib`) — the consumer links at compile time, no runtime dependency; **the only viable form for [[BareMetalProgramming|bare-metal]] firmware** which lacks a dynamic loader. `rlib` is the default Rust-internal form (preserves generics / metadata for Rust ↔ Rust linkage). The `name = "..."` line decouples the artifact filename from the crate name. ([[rust-embedded-book-interoperability-rust-with-c]]).

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-unsorted-speed-vs-size]] (The Embedded Rust Book — Optimizations: the speed size tradeoff)

- [opt-level](concepts/OptLevel.md) — [[Rustc|`rustc`]]'s **optimization-level dial** (`-C opt-level=<N>`), surfaced through [[Cargo]]'s `[profile.*]` tables in `Cargo.toml`.
