For `0xAABBCCDD` at `p`: bytes walk `AA BB CC DD` across `p, p+1, p+2, p+3` — same left-to-right order as the written numeral. **Where used**: [[NetworkByteOrder|network byte order]] (the [[IETF]]-mandated standard — *"the IETF defines big-endian as the network byte order"*), [[PowerPC]] (default), [[SPARC]], [[Motorola68k]] (classic Mac / Amiga / Atari ST), [[IBM360]] / [[IBMZArchitecture|z/Architecture]] mainframes, [[JavaVirtualMachine|JVM]] bytecode layout, [[JPEG]] / [[TIFF]] (MM mode) / [[PNG]] chunk headers. **Practical implications**: `gdb`'s `x/4xb` output matches the value's hex literal directly (no mental reversal); `htonl(x) == x` (no-op); `memcmp` preserves numeric ordering. **Decline**: rare in deployed CPUs as of 2025 — last major holdouts are [[IBMZArchitecture|IBM z/Architecture]] mainframes and network-protocol code paths. ([[dis-4-7-byte-order]]).
- [Little-Endian](concepts/LittleEndian.md) — The [[ByteOrder|byte-order]] convention where the **least significant byte** occupies the **lowest** memory address; subsequent bytes follow in **ascending** significance. For `0xAABBCCDD` at `p`: bytes walk `DD CC BB AA` across `p, p+1, p+2, p+3` — **reversed** from the written numeral. **Where used (dominant in 2025)**: [[X86]] / [[X86_64]] (universal since [[Intel8080]] 1974), [[ARM]] / [[AArch64]] (default — bi-endian capability dormant on [[Linux]] / [[iOS]] / [[Android]] / [[Windows]]), [[RISCV|RISC-V]] (default), [[Alpha]], [[POWER8]]+ on Linux, most modern binary formats ([[BMP]], [[WAV]] / [[RIFF]], [[PE|PE/COFF]] Windows executables, [[ELF]] on x86 / ARM targets, [[ZIP]]). **Why it persists despite visual confusion**: address-of-low-byte == address-of-value (truncating casts are no-ops); increment-with-carry flows naturally from low to high; multiprecision arithmetic mirrors single-precision. **Practical implications**: `gdb`'s `x/4xb` shows reversed bytes — perennial source of beginner confusion; `htonl` / `ntohl` are real byte-swap operations (not no-ops); `memcmp` is **unrelated** to numeric ordering of integers. **#1 cross-platform networking bug**: forgetting `htonl` on little-endian hosts. ([[dis-4-7-byte-order]]).

### Added with [[dis-4-6-bitwise]] (Dive into Systems — Ch 4.6 Bitwise Operators)

- [Bitwise Operator](concepts/BitwiseOperator.md) — Umbrella for the four bit-level boolean operators [[CLanguage|C]] exposes: [[BitwiseAnd|AND `&`]] (per-bit AND — `26 & 54 = 18`; masking), [[BitwiseOr|OR `|`]] (per-bit OR — `26 | 54 = 62`; bit-setting), [[BitwiseXor|XOR `^`]] (per-bit XOR — `26 ^ 54 = 44`; toggling / equality-test via `a ^ b == 0`), and [[BitwiseNot|NOT `~`]] (unary bit-flip — `~26 = -27` under [[TwosComplement|two's complement]] since *"bitwise NOT only flips the bits and doesn't add one"* — hence `~x = -x - 1`). Per [[dis-4-6-bitwise|Ch 4.6]] *"bitwise operators directly apply logic gate behavior to bit sequences"* — they instantiate [[LogicGate|AND / OR / XOR / NOT]] gates per bit position, execute in one clock cycle with no carry propagation, and are the cheapest ops in the [[InstructionSetArchitecture|ISA]]. Distinguished from the [[LogicalOperator|logical operators]] (`&&` / `||` / `!`) which short-circuit on truth values — the chapter's headline category warning. Canonical idioms: bit-test `x & (1<<i)`, set `x |= (1<<i)`, clear `x &= ~(1<<i)`, toggle `x ^= (1<<i)`, field-mask `(x >> shift) & ((1<<width) - 1)`, power-of-two test `(x & (x-1)) == 0`. Maps to x86 `AND` / `OR` / `XOR` / `NOT` and ARM `AND` / `ORR` / `EOR` / `MVN`. ([[dis-4-6-bitwise]]).
- [Bit Shift](concepts/BitShift.md) — The `<<` / `>>` operator family that moves all bits in an $N$-bit value left or right by some number of positions, discarding bits that fall off one end and filling the vacated positions on the other. Per [[dis-4-6-bitwise|Ch 4.6]], **left shift `<<`** zero-fills from the right and truncates at the [[MostSignificantBit|MSB]] — `13 << 3 = 104` (`0b00001101 << 3 = 0b01101000`); **effect = multiplication by $2^N$** (the [[dis-4-4-3-mult-div|Ch 4.4.3]]-deferred *bit-shift power-of-two shortcut* finally delivered). **Right shift `>>` splits into two variants by operand type**: [[LogicalRightShift|logical right shift]] (unsigned operands → zero-fill — `0xFF000000 >> 12 = 0x000FF000`; effect = floor division by $2^N$) and [[ArithmeticRightShift|arithmetic right shift]] (signed operands → replicate [[SignBit|sign bit]] — `0xFF000000 >> 12 = 0xFFFFF000`; preserves sign of negative [[TwosComplement|two's-complement]] values). *"The C compiler automatically selects the appropriate shifting variant based on variable declaration."* Arithmetic right shift floor-divides (rounds toward $-\infty$); disagrees with [[CLanguage|C]] `/` operator on negative dividends (which truncates toward zero — `(-1) >> 1 == -1` but `(-1) / 2 == 0`). **[[UndefinedBehavior|UB]] pitfalls** (wiki-only, not in chapter): shift by `>=` operand width is UB; negative shift count is UB; signed left-shift past the sign bit is UB; compilers strength-reduce `x * 8` to `shl 3` automatically. Hardware: single-cycle via barrel shifter (`SHL` / `SHR` / `SAR` on x86; `LSL` / `LSR` / `ASR` on ARM); ARM embeds free shifts in the second operand of data-processing instructions (`ADD r0, r1, r2, LSL #3`). ([[dis-4-6-bitwise]], [[dis-4-4-3-mult-div]]).

### Added with [[dis-4-5-overflow]] (Dive into Systems — Ch 4.5 Overflow)

- [Integer Overflow](concepts/IntegerOverflow.md) — The condition where the mathematical result of an integer operation exceeds the fixed-width storage holding it — *"a computation that lacks the storage to represent its result has **overflowed**"* ([[dis-4-5-overflow|Ch 4.5]]). All N-bit integer arithmetic is **modular** ($\text{result} \equiv \text{true} \pmod{2^N}$); whether the bit pattern counts as overflow depends on the encoding. **Unsigned rule**: *"the carry out must match the carry in, otherwise the operation causes overflow"* — MSB [[CarryOut|carry-out]] in addition = overflow, absent expected carry-out in subtraction = overflow (resolves [[dis-4-4-2-subtraction|Ch 4.4.2]]'s deferred caveat). **[[TwosComplement|Two's-complement]] rule**: same-sign operands producing a different-sign result indicates overflow; mixed-sign addition can never overflow. The **same adder** produces both `CF` (unsigned) and `OF` (signed) flag signals — software / [[CCompiler|the compiler]] chooses which to read. Distinct from [[BufferOverflow|buffer overflow]] despite the shared word. Real-world cases: YouTube's 32-bit Gangnam Style counter (2014), Pac-Man's level-256 kill screen (1980), Therac-25 safety-flag overflow (1980s). ([[dis-4-5-overflow]]).
- [Undefined Behavior (C / C++)](concepts/UndefinedBehavior.md) — The [[CLanguage|C]] / C++ standard category for constructs whose effect is deliberately unconstrained — *anything may happen*. Distinct from *implementation-defined* (must be documented) and *unspecified* (compiler picks from a finite set). The optimization licence the standard grants: *"if a path would invoke UB, the compiler may assume that path is never taken"* — and may prune it accordingly. Canonical case introduced by [[dis-4-5-overflow|Ch 4.5]]: **signed [[IntegerOverflow|integer overflow]] is UB** (compilers may delete `if (x + 1 < x)` for signed `x` because the predicate could only be true under UB), while **unsigned overflow is defined modular wrap**. Other major UB categories: out-of-bounds array access, [[NullPointer|null]]-deref, [[UseAfterFree|UAF]], data races, strict-aliasing violations, uninitialized reads, missing `return`, `INT_MIN / -1`. Mitigations: [[Valgrind]] / [[AddressSanitizer]] (subset coverage), UBSan (`-fsanitize=undefined`), `-fwrapv` (forfeits the licence), [[MISRA_C|MISRA-C]] / [[CERT_C|CERT-C]] coding standards (prohibits UB-prone constructs in safety-critical code). ([[dis-4-5-overflow]]).

### Added with [[dis-4-4-3-mult-div]] (Dive into Systems — Ch 4.4.3 Multiplication and Division)

- [Binary Multiplication](concepts/BinaryMultiplication.md) — The base-$2$ instantiation of pencil-and-paper **long multiplication** — *the decimal long-multiplication algorithm transferred to base 2 with only the base changing from $10$ to $2$*. Per [[dis-4-4-3-mult-div|Ch 4.4.3]], each multiplier bit produces a partial-product row that is **either the multiplicand itself (bit = 1) or zero (bit = 0)** — binary's digit alphabet $\{0,1\}$ eliminates decimal's $9 \times 9$ multiplication-table requirement, reducing the operation to *select-or-zero, shift, and add*. Each row is **shifted left** by its bit position ($d_0$ no shift, $d_1$ shift 1, etc.); the final result is the sum of all rows computed via [[BinaryAddition|Ch 4.4.1 binary addition]]. Worked example $\mathtt{0b0101} \times \mathtt{0b0011}$ (5 × 3): $\mathtt{0b0101}$ + $\mathtt{0b1010}$ = $\mathtt{0b1111}$ (15). Hardware multipliers (Booth's algorithm / Wallace trees) and the [[BitShift|bit-shift]] power-of-two shortcut are **explicitly out of scope** — Ch 4.4.3's disclaimer *"these methods do not reflect the behavior of modern hardware and are not meant to be comprehensive"* applies. ([[dis-4-4-3-mult-div]]).
- [Binary Division](concepts/BinaryDivision.md) — The base-$2$ instantiation of pencil-and-paper **long division** — *grade-school long division transferred to base 2 with only the base changing from $10$ to $2$*. Per [[dis-4-4-3-mult-div|Ch 4.4.3]], at each step the running remainder $R$ shifts left and the next dividend bit shifts in; the "how many times does the divisor fit?" decision reduces to a **single magnitude comparison** $R \ge B$ — quotient bit `1` and subtract, or quotient bit `0` and skip — eliminating decimal's $0$–$9$ digit-guess. Trial-subtraction uses [[BinarySubtraction|Ch 4.4.2 subtraction]], continuing the [[dis-4-4-arithmetic|Ch 4.4]] **hardware-reuse theme** (addition / subtraction / multiplication / division all built on the same N-bit adder core). Restates **integer-division truncation** explicitly — *"in most languages (for example, C, Python 2, and Java) the fractional portion of the result gets truncated"* — supplying the binary-level mechanism behind the [[IntegerDivision|integer-division]] trap [[dis-1-1-getting-started|Ch 1.1]] flagged at the C-language level; the `%` operator returns the integer remainder ($11 \% 3 = 2$). Worked example $\mathtt{1011}_2 \div \mathtt{11}_2$ (11 ÷ 3) → quotient $\mathtt{0011}_2 = 3$, remainder $\mathtt{10}_2 = 2$. Hardware dividers (restoring / SRT), the [[BitShift|bit-shift]] power-of-two divide shortcut (arithmetic-shift-right), signed-division sign conventions, and division-by-zero trap behaviour are **explicitly out of scope**. ([[dis-4-4-3-mult-div]]).

### Added with [[dis-4-4-2-subtraction]] (Dive into Systems — Ch 4.4.2 Subtraction)

- [Binary Subtraction](concepts/BinarySubtraction.md) — The base-$2$ subtraction operation implemented as **addition of the [[TwosComplement|two's-complement]] negation** $A + (-B)$ — *"subtracting $7 - 3$ is equivalent to expressing the operation as $7 + (-3)$"* ([[dis-4-4-2-subtraction|Ch 4.4.2]]). The existing [[dis-4-4-1-addition|Ch 4.4.1]] [[BinaryAddition|adder]] is reused with **one [[XOR|XOR]]-gate row** on operand B (the *flip-all-bits* step) plus **[[CarryIn|`CarryIn`]] = 1** on the LSB adder (the *add one* step), folding the [[TwosComplement|two's-complement]] negation into the addition at **zero extra arithmetic hardware**. Mode-switching unifies to one wire `Subtract`: `Subtract = 0` gives ordinary addition ($A + B$), `Subtract = 1` gives subtraction ($A + (\overline{B} + 1) = A - B$). Worked examples $7 - 3 = 4$ and $7 - (-3) = 10$ verify all four sign combinations work via the same circuit (the [[dis-4-4-arithmetic|Ch 4.4]] **interpretation-invariance** reapplied). MSB carry-out *"doesn't necessarily indicate overflow"* in subtraction mode — its meaning differs from the addition case; full [[IntegerOverflow|overflow]] rule deferred to a later Ch 4 section. ([[dis-4-4-2-subtraction]]).

### Added with [[dis-4-4-1-addition]] (Dive into Systems — Ch 4.4.1 Addition)

- [Binary Addition](concepts/BinaryAddition.md) — The base-$2$ instantiation of place-value column addition — *the decimal long-addition algorithm transferred to base 2 with only the base changing from $10$ to $2$*. Per [[dis-4-4-1-addition|Ch 4.4.1]], every column's elementary sum `DigitA + DigitB + CarryIn` lies in $\{0,1,2,3\}$, producing a one-bit `Sum` and a one-bit `CarryOut` per the [[FullAdder|full-adder]] truth table (`Sum = XOR`, `CarryOut = majority`). Operationally **simpler than decimal** because the carry is exactly $\{0,1\}$ rather than $0$–$9$. The same $N$-bit adder serves both [[UnsignedInteger|unsigned]] and [[TwosComplement|two's-complement]] operands (the [[dis-4-4-arithmetic|Ch 4.4]] interpretation-invariance principle); the MSB [[CarryOut|carry-out]] is **silently truncated**, the root mechanism of [[IntegerOverflow|integer overflow]]. ([[dis-4-4-1-addition]]).
- [Carry](concepts/Carry.md) — The bit (or digit, in non-binary bases) that propagates from one column-addition position to the next when the column sum exceeds the base. In [[BinaryAddition|binary addition]] always **exactly $0$ or $1$** — the only multi-bit elementary sum is $1+1=\mathtt{0b10}$. Per [[dis-4-4-1-addition|Ch 4.4.1]], every bit-position adder has a `CarryIn` (from the lower position) and a `CarryOut` (to the higher position), chained ripple-fashion. `CarryIn` is implicit `0` for ordinary addition but **exists architecturally** because [[BinarySubtraction|subtraction]] sets it to `1` to deliver the *add one* in [[TwosComplement|two's complement]]'s *flip-and-add-one* recipe. MSB `CarryOut` truncation = silent overflow; exposed as x86's **CF** flag / ARM's **C** flag. ([[dis-4-4-1-addition]]).

### Added with [[parproc-ch05-cuda-gpu-programming]] (ParProcBook Ch5: Introduction to GPU Programming with CUDA)

- [SIMT (Single Instruction, Multiple Thread)](concepts/SIMT.md) — NVIDIA's name for the [[Warp|32-thread]] lockstep execution model: same instruction fetched for every thread, divergent threads masked off — the GPU rename of classical [[SIMD]] ([[parproc-ch05-cuda-gpu-programming]] §5.4.2.1).
- [Thread Divergence](concepts/ThreadDivergence.md) — When threads in the same [[Warp]] take different branches, the hardware serializes the paths — *"performance killer"* within a warp; **free across warps** ([[parproc-ch05-cuda-gpu-programming]] §5.4.2.2).
- [Warp](concepts/Warp.md) — 32-thread SIMT execution unit on NVIDIA GPUs; the latency-hiding unit ([[parproc-ch05-cuda-gpu-programming]] §5.4.2.1).
- [Grid (CUDA)](concepts/Grid.md) — Totality of threads for one [[KernelLaunch|kernel launch]]; a 2D arrangement of [[Block|blocks]] ([[parproc-ch05-cuda-gpu-programming]] §5.4.4).
- [Block (CUDA)](concepts/Block.md) — Thread group bound to one [[StreamingMultiprocessor|SM]] for the kernel's lifetime; up to 3D, ≤512 threads on Tesla, 128–256 thread rule of thumb ([[parproc-ch05-cuda-gpu-programming]] §5.4.4 / §5.6).
- [Kernel Launch (CUDA)](concepts/KernelLaunch.md) — The `kernel<<<grid, block, sharedBytes>>>(args)` syntax; async semantics with `cudaThreadSynchronize` for explicit wait ([[parproc-ch05-cuda-gpu-programming]] §5.3).
- [Global Memory (CUDA)](concepts/GlobalMemory.md) — Off-chip, app-scope, hundreds-of-cycle latency; the bulk store, mitigated by [[MemoryCoalescing|coalescing]] + [[LatencyHiding|latency hiding]] ([[parproc-ch05-cuda-gpu-programming]] §5.4.3.1).
- [Shared Memory (CUDA)](concepts/SharedMemory.md) — On-chip, block-scope, 16K/SM Tesla baseline — *"used essentially as a programmer-managed cache"* ([[parproc-ch05-cuda-gpu-programming]] §5.4.3.1).
- [Constant Memory (CUDA)](concepts/ConstantMemory.md) — 64K cached read-from-device-write-from-host tier; populated via `cudaMemcpyToSymbol`; ideal for per-iteration kernel parameters ([[parproc-ch05-cuda-gpu-programming]] §5.4.3.5).
- [Texture Memory (CUDA)](concepts/TextureMemory.md) — Cached read-only tier with **2D-aware** caching geometry; suits stencil/image kernels ([[parproc-ch05-cuda-gpu-programming]] §5.4.3.5).
- [Unified Memory (CUDA)](concepts/UnifiedMemory.md) — `managed` data with automatic host↔device migration; hardware-assisted from [[NVIDIAPascal|Pascal]] via VM-page-table mechanism; convenience-not-performance ([[parproc-ch05-cuda-gpu-programming]] §5.17.2).
- [Memory Coalescing (CUDA)](concepts/MemoryCoalescing.md) — Hardware merges half-warp consecutive-word [[GlobalMemory|global-memory]] accesses into one transaction; the headline bandwidth optimization ([[parproc-ch05-cuda-gpu-programming]] §5.4.3.2).
- [Loop Unrolling](concepts/LoopUnrolling.md) — Replicating loop bodies for branch elimination + (on GPU) register allocation of small arrays; CUDA exposes `#pragma unroll k` ([[parproc-ch05-cuda-gpu-programming]] §5.15).
- [CUBLAS](concepts/CUBLAS.md) — NVIDIA's GPU BLAS callable from C; FORTRAN-style column-major; the canonical example: row sums as `cublasSgemv(A * ones)` ([[parproc-ch05-cuda-gpu-programming]] §5.18.1).
- [CUFFT](concepts/CUFFT.md) — NVIDIA's GPU FFT library; sibling of [[CUBLAS]] ([[parproc-ch05-cuda-gpu-programming]] §5.18.3).
- [Thrust](concepts/Thrust.md) — C++ STL-style template library for parallel algorithms — uniquely supports **both** [[CUDA]] and [[OpenMP]] backends ([[parproc-ch05-cuda-gpu-programming]] §5.18.2; deferred to Ch6).
- [Short Vectors (CUDA)](concepts/ShortVectors.md) — `int2`/`int4`/`char2`/etc. packed types treated as single words for memory access; potential 4× bandwidth ([[parproc-ch05-cuda-gpu-programming]] §5.16).
- [True Caching (CUDA)](concepts/TrueCaching.md) — Newer NVIDIA GPUs split on-chip storage between [[SharedMemory|shared memory]] and an automatic L1 cache; convenience-for-performance tradeoff ([[parproc-ch05-cuda-gpu-programming]] §5.17.1).
- [Streaming Multiprocessor (SM)](concepts/StreamingMultiprocessor.md) — NVIDIA's multiprocessor unit; contains [[StreamingProcessor|SPs]], schedules [[Warp|warps]] under SIMT, hosts a [[Block|block]] for its lifetime; *"multi-multiprocessor machine"* ([[parproc-ch05-cuda-gpu-programming]] §5.4.1).
- [Streaming Processor (SP)](concepts/StreamingProcessor.md) — The individual core inside an [[StreamingMultiprocessor|SM]]; 32-bit word size on Tesla ([[parproc-ch05-cuda-gpu-programming]] §5.4.1).
- [OS in Hardware (CUDA)](concepts/OSInHardware.md) — Matloff's framing of the [[StreamingMultiprocessor|SM]]'s warp scheduler as a hardware time-sharer that swaps warps on memory stall — the [[LatencyHiding|latency-hiding]] mechanism ([[parproc-ch05-cuda-gpu-programming]] §5.4.2.3).
- [Register Spill](concepts/RegisterSpill.md) — Compiler overflow store for per-thread variables that don't fit in registers; on CUDA, lands in [[GlobalMemory|global memory]] — *"local memory is physically part of global memory"* ([[parproc-ch05-cuda-gpu-programming]] §5.4.3.5).
- [Atomic Operation (CUDA)](concepts/AtomicOperation.md) — Uninterruptable read-modify-write on global or shared memory (`atomicAdd`, `atomicCAS`, `atomicExch`, ...); the primary inter-block coordination primitive ([[parproc-ch05-cuda-gpu-programming]] §5.5).
- [atomicAdd (CUDA)](concepts/AtomicAdd.md) — The fetch-and-add atomic; canonical primitive for cross-block reduction (used in the §5.9 mutual-outlinks example) ([[parproc-ch05-cuda-gpu-programming]] §5.5 / §5.9).
- [cudaThreadSynchronize](concepts/CudaThreadSynchronize.md) — Host-side blocking call that waits for all prior device work; the explicit host barrier and the standard inter-kernel synchronization point ([[parproc-ch05-cuda-gpu-programming]] §5.3 / §5.5).
- [__syncthreads (CUDA Thread Barrier)](concepts/ThreadBarrier.md) — The intra-[[Block|block]] barrier; **cannot synchronize across blocks** ([[parproc-ch05-cuda-gpu-programming]] §5.3 / §5.4.3.1 / §5.5).
- [NVIDIA Pascal](concepts/NVIDIAPascal.md) — NVIDIA's 2016 GPU architecture (P100, GTX 10x0); first to provide **hardware-assisted** [[UnifiedMemory]] via VM-page-table mechanism ([[parproc-ch05-cuda-gpu-programming]] §5.17.2).
- [Functor (Thrust / C++)](concepts/Functor.md) — C++ struct/class with an overloaded `operator()`; carries **state** in its member variables — the property that distinguishes it from a function pointer and the reason Thrust uses functors pervasively ([[parproc-ch06-thrust-programming]] §6.2).
- [Fancy Iterators (Thrust)](concepts/FancyIterator.md) — Umbrella term for [[CountingIterator|counting]] / [[TransformIterator|transform]] / [[ZipIterator|zip]] / [[DiscardIterator|discard]] / [[PermutationIterator|permutation]] iterators — special iterators that virtualize their underlying array to save memory traffic and overhead ([[parproc-ch06-thrust-programming]] §6.8).
- [Counting Iterator (Thrust)](concepts/CountingIterator.md) — Virtual `0, 1, 2, ...` iterator that replaces `thrust::sequence()` without materializing an array; also the idiomatic substrate for `for_each`-as-parallel-loop ([[parproc-ch06-thrust-programming]] §6.8 / §6.9).
- [Transform Iterator (Thrust)](concepts/TransformIterator.md) — Lazy iterator that applies a functor on read; implements **fusion** of `thrust::transform()` into the consuming algorithm via `make_transform_iterator` ([[parproc-ch06-thrust-programming]] §6.8.1).
- [Zip Iterator (Thrust)](concepts/ZipIterator.md) — Co-iterates parallel arrays as tuples; standard idiom for carrying an index alongside a value when composed with a [[CountingIterator|counting iterator]] ([[parproc-ch06-thrust-programming]] §6.8).
- [Discard Iterator (Thrust)](concepts/DiscardIterator.md) — `/dev/null` output iterator for side-effecting `transform()` calls; obviated by `thrust::for_each` for purely side-effecting work ([[parproc-ch06-thrust-programming]] §6.8 / §6.10).
- [Permutation Iterator (Thrust)](concepts/PermutationIterator.md) — Lazy form of [[GatherOperation|`thrust::gather`]]; `*pit == src[map[i]]` computed on read ([[parproc-ch06-thrust-programming]] §6.8).
- [Scatter Operation (Thrust)](concepts/ScatterOperation.md) — Parallel permutation primitive `dst[map[i]] = src[i]`; distinct from Ch1's [[ScatterGather|manager-worker scatter/gather pattern]] ([[parproc-ch06-thrust-programming]] §6.7 / §6.7.1).
- [Gather Operation (Thrust)](concepts/GatherOperation.md) — Parallel permutation primitive `dst[i] = src[map[i]]`; inverse of [[ScatterOperation|scatter]] and the only one of the pair that accepts counting-iterator maps ([[parproc-ch06-thrust-programming]] §6.7 / §6.9).
- [Prefix Scan](concepts/PrefixScan.md) — Running-result parallel primitive (`b_i = a_0 ⊕ ... ⊕ a_i`); `O(log n)` parallel depth via tree-based two-pass algorithm; exposed in Thrust as `inclusive_scan` / `exclusive_scan` ([[parproc-ch05-cuda-gpu-programming]] §5.11 / [[parproc-ch06-thrust-programming]] §6.11).
- [STL for GPU](concepts/STLForGPU.md) — The design pattern Thrust embodies: transplant the C++ STL's containers + iterators + algorithms + function objects onto parallel substrates so the same source compiles to CUDA, OpenMP, or TBB ([[parproc-ch06-thrust-programming]] §6 intro).
- [Hypercube](concepts/Hypercube.md) — 1980s–90s parallel-machine topology — a **d-cube** of $D = 2^d$ PEs with **bit-flip neighbors** (PE $(c_{d-1},...,c_0)$'s ith neighbor flips bit i; d neighbors per PE; max d hops); inductive *duplicate-and-prefix* construction; sub-cube / root / partner formalism; commercially extinct (Intel, nCube/Oracle) but algorithms remain influential — [[MPI]] collectives still use logical-hypercube schedules ([[parproc-ch07-message-passing-systems]] §7.2).
- [Network of Workstations (NOW)](concepts/NetworkOfWorkstations.md) — Commodity-PC message-passing substrate; *"the network is literally the weakest link"*; Ch7 explicitly retires *NOW* as a term, replacing it with [[Cluster]]; modern NOWs are hybrid (multi-core nodes → pure MPI or MPI+OpenMP); positioned as the *economic* answer to the [[Hypercube|hypercube]] market collapse + shared-memory-hardware expense ([[parproc-ch07-message-passing-systems]] §7.3).
- [Infiniband](concepts/Infiniband.md) — Switch-based [[NetworkOfWorkstations|NOW]] interconnect with **RDMA** (eliminates the app↔OS-space copy), 1.0–3.0 μs [[Latency]], 1.0–2.0 GB/s [[Bandwidth]], 5–10% CPU usage, 3–5 μs atomic-op latency, true hardware multicast; building block is a switch *"similar in concept to [[OmegaNetwork|Ω-net]]"*; the *"MPI_Bcast is O(P) sequential sends unless your hardware + MPI build support multicast"* warning lives here ([[parproc-ch01-intro-parallel-processing]] / [[parproc-ch07-message-passing-systems]] §7.3.1).
- [SPMD (Single Program Multiple Data)](concepts/SPMD.md) — The execution model behind [[MPI]] — every node runs the *same compiled program* on *different data partitions*, branching by rank with `if (me == 0) ...`; distinct from [[SIMD]] (per-instruction lockstep) and from MPMD (different binaries per node); [[CUDA]] is SPMD-at-thread-level + SIMD-at-warp-level ([[parproc-ch08-introduction-to-mpi]] §8.1.2).
- [Collective Communication](concepts/CollectiveCommunication.md) — The class of [[MPI]] primitives where *all nodes in a communicator participate simultaneously*; *"all the nodes in the group execute this line. The only difference is the action; most nodes participate by receiving, while node 0 participates by sending."* (§8.6.2); seven named ops ([[MPIBcast|Bcast]] / [[MPIReduce|Reduce]] / [[MPIAllreduce|Allreduce]] / [[MPIGather|Gather]] / [[MPIAllgather|Allgather]] / [[MPIScatter|Scatter]] / [[MPIBarrier|Barrier]]); guarantees are semantic, performance is conditional on hardware-multicast / RDMA / [[Hypercube|hypercube-style]] recursive-doubling schedules ([[parproc-ch08-introduction-to-mpi]] §8.6 / [[parproc-ch07-message-passing-systems]] §7.3.1).
- [MPI_Send](concepts/MPISend.md) — [[MPI]]'s fundamental point-to-point send — six-argument signature `(buf, count, datatype, dest, tag, comm)`; *"safe to overwrite the send buffer"* return semantic — **not** *"receiver has the data"*; typed messages exist as a **heterogeneity broker** for endianness (Intel little-endian vs Sun SPARC big-endian) + 32-vs-64-bit word width ([[parproc-ch08-introduction-to-mpi]] §8.3.3.3).
- [MPI_Recv](concepts/MPIRecv.md) — The matching point-to-point receive — seven args (six match send + output `MPI_Status` struct); wildcards `MPI_ANY_SOURCE` / `MPI_ANY_TAG` recoverable via `status.MPI_SOURCE` / `status.MPI_TAG`; variable-length receives use `MPI_Get_count(&status, type, &actual_count)`; always blocks until matching message arrives; on TCP/IP requires an OS-buffer → app-buffer copy [[Infiniband]] RDMA eliminates ([[parproc-ch08-introduction-to-mpi]] §8.3.3.4 / §8.4 / §8.7.1).
- [MPI_Bcast](concepts/MPIBcast.md) — One-to-all [[CollectiveCommunication|collective]] broadcast `(buffer, count, datatype, root, comm)`; *"all the nodes in the group execute this line"* (§8.6.2) — replaces a hand-rolled `if (me == 0) for (i=1; i<nnodes; i++) MPI_Send(...) else MPI_Recv(...)` loop; performance ranges from O(P) (linear-send fallback) to O(log P) (binomial tree) to O(1) (hardware multicast) depending on MPI build + fabric ([[parproc-ch08-introduction-to-mpi]] §8.6.2).
- [MPI_Reduce](concepts/MPIReduce.md) — All-to-one [[CollectiveCommunication|collective]] reduction with a 12-op vocabulary (`MPI_MAX` / `MPI_MIN` / `MPI_SUM` / `MPI_PROD` / `MPI_LAND` / `MPI_LOR` / `MPI_LXOR` / `MPI_BAND` / `MPI_BOR` / `MPI_BXOR` / `MPI_MAXLOC` / `MPI_MINLOC`); the `MAXLOC` / `MINLOC` variants return `(value, location)` pairs via `MPI_2INT`; canonical O(log P) tree implementation ([[parproc-ch08-introduction-to-mpi]] §8.6.3).
- [MPI_Allreduce](concepts/MPIAllreduce.md) — `MPI_Reduce` + `MPI_Bcast` collapsed into one call (drops `root` arg); recursive-halving/doubling schedule on a logical [[Hypercube]] achieves ~2× the latency of separate reduce+bcast; the operation behind [[AllReduce]] / [[RingAllReduce]] / [[NCCL]] / [[Horovod]] / PyTorch DDP gradient sync ([[parproc-ch08-introduction-to-mpi]] §8.6.3).
- [MPI_Gather](concepts/MPIGather.md) — All-to-one [[CollectiveCommunication|collective]] concatenation — each rank contributes a chunk; root receives *"chunk items sent from each node, stringing everything together in node order"*; *"the fifth argument is redundant with the second; same for the third and sixth"* is an acknowledged API wart; `MPI_Gatherv` adds variable-length per-rank chunks ([[parproc-ch08-introduction-to-mpi]] §8.6.4).
- [MPI_Allgather](concepts/MPIAllgather.md) — `MPI_Gather` with no `root` — every rank receives the full concatenated result; recursive-doubling on a logical [[Hypercube]] in `log P` rounds with bandwidth-optimal `(P-1)/P × |total|` per-rank traffic ([[parproc-ch08-introduction-to-mpi]] §8.6.4).
- [MPI_Scatter](concepts/MPIScatter.md) — One-to-all [[CollectiveCommunication|collective]] chunked distribution — *"the opposite of `MPI_Gather()`, i.e. it breaks long data into chunks which it parcels out to individual nodes"*; canonical opener for the manager/worker [[ScatterGather]] pattern; `MPI_Scatterv` for variable-length chunks ([[parproc-ch08-introduction-to-mpi]] §8.6.5).
- [MPI_Barrier](concepts/MPIBarrier.md) — [[CollectiveCommunication|Collective]] synchronization with sole `comm` argument; *"explicit barriers are less common in message-passing programs than in the shared-memory world"* — most MPI sync is implicit at send/recv boundaries and inside collectives; useful for timing, non-MPI side-effect ordering, and debugging ([[parproc-ch08-introduction-to-mpi]] §8.6.9).
- [MPI Communicator](concepts/MPICommunicator.md) — Group of processes + communication context; `MPI_COMM_WORLD` is the universal communicator; subgroups via the four-call recipe `MPI_Comm_group` → `MPI_Group_incl` → `MPI_Comm_create` → `MPI_Group_rank`; virtual topologies (`MPI_Cart_create` / `MPI_Graph_create`) carry topology metadata for the implementation to optimize routing ([[parproc-ch08-introduction-to-mpi]] §8.3.3.2 / §8.6.10).
- [Buffering, Synchrony, and Safety in MPI](concepts/BufferingMPI.md) — The three-layer abstraction (user MPI program / MPI internals / OS TCP/IP stack); TCP/IP coalesces N `MPI_Send`s into one byte stream that MPI re-parses; **the exact MPI standard send semantic**: *"`MPI_Send(x,...)` will return only when it is safe for the application program to write over the array which it is using to store its message"*; the OS-buffer → app-buffer copy [[Infiniband]] RDMA eliminates; the synchronous tag-mismatch [[Deadlock]] pattern; *"asynchronous communication is considered **unsafe** in MPI terminology"* but most production code accepts the risk for the performance ([[parproc-ch08-introduction-to-mpi]] §8.7).
- [Nonblocking Communication (MPI)](concepts/NonblockingComm.md) — *"Living dangerously"* with `MPI_Isend` / `MPI_Irecv` returning immediately + `MPI_Wait` / `MPI_Test` / `MPI_Probe` for completion checks; the *"don't touch the buffer until you've confirmed completion"* safety contract; canonical fix for the synchronous-deadlock pattern + the comm/compute overlap technique that makes [[Infiniband]] / HCA-driven RDMA worthwhile ([[parproc-ch08-introduction-to-mpi]] §8.7.3).
- [MapReduce](concepts/MapReduce.md) — Distributed batch-processing paradigm: map (parallel per-record transform) → shuffle/sort (group by key) → reduce (per-key aggregation); a [[ScatterGather]] variant with sorting; [[Hadoop]] is the canonical implementation ([[parproc-ch09-mapreduce-computation]]).
- [HDFS](concepts/HDFS.md) — Hadoop Distributed File System; replicates each block on ≥3 disks; stores MapReduce input/output; locality scheduling embodies *"Moving computation is cheaper than moving data"* ([[parproc-ch09-mapreduce-computation]] §9.1.5).
- [Hadoop Streaming](concepts/HadoopStreaming.md) — Language-agnostic stdin/stdout interface to [[Hadoop]]; enables R/Python mappers and reducers via tab-separated `key \t data` text format; combiner reduces shuffle traffic ([[parproc-ch09-mapreduce-computation]] §9.1.1).
- [WordCount](concepts/WordCount.md) — Canonical [[MapReduce]] "Hello World": count word frequencies across a distributed text file; implemented in R via [[HadoopStreaming]] and independently via [[Snowdoop]] ([[parproc-ch09-mapreduce-computation]] §9.1.2 / §9.4.1).
- [Snowdoop](concepts/Snowdoop.md) — [[NormMatloff]]'s lightweight pure-R [[MapReduce]] alternative: chunk files manually, run [[Snow]]'s `clusterCall`, combine with `Reduce` — no Java/configuration; worker data persists in RAM across iterations ([[parproc-ch09-mapreduce-computation]] §9.4).
- [Hillis-Steele Scan](concepts/HillisSteeleScan.md) — Data-parallel [[PrefixScan]] algorithm; $\log_2 n$ rounds, n threads; $O(n \log n)$ total work; requires red/black double-buffer for correctness; load balance degrades each round ([[parproc-ch10-parallel-prefix-problem]] §10.2).
- [Blelloch Scan](concepts/BlellochScan.md) — Work-efficient two-pass [[PrefixScan]] (up-sweep reduce + down-sweep propagate); $O(n)$ total work, $O(\log n)$ depth; standard GPU scan algorithm ([[parproc-ch10-parallel-prefix-problem]] §10.3 / literature reference).
- [Run-Length Encoding](concepts/RunLengthEncoding.md) — Lossless compression of consecutive-value runs as (count, value) pairs; decompression maps onto [[PrefixScan|exclusive prefix scan]] of run-counts → start offsets; OpenMP and [[Thrust]] implementations in §10.5–10.6 ([[parproc-ch10-parallel-prefix-problem]]).
- [Moving Average](concepts/MovingAverage.md) — Sliding-window mean $a_i = (x_{i-w+1}+\cdots+x_i)/w$; computed in parallel via [[PrefixScan|exclusive cumulative sum]] + element-wise subtract-divide using `thrust::exclusive_scan` + `thrust::transform` ([[parproc-ch10-parallel-prefix-problem]] §10.7).
- [Lambda Function](concepts/LambdaFunction.md) — C++11 anonymous function `[capture](params){ body }` used inline without a named declaration; replaces [[Functor|functor structs]] in [[Thrust]] / TBB; `[=]` captures outer variables by value, `[&]` by reference ([[parproc-ch10-parallel-prefix-problem]] §10.7.3).
- [Stream Compaction](concepts/StreamCompaction.md) — Parallel primitive that packs selected elements into a compact output array; implemented via predicate evaluation → [[PrefixScan|exclusive scan]] of indicators → scatter; exposed in [[Thrust]] as `copy_if` / `remove_if` ([[parproc-ch10-parallel-prefix-problem]] §10.6 / [[parproc-ch05-cuda-gpu-programming]] §5.13).
- [Profiling](concepts/Profiling.md) — Empirical measurement of a program's runtime behavior — instructions, time, [[CacheMemory|cache]] misses, heap allocation — to locate [[HotSpot|hot spots]] worth optimizing. The [[DiveIntoSystems]] Ch 12 methodological discipline: *"Optimization should never be based on gut feelings"*; serviced by the [[Valgrind]] triad [[Callgrind]] (instructions) + [[Cachegrind]] (cache) + [[Massif]] (heap) ([[dis-12-1-first-steps]] / [[dis-12-3-memory-considerations]] / [[dis-12-4-summary]]).
- [Benchmarking](concepts/Benchmarking.md) — Controlled empirical measurement of end-to-end program performance (wall-clock, throughput); the **aggregation** counterpart to [[Profiling|profiling]]'s decomposition. Validates every [[DiveIntoSystems]] Ch 12 optimization claim — `isPrime` 47% / matrix-vector 8× ([[dis-12-1-first-steps]] / [[dis-12-2-compiler-optimizations]] / [[dis-12-3-memory-considerations]]).
- [Hot Spot](concepts/HotSpot.md) — A disproportionately resource-consuming code region (function/loop/line) that dominates a program's runtime, cache misses, or memory allocation; the **diagnostic target** of [[Profiling]] and the only profitable optimization target per [[DiveIntoSystems]] Ch 12 / Knuth's *"premature optimization"* law ([[dis-12-1-first-steps]] / [[dis-12-4-summary]]).
- [Callgrind](concepts/Callgrind.md) — [[Valgrind]] sub-tool that counts **instruction executions per function** and records the dynamic call graph; canonical [[HotSpot|hot-spot]]-finding instrument in [[DiveIntoSystems]] Ch 12.1 — `valgrind --tool=callgrind ./prog` + `callgrind_annotate`; revealed `sqrt` = 20.5% of `isPrime`'s total instructions ([[dis-12-1-first-steps]]).
- [Massif](concepts/Massif.md) — [[Valgrind]] sub-tool that profiles **heap memory usage over time** — peak, per-function breakdown, allocation timeline; `valgrind --tool=massif ./prog` + `ms_print`; the memory-side counterpart to [[Callgrind]] and [[Cachegrind]], completing the [[DiveIntoSystems]] Ch 12 [[Valgrind]] triad ([[dis-12-3-memory-considerations]]).
- [Function Inlining](concepts/FunctionInlining.md) — [[CompilerOptimization|Compiler optimization]] that replaces a function call with the callee body, eliminating call overhead **and** exposing the body to downstream [[ConstantFolding|constant folding]] / [[DeadCodeElimination|dead-code elimination]]; auto-enabled by [[GCC]] at [[GccOptLevels|`-O3`]] via `-finline-functions`; the `static inline` keyword is a programmer hint, not a directive ([[dis-12-2-compiler-optimizations]] / [[dis-12-4-summary]]).
- [Constant Folding](concepts/ConstantFolding.md) — [[CompilerOptimization|Compiler optimization]] that evaluates constant expressions at compile time (`3*4+7 → 19`); composes with constant propagation, [[DeadCodeElimination|DCE]], and [[FunctionInlining|inlining]] — the downstream chain inlining unlocks; enabled by [[GCC]] at [[GccOptLevels|`-O1`]] and above ([[dis-12-2-compiler-optimizations]]).
- [Dead Code Elimination](concepts/DeadCodeElimination.md) — [[CompilerOptimization|Compiler optimization]] (DCE) that removes unreachable code and dead assignments whose results are never used; enabled by [[GCC]] at [[GccOptLevels|`-O1`]]+; composes with [[ConstantFolding]] and [[FunctionInlining]] to prune entire branches once constants prove them unreachable ([[dis-12-2-compiler-optimizations]]).
- [GCC Optimization Levels](concepts/GccOptLevels.md) — The `-O0` / `-O1` / `-O2` / `-O3` flag family controlling [[GCC]] aggression; `-O0` no-opt (debug default), `-O1` basic ([[ConstantFolding]] / [[DeadCodeElimination]]), `-O2` standard production, `-O3` adds `-finline-functions` ([[FunctionInlining|inlining]]) + vectorization. Sibling flags `-funroll-loops` ([[LoopUnrolling]]) and `-funroll-all-loops`. Distinct taxonomy from Rust's [[OptLevel]] ([[dis-12-2-compiler-optimizations]] / [[dis-12-4-summary]]).

### Added with Dive into Systems Appendix 2 *Using Unix* (first half)
- [Unix Command Line](concepts/UnixCommandLine.md) — The shell-driven text interface over the [[UnixFileSystem|Unix file system]]: read-eval-print loop (`bash` / `zsh`), `$` prompt, core navigation + file-manipulation vocabulary ([[dis-app2-1-cmdline-basics]]).
- [Unix File System](concepts/UnixFileSystem.md) — The single tree rooted at `/`; absolute vs relative paths; per-file type / [[FilePermissions|permissions]] / owner / mtime attributes ([[dis-app2-1-cmdline-basics]] / [[dis-app2-7-permissions]]).
- [SSH](concepts/SSH.md) — Encrypted remote login: `ssh user@host`. Key-based auth via `ssh-keygen -t rsa` mints `id_rsa` / `id_rsa.pub`; underlies password-less login + GitHub auth ([[dis-app2-3-remote-access]]).
- [SCP](concepts/SCP.md) — Encrypted file copy over [[SSH]]; mirrors [[UnixCommandLine|`cp`]] syntax with `user@host:path` endpoints; composes with [[Tar]] for bulk transfer ([[dis-app2-3-remote-access]]).
- [Vim Editor](concepts/VimEditor.md) — Modal terminal editor: *insert* mode (text) / *command* mode (operations); `h j k l` nav, `:wq` save+quit; `vimtutor` interactive tutorial ([[dis-app2-4-editors]]).
- [Emacs Editor](concepts/EmacsEditor.md) — Modeless chord-based terminal editor: `C-x C-s` save, `C-x C-c` exit, `C-k` kill, `C-y` yank ([[dis-app2-4-editors]]).
- [Nano Editor](concepts/NanoEditor.md) — Beginner-friendly single-mode terminal editor with on-screen shortcut hints; default in many distros ([[dis-app2-4-editors]]).
- [grep](concepts/Grep.md) — Content-search: print lines matching a regex pattern. Flags `-n` / `-i` / `-r` / `-H` / `-v` / `-E`; composed with [[Find]] via pipes ([[dis-app2-6-grep-find]]).
- [find](concepts/Find.md) — Filesystem-walk file-name search: `find <path> -name "*.c"`; predicates `-type` / `-mtime` / `-size` / `-exec` ([[dis-app2-6-grep-find]]).
- [File Permissions](concepts/FilePermissions.md) — Unix DAC model: 3 permission bits (r/w/x) × 3 principal categories (u/g/o); displayed by `ls -l` as `-rwxr-xr--` ([[dis-app2-7-permissions]]).
- [chmod](concepts/Chmod.md) — Mutates [[FilePermissions]]. Octal (`chmod 755`) or symbolic (`chmod u+w`, `chmod o-r`) notation ([[dis-app2-7-permissions]]).
- [tar](concepts/Tar.md) — Unix archiver — `-c` create / `-x` extract / `-t` list, optional `-z` (gzip) or `-j` (bzip2) compression. Canonical pre-[[SCP]] packaging tool ([[dis-app2-8-tar]]).
- [Job Control](concepts/JobControl.md) — Shell mechanism for foreground / background / suspended processes via `&` / `fg` / `bg` / `CTRL-Z`; layered on [[Signal|Unix signals]] ([[dis-app2-9-process-control]]).
- [Background Process](concepts/BackgroundProcess.md) — Process started with trailing `&` so the shell returns immediately; manipulated via `fg` / `bg` / `jobs` ([[dis-app2-9-process-control]]).
- [SIGINT](concepts/SIGINT.md) — Signal 2 (Interrupt) — sent by CTRL-C to the foreground process; default action: terminate ([[dis-app2-9-process-control]]).
- [SIGTSTP](concepts/SIGTSTP.md) — Signal 20 (Terminal Stop) — sent by CTRL-Z; suspends a process rather than terminating it; resumed via `bg` / `fg` ([[dis-app2-9-process-control]]).
- [time Command](concepts/TimeCommand.md) — Measures program execution: **real** (wall clock) + **user** (CPU user mode) + **sys** (CPU kernel mode); `user + sys ≠ real` reveals I/O blocking ([[dis-app2-10-timing]]).
- [Bash History](concepts/BashHistory.md) — Bash's record of executed commands; accessed via `history` and the `!`-prefix recall syntax ([[dis-app2-11-history]]).
- [history Command](concepts/HistoryCommand.md) — Bash built-in that prints numbered list of recent commands ([[dis-app2-11-history]]).
- [Bang-Bang (!!)](concepts/BangBang.md) — Bash history expansion: `!!` re-runs last command, `!n` re-runs entry `n`, `!string` re-runs most recent matching command ([[dis-app2-11-history]]).
- [I/O Redirection](concepts/IORedirection.md) — Shell operators (`>`, `>>`, `<`, `2>`, `&>`) that rewire a process's [[StandardStream|standard streams]] to / from files ([[dis-app2-12-io-redirect]]).
- [Standard Streams](concepts/StandardStream.md) — The three default I/O streams every process is born with: [[Stdin]] (fd 0), [[Stdout]] (fd 1), [[Stderr]] (fd 2) ([[dis-app2-12-io-redirect]]).
- [stdin](concepts/Stdin.md) — Standard input, fd 0; default = keyboard; redirected via `<` or pipe upstream ([[dis-app2-12-io-redirect]]).
- [stdout](concepts/Stdout.md) — Standard output, fd 1; default = terminal; redirected via `>` / `>>` or pipe downstream ([[dis-app2-12-io-redirect]]).
- [stderr](concepts/Stderr.md) — Standard error, fd 2; separate from stdout for error / diagnostic messages; redirected via `2>` ([[dis-app2-12-io-redirect]]).
- [File Descriptor](concepts/FileDescriptor.md) — Small non-negative integer the kernel hands a process as a handle to an open file / pipe / socket; fd 0/1/2 are the reserved standard streams ([[dis-app2-12-io-redirect]]).
- [Shell Pipe](concepts/ShellPipe.md) — Shell-level `cmd1 | cmd2` operator wiring stdout into stdin; shell-level surface of the [[Pipe]] IPC primitive ([[dis-app2-13-pipes]]).
- [xargs](concepts/Xargs.md) — Turns stdin items into per-call arguments for a downstream command; differs from a raw pipe (stdin vs argv) ([[dis-app2-13-pipes]]).
- [Dotfile](concepts/DotFile.md) — Unix file beginning with `.` — hidden by `ls`, holds program configuration ([[dis-app2-14-dotfiles]]).
- [.bashrc](concepts/BashRC.md) — Per-interactive-shell bash config; aliases, env vars, prompt; `source ~/.bashrc` to apply changes ([[dis-app2-14-dotfiles]]).
- [Environment Variable](concepts/EnvironmentVariable.md) — Per-process key/value table inherited at [[Fork]]; `export NAME=value` to set ([[dis-app2-14-dotfiles]]).
- [PATH Variable](concepts/PathVariable.md) — Colon-separated directory list the shell searches for bare command names ([[dis-app2-14-dotfiles]]).
- [Bash Alias](concepts/BashAlias.md) — Per-shell shorthand: `alias ll="ls -la"`; literal text expansion ([[dis-app2-14-dotfiles]]).
- [Shell Programming](concepts/ShellProgramming.md) — Treating bash as a programming language: variables, conditionals (`if [...]; then`), loops, `$@`/`$#` arguments ([[dis-app2-15-shell-programming]]).
- [Shell Script](concepts/ShellScript.md) — Executable text file with a [[Shebang]] first line; needs `chmod u+x` to run ([[dis-app2-15-shell-programming]]).
- [Shebang](concepts/Shebang.md) — `#!/path/to/interpreter` first-line directive that tells the OS which interpreter to load for an executable text file ([[dis-app2-15-shell-programming]]).
- [top Command](concepts/TopCommand.md) — Dynamic process viewer — live CPU / memory / process listing, refreshes once per second; `htop` is the friendlier alternative ([[dis-app2-16-sysinfo]]).
- [/proc Filesystem](concepts/ProcFS.md) — Linux pseudo-filesystem exposing OS state (CPU, memory, per-process status) as readable files ([[dis-app2-16-sysinfo]]).
- [/sys Filesystem](concepts/SysFS.md) — Linux pseudo-filesystem exposing the kernel's device + driver model as a directory tree ([[dis-app2-16-sysinfo]]).
- [lscpu](concepts/Lscpu.md) — Formats `/proc/cpuinfo` + `/sys` data into a compact CPU-topology summary (sockets × cores × threads) ([[dis-app2-16-sysinfo]]).
- [lshw](concepts/Lshw.md) — Walks `/sys` + `/proc` and prints a tree of all detected hardware ([[dis-app2-16-sysinfo]]).

<!-- Added with [[dspy-guardrails]] (Yu & He 2024) — LLM safety / jailbreak-defense vocabulary -->
- [Attack Success Rate](concepts/AttackSuccessRate.md) — Standard metric for [[Jailbreak]] attacks/defenses (fraction of adversarial prompts that succeed); lower = safer. [[dspy-guardrails|DSPy Guardrails]] drives ASR 75% → 5% on [[CodeAttack]] via [[BootstrapFewShot]].
- [CodeAttack](concepts/CodeAttack.md) — [[Jailbreak]] attack that reformulates harmful text-completion as code-completion ([[RenEtAl2024|Ren et al. 2024]], arXiv:2403.07865). >80% ASR across SOTA LLMs including [[gpt4|GPT-4]]; the benchmark used by [[dspy-guardrails|DSPy Guardrails]].
- [Colang](concepts/Colang.md) — [[Nvidia]]'s dialog-flow DSL for [[NeMoGuardrails]]; the "safety as hand-authored dialog flows" design point [[DSPyGuardrails]] critiques.
- [DSPy Guardrails](concepts/DSPyGuardrails.md) — [[BoxiYu]] & [[PinjiaHe]] 2024 method: build LLM safety guardrails as automatically-optimized [[DSPy]] programs ([[ChainOfThought]] + [[BootstrapFewShot]] on a `guardrails` [[DSPySignatures|signature]] field). [[CodeAttack]] [[AttackSuccessRate|ASR]] 75% → 5% on gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct; the optimizer is load-bearing (30% without it).
- [Guardrail](concepts/Guardrail.md) — Defensive layer around an LLM that filters unsafe inputs/outputs. Five-row taxonomy: trained classifier ([[LlamaGuard]]) / dialog-flow rules ([[NeMoGuardrails]] / [[Colang]]) / output validators ([[GuardrailsAI]]) / auto-optimized prompt programs ([[DSPyGuardrails]]) / external sound critics ([[LLMModuloFramework|LLM-Modulo]]).
- [Guardrails AI](concepts/GuardrailsAI.md) — [[Rajpal2023|Rajpal 2023]] output-validator library ([guardrailsai.com](https://www.guardrailsai.com/)). Manual-configuration baseline critiqued by [[DSPyGuardrails]].
- [Jailbreak](concepts/Jailbreak.md) — Adversarial inputs that bypass safety-trained LLMs' refusal behavior. Attack families: code reframing ([[CodeAttack]]), cipher ([[YuanEtAl2023]]), adversarial suffixes ([[WeiEtAl2024]]), role-play, multi-turn buildup. Defenses: [[LlamaGuard]] / [[NeMoGuardrails]] / [[GuardrailsAI]] / [[DSPyGuardrails]].
- [Llama Guard](concepts/LlamaGuard.md) — [[meta|Meta]]'s fine-tuned [[meta|Llama]]-family safety classifier over a fixed taxonomy ([[InanEtAl2023|Inan et al. 2023]], arXiv:2312.06674). Trained-classifier baseline critiqued by [[DSPyGuardrails]].
- [NeMo Guardrails](concepts/NeMoGuardrails.md) — [[Nvidia]]'s [[Colang]]-based programmable rails toolkit ([[RebedeaEtAl2023|Rebedea et al. 2023]], arXiv:2310.10501). Dialog-flow baseline critiqued by [[DSPyGuardrails]].

<!-- Added with [[2025-bionlp-archehr-qa-neural]] (Reddy et al., BioNLP 2025) — clinical-QA / evidence-grounded vocabulary -->
- [ArchEHR-QA 2025](concepts/ArchEHRQA2025.md) — BioNLP 2025 shared task on grounded clinical QA over [[MIMIC]]-derived EHR notes; 120 cases (20 dev / 100 test) with sentence-level `essential` / `supplementary` / `not-relevant` labels. Two-axis eval: Factuality (cite-set F1) + Relevance (mean of [[bleu|BLEU]] / [[ROUGE]] / [[SARI]] / [[BERTScore]] / [[AlignScore]] / [[MEDCON]]). Won by [[DMISLab]], runner-up [[Ours_Neural|Neural]] ([[2025-bionlp-archehr-qa-neural|MIPROv2-optimized]]).
- [MIMIC](concepts/MIMIC.md) — Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care — MIT Lab for Computational Physiology's de-identified ICU EHR corpus (MIMIC-III, MIMIC-IV). Source of the [[ArchEHRQA2025]] notes.
- [emrQA](concepts/emrQA.md) — Large-scale clinical-QA dataset ([[AnusriPampari|Pampari]] et al. 2018, arXiv:1809.00732); built by repurposing existing EHR annotations into QA pairs. Predecessor to [[ArchEHRQA2025]]'s more naturalistic design.
- [BERTScore](concepts/BERTScore.md) — Contextual-embedding-based generation metric ([[TianyiZhang|Zhang]] et al., ICLR 2020). Greedy-matched cosine sim over [[bert|BERT]] token embeddings → P/R/F1. Component of the [[ArchEHRQA2025]] relevance reward.
- [AlignScore](concepts/AlignScore.md) — Factual-consistency metric (Zha et al. 2023, arXiv:2305.16739); a unified alignment function trained on diverse alignment data. Task-agnostic; component of the [[ArchEHRQA2025]] relevance reward.
- [MEDCON](concepts/MEDCON.md) — Medical-concept-coverage metric ([[WenwaiYim|Yim]] et al., *Scientific Data* 2023, AciBench). UMLS-concept F1 between candidate and reference clinical generations. Component of the [[ArchEHRQA2025]] relevance reward.
- [ROUGE](concepts/ROUGE.md) — Recall-oriented summarization metric (Lin, ACL 2004). ROUGE-N / ROUGE-L / ROUGE-Lsum. Component of the [[ArchEHRQA2025]] relevance reward.
- [SARI](concepts/SARI.md) — Text-simplification metric (Xu et al., TACL 2016). Rewards add/keep/delete operations relative to input + references. Component of the [[ArchEHRQA2025]] relevance reward; [[Ours_Neural|Neural]] is best-in-class on SARI (73.1).
- [Evidence-Grounded QA](concepts/EvidenceGroundedQA.md) — QA paradigm where every answer claim must cite a supporting span. Two-axis eval (factuality + relevance); natural fit for [[LMProgram|multi-stage LM programs]] and [[MIPROv2]]-style per-stage prompt optimization. Canonical clinical instance: [[ArchEHRQA2025]].
- [GPT-4.1](concepts/GPT4_1.md) — [[openai|OpenAI]] frontier API model (April 2025). Backbone LM for [[2025-bionlp-archehr-qa-neural|Neural's]] MIPROv2-optimized clinical-QA pipeline; GPT-4.1 Mini is one of two evaluation LMs in [[2507.19457-gepa|GEPA]].

<!-- Added with [[2507.03152-medval]] (MedVAL — Aali et al., arXiv 2026) — clinical-text-validation / distillation / medical-NLP vocabulary -->
- [MedVAL](concepts/MedVAL.md) — Self-supervised distillation method for training LM validators of clinical text without physician labels or reference outputs. Three stages: synthetic perturbation → [[GeneratorValidatorConsistency|$\mathcal{M}_\mathrm{MedVAL}$ filter]] → [[BootstrapFinetune|`dspy.BootstrapFinetune`]] + [[QLoRA]] PEFT. Lifts avg 4-class F1 from 36.7% → 51.0% across 10 LMs; safe/unsafe binary F1 from 66.2% → 82.8%; GPT-4o MedVAL is **non-inferior to a single human expert** ($p < 0.001$).
- [MedVAL-Bench](concepts/MedVALBench.md) — 6-task / 840-output physician-annotated benchmark released with [[2507.03152-medval|MedVAL]]; 12-physician panel; covers medication QA, query summarization, radiology impression generation, radiology impression simplification, English→Spanish hospital-course translation, doctor-patient dialogue summarization. Krippendorff's $\alpha = 0.848$ overall.
- [MedVAL-4B](concepts/MedVAL4B.md) — Best-performing open-source distilled validator released with [[2507.03152-medval|MedVAL]]; Qwen3-4B base + [[QLoRA]] on a single A6000; F1 = 0.527 beats baselines of MedGemma-27B / Llama-3.3-70B / GPT-4o Mini / Gemini 2.0 Flash.
- [Risk Level Taxonomy](concepts/RiskLevelTaxonomy.md) — Physician-defined 4-class clinical safety taxonomy ([[2507.03152-medval|MedVAL]]): Level 1 No risk / Level 2 Low risk / Level 3 Moderate risk / Level 4 High risk; binary deployment gate at Level 2/3 boundary. Mapped to perturbation levels $\delta \in \{0, 0.33, 0.67, 1.0\}$ for synthetic-data generation.
- [Medical Text Validation](concepts/MedicalTextValidation.md) — Task family: given input + LM-generated medical output, assign a risk grade + identify error categories — without physician labels at training time, without reference outputs at test time, without restricting to a single sub-specialty. Defined by [[2507.03152-medval|MedVAL]].
- [Generator-Validator Consistency](concepts/GeneratorValidatorConsistency.md) — The $\mathcal{M}_\mathrm{MedVAL}$ filter metric ([[2507.03152-medval|MedVAL]] §2.1) — absolute + relative consistency between expected and validator-predicted degradation levels; bounds in $[0, 1]$; retain examples with $\mathcal{M}_\mathrm{MedVAL} \ge 0.9$. Ablation: filtering at $\tau = 0.9$ retains 57% of data and outperforms unfiltered 100%.
- [QLoRA](concepts/QLoRA.md) — Quantized Low-Rank Adaptation (Dettmers et al., NeurIPS 2023) — 4-bit NF4 quantization of frozen base + BF16 LoRA adapters + double quantization + paged optimizers. ~12× memory reduction vs full FT. **Integrated into [[DSPy]]'s local PEFT pipeline** via [[2507.03152-medval|MedVAL]]'s GitHub PR.
- [MedGemma](concepts/MedGemma.md) — [[google|Google]]'s medically-adapted [[google|Gemma]] LLM. **MedGemma-27B** baseline F1 = 0.482 on [[MedVALBench]] — strongest open-source baseline, but beaten by 7×-smaller [[MedVAL4B|MedVAL-Qwen3-4B]] (0.527).
- [LLM-as-a-Judge](concepts/LLMAsAJudge.md) — Evaluation paradigm where one LM scores another LM's output. Generic methods often miss subtle clinically-significant errors; [[MedVAL]] is the first wiki paper to demonstrate the paradigm reaching expert-level reliability on clinical text.
- [MEDEC](concepts/MEDEC.md) — Medical error detection/correction benchmark on the [[MedHELM]] leaderboard. [[2507.03152-medval|MedVAL]] §3.6 uses MEDEC as an out-of-distribution test: GPT-4o accuracy 58.0% → 63.3%, GPT-4o Mini 53.3% → 54.4%.
- [MedHELM](concepts/MedHELM.md) — Medical extension of Stanford's HELM leaderboard. [[2507.03152-medval|MedVAL]] uses MedHELM-reported baselines to set up fair external comparisons.
- [FActScore](concepts/FActScore.md) — Fine-grained atomic evaluation of factual precision (Min et al., arXiv:2305.14251, 2023). Domain-specific extractors + structured KB lookup. [[2507.03152-medval|MedVAL]] drops both dependencies.
- [GREEN](concepts/GREEN.md) — Generative Radiology Report Evaluation and Error Notation (Ostmeier, Xu, Chen, Varma, Blankemeier, Bluethgen, Michalson, Moseley, Langlotz & Chaudhari, arXiv:2405.03595, 2024) — direct radiology-only ancestor of [[MedVAL]] from the same Stanford lineage.
- [MedHAL](concepts/MedHAL.md) — Evaluation dataset for medical hallucination detection (Mehenni & Zouaq, arXiv:2504.08596, 2025) — physician-in-the-loop baseline that [[MedVAL]] drops as a requirement.
- [VeriFact](concepts/VeriFact.md) — Retrieval-based factuality verification of LLM-generated clinical text using EHR data (Chung et al., arXiv:2501.16672, 2025). [[MedVAL]] drops the retrieval dependency and adds LM training.
- [DocLens](concepts/DocLens.md) — Multi-aspect fine-grained evaluation for medical text generation (Xie et al., arXiv:2311.09581, 2023) — completeness / conciseness / attribution; requires reference outputs.
- [ReXTrust](concepts/ReXTrust.md) — Fine-grained hallucination detection for AI-generated radiology reports (Hardy, Kim, Ro & Rajpurkar, arXiv:2412.15264, 2024). Radiology-only prior art.
- [ReXErr](concepts/ReXErr.md) — Synthesizing clinically meaningful errors in radiology reports (Rao et al., Pacific Symposium 2024). Methodological ancestor of [[MedVAL]]'s perturbation injection.
- [FineRadScore](concepts/FineRadScore.md) — Line-by-line radiology report evaluation with severity scores (Huang, Banerjee, Wu, Pontes Reis & Rajpurkar, arXiv:2405.20613, 2024). Radiology-only prior art.
- [Non-Inferiority Test](concepts/NonInferiorityTest.md) — Statistical test that aims to show a new method is *not meaningfully worse* than a comparator. [[2507.03152-medval|MedVAL]] uses paired item-level bootstrap (B = 10,000) with $\mathrm{LCB}_{95\%}(\Delta) > -0.05$ to declare GPT-4o MedVAL non-inferior to a single human expert.
- [McNemar's Test](concepts/McNemarTest.md) — Non-parametric test for paired classification differences; used in [[2507.03152-medval|MedVAL]] §2.3.3 with Bonferroni correction over 40 baseline-vs-MedVAL comparisons.
- [Krippendorff's Alpha](concepts/KrippendorffAlpha.md) — Inter-rater agreement statistic; [[MedVALBench]] reports overall $\alpha = 0.848$ across 6 tasks (range 0.560 → 0.943).
- [Cohen's Kappa](concepts/CohensKappa.md) — Two-rater categorical agreement statistic; [[2507.03152-medval|MedVAL]] uses **linearly-weighted** $\kappa$ for ordinal 4-class risk grading.
- [MedicationQA](concepts/MedicationQA.md) — Real-world medication-related consumer health Q&A dataset. Source of the [[MedVALBench]] `medication2answer` task; in-distribution.
- [MeQSum](concepts/MeQSum.md) — Medical question summarization dataset. Source of the [[MedVALBench]] `query2question` task; lowest inter-physician $\alpha = 0.560$.
- [Open-i](concepts/Openi.md) — De-identified narrative chest x-ray reports from Indiana Network for Patient Care. Source of [[MedVALBench]] `report2impression` (in-dist) and `report2simplified` (train-only) tasks.
- [MIMIC-IV](concepts/MIMICIV.md) — Successor to MIMIC-III; Beth Israel Deaconess ICU EHR data. Source of [[MedVALBench]] `impression2simplified` task (OOD).
- [MIMIC-IV-BHC](concepts/MIMICIVBHC.md) — Curated brief-hospital-course sections from MIMIC-IV discharge summaries ([[AsadAali|Aali]] et al., JAMIA 2025). Source of [[MedVALBench]] `bhc2spanish` task (OOD, English → Spanish).
- [ACI-Bench](concepts/ACIBench.md) — Ambient Clinical Intelligence Benchmark (Yim et al. 2023) — 207 doctor-patient conversations + visit notes. Source of [[MedVALBench]] `dialogue2note` task (OOD, longest avg input at 1,497 tokens).

<!-- Added with [[2604.14585-prompt-optimization-coin-flip]] (Zhang et al., AWS GenAI + HSBC, arXiv 2026) — compound-AI-system optimization audit, ANOVA methodology, diagnostic framework -->
- [Agent Coupling](concepts/AgentCoupling.md) — Structural property of a [[CompoundAISystem|compound AI system]] determining whether per-agent prompts must be jointly optimized. Operationalized as the $A \times B$ interaction term in a two-way [[ANOVAVarianceDecomposition|ANOVA]]. [[2604.14585-prompt-optimization-coin-flip|Zhang et al. 2026]]: non-significant in all 6 tested model×task conditions ($p > 0.52$, $F < 1.0$).
- [ANOVA Variance Decomposition](concepts/ANOVAVarianceDecomposition.md) — [[2604.14585-prompt-optimization-coin-flip|Zhang et al. 2026]]'s methodological contribution: classical statistical decomposition of total variance into question / Agent-A / Agent-B / $A \times B$ / residual; offered as a **falsifiable evaluation protocol for compositional behavior in multi-agent systems**. ~$80, 1 day per pipeline.
- [Headroom Test](concepts/HeadroomTest.md) — Fast diagnostic from [[2604.14585-prompt-optimization-coin-flip|Zhang et al. 2026]] (Stage 2 of the [[CompoundAIDiagnostic|practitioner framework]]): generate 10–20 candidate prompts; if best-of-N gain $> 2$ pts over zero-shot, optimize — otherwise use zero-shot. ~$5, 10 min. Perfectly separated 1 successful from 3 failed tasks in the paper's data.
- ["Can But Doesn't" Pattern](concepts/CanButDoesntPattern.md) — Property of tasks where prompt optimization works ([[2604.14585-prompt-optimization-coin-flip|Zhang et al. 2026]]): the model has latent capability to produce the required output format but does not zero-shot default to it. Canonical example: [[HelpSteer2]]'s JSON rubric (68.0 → 74.8 on [[ClaudeHaiku45|Haiku]]).
- [Coin-Flip Optimization](concepts/CoinFlipOptimization.md) — The headline finding from [[2604.14585-prompt-optimization-coin-flip|Zhang et al. 2026]]: **49% of 72 optimization runs on [[ClaudeHaiku45|Claude Haiku 4.5]] score below zero-shot** (binomial $p = 0.91$). Two compounding mechanisms: 20-question evaluation noise + iterative-method overfitting.
- [Joint Optimization](concepts/JointOptimization.md) — The premise behind [[TextGrad]] / [[DSPy]] / [[GPTSwarm]] / [[Helix]] — falsified by [[2604.14585-prompt-optimization-coin-flip|Zhang et al. 2026]] for two-agent feed-forward pipelines on mid-tier models.
- [Independent Optimization](concepts/IndependentOptimization.md) — Per-agent prompt search; the alternative the [[ANOVAVarianceDecomposition|ANOVA]] test validates when $F_{A \times B} < 1$. Linear-cost in $|M|$ vs exponential for joint search.
- [Compound AI Diagnostic Framework](concepts/CompoundAIDiagnostic.md) — [[2604.14585-prompt-optimization-coin-flip|Zhang et al. 2026]]'s two-stage practitioner decision framework: Stage 1 ANOVA coupling test (~$80) → Stage 2 headroom test (~$5). Rules out $1K–$10K [[TextGrad]] / [[DSPy]] compilation runs in 3 of 4 tasks in the paper's data.
- [Model-Specificity Shelf Life](concepts/ModelSpecificityShelfLife.md) — [[2604.14585-prompt-optimization-coin-flip|Zhang et al. 2026]]'s meta-finding: any prompt optimization strategy has a shelf life shorter than the model release cycle. Headroom is shrinking as base models absorb scaffold techniques via RL training.
- [PROSE Optimizer](concepts/PROSEOptimizer.md) — *PRompt Optimization via Structured Evolution* — risk-aware evolutionary optimizer introduced by [[2604.14585-prompt-optimization-coin-flip|Zhang et al. 2026]] (Appendix C). Decomposes prompts into 5 components × 6 operators × risk-adjusted fitness (Sharpe ratio + DRO). Shows **no measurable advantage** over simpler methods — a deliberate negative result.
- [TextGrad](concepts/TextGrad.md) — Yuksekgonul et al., *Nature* 2025 — end-to-end joint optimizer propagating textual "gradients" through compound LM systems. Joint-optimization premise audited (and falsified for two-agent feed-forward pipelines) by [[2604.14585-prompt-optimization-coin-flip|Zhang et al. 2026]].
- [GPTSwarm](concepts/GPTSwarm.md) — Zhuge et al., ICML 2024 — agent graphs as optimizable structures. Joint-optimization sibling to [[TextGrad]] / [[DSPy]] / [[Helix]].
- [Helix](concepts/Helix.md) — Zhu et al. 2026 — dual-helix prompt + query co-evolution. Premise specifically called into question by [[2604.14585-prompt-optimization-coin-flip|Zhang et al. 2026]] Study 1.
- [PromptBreeder](concepts/PromptBreeder.md) — Fernando et al. 2024 — self-referential evolutionary prompt optimizer. Benchmarked by [[2604.14585-prompt-optimization-coin-flip|Zhang et al. 2026]]; wins 3/8 task×model cells (more than any other single method, but most gains below the 2-pt headroom threshold).
- [ProTeGi](concepts/ProTeGi.md) — Pryzant et al. 2023 — automatic prompt optimization with "gradient descent" + beam search. Single-prompt antecedent of [[TextGrad]]'s multi-component generalization.
- [XSum](concepts/XSum.md) — Extreme summarization benchmark (Narayan et al. 2018); single-sentence summaries of BBC articles. Used in **both** Study 1 (loose coupling, confirmed) and Study 2 (free-form, fails [[HeadroomTest|headroom]]) of [[2604.14585-prompt-optimization-coin-flip|Zhang et al. 2026]] — the cross-study bridge benchmark.
- [MBPP](concepts/MBPP.md) — Mostly Basic Python Problems (Austin et al. 2021); Python program synthesis benchmark. Highest interaction-variance share in Study 1 of [[2604.14585-prompt-optimization-coin-flip|Zhang et al. 2026]] (2.15% Haiku) — but still $F < 1$.
- [HelpSteer2](concepts/HelpSteer2.md) — Open helpfulness-rating dataset (Wang et al. 2024); requires JSON-formatted rubric output. **The sole task where all 6 prompt optimizers beat zero-shot on Haiku** in [[2604.14585-prompt-optimization-coin-flip|Zhang et al. 2026]] (best $+6.8$); the canonical [[CanButDoesntPattern|"can but doesn't"]] exemplar.
- [WildBench](concepts/WildBench.md) — Real-user prompts benchmark (Lin et al. 2024). Canonical Study 2 negative example: free-form output → no [[CanButDoesntPattern|"can but doesn't"]] gap → −0.82 avg gain across 6 optimizers in [[2604.14585-prompt-optimization-coin-flip|Zhang et al. 2026]].
- [Feedback-Bench](concepts/FeedbackBench.md) — [[Prometheus2|Prometheus 2]]'s evaluation benchmark (Kim et al. 2024); free-form fine-grained feedback. Best Haiku→Nova reversal example in [[2604.14585-prompt-optimization-coin-flip|Zhang et al. 2026]] (1/6 on Haiku → 4/6 on Nova).

### Added with [[2408.08849-ecg-chat]] (ECG-Chat — Zhao et al. 2025)
- [ECG](concepts/ECG.md) — Electrocardiogram modality; 12-lead 500 Hz / 10 s standard. Canonical input for cardiology MLLMs.
- [ECG Encoder](concepts/ECGEncoder.md) — ECG-Chat's 12-layer 1d-ViT (patch 50, hidden 768) over raw 12-lead signal; scaling shows encoder size is **not** the bottleneck (43M→128M params: F1 ~flat).
- [CoCa](concepts/CoCa.md) — Contrastive Captioner (Yu et al. 2022); dual contrastive + captioning loss; ECG-Chat's pretraining architecture.
- [Vicuna-13B](concepts/Vicuna13B.md) — Open-weight LLaMA-derivative chat model; ECG-Chat's LLM backbone under LoRA tuning, mirroring LLaVA-v1.5.
- [LLaVA-v1.5](concepts/LLaVA15.md) — Liu et al. CVPR 2024; the visual-MLLM architectural precedent ECG-Chat directly mirrors (2-layer MLP adapter, two-stage training).
- [GraphRAG](concepts/GraphRAG.md) — Microsoft's knowledge-graph RAG (Edge et al. 2024). ECG-Chat builds the graph from 7 cardiology textbooks; lifts [[RAGAS]] Faithfulness 39.87→76.60 alone.
- [Multimodal LLM](concepts/MultimodalLLM.md) — Adapter-on-frozen-encoder pattern; ECG-Chat extends it to a physiological-signal modality for the first time in the wiki.
- [Waveform Data Enhancement (WDE)](concepts/WaveformDataEnhancement.md) — Text-side augmentation appending NeuroKit2 morphology to ECG reports; **30× retrieval R@1 lift** (2.14→64.7) on PTB-XL.
- [Diagnosis-Driven Prompt (DDP)](concepts/DiagnosisDrivenPrompt.md) — Classifier-into-prompt technique; doubles BLEU-1 and triples Rhythm F1 in ECG-Chat ablation.
- [ECG-Instruct](concepts/ECGInstruct.md) — ECG-Chat's GPT-4o-generated instruction-tuning corpus (19K diagnosis + 25K dialogue); first open ECG instruction-tuning dataset.
- [ECG-ExpertQA](concepts/ECGExpertQA.md) — 123-pair ECG QA evaluation benchmark; substrate for ECG-Chat's RAGAS ablation.
- [MIMIC-IV-ECG](concepts/MIMIC-IV-ECG.md) — 800K-record diagnostic ECG subset of MIMIC-IV (Gow et al. 2023); ECG-Chat's primary training source (788,822 records after cleaning).
- [PTB-XL](concepts/PTB-XL.md) — 21,837-record ECG dataset (Wagner et al. 2020) with SCP-Codes; primary zero-shot evaluation set in ECG-Chat.
- [CPSC2018](concepts/CPSC2018.md) — 6,877-record 9-label ECG benchmark (Liu et al. 2018); secondary classification eval set.
- [Champan-Shaoxing-Ningbo (CSN)](concepts/ChampanShaoxingNingbo.md) — Chinese 12-lead ECG database with SNOMED CT codes (Zheng et al. 2020); 40,637-sample ECG-Chat training contributor.
- [Shandong Provincial Hospital (SPH)](concepts/ShandongProvincialHospital.md) — Chinese ECG dataset (Liu et al. 2022) with AHA/ACC/HRS-conformant statements; 20,616-sample ECG-Chat training contributor.
- [Med-CPT](concepts/MedCPT.md) — PubMed-search-log contrastive text encoder (Jin et al. 2023); ECG-Chat's production text-encoder choice (wins classification by 1.8 F1 on CPSC2018).
- [BioLinkBert](concepts/BioLinkBert.md) — Document-link-pretrained BERT (Yasunaga, Leskovec & Liang ACL 2022); wins ECG-Chat retrieval ablation by ~8 R@1.
- [BioClinicalBert](concepts/BioClinicalBert.md) — MIMIC-III-pretrained clinical BERT (Alsentzer et al. 2019); middle of the ECG-Chat text-encoder ablation.
- [NeuroKit2](concepts/NeuroKit2.md) — Python physiological-signal-processing toolbox (Makowski et al. 2021); supplies ECG-Chat's lead-II waveform features for [[WaveformDataEnhancement|WDE]].
- [RAGAS](concepts/RAGAS.md) — Reference-free RAG evaluation framework (F / AR / CR / CP / CU / CER / SS); ECG-Chat's metric suite for GraphRAG × DSPy ablation.
- [ZeRO](concepts/ZeRO.md) — Rajbhandari et al. (SC20, 2020); the memory-partitioning trick that lets ECG-Chat fit Vicuna-13B + ECG encoder + LoRA on 8×V100 32GB.
- [Promptmrg](concepts/Promptmrg.md) — Radiology MLLM (Jin et al. AAAI 2024); originator of the diagnosis-driven prompt pattern ECG-Chat adapts.
- [Dia-LLaMA](concepts/Diallama.md) — LLaMA-based CT report-generation MLLM (Chen et al. 2024); sibling radiology precedent for DDP.
- [torch_ecg](concepts/TorchECG.md) — PyTorch ECG framework (Wen & Kang); supplies ECG-Chat's signal augmentations (baseline wander, cut mix, random masking).
- [plasTeX](concepts/plasTeX.md) — Python LaTeX framework (Smith, GitHub); ECG-Chat's structured-report generation backend.

<!-- Added with [[leh-ch01-understanding-llm-twin-concept]] through [[leh-ch11-mlops-and-llmops]] — LLM Engineer's Handbook (Iusztin, Labonne, Vesa; Packt 2024) -->

### Added with the LLM Engineer's Handbook ingest

Architectural patterns:
- [LLM Twin](concepts/LLMTwin.md) — The book's running project: a fine-tuned + RAG-augmented LLM that imitates a specific person's writing style; "a digital projection of yourself into an LLM."
- [FTI Architecture](concepts/FTIArchitecture.md) — Feature / Training / Inference pipeline pattern (Jim Dowling, Hopsworks); the book's architectural backbone, replacing monolithic and stateless-real-time anti-patterns.
- [Monolithic Batch Architecture](concepts/MonolithicBatchArchitecture.md) — Anti-pattern rejected before FTI: features can't be reused, scaling requires rewriting, work can't be split across teams.
- [Stateless Real-Time Architecture](concepts/StatelessRealTimeArchitecture.md) — Anti-pattern in which the client must ship the full feature state with every request; rejected by the book.
- [Monolithic Architecture](concepts/MonolithicArchitecture.md) — Single-process ML serving design; simple to start but can't scale GPU and CPU paths independently.
- [Microservices Architecture](concepts/MicroservicesArchitecture.md) — LLM Twin's chosen deployment pattern: a GPU-bound LLM microservice decoupled from a CPU/I-O-bound business microservice.
- [Data Collection Pipeline](concepts/DataCollectionPipeline.md) — Data-engineering-owned ETL pipeline that precedes the FTI trio; standardizes scraped content into articles / posts / repositories.
- [Logical Feature Store](concepts/LogicalFeatureStore.md) — Pragmatic substitute for a specialized feature store: vector DB (online) + versioned artifacts (offline); cheaper and sufficient for the MVP.
- [Google Cloud MLOps Reference](concepts/GoogleCloudMLOpsReference.md) — Google Cloud's production-ready MLOps reference architecture; positioned by the book as too complex (~20 moving pieces) for starting small.

LLM Twin product concepts:
- [Digital Twin](concepts/DigitalTwin.md) — 1:1 digital representation of a physical entity bridging physical and digital worlds; LLM Twin is the LLM-shaped specialization for personal writing.
- [Co-Pilot](concepts/CoPilot.md) — Generic AI assistant that augments a human task; contrasted with a digital twin's 1:1 representation of a real entity.
- [Minimum Viable Product](concepts/MinimumViableProduct.md) — Product-strategy concept used in Ch 1's "What" lens; the smallest feature set that demonstrates the product's core value.
- [Prompt Engineering](concepts/PromptEngineering.md) — One of three style-conditioning mechanisms (alongside fine-tuning and RAG) for steering LLM output.

MLOps / LLMOps:
- [LLMOps](concepts/LLMOps.md) — "MLOps at scale" — adds prompt monitoring with full traces, input/output guardrails, RLHF/DPO feedback loops, and acknowledges most teams adopt foundation models rather than train from scratch.
- [Continuous Training](concepts/ContinuousTraining.md) — Orchestrator-triggered retraining on schedule, event, or drift; the third MLOps automation tier beyond CI/CD.
- [Prompt Monitoring](concepts/PromptMonitoring.md) — Observability discipline for LLM systems: log query, prompt template, input variables, generated answer, token counts, and per-step latency; non-standard logging because prompts are unstructured chains.
- [Artifact](concepts/Artifact.md) — Any file produced during the ML lifecycle (datasets, trained models, checkpoints, logs); the central versioned object in ZenML pipelines.
- [Orchestrator](concepts/Orchestrator.md) — System that schedules and coordinates ML pipelines; ZenML, Airflow, Prefect, Dagster, Metaflow.
- [Materializer](concepts/Materializer.md) — ZenML's serializer extension point; the book extends it to handle UUID return types.
- [Directed Acyclic Graph](concepts/DirectedAcyclicGraph.md) — ZenML pipeline runs visualized as DAGs; the canonical pipeline shape.
- [Serverless](concepts/Serverless.md) — Compute model with no server management; used to describe Bedrock and ZenML Cloud.

Data / RAG:
- [Vector Database](concepts/VectorDatabase.md) — Database optimized for vector similarity search with CRUD, metadata filtering, scalability, real-time updates, backups; production-grade alternative to standalone indices like FAISS.
- [Chunking](concepts/Chunking.md) — Splitting text into bounded units for embedding; sliding window, regex-sentence-aware, or two-stage (paragraph + token-bounded).
- [Embedding](concepts/Embedding.md) — Dense vector representation of text/images/audio in a learned space; the substrate of RAG retrieval.
- [Instruct Dataset](concepts/InstructDataset.md) — Fine-tuning-ready output of the feature pipeline; instruction/answer or instruction/chosen/rejected triples, versioned as a feature-store artifact.
- [BM25](concepts/BM25.md) — Classical sparse-retrieval scoring function; the keyword half of hybrid search in advanced RAG.
- [Web Crawling](concepts/WebCrawling.md) — Programmatic extraction of web content; LLM Twin's data-collection mechanism via Selenium + BeautifulSoup + LangChain fallbacks.

Object/data patterns:
- [Polymorphism](concepts/Polymorphism.md) — OOP mechanism that lets `CrawlerDispatcher.extract()` call any registered crawler uniformly; foundational to the book's dispatcher patterns.
- [ORM](concepts/ORM.md) — Object-Relational Mapping; the SQLAlchemy/SQLModel pattern that motivates the book's ODM analogy.
- [ODM](concepts/ODM.md) — Object-Document Mapping; the book's hand-rolled `NoSQLBaseDocument` on top of `pymongo` + Pydantic for typed MongoDB access.
- [CRUD](concepts/CRUD.md) — Create / Read / Update / Delete; the operations ORMs and ODMs encapsulate.

Fine-tuning / alignment:
- [Direct Preference Optimization](concepts/DirectPreferenceOptimization.md) — Rafailov et al. 2023; closed-form policy from the RLHF objective implemented as binary cross-entropy with a beta-weighted KL penalty against a frozen reference policy. Aliased as DPO in the wiki.
- [DPO](concepts/DPO.md) — Short alias for [[DirectPreferenceOptimization]]; the post-SFT preference-alignment technique used to produce `TwinLlama-3.1-8B-DPO`.

Inference optimization:
- [Continuous Batching](concepts/ContinuousBatching.md) — In-flight batching; evict completed requests and admit waiting ones mid-batch to keep accelerators saturated. Supported by TGI, vLLM, TensorRT-LLM.
- [Tensor Parallelism](concepts/TensorParallelism.md) — Column/row-wise sharding of weight matrices within a layer across GPUs (Megatron-LM); the preferred inference parallelism strategy; requires NVLink/Infiniband.
- [Inference Optimization](concepts/InferenceOptimization.md) — Umbrella concept for the engineering techniques (KV cache, continuous batching, speculative decoding, flash attention, paged attention, quantization, parallelism) that make LLM serving practical.

Deployment archetypes:
- [Online Real-Time Inference](concepts/OnlineRealTimeInference.md) — Synchronous HTTP/REST or gRPC inference with low latency budget; the LLM Twin's chosen archetype.
- [Asynchronous Inference](concepts/AsynchronousInference.md) — Queue-mediated archetype with polling or push notifications; smooths spikes and is appropriate for >5-minute jobs.
- [Offline Batch Transform](concepts/OfflineBatchTransform.md) — Pull data → process in bulk → store results in object store/warehouse; throughput-optimized; appropriate when predictions can be stale.

AWS-specific deployment concepts:
- [AWS SageMaker Inference Endpoint](concepts/AWSSageMakerInferenceEndpoint.md) — The managed-inference HTTPS resource SageMaker hosts; composed of endpoint + model + endpoint configuration + inference component.
- [Hugging Face DLC](entities/HuggingFaceDLC.md) — Hugging Face Deep Learning Container; pre-built Docker image bundling `transformers` + `datasets` + `tokenizers` + TGI for SageMaker.
- [Application Auto Scaling](concepts/ApplicationAutoScaling.md) — AWS autoscaling control plane for SageMaker inference components; configured via a scalable target + a scaling policy.
- [Target Tracking Scaling](concepts/TargetTrackingScaling.md) — AWS autoscaling policy type that automatically manages CloudWatch alarms to drive a chosen metric toward a target value (e.g., `SageMakerInferenceComponentInvocationsPerCopy` or GPU utilization ~70%).
- [Scalable Target](concepts/ScalableTarget.md) — AWS Application Auto Scaling registration for a SageMaker inference component (resource ID, service namespace, scalable dimension, min/max capacity).
- [Scaling Policy](concepts/ScalingPolicy.md) — Definition of when scaling actions occur for a registered scalable target.
- [Cooldown Period](concepts/CooldownPeriod.md) — The most important autoscaling stability lever; delays both scale-out and scale-in after a previous adjustment to prevent oscillation.
- [Application Load Balancer](concepts/ApplicationLoadBalancer.md) — AWS ALB; sits between client and replicas (typically round-robin) so adding/removing replicas doesn't change the client-facing endpoint.
- [Round-Robin Routing](concepts/RoundRobinRouting.md) — Simplest load-balancer routing strategy; the default in front of multi-replica SageMaker endpoints.
- [Inference Component](concepts/InferenceComponent.md) — SageMaker artifact that binds model + endpoint configuration to an endpoint; can be scaled independently and is the target of `InvokeEndpoint`.
- [Invoke Endpoint](concepts/InvokeEndpoint.md) — SageMaker's runtime API (`boto3.client("sagemaker-runtime").invoke_endpoint(...)`) used by the LLM Twin client wrapper.
- [GPU Utilization](concepts/GPUUtilization.md) — Candidate target metric for SageMaker autoscaling (~70% leaves headroom for spikes while limiting idle cost).
- [IAM User](concepts/IAMUser.md) — AWS identity used to authenticate the developer's CLI; distinct from a role.
- [IAM Role](concepts/IAMRole.md) — AWS identity assumed by a service (SageMaker, EC2) to act on AWS resources on the developer's behalf.
- [ARN](concepts/ARN.md) — Amazon Resource Name; globally unique identifier for AWS resources.

Protocols and wire formats:
- [REST](concepts/REST.md) — Representational State Transfer; JSON-based architectural style underlying most LLM HTTP APIs.
- [REST API](concepts/RESTAPI.md) — Concrete REST endpoint surface; the client-facing protocol for the LLM Twin inference pipeline.
