- [JSON](concepts/JSON.md) — REST's default wire format; widely used because of its accessibility and tooling, at the cost of verbose serialization.
- [Protobuf](concepts/Protobuf.md) — gRPC's compiled schema format; binary, schema-coupled, faster on the wire than JSON.
- [gRPC](concepts/gRPC.md) — Google's binary RPC protocol; preferred for internal services within the same ML system at the cost of client/server schema coupling.
- [Server-Sent Events](concepts/ServerSentEvents.md) — SSE protocol used by TGI to stream tokens; the canonical real-time LLM UX backbone.
- [WebSockets](concepts/WebSockets.md) — Bidirectional streaming protocol used by ChatGPT/Claude for real-time token streaming.

<!-- Added with [[hands-on-llm-ch02-tokens-and-embeddings]] — Tokens & Embeddings deep-dive -->
- [Special Token](concepts/SpecialToken.md) — Umbrella for non-text tokens (`[CLS]`, `[SEP]`, `[PAD]`, `[UNK]`, `[MASK]`, `<s>`, `</s>`, `<|endoftext|>`, FIM tokens, chat role tokens) that encode model-system protocol.
- [Fill-in-the-Middle (FIM)](concepts/FillInTheMiddle.md) — Training objective + special tokens (`<|fim_prefix|>`/`<|fim_middle|>`/`<|fim_suffix|>`) used by [[GPT4|GPT-4]] and [[StarCoder2]] for code completion conditioned on both prefix and suffix.
- [Token Embedding](concepts/TokenEmbedding.md) — Per-token row of the LLM's `vocab_size × embedding_dim` embedding matrix; learned jointly with the rest of the model.
- [Static Embedding](concepts/StaticEmbedding.md) — Lookup-table embedding (same vector regardless of context); the LLM-input-layer special case, and the kind [[Word2Vec|word2vec]] / [[GloVe]] / [[FastText]] produce.
- [Text Embedding](concepts/TextEmbedding.md) — Single dense vector per sentence / paragraph / document; the substrate of [[SemanticSearch|semantic search]] + [[rag|RAG]].
- [Sentence Embedding](concepts/SentenceEmbedding.md) — The sentence-level special case of text embedding; canonical training recipe is [[SentenceTransformers|Sentence-BERT]].
- [Word2Vec Recommender](concepts/Word2VecRecommender.md) — Recommendation pattern that trains [[Word2Vec|word2vec]] on sequences of objects (songs in playlists, products in baskets) to learn embeddings whose nearest neighbors are good recommendation candidates.
- [Byte-Level Tokenization](concepts/ByteLevelTokenization.md) — Tokenization-free encoding ([[CANINE]] / [[ByT5]]) vs subword-tokenizers with byte fallback ([[GPT2|GPT-2]] / [[RoBERTa]]).
- [Word Tokenization](concepts/WordTokenization.md) — The pre-subword scheme; one token per word. Lives on in recommendation systems where subword decomposition makes no sense.
- [Character Tokenization](concepts/CharacterTokenization.md) — One token per character; no OOV failures, ~3× longer sequences than subword.
- [`[SEP]` Token](concepts/SepToken.md) — BERT segment-separator special token.
- [`[PAD]` Token](concepts/PadToken.md) — Padding special token that aligns variable-length sequences to fixed-length batches; companion to the attention mask.
- [`[UNK]` Token](concepts/UnkToken.md) — Unknown / out-of-vocabulary special token; eliminated by byte-fallback BPE.
- [`[MASK]` Token](concepts/MaskToken.md) — BERT's masked-language-model pretraining special token.
- [Vocabulary Size](concepts/VocabularySize.md) — Number of distinct tokens a tokenizer can produce; determines the embedding-matrix row count. Trend: 30K (BERT) → 50K (GPT-2) → 100K+ (GPT-4).

<!-- Added with [[hands-on-llm-ch03-looking-inside-llms]] — Transformer-internals deep-dive -->
- [Grouped-Query Attention (GQA)](concepts/GroupedQueryAttention.md) — K/V projections shared within groups of attention heads; interpolates between [[multiheadattention|multi-head]] and [[multiqueryattention|MQA]]; used by [[Llama|Llama 2]] / [[Llama|Llama 3]].
- [Rotary Positional Embeddings (RoPE)](concepts/RoPE.md) — Relative-aware positional encoding (Su et al., RoFormer) applied at the attention step; rotates queries and keys before relevance scoring. The modern alternative to absolute / sinusoidal positional encodings.
- [RMSNorm](concepts/RMSNorm.md) — Simpler and more efficient normalization replacing LayerNorm in modern LLMs (Phi-3, Llama 2/3). Drops the mean-centering step.
- [SwiGLU](concepts/SwiGLU.md) — Gated-activation FFN variant (Shazeer, *"GLU Variants Improve Transformer"*) that replaces ReLU in modern LLMs. SiLU-gated.
- [SiLU (Swish)](concepts/SiLU.md) — Activation function `x · sigmoid(x)`; used inside the SwiGLU gated MLP in modern LLMs.
- [Language Modeling Head (LM Head)](concepts/LMHead.md) — Final linear layer mapping the Transformer stack's hidden state to vocab-sized logits; interchangeable with sequence/token classification heads.
- [Decoding Strategy](concepts/DecodingStrategy.md) — Umbrella term for picking a token from the LM head's probability distribution; greedy vs sampling regimes.
- [Local / Sparse Attention](concepts/LocalAttention.md) — Restricted-context attention used by [[GPT3|GPT-3]] (interleaved with full-attention blocks) and Longformer (sliding window).
- [Sliding-Window Attention](concepts/SlidingWindowAttention.md) — Longformer's local-attention variant restricting each position to a fixed-size window of previous tokens.
- [Sequence Packing](concepts/SequencePacking.md) — Training-time efficiency: pack multiple short documents into one fixed-length context. Motivates the move to relative-aware positional encodings ([[RoPE]]).
- [Query Projection Matrix](concepts/QueryProjection.md) — Learned matrix that projects input tokens into queries; one of three projection matrices in self-attention. Per-head even in MQA / GQA.
- [Key Projection Matrix](concepts/KeyProjection.md) — Learned matrix that projects input tokens into keys; shared across heads in MQA / within groups in GQA.
- [Value Projection Matrix](concepts/ValueProjection.md) — Learned matrix that projects input tokens into values; same sharing pattern as keys.
- [Attention Head](concepts/AttentionHead.md) — One parallel attention computation within multi-head attention; each head has its own Q/K/V projections (full multi-head) or shares K/V (MQA/GQA).
- [Token Stream](concepts/TokenStream.md) — Per-position computation track through a Transformer LLM; count of streams = [[ContextLength|context length]]; cross-stream interaction only in attention sublayers.
- [Model Dimension](concepts/ModelDimension.md) — Size of the per-token vector flowing through a Transformer LLM (`d_model`). Embedding, residual stream, and sublayer I/O are all this size.

<!-- Added with [[hands-on-llm-ch04-text-classification]] — text-classification chapter -->
- [Task-Specific Model](concepts/TaskSpecificModel.md) — A representation model pretrained-and-fine-tuned for one downstream task (sentiment, NER, intent); used frozen for inference. Ch 4's first pretrained-LLM classification regime.
- [Embedding Model](concepts/EmbeddingModel.md) — A representation model producing general-purpose embeddings consumable across many downstream tasks. Ch 4's frozen-embeddings + logistic-regression recipe (F1 = 0.85 on Rotten Tomatoes).
- [Zero-Shot Classification](concepts/ZeroShotClassification.md) — Classification without labeled training data; Ch 4's recipe uses [[LabelEmbedding|label embeddings]] + [[CosineSimilarity|cosine similarity]] (F1 = 0.78 on Rotten Tomatoes with no labels).
- [Label Embedding](concepts/LabelEmbedding.md) — Dense vector representation of a class label produced by embedding a natural-language label *description*; the zero-shot-classification primitive.
- [Generative Classification](concepts/GenerativeClassification.md) — Using a generative LLM (decoder-only or encoder-decoder) as a classifier via prompt instruction + free-text parsing back to a class label. Ch 4: Flan-T5 (F1 = 0.84), ChatGPT (F1 = 0.91).
- [Classification Head](concepts/ClassificationHead.md) — Trainable output layer turning the final hidden state(s) into class logits; can be baked into the pretrained checkpoint or be an external classifier like logistic regression.
- [Binary Sentiment Classification](concepts/BinarySentimentClassification.md) — The two-label (positive / negative) variant of sentiment analysis; Ch 4's task on Rotten Tomatoes.
- [Classification Report](concepts/ClassificationReport.md) — sklearn's per-class precision / recall / F1 / support table; Ch 4's evaluation primitive across all four model regimes.
- [Confusion Matrix](concepts/ConfusionMatrix.md) — 2×2 (binary) or K×K (multiclass) table of prediction-vs-truth counts; the data structure from which precision / recall / accuracy / F1 are derived.
- [Precision](concepts/Precision.md) — Fraction of positive predictions that were correct.
- [Recall](concepts/Recall.md) — Fraction of actual positives the model correctly identified.
- [Accuracy](concepts/Accuracy.md) — Fraction of all predictions that were correct; misleading on imbalanced data.
- [Exponential Backoff](concepts/ExponentialBackoff.md) — Retry strategy where sleep time doubles after each failure; Ch 4's recommended mitigation for OpenAI API rate limits.
- [Benchmark Contamination](concepts/BenchmarkContamination.md) — Alias for [[DataContamination|data contamination]]; the epistemological limit Ch 4 flags for closed-source-LLM evaluation on public datasets.

<!-- Added with [[hands-on-llm-ch05-text-clustering-topic-modeling]] — text-clustering + topic-modeling chapter -->
- [Text Clustering](concepts/TextClustering.md) — Grouping documents by semantic content using embeddings → dimensionality reduction → density clustering; Ch 5's primary subject.
- [Topic Modeling](concepts/TopicModeling.md) — Inferring thematic structure across a document collection; Ch 5 maps the classical LDA framing to BERTopic's modern embedding-based pipeline.
- [BERTopic](concepts/BERTopic.md) — [[MaartenGrootendorst|Grootendorst's]] modular topic-modeling framework ([[2203.05794-bertopic|2022]]); embed → UMAP → HDBSCAN → c-TF-IDF + reranking representation models.
- [UMAP (Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection)](concepts/UMAP.md) — Nonlinear dimensionality reducer ([[LelandMcInnes|McInnes]] et al. 2018); Ch 5's default reducer (384 → 5 dims).
- [HDBSCAN](concepts/HDBSCAN.md) — Hierarchical Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise ([[LelandMcInnes|McInnes]] et al. 2017); Ch 5's clustering algorithm (`min_cluster_size=50`, finds 156 clusters + outlier label).
- [DBSCAN](concepts/DBSCAN.md) — Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (Ester et al. KDD '96); HDBSCAN's parent algorithm.
- [Density-Based Clustering](concepts/DensityBasedClustering.md) — The clustering family DBSCAN / HDBSCAN belong to; finds clusters as connected regions of high density, marks low-density points as outliers.
- [Centroid-Based Clustering](concepts/CentroidBasedClustering.md) — The clustering family k-means belongs to; partitions points by distance to learned cluster centers; contrast with density-based.
- [Dimensionality Reduction](concepts/DimensionalityReduction.md) — Mapping high-dimensional embeddings to low-dimensional spaces while preserving structure; Ch 5's UMAP step.
- [Class-Based TF-IDF (c-TF-IDF)](concepts/ClassBasedTFIDF.md) — BERTopic's per-cluster TF-IDF variant: term frequency summed across a cluster, IDF computed across clusters.
- [KeyBERTInspired](concepts/KeyBERTInspired.md) — BERTopic representation model that reranks candidate keywords by cosine similarity to the per-topic average document embedding; modeled after KeyBERT.
- [Maximal Marginal Relevance (MMR)](concepts/MaximalMarginalRelevance.md) — Carbonell & Goldstein 1998 diversity-vs-relevance keyword selector; used in BERTopic to deduplicate redundant keyword candidates.
- [Generative Topic Labeling](concepts/GenerativeTopicLabeling.md) — Prompt an LLM with `[DOCUMENTS]` + `[KEYWORDS]` per topic to produce a short natural-language label; Ch 5's Flan-T5 + GPT-3.5 demos.
- [Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA)](concepts/LatentDirichletAllocation.md) — Classical Bayesian topic model (Blei, Ng & Jordan 2003); Ch 5's baseline contrasted against BERTopic.
- [Guided Topic Modeling](concepts/GuidedTopicModeling.md) — BERTopic variant where the practitioner supplies seed words/topics to nudge clustering.
- [Seeded Topic Modeling](concepts/SeededTopicModeling.md) — Synonym for guided topic modeling.
- [Dynamic Topic Modeling](concepts/DynamicTopicModeling.md) — BERTopic variant tracking how topics evolve over time.
- [Hierarchical Topic Modeling](concepts/HierarchicalTopicModeling.md) — BERTopic variant producing a topic tree by recursive topic merging.
- [Semi-Supervised Topic Modeling](concepts/SemiSupervisedTopicModeling.md) — BERTopic variant accepting partial document labels.
- [Zero-Shot Topic Modeling](concepts/ZeroShotTopicModeling.md) — BERTopic variant that aligns clusters with pre-defined topic names via embedding similarity.
- [Online / Incremental Topic Modeling](concepts/OnlineTopicModeling.md) — BERTopic variant streaming new documents into an existing topic model.
- [Multimodal Topic Modeling](concepts/MultimodalTopicModeling.md) — BERTopic variant clustering on text + image embeddings.
- [Outlier (cluster `-1`)](concepts/Outlier.md) — Points that don't belong to any density cluster; HDBSCAN's signature output; 14,520 of 44,949 ArXiv NLP abstracts in Ch 5.
- [Neural Search](concepts/NeuralSearch.md) — Embedding-based information retrieval (with reranking); Ch 5 forward-references Ch 8 as the neural-search chapter; Ch 5's representation-model abstraction is the same reranking pattern.
- [Plotly](concepts/Plotly.md) — Interactive plotting library; powers BERTopic's `visualize_documents()` and related interactive 2D views.
- [Datamapplot](concepts/Datamapplot.md) — Labeled 2D landscape visualization library; Ch 5's chapter-closing figure renders the top-20 GPT-3.5-labeled BERTopic topics over the 2D UMAP projection.

<!-- Added with [[hands-on-llm-ch06-prompt-engineering]] — prompt-engineering chapter; opens Part III of *Hands-On LLMs* -->
- [Instruction (Prompt Component)](concepts/InstructionPrompt.md) — The task itself; Ch 6's seven-component-prompt slot #2. Specificity is the most important property.
- [Context (Prompt Component)](concepts/ContextPrompt.md) — Background reason for the task; Ch 6's seven-component-prompt slot #3. Distinct from broader [[ContextConstruction|context construction]] / [[rag|RAG]].
- [Output Format (Prompt Component)](concepts/OutputFormat.md) — How the output should be structured; Ch 6's seven-component-prompt slot #4. The prompt-level alternative to [[GrammarConstrainedDecoding|grammar-constrained decoding]].
- [Audience (Prompt Component)](concepts/AudiencePrompt.md) — Who the output is for and at what level (e.g., ELI5); Ch 6's seven-component-prompt slot #5.
- [Tone (Prompt Component)](concepts/TonePrompt.md) — Voice / register of the generated text; Ch 6's seven-component-prompt slot #6.
- [Output Verification](concepts/OutputVerification.md) — Verifying and controlling LLM output before downstream consumption; Ch 6's four motivations (structure / validity / ethics / accuracy) × three methods (examples / grammar / fine-tuning).
- [Grammar-Constrained Decoding](concepts/GrammarConstrainedDecoding.md) — Token-level [[ConstrainedSampling|constrained sampling]] enforcing a formal grammar (JSON / regex / CFG); Ch 6's `llama-cpp-python` + GGUF Phi-3 + `response_format={"type": "json_object"}` worked example is the wiki's first runnable demonstration.
- [Prompt Chaining](concepts/PromptChaining.md) — Ch 6's vocabulary for breaking a problem across sequential LLM calls; equivalent to [[PromptDecomposition|prompt decomposition]] in Huyen Ch 5; worked example: name → slogan → sales pitch.
- [One-Shot Prompting](concepts/OneShotPrompting.md) — Single-example in-context learning; the middle point between zero-shot and few-shot. Ch 6's Gigamuru/screeg worked example.
- [Primacy Effect](concepts/PrimacyEffect.md) — LLMs focus more on beginning-of-prompt content; with the recency effect, drives Ch 6's *"place instructions at start or end, not middle"* tip.
- [Zero-Shot Chain-of-Thought](concepts/ZeroShotCoT.md) — Eliciting step-by-step reasoning without examples via the *"Let's think step-by-step"* trigger (Kojima et al. 2022); alternative triggers like *"Take a deep breath"* per Yang et al. 2023.
- [EmotionPrompt](concepts/EmotionPrompt.md) — Li et al. 2023 — appending emotional appeals (*"This is very important for my career"*) to prompts; Ch 6's example of a creative cross-cutting prompt component beyond the seven-component framework.

<!-- Added with [[hands-on-llm-ch07-advanced-text-generation]] — advanced text generation techniques and tools chapter; Part III Ch 2; first LangChain-centric source -->
- [ConversationBufferMemory](concepts/ConversationBufferMemory.md) — `langchain.memory.ConversationBufferMemory` — LangChain's full-history memory class; appends every prior turn to each prompt. Ch 7's baseline memory type; **instant but hogs tokens**.
- [ConversationBufferWindowMemory](concepts/ConversationBufferWindowMemory.md) — `langchain.memory.ConversationBufferWindowMemory(k=N)` — LangChain's last-`k`-turns memory class; the operationalization of [[FIFOMemory|FIFO eviction]]. Ch 7's worked example demonstrates the *forgotten-age* failure mode Huyen Ch 6 names.
- [ConversationSummaryMemory](concepts/ConversationSummaryMemory.md) — `langchain.memory.ConversationSummaryMemory` — LangChain's running-summary memory class; the operationalization of [[SummarizationMemory|summarization-based memory]]; two LM calls per turn (user prompt + summarization prompt); the summarization LLM can be different from the user LLM.
- [LangChain Expression Language (LCEL)](concepts/LCEL.md) — LangChain's pipe-operator composition syntax: `basic_chain = prompt | llm`. The structural composition primitive Ch 7 uses throughout — chains *are* the composition.
- [LLMChain](concepts/LLMChain.md) — `langchain.LLMChain(llm, prompt, output_key)` — LangChain's named-output chain primitive; the substrate for multi-step sequential chains like Ch 7's three-stage story-generation worked example (`title | character | story`).
- [`langchain.LlamaCpp`](concepts/LangChainLlamaCpp.md) — LangChain's wrapper around [[llamacpp|llama-cpp-python]] for loading [[GGUF]]-quantized models. Ch 7's Model-I/O primitive; surfaces the empty-output gotcha that chat templates are NOT auto-applied (unlike `transformers.pipeline`).
- [LangChain Agent (`create_react_agent` + `AgentExecutor`)](concepts/LangChainAgent.md) — LangChain's [[react|ReAct]] agent-construction surface; the wiki's first runnable LangChain-native ReAct receipt. Ch 7's four-line agent construction running DuckDuckGo + llm-math over [[ChatGPT|GPT-3.5-turbo]].
- [`llm-math` (LangChain built-in calculator tool)](concepts/LLMMathTool.md) — `load_tools(["llm-math"], llm=llm)` — LangChain's built-in calculator tool; uses an LLM to convert natural-language math into a Python expression and evaluate it. Ch 7's worked calculator extending the LLM's capability surface beyond native arithmetic.
- [`langchain.tools.DuckDuckGoSearchResults`](concepts/DuckDuckGoSearchResults.md) — LangChain Python class wrapping [[DuckDuckGoSearch|DuckDuckGo]] as an agent-callable tool. Ch 7's worked web-search tool; demonstrates the `Tool(name, description, func)` wrapping pattern for arbitrary callables.
- [Stateless LLM](concepts/StatelessLLM.md) — LLMs have no memory of prior forward passes; all memory in LLM applications is application-side. Ch 7's structural justification for the three memory classes (Buffer / BufferWindow / Summary).
- [Tool Use](concepts/ToolUse.md) — The general technique of giving an LLM access to external functions (calculators, search engines, APIs); the *action* half of [[react|ReAct]]'s Thought/Action/Observation cycle. Ch 7's two-tool agent demonstrates the technique with the smallest possible inventory.

<!-- Added with [[hands-on-llm-ch08-semantic-search-and-rag]] — semantic-search and RAG chapter; the book's headline RAG treatment -->
- [Dense Retrieval](concepts/DenseRetrieval.md) — Ch 8's name for embedding-based / semantic retrieval: embed query + documents, find nearest neighbors in vector space; alias of [[EmbeddingBasedRetrieval]].
- [Sparse Retrieval](concepts/SparseRetrieval.md) — Ch 8's name for keyword / lexical / [[BM25]]-style retrieval (alias of [[TermBasedRetrieval]]); high-dimensional sparse term-frequency vectors with saturating TF + length normalization.
- [Grounded Generation](concepts/GroundedGeneration.md) — The generation step of [[rag|RAG]]; *"the retrieved relevant information we provide the LLM establishes a certain context that grounds the LLM in the domain we're interested in."* Ch 8's name for what Cohere's `co.chat(documents=...)` does.
- [Generative Search](concepts/GenerativeSearch.md) — Search systems with a generative LLM at the end (subset of RAG); Ch 8's named examples are [[Perplexity]], Microsoft Bing AI, and Google [[gemini|Gemini]].
- [Citation Generation](concepts/CitationGeneration.md) — Span-level citations in RAG outputs (`ChatCitation(start=..., end=..., document_ids=[...])`); Ch 8's worked Cohere `co.chat` example produces these automatically — the wiki's first runnable demonstration.
- [Citation Recall](concepts/CitationRecall.md) — Liu / Zhang / Liang 2023 RAG-evaluation axis: *"the proportion of generated statements about the external world that are fully supported by their citations."*
- [Citation Precision](concepts/CitationPrecision.md) — Liu / Zhang / Liang 2023 RAG-evaluation axis: *"the proportion of generated citations that support their associated statements."*
- [Faithfulness](concepts/Faithfulness.md) — [[RAGAS|Ragas]] metric per Ch 8: *"whether the answer is consistent with the provided context."* Complements Ragas's seven-metric coverage in [[2408.08849-ecg-chat|ECG-Chat]].
- [Answer Relevance](concepts/AnswerRelevance.md) — [[RAGAS|Ragas]] metric per Ch 8: *"how relevant the answer is to the question."*
- [Fluency](concepts/Fluency.md) — Liu / Zhang / Liang 2023 RAG-evaluation axis: *"whether the generated text is fluent and cohesive."*
- [Perceived Utility](concepts/PerceivedUtility.md) — Liu / Zhang / Liang 2023 RAG-evaluation axis: *"whether the generated answer is helpful and informative."*
- [RAG Evaluation](concepts/RAGEvaluation.md) — The multi-axis evaluation surface for [[rag|RAG]]: Liu / Zhang / Liang 2023 four-axis taxonomy (fluency / perceived utility / citation recall / citation precision) + [[RAGAS|Ragas]] (faithfulness + answer relevance + others). Automatable via [[llmasjudge|LLM-as-a-judge]].
- [Multi-Query RAG](concepts/MultiQueryRAG.md) — Ch 8's Advanced-RAG extension where one user question maps to **multiple parallel queries** (Nvidia 2020 vs 2023 → two queries); also includes the no-search option.
- [Multi-Hop RAG](concepts/MultiHopRAG.md) — Ch 8's Advanced-RAG extension where one user question requires **sequential queries**, each consuming the previous result (largest car manufacturers 2023 → Toyota/VW/Hyundai → three EV-followups).
- [Query Routing](concepts/QueryRouting.md) — Ch 8's Advanced-RAG extension for **multi-data-source RAG**; the model decides which data source to query (HR → Notion, customer → Salesforce / CRM).
- [Agentic RAG](concepts/AgenticRAG.md) — Ch 8's most-delegated point on the Advanced-RAG continuum; LLM-as-agent over multiple data sources with **read+write tool symmetry**. *"Likely only the largest managed models may be able to attempt this behavior"* — the agent-capability-cliff caveat (cf. [[hands-on-llm-ch07-advanced-text-generation|Ch 7]]).
- [monoBERT](concepts/MonoBERT.md) — Nogueira & Lin's BERT-as-cross-encoder reranking architecture; *"Multi-stage document ranking with BERT."* Ch 8's named reference cross-encoder reranker.
- [Similarity Threshold](concepts/SimilarityThreshold.md) — Dense-retrieval mitigation for out-of-distribution queries returning nearest-but-irrelevant results; *"a max threshold of similarity score to filter out irrelevant results."*
- [Average Precision](concepts/AveragePrecision.md) — Per-query average of [[PrecisionAtK|precisions-at-k]] at the positions where relevant documents appear; the building block of [[MAP|Mean Average Precision]].
- [Precision at K](concepts/PrecisionAtK.md) — *"Number of relevant results at position k, divided by k."* The position-by-position primitive Ch 8 walks through to construct [[AveragePrecision|AP]] → [[MAP]].
- [Relevance Judgment](concepts/RelevanceJudgment.md) — Human-annotated ground truth for retrieval evaluation; the third component (alongside text archive + queries) Ch 8 names as required for IR evaluation. The annotation bottleneck of IR.
- [Information Retrieval](concepts/InformationRetrieval.md) — The parent IR field [[rag|RAG]] and [[SemanticSearch|semantic search]] inherit their evaluation vocabulary from ([[MAP]] / [[NDCG]] / [[MRR]] / [[PrecisionAtK|P@k]] / [[Recall]]).
- [Stop Word](concepts/StopWord.md) — High-frequency function words removed during [[BM25]] tokenization; Ch 8 uses `sklearn.feature_extraction._stop_words.ENGLISH_STOP_WORDS` in the worked BM25 example.

<!-- Added with the [[iir-ch01-boolean-retrieval|IIR]] (Introduction to Information Retrieval, Manning/Raghavan/Schütze 2008) 21-chapter ingest. Highest-value anchors — the load-bearing pre-neural IR concepts. ~100 more wikilinks introduced across the chapters remain as forward references for a future curation pass (see [[overview]] §XII "Pending consolidation"). -->
- [Vector Space Model](concepts/VectorSpaceModel.md) — Documents as |V|-dim term-weighted vectors; cosine similarity for ranking; COSINESCORE algorithm. Workhorse ranker of pre-neural IR. ([[iir-ch06-vector-space-model]])
- [PageRank](concepts/PageRank.md) — Stationary distribution of a teleporting random walk on the web graph; power iteration; combined as static quality score with content relevance. [[google|Google]]'s founding ranking signal. ([[iir-ch21-link-analysis]])
- [HITS (Hyperlink-Induced Topic Search)](concepts/HITS.md) — Kleinberg's query-dependent hubs-and-authorities algorithm; principal eigenvectors of AA^T and A^TA on the query-specific subgraph. ([[iir-ch21-link-analysis]])
- [Latent Semantic Indexing (LSI)](concepts/LatentSemanticIndexing.md) — Truncated SVD of the term-document matrix to project queries / docs into a $k$-dim "concept" space; partially handles synonymy/polysemy. Conceptual ancestor of dense [[EmbeddingBasedRetrieval]]. ([[iir-ch18-lsi-matrix-decompositions]])
- [Rocchio Algorithm](concepts/RocchioAlgorithm.md) — Vector-space relevance-feedback update $q_m = \alpha q_0 + \beta\,\text{centroid}(D_r) - \gamma\,\text{centroid}(D_{nr})$; also generalizes to [[RocchioClassification]]. ([[iir-ch09-relevance-feedback-query-expansion]])
- [Postings List](concepts/PostingsList.md) — Per-term sorted list of docIDs (optionally with frequencies/positions) inside the [[InvertedIndex]]; intersection / union / score-accumulation primitives; gap-encoded + γ/VByte compressed.
- [Boolean Retrieval](concepts/BooleanRetrieval.md) — Simplest retrieval model — queries as Boolean expressions over terms; binary match, no ranking; AND/OR/NOT via postings-list set operations. ([[iir-ch01-boolean-retrieval]])
- [Query Likelihood Model](concepts/QueryLikelihoodModel.md) — Probabilistic ranker: rank docs by $P(q \mid M_d)$ under a multinomial unigram LM with Jelinek-Mercer or Dirichlet smoothing (Ponte & Croft 1998). **Statistical** LMs — NOT modern neural [[LanguageModel]]s. ([[iir-ch12-language-models-ir]])
- [Binary Independence Model (BIM)](concepts/BinaryIndependenceModel.md) — Probabilistic-IR model under binary term occurrence + conditional independence given relevance; yields RSV = Σ log[p(1−u) / (u(1−p))]; direct ancestor of [[OkapiBM25|BM25]]. ([[iir-ch11-probabilistic-ir]])
- [Probability Ranking Principle (PRP)](concepts/ProbabilityRankingPrinciple.md) — Robertson's 1977 theorem: ranking by $P(R=1 \mid q,d)$ is optimal under 1/0 loss. Licenses the entire probabilistic-IR family ([[BinaryIndependenceModel]], [[OkapiBM25]]). ([[iir-ch11-probabilistic-ir]])
- [k-Nearest Neighbor (kNN)](concepts/KNearestNeighbor.md) — Lazy/instance-based classifier; predict majority class among $k$ nearest training points; Voronoi tessellation for $k=1$; test time $O(|D| \cdot M_a)$ without indexing. ([[iir-ch14-vector-space-classification]])
- [Shingling](concepts/Shingling.md) — Document fingerprinting via overlapping $k$-word subsequences; Jaccard similarity over shingle sets estimates near-duplicate-ness. The pre-neural near-duplicate stack with [[MinHash]]. ([[iir-ch19-web-search-basics]])
- [MinHash](concepts/MinHash.md) — Locality-sensitive hash family for Jaccard similarity: $\Pr[\min_x h(x) \text{ collides}] = J(A,B)$; $k$-tuple sketch + LSH bands. Production-scale near-duplicate detection (AltaVista 1997). ([[iir-ch19-web-search-basics]])
- [Mean Average Precision (MAP)](concepts/MeanAveragePrecision.md) — Mean over queries of per-query Average Precision; canonical TREC ad-hoc retrieval metric for binary-relevance test collections. ([[iir-ch08-ir-evaluation]])
- [Heaps' Law](concepts/HeapsLaw.md) — Vocabulary growth $M = k \cdot T^b$ with $b \approx 0.49$ — sublinear but never saturating. Empirically the type-side companion to [[ZipfsLaw]]'s token-side power law. ([[iir-ch05-index-compression]])
- [Cranfield Paradigm](concepts/CranfieldParadigm.md) — Standard offline IR evaluation methodology: fixed corpus + topic set + relevance judgments. Originated 1966; powers TREC, CLEF, NTCIR, FIRE, [[INEX]], MS MARCO. ([[iir-ch08-ir-evaluation]])
- [Pseudo-Relevance Feedback (PRF)](concepts/PseudoRelevanceFeedback.md) — Blind feedback: treat top-$k$ initial results as relevant and apply [[RocchioAlgorithm|Rocchio]]. Useful but topic-drift-prone. Used as a strong baseline for new retrieval methods. ([[iir-ch09-relevance-feedback-query-expansion]])
- [Web Crawler](concepts/WebCrawler.md) — Hyperlink-following downloader feeding an indexer; Mercator-style URL frontier with front (priority) + back (per-host) queues; DNS as bottleneck. Examples: [[Heritrix]], GoogleBot, ccBot. ([[iir-ch20-web-crawling-indexes]])
- [Anchor Text](concepts/AnchorText.md) — The visible click-target text of a hyperlink; treated as extra index content for the *target* page since others' descriptions often beat the page's own text; core signal for early Google. ([[iir-ch21-link-analysis]])
- [Markov Chain](concepts/MarkovChain.md) — Discrete-time stochastic process with memoryless transitions; stationary distribution $\pi = \pi P$; ergodicity ⇒ uniqueness + convergence under power iteration. The substrate of [[PageRank]]. ([[iir-ch21-link-analysis]])
- [Cluster Hypothesis](concepts/ClusterHypothesis.md) — *"Documents in the same cluster behave similarly with respect to relevance to information needs."* Justifies [[ClusterPruning]], cluster-based smoothing, result-page clustering. ([[iir-ch16-flat-clustering]])
- [Entity Extraction](concepts/EntityExtraction.md) — Umbrella for the *return-the-subset* task framing of entity-mention identification, distinct from per-token [[NamedEntityRecognition|NER]]. Encoder-fine-tuning vs decoder-LLM-with-structured-output operational templates compared; the latter is the [[dspy-entity-extraction-tutorial|DSPy entity-extraction tutorial]] receipt on [[CoNLL2003|CoNLL-2003]] (86 → 93% via [[MIPROv2]]).
- [Eckart-Young Theorem](concepts/EckartYoungTheorem.md) — Truncated SVD is the best rank-$k$ matrix approximation in Frobenius norm: $\|C - C_k\|_F^2 = \sum_{i>k} \sigma_i^2$. The optimality result behind [[LatentSemanticIndexing|LSI]] and PCA. ([[iir-ch18-lsi-matrix-decompositions]])
